title: Tomato Sheer Recipe -Tomato And Coconut Curry Recipe
instructions: To begin making Tomato Sheer Recipe, in a pan, heat the oil, add asafoetida and the fenugreek seeds.
Allow the fenugreek seeds to roast for a few seconds.
Add in the chopped onion and sauté until the onions turn transparent and soft.
Once the onions have softened, add the chopped tomatoes and cook till the onion and tomatoes combine to form a thick paste. This will take 8 to 10 minutes until the tomatoes cook through completely.

In the meanwhile, dissolve the besan in a few tablespoons of coconut milk. Add in the salt, chilli powder and sugar and mix well. Stir in the rest of the coconut milk and stir until well combined. The sugar is only intended to take the edge off the acidity of the tomatoes and should not overpower or sweeten the taste of this curry.
Add this coconut milk mixture to the pan with onion and tomato paste.

Whisk to combine it together. Simmer the Tomato Sheer low heat until lightly bubbly, about 5 to 8 minutes. Add a little water if required to adjust the consistency of the Tomato Sheer / Tomato Coconut Curry.
Check the salt and spices and adjust the taste accordingly. Once done, turn off the heat and transfer the Tomato Sheer Recipe to a serving bowl.
Serve Tomato Sheer/ Tomato Coconut Milk Curry with Manathakkali Kootu, Steamed Rice and Elai Vadam for a comforting lunch.

title: Classic Grilled Tomato Cucumber Chutney Sandwich Recipe
ingredients: 1 Cucumber, peeled and sliced into thin rounds
instructions: To begin making the Classic Tomato Cucumber Chutney Sandwich with Chutney Recipe, arrange two slices of bread next to each other.
Spread tomato ketchup on one slice and the Dhaniya Pudina Chutney on the other slice.
Arrange the sliced tomato & cucumber slices on one of slice. Sprinkle some chaat masala powder, pepper powder and salt. Close the sandwich with the other slice.
Heat a grill sandwich maker, lightly spread butter on the outside and cook until it turns golden brown, around 3-4 minutes or when the light turns off on the sandwich maker.
If you don't have a sandwich maker, you can grill the sandwich on the tawa on medium heat until each one of the sides turn golden brown and crisp.
Once the Tomato Cucumber Chutney Sandwich is grilled well, place it on a platter and cut into triangles and serve.

Serve the Classic Grilled Tomato Cucumber Chutney Sandwich for a quick weeknight dinner and serve it along with Indian Style Beetroot Soup Recipe and Bean Sprout & Corn Salad Recipe for a weeknight dinner, simple serve the sandwich along with a glass of Chikoo Banana Date Smoothie as an after school snack for kids.

title: Narkel Naru Ladoo Recipe | Bengali Style Coconut Ladoo Recipe
ingredients: 10 sultana raisins, and more to garnish
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, combine the grated coconut and sugar, pour in the milk and place the pan over medium heat.
Stir continuously until the sugar dissolves completely.
Continue to cook the mixture, stirring frequently, until it thickens and starts to leave the sides of the pan, about 10–12 minutes.
Add the cardamom powder and mix well; if using nuts or khoya, add them now and stir to combine.
Remove the mixture from heat and let it cool slightly until manageable but still warm.
Grease your hands with ghee, take small portions of the mixture and roll into round balls about the size of a golf ball.
Allow the ladoos to cool completely on a plate, then store them in an airtight container.
Narkel Naru Ladoos can be kept at room temperature for up to a week.
Serve the coconut ladoos as a dessert or snack with masala chai.

title: Masala Chaas Recipe - Indian Spiced Buttermilk
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a few sprigs, chopped
instructions: To begin making the Masala Chaas Recipe take your serving glasses and chill them in freezer for about 5 minutes before serving.

Mix all ingredients including curd, cumin powder, chaat masala powder, black salt, ginger, green chilli, black pepper powder, asafoetida, salt, chilled water except coriander leaves and mint leaves. Use a hand blender until everything is mixed and is smooth.

If desired – take your panchajiri / chaat masala / Jeeralu in a plate. Now dip the rim of your chilled glass on it making sure that the masala is coated around the edge of the glass rim. This gives an interesting look on the presentation and makes it even tastier.
Pour the Masala Chaas into your glasses. Top with chopped coriander leaves and mint leaves. You can also put in mint as a stirrer.
Serve Masala Chaas Recipe along with Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma, Gatte Ki Sabzi and Kachumber Salad for a weekend lunch.

title: Quick and Easy Bread Upma Recipe
instructions: To begin making the bread upma recipe, we will first toast the bread. You can toast it in your toaster or on a skillet.
Once the bread is toasted, apply the softened butter over the toasted bread. Next cut the bread into small dices and keep aside.

In a large wok or a kadai, heat 1 tablespoon of oil on medium heat and add in the mustard seeds. Allow the mustard seeds to crackle and add in the onions and green chillies. Saute the onions on medium heat, until soft and tender.
Once the onions are soft, add in the tomatoes, curry leaves, turmeric powder and sambar powder. Stir and cook the tomatoes until they turn lightly soft as well.
Finally add in the salt and the toasted buttered bread pieces. Stir well to combine all the ingredients and stir fry on medium to high heat for a couple of minutes.
We stir fry just to make sure the bread pieces have got all the spices and salted well. Check salt levels. Remember the butter you used could have some salt as well.
Stir in the chopped coriander leaves into the bread upma to get the delicious fresh flavour.
Serve the Bread Upma Recipe for a healthy breakfast along with Papaya Banana Smoothie Recipe.

title: Gluten Free Samosa Recipe
instructions: Peel, dice and boil the potatoes. Mash the potatoes and keep them aside in a bowl.
Heat butter in a pan, add the cumin seeds and fry the diced onions until soft and translucent.
Add the cooked onion, garam masala, and salt to the mashed potatoes. Mix until well blended.
Stir in the boiled peas into the potato mixture and set aside. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Fill a large bowl one‑quarter full with water. Soak each rice paper sheet for 1‑2 minutes until soft.

Place a softened rice paper sheet on a counter, put 1‑2 tablespoons of the potato mixture in the center, fold the bottom up, fold the sides in, and fold the top down. Brush each samosa with oil and place on a well‑oiled pan.
Bake the samosas for 20‑25 minutes, turning a few times during baking, until golden and crisp.
Serve the gluten‑free samosas hot with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai.

title: Whole Wheat Ladoo With Jaggery Recipe
instructions: Dry roast whole wheat flour in a heavy bottomed pan on low flame until fragrant, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Once the color changes slightly, remove and set aside to cool; then dissolve jaggery in water in a pan over heat.
Bring the jaggery mixture to a full boil, then continue boiling on medium‑high for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Do not let the syrup become too thick; add cardamom powder, mix well, and remove from heat.
Allow the syrup to cool, then pour it into the roasted flour and mix by hand until fully incorporated.
Add ghee, mix briefly, and shape the mixture into laddus (about 2 tablespoons each); store in an airtight container.
Serve the wheat ladoos with snacks such as crispy sweet potato or poha chivda for festivals.

title: Sweet Potato And Moong Sprouts Cutlet Recipe
instructions: Wash, peel and cook sweet potato until soft.
In a large mixing bowl, mash the boiled sweet potato and let it cool down.
Cook sprouts with a little water and a pinch of salt until tender.
Drain the sprouts, pat dry with a kitchen towel, and add them to the bowl with the mashed potato.
Add ground poha, coriander leaves, onion, mint leaves, green chillies, ginger, amchur powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder and salt; mix well and let the mixture rest for 20‑30 minutes.
Shape the rested mixture into tikkis or cutlets and set aside.
Heat a pan, add some oil and shallow‑fry the cutlets on both sides until golden brown.
Transfer the cutlets to a plate lined with oil‑absorbent paper to drain excess oil.
Place the cutlets on a bed of shredded purple cabbage, sprinkle with chaat masala and serve with a lemon wedge, alongside Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Date Tamarind Chutney.

title: Egg Rolls With Moringa Leaves Recipe-Eggs with Drumstick Leaves
ingredients: 1 cup drumstick leaves (moringa/murungai keerai), finely chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Line a 13 x 9 inch rectangular baking pan and grease it with butter.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a small wok/kadai, add the drumstick leaves, sprinkle salt, and cook until wilted and moisture evaporates; then let cool.
Whisk the eggs with flour, salt, pepper, and green chilies, pour into the prepared pan, spread the cooked drumstick leaves over the egg mixture, and sprinkle cheddar cheese on top.
Cover the pan with aluminum foil and bake until the eggs are set, about 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
Loosen the egg mixture from the sides of the pan, roll up in a jelly-roll fashion, and serve.

title: Ragi Oatmeal Porridge Recipe | Kanji Recipe | High Calcium Fibre and Protein Porridge Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Honey, or jaggery to taste
instructions: To begin making the Ragi Oatmeal Porridge Recipe, soak the rolled oats in water for about 1 hour. Soaking the rolled oats helps in faster cooker.
Into a saucepan over medium heat add the ragi flour and oatmeal. Stir in the water and dissolve the ragi powder until there are no lumps.
Once the ragi oats porridge/kanji begins to thicken (about 4 to 5 minutes) stir in the milk and keep stirring until the ragi oatmeal porridge thickens and gets cooked.

Keep stirring the porridge so that lumps don't form while cooking. Once the ragi oatmeal porridge thickens add honey/jaggery and turn off the heat. You can optionally add sliced bananas into the porridge and serve warm.
Transfer contents to a serving bowl and let it sit covered for 5 minutes.

Serve Ragi Oatmeal Porridge Recipe as for a wholesome high protein breakfast before the kids head out to school or even after a heavy workout, it gives instant energy with the added benefit of protein, calcium and fibre.

title: Drumstick Leaves Fried Rice Recipe
instructions: Heat enough oil in a wok, add the chopped carrots, sprinkle some salt and sauté till they turn soft.
Add the drumstick leaves and cook for a few minutes. Then add the chopped capsicum, soy sauce, ketchup, and green chilli sauce until the vegetables are cooked.
Immediately add the cooked rice and salt, then toss everything gently until well combined.
Serve the drumstick leaves fried rice on its own or with Chilli Baby Corn (Manchurian) to complete the meal.

title: Moong Dal Khasta Kachori Recipe
ingredients: Chilled water, to bind the dough
instructions: To begin making the Moong Dal Khasta Kachori Recipe, first we will make the dough of Khasta Kachori.

Mix the flour, salt and oil in a mixing bowl. Rub oil and flour between fingers to get bread crumb like texture. Add chilled water slowly, mixing with your fingers as you pour to make the kachori dough.
Add just enough water to get all the dough together and knead to make a soft and smooth dough. Cover the dough and let it rest for at least fifteen minutes.
Next, we will make the filling for the Kachori. To make the filling, add the moong dal namkeen in the blender and grind it a coarse powder.

Now, heat a heavy bottomed pan and add oil. Once the oil is warm add all the masalas required like the cumin powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, fennel powder, chaat masala and amchur powder, crushed namkeen, salt and saute till well combined. Turn off the heat and keep aside.
Finally, we will make the kachoris. Once the dough has rested for 15 minutes, knead the dough again to make it smooth. Divide the dough into large lemon‑size equal parts.
Take one part of the dough and with your fingers flatten the edges and make into a 3‑inch circle, leaving the center a little thicker than the edges.

Mold the dough into a cup and place 1 teaspoon of filling in the center. Pull the edges of the dough to wrap the dal filling. Repeat with the rest. Let the filled ball rest for 3 to 4 minutes before rolling.
Set the kachoris on a surface with the seams facing up. Using the base of your palm, slowly flatten them into about a 3‑inch circle.
Now, we will fry the kachoris. Preheat oil for deep frying the kachoris.

Once the oil is hot gently slide the Moong dal Kachoris into the pan. Fry these stuffed moong dal kachori on medium‑low heat. After they start to puff, slowly turn them over to the other side. Fry until golden‑brown on both sides.
Take them out on an oil‑absorbent paper to absorb the excess oil. Once done, transfer the Moong dal Kachoris onto a serving plate and serve.
Serve the kachoris with yogurt, green chutney, tamarind chutney and finely chopped onions as a snack or starter.

title: Doddapatre Tambuli Recipe (Karpooravalli Thayir Pachadi)
ingredients: 4 cups Indian borage (Doddapatre), cleaned and washed
instructions: Thoroughly wash the doddapatre leaves and wipe them dry between kitchen towels.

Heat a tablespoon of ghee in a kadai, add the doddapatre leaves and sauté on medium heat until they change colour, sweat, and the released water evaporates, reducing the leaves to about half the original quantity.
Remove the leaves from the kadai and transfer them to a mixer; set the jar aside.
In the same kadai, dry‑roast the cumin seeds and black peppercorns until the cumin darkens and becomes aromatic; add these roasted spices to the mixer jar.
Add the desiccated coconut and salt to the mixer, then grind with half of the yogurt until a smooth paste forms.
Transfer the paste to a serving bowl, add the remaining yogurt, and whisk until smoothly combined.
In a small ladle, melt a little ghee, add cumin seeds, allow them to crackle, and pour this tempering over the tambuli.
Mix well and serve the Doddapatre Tambuli with steamed rice.

title: Gulab Jamun Recipe With Khoya
ingredients: Milk or water to knead (if needed)
instructions: Take mawa and mix with maida, cooking soda and ghee in a bowl.
Knead everything and add milk or water a teaspoon at a time to combine into a firm dough.
Knead to a smooth gulab jamun dough and keep it covered for about 10 minutes.

Prepare sugar syrup by combining sugar and water in a pan, heat on low‑medium until it reaches half‑string consistency, then turn off the heat and add cardamom powder and a few drops of rose essence; keep covered.
Roll the rested dough into very small balls without any cracks.
Heat oil or ghee for deep frying in a pan or kadai on medium heat.
Once the oil/ghee is heated, drop 4‑5 balls at a time and fry until golden brown on all sides, cooking on low to medium heat to ensure they are cooked through.
Remove the fried gulab jamuns and drop them into the sugar syrup, allowing them to soak and swell.
Repeat with the remaining balls, fry and soak in syrup for 30 minutes or more if needed, then serve.
Serve the gulab jamuns warm, optionally with vanilla ice cream.

title: Corn And Drumstick Leaves Salad Recipe
ingredients: 100 grams Del Monte Whole Corn Kernels
instructions: To begin making Corn and Drumsticks Leaves Salad Recipe, first wash the corn kernels and clean the drumstick leaves.
In a heavy bottomed pan, add some oil and heat it on medium flame. Once the oil is hot, add cumin seeds and mustard seeds and turn to a low flame.
Once the mustard seeds splutter add the corn kernels and saute for 2 minutes.
Now add in the turmeric powder, chilli powder, salt and give it a stir until the masalas are combined with the corn.

Next add in the drumstick leaves and saute until everything is well combined. Adjust the salt, jaggery powder and cook on a low flame. Once the drumstick leaves have shrunk and corn kernels are soft, turn off the flame.
Serve Corn and Drumstick Leaves Salad along with a Rasam, Cabbage Poriyal and Rice for a healthy weekday lunch.

title: Beer Batter Prawns Recipe
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Red Chilli powder or paprika
instructions: Clean the prawns: wash, discard the heads, devein, remove the shell leaving the tail tip intact, and make a slit on the back of each prawn to flatten it like a butterfly.
Marinate the prawns with black pepper powder, red chilli powder, and salt; set aside for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare the beer batter: in a mixing bowl combine all-purpose flour, corn flour, black pepper powder, red chilli powder, pizza seasoning, garlic powder, cooking soda, and salt. Gradually add the chilled beer while whisking to form a thick batter.
Heat a kadai (wok) with the oil for deep frying. Hold each prawn by the tail, dip it into the batter, letting excess batter drip off, and carefully place it into the hot oil.
Deep fry the prawns in batches until they turn golden brown, about 3–4 minutes, turning them to ensure even cooking. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Serve the beer batter prawns hot, optionally with mayo or your favorite dipping sauce.

title: Raw Mango Raita Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Raw Mango Raita Recipe, prepare the mango by washing and peeling it. Grate the raw mango finely and set it aside.

Whisk the yogurt until it is smooth. Next add the grated raw mango, salt, chilli powder and roasted cumin powder to the curd and mix well to combine. Check the salt and seasoning and adjust to suit your taste.
Set the raita aside while you prepare the seasoning.

Heat the oil in a small tadka pan. When it is warm, add the asafoetida and saute for a few seconds. Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle. Gently add in the curry leaves and allow them to crackle. Once done turn off the heat.
Pour the mixture over the Raw Mango Raita, stir and serve.
Serve Raw Mango Raita Recipe with Spicy Paneer Pulao With Vegetables for a tasty lunch.

title: Healthy Bharwa Karela Recipe - Stuffed Bitter Gourd
ingredients: Oil, coconut oil or mustard oil as required (maximum 3 tablespoons)
1/2 inch Fresh turmeric root, or 1 teaspoon turmeric powder
instructions: To begin making Healthy Bharwa Karela Recipe (Indian Masala Stuffed Bitter Gourd), scrape the outer skin of the bitter gourds and make a deep vertical cut in the center leaving the base portion intact. Gently scoop out the seeds and the pith and set it aside.
Rub the bitter gourds with salt, inside out.
Mix about 1/2 teaspoon of salt to the pith and seeds and allow it to rest for at least half an hour. Squeeze excess water and wash and drain them. Pat the bitter gourds with a kitchen towel.
In the meantime, grind all the ingredients given under 'Ground Masala' in a mixer grinder including onion, tomato, raw mango, green chilli, garlic, ginger and fresh turmeric root.
Heat a pan and gently roast the ingredients given under the 'dry masala' except coconut including raw peanuts, coriander seeds, dry red chillies and tamarind.
Once it is done, grind them coarsely with coconut. Keep it aside.
Heat a pan/ kadai over a low flame with a little oil. When the oil heats up add the ground tomato onion masala and the pith of karela.
Mix dry (roasted) masala, kashmiri red chili powder, amchur powder and garam masala. Add salt as required. Adjust spices.
Allow it to cook for 8-10 minutes or till the time the excess water is absorbed and looks cooked, switch off.
Spoon the masala into each processed bitter gourd/Karela.
Heat a wide pan with 1-2 tablespoons of oil.
Gently place the stuffed bitter gourds in the pan and shallow fry them till all the sides are uniformly browned. You can keep the lid closed often to have them cooked evenly.
Delicious Healthy Bharwa Karela (Indian Masala Stuffed Bitter Gourd) is now all set to be served. Serve Bharwa Karela along with Palak Dal, Phulka and Boondi Raita for an everyday meal.

title: Bermuda Grass Ginger & Pepper Juice
instructions: To begin making the Bermuda Grass Ginger and Pepper Juice or the Arugampul juice, collect fresh grass and soak the cut grass in water for a few minutes to remove the dirt, wash it well again and then cut it into small pieces.
Add boiled water to it and grind in a blender along with ginger to make a fresh green juice and strain.
Add salt, pepper and lemon juice and pour the Bermuda Grass juice into a serving glass.
Drink the Bermuda Grass Ginger and Pepper Juice or the Arugampul juice early morning on an empty stomach to get the best results.

title: Kacche Aam Aur Lehsun Ki Dal Recipe -Curried Lentils With Mango & Garlic
instructions: To begin making the Kacche Aam Aur Lehsun Ki Dal Recipe, first clean and wash the toor dal.
Add the washed toor dal into pressure cooker along with raw mangoes, tomatoes, green chillies, turmeric powder, salt to taste and 2 1/2 cups of water.
Cover the pressure cooker and pressure cook for 4 whistles and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally and open the pressure cooker.

Now stir in chopped coriander leaves to the Kacche Aam Ki Dal, check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste. You can adjust the consistency of the dal by adding more water if required.
Transfer the dal to a serving bowl.
The next step is to make the tadka for the dal. Heat the ghee in a small tadka pan on medium heat.
Once the ghee is hot add cumin seeds, dry red chilies and garlic and saute for few seconds till the garlic starts to brown.
Once done add asafoetida and red chili powder into the hot ghee mixture and stir and immediately turn off the heat.
Spoon this tadka over the Kacche Aam Ki Dal and serve.
Serve the Kacche Aam Aur Lehsun Ki Dal with Phulkas or Steamed Rice along with papad and Beetroot Raita for wholesome weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Karathe Nonche Recipe - Bitter Gourd Pickle
instructions: Wash bitter gourds and cut them lengthwise, remove the seeds, then cube the deseeded bitter gourd and set aside.
In a saucepan, roast coriander seeds, mustard seeds, and methi seeds on medium‑low heat until the mustard seeds start to splutter and the mixture turns light brown, about 2–3 minutes.
Just before removing from heat, stir in asafoetida powder, mix well, and set aside to cool.
Allow the residual heat to roast the asafoetida powder.
Once cooled, blend the roasted spice mixture with a small lemon‑sized piece of tamarind into a powder.
In a large deep saucepan, add plenty of water to the chopped bitter gourds, covering them by about 1 inch.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium‑low, cover, and cook until the gourds are soft and almost done.
Add the spice powder, jaggery, and salt to the cooked gourds, mix well, and bring to a boil again; then lower the heat and simmer on medium‑low until the pickle thickens, about 15–20 minutes.
Taste and adjust jaggery and salt to achieve a balanced sweet‑salty flavor with a slight tang from the tamarind.
Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to a month and enjoy.

title: Radish Soup Recipe
ingredients: Mooli/ Mullangi (Radish) , slices, as required for garnish
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves , as required for garnish (chopped)
instructions: To begin making the Radish Soup recipe, wash, peel and slice the radish.
In a saucepan, add radish slices, garam masala powder, and water.
Cook the radish until tender. Remove from the stove and allow it to cool.
Once cooled down, blend and pass it through the strainer.
Mix the strained liquid with the required amount of water and pepper.
Boil the soup for few minutes, about 5 minutes.
Serve the soup hot, garnished with radish slices and coriander leaves.
Prepare Radish soup effortlessly and enjoy as a mid snack or just sip it before your lunch or dinner during winters.

title: Pudina Pyaz Kachumber Salad Recipe - Mint & Onion Salad
ingredients: 2 onions, peeled and cut into rings
instructions: Peel the onions and cut the whole onions into roundels to get onion rings.
In a mixing bowl, combine the coriander leaves, mint leaves, black salt, cumin powder, lemon juice, and the onion rings.
Toss the Pudina Pyaz Kachumber Salad and serve.
Serve the salad alongside Thalapakattu Chicken Biryani and Mirchi Ka Salan, or alternatively with Smoked Dal Makhani Dhaba Style and Homemade Butter Naan for a Sunday afternoon meal.

title: Baked Bitter Gourd Bhajji Recipe - Karela Fritters
ingredients: 3 Karela (Bitter Gourd/ Pavakkai), roughly scraped, sliced and seeds removed
Water, as required to make a thick batter
instructions: Slice the bitter gourd and remove the seeds if they are large; if the seeds are tender and edible, leave them.
Add some salt to the bitter gourd slices, let them rest for 15-20 minutes, then discard the water and rinse the slices.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the gram flour, rice flour, curry leaves, red chilli powder, asafoetida, turmeric powder, oil, and salt; add water as needed to form a thick batter.
Dip the bitter gourd slices in the batter, coat them well, place on the prepared baking sheet, and bake for about 18-20 minutes until golden brown.
Serve the baked bitter gourd bhajji with a dip such as roasted tomato sauce and enjoy with Irani chai.

title: Doodh Jhinge Curry Recipe-Ridge Gourd Cooked In Milk
ingredients: 500 grams Ridge Gourd (Turai/ Peerkangai), peeled & finely chopped
instructions: To begin making Doodh Jhinge Curry Recipe (Ridge Gourd Cooked In Milk), peel the ridge gourds, cut into half, and then chop well.
In a kadai, heat oil, once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Immediately add the whole dry red chillies and saute for a few more seconds.
Add in the chopped ridge gourd. Mix well to combine.
Now add sugar and mix - this helps in retaining the color of the vegetable.

Add salt and ginger paste. Saute for a minute and cover and cook on a medium heat till the vegetable is cooked and the moisture is all dried up. You can stir the vegetables a couple of times to help it cook evenly.
Meanwhile, add a pinch of besan to the bowl of milk and stir well. This helps in keeping the milk from curdling.
Once the ridge gourd is cooked, add green chillies to the kadai and slowly add milk. Stir well to combine and bring the Doodh Jhinge Curry to a brisk boil.

Reduce the flame and continue to cook for about 5-7 minutes to allow the curry to thicken to the desired consistency. Check that the sugar and salt and adjust to suit your taste, add a dollop of ghee and turn off the heat.
Transfer Doodh Jhinge Curry to a bowl and serve.
Serve Doodh Jhinge Curry Recipe (Ridge Gourd Cooked In Milk) with Gehun Bhajra Thepla Recipe or Phulkas along with Dry Chole Recipe (Dry Masala Chickpeas) for dinner or pack away for lunch box.

title: Lauki Raita Recipe - Grated Bottle Gourd Yogurt Salad
ingredients: 1 cup Bottle gourd (lauki), peeled and grated
1 small bunch Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Gather all the ingredients.

In a large mixing bowl, add the grated lauki, cucumber, yogurt, green chillies, salt, cumin and coriander. Stir all the ingredients well. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Transfer the Lauki Raita into a serving bowl and serve chilled.
Serve Lauki Raita along with a meal of Aloo Gobi Sabzi, Punjabi Dal Tadka and Tawa Paratha.

title: Bitter Gourd Chips Recipe
instructions: Wash bitter gourd and pat dry. Discard ends and cut into thin slices (the slices should neither be too thin nor thick). No need to de‑seed them.
Add all the flours and spice powders one by one to the bitter gourd slices.

Mix everything well. If required sprinkle just a few drops of water so that all slices are coated well with the masala mixture, or you can also add 1‑2 teaspoons of hot oil (don’t add more water as it will make them soggy).
Heat oil in a deep pan/kadai for deep frying. Once it’s hot, add the masala‑coated bitter gourd slices to the oil, slice by slice, in batches.
Fry on medium‑low flame on both sides until the bitter gourds are crispy. Remove them from oil and drain excess oil on a paper towel.
Repeat the process with the remaining bitter gourd pieces. Crispy bitter gourd fries are ready to munch.
Serve Bitter Gourd Chips as a tea‑time snack along with Hot Masala Tea and Baked Namak Masala Para.

title: Palak Kichdi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Spinach Leaves (Palak) , tightly packed and cleaned
instructions: To begin making the Palak Kichdi recipe, In a pressure cooker add rice, dal, broccoli, peas, turmeric, one pinch of hing, little oil and 2 -1/2 cups of water and pressure cook.

In a saucepan, bring water to a boil and add the cleaned spinach leaves and let it sit for a minute in the pot while the flame is still on. Now drain it in a colander and transfer it into a bowl of cold water.
Once its cool grind it to a paste in a mixer grinder and set aside.
In a wide pan, heat some oil and add bay leaf, jeera, chopped garlic, pinch of hing, green chillies, chopped onions and saute it until the onions have started to change colour to this mixture.
Once it is done, add the pureed spinach and mix everything properly.
Lower the flame, add the cool dal and rice mixture into the pot and mix until combined with the palak mixture, add the chopped tofu, some water if necessary and season with salt.
Also add the garam masala if using at this stage. Cook for 2-3 minutes and turn of the flame.
In a tadka pan, add some ghee/oil add sliced garlic and cook till its starts to brown, pour this onto the khichdi.
Garnish with sliced tomatoes and it is ready to be served.

title: Whole Wheat Beetroot Paratha Recipe
ingredients: Ghee, or oil to cook paratha
instructions: Peel the skin of the beetroots and chop them into small pieces.
Cook the beetroot with 2 tbsp of water until soft and tender.
In a blender, add the cooked beetroot pieces and grind into a thick, smooth puree, using very little water for grinding.

In a wide mixing bowl, combine the beetroot puree, whole wheat flour, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, roasted cumin powder, and salt. Mix well and knead to form a smooth, soft, non‑sticky dough; add a little more flour if the dough is very sticky.
Cover the dough and let it rest for about 15 minutes, then knead again and divide into equal portions.
Heat an iron skillet over medium flame. Roll each dough portion into a ball and flatten into a thin paratha, rolling all portions in the same manner.
Place one rolled paratha on the preheated skillet. After a few seconds, flip it, smear ghee on the side, and press while rotating to cook evenly on all sides.
Flip the paratha and cook the other side until brown spots appear and it becomes slightly crisp; remove from heat and place on a platter or serve hot.
Serve the Whole Wheat Beetroot Paratha with avocado raita or lauki raita.

title: Ambur Style Brinjal Curry Recipe
ingredients: 20 grams Tamarind, size of a small gooseberry
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan until hot.
Add mustard seeds, whole black peppercorns, curry leaves, and sliced onions; fry until onions become translucent.
Add tomatoes and cook until oil separates, then add ginger garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears. Add the brinjals and mix well.

Add red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and salt; mix well. Soak tamarind in water for about 20 minutes, squeeze out the water, and add the tamarind water to the pan. Cook until the brinjals become soft.

Dry roast peanuts, sesame seeds, and fresh coconut in a pan, let cool, then grind into a coarse powder. Add this ground masala to the brinjal gravy, mix well, and simmer for two minutes before turning off the heat.
Serve hot.

title: Sukha Bhel Recipe With Boiled Peanuts - Peanut Bhel Chaat
ingredients: Black Salt (Kala Namak), to taste or white salt
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Cook the peanuts in a pressure cooker with salt and 1 cup of water for a couple of whistles; let pressure release naturally, then strain, cool, and set aside.
Add the potatoes to a pressure cooker with 1 cup of water and cook for 3-4 whistles; allow pressure to release naturally, peel, dice, and set aside.
Cool the potatoes and peanuts completely before assembling the bhel.
In a mixing bowl, combine puffed rice, onion, tomato, green chilli, potatoes, mustard oil, red chilli powder, chaat masala powder, lemon juice, and black salt; mix well.
Divide the dry bhel into serving bowls, top with boiled peanuts and coriander leaves, and serve.
Serve the Sukha Bhel with Spiced Chutney Sandwich and a cup of Masala Chai, or pack for a snack.

title: Karela Dahi Puri Recipe - A Chatpata Chaat Made From Bitter Gourd
ingredients: 4 Karela (Bitter Gourd/ Pavakkai), sliced into rounds
1 teaspoon Black Salt (Kala Namak) (adjust to taste)
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Heat about 2 cups of water in a saucepan, add all the sliced bitter gourd and boil for about 2 minutes or until semi cooked.
Strain the karela slices out of water and keep aside.
In a mixing bowl, add the gram flour, red chili powder, black salt, coriander powder and asafoetida.
Toss the bitter gourd slices into this mixture, sprinkle some water if needed and mix till well coated.
Heat oil in a pan for shallow frying and fry the spiced bitter gourd in batches until done and crisp.
Whisk the yogurt along with chaat masala powder and keep aside.
Arrange the pan‑fried karela slices on a plate.
Drizzle the spiced yogurt and tamarind chutney on each slice, spread bhujia, sev, dates, and garnish with chopped coriander.
Serve Karela Dahi Puri with a hot cup of Masala Tea or Filter Coffee for evening snacks.

title: Ragi Wheat Phulka Recipe- Diabetic Friendly Ragi Roti
instructions: In a large bowl combine the ragi flour, wheat flour and salt; add water gradually to form a firm dough, then add a teaspoon of oil and knead until smooth, and divide the dough into equal portions.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat a tawa on medium‑high heat; take one dough ball and flatten it between your palms.
Toss the flattened ball in flour and roll it out into a thin circle about 6‑7 inches in diameter.
Place the rolled dough on the hot tawa; after a few seconds small air pockets will form, then flip it to the other side.
Flip it again and cook the first side while pressing lightly with a napkin; the phulka should begin to puff up.
Transfer the phulka to direct flame, allow it to puff, then flip with tongs and cook the other side for a few more seconds.
Remove the cooked phulka from the heat, place it on a plate and generously smear ghee on top before serving.
Repeat the rolling and cooking process with the remaining dough portions.

title: Corn And Onion Raita Recipe
instructions: Whisk the curd and salt to taste with the required amount of water in a mixing bowl and set aside.
Heat oil in a small pan, add cumin seeds, green chillies and onions, and sauté until the onions become soft and translucent.

Add the boiled corn, red chilli powder, and the required salt; sauté for a minute, then turn off the heat. Let the corn cool slightly, then add this mixture to the curd, mix well, and garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve the Corn And Onion Raita alongside Vegan Kofta Curry and Phulkas for a perfect weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Karela Bajji Recipe - Pavakkai Bajji Recipe | Bittergourd
instructions: Wash the karela thoroughly, lightly peel off the skin and cut them into roundels of medium thickness.
In a mixing bowl, combine gram flour, turmeric powder, ajwain, garlic, red chilli powder, asafoetida, and salt.
Mix in just enough water to form a thick batter that can coat the back of a spoon; set the batter aside.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan/kadai over medium heat for deep frying.
Coat each sliced karela roundel in the batter and carefully drop them into the hot oil; deep fry until golden brown.
Drain the fried karela bajji on absorbent paper to remove excess oil and serve hot.
Serve the karela bajji as an evening snack with green chutney and a cup of masala chai.

title: Karela Thepla Recipe - Bitter Gourd Indian Flat Bread
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, add whole wheat flour, gram flour, grated karela, ajwain, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, green chilli paste, ginger paste, and ghee or oil; mix well with a spoon or fork.
Slowly add lukewarm water and knead the mixture into a soft dough.
Heat a flat‑bottomed tawa. Pinch a lemon‑sized ball of dough, dust with flour, and roll out into a thin roti.
Place the rolled thepla on the hot tawa and dry roast from both sides until partially cooked.
Brush melted butter on both sides of the thepla and continue roasting until golden brown.
Transfer the theplas to a serving plate and serve hot, optionally with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita and Aam Ka Achaar.

title: Beetroot Gajar Mooli Salad Recipe - Radish & Beetroot Salad
instructions: To make the Indian Radish and Beetroot Salad Recipe, grate the radishes, carrots and beetroots and keep it ready.
Transfer these grated vegetables-radishes, carrots and beetroots into a mixing bowl, along with the peanuts, green chilies, lemon juice and salt.
Toss well and serve.
Serve this Beetroot Gajar Mooli Salad Recipe along with Awadhi Style Dal Masoor Musallam Recipe and Phulka Recipe (Roti/Chapati) - Puffed Indian Bread for a simple weeknight dinner.

title: Broken Wheat Upma Or Dalia Khichdi Recipe for Babies & Toddlers
instructions: To begin making Dalia Khichdi or Broken Wheat Upma for babies and toddlers, first steam the finely chopped carrots.
In a pressure cooker, add the chopped carrots along with a tablespoon of water.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles and release the pressure immediately by running the cooker under water.
Open the lid, take out the steamed carrots and keep aside.
In the same pressure cooker, add dalia/broken wheat along with 1/2 cup water.
Pressure cook on high for 3-4 whistles, then lower the heat and leave it on low for 2 minutes. Turn off the flame and allow the pressure to release naturally.
In a pan, add a teaspoon of ghee. Once the ghee is warm, add mustard seeds.
When the mustard seeds sputter, add torn curry leaves to the pan along with 1/4 teaspoon of turmeric powder.
Stir for a minute, then add the steamed carrots and mix well.
Finally, add the cooked dalia/broken wheat along with the required amount of salt and mix thoroughly.
Turn off the heat; the Dalia Khichdi or Broken Wheat Upma for babies and toddlers is ready to be fed.
Serve the Dalia Khichdi to babies and toddlers over 10 months with a cup of curd and chopped bananas on the side for breakfast or lunch.

title: Sabudana Khichdi Recipe With Vegetables (No Onion No Garlic Fasting/Vrat Recipes)
ingredients: 1/4 cup Green beans (French Beans), finely chopped
2 tablespoons Whole Almonds (Badam), boiled, peeled and sliced
instructions: We begin making the Sabudana Pulao recipe by soaking the sabudana in water for about 4 to 6 hours. Then drain the sabudana and keep it aside.
In the meantime keep all the vegetables prepared and ready. Heat a heavy bottomed kadai with a little bit of oil and add the cardamom and clove and fry till the aroma is released.
Add all the vegetables and saute for about 10 minutes till they are quite done. Once the vegetables are done add the spice powders and saute.
Now add the soaked sabudana and give it a stir. Half cover the kadai with the lid and cook for 10 more minutes till the sabudana cooks and separates.
Serve your scrumptious Sabudana Pulao with Cucumber Green Chilli Raita Recipe during the fast for the Navratri festival.

title: Spicy Quinoa Upma Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon ginger, finely grated or chopped
instructions: Dry roast the quinoa in a large pan over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until fragrant; set aside.
In the same heavy‑bottomed pan, heat the olive oil over medium‑low heat, then add ginger, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and green chillies.
When the cumin seeds sizzle, add the onions and sauté until translucent and soft.
Stir in the turmeric powder, tomatoes, and peas; sauté for a couple of minutes.
Add salt to taste and pour in 2 cups of water; bring to a brisk boil.
Add the roasted quinoa, cooking for 4–6 minutes on medium heat, then reduce to low, stir gently to prevent lumps, cover, and cook another 10 minutes until water is absorbed and quinoa is done.
Turn off the heat and garnish with chopped coriander leaves; optionally sprinkle lemon juice and serve warm.
Serve the quinoa upma with coconut chutney and a glass of green apple spinach juice.

title: Vegan Baingan Makhani Recipe (Eggplant In Rich Coconut Gravy)
ingredients: 400 grams Brinjal (Baingan / Eggplant), long purple ones, cut into cubes
2 teaspoons Kasuri Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves), crushed
instructions: Wash and cut the eggplants into cubes and keep them immersed in water until you cook, to avoid oxidation.
Blanch the tomatoes in enough water for 10 minutes, then remove the skin, make a smooth puree using a mixer grinder and keep aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add the drained eggplants and sauté until they are about three‑quarters cooked and turn golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, add the bay leaf and chopped garlic and sauté till golden.
Add the grated ginger, green chillies and tomato puree and sauté for a minute.
Add the coriander powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder and sauté till the oil separates on the sides.
Add the cardamom powder, fennel powder and salt and simmer for a few more minutes.
Add a cup of water if it gets too thick and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the sautéed eggplants and simmer until they are cooked through.
Switch off the flame, add the kasuri methi and coconut cream and mix well.
Garnish with sliced onions, coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve with flaky tawa parathas and kachumber salad.

title: Minced Mutton Spring Rolls Recipe
instructions: Mince the mutton by adding the pieces into a food processor and pulsing until coarsely ground.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add onions, ginger, garlic, and green chilies; sauté until onions are soft and translucent.
Add the minced mutton and sauté for another 2 minutes until the meat changes color.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala powder, and salt; sauté well to combine.
Add a little water if needed, cover and cook until the mutton keema is fully cooked and moisture evaporates, about 8–10 minutes.
Turn off heat, stir in chopped mint leaves, mix well, and set the filling aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine all-purpose flour, corn flour, salt, and water to make a thin batter; whisk until smooth and lump‑free.
Heat and grease a nonstick pan with oil; pour a ladle of batter, tilting the pan to spread a thin crepe.
Cook on medium heat until the edges start to peel, then flip and cook the other side briefly; avoid overcooking to keep the wrapper flexible.
Repeat to make the remaining wrappers and set aside.
Prepare a thick flour paste by mixing all-purpose flour with a little water.
Place a wrapper on a flat surface, spread a little flour paste along its edges, and put a tablespoon of the minced mutton filling at one corner.
Roll tightly over the filling, apply more paste to seal, fold the sides, and roll to form the spring roll.
Repeat the rolling process for all remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat oil for deep frying; fry the spring rolls in batches on medium heat until golden brown and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Serve the minced mutton spring rolls with green chutney and pudina pyaz kachumber salad.

title: Paneer Malai Makhani Biryani Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Paneer Malai Makhani Biryani recipe, the first step is to wash the rice and soak for 10 minutes.
Heat a heavy bottomed pot with enough boiling water and add rice for cooking. Strain the rice just before the grain is fully cooked.
Spread on a platter and cool it.

Cut the paneer in barfi shape. Take a wide glass bowl and mix together red chilli powder, turmeric powder, tomato puree, curd, lime juice and salt. Add the paneer to the mix and coat well. Leave it for 5 minutes
Heat a frying pan with oil and fry the marinated paneer for 5 to 8 minutes. Cook till paneer turn brown from both the sides. Remove the cubes from the pan and keep it aside.
Sprinkle lime juice and salt on rice then carefully run the fork through the rice to mix it up without breaking the grains.
Heat a big wok with ghee on low flame, add onion and fry till golden brownish and remove.
In the same wok, add the rice, 3/4 fried onions and the biryani masala. Cook for about a minute or two.
Now, to layer the biryani, add the rice in a platter, then put the paneer mixture on it and garnish it with the remaining fried onions.
Serve Paneer Malai Makhani Biryani along with Boondi Raita and Kachumber Salad for a weekday dinner.

title: Grated Cucumber Raita Recipe
instructions: Roast the cumin seeds in a preheated pan, sauté until they turn brown, then remove from heat and let cool.
Grind the cooled roasted cumin seeds into a powder using a mortar and pestle.
Whisk the yogurt in a bowl.
Add the grated cucumber, roasted cumin powder, red chilli powder, salt, and chopped coriander leaves to the yogurt and stir well to combine.
Serve the grated cucumber raita with a side dish such as Green Moong Dal Pulao or Punjabi Aloo Paratha.

title: Kiwi Guava Spritzer Recipe
ingredients: 2 Kiwi, peeled and cut into cubes
instructions: Wash and cut the guavas into cubes, peel and cut the kiwi into cubes, and set aside.
Place the guavas into a blender with ginger and blend into a smooth puree; pass through a sieve to discard seeds and residue.
Return the guava puree to the blender, add the kiwi cubes, lemon juice, sugar, and 1/2 cup water, then blend until smooth.
Just before serving, divide the mixture equally into 6 tall glasses, fill the remaining half of each glass with aerated water, and garnish with mint leaves.
Serve the Kiwi Guava Spritzer as a refreshing welcome drink.

title: Spicy Lime Pickle Recipe (Naranga Achaar)
ingredients: Water (to cover the limes by 1 inch)
instructions: In a large saucepan, bring the whole limes with water and salt to a boil; reduce to medium heat and simmer for 20 minutes until the lemons are soft. Drain, let cool, then cut into small pieces (quarter each lime, then cut each quarter into 3-4 pieces).
In a small bowl, combine the red chilli powder and turmeric powder with a little water to form a paste; set aside.
Heat the sesame oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan over low heat, add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add fenugreek seeds and curry leaves and stir for about a minute.

Add the chopped ginger and garlic and sauté for about 10 minutes on medium heat. Stir in the chilli‑turmeric paste and cook for 4 minutes. Add the chopped lemons, mix well, adjust salt to taste, then add jaggery and turn off the heat, stirring until everything is well combined. Allow the mixture to cool.
In a separate pan, bring the vinegar to a boil, then let it cool. Stir the cooled vinegar into the lime‑pickle mixture, transfer to a clean glass jar, seal tightly, and store.

title: Khichdi Roti Recipe
instructions: Cut out a large sheet of baking paper to the size of your tava and smear it with some oil.
In a mixing bowl add the khichdi (use room‑temperature or cold; hot khichdi will get messy), enough rice flour, a pinch of salt to adjust seasoning, and the chopped onions.
Mix everything together until you have a well‑combined mixture that is not very moist; if it is still moist, add an extra tablespoon of rice flour at a time.
Heat the tava on low flame.
Place a golf‑ball‑sized portion of the mixture on the baking sheet, smear some oil on your palm and pat it on the sheet to form a round roti.
Pat the roti as thin or thick as you like, then transfer the sheet onto the hot tava, let it sit for 15–20 seconds, and gently peel off the baking paper.
Drizzle some oil around the roti, cook until golden brown, then flip and cook the other side.
Adjust the amount of rice flour as needed based on the consistency of the khichdi, adding more by eye if required.
Serve the Khichdi Roti with Burani Raita and Aam Ka Achaar.

title: North Arcot Special Godumai Rava Puliyodharai Recipe - Broken Wheat/Dalia Puliogare
instructions: To begin making North Arcot Special Godumai Rava Puliyodharai, heat a pan over low flame and dry roast the dalia till it becomes fragrant and then transfer it to a vessel.
Wash and cook the dalia in a pressure cooker with 2 cups of water and pressure cook for two whistles. Once the dalia is cooked, keep it aside. Make sure that you don’t overcook the dalia.
Heat one teaspoon ghee or oil in a wide pan over low heat. Saute the peanuts and cashew nuts till golden brown and set it aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining oil, add curry leaves, mustard seeds, Puliyodharai powder and a half cup of water. Keep stirring. It will start leaving oil when it gets thick.
Once it starts leaving oil, add the cooked dalia, mix well and cook over low heat for 1-2 minutes. Add salt if required and turn off the heat.
Transfer the Godumai Rava Puliyodharai into a serving plate and serve.
Serve North Arcot Special Godumai Rava Puliyodharai as one dish recipe or you can have it with Tomato Onion Raita too.

title: Pumpkin Coconut Ladoo Recipe
instructions: To begin making Pumpkin Coconut Ladoo, grate the pumpkin and keep all the ingredients ready.
In a non-stick kadai, dry roast the desiccated coconut on medium heat until aromatic, then set aside.
Add the yellow pumpkin to the same pan and cook until mushy, stirring as required; mash the pumpkin with the back of a ladle once soft.
Reserve about 2 tablespoons of the roasted desiccated coconut for coating later, and add the remaining coconut to the pan, mixing well with a wooden spoon.
Add the cane sugar and mix until evenly incorporated.
Add the ghee, nutmeg, and cardamom powder, mixing until the mixture comes together without sticking to the pan; then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Place the reserved desiccated coconut powder in a separate bowl.
When the mixture has cooled enough to handle, shape small lemon‑sized balls, coat them with the desiccated coconut, and store in an airtight container.
Serve the Pumpkin Coconut Ladoo as a snack or after‑workout treat, optionally with a glass of Turmeric Milk.

title: Hara Pyaz Paratha Recipe - Spring Onion Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Spring Onion (bulb & greens), washed, pat dried and chopped fine
instructions: To begin with Spring Onion Paratha/Hara Pyaz Paratha, first chop the spring onions using the turbo chop and keep aside.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the flours, salt, turmeric powder, cumin powder and the chopped spring onions. Add little water at a time and make a smooth and yet firm dough.
Divide the Hara Pyaz Paratha dough into 8 portions. Preheat the iron skillet on medium heat.
Roll the Hara Pyaz Paratha portions into balls and flatten them with the palm of your hand. Toss them on flour and roll them out into circles of approximately 3 inches in diameter.
We need to get a triangle shape; to do so, first fold into a semi-circle, then fold the semi-circle into half again. You get a mini triangle shape.
Toss the triangle on a little flour, roll it out gently into a larger triangle. Continue the same process of rolling with the remaining dough portions.
With skillet on medium‑high heat, place one rolled‑out Hara Pyaz Paratha on the skillet. After a few seconds you will notice air pockets popping out.
At this point flip the Hara Pyaz Paratha and smear about 1/2 teaspoon of ghee. Using a flat spatula do a light pressing and turning motion to cook the paratha.

Flip to the other side and press and turn the Hara Pyaz Paratha in a similar way. You will notice brown spots around the paratha and it will be slightly crisp. Remove the Hara Pyaz Paratha from heat and place on a platter or serve hot.
Continue the similar process with the remaining rolled Hara Pyaz Paratha portions and stack the cooked Hara Pyaz Parathas one above the other.
Serve Spring Onion Parathas/Hara Pyaz Paratha with Burani Raita or Tomato Onion Cucumber raita and Dhaniya Pudina chutney for a delicious meal.

title: Chatpati Chana Dal Chaat Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Chana dal (Bengal Gram Dal), washed and soaked overnight
1 teaspoon Black Salt (Kala Namak), or to taste
instructions: Take the washed and soaked chana dal, drain the excess water and spread it on a kitchen towel to dry completely.
Once dry, place the chana dal in a small bowl and add the red chilli powder and black salt; set aside for a few minutes.
Preheat the oven to 160°C. Spread the chana dal on a baking sheet and roast until crisp and golden brown, stirring occasionally, about 30–40 minutes.

Remove the roasted dal from the oven and let it cool. In a large mixing bowl, combine the dal with green chillies, onion, coriander leaves, tomato, lemon juice and salt to taste; adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve the Chatpati Chana Dal Chaat with masala chai as a tea‑time snack.

title: Badam Pottukadalai Ladoo Recipe - Almond Chana Dal Ladoo
instructions: Dry roast the already roasted channa dal until it releases a roasted aroma and slightly changes color.
Allow the roasted channa dal to cool down and powder it using a mixer grinder.
In a large bowl, combine the roasted chana dal powder, powdered jaggery, crushed cardamom powder, almond meal, and ghee.
Knead the mixture with your hands until it holds together into lemon‑size balls, adding more ghee only if needed.
Roll the mixture into lemon‑size balls and store the ladoos in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Serve the Badam Pottukadalai Ladoo as a tea‑time snack with filter coffee or pack them in a snack box.

title: Healthy Jamun Cooler Recipe (Black Plum Juice)
ingredients: 1 cup Jamun (black plum), washed and deseeded
1 tablespoon honey (add or reduce as per taste)
instructions: Add the deseeded jamun, honey, chilled water, black pepper powder, and salt into a blender and blend till a smooth texture is formed.
Adjust lemon juice, pepper, and salt at this stage; add more if necessary.
Pour into serving glasses, garnish with mint leaves and serve immediately.
Serve the healthy jamun cooler with some phool makhana and palak pakora during tea time.

title: Spicy Mushroom Pulao Recipe | Easy and Flavorful Kumbh Pulao
instructions: 1 To begin making the Spiced Kumbh Pulao Recipe, prep all the ingredients and ke

title: Sabudana Khatti Meethi Namkeen Recipe
instructions: In a Kadai, heat some oil. Drop one pearl of sabudana into the hot oil to test; if it rises instantly to the surface, the oil is ready to fry.
Add sabudana to the oil and fry until it puffs up for a couple of minutes without changing color. Remove onto a plate lined with a paper towel to absorb excess oil.
In the same way, fry the peanuts until golden brown, being careful not to over‑fry them as they can become bitter.
Remove the fried peanuts onto the same plate with the sabudana.
In a shallow pan, add a few drops of oil and shallow‑fry the cashews until golden brown, then add them to the peanut‑sabudana mixture.
Add the raisins to the same pan and toss in oil until they puff up; then transfer them to the plate.
Finally, sauté washed and dried curry leaves and chopped green chilies until crisp.
Transfer everything to a bowl and add powdered sugar, rock salt, and ground black pepper.
Toss all ingredients together and, after cooling, transfer to an airtight container. Enjoy whenever hunger strikes.
Serve the Sabudana Khatti Meethi Namkeen in the evening along with Irani chai.

title: Coconut Ladoo Stuffed With Pistachios Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup desiccated coconut, plus a few more tablespoons for rolling
Ghee, to grease palms when rolling ladoos
instructions: Grind the pistachios into a fine powder, place in a bowl, and set aside.
In a non-stick pan, combine the condensed milk and desiccated coconut; cook over low heat, stirring continuously.
After about 5 minutes, the mixture will thicken to a dough-like consistency; add rose water now if using.
When the mixture reaches a dough-like consistency, stop cooking and mix in the rose water uniformly.
Remove the mixture from heat and let it cool slightly until it is easier to handle.
Grease your palms with ghee or butter, pinch a lemon-sized portion of the dough, and roll it into a rough round ladoo.
Flatten the ladoo slightly and make a depression in the center with your thumb; add a teaspoon of ground pistachios to the center.
Roll the ladoo again, encasing the pistachio filling inside to form a perfect round.
Roll the finished ladoo in desiccated coconut and set aside; repeat with the remaining dough.
Serve immediately or store the ladoos in an airtight container in the fridge for 2-3 days.
Serve the coconut ladoos stuffed with pistachios with Sabudana Khatti Meethi Namkeen or masala chai.

title: Khira Gaintha Recipe - Rice Dumplings In Sweetened Milk
instructions: Soak the rice in water for about 5 to 6 hours, then wash, drain, and dry it. Grind the rice to a fine powder.
Boil water in a deep pan, add a tsp of oil and salt, then gradually add the rice flour while stirring to avoid lumps. Cover and cook on low flame for five minutes.
Transfer the cooked mixture to a plate, let it cool, knead into a soft dough, and shape small balls. Boil these rice balls in water for 4 to 5 minutes (or steam) and set aside.
Boil the milk on low flame until it thickens, then add sugar, cardamom powder, and cashew nut powder, continuing to thicken the milk.
Drop the rice balls one by one into the boiling milk, stir and cook for one more minute, then turn off the heat.
Garnish with chopped pistachios and almonds and serve chilled.

title: Gajar Halwa Barfi Recipe (Carrot Fudge)
instructions: To begin making the Gajar Halwa Barfi recipe, in a medium sized non-stick pan, add grated carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add milk, saffron milk and mix it well. Put the lid on top and cook for about 3 to 4 minutes. Now once milk gets evaporated, add sugar, cream and stir it continually for 5 minutes.
Once it gets dry, add half khoya/mava (100 grams) and again mix it well and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Your Halwa layer is ready, take it out into greased tart plate or any other plate with ghee. And gently press it using your palm once it gets warm.
Place the tart plate into refrigerator for 10-15 minutes, meanwhile start preparation of khoya layer. Into another medium sized non-stick pan, add ghee, once melted, add khoya and mix it well.

Once it gets sticky, add remaining sugar into it and mix it well. Switch off the gas and spread this khoya layer on the carrot halwa layer you prepared earlier and again press it gently using your palm.
Garnish it with dry fruits of your choice and cut it in desired shapes and serve it to your loved ones on this Diwali!
Serve this Gajar Halwa Barfi as a dessert after your festive meal of Dum Aloo, Puri and Boondi raita.

title: Aromatic Vegetable Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Potato (Aloo), cut into small cubes
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch finely chopped
Mint Leaves (Pudina), a few sprigs finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Aromatic Vegetable Pulao recipe, wash and soak rice for at least 30 minutes. Drain the water and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a saucepan and add onions, whole spices and cook until the onion turns golden brown.
Meanwhile add 4 cups of water in a different saucepan and bring it to rolling boil.
Add ginger garlic paste and tomatoes with the onions and whole spices. Let it cook until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Once the tomatoes are soft, add all the remaining spices and veggies and cook for a minute. After a minute, add the hot water to the veggies.
Add the soaked rice into the pan and cover it with a lid. Let it cook till the rice is 3/4 cooked and turn the flame to low heat.
Cook it for few more minutes till the rice is almost done and it is ready to be served.
Serve Aromatic Vegetable Pulao along with Burani Raita, Raw Mango Raita or any other raita of your choice.

title: Bhakri Chaat Recipe With Green Moong Sprouts And Aloo
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Ajwain (Carom seeds) or sesame seeds
1/2 teaspoon Whole Black Pepper Corns, coarsely pounded
1/2 cup Tomatoes, deseeded and finely chopped
1/4 cup Boondi, masala boondi to garnish
instructions: To begin making the Bhakri, in a wide bowl combine the wheat and jowar flour, Nutralite Classic Spread (or ghee), ajwain (or sesame seeds), coarsely pounded black pepper, turmeric powder, dry ginger powder, and salt; add water a little at a time and knead into a very firm dough. Cover and set aside for 15 minutes.
Preheat an iron skillet on medium heat. Divide the dough into 5 equal portions and roll each portion into a 4‑inch diameter circle. Place the rolled dough on the heated skillet.
Cook each rolled bhakri on both sides until golden brown, applying light pressure with a wooden press so the insides cook evenly.
Watch for brown spots forming quickly if the heat is too high; adjust heat to medium.
Cook the bhakri evenly on medium heat; optionally brush with classic spread for extra flakiness and crispiness.
For the Green Moong Sprouts and Aloo topping, use store‑bought green moong sprouts or homemade sprouts.

In a mixing bowl combine green moong sprouts, boiled diced potatoes, finely chopped onion, deseeded tomatoes, green chutney, sweet chutney, chaat masala powder, cumin powder, red chilli powder, lemon juice, and finely chopped coriander leaves; toss well.
Place each bhakri on a serving platter, smear with Nutralite Achari Mayo, top with the sprout‑potato mixture, garnish with masala boondi, and serve immediately.

title: Mozzarella Stuffed Potato Balls Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Mozzarella cheese, cut into small cubes
instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes in a mixing bowl, add pepper powder, corn flour and salt, and mix all the ingredients well.
Cut the mozzarella cheese into medium sized cubes and set aside.
Mix all purpose flour and corn flour with some water to make a paste that is not too watery, then set the flour paste aside.
Take a medium sized portion of the potato mixture and shape it into a round ball with your hands.

Press the centre of the ball, place a cheese cube inside, close the cheese completely with the potato mixture, and roll again into a ball; dip the ball in the flour paste and roll it in bread crumbs. Repeat for all balls and refrigerate for 10-15 minutes.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium heat and deep fry the potato balls until golden brown; drain excess oil with a paper towel or alternatively cook them in an air fryer.
Serve the Mozzarella Stuffed Potato Balls on a plate with your favorite dip or simple tomato sauce.

title: Peanut Cucumber Salad Recipe
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the roasted peanuts with the finely chopped tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and green chilli.
Add salt to taste, chaat masala, and lemon juice, then toss the peanut cucumber salad well.
Transfer the peanut cucumber salad to a serving bowl and serve.
Serve the peanut cucumber salad alongside Raw Papaya and Red Bell Peppers Stuffed Paratha, Boondi Raita, and Lemon Pudina Curry Leaf Shikanji for a lovely afternoon meal.

title: Beetroot Paneer Curry Recipe In Coconut Milk
instructions: To begin making the Beetroot and Paneer Curry Recipe in Coconut Milk, we will first cook the vegetables together in a pressure cooker.

Place the beetroot, onions, ginger, garlic and green chillies into a pressure cooker adding half a cup of water, turmeric powder and salt. Cook for about 2 whistles. After two whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure releases from the cooker, open the cooker, stir in the coconut milk, paneer, coriander powder, garam masala powder and bring the beetroot curry to a brisk boil.
Turn off the heat and transfer the beetroot and paneer curry to a serving bowl.
Serve Beetroot And Paneer Curry along with Chilli Cheese Stuffed Kulcha, Peas Pulao (North Indian Matar Pulao) and Coriander Tadka Raita for a complete meal.

title: Classic Indian Sliced Salad Recipe
instructions: Wash and wipe all the veggies clean. Peel the skin of the cucumber and the carrot. Cut the tomato and onion into slices and have them ready.
Attach the thin slicing blade into the masterchef jar, close the lid, add the cucumber into the spout of the lid and turn on the processor to make thin cucumber slices.
Transfer the sliced cucumber into a bowl and set aside.
Add the carrots into the spout of the lid and turn on the processor to make thin carrot slices.
Arrange the carrots at the edge of a serving plate, then layer the sliced cucumbers, followed by the tomato slices and the onion slices.
Sprinkle salt and crushed black pepper, then squeeze lemon juice over the sliced vegetables.
Serve the sliced salad alongside dishes like Smoked Dal Makhani, Palak Paneer, Jeera Rice or Tawa Paratha, or enjoy it as a midday snack.

title: Capsicum Bath Recipe
ingredients: 2-3 Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), chopped into medium size pieces
instructions: Wash rice and cook it with water and salt in a saucepan until the grains are separate and not mushy.
Spread the cooked rice on a wide plate to cool and keep the grains separate.
Heat oil in a kadhai and add mustard seeds, lentils and cashew nuts; once they splutter, add curry leaves, red chili and green chili.
Add onion, green peas, turmeric and salt; sauté until the raw onion smell disappears.
Add chopped capsicum and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add Vangi Bath powder and tamarind juice, mix well, cover and cook for another 3-4 minutes so the capsicum absorbs the flavour.
Stir in grated coconut and mix gently; turn off the heat after any extra moisture evaporates.
Add the cooled rice to the pan and mix everything properly.
Drizzle a few drops of lemon juice, adjust salt if needed, and mix well again before serving.

title: Traditional Rasmalai Recipe
instructions: To begin making Traditional Rasmalai Recipe, get all the ingredients ready. Make sure that the chena or paneer should is not too much moist or be too dry.

Take all the chenna on a plate and add sooji to it and knead for about 5 minutes. Reason to add semolina is to help it act as a binding agent. Knead it well with your palms for 5 to 6 minutes to get smooth texture. This kneading process is very important and it decides the texture of rasmalai.

Divide the paneer/cottage cheese/chhena into equal portions and roll into balls and then press lightly to make patties, taking care that there are no cracks. Prepare all the rasmalai patties in this way. Keep in mind that the rasmalai patties will expand in size while cooking.
Meanwhile, in a large saucepan, add sugar and water, and bring it to boil in medium heat. Mix and continue stirring the sugar syrup until it will be dissolved.

When the sugar syrup will start to boiling, drop Rasmalai Patties gently to the sugar syrup, drop patties according to the size of your pan. The size of the rasmalais will be doubled on cooking in sugar syrup.
Cover the vessel with lid and cook 25 minutes on medium flame. Open the lid and gently stir every 5 minutes to ensure even cooking and puffing.

Turn off the heat, transfer the Rasmalai Patties into a serving bowl without sugar syrup, and allow them to cool. After cooling down you can press the rasmalai patties in your palms. Be gentle and don’t apply too much pressure, as then the rasgullas will break. There should be no sugar syrup in the Rasmalai after cooking and hence we gently squeeze out all sugar syrup out of them.
Take the prepared rabdi now, and add the additional dry fruits or nuts, and pour over the rasmalai. Keep refrigerated for 3-4 hours.
After 3-4 hours, take out from fridge, garnish rasmalai with saffron strands and serve.
Serve as a dessert after a diwali dinner along with desserts like Kesari Gujiya and Kaju Katli or even during evening when you have guests at home.

title: Crispy Paneer Pakora Recipe With Garlic Chutney
instructions: Make the garlic chutney: add garlic, red chillies, cumin seeds, lemon juice and salt to taste into a mixer grinder and blend to a smooth chutney.
In a mixing bowl combine gram flour, rice flour, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, asafoetida, Enos fruit salt and salt.
Mix in just enough water to form a thick batter that coats the back of a spoon; set aside.
Heat oil in a kadai for deep frying.
Cut the paneer into halves, spread garlic chutney on both sides and sandwich them; then cut the sandwich into 2‑inch slices.
Dip each paneer sandwich in the prepared batter and carefully slide into the hot oil; deep fry until crisp and golden brown.
Drain the fried pakoras on paper towels, sprinkle with chaat masala powder and serve hot, optionally with green chutney and kesar chai.

title: Lebu Lonka Murgi Recipe - Chicken With Gondhoraj Lebu & Green Chillies
ingredients: 2 tablespoon Ginger, cut into fine juliennes
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with a little salt, Gondhoraj lebu lemon juice, onion juice, ginger juice, green chili paste and half of the yoghurt. Refrigerate for 1-2 hours.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until smoking hot, then add the black peppercorns and garlic. Saute until lightly browned.
Add the marinated chicken to the pan and set the remaining marinade aside.
Stir the chicken and garlic over high heat until lightly browned.
Add the ginger juliennes, black pepper powder, green chillies, remaining yoghurt and the set-aside marinade; cook for 4-5 minutes. Optionally add a touch of honey to balance flavors.
Add 1/2 cup warm water and the kaffir lime leaves; continue cooking until the chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning to taste, turn off the heat, add lemon slices, cover and let stand for about 10 minutes. Serve hot.
Serve Lebu Lonka Murgi with steamed rice or whole wheat laccha paratha.

title: Chatpata Aloo Moong Sprouts Recipe With Buttered Pav Buns
ingredients: 1/4 cup Tomatoes, deseeded and finely chopped
instructions: Use either store‑bought green moong sprouts or make them at home.

In a mixing bowl, combine the green moong sprouts, boiled diced potato, finely chopped onion, finely chopped tomatoes, green chutney, sweet chutney, chaat masala powder, cumin powder, red chilli powder, lemon juice, and coriander leaves; toss well to combine.
Check the salt and spices of the chatpata moong sprouts mixture and adjust according to taste.
Slice the pav buns horizontally into two halves and spread butter on the cut sides.
Heat a tawa over medium heat and place the buttered side of the pav buns on the tawa.
Toast the pav buns until golden brown on both sides.
Remove the toasted pav buns from the tawa and set aside on a serving platter.
Spoon the chatpata aloo and moong sprouts filling onto the inside of the pav buns, forming a sandwich.
Serve the Chatpata Aloo Moong Sprouts with buttered pav buns alongside Gujarati Khandvi, Pani Puri, and Dahi Vada for a chaat party.

title: Til Ke Ladoo Recipe - Sesame Ladoo Recipe
instructions: To begin with Til Ke Ladoo Recipe, we have to keep all the ingredients ready.
Take a skillet and dry roast the sesame seeds on medium heat for 2 minutes until lightly browned, then remove to a bowl and let cool.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, add water and jaggery and melt the jaggery completely while stirring.
Allow the melted jaggery mixture to cool until it thickens enough to add the roasted sesame seeds.
Test the consistency by dropping a small amount of the thickened syrup into cold water; it should form a solid ball without dissolving.
Add ghee, cardamom powder, and the roasted sesame seeds to the jaggery syrup and turn off the heat.
Transfer the mixture onto a plate greased with ghee and let it cool for about 2 minutes, but not completely, so it can be shaped.
If desired, spread the mixture on the greased plate and cut into squares to make barfi instead of ladoos.
Grease your palms with ghee, take a small portion of the mixture (about half the size of a golf ball), and shape into ladoos.
Repeat the shaping process for the remaining mixture, let the ladoos cool completely, and store them in an airtight container.
Serve Til Ke Ladoo with other snacks such as Baked Masala Namak Para and Aloo Dal Pakoras.

title: Moong Sprouts And Sweet Potato Cutlet Recipe
instructions: Blend the moong sprouts in a mixer to make a coarse paste, using minimal water to avoid a runny texture.
Place the ground moong sprouts in a mixing bowl, add all other ingredients, and mix well.
Let the mixture rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a kadai, add enough oil for shallow or deep frying as preferred.
Shape the mixture into small tikki-like cutlets and fry until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with green chutney and tomato ketchup.

title: Sweet Lime Soda Recipe
ingredients: Ice cubes, a few per glass
instructions: Keep all the ingredients handy.
Take a mixing bowl, add water, lemon juice, cumin powder, black pepper powder, and black salt. Mix.
Add sugar and stir till dissolved; for a quicker version, you can even add powdered sugar.
Once sugar is dissolved, add soda, mint leaves and ice cubes. Serve immediately.
Serve Sweet Lime Soda with Indian Style Jeera Biscuit and North East Khapse (deep fried biscuits) during evening.

title: Chatpatti Makai Masala Recipe - Spicy Steamed Corn Masala
ingredients: 1 cup raw peanuts (moongphali), roasted and coarsely ground
4 sprigs coriander (dhania) leaves, chopped for garnish
instructions: Steam the sweet corn kernels by placing them in a pressure cooker with 1/4 cup water and a pinch of salt; cook for 2 whistles, then turn off heat and let the pressure release naturally.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add cumin seeds, grated ginger, asafoetida, and the coarsely ground roasted peanuts; stir for about a minute.
Add tomato puree, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, and finely chopped green chillies; sauté until the mixture blends well and begins to boil.
Add the steamed corn, adjust salt, lower the heat and sauté until the corn is well coated with the masala; cover and cook for at least 10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the Chatpatti Makai Masala as a side dish with Panchmel Dal and hot Phulkas.

title: Green Tea Coconut Ladoo Recipe - Coconut Energy Balls
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Tetley long leaf green tea, powdered
1/4 cup desiccated coconut, for outer cover
instructions: Gather all the ingredients and keep them by the side.
Heat the ghee in a wide pan, add the coconut and roast for about 5 minutes until you get a roasted aroma, taking care not to brown the coconut while roasting it.

Add the Tetley green tea powder, cardamom powder and the condensed milk. Cook the coconut in the condensed milk on low to medium heat until the mixture begins to thicken and starts to leave the sides of the pan, about 5 to 10 minutes.
If the mixture does not leave the sides of the pan, add some oats flour to thicken; oats act as a binding agent without altering taste.
When the mixture comes away from the sides of the pan, turn off the heat, transfer to a flat plate and allow it to cool.
Once cool enough to handle, roll the mixture into round balls.
Roll the balls over the desiccated coconut to give a snowy finish.
Store the ladoos in the refrigerator for up to a week and serve them with masala chai or filter coffee.
Serve the green tea coconut ladoos for the festive season.

title: Sama Khichdi Recipe - Barnyard Millet Khichdi -Navratri Fasting - Vrat Recipe
instructions: Dry roast the barnyard millet in a pan until it turns slightly brown, then turn off the flame and let it cool.
In a pressure cooker, add 1 teaspoon cooking oil.
When the oil is hot, add green chillies, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and crushed black peppercorns; stir well.
Add the chopped potatoes, carrots, and tomatoes and sauté for a few minutes until slightly soft.
Add 2 cups of water for 1 cup of millet to achieve a creamy consistency.
Allow the water to boil, then add the millet, cover, cook for 5 minutes and let it pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally.
Transfer to a serving dish, garnish with coriander leaves, squeeze in lemon juice, and mix gently.
Serve the creamy Sama Khichdi with Cucumber Green Chilli Raita and Makhana Moongphali Ki Kadhi.

title: Refreshing Sweet Lime Soda Recipe
instructions: In a big bowl, add Lemon juice, Water, Sugar, Jeera powder, and Black pepper powder, then mix everything properly.
Continue mixing until the sugar dissolves completely.
In a glass, add ice cubes, mint leaves, the Lemon juice mixture, and soda water; mix everything properly and serve chilled.
Serve Sweet Lime Soda along with Baked Mathri for your evening snacks.

title: Kaju Badam Ladoo Recipe
instructions: Soak the almonds in hot water for 15 minutes, peel the skin, drain and wipe the almonds dry.
Soak cashews for 15 to 20 minutes, then drain and wipe dry.
Grind soaked almonds and cashews together into a smooth paste and set aside.
Make a sugar syrup by boiling sugar and water until it reaches one‑string consistency.
Add the cashew‑almond paste and cardamom powder to the syrup, mix well, and keep the flame on medium‑low while stirring continuously.
Continue stirring as big bubbles form, ensuring the mixture does not burn.
Stir until the mixture thickens (about 30–40 minutes) and pulls away from the sides of the pan, forming a soft dough.
Test the dough by rolling a small piece into a ball; if it holds its shape, the mixture is ready.
If desired, grease a pan with ghee, spread the dough and level it, or roll the warm dough into bite‑size balls.
Cool the Kaju Badam Ladoo completely and store in an airtight container for up to 5 days, or refrigerate for longer storage.
Serve the Kaju Badam Ladoo after meals such as Jodhpuri Aloo, Ajwain Puri, and Boondi Raita.

title: Baked Beans & Potatoes Chaat Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Gather all the ingredients.
Prepare homemade baked beans (refer to the separate baked beans recipe).

Boil, peel and dice the potatoes; in a bowl combine boiled potatoes with salt, cumin powder, chaat masala powder, a tablespoon of butter and chopped coriander leaves, then mash thoroughly and adjust seasoning.
Butter the bread slices, cut them in half, and spread the mashed potato mixture evenly over each slice.
Preheat the oven to 200°C, place the buttered bread with potatoes on a baking tray, and bake for about 10 minutes until the sides turn brown and crisp.
In a separate bowl, toss the finely chopped onions with some chaat masala and chopped coriander leaves; set aside.
Warm the baked beans and spoon them over the mashed potatoes on each bread slice, then sprinkle the onion mixture and finish with a topping of crisp sev.
Serve the Baked Beans & Potatoes Chaat immediately as a snack or appetizer.

title: Hare Pyaaz Ki Puri Recipe - Spring Onion Puri
ingredients: 1/2 cup Spring Onion Greens, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Hare Pyaaz Ki Puri Recipe, first make the puri dough.
In a mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour with oil, cumin seeds, ajwain, salt, spring onion greens, and coriander leaves.
Mix well and add water little by little to knead and form a stiff puri dough.
Add a few drops of oil once the dough has come together, smoothen it evenly, then cover and let it rest for a while.
Preheat oil in a kadai to deep fry the puris on high flame.
