Divide the dough into equal portions to make lemon-sized dough balls.
Dust each ball with flour and roll into a 3‑inch diameter disc using a rolling pin.
Ensure the puris are evenly flattened to a medium thickness.
Once the oil is well heated, drop the flattened puri into the oil and fry.
Fry with a spider strainer, continuously yet gently pouring oil onto the puri to allow it to puff.
Because of the spring onion greens, cumin seeds and ajwain, the puri will puff only slightly, not as much as a classic plain puri.
Remove the puri from the oil, place on absorbent paper, and serve hot.

title: Chatpata Potato Canapes Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon red chilli powder, mixed with water to make a paste
2 potatoes (Aloo), boiled and grated or mashed
12 crackers, salted or any crackers of your choice
instructions: Heat a little oil in a kadai, add cumin seeds and urad dal, and sauté until the dal turns golden brown.
Add chopped curry leaves, red chilli powder paste, turmeric powder, and asafoetida; cook for a minute.
Add the boiled and grated potatoes, mix well, then add garam masala, salt, sugar, chaat masala, and chopped coriander; cook 1-2 minutes, turn off heat, and let the mixture cool slightly.
Spread a little sweet date‑tamarind chutney on each cracker.
Top each cracker with the prepared chatpata potato mixture.
Garnish with coriander and/or mint leaves and serve as an appetizer or tea‑time snack.

title: Flax Seed Ladoo Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Flax seed powder (flax meal), freshly ground
instructions: To begin making the Flax Seed Ladoo Recipe, we will first dry roast the already roasted chana dal until it releases the roasted aroma and slightly changes its color.
Allow the roasted gram dal to cool down and powder it.
Keep all the remaining ingredients powdered and ready to be combined to make into a ladoo.
Next in a large bowl, combine all of the ladoo ingredients including roasted chana dal powder, jaggery, cardamom powder, flax seeds powder, almond meal and ghee.
Knead using your hands until it holds into a ball of mass. Keep kneading until you can make lemon size balls of the flax seed ladoos.
The heat in your hands will help all the ingredients to bind itself together. So resist adding more ghee and add only if needed.
Roll them into lemon size balls and the flax seed ladoos are ready. Store the ladoos in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Serve the Flax Seed Ladoo as a Dessert for any festive occasion. You can also serve it as a snack in the evening with your hot cup of Masala Chai or Filter Coffee.

title: Potato And Peas Curry Recipe In Coconut Milk Gravy
ingredients: 2 cups Fresh coconut, chopped or grated
1/2 teaspoon Whole Black Peppercorns, coarsely pounded
instructions: Peel, wash and cut the potatoes into cubes and keep them immersed in water to avoid discoloration.
In a zodiac mixer grinder with the super extraction blade, add the coconut and warm water and extract the coconut milk. Set the coconut milk aside.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker; add the onions, ginger, and garlic and sauté until the onions are softened.
Add the cloves, cumin powder, black peppercorns, turmeric powder, and garam masala powder. Sauté for a few seconds.
Add the potatoes and 1/4 cup of water, season with salt, and pressure cook the potatoes for 3 whistles. Once cooked, turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
After the pressure has released, open the cooker, stir in the coconut milk and steamed green peas. Bring the curry to a brisk boil and adjust salt to taste.
Serve the Potato and Peas Curry in coconut milk gravy with phulkas and a carrot cucumber tomato salad.

title: Homemade Idli Dosa Batter Recipe
instructions: Soak the rice in water, ensuring it is completely immersed, for about 6 hours.
Soak the urad dal and fenugreek seeds in water, ensuring they are completely immersed, for about 6 hours.
Grind the soaked urad dal into a very smooth, fluffy batter, adding just enough water; pour this batter into a large container.
Grind the soaked rice into a smooth paste, adding only the necessary water to achieve an almost smooth batter, being careful not to make it too watery.
Note that the rice batter will be slightly coarser while the urad dal batter is super smooth.
Combine the urad dal and rice batters, add salt to taste, and set aside for at least 12 hours or overnight to ferment, allowing the batter to rise in volume.
Ensure the batter is placed in a large container with enough room for it to increase in volume during fermentation.

title: Panjiri Ladoo Recipe
instructions: To begin making Panjiri Ladoo Recipe, prep with all the ingredients. In a mixer grinder, take all the ingredients including dry ginger powder, cumin sesds, ajwain, coriander seeds, whole black peppercorns, fennel seeds except sugar and ghee, and grind into fine powder.
Take the mixture out into a mixing bowl, and add sugar and mix, making ladoos from the mixture.
When doing this recipe specifically for janmashtami prashad, you can arrange these Panjiri Ladoo Recipe along with holy basil leaves for Naivedyam.
Serve these Panjiri Ladoo Recipe along with Radhaballabhi Recipe (Bengali Stuffed Poori With Spiced Urad Dal) and Aloo Dum for a festive meal.

title: Potato and Chickpea Salad Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (white chickpeas), soaked overnight and cooked al dente
Coriander (dhania) leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients.
In a serving dish, add the cooked potatoes and chickpeas.
Toss in the remaining ingredients, stir well until combined, adjust seasoning to taste, and serve chilled.
Serve the Potato and Chickpea Salad with Moroccan Chickpeas And Vegetable Stew or Vegetarian Pumpkin And Chickpea Soup, if desired.

title: Mixed Flour And Spring Onion Cheela Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Spring Onion (Bulb & Greens), finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Mixed Flour And Spring Onion Cheela Recipe, start with mixing all the flours and spices in a large mixing bowl including Bajra Flour, Jowar Flour, Rice Flour, Ginger Garlic Paste, Coriander Powder, Turmeric Powder, Salt and Red Chilli Powder. Mix everything well.
Next, add water slowly to make a pouring batter. Make sure the batter should be flowy and not runny. Adjust salt according to taste.
Now add cumin seeds, spring onions and mix well. Stir well to remove lumps.
Meanwhile, heat some oil in a non-stick flat bottomed tawa. Once the oil is hot, take a ladle full of batter and spread on the tawa evenly in circular moves.
Add few drops of oil from sides and fry from both sides by flipping in regular intervals. Once it is nicely done, remove from the pan and serve.
Serve Mixed Flour And Spring Onion Cheela Recipe along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai for breakfast.

title: Fenugreek Spiced Sardine Fish Curry Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Sardine fish, cleaned and chopped
Gingelly oil, or sunflower oil to cook
1/2 tablespoon Red Chilli powder (adjust to taste)
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients, clean the fish and chop it to the desired size.
Heat a tawa with some gingelly oil; once heated, add jeera, whole black peppercorns, dry red chillies, and coriander seeds on medium heat and roast until aromatic.
Add the coarsely chopped onions and garlic and sauté until the onions become translucent.
Add the fresh grated coconut, stir for a minute until toasted, then switch off the heat and let it cool for grinding.
In the same kadai/pot, heat a bit of gingelly oil, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle. After a few seconds, add the curry leaves and stir until they splutter.
Immediately add the finely chopped onions and fenugreek seeds, sauté and cook until the onions are translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes to the kadai and cook on medium heat until the tomatoes turn mushy; then turn off the heat.
Grind the cooled roasted ingredients into a smooth paste with enough water using a mixer grinder.
Add this paste to the mushy tomatoes in the kadai, cook on medium heat for about 5 minutes until the gravy comes together.
Add the tamarind paste and required water for the gravy.
After a minute, add the sardine fish pieces, salt to taste, and cook covered for about 8‑10 minutes on medium heat until the fish is cooked through.
Serve the fenugreek spiced sardine fish curry with chicken cutlet and steamed rice or ghee rice for a complete meal.

title: Amrood Raita Recipe - Guava Raita
instructions: Chop the ripe guava into small pieces and add it into a bowl filled with curd.
Sprinkle a little salt and mix well.
Heat a tempering pan with oil, add mustard seeds and urad dal and allow it to sizzle.
Add curry leaves and dry red chillies and leave it to crackle. Sprinkle hing and pour it on top of the raita and serve.
Serve the Guava Raita along with Cabbage Paneer Parathas or Gobi Biryani.

title: Vegan Soya Aloo Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Soy Chunks (Nuggets), cooked in water
1/2 teaspoon Kasuri Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves), crushed
instructions: Boil enough water in a pan, add the tomatoes, let them sit, remove the skin and chop them finely.
Heat oil in a kadhai, add the asafoetida powder and cumin seeds, and fry.
Add grated ginger, chopped garlic, and chopped onions; cook until the onions turn translucent. Then add the potatoes, all the spice powders, and salt.
Cook for a few minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes, slit green chillies, and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Finally add the soya chunks, cook for a few minutes, and add water as needed.
Serve the Vegan Soya Aloo Curry with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha or Achari Masala Puri.

title: Chicken Masala Fry Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Boneless chicken , chopped to chunks
instructions: To begin making Chicken Masala Fry Recipe, in a pressure cooker, add the boneless chicken pieces along with salt, red chilli powder, curd and garlic paste.
Add 1 to 2 cups water, mix well and pressure cook till tender, for 10 minutes or 2 whistles.
Switch off the heat, allow the steam to release naturally and once the steam is released, take out the chicken and keep aside.
Heat about half a cup of oil in a deep frying pan, and add the cooked chicken mixture to this, once the oil is hot.
Keep stirring for about 5 to 10 minutes till all the water has evaporated and the chicken has absorbed the flavour of masalas added. Take them out, garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve Chicken Masala Fry Recipe along with Steamed Rice and Lahsuni Palak Dal Recipe (Spinach & Lentil Curry with Garlic) for a weekday lunch.

title: Cheese Stuffed Aloo Bonda Recipe
ingredients: 50 grams Mozzarella cheese, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a frying pan, add mustard seeds and allow it to crackle.
Add the onions and sauté for a couple of minutes till onions are soft and light golden in colour.

Add ginger, green chillies, asafoetida, turmeric and salt. Saute for a minute and add the mashed potatoes. Stir in the coriander leaves and combine. Turn off the heat and allow the potato mixture to cool down.

Once the potato mixture has cooled down divide it into 8 portions. While shaping, flatten the potatoes in the palm of your hand, place a piece of the Mozzarella cheese in the center and cover it to make a ball. Shape the bonda into round balls and keep aside.

Combine gram flour, turmeric powder, and salt to taste in a bowl. Add a little water at a time to make a thick batter that coats the back of a spoon. Whisk the batter well until light and fluffy. Keep aside.
Preheat a kuzhi paniyaram pan. Add a few drops of oil into each cavity.

Dip and coat each of the potato cheese balls in the gram flour batter and gradually place them into the cavities. Cover the pan and allow the bonda to steam. Once the batter is cooked, uncover the pan and cook all sides by flipping and turning.
When the Cheese Stuffed Aloo Bonda turns golden brown on all sides, transfer them onto a plate with oil-absorbent paper and serve hot.
Serve the Cheese Stuffed Aloo Bonda with a spicy Coconut Chutney or Green Chutney and a cup of steaming Filter Coffee.

title: Broccoli And Aloo Lifafa Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Broccoli, florets, steamed and mashed
Ghee or oil to smear on paratha
instructions: To begin with Broccoli And Aloo Lifafa Paratha Recipe, we will first make the dough ready. Take a Mixing Bowl. Mix 1 cup Vivatta Whole Wheat flour with water, oil and salt. Add a little water at a time and keep on mixing it with your fingers till the dough reaches a soft consistency. Once the dough becomes smooth and soft, cover and keep the dough aside for 30 minutes. Meanwhile proceed to make the broccoli and potato stuffing.

To make the broccoli and potato stuffing, in a Mixing Bowl add the boiled and mashed potato, steamed and mashed broccoli, cumin seeds, garam masala, black pepper powder and freshly chopped coriander leaves. Add salt to it. Add lemon juice and mix all the ingredients well. Keep it aside. The broccoli and potato mixture is now ready.
In a small bowl, mix the cornflour and water to make a smooth paste.

Once the dough is well rested, make 6 small balls of equal size from the dough. Sprinkle some dry flour on the rolling board and flatten the ball into a round shape using a rolling pin similar to making a roti.

Heat a Cast Iron Tawa and semi cook the flattened roti from both sides. Once fine bubbles start appearing on the roti, remove it from the tawa and spread good amount of broccoli and potato stuffing right at the center and spread it around leaving a little space from the sides to close the paratha into an envelope shape.
Once the broccoli and potato mixture is evenly spread, apply the corn flour paste at the edges where the stuffing is not present.
Apply corn flour paste on the edges of the roti. Fold the opposite corners of the roti over the stuffing. Now fold the remaining edges sealing the filling well. This will look like a folded envelope.
Place the stuffed broccoli paratha over hot tawa, drizzle oil or ghee and cook on both sides until they turn brown on both sides. Using the same process, make the remaining parathas.
Serve the Broccoli And Aloo Lifafa Paratha for your breakfast, packed lunchbox or weeknight dinner with Raw Mango Raita and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Delicious Aloo Poha Recipe (Batata Poha): A Quick and Easy Breakfast Delight
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
3/4 cup Fresh Pomegranate Fruit Kernels, to serve
instructions: Rinse the poha or flattened rice under cold water, drain excess water using a large strainer.
Transfer the rinsed poha to a large bowl; stir in the turmeric, salt, sugar, lemon juice, asafoetida and set aside.
Cook the peas: place frozen peas in a bowl with 1/2 cup water, pinch of salt; microwave 3-4 minutes on high or pressure cook 2 whistles, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a small pan over medium heat, add raw peanuts and roast on low‑medium heat for about 5 minutes until evenly roasted.
If using pre‑roasted peanuts, toss them briefly in oil for extra flavor during the mustard stage.
In a kadai or stir‑fry pan, heat oil on medium, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them crackle.

Add onions, curry leaves, ginger, and green chillies; sauté until onions are translucent. Then add diced potatoes with 1/4 cup water, a pinch of salt, cover and cook 4‑5 minutes until potatoes are done.
Stir the prepared poha mixture into the onion‑potato mixture, sprinkle about 3 tablespoons water and gently combine.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 4‑5 minutes until poha becomes fluffy.
Turn off heat, mix in lemon juice, cooked peas, roasted peanuts, and chopped coriander leaves; let rest covered for a minute, adjust salt and sugar to taste.

title: Mooli Raita Recipe - Spiced Yogurt Salad with Radish
ingredients: 2 Mooli/ Mullangi (Radish), grated or thinly sliced
1 small bunch Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped (or dill)
instructions: To begin making the Mooli Raita, gather all the ingredients.

Whisk the yogurt in a bowl until smooth. Add the grated mooli, red chili powder, cumin powder, green chilies, coriander leaves, and salt to the yogurt and whisk well. Check the salt and spices and adjust to taste. Serve chilled.
Serve Mooli Raita with Homemade Butter Naan and Paneer Makhani for a weekend meal.

title: Creamy Beetroot and Potato Puree Recipe - Baby Food
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Turmeric powder (Haldi) (8 months and above)
1/4 teaspoon Cumin powder (Jeera) (8 months and above)
instructions: Wash the vegetables well in water, peel the skin, and cut the vegetables into dice.

Place the beetroot and potatoes into a pressure cooker, add 3 to 4 tablespoons of water, and pressure cook until you hear a couple of whistles; then turn the heat to low, simmer for a couple of minutes, and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally in the cooker.
Open the cooker and transfer the beetroot and potatoes to a mixer grinder; blend into a smooth paste.
If the baby is very small (around 6 months) and can handle textures, make a slightly coarse puree.
Adjust the consistency of the puree by adding water, add a pinch of salt, and serve to the baby.
For babies 8 months and older, add turmeric powder and cumin powder for extra taste.
Optionally, serve the puree with a bowl of plain yogurt for babies older than 8 months.

title: Roasted Eggplant And Chickpea Curry Flavored With Curry Leaves And Mustard Seeds
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked overnight and cooked
instructions: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy-bottomed pan; add the cut eggplant wedges with a little salt and roast on medium heat until tender, then transfer the roasted eggplant to a bowl.

In the same pan, add a teaspoon of oil, heat, then add mustard seeds and curry leaves until they crackle; stir in the chopped onions and dry red chillies and sauté until the onions are soft and tender.
Add turmeric powder, salt, coriander powder, garam masala powder, and a little coconut milk; sauté until the ingredients come together.

Add the cooked chickpeas and tomatoes and simmer for about 10 minutes; finally stir in the remaining coconut milk and the roasted eggplant and simmer for another 5 minutes until the curry attains a rich color.
Turn off the heat and serve the Roasted Eggplant and Chickpea Curry with hot steamed rice or Indian breads.

title: Onion Pakora Roll Recipe
ingredients: 4 tablespoons Veeba Carrot Cucumber Sandwich Spread
Coriander (dhania) leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Prep all ingredients and set them aside.

Make the green chutney: combine coriander leaves, mint leaves, curry leaves, roasted peanuts, ginger, green chilies, sugar, lemon juice and salt in a mixer grinder, add a little water and blend to a smooth paste; set aside.

Prepare the onion pakora batter: in a large mixing bowl combine rice flour, gram flour (besan), thinly sliced onions, ajwain, chopped green chilies, chopped coriander leaves, turmeric powder, red chili powder, Enos fruit salt and salt; mix well.
Add water gradually to the batter, stirring until a smooth, thick consistency is achieved; adjust seasoning if needed.
Heat a Kuzhi Paniyaram pan over medium heat and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.
Spoon portions of the onion pakora batter into the cavities and cook on medium heat until browned and crisp on both sides, flipping as necessary.
Transfer the cooked onion pakoras onto a platter.
Warm each tortilla (or roti) on a pan with a little oil, then place on a flat surface.

Spread the carrot‑cucumber sandwich spread over the tortilla, layer with sliced onions, julienned tomatoes, julienned cucumber, and the cooked onion pakoras; sprinkle chaat masala, drizzle green chutney, and roll up to form a wrap.
Serve the onion pakora rolls immediately with hot adrak chai.

title: Lauki Burfi With Paneer Recipe - Bottle Gourd Fudge With Cottage Cheese
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Ghee, or butter for greasing
instructions: Place a pan on medium heat, add ghee, and once warm add grated lauki. Saute for 2-3 minutes until soft and water releases.
Add sugar, mix well, and saute on medium heat until all water from the lauki‑sugar mixture evaporates.
Add the homemade chenna (paneer) to the lauki mixture and mix thoroughly.
Saute on low flame for 3-4 minutes until well combined, then add cardamom powder, mix, turn off heat, and set the pan aside.
Grease a tray with some ghee and set aside.
Transfer the lauki mixture to the greased tray, spread evenly, garnish with slivered almonds, let cool 10‑15 minutes, then cut into squares with a sharp knife.
Serve the Lauki Burfi as a nutritious sweet, optionally packing it for a snack box or serving after meals.

title: Authentic Adrak Chai Recipe - Learn How to Make Indian Style Ginger Tea at Home
ingredients: 2-1/2 teaspoons loose leaf tea (Red Label, Lipton, or Assam)
instructions: Prep all the ingredients.
Pound the ginger using a pestle and mortar.
In a saucepan, add 1-1/2 cups water and the pounded ginger; bring to a brisk boil.
Allow it to boil for a few minutes so the water is flavored with ginger.
Add the tea leaves and bring the mixture to a brisk boil again. Add the milk at this stage and continue until the chai turns a golden brown (less than a minute). Do not over‑boil.
Turn off the heat and let the chai rest and brew for about a minute.
Strain the chai into cups or a teapot, stir in sugar to taste, and serve.
Serve the Adrak Chai with your favorite tea‑time snack.

title: Microwave Ashoka Halwa Recipe | Moong Dal Halwa
ingredients: Food Color, few drops (I used natural food coloring)
instructions: To begin making the Microwave Ashoka Halwa, pressure cook the moong dal first. Take a bowl and add moong dal and water. You may soak this for 1 hour (optional).
Pressure cook moong dal for 3 whistles (or till soft), then release pressure, drain excess water, and mash it well. Set aside.

In a small microwave‑safe glass or ceramic bowl, add about 2 teaspoons ghee and cashew nuts, mix, and microwave for 1 minute 40 seconds until the nuts are fried. Transfer the fried cashews to another bowl and keep the ghee.
While the ghee is still hot, stir in the whole wheat flour. Set aside.
Take a large microwave‑safe glass or ceramic bowl and optionally coat it with a spoon of ghee.
Add the mashed dal and sugar to the bowl and mix well.
Microwave on high for 4 minutes, stirring at the 2‑minute mark, until the sugar dissolves completely.
Add 1 teaspoon ghee and microwave for 2 minutes. Continue adding 1 teaspoon ghee every 2 minutes until the ghee separates and the mixture comes together, about 4 minutes total.
Stir in food coloring, cardamom powder, fried cashew nuts, wheat flour and 3 teaspoons ghee, then add another 3 teaspoons ghee and mix well.
Microwave on high for 1 minute, then remove and let it stand a few minutes before serving.
Serve the Ashoka Halwa as a dessert, optionally with Baked Bhakarwadi and South Indian Filter Coffee, or with a South Indian thali.

title: Bakery Style Baked Nippattu Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Bakery Style Baked Nippattu recipe, take maida, oil and butter in a mixing bowl. Mix nicely with the tips of your fingers till the mixture looks like breadcrumbs. Add more oil if required to get the breadcrumb like texture.

To the flour add milk powder, baking soda, salt, sugar, pepper powder, sesame seeds, onion, green chillies, coriander leaves and curry leaves. Mix the ingredients nicely with your hand. Add warm water slowly, little by little and make a tight firm dough.
Knead the dough well, cover and keep aside for 10 to 15 minutes. Meanwhile preheat the oven at 180 °C for 10 minutes.

Once the resting time for dough is over, divide the dough into lemon sized balls. Take one ball, place it between two thick greased plastic sheets and roll gently to form a 3 to 4 inch diameter thin disc.
Gently place the nippattu on a greased baking tray. Poke the nippattu with a fork randomly to avoid fluffing up.
Continue with the remaining dough in a similar way. Bake the nippattu for about 15 to 20 minutes at 170 °C. Midway flip once after 10 minutes.
Once the nippattu have turned golden brown in colour and cooked through, remove them from the oven and place them on a cooling rack to cool.
Your Bakery Style Baked Nippattu is ready to serve. Store in an airtight container.
Serve along with hot Masala Chai for your tea time break.

title: Aloo Chaat Recipe With Baked Beans - Roz Ka Khana With Figaro Olive Oil
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
Anardana Powder (Pomegranate Seed Powder), for serving
Extra Virgin Olive Oil, for toasting the bread
instructions: To begin making the Aloo Chaat with Baked Beans recipe, we first have all the ingredients ready.
First, have the homemade baked beans ready.

In a bowl, add the boiled potatoes, sprinkle salt, cumin powder, chaat masala powder, a tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil and some chopped coriander leaves. Using a fork, mash the potatoes well and check the seasoning and adjust to suit your taste. Keep the mashed potato mixture aside.
Apply extra virgin olive oil on the bread slices and cut them into half. Spoon the potato mixture over the bread slices and spread it evenly on the top.
Preheat the skillet on medium heat and place bread with potatoes on the baking tray and cook it on both sides like a patty. Once it is getting crisp and golden, you can keep it aside.
In a bowl, toss the onions, some chaat masala and chopped coriander leaves. Keep this aside.
When ready to serve, warm the beans and spoon the baked beans on each of the mashed potatoes. Sprinkle them with the onion mixture and finally top with crisp sev.
Serve the Aloo Chaat with Baked Beans recipe immediately as a teatime snack or as an appetizer for your parties.

title: Amtekai Gojju Recipe - Indian Hog Plum Curry
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients.
Wash and lightly scrape the skin of the amtekai, cut into pieces, and keep the seed.
Place the amtekai with seed in a saucepan with a cup of water and jaggery; bring to a brisk boil, then simmer on low until the fruit is soft.

In a small pan, add a few drops of oil and roast all masala ingredients except coconut and sesame until chilies are crisp and dal turns golden; add grated coconut and sauté briefly, then transfer to a mixer jar.
Dry‑roast the sesame seeds in the same pan until golden, add them to the mixer jar, let cool slightly, add a little water and blend into a smooth paste.
Add the ground gojju masala paste and salt to the cooked amtekai, mix well, and cook on medium heat until it starts boiling.
Reduce heat to low, add a tablespoon of raw coconut oil, and simmer 8‑10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the curry thickens; adjust seasoning and turn off heat.
Transfer the curry to a serving bowl.
For the seasoning, heat oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds until they crackle, then add curry leaves and asafoetida, stir briefly, and pour over the curry.
Serve the Amtekai Gojju with steamed rice (topped with ghee) or with idlis/dosas.

title: Lauki Ki Kheer Recipe
instructions: Add milk in a saucepan and keep it for boil.
Heat ghee in a heavy bottomed pan, add grated lauki and sauté it for 10 minutes or until the lauki turns soft and tender.
Once the lauki becomes soft and tender, add boiled milk. Once the milk comes to a boil, turn the heat to low and simmer it.
While boiling, keep stirring occasionally so that the milk does not burn. Once the milk thickens, add sugar, cardamom powder, almonds, cashews and pistachios as per your choice.
Once the sugar melts, turn off the heat and transfer to the serving bowl. Garnish with dry fruits and serve the Lauki Ki Kheer chilled as a dessert.
Serve Lauki Ki Kheer after your delicious meal of Jodhpuri Aloo, Ajwain Puri, Palak Chana Dal and Kachumber Salad.

title: Mushroom Baby Corn Kaalimirri Recipe - Pepper Cashew Gravy
ingredients: 150 grams Baby corn, cut into wedges
Salt, to taste (for mushrooms & baby corn)
Whole Black Peppercorns, crushed for garnish
instructions: Heat a skillet on medium-low flame and dry roast the cloves, cinnamon stick, cardamom, cumin seeds, whole black peppercorns, cashew nuts and poppy seeds for about 3-4 minutes.
Turn off the heat, let the roasted spices cool, transfer to a mixer jar, add 1/2 cup milk and grind to a smooth paste; set aside.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium flame, add the halved mushrooms, sprinkle salt and sauté for about 10 minutes until cooked through.
Transfer the cooked mushrooms to a bowl and set aside.
In a pressure cooker, add the baby corn with a pinch of salt and about 1/4 cup water; pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the flame and allow the pressure to release naturally; set the cooked baby corn aside.
Make a paste of ginger, garlic and onions; keep aside.
Heat a kadai with ghee on medium heat, add the ginger‑garlic‑onion paste and sauté on low heat for 3‑4 minutes until the raw aroma disappears.
Add the freshly ground spice‑masala paste to the sautéed onions and cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Stir in the sautéed mushrooms, boiled baby corn, fresh cream, remaining milk and salt; mix well.
Simmer the mixture until it comes to a brisk boil, then check seasoning and adjust salt or spices as needed.
Turn off the heat, transfer the Mushroom Baby Corn Kaalimirri to a serving bowl, garnish with crushed black peppercorns and serve hot.

title: Bottle Gourd & Mint Vegetable Juice Recipe - Lauki Juice
ingredients: Salt or kala namak to taste
instructions: Place the bottle gourd, ginger, and mint leaves into a juicer and run the juicer until all the juice comes out.
Add a little more water to the juicer to extract additional nutrition from the pulp.
Pour the juice into a jug, add salt to taste and lemon juice, then serve immediately.

title: Baked Sweet Potato Boats Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Black beans, cooked, rinsed and drained if canned
1/4 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), finely diced
1/4 cup Red Bell Pepper (Capsicum), finely diced
1/2 cup Sweet corn, steamed and cooled
Extra Virgin Olive Oil, as needed
1 tablespoon Apple cider vinegar, or white vinegar
1/4 cup Cashew nuts, soaked for an hour
1 teaspoon Apple cider vinegar, or white vinegar
1 teaspoon Lemon zest, optional but preferred
instructions: Grease the sweet potatoes with olive oil on a baking tray and bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 45-60 minutes.
In a small jar, combine cashews, apple cider (or white) vinegar, lemon juice, lemon zest, water, and salt.
In a small mixing bowl, add apple cider vinegar, red wine, and olive oil; whisk continuously until combined.
Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, dried oregano, sugar, black pepper, and minced garlic to the vinegar and wine mixture; whisk thoroughly.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the black beans and the diced vegetables; drizzle the dressing over the mixture and toss to coat.
Create a cavity in each baked sweet potato using a fork, fill with the bean‑vegetable salad, and top with the cashew sour cream and hot sauce.
Serve the baked sweet potato boats warm for lunch or an early dinner.

title: Carrot Tadka Raita Recipe- Crunchy Grated Carrot In Yogurt
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine yogurt, black salt, cumin powder, and salt to taste; whisk well until smooth.
Add coriander leaves, mint leaves, green chillies, and grated carrots to the whisked curd; mix well and set aside.
To make the tadka, heat oil in a pan over medium heat, add cumin seeds, asafoetida, and chopped garlic; sauté until the garlic turns golden brown, then turn off the heat.
Pour the tadka over the carrot raita and serve chilled.
Serve Carrot Tadka Raita with Stuffed Mooli Paratha or Baby Corn and Tomato Mixed Rice.

title: Zucchini Paratha Recipe
instructions: Squeeze out the water from the grated zucchini and reserve the water to knead the dough later.
To the wheat flour, add ajwain, turmeric, chilli powder, amchur, jeera powder, and salt. Mix well.
Add the grated zucchini.
Knead the dough with the reserved zucchini water, adding additional water only if required, to make a pliable dough.
Let the dough rest for 20 minutes. Heat a tawa.
Pinch out a small ball of the dough and heat a flat‑bottomed pan.
Roll the ball of dough into a circular shape and cook the paratha with some ghee on both sides for about 2 minutes.
Serve the zucchini paratha with instant red chilli pickle.

title: Yellow Pumpkin Pulao Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Yellow Pumpkin Pulao Recipe, wash the basmati rice couple of times and soak in water for 20 minutes. Meanwhile cut the yellow pumpkin, wash them and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker and once the oil is hot add the bay leaves, cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise and cumin seeds.
Once the cumin seeds splutter, add in the green chillies, yellow pumpkin & coconut. Saute them for a minute.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pressure cooker along with turmeric powder, salt & sugar. Saute them in low heat for a minute until combined.
Add in the water and when it comes to a rolling boil, close the pressure cooker and cook the pumpkin pulao on medium heat for 2 whistles. After two whistles turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally and open the pressure cooker. Fluff the pumpkin pulao with a fork slightly, transfer to a serving plate and serve.
Serve Yellow Pumpkin Pulao along with Manipuri Style Sana Thongpa and Boondi Raita for a wholesome lunch.

title: Lauki Bharta Recipe - Spiced & Mashed Bottled Gourd Recipe
instructions: To begin with the Lauki Bharta Recipe, first peel the lauki/bottle gourd and grate the bottle gourd. Keep this aside, as we proceed to make the masala for the bharta.
In a wok heat a tablespoon of oil, add jeera and let it crackle. Now add ginger garlic paste and let it brown.
Add chopped onions and saute' till they start turning brown later add tomato and cook till the tomatoes are soft and the oil starts separating.
To this mixture, add red chilly powder, salt and saute for a few seconds.

Add grated bottle gourd to this, give this a good mix. Cover the pan and allow the lauki to cook in low to medium heat. The lauki will give out its own liquid as it comes in contact with salt. If required, add just a little more water to cook the bottle gourd.

Cook till the lauki is cooked and is well combined with the spices. At this stage, add garam masala powder, cook further till until combined and the lauki bharta consistency should remain thick. Chesck the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste.
Once done, turn off the heat and stir in chopped coriander leave and sugar. Give it a mix and transfer the Lauki Bharta to a serving bowl.
Serve the Lauki Bharta along with Phulkas, Jeera Pulao & a Mint & Pomegranate Raita for a perfect weeknight dinner or even pack into the lunch box for work.

title: Aloo Matar Masala Khichdi Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Coriander (Dhania) Leaves , finely chopped for garnish
instructions: To begin making Aloo Matar Masala Khichdi Recipe, wash the rice and keep it soaked in water till you add it into the recipe.
Wash, de-skin, cut the potatoes into big cubes and keep it immersed in a bowl of water until further cooking.
Heat ghee in a pressure pan, add the whole spices - bay leaf, black and green cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves and let it release its flavours into the ghee.
Add the cumin seeds and let it splutter.
Add the sliced onions, green chilies and saute until the onions turns translucent.
Drain the potatoes from water and add it to the pressure pan along with peas and saute for a minute.
Add the coriander powder, cumin pepper and red chilli powder and mix well.
Add the drained and soaked rice, about 5 cups of water, season with salt and bring it to a rolling boil.
Close it with the pressure pan lid and cook for 4 to 5 whistles, or till done.
Switch off the heat, let the pressure release on its own before opening the lid.
Garnish with coriander leaves use a fork to carefully mix the khichdi.
Serve the Aloo Matar Masala Khichdi Recipe along with Cauliflower & Cucumber Raita Recipe and Papad for a simple yet delightful weeknight dinner.

title: Aam Pudina Ka Panna Recipe
instructions: Wash the mangoes, remove the stems and add them to a pressure cooker with 2 cups of water. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles, then turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally.
Open the pressure cooker, remove the mangoes, and reserve some of the cooking water. Let the mangoes cool down.
Remove the skin and take the pulp of the mangoes. Add the mango pulp to a mixer grinder, add the washed mint leaves, and blend at high speed until well combined.
Transfer the blended mixture to a bowl containing the reserved mango water and stir well to combine.
Add cumin powder, black salt, lemon juice, and optionally jaggery. Stir, then add cold water as needed and mix thoroughly.
Heat a small tadka pan with ghee, add cumin seeds and a pinch of asafoetida, and let the seeds splutter.
Pour the tadka into the aam panna mixture and give it a good mix.
Pour the Aam Pudina Ka Panna into serving glasses with ice and serve.
Serve Aam Pudina Ka Panna in the evenings with snacks such as Gujarati Khatta Dhokla or Mushroom Masala With Corn, or to relieve bloating and digestive complaints.

title: Authentic Moong Dal Halwa Recipe: Step-by-Step Guide to Make Delicious Indian Dessert
instructions: To begin making the Moong Dal Halwa Recipe, soak the moong dal in water for at least 3 hours.
Once soaked, drain the water completely and grind the moong dal into a coarse mixture using the food processor. You need to ensure that it does not become a paste, but has a coarse texture.
Heat ghee in a heavy bottomed pan on medium heat; add the ground moong dal and reduce the heat to low, stirring the mixture continuously, allowing it to turn golden brown from its yellowish texture.

The above process of cooking the lentil in low heat is very crucial to a delicious tasting halwa. It takes a good 45 minutes for it to cook in the low heat and get to a beautiful golden brown state. Take care not to turn the heat to high to speed up the process.
The low heat cooking helps the moong dal to cook well and turn brown evenly releasing the perfect rustic aroma.
Once the moong dal is well cooked and reached a golden brown state, add the sugar, milk, saffron and mix well until combined.

Continue to stir on low heat until the mixture thickens and releases itself from the sides of the pan; this process would take another 20 to 30 minutes. Turn off the heat and transfer the Moong Dal Halwa to a serving bowl and serve hot along with your meal.

Serve the Moong Dal Halwa as a dessert when you make elaborate lunches for your friends and family or during festive and special occasions, or after a one pot meal of One Pot Spicy Vegetable Pulao Recipe with Coconut Milk or One Pot Vangi Bath Recipe.

title: Ginger, Lemon And Honey Kadha Recipe
ingredients: 8 inch ginger, grated (you will need 5 tablespoons of ginger juice from it)
instructions: To begin making Ginger, Lemon & Honey Kadha Recipe, clean the ginger and remove skin, grate the ginger root using a grater and squeeze the juice in a small bowl.
We need to get about 5 tablespoons of this juice, you can grind in an ammikallu and then extract juice as well.
Add honey and lemon juice to the ginger juice in a tumbler and quickly stir well till the honey is dissolved well.
Store this kadha recipe refrigerated in an airtight jar for about 2 weeks and use as needed.
Take 1 tablespoon of this Ginger, Lemon & Honey Kadha Recipe with a glass of warm water 2 times a day for better health and for a cure to cold and cough.
Serve Ginger, Lemon & Honey Kadha Recipe on an empty stomach with a glass of warm water to reap the most benefits.
Note: You can also make fresh juice daily by using 1 inch ginger to grate, 1 tablespoon honey & 1/2 tablespoon lemon juice.

title: Quinoa and Vegetable Saute Recipe
instructions: Cook 2 cups of quinoa with 4 cups water and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a rice cooker or a covered saucepan until fully cooked and the seeds sprout, about 15 minutes.
Fluff it with a fork and set aside.
Add a tablespoon of olive oil, add cumin seeds into a pan and cook on medium flame.
Once the cumin crackles, add the ginger, followed by peas and carrots.
Turn the heat and let them cook for a few minutes.
After a few minutes add the chopped onions and pepper and sauté them for another few minutes.
Add the spice powders and salt, stir, and let sit for a few seconds so the powders infuse in the oil.
Add the quinoa and toss everything together gently. Adjust salt to taste.
Garnish with fresh herbs of your choice and a teaspoon of olive oil, toss and serve hot.
Serve as a side dish during weeknight dinner or as a breakfast dish with fresh juice or masala chai.

title: Hari Matar Ke Pakode Recipe - Green Pea Fritters
instructions: Coarsely blend a few of the pakora ingredients in a chopper or mixer‑grinder.
Place the coriander leaves, peas, green chilies, garlic and cumin seeds in the blender and pulse to get a coarse mixture.
Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl, add salt, onions and gram flour and mix well; add a little water if needed to make a thick batter, then adjust seasoning.
Heat a kadai with enough oil to deep fry the pakoras.
When the oil is hot, spoon the batter into the kadai and fry until golden brown and crisp on all sides, avoiding overcrowding.
Remove the fried pakoras, drain on oil‑absorbent paper.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve the Hari Matar Ke Pakode as a snack with ginger cardamom chai or as an appetizer with pudina dahi chutney.

title: How To Make Ragi Sprouts At Home
instructions: To make ragi sprouts at home, first soak the ragi seeds in sufficient water for an overnight or 6-8 hours.

After soaking time, drain all the ragi seeds and spread them evenly on a wet cloth on a corner of your house that is warm. Remember that the cloth should not be too wet till dripping, nor be too dry. Close in another wet cloth on top of the sprouting ragi and set aside.
Do not disturb this set up for at least 4 hours. Remember that sprouting depends on the constant and warmer temperature. If the weather is cold, you can keep this set up in an oven.
Preheat oven to 120 degree C for 3 minutes. Switch off. And keep the bundled cloth within and close the oven. Do not disturb for 4 hours.
After sprouting time, you can take the cloth and the small sprouts will have emerged.
You can use these ragi sprouts in cutlets, or dry them under shade on a sunny day for an hour or two and dry grind to use in recipes which call for ragi flour.

title: Masala Lemonade Recipe
instructions: Take a bowl and squeeze the lemon juice.
Add sugar, crushed ginger, crushed fresh mint leaves and 1 glass of water.
Mix everything well until the sugar is dissolved.
Filter the juice, then add pepper powder, cumin powder, black salt and mix well.
Add ice cubes and serve it cool in a glass; optionally add soda for fizz.
Serve the Masala Lemonade during tea time with snacks such as Sukha Bhel and Onion Bajji.

title: Healthy Soya Sabudana Kebabs Recipe With Spicy Tomato Chutney
instructions: Soak the soy nuggets in boiled water for 10-15 minutes until soft, drain, and grind to a coarse mixture.

In a large bowl combine boiled potato, minced soy, Sabudana, soaked poha, green chillies, ginger, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, garam masala, chaat masala, and salt; mix well with a masher until smooth.
Shape the mixture into 6-8 round patties and let rest for a while.
In a mixer grinder, blend tomatoes, green chillies, ginger, and salt into a smooth chutney; add water if needed and adjust salt.
Heat oil in a shallow pan and shallow-fry the kebabs until crispy and golden brown on both sides; drain on absorbent paper.
Garnish kebabs with onion rings and serve with the tomato chutney.
Serve as an evening snack with Masala Chai.

title: Tandoori Aloo Gobi Kathi Roll Recipe - Spicy Aloo Gobi Frankie
ingredients: 1 Onion, thinly sliced, for the wrap
1 Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), thinly sliced, for the wrap
instructions: Begin by cooking the aloo and gobi.
Into a pressure cooker, add the potatoes with 1/2 cup water and pressure cook for 3 to 4 whistles; turn off heat and allow natural pressure release.
Peel the potatoes and set aside.
Steam the cauliflower florets for 3 to 4 minutes until just cooked but still firm, or pan‑roast with a little salt until lightly cooked.
In a bowl, combine 1/2 cup curd (yogurt) with chaat masala, red chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt.
Add the baby potatoes and cauliflower florets to the curd mixture, coat evenly, adjust seasoning and marinate for 15 minutes.
Thread the potatoes and cauliflower onto sticks or skewers for roasting.
Heat a skillet over medium, add 1 teaspoon oil, then add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Place the skewered aloo gobi on the skillet and roast until brown spots appear and the vegetables are roasted.
Roast all skewers on low to medium heat, then set aside.
For the paratha, mix whole wheat flour, salt and 1 teaspoon oil; add water gradually to form a smooth dough, cover with a cloth and rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Dust a surface with flour and roll each ball into a thin paratha.
Cook each paratha on a medium‑hot tawa with ghee or oil until done; keep the cooked parathas aside.
In a medium bowl, mix sliced onions, capsicum slices, lemon juice, salt and green chillies.
Place a cooked paratha on foil, add a portion of the onion‑capsicum mixture.
Lay a skewer of roasted tandoori aloo gobi in the centre of the paratha, then remove the skewer.
Roll the paratha (with foil) to form the Kathi roll; repeat for the remaining parathas.
Serve the Tandoori Aloo Gobi Kathi Rolls with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and a cup of Masala Chai or curd.

title: Crispy Baby Corn Lollipop Recipe / Spring Rolls
ingredients: Water, as required for the dough
Milk, as required for coating the crust
2 tablespoons all purpose flour (maida) for maida paste
instructions: Marinate the baby corn.
In a large bowl add the baby corn, lemon juice, cumin powder, chaat masala, red chilli powder, garam masala and salt; mix well to coat all the corn and set aside.
Make the maida paste: in a mixing bowl combine all purpose flour with enough water to form a thick paste.

Prepare the spring roll dough: in another bowl combine herb butter, all purpose flour, whole wheat flour and salt; mix until the mixture holds together as a ball, then knead into a smooth, firm dough.
Dust the dough with flour and roll it out to a medium thickness, like a roti.
Cut the rolled dough into thin strips about 1 cm wide using a pizza cutter.
Take one strip, spread the maida paste over it, place a baby corn at one end and wind the strip around the corn to form a spiral; press the edges to seal.
Arrange all the rolled baby corn lollipops on a baking sheet, brush with milk, and sprinkle with chaat masala and kalonji.
Pre‑heat the oven to 165 °C and bake the rolls for 20‑25 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
Remove from the oven and serve hot, optionally with a dip such as tzatziki.

title: Badam And Khus Khus Milk Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Whole Almonds (Badam), soaked overnight & peeled
Saffron strands, a few, soaked in a teaspoon of milk for 15 minutes
instructions: Soak almonds and khus khus (poppy) seeds separately for 6 hours or overnight.
Peel the almonds and wet grind them with a spoon or two of water to a thick smooth paste.
Grind the drained soaked khus khus (poppy seeds) to a thick paste.
In a saucepan, bring milk to boil together with the almond and khus khus pastes, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Add sugar and stir until dissolved; add cardamom powder once the milk thickens a bit and stir well until the flavor is uniform. Switch off.
Let the mixture cool.
Serve topped with pistachios, glazed cherries, and soaked saffron strands, either at room temperature or chilled.
Optional: Serve with snacks like Poha Chivda, Makki Paneer Pakora, or Sukha Bhel.

title: Kalonji Gobi Aloo Recipe (Cauliflower & Potato Stir Fry with Nigella Seeds)
ingredients: 1 Cauliflower (gobi), cut into medium sized florets
2 tablespoons Mustard oil (or any other cooking oil)
3 Green Chillies, cut into very thin long slices
instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and add the nigella seeds. On medium heat, sauté the seeds until they release a roasted aroma; when they start to sizzle, add the mustard seeds and green chilli.
Once the mustard seeds start to crackle, add the cauliflower florets and diced potatoes along with salt and sugar. Stir to combine and increase the heat to medium-high.
When the cauliflower and potatoes turn slightly brown at the corners, add a little water—just enough to steam the vegetables—cover the pan and cook over low heat.
After about 15 minutes, uncover the pan and check for tenderness; the cauliflower should be tender but firm, not mushy or falling apart.
If any water remains, turn the heat to high and toss the vegetables until dry. Turn off the heat, drizzle the remaining mustard oil over the hot mixture, and stir to combine.
Serve the Kalonji Gobi Aloo with hot phulkas and cholar dal.

title: Lauki Halwa Recipe: How to Make Mouthwatering Bottle Gourd Halwa at Home
instructions: To begin making the Lauki Halwa, first prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Peel the bottle gourd and grate it using a grater or a food processor.
Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadhai over medium heat.
Add the grated bottle gourd and sauté for 4-5 minutes until it softens and the raw smell disappears.
Pour in the milk and sugar and stir well.
Let it simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the milk reduces and thickens, and the bottle gourd is completely cooked, about 15-20 minutes.

Once the milk has reduced, add saffron strands and mix well. Continue to cook for another 5 minutes until the flavors infuse, then turn off the heat. Cook until the halwa reaches a thick, pudding-like consistency.
In a separate small pan, heat the remaining ghee on medium heat. Add the chopped nuts and sauté until they turn golden brown and crisp. Set aside.
Turn off the heat and garnish the Lauki Halwa with the toasted nuts, then transfer to a serving dish. Serve warm or chilled; it keeps in the refrigerator for about 1 week.
Serve the Lauki Halwa warm or cold, as desired. Enjoy the delightful flavors of this traditional Indian dessert!
Feel free to adjust the sweetness and the quantity of ghee according to your taste preferences.

title: Pepper Tea Recipe - Kali Mirch Chai
instructions: In a saucepan, add crushed pepper and ginger (if using) to water and boil for about 5 minutes on medium heat.
When the water is reduced to about 2 cups, strain the water and add to the serving cups.
Add honey and lemon juice as per taste in each serving cup and enjoy.
Optionally, serve with Baked Masala Namak Para or Guilt-free Amaranth, Dates and Almond Ladoo.

title: Baby Corn And Paneer Kathi Roll Recipe
ingredients: 200 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), cut into strips
4 Tortillas (or Whole Wheat Tawa Paratha made into large round sizes for rolls)
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Make the tortillas according to the Homemade Whole Wheat Flour Tortillas recipe and set aside.
Prepare the herb butter by following the Homemade Herb Butter recipe.
Heat herb butter in a saucepan over medium heat; add garlic, onions, bell peppers, carrots, and baby corn. Sauté until the vegetables are soft and tender.
Add the cut paneer pieces and Achari Mayo to the vegetables, tossing until well coated. Avoid overcooking the paneer.
Stir in the chaat masala, mix well, adjust seasoning to taste, then turn off the heat and set aside.
Place the tortillas on a preheated pan, spread a little herb butter, flip and cook until just warmed and soft. Remove and place on a flat surface.
Put a portion of the baby corn‑paneer filling in the center of each tortilla, top with cucumber, tomato, and onion slices, add extra Achari Mayo, and roll up tightly.
Serve the Baby Corn And Paneer Kathi Rolls with a glass of Chikoo Banana Date Smoothie or as desired.

title: Delicious Bharva Bhindi Recipe: Pan-Fried Stuffed Okra with Crushed Roasted Peanut Sesame and Tangy Amchur Masala
instructions: To begin making the Bharva Bhindi Recipe, prep all the ingredients and keep them ready. Ensure you buy tender and even sized bhindi; the thin ends should break easily when bent.
Remove the stem of the bhindi and make a vertical slit without separating the ends, so the bhindi stays in one piece.

In a pestle and mortar, grind the roasted peanuts and sesame seeds to a coarse powder. Add coriander powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, garam masala, turmeric powder, amchur, gram flour, and salt. Add a little water to form a smooth, thick filling paste and adjust seasoning.
Stuff a small amount of the filling into each slit of the bhindi, continuing until all bhindi are filled. Reserve any leftover filling to add while cooking.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan over medium heat; add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Gently add the stuffed bhindi and sprinkle any remaining masala over them.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for about 15 minutes until the bhindi are fully cooked. Halfway through, stir gently to ensure even cooking.
Uncover the pan and stir the lady fingers, turning them to cook uncovered for another couple of minutes.
Observe the color change from green to pale green with roasted brown spots; the bhindi will have shrunk, indicating doneness. Adjust salt and spice levels if needed.
Turn off the heat, transfer the bhindi to a serving platter, garnish with chopped coriander leaves, and serve hot.
Serve the Bharva Bhindi.

title: Karela Tikki Recipe - Healthy Diabetic Snack
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and set them aside.
Use the skin and juice of the karela to retain nutrition.
Combine the grated bitter gourd, carrot, paneer, oats flour, chaat masala, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, green chillies, coriander leaves, and salt in a mixing bowl; mix well.
Check the taste and adjust salt if needed.
Divide the mixture into equal portions and shape each into a round, flat tikki.
Preheat a pan over medium heat, place each tikki, drizzle oil, and cook on both sides until golden brown.
Cook on low to medium heat so the tikki cooks through; then transfer to a plate lined with oil‑absorbent paper and serve hot.
Serve the Karela Tikkis with green chutney and a cup of masala chai.

title: Aloo Chana In Mint Coriander Gravy Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked overnight and cooked until soft
1/2 cup Chana dal (Bengal Gram Dal), boiled still soft
instructions: Take 1/2 cup of cooked channa and grind it coarsely in a mixer; set aside. Mix the remaining half cup of chana with chana dal and reserve.
Grind all the gravy ingredients into a smooth paste and keep aside.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add all the seasoning ingredients and sauté for about a minute.
Add chopped onions and sauté on low heat until soft. Stir in ginger, garlic, and capsicum and cook until tender, reserving a few onion slices for garnish.
Add the cooked chana, dal, and potatoes; sauté for 4–5 minutes. Pour in the ground channa, the ground gravy paste, salt, and turmeric powder, stirring slowly over medium flame until well combined.
Add about 1/2 cup of water (using the water left from cooking the chickpeas) and simmer for 10 minutes. Finally add lemon juice and remove from heat.
Garnish with chopped chillies and onions, then serve warm with aromatic vegetable pulao or phulkas.

title: Amaranth Leaves Khichdi Recipe
ingredients: 100 grams Green Amaranth Leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep aside.
Wash the rice and dal and keep aside.
Into a pressure cooker, add the rice, dal, amaranth leaves, turmeric powder, salt and green chilies. Add 5 cups of water to get a good mish mash khichdi.
Cover the cooker, place the weight on and cook for 2 whistles. After two whistles turn the heat low, and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes and turn off the heat.

Allow the pressure to release naturally. Once the pressure is released, open the cooker and give the khichdi a stir. Check the salt and adjust accordingly. Transfer the amaranth khichdi to a serving bowl.
For the tadka, heat a tablespoon of ghee in a pan, add mustard seeds and cinnamon stick and allow them to crackle. Pour the tadka over the amaranth khichdi and serve.
Serve Amaranth Leaves Khichdi with Gujarati Kadhi or Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita.

title: Curd Rice With Carrots Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped
2 Green Chillies, finely chopped (adjust according to your taste)
instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 to 30 minutes.
Add water and salt to a pressure cooker and cook the rice.
Fluff or lightly mash the cooked rice and let it cool completely.
Stir in the curd (and milk, if using) until well combined with the cooled rice.
Heat oil in a tadka pan, add cashew nuts and raw peanuts, and fry until golden brown.
Add cumin and mustard seeds; when they splutter, add the dals and fry until golden.
Add ginger, dry red chilli and green chillies, then curry leaves; when the leaves turn crisp, add hing and turn off the heat.
Mix in coriander leaves and grated carrot into the curd rice, pour the tempering over it, and combine.
Serve the curd rice with carrots as a side dish or a light lunch.

title: Ginger-Holy Basil Tisane - Adrak Tulsi Chai Recipe
instructions: Wash and clean the ginger thoroughly, then grate it without peeling (the peel is rich in nutrients).
Bring water to a boil in a saucepan.
Add the grated ginger and boil for 2-3 minutes, then simmer for another 3 minutes.
Roughly tear the tulsi (holy basil) leaves and add them to the simmered ginger-water.
Turn off the heat, cover the saucepan and let the mixture steep for 2-3 minutes.
Strain into serving cups, drizzle honey, squeeze lemon juice, stir quickly, and serve hot.
Drink the ginger‑holy basil tisane on an empty stomach.

title: Turai Aloo Ki Sabzi Recipe - Ridge Gourd Potato Curry
instructions: To begin making the Turai Aloo Ki Sabzi, firstly prepare all the ingredients required for the sabzi and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Once it is hot, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Let it splutter.
Add garlic and ginger, saute till the raw smell disappears. Soon after they splutter, add in onions and saute till translucent.
Add tomatoes and cook till tender and mushy.
Add potatoes, saute for few minutes and add the turai cubes in it and occasionally saute. Keep the sabzi covered while cooking. Add water just enough to make a curry like consistency.

Once the potatoes and ridge gourd are cooked, add in the remaining spices including cumin powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder and saute till combined well. Check the salt and spices adjust to suit your taste.
Let it cook for 4 to 5 minutes more and serve hot.
Serve Turai Aloo Ki Sabzi Recipe along with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita and Phulka for your everyday meals.

title: Black Cherry Glazed Thandai Burfi Recipe
instructions: Heat a pan with clarified butter and add the grated bottle gourd.
Cook the bottle gourd for about 6-7 minutes until soft, then add sugar and cook until the mixture becomes dry.
Add mawa, thandai masala, chopped cashews, chopped almonds, cardamom powder and a pinch of green colour; mix well (green colour optional).
Grease an aluminium tray with ghee, pour the mixture into the tray and spread it evenly.
Let it cool for 3-4 hours, then cut into desired shapes, spread cherry glaze on the burfi and garnish with chopped almonds.
Serve the Black Cherry Glazed Thandai Burfi as a dessert.

title: Rock Toast Recipe - Semolina Bread Toast
ingredients: 1/2 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Rock Toast, in a mixing bowl, combine semolina, yogurt, onion, capsicum, coriander leaves, green chilli, salt and pepper powder.
Adjust the topping mixture with a little water, making sure you get a spreadable consistency. Let it sit aside for about 5-7 minutes.
In the meanwhile, heat a griddle on medium flame, spread some oil.
Take a slice of bread, spread the semolina topping on it with a spoon and place the bread in a way that the topping is facing down on the griddle.
Cook this on medium-high heat for about three minutes and flip.
Remove from the tawa and serve hot.
Serve this Rock Toast along with tomato ketchup or Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Homemade Pomegranate Juice with Ginger.

title: High-Protein Peanut Chutney Recipe-Indian Style Peanut Chutney Without Coconut
instructions: To begin making the Peanut Chutney Recipe, first place a pan on the heat. Melt the ghee in it, reduce the heat to low and add peanuts. Roast them for two to three minutes on a low flame till the peanuts are slightly brown.
Next, add urad dal and chana dal to it and roast again till the dals start turning light brown and smell toasted and nutty.
Once done add curry leaves and the green chilli. Stir this for a minute and turn off the heat. Allow the roasted ingredients to cool down for 5 minutes.
Once cooled, place all the roasted ingredients to a mixer grinder and grind it together with ginger, salt and a little water to a smooth paste. Transfer the peanut chutney into a bowl and keep aside.
Now to temper the chutney, place a tadka pan on the heat. Warm some ghee in it.

Add in the mustard seeds and allow the seeds to crackle. After the mustard seeds have crackled add the urad dal, curry leaves and the red chilis and allow them to splutter as well. Turn off the heat and pour the tempering over the peanut chutney, mix well and serve.
Serve the Peanut Chutney along with Aval/ Poha Dosa, Goan Shepeche Polle, Ragi Idli or even Kuzhi Paniyaram as a healthy accompaniment.

title: Stuffed Half Moon Shaped Kaju Burfi Recipe
instructions: First, make the stuffing for the kaju burfi.
Heat 50 ml of water in a saucepan, add desiccated coconut and paneer and cook for 2-3 minutes.

Add milk powder, powdered cashew and oats flour, mix well. Then add sugar and melted white chocolate and continue mixing until the mixture forms a dough that separates from the sides of the pan; set aside to cool.
To prepare the kaju katli/burfi, heat a pan, add water and sugar and boil until a two‑thread consistency is achieved.
Turn off the flame, add the soaked saffron strands, then the powdered oats and powdered cashew nuts; stir vigorously until a dough‑like consistency forms.
Grease your hands and a rolling pin, place the dough on wax/butter paper and roll out to the desired thickness.
Cut the rolled dough into circles with a cookie cutter or any desired shape.

While still warm, gently shape each circle into a half‑moon, spoon in some of the prepared filling, and seal the shape. Store the stuffed half‑moon burfi in an airtight box and refrigerate for a week.
Serve the stuffed half‑moon shaped kaju burfi as a festive mithai.

title: Curd Oats Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup Curd (Dahi / Yogurt), beaten to a smooth consistency
instructions: To begin making the Curd Oats Recipe, we first need to cook the oats in plain water.
Bring a cup of water to a rolling boil in a saucepan, add the oats and season with salt, mix and simmer for 3 minutes until the oats is cooked. Turn off the heat and keep aside to cool.
Take a bowl, add curd and beat the thick curd to the silky smooth texture.
To the curd add the finely chopped ginger and green chilli and the cooled oats. Mix well to combine. If the curd oats is too thick, add a little milk or water to bring it to the desired consistency.
To prepare the tadka, heat oil in a tadka pan on low heat, add the chana dal and mustard seeds and let it splutter.
Once the mustard seeds have spluttered add the curry leaves and asafoetida and once the curry leaves crackle turn off the heat.
Add this tadka over the prepared curd oats and mix well. Season with salt if required and serve.
Serve this delicious Curd Oats Recipe for a light lunch or early supper along with Kachumber salad and Pisarna Manga Recipe -Instant Raw Mango Pickle to make it a complete meal.

title: Bedmi Poori Recipe - Spiced Split Black Lentil Pooris
ingredients: 1 cup Black Urad Dal (Split), soaked for 5-6 hours
instructions: Dry roast the red chilies, coriander seeds and cumin seeds until lightly toasted and aromatic; avoid burning them.
Cool the roasted spices and grind them into a coarse powder; set aside.
Drain the water from the soaked urad dal and blend it to a coarse paste without adding any water.
Transfer the ground dal to a large bowl and add the ground chilli‑coriander powder, amchur, a teaspoon of oil, ginger, salt, fennel powder, and asafoetida; mix well.
Add the whole wheat flour to the mixture and gradually add a little water, as needed, to knead the dough.
Knead until the dough reaches a medium‑soft consistency—firm yet pliable.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
After resting, knead the dough again, then divide it into 18‑20 equal small balls about the size of a golf ball.
Heat enough oil in a kadhai or deep pan for deep frying.
Take one ball at a time and roll it out into a 4‑inch disc.
When the oil is hot, gently slide the rolled poori into the oil and fry on medium‑high heat until puffed and golden brown on both sides.
Remove the cooked poori with a slotted spoon and place on absorbent paper.
Repeat the process with the remaining dough balls.
Serve the Bedmi Pooris with Dubki Wale Aloo or Aloo Tamatari Curry for a wholesome breakfast.

title: Milk Powder Chena Burfi Recipe
instructions: Boil the milk on high heat in a thick bottomed pan to begin preparing chena.
When the milk starts boiling, turn the heat to medium and add white vinegar or lime juice, stirring slowly.
After 2-3 minutes, whey separates; pour the curdled milk into a pan or bowl lined with a thin cotton napkin.
Gather the edges of the cotton napkin and gently squeeze out the remaining whey.
Rinse the chena bundle in water to remove the taste and smell of the acid, then place a weight on it for 6-7 minutes.
Chena is now ready.
Mash the chena coarsely and add sugar, condensed milk, cardamom powder, and ghee; mix well.
Heat the mixture in a thick bottom pan.
When the sugar dissolves completely, add milk powder and cook on medium heat, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Turn off the flame, spread the mixture onto a greased plate, and garnish with pistachios and saffron.
Cool, then cut into squares or desired shapes; the Milk Powder Chena Burfi is ready to serve.
Serve the Milk Powder Chena Burfi during festivals or as a dessert after meals.

title: Crispy Sweet Potato Recipe
instructions: Mix all the ingredients for the batter including corn flour, red chilli powder, salt, chaat masala and black pepper powder.
Add water to make a batter, ensuring it is not too thin.
In a separate bowl, mix all coating ingredients including semolina, red chilli powder, chaat masala, black pepper powder and salt; set aside.
The masala in both batter and coating ensures the sweet potato coats nicely.
Dip the sliced sweet potato in the batter, then coat it with the semolina mixture; repeat for all slices.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan and shallow‑fry the coated sweet potato slices until golden brown; transfer to oil‑absorbent paper and serve hot.
Serve the crispy sweet potato with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Date Tamarind Chutney, or any chutney of your choice.

title: Spicy Egg Biryani Recipe Made Easy In A Pressure Cooker
ingredients: 2 cup Seeraga (Jeeraga) Samba rice, or basmati or govind bhog
Saffron strands, a few strands soaked in milk
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs chopped (for garnish)
1/4 cup Cashew nuts, roasted in ghee until browned (for garnish)
instructions: To begin making the Spicy Egg Biryani, prep all the ingredients and keep ready. Boil the eggs in water for about 10-15 minutes. Peel and keep aside.

For caramelised onions, heat oil in a pan over low heat, add the sliced onions and saute for about 15 to 20 minutes on lowest heat until caramelised and slightly crisp. Ensure this is done on the lowest heat and keep stirring intermittently for even caramelisation. Keep this aside. For roasted cashews, heat ghee in pan, add the broken cashew nuts and stir fry on medium heat until lightly golden brown and crisp. Once done, turn off the heat and keep aside.
Add the ginger, garlic and green chillies into pestle and mortar and make a coarse paste.
Heat ghee in the pressure cooker on medium heat, add the sliced onions and cook them till they soften. This will take about 5-7 minutes.
Add the ginger garlic paste and add whole spices. Saute until you can smell the delicious aromas.
Add the chopped tomatoes, the turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala powder, and mix well.
When the masala is mixed properly, add the boiled eggs.
Next add the rice, saffron milk, yogurt, salt and mint. Add 3 cups water and cook for two whistles and turn the heat to low. Simmer for another 3 minutes and turn off the heat.
Allow the egg biryani to rest for a few minutes and the pressure to release naturally. This will take about 20 minutes.
Garnish with caramelised onions and more leaves and roasted cashew nuts (optional).
Serve Spicy Egg Biryani along with Onion Raita and Mirchi Ka Salan for a delicious weekend meal.

title: Moong Dal Halwa Burfi Recipe
instructions: Add ghee in a pan and roast all the dry fruits; set aside.
Grease a thaali/plate for the halwa and keep it aside.
Roast the moong dal in a dry pan until uniformly roasted, noting the color change and toasty aroma.
Soak the moong dal in 1 cup of water for 45 minutes to an hour.
Grind the soaked moong dal with the water to a slightly coarse, smooth batter.
Pour the batter into a heavy‑bottomed pan and whisk in the milk, sugar, and cardamom.
Heat to medium, stirring continuously until the halwa thickens and leaves the sides of the pan; add saffron strands at this stage.
Continue stirring to prevent lumps and sticking to the pan.
When the halwa separates from the pan, transfer it to the greased thaali, top with the fried dry fruits, and let it cool.
Slice the cooled halwa into desired shapes and serve.

title: Sprouted Methi & Kachha Aam Salad Recipe
instructions: To begin making Sprouted Methi & Kachha Aam Salad, get the sprouts ready and raw mangoes chopped.
In a bowl, combine raw mango, dried cranberries, walnuts and methi seed sprouts. Mix well.
Add lemon juice, honey, paprika and salt. Toss well so that the flavours combine.
Serve Sprouted Methi & Kachha Aam Salad alongside Doli Ki Roti and Kasuri Methi Aur Aloo Rasedar for lunch or breakfast.

title: Khurchan Mawa Burfi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Khurchan (leftover from homemade ghee), or ghee
1 Edible Silver Foil/Leaf (Chandi Ka Vark), to garnish, optional
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai, fry chopped cashews and raisins, and drain on a plate to keep aside.
In the same kadai, add besan and roast until the aroma fills the kitchen and the flour turns brownish in color.
Collect the roasted flour in a bowl and sift with a sieve.
Add khurchan (ghee residue) to the sifted flour, mix with a spoon or fork, and set aside.
Heat mawa in a pan/wok until it loosens, then add condensed milk and sugar, stirring well.
Add cardamom powder and the flour mixture slowly, stirring vigorously to avoid lumps.
Continue stirring continuously until everything combines, comes together, and starts forming a lump.
Turn off the heat, spread the thick mixture on a greased pan, and sprinkle chopped nuts over it; optionally decorate with edible silver foil.
Let the mixture set for 1–2 hours or more, then cut into desired shapes.
Store in a clean dry container and consume within 2–3 days.

title: Crispy Chicken Pakoda Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Crispy Chicken Pakoda Recipe, clean and wash chicken pieces well.

Add chicken pieces, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, pepper powder, and salt to taste into a large bowl and mix well to combine. Next add gram flour and corn flour, and mix again to coat all chicken pieces well.
Finally add the egg and mix again. Cover and let it sit in the fridge to marinate for about 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan for deep frying on a medium flame.
Add a handful of chicken pieces into the oil separately. Do not overcrowd the kadai. Remove from oil when cooked well and crisp, and drain excess oil on a kitchen towel.
Repeat deep frying all the chicken pieces in batches.
At last, slit green chilies and curry leaves into the oil and mix with the deep‑fried Chicken Pakoda, then serve hot.
Serve Crispy Chicken Pakoda immediately with tomato sauce or any delicious dip like Mirchicha Chatka or Peanut Chilli Dipping Sauce during tea time.

title: Dill Cucumber Raita Recipe
instructions: Whisk the yogurt until smooth in a mixing bowl.
Add water, salt, cumin powder, pepper powder, chaat masala, cucumber, mint leaves and dill leaves to the yogurt.
Mix the Dill Cucumber Raita well and serve chilled.
Serve Dill Cucumber Raita along with Ragi Tawa Paratha, Spinach Paneer Kofta Curry, or Aromatic Vegetable Pulao for a simple weekday lunch.

title: Ajwain Besan Ka Paratha Recipe (Masala Paratha)
instructions: To begin making the Ajwain Besan Ka Paratha, we will first make the dough. Add in the flour and a pinch of salt into a large bowl. Add a little water at time and knead to make a firm yet smooth dough.
Knead well for about 3 to 4 minutes, this will make the parathas soft. Drizzle a teaspoon of oil over the dough and knead for another couple of minutes. Cover and keep aside.
Now to begin making the paratha, keep some flour aside for dusting. Divide the dough into large lemon side balls.
Dust the dough portions in flour, flatten it and roll it into a 3 inch diameter circle.
Now add some besan, ajwain, salt, red chilli powder, cumin seeds, turmeric powder and coriander leaves on half side of the circle. Mix everything properly and drizzle some oil on the mixture.
Close the paratha by folding it with the other half. We will have a semi circle oval shape.
Press the sides of the paratha down to seal the edges and gently using the rolling pin to flatten it. Take care, the filling can ooze out if the dough is rolled out too thin.
Now to cook the ajwain besan Paratha, first preheat the skillet on medium heat. Place the rolled paratha on top and allow it to cook on one side. After about 10 to 15 seconds, flip the paratha.
At this stage, smear some oil or ghee to cook the paratha. Cook the paratha by flipping over a couple of times until you see golden brown spots on both sides.
Proceed the same way with the remaining dough portions and serve the parathas hot.
Serve Ajwain Besan Ka Paratha with Mango Pickle and Mooli Raita for a delicious breakfast.

title: Besan Burfi Recipe
ingredients: 125 grams Ghee (or half ghee and half oil)
instructions: We begin making Besan Barfi Recipe, in a deep non stick pan or kadai add mawa/khoya and roast on medium heat until you observe a slight change in colour and turns aromatic. Scoop it into a bowl and set it aside.
Now to the same pan, add the ghee and oil. You can add only ghee as well. Allow it to heat up slightly.
Add the gram flour and roast on medium heat stirring continuously.
After four to five minutes, you can observe that the gram flour turning frothy and bubbly.
Continue stirring and roasting for 6 to 8 minutes or until the froth settles, most of the bubbles disappear, and until its aroma is felt and turns golden in colour.
Now sprinkle a few drops of water (1 to 1‑1/2 teaspoons) precisely after which tiny white bubbles will be formed. This makes the flour slightly grainy that helps in its texture.
Continue roasting on medium heat until all the droplets disappear, about 4 to 5 minutes.

Later turn off the heat and place the pan over a cold water bath (pan or a larger plate filled with water up to an inch or two depending on the size of your kadai/pan) to cool the mixture until lukewarm.
Once the mixture is cooled, add the roasted mawa/khoya.
Work with the wooden spatula or spoon and ensure to mix it thoroughly without any lumps.
Now add the powdered sugar and cardamom powder. Blend them well with the mawa and besan mix. Use your hands if needed.
Grease and line a square pan with parchment, leaving hanging ends to help remove the set dessert mixture in one go and ease cutting into shapes.
Press the dessert mix onto the lined pan, leveling its top with the back of a spoon, bowl, glass, or any flat object to create a smooth and even surface.

Set the pan in a dry place for about 20 minutes, then hold the hanging edges of the parchment to remove it onto a flat surface. Trim any uneven edges and cut into desired shapes using a knife or pizza cutter.
Remove the pieces onto a serving plate, garnish with chopped nuts and serve.
Serve Besan Barfi with Aval Mixture (Poha Chivda) and Ginger Cardamom Chai to your guests in the evening.

title: Mixed Vegetable Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 3 cup Whole Wheat Flour (more for dusting)
2 cup Water (to knead, adjust as needed)
1/2 cup Green peas (Matar), boiled and mashed
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped
instructions: In a bowl, mix together whole wheat flour, salt, and oil.
Add water little by little and knead to form a soft dough, similar to chapati dough.
Grease your hands with oil, knead the dough well, cover, and let it rest for a while.
Prepare the stuffing by mixing mashed potatoes, chopped onions, mashed peas, grated carrot, grated cauliflower, finely chopped green chillies, and fresh coriander.
Add the dry spices – salt, red chilli powder, garam masala, and coriander powder – to the vegetable mixture and mix thoroughly.
Divide the dough into even-sized balls and roll each ball into a small circle, dusting with wheat flour as needed.
Place some stuffing in the center of each rolled-out dough, gather the edges, seal well, and press lightly.
Dust the sealed dough with wheat flour and gently roll it out into a larger circle, taking care not to apply too much pressure.
Heat a tawa (griddle), place the rolled paratha on it, and cook briefly on one side.
Flip the paratha, spread ghee on the half‑cooked side, and continue cooking.
Flip again when the second side is half cooked, spread more ghee, and cook further.
Flip once more, cooking and pressing repeatedly until the paratha is browned and fully cooked; top with butter and serve hot.
Serve the mixed vegetable paratha with Tadka Raita, Boondi Raita, and Mango Pickle for a complete breakfast.

title: Seer Fish Fry Recipe
instructions: Wash and clean the fish slices with water and turmeric powder and keep ready.
Add red chilli powder, salt, tomato sauce, ginger garlic paste, cornflour and lemon juice to a bowl and mix to form a thick paste; if the mix is too thick, add a few drops of water.
Check for taste, add salt or chilli powder if necessary. Take the fish slices one by one and coat both sides with the masala mix.
Allow the fish slices to marinate for 3 to 4 hours.
After 3 to 4 hours, heat oil in a tava and shallow fry the fish slices from both sides until cooked.
Serve Seer Fish Fry as a side dish with Bengali Style Lau Die Tetor Dal and Steamed Rice.

title: Sabudana Vada Recipe - Deep Fried Sago Patties/Cutlets
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and heat oil in a kadai for deep frying.
