Combine the soaked sabudana pearls, mashed potatoes, lightly crushed roasted peanuts, cumin seeds, finely chopped green chillies, coarsely ground sugar, lemon juice, finely chopped coriander leaves, and salt in a bowl.
Mix well until the mixture forms a cohesive dough.
Shape the dough into lemon-sized balls and flatten each ball into a patty.
Deep fry the patties on medium flame until they turn golden brown and become crisp on the outside while being cooked through.
Drain the fried vadas on absorbent paper and serve immediately with chutney.
For the curd chutney, whisk the curd, then add the mashed potato, coarsely ground roasted peanuts, finely chopped green chillies, sugar, and salt; mix well and serve alongside the sabudana vadas.

title: Apple Burfi Recipe
ingredients: Canned cherries, a few to garnish
instructions: Scrape the coconut and churn it into a fine paste without adding any water in a mixer grinder; set aside. Peel and chop the apples.
In a mixing bowl, combine the chopped apples, coconut paste, condensed milk, chopped nuts, raisins, and milk. Mix well.
Heat ghee in a pan and add the apple mixture, stirring well.
When the moisture dries up and the color changes to brown, and the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, add cardamom powder.
Give it a nice mix, cook for a few seconds, and switch off the flame.
Grease a dish with ghee, pour the mixture onto it, and let it cool.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, garnish with chopped nuts, raisins, and cherries. Run a knife around the edges, cut into barfi shapes, and serve.
Serve the apple burfi along with Gujarati Fafda and Omapodi Diwali Mixture for snacking during special occasions and festivals.

title: Stuffed Corn and Capsicum Paratha Recipe with Herbs
ingredients: 4 Phulka (Made of Vivatta whole wheat flour chakki atta)
2 cups Red Yellow and Green Bell Peppers (Capsicum), thinly sliced
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan or wok, add the onions and garlic and sauté on a high flame for a minute.

Add baby corn and capsicum and sauté on high flame for another 2 minutes until they become soft and tender. Once soft and tender, add the chilli flakes, mixed herbs, salt and mix everything well. Sauté on a high flame for another 30 seconds.
Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions and keep aside to cool for 5 minutes.
Place a portion of the mixture in the centre of the roti, fold 2 opposite corners of the roti over the filling, overlapping them slightly. Now fold the remaining 2 sides to seal the stuffing well.
Heat a skillet or roti tawa and cook the envelope using oil, till they are golden brown in colour from both the sides.
Repeat with the remaining rotis and stir-fry to make 3 more envelopes.
Serve Stuffed Corn and Capsicum Paratha with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or any other chutney of your choice.

title: High Protein Zucchini & Corn Patty Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Soy granules, or foxtail millet (cooked according to instruction with salt)
1/2 cup Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), or parmesan cheese, grated
1/2 cup Foxtail Millet flour, or wheat flour to act as binder
Parsley leaves, small bunch, or coriander leaves, finely chopped
Za'atar, or bread crumbs or sesame seeds
instructions: In a large bowl combine all the ingredients except the oil. Make sure the patty dough is firm and can be shaped into balls or flat discs.
Divide the mixture into 10 to 12 equal portions, shape them into balls, and flatten them to make disc shapes or any other shape of your choice. Keep aside.
Heat a skillet on medium heat; if using an iron skillet, be sure to season it with oil to prevent the patties from sticking to the bottom.
Toss the zucchini‑corn patties in the bread crumbs, Za'atar spice mix, or sesame seeds and lightly flatten them.
Place the zucchini patties on the skillet and cook on both sides, adding a little oil over the top. Cook until each side is golden brown.
Serve the high protein zucchini patties as a burger between buns or as an appetizer, accompanied by sour cream, roasted tomato pasta sauce, or cottage cheese dip.

title: Walnut Burfi Recipe - Akhrot Barfi
instructions: Clean walnuts and grind them into a smooth paste in a mixer grinder by adding some water along with cardamom and sugar.
Heat the kadai and pour some ghee. Reserve half of the ghee to add later.
Add the walnut paste and keep stirring until it thickens.

Add some ghee in between to achieve the proper consistency. The end result will be brown and thick dough; take off the burfi dough when it comes together well and does not stick to the sides of the pan.
Transfer it to a plate and allow it to cool to room temperature. Cut it into desired shapes once it cools down.
Serve Walnut Burfi with other burfis like Sing Paak and Jwarichya Lahyancha Chivda to your guests on festivals.

title: Beetroot Paratha Recipe Flavored With Peanuts
ingredients: 1 small bunch coriander (dhania) leaves, finely chopped
instructions: In a large bowl add 2 cups whole wheat flour and salt; stir with fingers to combine.
Add water a little at a time and knead to make a soft, pliable dough; knead for a couple of minutes until smooth and elastic.
Add a teaspoon of oil to coat the dough and knead a little more until the dough is soft, smooth and not sticky.
Divide the dough into 14 to 16 equal portions, cover, and let rest while preparing the filling.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan, add the grated beetroot with a dash of salt and sauté on medium heat until soft; cover to speed up, then turn off heat and let cool.
Add the chopped onion, softened beetroot, chopped coriander, green chillies, cumin powder, roasted peanuts and salt to the pan; combine well.
Divide the filling into 14 to 16 equal portions.
Dust a dough portion with flour and flatten on a rolling board; roll into a ~3‑inch diameter circle.
Dust another dough portion with flour and roll into a ~3‑inch diameter circle.
Place a portion of the filling onto the first circle and spread evenly.
Place the second rolled dough circle over the filling.
Press and fold the edges to seal, press down to release air pockets, and gently roll with a pin to even out; repeat with remaining portions.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat and place the filled dough.
Cook for about 30–45 seconds, flip, and add a teaspoon of ghee or oil, spreading it around.
Flip again, allowing the oiled side to cook; press the paratha while on the skillet to cook evenly.
Continue flipping and pressing until both sides are browned, crisp, and cooked through, keeping heat on medium.
Transfer the cooked paratha to a plate; repeat for the remaining dough portions.
Serve the stuffed beetroot paratha with raita and pickles, or pack for a lunch box.

title: Dhania Wale Aloo Recipe - Coriander Potato Dry
ingredients: 2 teaspoons sesame seeds (til seeds), dry roasted
instructions: Wash and boil the baby potatoes in a pressure cooker for two whistles until cooked yet firm, then peel and set aside.
Dry roast the sesame seeds in a pan over low heat until golden brown and set aside.
Combine all the chutney ingredients – coriander leaves, green chilli, ginger, and the roasted sesame seeds – and grind to a smooth paste with a little water using a hand blender or mixer; set aside.
Heat ghee in a heavy‑bottomed pan over low flame, add cumin powder, black pepper, garam masala, and rock salt.
Add the boiled baby potatoes and sauté until mildly roasted, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the prepared dhania chutney and toss the potatoes well.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are fully coated with the masala paste.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice, and give a final toss.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: Sooji Manpasand Burfi Recipe - Semolina Coconut Fudge
instructions: To begin making Sooji Manpasand Burfi Recipe, in a large kadai or thick bottomed deep pan, mix all the ingredients; suji, coconut, milk, sugar, ghee and saffron. Keep aside for 2 hours.
Grease a pan or tray with ghee and keep aside.
After 2 hours, start cooking the suji mixture on medium high heat and let it come to a boil, stirring constantly.
Keep cooking, stirring and scraping the sides continuously.
You will notice that after 15 to 20 minutes, the mixture will start to thicken. At this point, stir in crushed cardamom powder.
Once it starts leaving the sides of the pan and starts to form a thick fudgelike dough; in about 35 to 40 minutes, pour the mixture into the greased pan.
Spread evenly with a greased spatula and stud with slivered almonds (optional).
Leave aside to cool. When warm, cut into desired shapes with a sharp knife.
Store in an airtight container and serve when needed. Serve Sooji Manpasand Burfi with Omapodi Diwali Mixture and Masala Chai for snacks.

title: Coconut Jaggery Burfi Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Coconut Jaggery Burfi recipe, add ghee, grease a plate and keep aside. Take coconut and jaggery in a pan and cook on medium flame stirring with ladle.
Add cardamom powder and mix. Keep stirring continuously until the mixture starts coming together, leaving the sides of the pan.
Remove from flame and add the coconut mixture to a greased plate. Spread and level the surface.
Allow to cool a bit. Cut into squares when it is warm. It becomes slightly firm when cooled. Decorate with nuts if needed and serve.
Serve Coconut Jaggery Burfi for dessert after your festive meal of Jaipuri Aloo Pyaaz ki Sabzi, Boondi Raita and Phulka.

title: Makhana Moongphali Kadhi With Samvat Rice Recipe
ingredients: Rock Salt, as required (used during fasting)
instructions: Add water chestnut flour, makhana powder, peanut powder, rock salt, red chilli powder and cinnamon powder to yogurt in a mixing bowl and whisk well.
Add water as required and mix well. Heat ghee in a kadhai and add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, dry red chilli and curry leaves.
Sauté until the cumin seeds splutter, then add the yogurt mixture and cook till it thickens slightly. Add sugar, salt and simmer for five minutes.
Add peanuts and lotus seeds, cook for 2 minutes, then garnish with coriander leaves.
Rinse the sama rice a couple of times and soak in water for 20-30 minutes.
Dry roast the peanuts until crunchy and coarsely powder them.
Heat oil or ghee in a wide pan, add cumin seeds, cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom and black pepper; sauté until fragrant and cumin crackles.
Add crushed ginger and green chilli and sauté for half a minute over low heat.
Add cubed potatoes, curry leaves, and chopped coriander leaves; sauté for 3-4 minutes on low flame. Then add the powdered peanuts and stir.
Drain the soaked rice and add to the sautéed mixture. Add water and salt, then pressure cook until 4-5 whistles or until water is absorbed and rice is cooked.
While the pulao is cooking, dry roast cashews, peanuts and whole chillies for garnish.
Serve the Makhana Moongphali Kadhi with Samvat Rice on its own or with Vrat Wale Aloo.

title: Cheese and Spring Onion Stuffed Parathas
ingredients: 1 cup Whole Wheat Flour (more for dusting)
1/2 cup Cheese, grated (I used Amul cheese)
instructions: Combine all the dough ingredients and knead with a little water to make a soft, smooth dough; cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan, add the spring onions and sauté for a few minutes until soft and tender; turn off the heat and let cool.
Mix the cooled spring onions with the remaining stuffing ingredients in a large bowl, then divide into 6 equal portions.
Divide the rested dough into 6 equal portions, according to the desired paratha size.
Roll each dough portion into a thick 3‑inch diameter circle, place a portion of the cheese‑onion filling in the center, and bring the edges together to fully enclose the filling.
Pinch the top to seal, pat and press the filled dough with your palms, dust with wheat flour, and gently roll out to form a paratha; repeat for all portions.
Preheat a skillet over medium flame, place each rolled paratha on it and cook both sides with oil or ghee until golden brown.
Spread butter on the hot parathas and serve immediately with plain yogurt or beetroot raita.

title: Moong Dal Palak Cheela Recipe (Yellow Lentil And Spinach Crepes)
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves , a bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Moong Dal Palak Cheela Recipe, clean, wash and soak the moong dal in water for 4 to 5 hours. Once ground, drain the water to a separate bowl.
Grind the soaked moong dal adding little water at a time to make a smooth and thick batter. The batter should be of pouring consistency.
Pour the cheela batter into a large mixing bowl. Add the remaining ingredients except the oil and stir well to combine. Check the salt and adjust to suit your taste.
Heat a skillet on medium heat and grease it with oil. Pour a ladleful full of batter and spread it into a thin crepe. Drizzle some oil around the center and the edges of the Palak Cheela.

Let it cook well until the base gets light golden brown color and the top of cheela gets dried. Flip and cook on the other side. Once done, remove from the pan and proceed to make the Palak Cheelas the similar way.
Serve the Moong Dal Palak Cheela along with Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney for breakfast, evening snack or even a weeknight dinner.

title: Ajwaini Tamatar Bhindi Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Cashew nuts, soaked and ground to paste
instructions: Cut bhindi into half and dry them thoroughly so they are not wet.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add bhindi and stir for a couple of minutes; cook on medium flame.
Cover the pan and let the bhindi cook until done, stirring occasionally.
Remove the cooked bhindi from the pan and set aside.
Heat oil in the same heavy-bottomed pan again to prepare the gravy.
When the oil is hot, add ajwain seeds and asafoetida powder.
After a minute, add the pureed tomatoes and the red chilli powder.
Cook on medium flame until the tomato puree is cooked through; add sugar and salt to taste and continue cooking for a short while.
Add the cashew paste, salt (if needed), the pre‑cooked bhindi, and mix everything well. Cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve the Ajwaini Tamatar Bhindi hot, preferably with Butter Garlic Naan and Boondi Raita.

title: Grated Carrot Cucumber Tomato Raita Recipe
instructions: Prep all the vegetables and keep them aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cucumber, tomato, carrot, green chili, and plain yogurt; whisk well and add black salt, salt, and pepper, then mix thoroughly.
Sprinkle cumin powder and red chilli powder as a garnish and serve.
Serve the raita as a side dish with Chana Dal Pulao or Mumbai Style Tawa Pulao with Moong Sprouts.

title: Mango Shikanji Recipe - Chatpata Mango Spritzer
ingredients: 500 ml Bisleri Fonzo (the bubbly mango drink)
instructions: Gather all the ingredients.
In a large jug, combine the Bisleri Fonzo, black salt, cumin powder, chaat masala powder, black pepper powder, lemon juice, and some ice cubes.
Mix the shikanji well and serve chilled immediately.
Serve the mango shikanji alongside Cheesy Pav Bhaji and Chole Aloo Tikki Chaat for a weekend chaat party.

title: Besan Aur Pyaz Ka Cheela Recipe - Roz Ka Khana With Figaro Olive Oil
ingredients: Extra Virgin Olive Oil, for cooking
instructions: Combine all the listed ingredients in a large bowl.
Gradually add water to make a thick batter.
Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to taste.
Ensure the batter has the consistency of dosa or pancake batter and can coat the back of a spoon.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin crepe/dosa.
Drizzle olive oil around the cheela and cook until the top is set and edges turn brown; flip and cook the other side briefly.
Transfer the cooked cheela to a plate and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve the Besan Pyaz Ka Cheela with Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Tomato Onion Tadka Raita Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Cucumber, peeled and finely chopped (optional)
instructions: Chop the tomato, onion, and cucumber finely and set aside.
In a bowl, whisk the curd with a little water until smooth; add the chopped vegetables and salt, then mix well.
Heat a tadka pan with the required oil, add curry leaves, cumin seeds, and mustard seeds, and let them crackle for about 10-15 seconds.
Turn off the heat and pour the tadka over the curd mixture, mixing thoroughly.
Serve the Tomato Onion Tadka Raita with Aloo Sabz Dum Biryani and papad.

title: Khatti Meethi Dal Chawal Recipe
instructions: Wash and clean the dal and keep aside. Wash and soak the rice for 1/2 an hour; drain and keep aside.

Heat ghee in a pressure cooker or a heavy bottomed pan; add cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and cumin seeds. When cumin seeds crackle, add the chopped garlic, ginger, green chilli and onions and sauté until the onion turns soft and light brown. Add chopped tomatoes and sauté till soft.
Now add the remaining ingredients, rice and dal except the vegetables.

Add 3 1/2 cups of water along with salt and sugar and pressure cook for 3 to 4 whistles or cook in the pan simmering on medium heat until all the water is completely absorbed. Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release completely from the cooker. If cooking in a saucepan, then allow the rice to rest for 10 minutes.
Once the steam has released completely, add the roasted peanuts, steamed vegetables and coriander leaves and mix well until all the ingredients are well combined.
Serve Khatti Meethi Dal Chawal on its own with a papad for a weeknight meal.

title: Maharashtrian Gavachi Kheer Recipe (Whole Cracked Wheat Pudding)
ingredients: 2 tablespoon Rice, soaked in water for 30 minutes
2 tablespoon Chironji, or any other nuts of choice
Slivered Almonds (Badam), or pista or cashews, for garnish
instructions: Heat ghee in a saucepan.
Add the chironji and any other nuts.
Sauté for a minute and take out the nuts onto a plate.
In the same pan add daliya, stir and roast till you get the distinct aroma.
Take it off the heat.
Cool slightly and pressure cook the daliya and rice with 2 1/2-3 cups of water until soft, about 3 whistles and 10 minutes on simmer.
In the saucepan add daliya, coconut and jaggery and heat the mixture until the jaggery dissolves, adding a little water if required.
Add the saffron and nutmeg to the milk.
Add milk and nuts to the kheer and cook for a few minutes.
Serve hot or cold, garnished with slivered nuts.

title: Pista Burfi Recipe - Indian Spiced Pistachio Fudge
instructions: Soak the pistachios in warm water for about half an hour, then drain and blend the pistachios with the grated coconut until almost smooth; set aside.
In a medium saucepan, combine the sugar and 1/4 cup water over medium heat, melt the sugar and continue boiling until the syrup reaches a two‑string consistency.
Test the syrup consistency by dropping a small amount into cold water; if it forms a soft ball that holds its shape, the syrup is ready.
Add the ground pistachio‑coconut mixture and cardamom powder to the syrup.
Continue stirring over medium heat frequently to prevent the mixture from sticking to the pan.
Cook for 10‑15 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan as the pistachios and coconut release their oil.
Turn off the heat and stop stirring to avoid over‑cooking, which can cause the sugar to crystallize and make the burfi hard.
Transfer the mixture to a greased square pan, spread evenly, press down, and let it cool completely.
Once cooled, cut the pistachio burfi into squares and serve.

title: Ginger Lemon Black Tea Recipe
instructions: To begin making Ginger Lemon Black Tea Recipe, take a saucepan and start heating water on a medium heat.
Once the water starts boiling, add the grated ginger and assam black tea leaves.
After a minute more of boiling, turn off the heat and then add the lemon juice. Keep it covered for a minute.
Strain the tea into the tea cups.
Add honey to taste (only as a sweetener, you can completely skip it), give it a swirl and serve.
Serve and enjoy this simple Ginger Lemon Black Tea Recipe with a Oatmeal Cranberry Cookie Recipe or with Phool Makhana for your evening tea.

title: Pudina Mushroom And Soya Biryani Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups Basmati rice, parboiled with spices infused water (Spices include Cinnamon, One Mint branch, 2-3 Cloves and Cardamoms, 1 Bay leaf)
1 cup Button mushrooms, cut into quarters
1 cup Soy Chunks (Nuggets), soaked in hot water
instructions: To begin making the Pudina Mushroom And Soya Biryani recipe, wash and soak the rice in water for 20 minutes.
In a bowl, place the soya chunks, and pour boiling hot water over it and allow it to soak in it.

In a pressure cooker, heat ghee on low flame, add the whole spices - cumin seeds, bay leaf, star anise, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, once these begin to sizzle, add in the ginger, garlic, green chili, saute for a couple of minutes.
Next increase the heat to medium-low and add the sliced onions and cook until transparent, this will take about 2-3 minutes.
At this stage, add the mushrooms, and the dry masalas - biryani masala, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, salt and give it a good mix.
Now add the curd, drained soya chunks, pudina leaves, drained rice and 2 cups of water and close the pressure cooker.
Allow the Pudina Mushroom And Soya Biryani recipe to pressure cook for 2 whistles and turn off the flame. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once released, open the pressure cooker and gently fluff up the Pudina Mushroom And Soya Biryani recipe and transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve hot Pudina Mushroom And Soya Biryani along with Boondi raita and Kachumber Salad for a weeknight dinner.

title: Brown Rice Flakes Pudding / Desi Poha Kheer Recipe
instructions: Rinse the poha well and soak in a cup of water for about 15 minutes.
Drain all excess water.
Transfer poha into a pressure cooker.
Add the milk and cardamom powder.
Close the lid and pressure cook at low heat for 15-20 minutes until 1 whistle, or till cooked well.
Switch off the flame and allow the pressure to release by itself.
Mix in the condensed milk and serve.

title: Instant Tindora And Carrot Pickle Recipe
instructions: Wash and trim the edges of the tindora (ivy gourd), slit them lengthwise, first halve each and then slice each half into three pieces.
Wash, peel, and chop the carrot into 1‑inch pieces; spread the vegetables on a dry kitchen towel for at least 15 minutes.
Dry‑roast the mustard seeds, methi seeds, coriander seeds and dry red chillies separately over low flame, being careful not to burn them.
Cool the roasted spices and grind them in a mixer‑grinder to a fine powder.
Heat a kadai or pan and add the gingelly (sesame) oil.
Add the minced garlic to the hot oil, followed by the slit green chillies and curry leaves; sauté for about a minute.
Add the asafoetida (hing) and sauté for another minute.
Add the prepared tindora and carrot pieces, along with turmeric powder; sauté briefly, then cook on medium heat for 10‑12 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking or burning.
Stir in the ground masala powder and salt; mix well.
Simmer the mixture for another 5 minutes, then remove from heat and let it rest for 2‑3 hours for the flavors to meld.
Serve the instant tindora and carrot pickle with Keerai Sambar, steamed rice, Chow Chow Thoran, and Elai Vadam.

title: Suran Moongphali Curry Recipe (Yam/Jimikand Curry with Peanuts)
ingredients: 250 grams Elephant yam (Suran/Senai/Ratalu), chopped and boiled
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add cumin seeds once the oil is hot, and add the finely chopped green chillies.
Add the finely chopped boiled pieces of suran and stir well.
Add ground peanuts, black salt, sugar, and turmeric powder to the suran and mix well.
Add 1 cup of water to the suran curry, cover and cook for 5 to 10 minutes until the suran is cooked through; turn off the heat and adjust salt and spices to taste.
Serve the Suran Moongphali Curry hot with Sabudana Khichdi during a fast or with steamed rice for a weeknight dinner.

title: Phool Makhana Recipe - Healthy Roasted Lotus Seeds Snack
instructions: In a small bowl, combine the melted ghee, turmeric powder, salt and pepper.
In a heavy bottom pan, dry roast the phool makhana on low to medium heat, roasting for about 8 to 10 minutes until evenly roasted.
Add the melted ghee, salt and pepper mixture to the roasted phool makhana and roast for a couple more minutes until crunchy; then allow to cool completely and store in an airtight container.
Serve the roasted Phool Makhana as a healthy snack for kids.
Serve as an evening snack along with a cup of hot Masala Chai.

title: Stuffed Kathal Recipe
ingredients: 50 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Stuffed Kathal, let us first cut the raw jackfruit. In order to do that we have to first, grease our hands and the knife that we are going to use, with some oil.
This important tip ensures that the hands don't get sticky from the natural fruit latex/sap present in the fruit does not get onto your hands and makes the cutting process hassle-free.
Keep a bowl of water mixed with some salt, ready to put the cut raw jackfruit pieces to avoid discolouration of the fruit.
Now that your hands and knife are well greased, cut the jackfruit in half, discard the skin and start making 1 inch pieces and soak them in the salted water.
Place the jackfruit in a pressure cooker with 1/4 cup of water and pressure cook for 1 whistle and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally. Drain any water from the jackfruit and set aside.
Heat mustard oil in a pan on medium heat, shallow fry until crisp. This will take about 5-7 minutes. Drain on an absorbent paper and set aside.
In a pan, heat garlic butter on low heat, add fennel seeds and allow it to sizzle, next add the onions and fry till soft, for about 3 minutes.
Next add paneer and fry well. Turn off the flame. Stuffing for the stuffed kathal is ready.

Take Kathal pieces and stuff the jackfruits with the onion-paneer stuffing. Sprinkle salt and pepper over the stuffed kathal, give it a quick mix and let it rest for an hour while the flavours infuse.
Meanwhile, to prepare the gravy.
Heat oil in a pan, on medium heat, add onions and saute for a couple of minutes.
Once the onions are transparent, add tomatoes and give it a good mix, cover and cook until mushy, this will take about 3-4 minutes. turn off the flame.
Once the onion-tomato cools down, grind it in a mixer to a coarse paste.
Heat a kadai on medium flame, transfer the coarse tomato-onion mixture and add chilli powder, garam masala and turmeric powder, curd and saute till the masala is cooked well and comes together.
Adjust spices and salt according to your taste.
Once done, pour this thick masala in an Oven Safe Bowl. Put in the stuffed Kathal/jackfruit.
Sprinkle grated mozzarella and bake in the preheated oven at 180 degrees Celsius for 10-15 minutes.
Garnish with spring onions and serve Stuffed Kathal with hot Laccha paratha / tawa paratha for a weeknight dinner.

title: Mutton Dak Bungalow Curry Recipe
ingredients: Dry Red Chilli, as per taste
instructions: To begin making the Mutton Dak Bungalow Curry recipe, we will first marinate the mutton.
Take the goat meat under the water at room temperature, clean it well, and place it in a large pasta strainer for 30 minutes to drain excess water.
Put the cleaned meat in a large bowl, add sour curd, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, and mustard oil; marinate thoroughly.
Rub the meat pieces with the marination, cover, and let the marinated meat rest overnight or for 6‑8 hours.
Remove the marinated meat 2 hours before cooking.
Grind all the ingredients listed under "Special Spice Powder" into a dry powder, store in an airtight container and set aside.
Prepare the gravy: prick the boiled eggs to prevent bursting, then marinate the boiled eggs and potatoes with salt and turmeric powder for 10 minutes.
Heat oil and ghee in a large non‑stick pan, fry the marinated eggs and potatoes until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add bay leaf, radhuni and methi leaves; fry briefly, then add sliced onion and salt, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Uncover, fry the onion until golden brown, add ginger garlic paste and fry for 1 minute, then add sliced tomatoes and cook until pulpy.
Add the marinated meat and the special spice powder to the pan, cover for 5 minutes; then uncover and fry over medium heat for 30 minutes.
If the masala begins to stick, sprinkle water and continue frying; add the fried potatoes and 2 cups of water.
For pressure‑cooker method: add all meat and spices to the cooker, close the lid and cook for 10 minutes or up to 4 whistles.
Allow pressure to release naturally, open the cooker, add the fried eggs, boil the curry for 5 minutes, then turn off heat and serve with plain rice and cucumber salad.
OR
For pan‑cooking method: cover the pan, lower the heat and simmer the gravy for 20‑30 minutes until the meat is soft and tender; then uncover and serve hot.
Serve Mutton Dak Bungalow with Phulka and Jeera Rice for a weekday meal.

title: Black Currant Dates Kheer Recipe
instructions: Roast the dry fruits, poppy seeds, dates and black currant with ghee in a small pan on medium heat until a wonderful aroma emanates.
Reduce heat to low, add jaggery and coconut milk to the roasted mixture and mix everything together.
Mix the rice flour in a little water separately, then add it to the mixture, stir to combine well, bring to a boil and simmer until slightly thickened for 5 to 10 minutes.
The Black Currant Dates Kheer is now ready to be served hot or can be refrigerated and served chilled.
Serve the Black Currant Dates Kheer after a one-pot meal such as Spiced Kumbh Pulao.

title: Jeera Rice Recipe | Jeera Pulao | Cumin Flavoured Ghee Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice well in water.
Place the washed rice in the pressure cooker, add salt, green chillies and two cups of water.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook for 2 whistles on high heat. Turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes and turn off the heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Allow the rice to rest for 10 minutes before opening the cooker.
Heat ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and allow them to crackle; turn off the heat once the roasted aroma is released.
Pour the roasted cumin into the cooked rice and, using a slotted spoon, stir the rice gently and fluff it up.
The Jeera Rice is now ready to be served along with Dals & Kadhi's for a great weeknight dinner.
Serve Jeera Rice with Tadka Dal, Paneer Butter Masala, and Garlic Naan for a weekend lunch.

title: Baked Palak Ki Mathri Recipe (Baked Spinach Spicy Tea-Time Crackers)
instructions: To begin making the Baked Palak Ki Mathri Recipe, first clean the spinach thoroughly. Then, finely chop the leaves up and keep them aside for later use.

Sieve the whole wheat flour, semolina and salt 2 to 3 times into a mixing bowl. Add the carom seeds, chopped spinach, ghee (or oil) and salt and combine well with your fingertips till the mixture resembles wet sand or coarse bread crumbs.

Next, slowly add cold water little at a time, and knead the mixture together to get a stiff yet pliable dough. Roll it around in the mixing bowl and keep place it in a covered dish, in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 180 degrees C.
When you are ready to bake the mathri, take the dough out from the refrigerator and keep aside for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into two parts. Roll each part into a circle of thickness of your choice. Dust the flour if you find it hard to roll.
Then, using a cookie cutter, portion out small circular mathris. Prick them all over with a fork and arrange them on the baking tray lined with baking paper.
Brush the surface of the mathri with melted ghee and bake at 180 degrees C for 10 to 12 minutes, until they are cooked through.
Remove the tray from the oven, allow the mathris to cool completely on a wire rack. Once cooled the palak mathris are ready to be served.
Serve the Baked Palak Ki Mathri along with Masala Chai and some other treats like Sabudana Vada, Nariyal Ki Kachori and Green Spinach & Oats Cutlet for a delicious spread.

title: Raw Mango Cucumber Salad Recipe with Roasted Peanuts
instructions: To begin making the Raw Mango & Cucumber Salad Recipe, keep all the ingredients ready.
In a large mixing bowl, add the raw mango, cucumber, peanuts, coriander leaves and mint leaves.
Add all of the dressing ingredients like the sweet chutney, paprika and salt into a small bowl and whisk to combine well.

Drizzle the dressing over the top of the Raw Mango & Cucumber Salad and toss well. Check for seasonings and adjust if required. Transfer the Raw Mango & Cucumber Salad into a serving bowl and serve as a side dish with meals.
Serve the Raw Mango & Cucumber Salad Recipe along with Spinach Rice Recipe and Nawabi Kofta Curry Recipe for weekend lunch.

title: Mithi Mathri Recipe (Crispy Fried Sweet Fritters)
instructions: Prepare the dough: mix the maida, sooji and salt together in a mixing bowl.
Add the ghee to the mixture and rub between your fingers until the dough turns crumbly and resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the warm water gradually, knead into a dough, press together to form a ball, knead 3-4 minutes until non‑sticky, set aside to rest 5 minutes, then knead again till soft for about 5 minutes.
Cover the dough with a muslin cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 16 equal parts, shape balls and let rest 5 minutes.
Roll each ball into a disc about 1/4 inch thick and 2‑3 inches in diameter; poke with fork or knife.
Heat oil in a kadhai and deep‑fry the mathris 2‑3 minutes on each side until golden brown; remove with slotted spoon and cool.
Prepare the sugar syrup by boiling water, sugar and cardamom powder in a heavy‑bottomed saucepan.
When mixture boils, reduce heat and cook until syrup reaches two‑string consistency, about 8‑10 minutes on low heat.
Turn off heat and dip the fried mathri into the sugar syrup, submerging for about 30 seconds to coat completely.
Place sugar‑coated mathri on a tray to dry completely; store in airtight container once cool.

title: Kathal Biryani Recipe |  Jackfruit Biryani Topped with Caramelised Onions
instructions: To begin making the Kathal Biryani Recipe (Raw Jackfruit Biryani), first prep all the ingredients and keep ready.

To cut raw jackfruit, grease hands and the knife that we are going to use to cut, with oil. This important tip ensures that the hands don't get sticky from the natural fruit latex/sap present in the fruit does not get onto your hands and makes the cutting process hassle-free.

Keep a bowl of water mixed with some salt to put the cut raw jackfruit pieces to avoid discolouration of the fruit. Cut the jackfruit in half, discard the skin and start making 1 inch pieces and soak them in the salted water. Keep aside.

To begin making the jackfruit biryani, heat ghee in a pressure cooker over medium heat; add the onion, ginger and garlic and saute until the onions turn slightly caramelised. This will take about 5 to 8 minutes.
Next add all the whole spices along with bay leaf in the remaining ghee. Allow them to sizzle and the aromas to come through.

Stir in the chopped jackfruit/kathal pieces, yogurt, coriander powder, red chilli powder, nutmeg powder, saffron strands and mix everything well so that the curd mixes well with the kathal. Give it one brisk boil and stir in the mint leaves and salt to taste.
Add the washed jeera rice over the jackfruit masala, give it a stir and add 4 cups of water.

Cover the pressure cooker and cook on high heat till you hear two whistles. After two whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes and turn off the heat. Once done, allow the pressure to release naturally and the biryani to rest.
Open the cooker after the resting period and give the Kathal Biryani/Jackfruit Biryani a gentle stir, to combine all the masala and jackfruit into the rice.

To caramelise the onions; heat oil in a pan over medium heat; add the sliced onions and keep sautéing on low to medium heat until the onions get caramelised and crisp. Transfer to a bowl and keep aside. This will take 20 to 30 minutes. A good idea to do this while the biryani is cooking and cooling down.
For garnish, heat ghee in a pan; add the cashew nuts and roast them on medium heat until golden and crisp. Towards the end add the raisins and stir for a few seconds.
Gently stir the caramelised onions, raisins, cashew nuts and mint leaves into the Kathal Biryani and serve hot with a raita and salan.
Serve the Kathal Biryani as a one dish meal for a weeknight dinner or as a party food along with Sweet & Spicy Coriander Tadka Raita.

title: Khichdi With Fresh Spices Recipe
instructions: To begin making Khichdi with Fresh Spices Recipe, first rinse and wash rice and the lentils together. Soak them for about 30 minutes in water.
Heat 1 tablespoon ghee in a pressure cooker and add cumin seeds. When it starts to sputter add bay leaf, dry red chillies, green cardamom, cinnamon, ginger and asafoetida.
Saute for 10 to 15 seconds and add the drained rice and moong dal to the pressure cooker and saute for a minute.

Pour 3 cups of water into the pressure cooker, turmeric powder and salt to taste. Close the lid tightly and pressure cook the khichdi on a medium heat till the cooker releases a whistle. Once the whistle comes, turn the flame to low and cook for 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes turn off the heat and wait till the pressure is released naturally and open the lid. Transfer the Khichdi with Fresh Spices into a serving bowl.
Add ghee on top if you like and garnish the Khichdi with Fresh Spices with coriander leaves, green chillies and a wedge of lemon and serve hot.
Serve Khichdi With Fresh Spices Recipe with Pudina & Dhaniya Raita Recipe and Aam Ka Achaar Recipe for a simple comforting weeknight dinner.
Editor’s Notes: The contest is in association with Preethi Kitchen Appliances.

title: Shredded Mutton With Caramelized Onions Recipe
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the mutton pieces with water, salt, and turmeric powder; cook for 8-10 whistles or until done, then let the pressure release naturally.
Allow the cooked mutton to cool, then pulse it in a blender to obtain thin threads; heat coconut oil in a pan and add the chopped onions.
Cook the onions until fully caramelized, then add the green chili paste, ginger garlic paste, and salt.
Stir in the pulsed mutton threads and cook on very low flame for another 15 minutes before turning off the heat.
Serve the shredded mutton with caramelized onions alongside Burani Raita and Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha.

title: Stuffed Karela With Aloo Recipe
instructions: Clean the karelas/bitter gourds, rinse with salt and turmeric to remove bitterness, and let rest for 20-25 minutes.
Make a vertical slit on each karela and scoop out and discard the seeds and pulp.
Prepare the potato masala: smash the boiled potatoes in a bowl, then add turmeric powder, red chili powder, chaat masala, garam masala and salt; mix well.
Fill the karelas tightly with the potato masala mixture.
Heat oil in a shallow frying pan and shallow-fry the stuffed karelas lightly for about a minute so the stuffing stays intact; then cover and cook on low‑medium heat until the karelas are well cooked.
When the karelas are soft, turn off the heat; the dish is ready to serve.
Serve the stuffed karela with aloo alongside Moong Dal Tadka, Palak Raita and Phulka.

title: Spiced Buttermilk With Coriander And Ginger Recipe
instructions: Chop the coriander leaves and ginger and set aside.
In a mixer or blender, add the curd and the required amount of water and blend until smooth.
Add salt, the chopped coriander leaves, and ginger; blend again and pour the spiced buttermilk into serving glasses.
Serve the spiced buttermilk with coriander and ginger alongside palak dal, Kalyana Veetu Senai curry, and steamed rice.

title: Vermicelli & Oats Kheer Recipe
instructions: Soak the raisins in water.
Dry roast the oats in a wok or heavy-bottomed pan, then transfer them to a small bowl.
In the same pan, add ghee and roast the cashew nuts until golden brown, then set aside.
Boil the milk in a saucepan, add vermicelli and stir continuously for about 5-6 minutes; lower the heat and let the vermicelli cook in the milk.
Add the roasted oats, soaked raisins, sugar, and cardamom powder to the cooked vermicelli; stir well until the kheer thickens.
If the kheer is too thick, add a little water to adjust consistency; check and adjust sugar and flavors as needed, then top with roasted cashew nuts.
Serve the Vermicelli & Oats Kheer.

title: Vazhaithandu Pachadi Recipe - Banana Stem Raita
ingredients: 1 cup Banana Stem, cut into small dices (with outer thick skin removed)
instructions: Whisk the yogurt with salt.
Add the diced banana stem to the whisked yogurt and set aside.

Heat 1/2 teaspoon of oil in a small pan; add mustard seeds and split white urad dal. Allow the seeds to crackle and sauté until the dal turns brown. Then add the green chillies and curry leaves and stir for a few seconds.
Add the tempered seasoning to the banana stem yogurt mixture and stir well. Adjust salt to taste.
The Vazhaithandu Pachadi is now ready to be served.
Serve the Vazhaithandu Pachadi with steamed rice and mixed vegetable sambar for a weekday meal.

title: Whole Moong Dal Vada Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Whole Moong Dal Vada Recipe, soak the moong and chana dal in warm water in a bowl for at least 5 to 6 hours or overnight.
Once the dal has soaked well, drain the water and grind the dal using very little water to make a coarse thick vada batter.
Transfer the Whole Moong Dal Vada batter to a mixing bowl. Add chopped onions, chili's, ginger-garlic paste, asafoetida and salt to taste. Mix well to combine and allow it rest for 10 minutes.

Heat oil for deep frying in a deep frying pan. Once oil is hot, make small balls of the Moong Dal Vada batter and drop in the hot oil carefully. Deep fry the vadas on medium heat till the moong dal vadas turns golden brown and crispy.
Once done, transfer the moong dal vada onto a plate with an oil absorbent paper and drain the excess oil using Serve warm.
Serve the Moong Dal Vada with Coconut Chutney and Green Chutney as a evening tea time snack, for a weekend breakfast or as an appetizer for parties.

title: Sooji Halwa Breakfast Bowl Recipe
ingredients: Mixed fruits (figs, chopped bananas, pomegranate & Kiwi)
instructions: Get all the ingredients ready.
Heat ghee in a saucepan or kadai. Once hot, add semolina (sooji) and roast it on low heat till you get a nutty aroma.
Add cardamom powder, cashews and almonds. Mix well.
Add water (about 1-1/4 cup for 1/2 cup semolina) and cane sugar together and mix well. Adjust water if needed to maintain a thick porridge consistency.
Switch off the heat once the halwa is nicely cooked and the semolina has reached its optimal cooked size.
Serve with a lot of fruits such as coconut slices, banana, fresh figs, pomegranate and kiwi.
Garnish with slivered almonds and some cashews.
Optionally serve with turmeric milk (Haldi Doodh) and boiled eggs for a complete breakfast.

title: Till Wale Aloo Recipe - Sesame Potato Sabzi
ingredients: 3 Potato (Aloo), boiled, peeled and cut into cubes
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Once the oil is hot, add ginger and green chillies. Make sure you don't burn them.
After a minute, add sesame seeds and sauté for a while. Add potatoes and toss for about 2 minutes.
Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala and salt to taste. Sauté for 3-4 minutes on low flame.
Add tamarind chutney, mix well and cook for one more minute. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve Till Wale Aloo along with Gujarati Dal, Roti and Kachumber Salad for a weekday meal.

title: Pheki Mathri Recipe - Crispy Fried Savoury Fritters
instructions: To begin making the Pheki Mathai Recipe, first mix the dry ingredients - maida and sooji together.
Add the ghee to the mixture and rub between your fingers till the dough turns crumbly and resembles breadcrumbs.
Gradually add warm water, little at a time, while bringing the dough together into a ball. Knead for 3-4 minutes till the dough stops sticking and comes together into a neat ball.
Cover with a muslin cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, divide the dough into 8 equal parts. Make balls and keep aside for 5 minutes.
Now roll the mathris out by rolling each ball into a disc about 1/4 inch thick and 5-6 inch diameter. Poke the rolled out mathri with fork or knife so that it doesn't fluff up while frying.
Next, to deep fry the mathri, heat sufficient oil in a kadai.
Fry the mathris for 2-3 minutes on each side till golden brown. Remove from the oil with a slotted spoon and keep aside to cool.
Allow the mathris to cool completely, and then store them in an airtight container.
Serve Pheki Mathri Recipe as a tea time snack along with Aam Ka Achaar Recipe and a hot cup of Masala Chai.

title: Sukha Mutton Vindaloo Recipe
ingredients: 750 grams Lamb, boneless, cut into small pieces
instructions: To begin making the Sukha Mutton Vindaloo recipe, soak the black pepper, cloves, red chili, cumin seeds, ginger garlic in Sugarcane vinegar for at least half an hour.
Grind these soaked spices into a fine paste. Apply the paste, turmeric powder, lemon juice and salt to the mutton pieces.
Marinate for at least 6 hours or over night.
Cook the marinated mutton in a pressure cooker for 4-5 whistles and release the pressure naturally.
Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add the cinnamon stick and add the onion paste.
Fry till the onions translucent brown in color then add the cooked mutton pieces, brown sugar and cook for few minutes till it is dry and attains a beautiful golden brown colour.
Serve Sukha Mutton Vindaloo as a side dish along with Goan Raw Banana Sabzi Recipe, Goan Chana Ros Recipe (White Peas Curry) and Steamed Rice for a Goan Style weekend meal.

title: Thulli Recipe (Broken Wheat Halwa)
instructions: Mix lukewarm milk and saffron in a small bowl and keep it aside.
In a heavy bottom cooking vessel, add 1 tablespoon of ghee and fry cashews on low flame until they turn light brown. Turn off the flame and set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining ghee and fry broken wheat until lightly coloured on low flame. Set it aside.
Add water, fennel seeds, milk+saffron mixture and cardamom powder to the pan. Stir and allow it to boil.
Lower the flame and start adding the broken wheat by continuously stirring to avoid lumps. Cook till broken wheat is completely cooked.
Add sugar to the mixture and stir. Cook until the sugar dissolves. Garnish with fried cashews and serve hot or at room temperature.
Serve Thulli as a dessert after your everyday meal of Dal Tadka, Makai Wali Bhindi and Phulka.

title: Matar Ki Puri (Crispy Puffed Indian Bread With Peas)
instructions: To begin making Matar Ki Puri, first prepare the dough.
Mash the green peas lightly with your hands, in a mixing bowl.
Add flour, chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, mint and salt to it.
Knead together with little water at a time to form a smooth, soft dough.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a kadhai for frying puris.
Take a lime sized ball of dough and roll it out into a circle which is two and a half inch in diameter. Roll out the remaining dough into similar puris.
When the oil is hot, slip the puris in one by one pressing down gently so they puff up. Flip them to make them brown on either side.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on kitchen paper and serve immediately with Tamatari Aloo, Aloo Bhey Ki Sabzi or Dubki Waley Aloo.

title: Buckwheat Cracker Recipe
instructions: To begin making Buckwheat Cracker Recipe, mix the buckwheat flour with oil, salt, sugar, chilli flakes, mixed herbs, flax seeds and roasted sesame in a large mixing bowl.
The texture should look like breadcrumbs. Add more oil if required to get the right texture.
Add ice cold water little by little so that you have a good, uniform, and a non sticky dough. Keep it aside for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile preheat Oven at 180 c for 10 minutes.
Roll out the dough on one sheet of parchment paper. Roll as thinly as you can manage.
Using a pizza cutter, cut the dough into squares or rectangles. Make some pricks using a fork.
Bake for 10-15 minutes at 180 C or until browning and crispy. Be careful not to overbake or the Buckwheat crackers will burn. Keep checking after every few minutes.
Once done remove the baking tray from the oven, cool down the buckwheat crackers and serve.
Serve Buckwheat Crackers during tea time with a Tomato and Sunflower Seed Dip Recipe and Cinnamon Spiced Orange Iced Tea Recipe.

title: Lauki Kheer Recipe - Bottle Gourd Pudding
ingredients: 250 grams Bottle gourd (lauki), peeled, de-seeded, washed and grated
instructions: Boil milk in a heavy bottomed pan on medium heat. Bring to a boil, then turn heat to low and simmer until reduced to half its quantity.
When the milk is almost condensed, add saffron, cardamom, almonds, and sugar. Stir well and continue simmering until further reduced.
Stir the milk occasionally while boiling to prevent burning and scrape the sides. Once done, set the milk aside.
Heat ghee in another heavy bottomed pan, add the grated lauki, and sauté on medium heat until the lauki becomes soft and tender.

Combine the cooked lauki with the condensed milk and simmer for another 10 minutes until the flavors meld and the kheer thickens. Turn off heat and transfer to a serving bowl; it will thicken further as it cools.
Garnish the lauki kheer with chopped pistachios and serve chilled.

title: Beetroot Halwa Recipe (With Vegan Option)
ingredients: 2-3 teaspoons ghee or extra virgin coconut oil
1-1/2 cups almond milk or coconut milk (freshly extracted)
1/2 cup dates (adjust), soaked in warm water for 20 minutes
instructions: Soak the dates in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain and grind into a smooth paste using the soaking liquid if needed.
In a thick-bottomed pan, heat the ghee or coconut oil and sauté the grated beetroot for 3-5 minutes until fragrant.
Add almond milk (or coconut milk) and cook covered on low heat, stirring occasionally, until all the liquid evaporates (8-12 minutes).
Stir in the date paste and ground cardamom, mix well, and continue cooking on low heat until the mixture comes together and excess moisture is absorbed (5-8 minutes).
Top the beetroot halwa with sliced pistachios and serve warm or chilled.

title: Butter Coriander & Lemon Sweet Corn Recipe
instructions: Get all the ingredients ready.
Steam the corn using a steamer along with a pinch of salt. Once done, place it in a mixing bowl.

Melt butter along with the coriander and add it to the sweet corn. Add the remaining ingredients: green chilli, chaat masala powder, red chilli powder, and lemon juice. Toss the sweet corn well with the spices and lemon juice. Check the salt and tanginess and adjust to suit your taste.
Serve the Butter Coriander & Lemon Sweet Corn warm.
Serve as an evening tea time snack along with Masala Chai or as an afternoon snack for kids.

title: Coconut Rice Pulao With Coconut Cream Recipe
instructions: Wash and clean the basmati rice 2-3 times, then soak for 30 minutes.
Blend coconut cream with 2 cups of water in a mixer/blender until smooth to make coconut milk; set aside (skip if using ready coconut milk).
Drain the soaked rice and add it to an electric rice cooker; add the coconut milk (or use a pressure cooker/Open container).
In a small pan, heat oil or ghee, then add bay leaf, cardamom pods, cloves, and black peppercorns; sauté on low heat until aromatic.
Add cumin seeds; when they stop sizzling, add grated ginger and sauté for 2 minutes to remove raw smell.
Add chopped carrots and green peas; sauté on medium heat for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer the carrot‑pea mixture to the rice cooker, add water as needed, cover, and cook until the rice is done.
For tempering, heat 2 teaspoons of ghee or oil in a small pan, sauté cashews and coconut slices for 2 minutes on low heat, then mix this tempering into the cooked rice.
Serve the coconut rice pulao with Cabbage Onion Vada and Vegetable Stew for a comforting lunch.

title: Mango Sago Kheer Recipe - Sabudana Kheer With Mangoes
ingredients: 1/2 cup nylon sabakki, soaked in water for 20 minutes
instructions: Wash and soak the nylon sabudana in water for 20 minutes.
In a pressure cooker, combine the drained sabudana with 1/2 cup water and 1/2 cup milk, close the lid and pressure cook for 3 whistles; then turn off the flame and let the pressure release naturally.
After the pressure releases, open the cooker, add the sugar and the remaining milk, and mix well until the sugar melts with the residual heat.
Observe that the sabudana is well cooked and the kheer is thick; mix well and refrigerate to cool for a couple of hours. If it becomes too thick, add cream or extra milk and stir to combine.
While the kheer is chilling, peel the mangoes and mash them by hand in a bowl to make a chunky fresh mango puree.
To assemble, place the chilled sabudana kheer in a serving glass, gradually mix in the mango puree, and garnish with slivered almonds.
Serve the Mango Sago Kheer as a dessert.

title: Vegan Carrot Halwa Ice Cream Recipe
instructions: Prepare the recipe by chopping and grating the ingredients and extracting the coconut milk required.
Mix shredded carrot, coconut milk, and water in a thick-bottom pan. On low to medium heat, bring the mixture to a boil, then simmer.
When the mixture starts to reduce, add sugar, cardamom powder, and the chopped pistachios and cashews. Stir well and continue to simmer.
Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking as the liquid reduces and thickens.
Switch off the flame when completely cooked and set the vegan carrot halwa aside to cool.
Transfer the mixture into a freezer-safe container, layer the surface with parchment paper, press gently, seal with a lid, and freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight until firm.
To serve, remove from the freezer, scoop into a bowl, and garnish with additional chopped nuts, raisins, or tender coconut slices.

title: Moong Dal Methi Ki Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Green Moong Dal (Split), soaked for 3 hours
2 cups Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), finely chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a kadhai and add cumin seeds and allow it to crackle.
Add green chillies and hing and let it cook for a few seconds.
Add onion and fry until it becomes soft and pinkish.
Add ginger, sliced tomato and cook on high flame for 2 minutes or until the tomatoes get soft.
Add soaked and drained moong dal, turmeric, coriander powder and sauté well for a minute.
Add half cup of water and salt and mix everything properly.
Cover and cook the dal for 7 to 8 minutes or until the dal is cooked well and the water is dried up (Do not overcook or it will get mushy).
Add methi and sauté on high heat for 2 to 3 minutes (Do not cover and cook). After 2 to 3 minutes, it is ready to be served.
Serve Methi Moong Dal Sabzi with phulkas, jeera rice and Rajasthani dal for a delicious meal.

title: Doodhi Sabudana Kheer Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Sabudana (Tapioca Pearls), soaked for 2 hours
instructions: Wash the rice and soak it in water for at least an hour; meanwhile grate the lauki/doodhi.
In a large saucepan, bring the milk to a boil.
Grind the soaked rice in a mixer grinder with a little water, if needed, to a fine paste.
Add the rice paste to the boiling milk and let it cook over simmered heat.
In a kadai, while the rice is cooking in the milk, add ghee and the grated doodhi; sauté until the doodhi releases its water, becomes cooked and translucent, then switch off heat.
When the rice paste is about half‑cooked, add the sautéed lauki/doodhi to the milk mixture and stir.
Continue stirring and boil on medium flame until the milk thickens substantially, which may take about an hour.
Once the milk has thickened, add sugar, cardamom powder, khoya, and ground pistachios; cook for roughly 10 more minutes.
Serve the Doodhi Sabudana Kheer as a dessert, optionally garnished with slivered almonds and accompanied by Paneer Kolhapuri, Palak Raita, or Tawa Paratha.

title: Masala Couscous Pulao Recipe
ingredients: Few coriander (dhania) leaves, chopped for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaf and sauté for about 30 seconds.
Add sliced onions and cook until they become soft and transparent.
Add ginger garlic paste and sauté for 2 minutes. Then add carrots, green peas, red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, and salt; sauté for another 5 minutes.
Add 4 cups of water and bring to a boil. Once boiling, add mint leaves and couscous.
Reduce heat and simmer until the water is completely absorbed. If the couscous is still firm, add a cup of hot water and continue cooking.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve.
Optionally serve the Masala Couscous Pulao with beetroot raita, lauki raita, or any raita of your choice, along with a roasted papad.

title: Matar Masala Recipe - Peas In Onion Tomato Gravy
ingredients: pinch kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), generous pinch
1-2 teaspoons almond milk (badam milk) or water
instructions: Steam the peas until cooked and set aside.
In a preheated kadai, add oil, then add onions, ginger, garlic, and green chilies and sauté until onions turn translucent.
Add finely chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy, then turn off the heat.
Let the mixture cool, then blend the tomato‑onion mixture in a mixer grinder to a smooth paste and set aside.
Blend cashew nuts with almond milk or water into a thick paste for the cashew cream and set aside.
In a wok or kadhai, add the remaining oil, add cumin seeds and let them splutter, then add the ground onion‑tomato paste and cook until the oil separates from the sides of the pan.
Add all the spice powders, mix well, and cook for another 3 minutes on medium flame.
Add the cooked green peas, continue to cook for another 5 minutes on low flame, season with salt and add kasuri methi, mixing well.
Stir in the cashew cream, mix, and let it bubble for 2–3 minutes on low heat until the masala thickens.
Sprinkle garam masala, mix, turn off the heat, and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve the matar masala with phulka, pudina rice, and tomato onion cucumber raita.

title: Andey Ki Kheer Recipe - Egg White Kheer
ingredients: Dry Fruits, a handful of dry fruits (almonds, pista, cashews, raisins)
instructions: To begin making Andey Ki Kheer (Egg White Kheer) Recipe, take a sauce pan and add milk and cardamom powder to it. Boil it to reduce it to half its initial amount. It takes 30 minutes at medium flame.
Meanwhile, separate the egg yolk from the eggs and keep aside.
Once the milk reduces to half, add all the chopped dry fruits like almonds, pistachios and cashew nuts. Do not add raisins at this point since it may sour the milk causing it to curdle.

Add sugar and keep stirring till the sugar gets completely dissolved. This may cause a thinning effect on milk. Hence, keep stirring and let the mixture boil again until reduced to a creamy consistency.
Once we add sugar the milk may get thin again, so keep stirring and boil the milk till it acquires a thick and creamy consistency.
Take the egg whites in a separate bowl and beat them till frothy.
With the help of a spoon gradually add beaten egg white into the boiling milk on low flame, stirring.

Beat the remaining egg white again to make froth. Again with a spoon take the frothing egg white and add it to the milk, stirring. Repeat the process till all the egg white is spooned into the saucepan. The egg white froth appears like little dumplings in milk. Keep stirring.
Keep the flame low and let the dumplings cook well. Allow the milk to cook till it becomes golden in color and gets a creamy texture.
Now add Kewda water into it. This gives a royal aroma to the kheer and eliminates the smell of eggs.
Now add in raisins and put off the flame.
Allow the Andey Ki Kheer (Egg White Kheer) to cool down to room temperature.
Refrigerate it for a couple of hours to enjoy the chilled Andey Ki Kheer or serve it warm.
Serve Andey Ki Kheer as a dessert after your delicious meal of Palak Dal, Sev Tamatar Ki Sabzi and Tawa Paratha.

title: WeetBix Halwa Recipe
instructions: If using almonds, soak them for 2 hours; otherwise skip this step.
Remove the skin from the almonds, then blend the nuts with saffron and less than 1/2 cup water to a smooth paste.
Take a microwave‑safe bowl, brush it with ghee, and crush the Weet Bix biscuits by hand.
Add 1 teaspoon ghee to the crushed biscuits, mix well, and microwave for 30 seconds; stir again.
Microwave for another 30 seconds, stir, and if needed repeat another 30‑second interval, ensuring the total time does not exceed 1.5 minutes.
Add the nut‑saffron paste, any remaining water, palm sugar, and cardamom to the biscuits; mix thoroughly as the water is quickly absorbed.
Add 1 teaspoon ghee on top, then microwave for a total of 4 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes and adjusting sweetness if desired.
After the 4 minutes, remove from the microwave and stir in another teaspoon of ghee; the halwa will thicken in about 5 minutes from residual heat.
Serve the halwa hot, warm, or cold; the consistency remains the same.
Enjoy the Weet Bix Halwa as a dessert after a festive Diwali meal or with a light dinner such as Paneer Pav Bhaji.

title: Tamter Wangun Recipe
instructions: Wash brinjals/eggplants, cut them lengthwise, and allow the pieces to air dry.
Heat a non-stick kadai, add oil, and fry the brinjal pieces until slightly brown.
Chop the tomatoes and set aside; heat some oil in the same pan.
When the oil is hot, add cumin seeds and fry until brownish, then add asafoetida.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy.
Stir in dry ginger powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and salt; mix well.
Simmer the tomato mixture until oil separates from the gravy.
Add the fried eggplants to the tomato base and toss so they are fully coated with the spicy mixture.
Sprinkle additional salt as needed.
Cook the eggplant in the tomato base for about 3 minutes with the lid off.
Turn off the flame and serve.

title: Paal Payasam Recipe - Rice Kheer/Pudding
ingredients: 2 liter Milk (low fat or full cream for richer texture)
instructions: Wash the rice and dry it with a cloth.
Heat ghee in a heavy‑bottomed saucepan on low heat, add the rice and roast on medium heat until a lightly roasted aroma develops, taking care not to brown the rice.
Add the milk to the roasted rice, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer the milk and rice on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the milk reduces to about half its original volume and the rice is fully cooked.
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves; at this point you may add saffron and nuts if desired, and serve hot or cold.
Serve the Paal Payasam as a comforting dessert.

title: Moong Dal Potli Recipe - With Baked Option
instructions: Take a big bowl, add refined flour, clarified butter and salt to it. Mix well, add enough clarified butter to get a crumb-like texture, then add water a little at a time and knead the dough; cover and keep aside for 30 minutes.
Coarsely grind the soaked moong dal without adding any water and set aside.

Heat oil in a preheated nonstick pan, add hing, red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, amchur powder and fennel seeds; mix, then quickly add chopped almonds, raisins and ground moong dal. Stir continuously and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes until well combined.
Turn off the heat and transfer the stuffing mixture into a bowl.
Divide the dough into ten equal portions, roll into balls, flatten slightly into discs, then roll out the discs into small poori-sized sheets and apply a little water on the edges.
Place 2 teaspoons of the moong dal stuffing in the center of each disc, form pleats and bring the edges together to form a pouch.
Heat oil in a kadai or deep pan and fry the potlis over medium heat until golden brown; drain on a kitchen towel.
For a healthier option, brush each potli with oil, arrange them 2 cm apart on a baking tray and bake in a pre‑heated oven at 180 °C for 18‑20 minutes or until crisp and done.
Serve the Moong Dal Potli as starters or during tea time with khajoor imli chutney or dhaniya pudina chutney and Masala Chai.

title: Pumpkin Halwa (Kaddu Ka Halwa) Recipe
ingredients: 3 cups Kaddu (Parangikai/ Pumpkin), red one, peeled and grated
instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a kadhai.
When ghee gets heated, add the raisins. After the raisins puff, remove them from the kadhai and keep them on a separate plate.
In the same kadhai, add the other chopped dry fruits and roast them. Keep them in the same plate where the raisins are kept.
Add 3 more tablespoons ghee to the same kadhai. Add the grated pumpkin and fry it on low flame till the raw smell goes away.
Add milk and let the pumpkin get cooked for some time. Add khoya and mix everything well.
Keep stirring in between to avoid it sticking to the bottom of the kadhai. After some time, the halwa will start thickening. Add sugar and mix well.
Keep stirring continuously when the halwa starts to thicken, add the dry fruits.
Crush the cardamom pods with a mortar and pestle, discard the peels.
Sprinkle the cardamom powder on the halwa and mix well. When the halwa starts leaving the sides of the kadhai, it is done and ready to be served.
Serve Pumpkin Halwa as a dessert to your friends and family during Holi lunch or dinner.

title: Lemongrass Coconut Rice Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup rice, washed and soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add ginger and vegetables and saute for a minute.
Add the rice and stir well for a few seconds.
Add the coconut milk, water, lemongrass stalk, peppercorns and salt to the rice, and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover the pan and cook until the liquid evaporates and the rice is tender.
Turn off the heat and let the lemongrass rice stand for 8-10 minutes.
Gently toss the rice and discard the lemongrass stalks.
Serve the lemongrass coconut rice with a simple vegetarian Thai green curry and mushroom bok choy stir fry.

title: Chocolate Peda Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Ghee (to rub it in hands before shaping peda)
instructions: Melt the butter in a non-stick pan on low heat, then switch off the heat and add milk powder and dark cocoa powder.
Mix the ingredients well with a spatula, add the condensed milk, turn the heat back on and keep it on a low flame.
Stir the mixture, slowly add milk and cardamom powder, and continue stirring for about 10-12 minutes.
When the chocolate mixture starts to leave the sides of the pan, turn off the flame and transfer it to a plate greased with ghee.
Rub your hands with a tablespoon of ghee and shape the pedas.
Allow the pedas to set; they will be sticky initially and will hold their shape after 3-4 hours.
Make an impression in the centre of each peda with your thumb and fill it with chopped pistachios.
Serve Chocolate Peda as a sweet dish during special occasions and festivals.

title: Red Beans And Oats Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Instant Oats (Oatmeal), more to dust
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
Oil, for shallow frying the cutlets
instructions: To begin making the Red beans and Oat Cutlet Recipe, first clean, wash and soak red kidney beans in water overnight or for at least 7-8 hours.
Make powder of oats in grinder. Keep aside until required.
In a pan boil 1 cup of water, add soy granules and bring to a boil. Soy granules will puff up after one boil; turn off the heat, drain the soy granules using a colander and keep aside.

Once red kidney beans are soaked, in a pressure cooker add beans along with 1 cup of soaked water, add salt, stir, cover and place its weight on. Cook until you hear 4-5 whistles, then turn the heat to low and simmer for another 15 minutes before turning off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, open the cooker and drain beans in a colander, keeping them until all excess water is drained off.

In a large bowl add boiled beans, powdered oats (reserving 2 tablespoons for dusting), cooked soy granules, onion, salt, coriander leaves, red chili powder, cumin powder and salt to taste. Mix nicely with dry fingers.
Divide the mixture into equal portions, grease your palms and shape each portion into a flat round of about 1/2 inch thickness. Place the cutlets on a tray or plate and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, remove the cutlets from the fridge and dust with the reserved 2 tablespoons of powdered oats.
Heat a heavy-bottomed frying pan over medium heat. Place the oat‑coated cutlets on the pan and drizzle a teaspoon of oil over each cutlet.
Shallow‑fry each cutlet until golden brown on both sides, then drain on absorbent paper with a slotted spoon.
Serve Red Beans and Oats Cutlet as an evening snack with green chutney and hot ginger cardamom chai.

title: Habshi Halwa Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Lemon Salt, mixed in 2 teaspoon water
instructions: To begin making Habshi Halwa, first bring the milk to a boil in a heavy bottomed pan or kadhai.
Once boiled turn off the heat and add lemon salt mixed with water. Cover the milk and allow it to sit for 5 minutes. This is the time the milk will take to curdle.

When you open the lid, you should find the milk curdled. Now, put the pan back on the heat and cook the curdled mixture on medium-high heat for about 30-40 minutes until half of the whey (or the water that has separated) has evaporated.
Next add the sugar and stir well until it has dissolved completely. Add white vinegar and cook for 8 to 10 minutes.

Then, add the cocoa powder and maida along with ghee. This will make the mixture glossy. Continue to stir and once the halwa starts to leave the sides of the pan, sprinkle the Elaichi powder and saffron strands over it. Mix well till combined.
Lastly add the slivered almonds and mix well.

To set the Habshi Halwa, grease a large plate with a rim, with ghee. Transfer the cooked halwa to it and press it evenly into a slab, with your fingers. Allow it to cool down completely and turn firm. Slice it.
Serve Habshi Halwa as a dessert along with Paal Payasam during a festive lunch.

title: Tangy Tamarind Pumpkin Curry Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Kaddu (Parangikai/ Pumpkin), cut into cubed
instructions: To prepare Tangy Tamarind Pumpkin Curry Recipe, heat oil in a deep pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds and let it splutter.
Add chopped onion, ginger garlic paste, green chillies, curry leaves and saute it till onion turns golden in colour.
Add red chilli powder, coriander powder and turmeric powder. Mix everything well for a minute and add pumpkin.
Sprinkle salt over pumpkin and add water. Cover the lid and cook it 3-4 minutes.
After 3-4 minutes, check if pumpkin is properly cooked or not; if it is not, then let it cook for another minute.
If it is cooked then add tamarind paste, you can mix tamarind paste in a bowl with little water and add it to the pumpkin curry.
Add jaggery, cook uncovered for 1-2 minutes more and make sure that all the water is absorbed.
Serve Tangy Tamarind Pumpkin Curry Recipe with chapati, Spicy yogurt chapati or paratha.

title: Homemade Chikoo Ice Cream Recipe
ingredients: 250 grams Fresh cream (little more than 1/2 cup)
1 1/2 cups Milk (full fat milk is required)
instructions: Clean, peel, and deseed the chikoos/sapotas.
Blend the fruit to make a smooth pulp with a hand blender or mixer grinder and set aside.
In a large steel vessel, add the fresh cream, milk powder, sugar, and milk; whisk with a hand whisk until no lumps remain.
Add the chikoo pulp and whisk with a mixer for 1 minute until fully incorporated; taste and adjust sweetness if needed.
Transfer the mixture to an airtight container, let it set for 2 hours to achieve a soft‑serve consistency, then churn in a mixer for 2‑3 minutes and return to the airtight container.
Refreeze the ice cream for 12‑15 hours at the freezer's maximum temperature to prevent crystallization.
Serve the homemade chikoo ice cream with a few pieces of fresh chikoos.

title: Milk Peda Recipe
instructions: Soak saffron in milk for 10 to 15 minutes or refrigerate overnight for better colour results.
Heat ghee in a kadai and add condensed milk to it, allowing it to cook on low flame until it comes to a boil.
Add powdered milk and stir vigorously to avoid forming lumps; break any lumps for a smooth finish.
Continue stirring continuously until the mixture starts to thicken.
Add the saffron‑infused milk and cardamom powder, then stir nicely.
The mixture will loosen; keep stirring until it thickens again.
Gradually the mixture will gather and fold up, leaving the sides of the pan.
Carefully pinch a lime‑size ball and roll it between greased palms, being cautious as it may be hot.
If the mixture forms a dough and rolls into a smooth ball, it is ready; if sticky, stir and cook on low heat for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn off the gas and remove the pan from the stove; set aside to cool.
When warm, grease your hands with ghee, pinch a lime‑sized ball, roll and flatten it into a disc.
Make impressions with a flower stencil or a simple dimple in the centre using your index finger.
Garnish/decorate with chopped pistachios (optional) or saffron strands.
Serve Milk Peda to friends and family during festivals and special occasions.

title: Red Kidney Beans Chocolate Barfi Recipe
instructions: Soak red kidney beans for 5 to 6 hours.
Transfer red kidney beans to a mixer and make a smooth paste, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons water if needed.
Heat clarified butter (ghee) in a nonstick pan, add the red kidney beans paste, mix constantly and cook on low‑medium flame.
Roast the beans until the color changes and ghee starts separating; this takes about 25 minutes.
Roast milk powder in a nonstick pan on low flame, then mix it into the red kidney beans mixture.
Prepare sugar syrup by cooking sugar with 1 cup beetroot juice in a pan for 4 minutes.
Add the sugar syrup to the red kidney beans halwa mixture, cook on low flame and stir constantly until it thickens, then switch off the heat.
Add cardamom powder, vanilla extract, and cocoa powder; mix well and transfer the mixture onto a greased plate, pressing gently.
Allow the fudge/barfi to set for 2 hours, then garnish with silver leaves and cut into square pieces.
Store the barfi in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 8 to 10 days.
Serve the Red Kidney Beans Barfi with other sweets for festivals.

title: Jowar Atta Roti Recipe - Sorghum Wheat Phulka Recipe
instructions: Begin making the Jowar Atta Roti/Phulka by gathering all the ingredients.

In a large mixing bowl, combine jowar flour, whole wheat flour, and salt; add water gradually to knead a smooth dough, then drizzle oil and knead until the dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl and is smooth.
Divide the dough into lemon-sized portions, dust each with wheat flour, and roll into 5-6 inch diameter circles.
Place the rolled dough on a preheated skillet and cook for a few seconds until small bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip the roti, cook a few more seconds, then place it over an open flame; cook until it puffs up, flipping as needed, until brown spots appear on both sides and the roti is fully cooked.
Transfer the cooked roti to a serving plate, drizzle ghee around it, and serve immediately.
Serve the Jowar Atta Roti with Panchmel Dal, Aloo Baingan Ki Sabzi, and Satvik Carrot Sprout Salad for a complete meal.

title: Sweet and Spicy Raw Mango Chutney Recipe
instructions: Heat 1/2 cup of water in a pressure cooker on medium heat; stir in the mangoes along with the turmeric powder, ginger, cumin seeds, red chilli powder and salt.
Cover the pressure cooker and pressure cook the raw mango chutney for 2 whistles and turn off the heat.
Once done, add lemon juice and simmer the raw mango chutney for a couple of more minutes.
Turn off heat and allow the sweet and spicy raw mango chutney to cool completely and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Serve the chutney alongside vegetables and breads such as paratha, bajra na rotla, thepla, or as a spread on oven‑toasted bread.

title: Filter Coffee Choco Peda Recipe - Microwave Method
instructions: Prepare coffee decoction: add 5 tablespoons coffee powder to a coffee filter, press, add hot water, and let brew for about 15 minutes.
In a microwave‑safe bowl, combine 4 tablespoons ghee, milk powder, and condensed milk; mix well.
Microwave the mixture for 1 minute, then remove and stir.
Add cocoa powder, 1 tablespoon of the prepared coffee decoction, and 30 ml water to the bowl; mix.
Microwave for another 1 minute; the mixture will double in volume. Stir well and adjust coffee strength if desired.
Repeat microwaving two more times, heating for 1 minute each time with stirring in between.
After the fourth minute, add 1 tablespoon ghee and mix well.
Microwave for 1 additional minute; the mixture will be soft, not fully set. Stir and allow it to cool for 6–10 minutes until handleable.
Grease your palms with ghee and roll the softened mixture into pedas; optionally stuff with mixed nuts or almonds.
Serve the filter coffee choco pedas at festivals or family gatherings.
Enjoy!

title: Saffron Milk Masala Recipe
instructions: Grind the pistachios, chironji, and almonds separately into a coarsely ground powder.
Grind the cardamom together with the sugar separately, then mix all the dry fruit powders and add saffron strands to create the masala.
Mix the masala with milk and enjoy it with or without additional sugar, optionally serving with snacks like baked banana chips or cheese crackers.

title: Strawberry And Sooji Halwa Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mixed nuts , sliced, for garnishing (I used almonds & cashewnuts)
instructions: We begin making Strawberry And Sooji Halwa Recipe with heating ghee in a kadai.
Once the ghee melts, add semolina and roast till it starts giving a nice aroma and the color changes to light golden brown. You can use less ghee to roast semolina, too.
Now add the hot boiling water (or milk if using) slowly and keep stirring the halwa.
Add sugar and cardamom powder and mix well.
Once the sugar mixes completely, cover the kadai and let the halwa simmer for 2 more minutes.
Now add strawberry puree and cook for another 2 minutes or till done.
Transfer the halwa into a serving bowl and garnish with the sliced almonds and cashewnuts.
Halwa is ready to serve. Serve Strawberry And Sooji Halwa Recipe as a party dessert along with Gujarati Badshahi Pulao Recipe - A Rich Preparation Of Rice, Vegetables, Nuts And Spices.

title: Besan & Atta Ki Roti Recipe (Chickpea Flatbread)
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Gather all the ingredients and set them aside.

Combine all the ingredients (except the oil or ghee) in a large mixing bowl. Add a little water gradually and knead to form a smooth dough. Drizzle a teaspoon of oil over the dough and knead for a couple of minutes until smooth and firm, then divide the dough into 10 portions.
Preheat a roti tawa (griddle) over medium heat.
Roll each dough portion into a thin circle, dusting with flour as needed; the thickness depends on how thin you can roll it.
Place the rolled roti on the hot tawa and cook for a few seconds until air bubbles appear, then flip. Smear ghee or oil on the roti and cook both sides until browned and lightly crisp.
