Remove the cooked roti from the tawa and repeat the process with the remaining dough portions.
Serve the Besan & Atta Ki Roti with Baingan Bharta, Sweet & Spicy Tomato Chutney, and Kachumber Salad.

title: Aam Peda Recipe - Delicious Mango Peda Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Ghee (more for greasing palms and plate)
instructions: To begin making Aam Peda Recipe - Mango Peda Recipe, get all the ingredients ready and handy. Prepare cornstarch paste by mixing in a tablespoon of cornstarch in a tablespoon of cold water.
Grease a plate with some ghee and keep aside.
In a big bowl, mix together condensed milk and milk powder until smooth paste.
Add 2 tablespoons melted ghee. Mix again and keep aside.
Take mango puree in a non stick saucepan kept on medium heat. Add the prepared corn starch paste, the condensed milk mixture in the mango puree and mix well.
Let it cook on medium high heat until the mango peda mixture thickens.
Keep scraping the bottom and the sides of the pan.
After about 10 minutes, add cardamom powder and continue cooking till the mango peda mixture starts leaving the pan and forms into a dough. Once done turn off the heat.
Remove the Mango Peda on a greased plate and let the mixture cool down for about 5 minutes or till you can handle the hot peda mixture.
After about 5 minutes, grease your palms with ghee and take a tablespoon of the aam peda mixture on your palm and shape up into a ball.

Press it a little to give it a disc shape and place on a plate. I have used my icing tip coupler to slightly press on these pedhas in order to make a design, but you can skip this step if you like them plain.
Repeat for all the amm peda and then you can just press 1 or 2 slit almonds on top of each aam peda.

Serve the Aam Peda Recipe - Mango Peda Recipe as a bite of dessert along with an Indian thali of Vegetable Bajji Recipe, Mirchi Ka Salan, Matar Paneer Kulcha, Sweet & Spicy Coriander Tadka Raita, and Baby Potatoes Pulao Recipe.

title: Crispy Oven Roasted Curried Chickpeas Recipe
instructions: Rinse the chickpeas and soak them in enough water overnight.
Drain and pressure cook the soaked chickpeas for 2 whistles, then let the pressure release naturally.
Drain the water, pat the chickpeas dry with a kitchen towel ensuring no moisture remains.
In a wide bowl, combine all the spice powders, salt, olive oil, and the chickpeas; toss well to coat evenly.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Spread the spiced chickpeas in a single layer on the prepared tray.
Roast in the oven for 45–55 minutes, checking after 30 minutes and continuing as needed until crunchy, being careful not to burn.
Remove from the oven, let cool completely, then serve.
Serve as an evening snack, optionally with cold coffee smoothie or masala chai.

title: Chole Aloo Tikki Chaat Recipe - An Indian Street Food Snack
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked and cooked
2 tablespoon Sev, for garnishing and crunch
instructions: Soak the chickpeas (chola) in water for 8–10 hours, then cook them with salt until soft; set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan, add cumin seeds, ginger and bay leaf; stir‑fry briefly until aromatic.
Add tomato puree and all spice‑mix ingredients (turmeric, amchur, garam masala, coriander powder, anardana, Kashmiri red chilli, black pepper, black salt); sauté until the mixture turns dark brown.
Add the cooked chickpeas, stir to coat with the masala, adjust salt and spices, cover and simmer on low heat for 20–30 minutes.
Continue simmering on low for about 30 minutes until the chickpeas are well coated and brown; taste and set aside.
In a large bowl mash boiled regular potatoes and boiled sweet potato together.
Add steamed green peas, grated ginger, chopped green chillies, chopped onion, green chutney, salt, and corn flour; mix thoroughly.
Shape the mixture into small discs about 1–1.5 inches in diameter.
Dust each disc with whole‑wheat bread crumbs, place on a baking sheet, drizzle with oil and bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes (or 15 minutes for lighter browning).
After about 15 minutes, remove the tikkis; for extra crispness, drizzle a little more oil and continue baking, or alternatively pan‑fry on a tawa with little oil until golden brown on both sides.
Optionally, shape the mixture into cylinders, breadcrumb, skewer and grill or bake for 15 minutes.
To assemble, place a hot aloo tikki on a platter, top with hot chana masala, sprinkle chopped green chillies and onions, add a spoon of green chutney and a spoon of date‑tamarind chutney.
Garnish with additional onions, chopped coriander leaves and sev; serve immediately.

title: Saffron Paneer Peda Recipe
instructions: Keep the paneer ready; you can use store-bought paneer or make it at home.
If needed, follow the Homemade Paneer Recipe to make fresh paneer.
Place the paneer in a mixing bowl and crumble it well using your fingers, then transfer the crumbled paneer to a mixer grinder.
Add saffron, cardamom powder, sugar, and water to the mixer‑grinder and grind everything together into a smooth paste.
Heat ghee in a heavy‑bottomed pan on medium‑low heat, transfer the paneer mixture from the mixer jar and cook it on low flame.
Add rose water and keep stirring continuously until everything comes together, leaving the sides of the pan.
Turn off the flame, allow the mixture to cool, and transfer it into a bowl.
Grease your hands with some ghee and knead the paneer mixture into a smooth dough without cracks.
Roll the dough flat using a rolling pin and cut into desired shapes for pedas; the paneer pedas are ready. Transfer to a platter.
Serve the Saffron Paneer Peda as a dessert or with snacks like Poha Chivda.

title: Soya Chunks Pepper Curry Recipe
ingredients: 12 pearl onions (sambar onions), peeled and halved
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a small saucepan.
Remove from heat, add the soy chunks and let them sit for about 10 minutes.
Drain the water from the soy chunks and squeeze out any excess moisture.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium flame; add garlic cloves and curry leaves and fry for a minute.
Add green chilies and fry for a minute, then add the chopped onions and cook until translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until mushy; then add sambar powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder and cook for a few minutes.
Add the soaked soy chunks and capsicum pieces to the mixture and combine well.
Add water and cook until the soy chunks are fully cooked and the curry reaches the desired consistency.
Season with salt, switch off the flame, and serve hot.
Serve the Soya Chunks Pepper Curry with tomato onion cucumber raita and tawa parathas.

title: Bajra Aloo Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), chopped finely
instructions: Add all the ingredients in a large bowl and mix everything well.
Gradually add warm water a little at a time and knead the dough until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough into equal-sized balls depending on the desired paratha size.
Dust each ball and roll out into a paratha to the desired thickness.
If rolling with a pin is difficult, use your hands to pat the dusted ball uniformly into a paratha.
Heat a griddle well, place the rolled paratha on it, and cook until brown spots appear, then flip and cook the other side.
Apply oil and fry both sides until cooked well.
Serve Bajra Aloo Paratha with Tomato Onion and Cucumber Raita and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Kala Chana Salad Recipe With Carrots, Cucumber & Tomatoes
instructions: Soak the black chickpeas (Kala Chana) in water overnight to make them soft.
Pressure cook the soaked kala chana with a little salt on medium heat for about 20 minutes until cooked through.
Allow the pressure to release naturally once cooking is done.
Drain the excess water from the cooked kala chana; reserve the water for other uses if desired.
Prepare the vegetables: grate the carrots, peel and chop the cucumber, chop the tomatoes, and finely chop the green chillies.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked kala chana, grated carrots, chopped cucumber, chopped tomatoes, green chillies, salt, chopped coriander leaves, and freshly squeezed lemon juice.
Stir well to mix all ingredients, adjust salt and spices to taste, and serve.
Serve the Kala Chana Salad alongside Palak Mushroom Makhani, Punjabi Kadhi, and Jeera Rice (Pulao) for a complete meal.

title: Bhindi Gosht Recipe-Okra With Meat In Coconut Gravy
instructions: To begin making the Bhindi Gosht recipe, heat half oil in pressure cooker, add onion to it and saute it till the onion turns translucent. Add ginger garlic paste, add all the spices to it and cook for few minutes.
Add the meat to the above mixture along with coconut milk and curry leaves cook till the meat is tender. Pressure cook till 15-20 minutes.
In another pan, add oil and sauté big chunks of okra till 3/4 is cooked. Drizzle some lemon juice on it and mix properly. When done keep it aside.
Open the pressure cooker and add tamarind pulp and okra. Mix everything well and let it cook for another 5-10 minutes till okra is completely cooked.
Serve Bhindi Gosht along with Tawa Paratha and Jeera Rice for your weekday meal.

title: Nariyal Ki Kheer Recipe - Coconut Pudding
instructions: Crush and soak the saffron strands in 1 teaspoon warm milk.
In a thick bottom pan, bring the rest of the milk to boil on medium heat, stirring continuously to avoid sticking, until the milk is reduced to half its original amount.
Add grated coconut to the milk and stir firmly until it starts boiling again.
Cook on low-medium heat for about 15-20 minutes or until the coconut is cooked well.
Add sugar, cardamom powder, saffron, almonds, cashews and pistachios. Stir well and cook for 5-7 minutes further, or till the nuts are cooked.
Garnish with some remaining dry fruits and serve warm or chilled.

title: Sweet Potato, Broccoli And Tofu Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Broccoli, cut into small florets
1 Sweet Potato, skin removed and cut into cubes
150 grams Tofu, cut into small cubes
instructions: Heat a saucepan with oil, add onions, ginger and garlic and sauté until softened.
Add the spice powders (jeera powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder), mix, then add tomatoes, green chillies, and a little salt.
Mash until the tomatoes are cooked and the raw smell disappears; add cashew nuts and sauté for 2 more minutes.
Cool the mixture and blend it with water in a mixer until smooth.
Heat a saucepan or kadai, add oil, and once hot add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add the sweet potato and cook until lightly soft, then add broccoli and tofu and toss for about 10 more minutes.
Stir in the masala paste, mix well, then add water and salt to reach desired consistency; simmer for 10 minutes and serve hot.
Serve the Sweet Potato, Broccoli and Tofu Curry with steamed rice, jeera rice, or peas pulao.

title: Masala Roasted Aloo Recipe
instructions: Wash the potatoes and par‑boil them in a pressure cooker for one or two whistles over medium heat; release the pressure, peel the boiled potatoes and set aside in a bowl.
In a cast‑iron skillet, dry‑roast the coriander seeds, fennel seeds, cumin seeds, dry red chilies, and black peppercorns for the spice mix until they are slightly browned and fragrant.
Turn off the heat, allow the roasted spices to cool a bit, then grind them into a fine powder; transfer the spice mix to a bowl and set aside.
Heat oil in a stir‑fry pan over medium heat and add cumin seeds and asafoetida; let them crackle.
Add the boiled baby potatoes to the pan along with the freshly ground spice mix, dry mango powder, and salt; stir to combine well.
Roast the potatoes until they turn crisp on the outside.
Garnish the Masala Roasted Aloo with freshly chopped coriander leaves and drizzle lemon juice just before serving.
Serve the Masala Roasted Aloo with Rajasthani Kadhi, Satvik Carrot Sprout Salad, and Phulka for an everyday meal.

title: Dry Fruit Halwa Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Dried Figs, dried, finely chopped
instructions: Pulse the nuts in the chopper to get a roughly chopped mixture. Keep the nuts aside.
Blend the finely chopped dates and figs with 1 tablespoon of milk and ghee until smooth.

Add ghee to a preheated pan and add the nuts and the dates‑and‑figs blend to the pan. Sauté the dry fruit halwa until well combined, about 4 to 5 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes until the mixture comes away from the sides of the pan. Turn off the heat.
Serve the dry fruit halwa as is, or with vanilla ice cream, or set it into a pan and cut into slices once chilled.
To set into a pan, pour and layer the dry fruit halwa mixture into the pan, smooth it well, and allow it to rest until completely cooled and set; refrigeration speeds up setting.
Cut the dry fruit halwa into equal squares and store in an airtight container.
Serve the dry fruit barfi for festivals or as a tea‑time snack.

title: Mirchi Pakodi Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped, as required
instructions: Mix the tamarind paste and jaggery in a bowl.
Make a slit in the green chillies and remove the seeds.
Add ajwain seeds, fennel seeds, roasted gram flour, red chilli powder, and salt to the tamarind‑jaggery mixture; mix well.
Stuff this mixture into the green chillies one by one and set aside.
Prepare the gram flour batter by combining gram flour, baking soda, turmeric powder, ajwain, and water to a thin, coat‑able consistency.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan.
Dip the stuffed chillies into the batter and fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Remove, let cool slightly, then cut each pakodi in half and place in a serving bowl.
Garnish with finely chopped onions, roasted peanuts, coriander leaves, lemon juice, and chaat masala powder.
Serve the Mirchi Pakodi hot as a snack.

title: Matar Mushroom Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup button mushrooms, diced (canned or store-bought fresh mushrooms)
1/2 teaspoon tomato ketchup (or sugar can be used)
1 tablespoon coriander (dhania) leaves, chopped, for garnishing
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds; let them splutter.
Add the chopped onions and fry them till light brown on medium heat.
Add ginger garlic paste and sauté it till cooked.
Stir in tomato puree and salt; cook for 2 minutes until combined.
Add coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and garam masala; sauté for about 2-3 minutes.
Add the green peas and mushrooms, mix well, and cook for another 5-6 minutes until the mushrooms' water evaporates.
Stir in kasuri methi and a little water; cook until the peas are tender.
Add fresh cream and mix well to combine.
Turn off the heat, transfer to a serving bowl, garnish with chopped coriander leaves, and serve.
Serve the Matar Mushroom Curry with whole wheat phulkas, tawa paratha, or any other flatbread.

title: Slow Cooker Winter Supper Stew Recipe
ingredients: 1 Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), cut into cubes
instructions: To begin making the Slow Cooker Winter Supper Stew recipe, first clean and cut all the vegetables. Keep it aside.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add bay leaf, pepper, garlic and ginger and let it cook for about a minute.
Add the vegetable stock and vegetables except capsicum, close the lid and cook for up to 2 whistles.
Open the lid, add capsicum, coriander leaves and adjust the seasoning. Let it cook for one more minute and switch off the gas. Serve hot.
Serve Slow Cooker Winter Supper Stew on its own along with toasted bread or Smoked Tofu and Grilled Vegetable Salad for a healthy meal.

title: Kesar Pista Lassi Recipe - Saffron & Pista Lassi Recipe
instructions: Add the curd, pistachios, saffron strands, fresh cream, and sugar (or honey) into a mixer grinder.
Blend until smooth or slightly chunky, according to personal preference.
Transfer the lassi to a serving glass, add a few ice cubes, garnish with additional saffron strands, and serve chilled.
Serve the Kesar Pista Lassi with Peshawari naan or Malai Kofta for a complete meal.

title: Shahi Tukda Gajar Halwa Shots With Rabri Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Carrots (Gajjar), washed and peeled (preferably red)
instructions: Condense the milk for Basundi: place 2 liters of milk in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over high heat, bring to a boil.
Add 3/4 cup sugar and stir continuously until dissolved; reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring, until the mixture reduces to about three‑fourths of its original volume.
Scrape the cream that forms on the sides and bottom back into the milk throughout the reduction.
Continue stirring until the mixture thickens and attains a creamy texture, monitoring closely to prevent burning.
When the milk has reduced to roughly half its original quantity, turn off the heat.
Stir in 1 teaspoon cardamom powder, 2 saffron strands, and 1/4 cup pistachios.
Transfer the Basundi (Rabri) to a serving dish, cool, and refrigerate for 3–4 hours.
Cut each bread slice into four triangles.
Heat a saucepan over medium flame, add 2 tablespoons ghee, and shallow‑fry the bread triangles until deep golden on both sides; set aside.
In another pan, combine 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 tablespoon water, and 1/2 teaspoon rose water; bring to a single boil, then turn off the flame.
Dip each fried bread triangle into the sugar‑rose water syrup, drain, and set aside.
Grate the peeled carrots.
Heat a pressure cooker over medium flame, add 1/4 cup ghee and the grated carrots, sauté for a couple of minutes, then sprinkle a little water and close the cooker.
Pressure cook the carrots for one whistle, then turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Meanwhile, in a kadai, bring 400 ml milk to a rolling boil over medium heat, then reduce heat and let the milk reduce to about three‑fourths of its original volume.
Add 150 grams grated khoya, 1 teaspoon cardamom powder, and 200 grams sugar to the reduced milk; stir until the khoya and sugar melt and the mixture becomes homogeneous.
Transfer the cooked carrots into the milk‑khoya mixture and stir continuously over low heat until a thick halwa forms.
Adjust sugar and cardamom to taste, then add an additional 2 tablespoons ghee and give a final stir.
Gajar halwa is ready.
To assemble the shots, place 2 tablespoons of the prepared gajar halwa into each shot glass.
Top each with 1 tablespoon of the chilled Basundi (Rabri).
Place a sweet fried bread triangle on top of the rabri in each glass.
Garnish with chopped pistachios.
Serve the Shahi Tukda Gajar Halwa Shots with Rabri as a dessert.

title: Gulab Jamun Trifle Recipe
instructions: Crumble the gulab jamun along with its sugar syrup, reserving some for garnish; you may also slice them.
Heat milk in a saucepan. In a bowl, take custard powder, add a little water or milk and mix to a smooth paste without lumps.
When the milk reaches a boil, reduce the flame, add sugar and the custard mixture, and stir continuously until the custard thickens.
Allow the custard to cool. In a tall serving glass, add 3 tablespoons of the cooled custard, then add 2 tablespoons of gulab jamun crumbles.
Layer more custard followed by gulab jamun mixture repeatedly until the glass is about three‑quarters full.
Garnish the top with remaining gulab jamun pieces and some crushed nuts, then refrigerate for 30 minutes.
The Gulab Jamun Trifle is ready; serve it chilled and enjoy.
Optionally serve the trifle with snacks like baked banana chips or spicy mushroom puffs.

title: How To Make Homemade Yogurt - Curd
instructions: To begin making Homemade Yogurt (Curd), boil the milk and keep it aside to cool.
Once the milk is completely cooled, pour it in a large bowl and add a teaspoon of curd to act as a starter.

Leave in a warm and cozy corner of your kitchen for at least 4 hours in humid areas and overnight if you live in cooler climate. Remember to keep the bowl of milk with curd starter in a warm place, to set properly.
The curd will have set when the top is wobbly and looks firm.
Use yogurt as it is along with Parathas and Pickle, or as an addition to recipes like Mango Lassi Recipe or Pineapple Banana & Oat Smoothie Recipe.
Serve Homemade Yogurt (Curd) with a lunch meal of Mixed Vegetable Sambar, Steamed Rice and Pisarna Manga.

title: Sitaphal Rabdi Recipe
ingredients: 3 custard apples (sitaphal), de-seeded and pulp collected
instructions: De-seed the custard apples and collect the pulp in a bowl; set aside.
Pour the milk into a heavy‑bottomed pan and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the cardamom powder and simmer the milk.
Lower the heat and simmer until a thick layer of cream forms on the surface.
Collect the cream from the sides of the pan and continue simmering the milk.
Keep collecting the thick cream layer until the milk is reduced to a considerable amount.
Switch off the heat, transfer the collected cream to a large bowl, and let it cool completely.
Add the custard‑apple pulp, slivered almonds, and pistachios; mix gently.
Refrigerate for 2–3 hours before serving.
Serve the chilled Sitaphal Rabdi, optionally alongside other Diwali desserts or snacks.

title: Maheri Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Barnyard Millet, washed and soaked for 30 minutes
instructions: To begin making Maheri, heat ghee or oil in a pressure cooker. Once the ghee is hot add hing, cumin seeds and allow the seeds to crackle. Once they start crackling, add turmeric powder.
Add 2 cups of water and salt and bring it to boil. Once the water starts boiling add buttermilk and bring it to boil again.
Now add the barnyard millet and mix well. Cover the pressure cooker and turn the heat to low. Pressure cook for 2 whistles. Let the pressure release naturally and then open the pressure cooker.
Transfer the Maheri to a serving dish and serve.
Serve Maheri as a healthy breakfast with pickle or Green Chutney for a comforting breakfast.

title: Egg Scramble With Drumstick Leaves Recipe
instructions: Wash and pat dry the drumstick leaves with a kitchen towel to avoid a soggy scramble.
In a medium sized bowl, crack the eggs and beat well with black pepper powder and salt; then add the drumstick leaves and mix well.
Place a pan on medium heat, add oil or butter, and fry the onions for a minute.
Add the beaten eggs, cook on low heat to avoid burning, using a fork to fold and separate the egg layers as they scramble; garnish with chopped chillies when done.
Serve the egg scramble with drumstick leaves for breakfast alongside a cup of Adrak Chai.

title: Tangy Red Purifier - Tomato Beetroot Juice Recipe
ingredients: 1 Beetroot, peeled and cut into cubes
1/2 Cucumber, peeled and cut into cubes
instructions: To begin making Tangy Red Purifier- Tomato Beetroot Juice Recipe, prepare all the vegetables as mentioned, after cleaning them thoroughly.
Take a juicer and add all the ingredients. Blend for a few seconds till coarsely done and then add a little water.
Grind till you get a smooth consistency. At this stage, check for salt and add more water to get the desired juice consistency. Give it a quick pulse once again till everything is well combined.
Chill Tangy Red Purifier - Healthy Fresh Juice Recipe in the refrigerator for some time (if needed) or serve immediately.
Serve Tangy Red Purifier- Tomato Beetroot Juice Recipe with Multigrain Crepe Recipe Filled With Spicy Mashed Potatoes for a wholesome breakfast.

title: Chole Semiya Pulao Recipe - Chickpea Vermicelli Pulao
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked for 8 hours & boiled until soft
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, as required, chopped for garnishing
instructions: Boil about 3 cups of water in a pan, add a little salt and the semiya, and cook for 5-7 minutes until the semiya is cooked.
Drain the cooked semiya, wash under running water, and let it drain completely.
Fluff the semiya gently with a fork and set aside.
Heat oil and ghee in a heavy‑bottomed pan, add cumin seeds and when they splutter, add the onions; sauté until soft and translucent.
Add the chopped carrot and sauté for a few seconds, then add the capsicum and continue sautéing for a few seconds.

When the carrot and capsicum are soft, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, dry mango powder, chole masala powder and salt to taste; mix well and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add the cooked chickpeas and mix everything well.
Add the semiya, turn the heat to high and cook for a minute or two; adjust salt and spices as needed, garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve Chole Semiya Pulao on its own for breakfast with filter coffee or masala chai, or pack it for a lunch box with curd and Satvik carrot sprouts salad.

title: Microwave Oats Milk Halwa Recipe
instructions: In a mixer grinder, add oats and water and blend well until you get a smooth texture.
Place a thin muslin or cotton cloth over a bowl and pour the mixture into it.
Squeeze the cloth well, discard any remaining oat pieces, and collect the oat milk (about 1.5 cups).
Take a microwave‑safe glass bowl and brush it with ghee.
Add ghee and the pistachios to the bowl, mix well, and microwave for 1 minute to toast.
Remove the bowl and add the oat milk, sugar, and cardamom; mix thoroughly and adjust sugar to taste.
Microwave on high for a total of 4 minutes in 1‑minute bursts, stirring well after the second burst.
Remove from the microwave and drizzle a teaspoon of ghee on top for added flavor.
Serve the Microwave Oats Milk Halwa warm, optionally alongside Palak Tovve, Palak Dal, Besan & Atta Ki Roti, or Boondi Raita.

title: Homemade Coconut Milk Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups fresh coconut, cut into pieces or grated
instructions: To begin making the Homemade Coconut Milk Recipe, first grate the coconut using a shredder and keep aside.
If you have a juicer attachment in your mixer grinder, then it is really convenient to extract the coconut milk. Fix the extraction blade and the juice attachment.

Add the grated coconut and 1 cup of warm water and blend to extract the coconut milk. This will be the first extraction. You can add more water and then extract more coconut milk after the first extraction.
If you don't have the extraction blade, then place the grated coconut in a blender jar and add 1 cup warm water and blend till the coconut is ground well.
Once the coconut is ground well, place the coconut in a muslin cloth sieve and then press to extract the coconut milk.
If you don't have muslin cloth sieve, then you will have to extract the coconut milk by pressing it between your fingers, until the coconut becomes dry.
Add water and get two and maximum three extractions of coconut milk.
Use the homemade coconut milk as required in curries and stews.

title: Beans And Carrot Masala Pulav With Black Eyed Beans Recipe
ingredients: 5 to 6 green beans (French beans), finely chopped
instructions: Cook the black eyed beans with salt in 1 cup water in a pressure cooker for 2–3 whistles, then simmer on low for 5 minutes and set aside.
Steam the carrots and green beans with a pinch of salt for 4–7 minutes until just cooked; set aside.
Drain the cooked beans. Wash the rice and soak in 2 cups water for 1 hour. Pound the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves to a fine powder and set aside.
Heat ghee in a large saucepan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds, allowing them to crackle.
Add the powdered spices, bay leaf, turmeric powder, slit green chillies and chopped tomatoes. Sauté until the tomatoes become soft.
Stir in the soaked rice, salt and the soaking water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and begin cooking the rice.
After about 10 minutes, mix in the cooked black eyed beans and chopped mint leaves.
Continue cooking until the rice is fully cooked and all water is absorbed (about 15 minutes more). Turn off the heat and let the pulao rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Gently fold in the steamed carrots and green beans, adjust seasoning if needed, and serve warm.

title: Paneer Gulab Jamun Recipe (Delicious Diwali Sweet)
ingredients: 8 Whole Almonds (Badam), blanched and roughly chopped
instructions: Take the homemade paneer in a large bowl, add the flour, baking powder and milk, and knead all the ingredients well to make a soft dough.
Cover the dough with cling film and let it rest in the refrigerator for about 10–15 minutes.

For the sugar syrup, boil the sugar, water and cardamom powder in a heavy‑bottomed saucepan, stirring continuously until it reaches a one‑string sticky consistency; then remove from heat and set aside.
Shape the paneer dough into round lemon‑sized balls, placing a raisin inside each ball.
Preheat oil for deep frying; add a few paneer balls at a time and deep‑fry on medium heat until lightly browned on both sides.
Remove the fried jamuns, drain excess oil, and set them aside.
Add the fried jamuns to the warm sugar syrup and let them rest for about 2 hours to absorb the sweetness.
Serve the jamuns warm, garnished with chopped almonds.

title: Red Lentil Curry Without Coconut Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Red Lentil Curry Without Coconut recipe, soak the lentils in water for about 20 minutes.
Boil them using 3 to 4 cups water until soft in a saucepan. Cover the pan with a lid while cooking.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a saucepan and fry the sliced onions on medium heat until slightly browned.
Add tomatoes and mix. Cover and cook till tomatoes are soft and mushy. Stir in between.
Let the mixture cool down, then grind it to smooth paste along with ginger and garlic. Use very little water while grinding.
Pour the prepared paste over cooked lentils and add little water.
Add green chilies and let it boil on medium heat for 5 minutes. Add all the spices and mix.
Add salt and sprinkle crushed Kasuri methi. Mix and let it simmer on low heat for about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and serve hot.
Serve Red Lentil Curry Without Coconut along with Palak Raita, Aloo Bhindi Ki Sabzi and Phulkas for your weekday meal.

title: How To Roast A Papad
ingredients: Papad (Urad dal papad or any preferred papad)
instructions: Stove top method: Hold the papad with tongs and roast it evenly over a low‑medium flame.
Stove top method: Rotate the papad so the blisters become even and golden‑colored, preventing charcoal spots.
Stove top method: Use the tongs to flip and roast the side that was previously held away from the fire.
Microwave method: Place a papad on the microwave plate (away from the centre) and microwave on high for 15 seconds.
Microwave method: Open the microwave, tilt the papad to the un‑roasted side, and continue microwaving for another 15‑20 seconds until done, watching closely to avoid burning.
Serve the roasted papad alongside Indian meals.

title: Carrot Rice Recipe - Spiced Carrot Pulao
ingredients: 1 small bunch Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Heat a teaspoon of oil in a heavy-bottomed pan; add the mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add the shallots and ginger; sauté until the onions are tender and golden.
Add the grated carrots, sprinkle some salt and sauté until the carrots are soft and cooked. Stir in the curry leaves, sambar powder, cardamom powder, and mix well. Cook for about 2 minutes.
Gradually stir the cooked rice into the carrot mixture and fold gently so all ingredients are well combined.
Add the coriander leaves and a tablespoon of ghee or sesame oil; stir into the rice. Check and adjust salt and spice levels to taste.
Serve the carrot rice with Boondi Raita and roasted Papad, if desired.

title: Brinjal Capsicum Sabji Recipe
instructions: Heat a pan with enough oil.
Add chopped garlic and hing; sauté for a few seconds.
Add the brinjal and capsicum to the pan.
Add all the dry spices, sauté, then cover the lid and let it semi-cook, stirring every few minutes.
Add chopped tomato and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked to your liking.
Add salt to taste, sauté briefly, and then stir in the chopped fresh coriander.
Serve the Brinjal Capsicum Sabji with phulka or chapati for a light lunch.

title: Palak Bhajia Recipe - Spinach Pakoras
ingredients: 3/4 cup Spinach Leaves (Palak), tightly packed, chopped
instructions: To begin making Palak Bhajia, firstly let us make the pakora batter.
In a mixing bowl, combine spinach, besan, rice flour, baking soda, asafoetida, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, salt and ajwain.
Add enough water and mix everything to form a batter. The batter should not be very thick or watery.
Heat oil for frying in a deep fry pan. Drop bits of spinach batter and cook till it turns crispy and golden brown.
Remove from the heat and similarly deep fry the remaining bhajias too.
Serve Palak Bhajia with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or Tomato Onion Chutney.

title: Green Coriander Coconut Chutney Recipe
instructions: Grind together the fresh coconut, coriander leaves, green chillies, salt, and warm water in a mixer grinder until smooth.
Add the lemon juice from one lemon to the grinder and blend again.
Transfer the green coriander and coconut chutney to a serving bowl.
Prepare the tempering.
Heat oil in a tadka pan; once hot, add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Then add urad dal and sauté until the dal turns crisp and golden brown.
Add the red chillies and curry leaves to the dal, roast for a few seconds until the curry leaves turn crisp, then remove from heat and pour the tempering over the chutney.
Serve the green coriander coconut chutney with Mini Idli Upma or Ragi and Oats Dosa, accompanied by South Indian filter coffee.

title: Kohlrabi Recipe (Knol Khol Poriyal)
ingredients: 3 cups Kohl rabi, peeled and sliced
instructions: To begin making the Kohlrabi recipe, take kohlrabi and peel the outer fibrous part and cut into small squares.
Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. When heated, add cumin seeds and mustard seeds. When they splutter, add a teaspoon of black urad dal.
Saute until the dal turns brown. Now add curry leaves, dry red chillies and turmeric powder.
After 1 minute, add sliced onions and fry till the onion becomes soft.
Add tomato slices and cook till they become a little soft. Add fresh peas followed by kohlrabi slices and mix everything.
Now close the lid and cook for some more time, mixing at regular intervals.
Add spices - coriander powder, red chilli powder and salt as per taste.
Add dry dessicated coconut, mix everything and cook for a few minutes by closing the lid.
Cook till kohlrabi slices become soft. Turn off the heat and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve Kohlrabi along with Dal Tadka and Steamed Rice for a weekday meal with your family.

title: Vegan Jackfruit Ice Cream Recipe With Coconut Milk
instructions: To begin making the Vegan Jackfruit Ice Cream Recipe With Coconut Milk, the first step is to freeze the ice cream bowl for at least 2 days in the freezer. This ice cream bowl comes along with the KitchenIf ice cream maker.
Once you have a frozen bowl; you can get started to prepare the mixture for the jack fruit ice cream.
Into a blender jar, add the coconut milk, jackfruit puree, sugar and blend until well combined. Refrigerate for two hours.
Place the frozen ice cream bowl into the kitchenif ice cream maker. Attach the paddle and set the timer for 30 minutes.

Start the ice cream maker and pour the blended jackfruit ice cream mixture through the opening into the ice cream maker. Do not turn off the machine in between till 30 minutes is up. You will see that slowly, the ice cream will start turning thick and creamy.
At the 20 minutes mark add in the finely chopped Jackfruit into the ice cream maker.
Once done, spoon half the mixture into an ice cream bowl (you can also use a loaf pan).
Cover the pan with an airtight lid or aluminium foil or cling film and freeze for at least 8 hours.
Once the ice cream is frozen, scoop out the ice cream into a cone or a bowl and top it with some more fresh chopped jackfruit if you like and serve.
Serve Vegan Jackfruit Ice Cream Recipe With Coconut Milk as a dessert after a meal of Beans Mezhukkupuratti, White Pumpkin Mor Kuzhambu, Matta Rice/Chemba Rice and Muringakka Manga Mulakushyam.

title: Pan Fried Onion Pakora Recipe - A Perfect Diwali & Evening Snack
instructions: To begin making the Pan Fried Onion Pakora Recipe, first get all the ingredients together for making the pakora.

In a large mixing bowl, add all the ingredients—besan, rice flour, onions, coriander leaves, green chilies, ginger, turmeric powder, red chili powder, ajwain, asafoetida, salt, except the oil and the chaat masala—into a large mixing bowl and combine them well.
Add very little water to make a thick batter. Check the salt and spice and adjust to suit your taste.
We will be using a Kuzhi Paniyaram Pan to make the pan fried onion pakoras; you can also optionally cook these in an air fryer or even on a skillet with little oil.
Preheat the Kuzhi Paniyaram Pan on medium heat. Add a few drops of oil into each of the cavities.

Spoon a portion of the onion pakora mixture into the cavities and allow the pakoras to cook on medium heat until browned and crisp on both sides. Flip the pakoras around as you are cooking so it cooks evenly on all sides.

Once done, place the Pan Fried Onion Pakoras on a platter and serve them with Tetley Lemon & Honey Green Tea and a favorite chutney such as Sweet & Spicy Raw Mango Chutney, Coriander Chutney, or Moroccan Harissa Sauce for a unique twist.

title: Hare Tamatar Ki Sabzi Recipe - Raw Tomato Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a wok/kadhai and add hing, mustard and cumin seeds; wait till they crackle.
Add chopped raw tomatoes and green chilies, mix well, and cook on high flame until moisture evaporates and tomatoes become soggy, about 3 minutes.
Add salt, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, and garam masala powder.
Mix thoroughly and let cook for a few minutes on low heat with the lid closed.
Allow the tomatoes to turn mushy and the oil to separate from the sides.
Increase heat to high and cook the sabzi until it reaches the desired consistency.
Stir in crushed kasuri methi, remove from heat, and serve hot.
Serve the raw tomato curry with Pudina Tawa Paratha, Boondi Raita, and Panchmel Dal.

title: Aam Ka Panna Recipe - Raw Mango Juice Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Whole Black Peppercorns, crushed coarsely
instructions: To begin making the Aam Ka Panna Recipe - Raw Mango Juice, first we will cook the mangoes.
Using a large saucepan boil the whole raw mangoes in water till they become soft and tender. Drain the water and allow the mangoes to cool.
Once they get cooled completely peel the skin of the mangoes. With your hands squeeze the pulp of the mangoes into a saucepan to make the Aam Ka Panna.
Puree the Aam Ka Panna pulp along with sugar, cardamom powder and saffron either in a mixer grinder or with the help of a hand blender.
Stir in the black pepper and salt. Store the Aam Ka Panna in an airtight container and refrigerate the Aam Ka Panna.
When you are ready to serve the Aam Ka Panna, spoon out two tablespoons of the spiced mango pulp into a glass; add water and ice and stir well to combine.
Adjust the concentration of the Aam Ka Panna to suit your taste and serve chilled.
Serve Aam Ka Panna with Raj Kachori or Chole Aloo Tikki Chaat for your next chaat party.

title: Crispy Palak Pakora Recipe - Monsoon Snack
instructions: To begin making the Crispy Palak Pakora Recipe, first get all the ingredients ready.
In a large mixing bowl, add the gram flour, turmeric powder, salt, and red chili powder. Stir to combine well. Add a little water at a time to make a thick pakora batter.

Preheat oil in a kadai (wok) for deep frying. Once the oil is sufficiently heated, dip each spinach leaf in the batter to coat it evenly. Drop the leaf gently into the oil and fry on medium heat until the pakoras are crisp.
When the Palak Pakoras are golden brown and crisp, remove them from the oil and drain on absorbent paper.
Proceed the same way with the remaining spinach leaves.
Sprinkle chaat masala on the Palak Pakoras and serve them hot with Date Tamarind Chutney, Green Chutney, or plain ketchup.
Note: If you don't have baby spinach, you can use regular spinach, chop it finely, and mix it into the batter to make the pakoras.

title: Aloo Bhindi Sabzi Recipe - Potatoes Lady's Finger Stir Fry
ingredients: 500 grams Bhindi (Lady Finger/Okra), cut into 1 inch pieces
3 Potatoes (Aloo), peeled and cut into wedges
instructions: To begin making the Aloo Bhindi Sabzi Recipe, heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy bottom pan over medium heat.
Add a teaspoon of cumin seeds, allow seeds to crackle. Add half the curry leaves, cut potatoes along with salt, 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder. Stir to combine.
Cover the pan with the lid and cook the potatoes for few minutes, stirring occasionally.
Open the lid of the pan and add 1/2 teaspoon of coriander powder, red chilli powder, stir to combine.
Simmer for a few more minutes and turn off the heat. Keep covered aside, while you cook the bhindi.
Heat oil in another heavy bottomed pan, add the remaining cumin seeds and allow seeds to crackle.
Add the chopped bhindi, asafoetida and salt. Cover the pan (with lid slightly open) and allow the bhindi to simmer, stirring occasionally.
Bhindi releases moisture when cooked covered and will get sticky. But after sometime it will turn fine.
Once the bhindi is slightly tender, add the turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon of coriander powder and red chilli powder.
Keep the pan slightly open and cook till bhindi is done. The bhindi will change its color to brown.
Once done, gently stir in the sauteed aloo into the bhindi and combine well. Cover the pan with the lid and simmer for another couple of minutes.
Turn off the heat and allow the vegetable to rest in the pan, covered for another 3 to 4 minutes. This helps the vegetable to gain a little moisture and gather itself together.
Serve this Aloo Bhindi Sabzi along with Phulkas or South Indian Style meal along with Steamed Rice, Beetroot Sambar and a big dollop of Ghee.

title: Pudina Quinoa Recipe
instructions: Wash 1 cup quinoa and soak for two hours, ensuring it is cleaned thoroughly.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, add garlic and onions, sauté until onions soften.
Stir in green chilli, quinoa, and the dry spices (cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom); add salt to taste and toss on high heat for two minutes.
Add two cups of water, give two whistles; after whistles reduce flame to low and simmer for 15 minutes, then turn off heat.
Allow pressure to release naturally; open the cooker and fluff the quinoa with a spoon.
Add the finely chopped mint leaves, combine, turn off flame, and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve Pudina Quinoa with Dhingri Matar, Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, or as a lunch box snack.

title: Whole Wheat Spinach Paratha Recipe
ingredients: Ghee, or oil to grease the pan
instructions: Blend spinach, coriander, garlic and chilies in a mixer grinder to make a paste.
Add this paste to the wheat flour. Add salt to taste, ajwain and oil to the mixture and knead together to make a smooth dough. Add water if required.
Divide the dough into equal lemon size portions.
Take one portion and dust in dry flour. Flatten the ball with your fingers and roll the rough into a 5 to 6 inch diameter circle.
Heat the non-stick tawa and place the rolled spinach paratha on the tawa. Cook till small blisters appear on the surface. Flip and cook the roti on the other side as well.
Flip a couple of times to get the parathas browned and cooked well on both sides. Smear ghee on top and transfer into a plate and serve.
Serve Wheat Flour Spinach Paratha with Raw Mango raita or Avocado raita or any raita of your choice.

title: Semiya Payasam Recipe - Vermicelli Kheer Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Semiya Payasam, cook the semiya (vermicelli) in water.
Into a saucepan, add the water and the semiya and bring to a boil; then reduce heat to medium and cook until the semiya is soft and done.
Add the 500 ml milk, sugar, cardamom powder and saffron, stirring until the sugar fully dissolves.
Simmer the payasam for another 5 minutes until it becomes thick and creamy and the flavors are well absorbed.
Adjust the consistency if needed; note that the semiya will absorb more milk and thicken as it cools.
While the payasam is simmering, roast the cashew nuts in a small pan with ghee over low heat until golden, then add the raisins and stir briefly until they puff up; set aside.
Turn off the heat, garnish the payasam with the roasted cashew nuts and raisins, and serve hot or cold as desired.

title: Methi Pakoras Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Methi Pakoras, sieve both the flours-besan & rice flour together with salt. Add a ladle of hot oil (heated separately for 1 minute) and gently mix with a spoon. Now add the methi leaves, salt, red chilli powder, hing, turmeric powder, ajwain and coriander seeds and mix well.
Methi leaves would leave out water in 2-3 mins. Add water very slowly and make a thick batter. Once it is done, adjust the spice and salt according to your taste.

Pour the rest of the oil in a pan on medium flame. Once it is hot enough, use a greased spoon or wet hands to drop small pakoras (or bite sized pieces) into the hot oil. Be sure not to overcrowd the frying pan (or kadai).
Fry on medium heat turning the batch over in the oil occasionally. Fry till golden brown and drain the pakoras on the kitchen towel.
Fry the rest of the pakoras similarly.
Serve the Methi Pakoras with hot Masala Chai or Papaya Banana smoothie.

title: Grilled Paneer Methi Tikki Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), cut into large cubes
1/2 teaspoon Kasuri Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves) for garnish
instructions: Prep all ingredients. In a mixer, grind the ingredients listed under 'Ground paste' (Methi leaves, Mint leaves, Green chillies, Garlic, Ginger, Onion) to a smooth paste without adding water and transfer to a large bowl.
Add lemon juice, salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and 1 teaspoon of oil to the paste and mix well.
Add the paneer cubes to the mixture, mix thoroughly, cover the bowl with cling film or a lid and marinate for at least 3 hours.
Heat a grill pan (or regular pan) with oil and fry the marinated paneer over low to medium heat until crisp and browned on all sides.
Remove the paneer and sprinkle hand‑crushed Kasuri Methi on top; optionally add chaat masala just before serving.
Serve the grilled paneer methi tikki with green chutney as an appetizer.

title: Egg Pakora Recipe - Egg Fritters
ingredients: Oil, as required for deep frying
instructions: In a small pot, add water and bring it to a boil; once boiling, add a pinch of salt and the eggs.
Cook the eggs for about 15 minutes, remove from heat, run under cold water, and peel them.
Slice the boiled eggs into halves and set aside.
In a bowl, combine gram flour, rice flour, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt.
Add water little by little, mixing to form a batter slightly thinner than Idli batter but not as runny as dosa batter.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium flame; test the oil by dropping a small ball of batter—if it rises steadily, the oil is ready.
Dip each egg slice in the batter and gently drop into the hot oil.
Fry until golden on both sides, flipping occasionally.
Remove the pakoras onto a dish towel and repeat with the remaining egg slices.
Serve the spicy egg pakoras with Tomato Garlic Chutney or any chutney of your choice.

title: Prawns Biryani Recipe
instructions: Dry roast the biryani masala ingredients (ajwain, fennel seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves) and grind them into a fine powder.
Heat oil in a wok or kadhai and sauté the sliced onions on medium heat until brownish and crispy.
Soak the basmati rice in water for about 30 minutes.

In a mixing bowl, combine the cleaned prawns, turmeric powder, 1 tablespoon of the prepared biryani masala, red chilli powder, half lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/2 cup chopped mint leaves, half of the fried onions, and curd; mix well.
Let the marinated prawns rest for about an hour.
In a medium saucepan, add 5 cups water, 1 tablespoon biryani masala, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, 1/4 cup mint leaves, 1 tablespoon oil and remaining salt; bring to a boil.
Boil the water over high flame.
Add the soaked rice to the boiling water and cook on high flame for 4–5 minutes, being careful not to overcook.
Drain the rice immediately and set aside.
In another wide saucepan, spread the remaining half tablespoon of oil on the bottom.
Layer the marinated prawns as the bottom layer of the pan.
Add half of the remaining fried onions, sprinkle mint leaves, then layer the cooked rice evenly over the prawn mixture.
Garnish with the leftover fried onions, dissolve a pinch of saffron in hot water and drizzle over the layered rice.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook on high flame for about 10 minutes without opening the lid.
Reduce the flame and continue cooking the biryani for about 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest, covered, for 15 minutes.
Gently combine the biryani so that the masala and rice are well mixed, taking care not to break the rice grains.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve.

title: Chicken Pakora Recipe - Chicken Fritters
ingredients: Chaat Masala Powder, as required, for garnishing
Pickled onions, as required, for garnishing
instructions: Combine all the ingredients together in a bowl including chicken, gram flour, onion, cumin seeds, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander leaves and salt.
Add water little at a time to make a thick pakora batter, then check the salt and spices and adjust to taste.
Preheat the Kuzhi Paniyaram pan on medium heat; add a few drops of oil into each cavity.
Spoon the chicken pakoda batter into the cavities and pan‑fry until browned and crisp on both sides, adding a little more oil if desired; this takes 3–4 minutes.
Proceed the same way with the remaining chicken pakora batter.
Cooking pakoda in a pan preserves nutrition, and the addition of lotus seeds adds extra taste and nutrition for this classic teatime snack.
Arrange the chicken pakora on a serving platter, sprinkle with chaat masala, place pickled onions on the side, and serve as a snack or appetizer.
Serve the chicken pakora with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or Garlic Chutney for evening snacks and enjoy it with Masala Chai.

title: Quick Paneer Masala Recipe - 15 Minute Paneer Gravy
instructions: Soak store‑bought paneer in hot salt water for about 10 minutes (or use homemade paneer) to make it soft and tasty.
Cut the tomatoes and puree them in a blender; set aside.
Heat ghee in a pan, add the onion, ginger and garlic and sauté until the onion softens and turns lightly golden.
Add the tomato puree, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, salt, paneer, jaggery and cream; stir quickly.
Cover the pan, turn the heat to medium and bring the gravy to a brisk boil; simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir, check seasoning and adjust salt or spices as needed.
Turn off the heat, transfer the gravy to a serving bowl, stir in kasuri methi and serve hot.
Serve the Quick Paneer Masala gravy with phulkas.

title: Green Moong Dal Pulao With Vegetables Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Green Moong Dal (Whole), soaked for 5 to 6 hours
instructions: To begin making Green Moong Dal Biryani With Vegetables, soak the green moong beans for 5 to 6 hours or overnight. Wash and soak the rice in 2 cups of water for about an hour. Drain the water and keep it aside.
Heat ghee in the pressure cooker on medium heat; add the cumin seeds and allow them to crackle. Add in cinnamon and cardamom pods, allow them to release their aroma.
Stir in the ginger, garlic, green chillies and onion and saute on medium heat until the onion turns translucent and soft and begin to get a sweet smell.

Stir in the tomato puree or chopped tomatoes and turmeric powder. Sauté the above mixture until the tomatoes have cooked through. Stir in the rice, soaked green moong, vegetables and salt along with 2-1/2 cups of water.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook the Green Moong Biryani for 3 to 4 whistles and turn off the heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure releases, open the pressure cooker, stir in the chopped coriander leaves and transfer the Green Moong Dal Biryani to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Green Moong Dal Biryani With Vegetables makes a great wholesome one dish meal along with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita. Serve it for your everyday meals along with a Papad.

title: Puffed Lotus Seed Pakoras Recipe - Makhana Pakora
ingredients: 100 grams Phool Makhana (Lotus Seeds), roasted in ghee
instructions: Make the pakora batter by combining lotus seeds, besan flour, onion, green chilli, cumin seeds, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt, coriander leaves, and curry leaves in a mixing bowl.
Add water little at a time to form a thick batter; adjust salt and spices to taste.
Preheat a Kuzhi Paniyaram pan on medium heat and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.
Spoon the batter into the cavities and pan‑fry until brown and crisp on both sides, adding a little more oil if desired for extra crispness.
Repeat the process with the remaining batter.
Arrange the cooked pakoras on a serving platter, sprinkle with chaat masala, and serve with pickled onions or a dipping sauce.
Serve the puffed lotus seed pakoras with hot chai as a snack or appetizer.

title: Paneer Carrot Stuffed Paratha Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Paneer Carrot Stuffed Paratha, we will first make the dough.
Add in the flour and a pinch of salt into a large bowl. Add a little water at a time and knead to make a firm yet smooth dough. Knead well for about 3 to 4 minutes, this will make the parathas soft.
Drizzle a teaspoon of oil over the dough and knead for another couple of minutes. Cover and keep aside till we make the Paneer Carrot filling for the paratha.

Next, we will combine the paneer, grated carrots, onions, green chillies, mint leaves, cumin powder and salt. Stir to combine the ingredients well. We will be using raw carrots as a stuffing as they will get cooked while cooking the parathas.
Now to begin making the Paneer Carrot Stuffed Paratha, keep some flour aside for dusting. Divide the dough into large lemon‑sized balls.

Dust the dough portions in flour, flatten them and roll into a 3‑inch diameter circle. Place the Paneer Carrot filling on half of the circle and close the paratha by folding it with the other half, forming a semi‑circle/oval shape.
Press the sides of the paratha down to seal the edges and gently flatten it with a rolling pin, taking care not to roll too thin to avoid the filling oozing out.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat. Place the rolled paneer carrot paratha on the skillet and let it cook on one side for about 10 to 15 seconds, then flip the paratha.
Smear some oil or ghee on the pan and continue cooking, flipping a couple of times until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
Repeat the same process with the remaining dough portions.
Serve the Paneer Carrot Stuffed Paratha with sweet lime pickle or Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita.

title: Whole Wheat Spinach Paneer Lifafa Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup Spinach Leaves (Palak), finely chopped (tightly packed)
1 teaspoon Cumin powder (Jeera), roasted and ground
instructions: To begin making the Whole Wheat Spinach Paneer Lifafa Paratha Recipe, in a mixing bowl add the whole wheat flour, salt, 1 tablespoon melted ghee and mix. Next add water little by little and start kneading the dough. If you are looking for softer texture add only milk to knead the dough and no water. Knead till you get soft, smooth dough. Cover and let the paratha dough rest for 30 minutes.
While the lifafa paratha dough is resting we can make the stuffing.
Heat oil in a pan. To hot oil add cumin seeds and wait till they turn slight brown. Add onions and green chilies and sauté till onions turn soft.
Add finely chopped spinach and cook until spinach looses all its moisture. Add salt to taste. Once spinach is completely dry, turn off heat and keep it aside to cool down.

Add roasted cumin powder, chaat masala to grated paneer. Add cooked spinach mix and mix them all together. This paratha stuffing mixture should be dry. If you find any liquid in it, squeeze it out. Divide them into equal sized balls.
In a small bowl, combine the corn flour along with water to make a thick paste. This will be used for sealing the edges.

Knead the paratha dough once more and divide them into equal sized balls (lemon sized). Roll it thin about 10 inch. Place it on hot griddle/tawa and cook for 10 seconds on each side, without oil. Don't overcook it. Take it out of tawa. Repeat this for rest of the dough.
Now place half cooked rotis on a flat surface. Place a small portion of spinach paneer stuffing in the center. Spread the stuffing all over leaving out the edges.

Apply corn flour paste on the edges of the roti. Fold the 2 opposite corners of the roti over the stuffing. Now fold the remaining 2 edges sealing the filling well. This will look like a folded envelope.
Place the stuffed lifafa spinach paneer paratha over hot tawa, drizzle oil or ghee and cook on both sides until they turn brown on both sides.
Serve the Whole Wheat Spinach Paneer Lifafa Paratha immediately with some yogurt and pickle for breakfast or even a weeknight dinner.

title: Puri Recipe - Learn to Make Soft Puffed Puris At Home
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Oil, to knead and more to deep fry
instructions: To begin making the Puri recipe, in a large bowl combine the flour, nigella seeds and salt together and then add 2 teaspoons of the oil. Add a little water at a time to the flour mixture and knead well to make a firm and smooth dough.
Add the remaining one teaspoon of oil to coat the dough and knead again. Cover and set aside for 15 minutes. Punch down the dough, knead for a minute and divide the dough into 20 equal portions.

Heat oil in a deep frying pan with heat on medium high. With a rolling pin, roll out each ball into a 5-7 inch circles tossing in a little oil while rolling to prevent it sticking to the base. Continue the same process of rolling with the remaining dough. Keep the rolled dough aside.

When the oil is hot and ready about 190°C, gently slip one rolled out dough into the oil. Fry the bread with a slotted spatula, continuously yet gently pouring oil onto the frying bread and allowing it to puff.

Once the puri puffs, turn over and fry for just a few seconds. Using the slotted spatula drain the oil by the side of the pan and remove from heat. Place the fried puri’s on paper towels to absorb excess oil. Continue the frying with the remaining rolled portions and serve hot.
Serve the Puri's along with Chana Masala and Aamras for a delicious Sunday lunch.

title: Crispy Pan Fried Pomfret Recipe
ingredients: 1 Pomfret fish, cut into 1 inch size pieces
1 teaspoon Salt, + Extra for pomfret pieces
instructions: Wash the pomfret with water, drain, sprinkle some salt and set aside for 5 minutes.
In a mixer grinder, add coriander leaves, fennel seeds, whole black peppercorns, cloves, turmeric powder, dry red chillies, garlic, ginger and tamarind.
Grind all the masala with about 1/3 cup water to a smooth batter for the fish; add a teaspoon of salt into the paste and mix well.
Apply this batter or paste to the pomfret pieces and marinate for about 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet and add oil. Coat the marinated pomfret pieces well with semolina on both sides.
Place the coated pieces in the skillet over oil and fry on medium heat for about 3 to 4 minutes.
Flip and fry the other side until brown and crispy; switch off the heat and transfer to a serving plate.
Serve the crispy pan‑fried pomfret with Prawns Coconut Curry and steamed rice.

title: Cheese Broccoli Fritter Recipe - Pan Fried Broccoli Pakora
ingredients: 500 grams Broccoli, cut into small florets
1/2 teaspoon Red Chilli powder, or smoked paprika
instructions: To begin making the Broccoli Fritters first get all the ingredients ready and keep aside.

To make the batter to coat the fritters (pakora), in a mixing bowl combine the corn flour, all purpose flour, baking powder, salt, chilli powder, garlic and the grated cheese. Add a little water at a time to make a smooth and thick batter. The batter should coat the back side of a spoon well, indicating the right consistency. Adjust the seasoning in the batter.
Preheat a kuzhi paniyaram pan on medium heat.

To pan fry the fritters, dip each floret in the batter and place a batter‑coated floret in each cavity of the pan. Drizzle some oil on each broccoli piece. Cover the pan and allow it to cook, adding a little more oil or spray to make the florets crispier.
Proceed the same way with the remaining florets.
Serve the delicious Broccoli Cheese Fritters (Pakora) along with a Greek Yogurt Dip as a snack or appetizer.

title: Mushroom Biryani Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped
instructions: Wash basmati rice and soak in water for at least 30 minutes.
Clean the mushrooms and chop them in two halves.
Heat a heavy bottomed pan, add ghee and oil with cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay leaf.
Add chopped onions, ginger garlic paste and stir well till the aroma fades.
Add finely chopped tomatoes, sprinkle some salt, and cook until the tomatoes become mushy.
Add spice powders (red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and garam masala) and mix well.
Add the cleaned and chopped mushrooms and stir for 3 minutes or until they shrink slightly.
Add 3 cups of water and 1 cup of coconut milk; once boiling, rinse the soaked rice, drain it, and add to the pan.
Cover and cook on medium flame for about 8 minutes, then turn off the flame.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve.

title: Mutton Keema Samosa Recipe-Mangsher Singara
instructions: To begin making the Mutton Keema Samosa recipe, sift flour in a mixing bowl and add chilled butter cubes and salt to taste.
Combine gently with hand until the flour resembles a coarse crumbs.
Gradually start adding water to make a firm dough.
Cover it with a cling wrap and refrigerate till you prepare the filling.
The next step is to make the filling.

Into a preheated pan add oil. Once the oil is hot add the chopped onions, green chillies, ginger, garlic and saute till the onions are cooked. Now add the minced mutton and all the spice powders like the red chilli powder, coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, garam masala and salt to taste.

Saute and add about 3 tablespoon of water. Cover and cook till mutton is cooked. Once done open the lids and saute on high heat till all the water in the minced mutton mixture is evaporated. Turn off the heat and allow the filling to cool.
To make Keema Samosa prepare the samosas.
Pinch a large ball from the dough and roll out as thin as possible on a dusted floor.
Cut the rolled dough into long 1.5 inch x 4 inch strips.
Take a teaspoon of filling and place it at one end of the strip and fold inwards in triangular shape.
Keep folding from one end to the other and seal the last edge by applying little water on the folds.
Similarly make more samosas with rest of the dough and filling.
Once done heat oil in a kadai or wok.
Drop a pinch of dough to check whether the oil is hot or not. If the dough ball rises up immediately, the oil is ready.
Carefully slide 1-2 samosas in the oil and deep fry them in medium to low flame till crisp and golden.
Transfer them on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil and serve hot.
Serve Mutton Keema Samosa as a snack with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Healthy Kala Chana Pakora Recipe - Black Chickpea Pakora
instructions: To begin making the Healthy Kala Chana Pakora Recipe, wash and soak the kala chana overnight in a bowl of water.
Next morning, transfer the kala chana and the water into the pressure cooker and pressure cook on medium flame for 30 minutes. Turn off the flame and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure has released, drain the water and transfer the kala chana into a mixing bowl.

Mash the cooked kala chana with your fingers, to this bowl add the chopped onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli, coriander leaves, mint leaves, lemon juice and the dry masalas- salt, chaat masala, amchur, cumin powder and finally add besan.
Mix well and bring the Kala Chana Pakora mixture together.
Heat a kuzhi paniyaram pan on medium heat, add very little oil in each of the cavities, drop a tablespoon of the Kala Chana Pakora mixture in each of those cavities and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Flip on the other side and cook till until the Kala Chana Pakora turns brown in colour.
Remove the Kala Chana Pakora from the paniyaram pan and place it on a plate with absorbent paper to drain the excess oil.
Serve Healthy Kala Chana Pakora Recipe along with Mumbai Style Tawa Pulao Recipe with Moong Sprouts and Carrot Tadka Raita Recipe- Crunchy Grated Carrot In Yogurt for a complete meal.
You could also serve it at tea time along with Green chutney and Masala Chai Recipe - Indian Spiced Tea.

title: Salted Caramel Popcorn Recipe
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot, add corn kernels and cover; shake intermittently until all kernels have popped properly, then set aside.
Melt butter in a large pan, add corn syrup and sugar over medium flame; bring the mixture to a boil and continue boiling until it turns an amber colour.
Remove the mixture from heat and stir in vanilla extract, baking soda, and salt.
Place popcorn in a large bowl, pour the sugar mixture over it, and coat all popcorn evenly.
Spread the coated popcorn on a baking sheet and let it cool completely; the salted caramel popcorn is ready.
Serve the salted caramel popcorn with Cold Coffee Smoothie on a movie night.

title: Sweet Potato & Neem Leaves Vegetable Curry Recipe
instructions: Clean the neem leaves and tear the stem out of them.
Pressure cook the sweet potatoes for just 1 whistle or 5 minutes, whichever is earlier, on full flame.
Take out, peel, and chop the sweet potatoes into cubes.
In a non-stick pan, add oil, asafoetida, mustard seeds, urad dal, red chilli, and chana dal; fry them well.
Add the neem leaves and fry for 3-4 minutes until they turn slightly crispy.
Add the chopped sweet potatoes and salt; cook until the sweet potatoes are well fried.
Garnish with roasted peanut powder.
Serve the curry with hot steaming rasam rice.

title: Masala Chai Recipe - Indian Spiced Tea
ingredients: 1 tablespoon loose leaf tea (Red Label, Lipton, or Assam)
instructions: Warm the milk and set it aside.
In a saucepan, bring two cups of water, the ground spices, and ginger to a boil. Boil for a few minutes to flavor the water.
Add the tea leaves, bring the mixture to a boil, and simmer for less than a minute until the water turns a maroon colour. Turn off the heat, cover, and let the tea brew for a few minutes.
Pour in the warm milk and stir the tea.
Using a small strainer, filter the tea into individual cups or a teapot and stir in sugar to taste.
Serve the Masala Chai hot with tea‑time snacks.

title: Capsicum Bajji Recipe -Kuda Milagai Bajji/ Bell Pepper Bajji
instructions: Remove the top stem of the capsicum, cut it into two equal halves vertically, and deseed it.
Cut long, thick strips of the capsicum.
In a mixing bowl combine gram flour, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, asafoetida, and salt.
Add enough water to form a thick batter that coats the back of a spoon; set aside.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium heat for deep frying.
Coat each capsicum strip in the batter and gently place into the hot oil; fry until golden brown.
Drain the fried capsicum bajji on absorbent paper to remove excess oil and serve hot.
Serve the capsicum bajji with coconut chutney and South Indian filter coffee, or as a tea‑time snack with Gulkand chai.

title: Peanut Butter Lassi Recipe - Peanut Butter Yogurt Smoothie
instructions: To begin making the Peanut Butter Lassi, get ready with all the ingredients.
Add all the ingredients into the blender including curd, fresh cream, peanut butter, sugar, salt, and ice cubes and blend until smooth.
Add water if required to adjust the consistency of the Peanut Butter Lassi.
Serve Peanut Butter Lassi along with Palak Masala Bhurji and bread toast for breakfast.

title: Khakhra Pizza Recipe With Cheese Spread & Roasted Vegetables
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Britannia Cheese Spread - Peppy Pizza
instructions: To begin making the Khakhra Pizza Recipe (Whole Wheat Crisp Flatbread Pizza), you can either make your khakra at home or buy the store‑bought ones. Here is the recipe to make the homemade khakra.

Heat the butter in a broad skillet pan, add capsicum and saute for a few minutes until softened. Add the blanched and chopped tomatoes, corn and italian seasoning and cook until the corn gets well coated with the capsicum and seasoning. Stir in the basil leaves and turn off the heat.
The final step is to make the Khakhra pizza.
Place a khakhra on a serving plate, spread a large tablespoon of Britannia Peppy Pizza Cheese Spread which adds a great taste and flavor to the pizza.
Once spread, sprinkle the corn topping over the khakhra and voila the pizza is ready to be served.
Serve the Khakhra Pizza as a tea‑time snack or as a quick after‑school snack for kids, or serve it along with Masala Chai or Espresso Coffee.
Editor's Notes: Equipment used – broad skillet pan.

title: Crispy Corn And Bell Peppers Chaat Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), stir fried
1 tablespoon Sweet Chutney (Date & Tamarind), (adjust to taste)
1 tablespoon Green Chutney (Coriander & Mint), (adjust to taste)
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Get all the ingredients ready. Stir fry the chopped capsicum for a couple of minutes in a pan until crunchy, then set aside.
In a large mixing bowl combine corn kernels, maida, corn flour, rice flour, black pepper powder and salt; mix with a little water so the corn is coated.
Heat enough oil in a kadai for deep frying.
When the oil is hot, add the coated corn and fry until crisp and golden, being careful of splatters.
Transfer the fried corn onto kitchen tissue to absorb excess oil.
In another bowl combine the sautéed capsicum, onion, sweet chutney, green chutney, red chilli powder, chaat masala, kala namak, lemon juice and salt; toss well, add the fried corn and toss again.
Add the remaining crispy corn, give a final toss and serve immediately.
Serve the chaat alongside Sev Puri (Papdi Chaat) for a snack party.

title: Chatpata Kala Chana Pakora Roll/ Frankie Recipe
instructions: Wash and soak the kala chana overnight in a bowl of water.
Transfer the soaked kala chana with water into a pressure cooker and cook on medium flame for 30 minutes; then turn off the flame and let the pressure release naturally.
Drain the cooked kala chana and place it in a mixing bowl.

Mash the kala chana with your fingers, then add chopped onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli, coriander leaves, mint leaves, lemon juice, salt, chaat masala, amchur, cumin powder, and besan; mix well to form a pakora batter.
Heat a kuzhi paniyaram pan on medium heat, add a little oil to each cavity, drop a tablespoon of the batter into each, and cook for 3–4 minutes.
Flip the pakoras and cook the other side until they turn brown.
Remove the pakoras and place them on absorbent paper to drain excess oil.

Place a tawa paratha on a flat surface, spread green chutney and sweet (date‑tamarind) chutney, crumble two pakoras onto the center, top with pickled onions, sprinkle chaat masala, and roll the paratha tightly from both edges.
Serve the Kala Chana Pakora Roll immediately.

title: Passion Fruit- Shrikhand Shots Recipe
ingredients: 1 pinch Saffron strands, mixed with 1 tablespoon warm milk
instructions: Put a strainer on a bowl, arrange a thin muslin cloth over it, pour curd into the strainer, tie the edges, and refrigerate for at least 3-4 hours.
Cut a passion fruit into two halves and scoop out the flesh; reserve the pulp for mixing into the curd and keep another fruit's pulp for assembling the shots.
After 3-4 hours, squeeze out the excess water from the curd and transfer the thickened curd to a wide bowl.
Whisk the curd with a beater, then add powdered sugar, cardamom powder, saffron milk mixture, and passion fruit pulp; whisk well to combine.
Take 4 shot glasses, add about a teaspoon of passion fruit pulp to each, then fill with the prepared shrikhand.
Top each shot with chocolate chips, chill the shots, and serve (optional: garnish with chopped nuts).

title: Chana Dal Aloo Cutlet Recipe - Gram Dal Potato Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Chana dal (Bengal Gram Dal), soaked for 3 hours
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch, chopped
Mint Leaves (Pudina), a small bunch, chopped
instructions: Wash the chana dal and soak in water for 1 hour or more.
Heat a pressure cooker, add the chana dal and water, and cook for 2 to 3 whistles.
Strain the water from the chana dal and make a dry fine paste using a mixer grinder.
Heat a teaspoon of oil, temper with cumin seeds and asafoetida, and sauté for about 10 seconds.
Add ginger, coconut, red chilli powder, and cardamom powder; sauté for a few seconds.
Add the chana dal paste, boiled mashed potatoes, besan, coriander leaves, mint leaves, and chaat masala; stir‑fry the mixture for about 2‑3 minutes on medium‑low flame until it thickens.
Turn off the heat once the mixture thickens.
Shape the mixture into flat, medium‑thick balls and refrigerate for about 15 minutes.
Heat a frying pan with oil and fry the cutlets on both sides for 5 minutes each or until golden brown, using low to medium heat for crispness.
Remove the cutlets onto a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil and serve hot.
Serve the cutlets with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and a cup of Masala Chai or Filter Coffee for evening snacks.

title: Guava Jam Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups sugar (quantity varies based on sweetness of guava)
instructions: Wash and wipe the guavas, then cut into small pieces.
Place the pieces in a thick pan, add 4 cups water and boil until the guava is fully soft and mushy; mash the cooked guava and sieve to remove the seeds.
Add lemon juice, sugar, and salt to the extracted pulp and mix well.
Keep the pan on medium flame, bring the mixture to a full boil while stirring frequently; as it thickens, stir consistently and reduce the flame, avoiding overcooking.
When the jam reaches a thick sauce consistency, turn off the flame, cool for about 10 minutes, and pour into clean sterilized glass bottles.
Let the jam thicken further, then refrigerate or store in a cool dry place.

title: Lachedar Kakdi Pyaz Kachumber Recipe - Onion Cucumber Salad
ingredients: 2 Cucumber, peeled & cut into thin strips
instructions: Peel and cut the onions into thin roundels.
Separate the onion rings from each other.
Peel the cucumbers, slice vertically, and then cut into thin strips to appear like noodles.
In a mixing bowl, toss the cucumber strips and the onions together.
In a small bowl, make the dressing by combining the freshly squeezed lemon juice, cumin powder, salt, chaat masala and red chilli powder.
Pour the dressing over the cucumber and onions and toss well; the Lachedar Kakdi Pyaz Kachumber is ready.
Serve the Lachedar Kakdi Pyaz Kachumber alongside a meal of Pudina Tawa Paratha, Tadkewali Masoor Dal, Achari Aloo Sabzi and Methi Raita Flavoured With Garlic.

title: Sweet & Spicy Ripe Mango Curry Recipe
instructions: Peel the mangoes.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the mustard, cumin, methi and fennel seeds and let them crackle. Add the whole chillies and then add the remaining masalas.
Add the peeled mangoes and sauté on low heat for two minutes so they absorb the flavors of the masala.
Add 2 cups of water and the tamarind paste. Cover the pan and cook on low heat for about half an hour until the flavors meld.
Switch off the flame and check the salt and spices, adjusting as needed.
Serve the sweet & spicy ripe mango curry with steamed rice (or jeera rice, chapati, paratha, poori) for a delicious lunch or dinner.

title: One Pot Methi Mushroom Brown Rice Pulao Recipe
instructions: Wash and soak the rice in water for 30 minutes.
Wash the mushrooms and fenugreek leaves properly and chop them.
Heat the oil in a pressure cooker; once hot, add cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, and cumin seeds.
When the spices crackle, add slit green chilli and ginger garlic paste; sauté for about a minute.
Add chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent.
Add fenugreek leaves and mushrooms; cook for 2-3 minutes until the mushrooms become soft.
Drain and add the soaked rice; sauté for a minute. Add 2½ cups of water with salt, stir well, and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, close the cooker with the lid and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally; open the lid and gently fluff the pulao with a fork. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve the Methi Mushroom Brown Rice Pulao with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita and Papad, or pack it in a lunch box.

title: Apple Pie Ice Cream Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Apple Pie Ice Cream recipe, peel the apples & chop them into really small cubes.
In a large, heavy saucepan, melt butter on medium heat until foam subsides, then raise heat to high and stir in apples and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Next add the cinnamon powder into the pan and cook till the apples get caramelized. Turn off the heat and leave it for cooling.
Take whipping cream in a big bowl and keep it whisking till you are able to see the peaks. Now add the condensed milk into the whipped cream and whisk it again for like 5 to 7 minutes.

Add rest of the cinnamon powder to bowl and whisk everything together till everything is mixed properly. At this point you can taste it and decide if you want to add powdered sugar if want it more sweet. Whisk again if added sugar.
Now take a loaf pan and transfer the mixture into and cover it tightly using a cling wrap. You can have to after 5-6 hours but for best results, leave it overnight in the freezer.
In the end, add the apple cubes and fold it gently.
Now take a loaf pan and transfer the mixture into and cover it tightly using a cling wrap. You can have to after 5-6 hours but for best results, leave it overnight in the freezer.
Serve Apple Pie Ice Cream to your kids after their weekend meal of Pav Bhaji. You can also serve this ice cream to your guests.

title: Gopalkala Recipe - Janmashtami Special)
instructions: Soak beaten rice in water for about 1-2 minutes (or up to 5 minutes if a thicker variety) until softened.
If the beaten rice is a thicker variety, allow it to soak for about 5 minutes to soften.
Once softened, drain all the water and keep the rice in a strainer for a minute to ensure all water is removed.

Prepare the seasoning: heat ghee in a pan over medium heat, add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add cumin seeds, green chilies, and ginger pieces and fry for a minute before turning off the heat.
Add the seasoning to the drained beaten rice along with yogurt, finely chopped cucumbers, grated coconut, and salt to taste; stir gently to combine and adjust salt as needed.
Stir in the chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the Gopalkala as a special dish for Krishna Jayanti (Janmashtami Special).

title: Corn And Peas Curry Recipe
ingredients: 2 Corn Cob, cut into 1 inch pieces
instructions: To begin making the Corn and Peas Curry Recipe, we will first cook the corn on the cob.
Into a pressure cooker, add the cut corn along with salt and water, pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once done, open the cooker, drain off the excess water and keep the corn aside.
The next step is to make the gravy for the Corn and Peas Curry.
Heat a skillet on medium flame, dry roast the cumin seeds, coriander seeds and dry red chillies until fragrant (about 3-5 minutes).
