Transfer the dry roasted whole spices into a mixer jar.
In the same pan, add some oil, then add the garlic cloves, ginger and onions and sauté for 5-7 minutes until the onions turn soft and lightly brown.
Stir in the grated coconut and sauté for a minute.
Mix well, turn off the heat, allow the mixture to cool, and add it to the mixer jar with the whole spices.
Grind everything into a smooth paste using some water and set aside.
Heat a kadai with oil on medium flame, add mustard seeds and curry leaves and allow them to crackle.
Add the tomato puree and bring it to a single boil.
Once boiling, add the freshly ground spice‑onion paste mixture and mix well.
Add the turmeric powder, garam masala powder and Kashmiri red chilli powder and mix well.
Add the boiled corn to the gravy and adjust the consistency by adding water as needed.
Add the peas, cover and bring the curry to a brisk boil; check salt and spices and adjust the taste.
Turn off the heat, transfer the Corn and Peas Curry to a bowl and serve hot.
Serve the Corn and Peas Curry with Jeera Rice, Lachedar Kakdi Pyaz Kachumber (onion cucumber salad) and optionally finish the meal with Paan Matka Kulfi.

title: Sindhi Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Basmati rice , cleaned and washed
instructions: To begin making the Sindhi Pulao Recipe, take the cleaned and washed rice in a large bowl, cover it completely with water and soak it for at least 10-15 minutes. Drain the water and keep aside.

Next, heat oil or ghee in a pressure cooker, add the onions, a pinch of salt and fry the onions till they become golden brown in colour. Make sure you saute the onions on low heat, else they will brown too quickly and wont get caramelized.
Once the onions are caramelized, add the green chilies, cumin seeds, bay leaves, cinnamon and tomato to the onions and sauté them for another 2 minutes until the tomatoes have become soft.
Stir in the rice to the spices and salt to taste in the cooker and add 3-1/2 cups of water. Cover the lid of the pressure cooker, place the weight on and cook the rice until you hear one whistle.
After the first whistle, turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure cooker to rest, so the pressure released naturally on its own. This takes about 10 minutes. Once the pressure has released open the cooker and fluff the rice with a fork.
The delicious and fragrant Sindhi Pilaf with Caramelised Onions, is ready to be served.
Serve Sindhi Pulao Recipe along with Sai Bhaji and Lauki Raita for a weekday meal. You can also pack this meal in your Lunch Box.

title: Healthy Ragi & Rice Breakfast Porridge Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Palm sugar, or to taste
instructions: To begin making the Healthy Ragi & Rice Breakfast Porridge Recipe, we will first combine the ragi flour, cocoa flour in a sauce pan. Add little milk at a time and make a lump free mixture.

Place the saucepan on medium heat and keep stirring continuously until the ragi cocoa porridge mixture thickens. Once you notice the ragi porridge thickening, add the cooked rice, flax seed powder, almond powder and sugar.
Stir well until you get a thick porridge like consistency. Check the taste and adjust sugar. Add milk or water to adjust the consistency.
Serve Healthy Ragi & Rice Breakfast Porridge Recipe with Vegan Instant Coffee Recipe for a quick complete breakfast or Turmeric Milk Recipe (Haldi Doodh) during snack time for kids.

title: Beetroot Carrot Raita Recipe
instructions: Grate the carrots and beetroots and set aside.
Whisk yogurt in a bowl, then add roasted cumin powder, red chilli powder, chaat masala, and salt to taste.
Add the grated carrot and beetroot, mix everything well, and garnish with mint leaves. Serve cold.
Serve the Beetroot Carrot Raita along with Peshawari Chole and Phulkas for a weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Quick Pulao With Onions And Tomatoes Recipe
ingredients: Few sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Quick Pulao With Onions And Tomatoes, firstly prepare all the ingredients.
Heat ghee in a heavy bottomed pan and add cumin seeds. Once it splutters, add the green chillies and curry leaves.
After a minute, add the onions and cook till they become soft and translucent. Add the tomatoes and cook for about a minute or two.
Add the leftover rice, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt and cook for about 3 to 5 minutes.
Once done, switch off the stove, put lemon juice on the quick pulao, mix and garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Pair Quick Pulao With Onions And Tomatoes along with Burani Raita or any Raita of your choice and a roasted Papad. It can be packed for picnics or lunch boxes.

title: Rice With Quinoa Recipe- Pressure Cooker Method
instructions: Rinse the rice and quinoa together well under running water.
Place rice and quinoa along with two cups of water in the pan of the pressure cooker.
Keep the weight on, cover the pressure cooker. Cook the rice in the pressure cooker on medium high heat and after the first whistle turn the heat to low.
Once you turn the heat to low, simmer the rice for 3 minutes.
After 3 minutes, turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally and then open the pressure.
Serve Rice and Quinoa with Masoor Dal Gassi, Muttaikose Poriyal and a bowl of curd.

title: Curry Leaves Buttermilk Recipe - Curry Patta Chaas Recipe
instructions: Keep the curd ready (store‑bought or homemade).
In a mixer jar, combine the curry leaves, salt, black pepper powder, and green chilli and grind to a coarse paste.
Add the curd and water and blend again until the buttermilk is well combined.
Pour into a glass and serve chilled.
Serve the curry leaves buttermilk along with a healthy meal such as Iyengar style vendhaya keerai pulao, onion bajji, and South Indian kosambari.

title: Matta Rice Peas Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Red matta rice, soaked in water for 30 minutes
instructions: Pressure cook the matta rice with 4 cups of water in a pressure cooker for about 6 whistles until just cooked.
Heat a kadai with ghee, add whole spices (cardamom pods, cinnamon sticks, bay leaf, and cumin seeds) and allow them to splutter.
Add green peas and fry for 10 seconds. Add the cooked rice, stir well, sprinkle salt and sugar to taste, mix everything, and let it cook for 2 more minutes.
Switch off the heat; the pulao is ready to be served.
Serve the Matta Rice Peas Pulao with Spinach Paneer Kofta Curry, Palak Paneer, and Lauki Raita.

title: Quick Beetroot Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 2 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped, for garnish
instructions: To begin making the Quick Beetroot Pulao, cook rice either in a pressure cooker or open pan method like you normally do and keep aside. The grains needs to be fluffy and separate for this recipe.
Next, heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add the cumin seeds and let it splutter.
Add the coriander and black pepper powder and sauté for about 15 seconds.
After 15 seconds, add the cubed beetroot, season with a little salt and mix well.
Sprinkle a little water, cook the beetroot cubes well with the lid closed.
Once the beetroot cubes are cooked, add the cooked rice and stir well.
Add salt if required, switch off the flame and add lemon juice and mix well.
Garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve this Quick Beetroot Pulao with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, Boondi Raita or any other Raita of your choice in your kids lunch box or have it for a nutrient enriched light lunch.

title: Strawberry Yogurt Lassi Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Honey, or cane sugar (depending on the sweetness of strawberries)
Mint Leaves (Pudina), as required and chopped
instructions: Remove the green head of the strawberries and chop them roughly.
Add all the ingredients—including curd, milk, honey, cardamom powder, strawberries, and ice cubes—into a blender and blend until smooth and frothy.
Add more milk or water to adjust the consistency to your preference.
Pour into tall glasses, garnish with mint leaves and sliced strawberries, and serve chilled.
Serve the Strawberry Yogurt Lassi as an evening drink alongside Baked Mathri and Iyengar Style Masala Toast.

title: Savory Shrimps On Skillet Recipe
instructions: Devein and de-shell the shrimps, keeping the tail on if desired.
In a small bowl, mix together the sauce ingredients, add the shrimps, mix well, and marinate for 20 minutes.
Add 3-4 drops of orange food color to the marinated shrimps and mix well (optional).
Heat a skillet, add 1/2 tablespoon butter, melt, then remove shrimps from the marinade and place them in the skillet without overcrowding.
Fry in two batches if needed; reserve the remaining sauce. Cook on medium heat for about 2 minutes on one side, then flip.
Fry the other side until browned and cooked through, then remove to a plate and repeat for the next batch.
Turn off the stove, combine all fried shrimps in the same skillet and drizzle the reserved sauce over them.
Mix well and serve.

title: Spicy Lemon Chicken Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 1 Red Bell pepper (Capsicum), cut into squares
instructions: Thoroughly wash and clean the chicken, and cut it into cubes.

In a mixing bowl, combine the chicken pieces with the bell peppers, onions, lemon juice, dried thyme, red chilli flakes, black pepper powder, olive oil, and salt; mix well and let marinate for about 1 hour.
Skewer the ingredients by placing a red bell pepper piece, a chicken cube, and an onion chunk in sequence, then repeat the sequence once more, ensuring the skewer is not overcrowded.
Heat a grill pan, drizzle some oil, place the skewers on it, and cook for at least 25 minutes, brushing with extra marinade and turning frequently for even cooking.
Serve the kebabs with tzatziki dip, sliced onions, and green chutney.

title: Chatpata Aam Panna Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Black pepper powder, crushed coarsely
instructions: To begin making the Chatpata Aam Panna Recipe, first we will cook the mangoes.
Peel the skin of the mango and place the whole raw mango into the pressure cooker with 1/4 cup of water. Pressure cook the mango for 3 to 4 whistles and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally. Once the pressure releases, squeeze out the pulp from the raw mango until all the pulp is out. Discard the see of the mango.
You can either puree this pulp or mash it with a potato masher, depending on the texture you want from the Aam Panna Spritzer.
Roast the fennel seeds in a pan over medium heat until crisp. Once the fennel seeds are roasted, crush them with a pestle and mortar and keep aside.
Once you have the raw mango pulp ready, add the cardamom powder, black pepper powder, crushed fennel seeds, kala namak. Stir well to combine.
When you are ready to serve, pour the Bisleri Fonzo into the raw mango pulp, some ice cubes and stir well to combine.
Pour the Chatpata Aam Panna into serving glass and serve chilled immediately.
Serve Chatpata Aam Panna with Raj Kachori Recipe or Bhel Puri With Raw Mango Recipe when you have a chaat party at home.

title: Palak Paratha Recipe-Spiced Spinach Flatbread
ingredients: 200 grams Spinach Leaves (Palak), washed and finely chopped
1 teaspoon Fennel seeds (Saunf), roasted and coarsely pounded
instructions: In a large bowl combine all the ingredients and knead, adding a little water at a time to make a firm and smooth dough; add one tablespoon of oil to coat the dough, knead again, cover and set aside for 15 minutes.
Knead once more and divide the dough into 8 portions; preheat an iron skillet on medium heat.
Roll each dough portion into a ball, flatten with the palm, toss in flour and roll out into circles about 3 inches in diameter; drizzle a little ghee and spread it on the rolled dough.
Fold the circle into a semi‑circle, then fold again to form a small triangle; toss the triangle in a little flour, roll it out gently into a larger triangle. Repeat with the remaining dough portions.
Heat the skillet on medium‑high, place one rolled paratha on it; when air pockets appear, flip and smear about ½ teaspoon of ghee, then press lightly with a flat spatula and turn to cook.
Flip to the other side, press and turn similarly until brown spots appear and the paratha is slightly crisp; remove from heat and serve hot.
Repeat the process with the remaining portions, stacking cooked parathas one above the other and serve hot.
Optional – No Oil Method: Skip smearing with oil; cook the paratha directly over the flame like a chapati until fully cooked on both sides and serve with raita and chutney.
Serve the Palak Paratha with Batata Nu Shaak, Baingan Bharta, or any other dry vegetable or vegetable in gravy.

title: Bottle Gourd Ice Cream Recipe - Lauki Ice Cream
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Slivered Almonds (Badam), or chopped almonds
instructions: Wash, peel the lauki and grate/shred the bottle gourd and keep aside.
In a shallow frying pan, heat a tablespoon of ghee and stir fry the shredded bottle gourd for about 3-4 minutes on medium heat, until most of its moisture is evaporated and the lauki appears lumpy.
Add milk to the pan and keep stirring. Bring it to a boil.
Once the milk and lauki have come to a boil, add sugar and cook on medium flame, stirring until the milk is reduced to half of its initial quantity (about 20-30 minutes).
Turn off the heat and allow the mixture to cool down to room temperature.
Pour the cooled mixture into a blender and blend for about 2 minutes.
Take an airtight container, pour the mixture into it and add 2 tablespoons of fresh cream (malai) on top. Wrap with cling wrap.
Freeze the bottle gourd ice cream for 4 to 5 hours until set.
After 3-4 hours, take the container out of the freezer, put all its content in a deep mixing bowl and beat the ice cream with a handheld mixer for about 2-3 minutes.
Add chopped almonds and cardamom powder, saving a few chopped almonds for garnish. Beat the ice cream again for about 30 seconds.
Pour the mixture back into the airtight container and freeze for 6 hours or overnight.
Scoop out and serve the bottle gourd ice cream (lauki ice cream) as a summer dessert.

title: Tangy Raw Beetroot & Tomato Chutney Recipe
instructions: To begin making Tangy Raw Beetroot & Tomato Chutney, get all the ingredients prepped and handy.
In a food processor, add coarsely chopped raw beetroots, coriander, tomatoes, chillies, and pulse till they form a coarse mix.

Add lemon juice and salt to taste, then blend again for about 20 seconds or until the desired consistency, using a little water as needed. Transfer to a serving bowl and adjust lemon and salt if necessary.
Serve the Tangy Raw Beetroot & Tomato Chutney with Carrot Onion Uttapam, Paruppu Podi, and South Indian Filter Coffee for breakfast.

title: Methi And Palak Paratha Recipe
ingredients: Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), a bunch, roughly chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, add cumin seeds and let them sputter, then add chopped onions and grated garlic and fry until fragrant.
When the onions turn light brown, add turmeric powder and red chilli powder, sauté for about a minute, then add cumin powder and coriander powder and sauté for a few seconds.

Add the chopped spinach and methi leaves along with salt and chaat masala, stir and cook over medium flame until the greens release water and it evaporates completely; turn off heat, transfer the mixture to a bowl and let it cool completely.
In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour with the cooled spinach‑methi mixture and rub together with your fingers.
Knead the mixture with a little water at a time to form a firm, smooth dough; drizzle a teaspoon of oil on top and continue kneading until the dough is smooth but not sticky.
Divide the dough into 8‑10 equal portions, roll each portion into a flat paratha about 6‑7 inches in diameter.
Preheat a skillet (tawa) on medium heat; place a rolled paratha on the hot tawa and cook for about a minute on each side until brown spots appear.
If using the No Oil method, skip smearing oil and cook the paratha directly over the flame like a chapati until fully cooked on both sides; serve hot with raita and chutney.

If using the With Oil method, when brown spots appear, smear a teaspoon of ghee or oil on both sides and continue cooking until the paratha turns golden brown and lightly crisp; repeat for remaining parathas.

title: Easy Homemade Sugar Free Dates Flavored Yogurt Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Dates, pitted (plus reserve 2 dates chopped to garnish)
instructions: To begin making Easy Homemade Sugar Free Dates Flavored Yogurt Recipe, blend dates with just enough milk to make a fine paste.
Run the date paste through a sieve with small holes to remove all the skin. Keep the smooth date paste aside.
Heat the rest of the milk in a saucepan; stir in powdered milk and mix well.
Reduce heat and stir in the date paste; whisk until well incorporated and smooth. Heat the whole mixture until it is hot but not boiling.
Remove from heat and let cool until it is lukewarm. You should be able to hold a clean finger in it for at least 10 seconds without feeling uncomfortable. Do not let it cool too much.
Once it reaches that temperature, gently stir in the starter culture; plain yogurt and whisk until smooth.
Gently decant the date flavored mixture into containers in which you want the yogurt to set.

There are various ways you can incubate the mixture to form yogurt. I normally place the bowls in an insulated container which has a lid and leave it aside for 6 to 8 hours or until the yogurt has set completely; it all depends upon the culture used, the temperature of the yogurt, and whether you want it sweet or sour.
If you have an oven, you can turn the oven on and heat it until it reaches 120 degrees F; turn it off, place the yogurt container in the oven, close the door but leave the oven light on.
Incubate for 4 to 6 hours or more if you want a tarter yogurt. Check in between to see if it has set.
Once set, refrigerate until serving time. Enjoy sugar free date yogurt topped with more dates!
Serve Easy Homemade Sugar Free Dates Flavored Yogurt Recipe as a cheat dessert after a dinner like Paneer Pulao With Green Peas, Yellow Pumpkin Dal, and Kachumber Salad.

title: Raw Banana Chivda Recipe
instructions: To begin making Raw Banana Chivda Recipe, heat oil in a kadai on medium flame.
Wash and peel the bananas and directly grate the bananas into hot oil. Fry in batches. Peel only that much portion of banana that can be fried in one batch, to avoid the change in colour.
Let them fry on low to medium heat and keep turning until they turn golden brown and crisp. Drain on an absorbent paper and set aside.
In the same frying pan, fry peanuts, cashews and almonds till they turn light golden brown. Keep aside on kitchen towel.
In the same manner, fry green chillies and curry leaves. Fry till they turn crisp and all the moisture evaporates from them. Drain on kitchen towel.

In the end, fry raisins. Be careful while frying raisins, as they burn quickly. Fry only for a few seconds. Combine fried grated banana, peanuts, cashews, almonds, raisins, green chillies and curry leaves in a wide bowl.
Add salt, red chilli powder, chaat masala and powdered sugar to it. Mix well.
Once it cools down completely, store the chivda in an airtight container.
Serve Raw Banana Chivda Recipe with Masala Chai Recipe - Indian Spiced Tea or coffee during evening.

title: Spiced Onion Pulao Recipe - Pyaz Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Mint Leaves (Pudina) , loosely packed & finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Spiced Onion Pulao Recipe, wash the rice thoroughly, and drain off all the excess water using a strainer.
Now pat dry the rice on an absorbent paper.
Heat a kadai, on medium-low flame, and dry roast the rice for about 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously. We are not looking for any colour here.
Turn off the flame and set aside.
Heat a pressure cooker with ghee on medium flame, into the cooker add the whole spices - bay leaves, cloves and cinnamon and allow them to sizzle.
Once the spices sizzle, add the onions, ginger and garlic and saute until the onions have softened.
Now add the slit green chillies, chopped tomatoes and saute until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Once soft, mash the tomatoes slightly with the back of the ladle.
Finally add in the dry roasted rice, 2 cups of water, salt to taste and close the pressure cooker.
Pressure cook for 2-3 whistles and turn off the heat. Wait for the cooker to depressurise and then open the lid.
Once done, gently fluff with the Spiced Onion Pulao and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve Spiced Onion Pulao Recipe along with Smoked Dhaba Dal Recipe or Bhune Pyaz Ka Gosht Recipe, Onion Raita Recipe and finish the meal with a dessert of Oats Apple Phirni Recipe.

title: Aloo Methi Masala Recipe - Potato & Fenugreek Leaves Gravy
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Turmeric powder (Haldi), (to add to boiling veggies)
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the potatoes with required water, close the cooker and cook till it releases 2 whistles.
Switch off the gas and let the pressure release naturally; then open the cooker and take out the potatoes.
Let the potatoes cool, peel them and cut into cubes. Set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan. Once the oil is hot, add cumin seeds and asafoetida and allow the cumin seeds to crackle.
Add the bay leaf, whole black peppercorns, dry red chilli and cloves. Roast for about a minute.
Add the onions and cook till they turn soft and translucent. Then add the tomatoes, salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and cook till soft and mushy.

Cook for about 3–4 minutes, then add the methi leaves and cook till they become soft. Add the cubed potatoes, required water, garam masala, and salt; mix and give a brisk boil for 3–4 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Check the taste and adjust if needed. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves, transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve Aloo Methi Masala with Pudina Tawa Paratha, Jeera Rice, and Carrot Raita for a complete meal.

title: Diwali Cornflakes Mixture Recipe - A Savory Evening Tea Snack
instructions: To begin making the Diwali Cornflakes Mixture Recipe, first get all the ingredients prepared and ready.
Our first step is to deep fry the Makai (corn) Flakes. Preheat the oil for deep frying in a wide deep frying pan over medium heat.
Add a handful of Makai (corn) flakes at a time and deep fry them until golden, crisp and puffed up. It takes just a few seconds to deep fry these flakes. They are similar to papads.
Once you have deep fried the Makai (corn) flakes, drain them on kitchen paper towels and keep aside.

In the same oil, place the poha in a steel colander and deep fry the poha by dipping the colander in the oil. Once you notice the poha has puffed up, immediately remove the poha from the oil. Place them on kitchen paper towels to drain the excess oi.
Finally we will roast the nuts in the oil. Place the nuts and peanuts in the same colander and deep fry them until golden brown and crisp. Once done drain and keep aside.
Finally deep fry the curry leaves and raisins in hot oil placed in the colander. Once crisp and raisins have puffed up, remove from oil and place on the paper towel to drain.

Place all the fried ingredients in a wide mixing bowl or a flat baking sheet. Sprinkle the salt, red chili powder, sugar and asafoetida powder and stir to combine well with your hands. Do this when all the ingredients are hot, so the spices and salts get well combined into them.
Check the spice and salt levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Once done, cool and store the Corn Flakes Mixture in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
Serve the Corn Flakes Mixture as a perfect evening snack or for festivals like Diwali along with a cup of Masala Chai.

title: Jeera Hing Aloo Recipe - No Onion No Garlic Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, as required, chopped for garnish
instructions: To begin making the Jeera Hing Aloo recipe, wash and clean the potatoes.
In a pressure cooker add the potatoes along with some water and salt. Close the pressure cooker and pressure cook for 2 whistles. Turn off the flame and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure has released naturally, open the pressure cooker and drain off all the excess water.
Peel the baby potatoes and set aside.
In a wide pan heat oil. Add cumin seeds and hing. After it crackles, add the ginger and mix well.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, salt and give it a quick mix and then add potatoes immediately.
Mix gently so all the spices are coated all over the potatoes. Sauté for 5 minutes on low flame until the potatoes get a lightly roasted texture and a good outer crust.
Add amchur powder, give the Jeera Hing Aloo a good mix.
Turn off the heat and garnish the Jeera Hing Aloo Sabzi with coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve Jeera Hing Aloo Sabzi as an appetizer or as side dish with Phulka or Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha and Gujarati Kadhi for an everyday meal.

title: Tender Coconut Ice Cream Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Tender coconut meat, + Little extra
instructions: In a grinder or blender, grind tender coconut meat with tender coconut water to make a puree; then add full-fat cream, sugar, and condensed milk and beat until well combined.
Chop the extra tender coconut into small chunks and mix it into the tender coconut ice cream.
Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe bowl with a tight lid and freeze for a minimum of 5-6 hours.
Remove the bowl, scoop the frozen ice cream into a serving bowl, drizzle with honey and add broken ice cream cone pieces, then enjoy.
Serve Tender Coconut Ice Cream as a dessert after a simple meal of Mixed Vegetable Sambar, South Indian Coconut Chutney, and Ghee Masala Dosa.

title: Ratalu Ki Chutney Recipe - Yam Chutney Recipe
ingredients: 150 grams Elephant yam (Suran/Senai/Ratalu), peeled and diced
instructions: Add yam in a pressure cooker with 1/4 cup water and cook until the cooker releases 2 to 3 whistles; then open and set aside.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dry red chilli for about a minute; set aside.
Heat oil in the same pan and add the yam; sauté until it changes color, then set aside.
Combine the fried yam with the dry-roasted coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dry red chilli in a mixer grinder.
Add salt to taste and tamarind paste, then grind to a smooth paste and transfer the chutney to a small bowl.
Prepare the tempering: heat oil in a tadka pan, add mustard seeds and asafoetida, allowing the seeds to crackle.
After 30 seconds, add chana dal and curry leaves; roast for another 15 seconds, then switch off the heat and pour the tempering over the chutney.
Serve the Ratalu Ki Chutney with Keerai Sambar, steamed rice, beetroot thoran, or Dosa/Idli.

title: Paneer Biryani Recipe
ingredients: 250 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), cut into medium sized cubes
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients and keep them ready for cooking.
Wash and rinse the rice in water and keep aside.
Heat ghee in the pressure cooker over medium heat; add the onion, ginger and garlic and sauté until the onions have softened and turned slightly brown.
Stir in the spices - cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaves and sauté for a couple of minutes.
Stir in chopped tomatoes along with turmeric powder, chili powder and coriander powder. Sauté until the tomatoes become mushy and soft.
Add the paneer, rice, coconut milk and salt. Stir well to combine. Add 1‑½ cups of water and close the pressure cooker.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles. After 2 whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally. Once released, open the cooker, wait a few minutes, then add the chopped pudina leaves and stir to combine the Paneer Biryani.
Serve hot Paneer Biryani along with Onion Raita (Pyaz Ka Raita) for a simple soulful meal.

title: Moong Dal Khichdi Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Moong Dal Khichdi Recipe, first prepare all the ingredients and keep them ready.

Wash the rice, yellow moong dal, and green moong dal and keep aside. Heat oil in the pressure cooker on medium-high heat; stir in the cinnamon, bay leaf, washed rice and dals, turmeric, salt, crushed peppercorns, and the diced vegetables.
Stir in five cups of water and close the pressure cooker.
Allow it to cook until the cooker releases 2 whistles. Turn the heat to low after 2 whistles and keep simmered for 5 minutes. Once 5 minutes of simmering has passed, turn the heat off.
Wait for the pressure to release completely. Once the pressure releases, open the cooker and stir the khichdi to combine all the ingredients.
Heat ghee in a tadka pan, add the cumin seeds and allow them to crackle. Stir in the asafoetida and turn off the heat. Pour this tadka over the khichdi, stir and serve.
Serve the Moong Dal Khichdi with Batata Nu Shaak, Gujarati Kadhi, or Punjabi Kadhi topped with a spoonful of ghee.

title: Turmeric Latte Recipe
ingredients: Black pepper powder, optional, to taste
instructions: Take a saucepan, lightly warm the milk and add fresh turmeric powder. Stir and adjust turmeric to taste.
Add cinnamon and nutmeg powder into the milk and stir again. Turn off the heat and add honey and maple syrup (or vanilla extract) into the milk.
Mix everything well, let it sit for a couple of seconds, then pour the warm milk into a mug and top with grated coconut, a pinch of black pepper powder, and star anise.
Cuddle up with your favorite book and enjoy this heartwarming drink.
Serve Turmeric Latte along with Savoury Baked Arbi Chips for your tea time break.

title: Mixed Vegetable Pulao Recipe
instructions: Wash and soak the rice in 2 cups of water for half an hour.
Steam the vegetables with a bit of salt while the rice is soaking, then set aside.
Grind the whole spices (cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon) into a powder using a pestle and mortar and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee in a large saucepan, add the grated garlic and the powdered spices, and stir‑fry for a few seconds.
Add the soaked rice, salt, green chillies, bay leaf, and the soaking water; increase heat to high and bring to a boil.
When boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the rice absorbs all the water.
Check if the pulao is fully cooked; if it needs to be softer, add a little more water and cook a bit longer.
Turn off the heat and let the pulao rest for at least 10 minutes so the grains firm up.
Stir in the steamed vegetables and chopped mint leaves, then adjust salt to taste.
Transfer the vegetable pulao to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve the mixed vegetable pulao with Boondi Raita, Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, or any raita of your choice, and a roasted papad.

title: Pumpkin Raita Recipe
ingredients: 200 grams Kaddu (Parangikai/ Pumpkin), peeled and grated
instructions: To begin making the Pumpkin Raita Recipe, we will cook the grated pumpkin in a pan.

Heat a teaspoon of oil in a pan on medium flame, add the grated pumpkin, sprinkle some salt to taste and stir fry until the pumpkin wilts down. Cover the pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes and your pumpkin will be cooked.
Pumpkin also releases water when cooked, so there is not need to add water to cook the pumpkin. Once the pumpkin is cooked, transfer to a serving bowl and allow it to cool.

In the meanwhile, whisk the yogurt in another bowl along with some salt, red chili powder, roasted cumin powder and coriander. Finally stir in the cooked pumpkin into the yogurt mixture. Adjust the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Serve Pumpkin Raita along with Ajwaini Tamatar Bhindi and Phulka for a weekday lunch or dinner. Finish the meal with Gulab Jamun Trifle Recipe as dessert.

title: Dangar Pachadi With Grated Carrots Recipe (Urad Dal Raita)
instructions: Whisk the yogurt in a mixing bowl along with the salt and keep aside.
In a small tadka pan, dry roast urad dal till golden brown and allow it to cool.
Using a blender, grind the roasted urad dal into a fine powder and stir it into the whisked yogurt.
Heat half a teaspoon of oil in the same tadka pan; add mustard seeds, finely chopped green chilli, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Let the seeds crackle, then turn off the heat.
Add the tempering to the yogurt mixture and stir to combine well. Finally, stir in the chopped coriander leaves, grated carrot, and chopped tomato.
Serve the Dangar Pachadi with Keerai Sambar, steamed rice, and Elai Vadam.

title: Papaya Banana Smoothie Recipe
instructions: Combine 1 cup of milk, banana, papaya, dates, and ice cubes in a blender or grinder; blend until smooth.
Add the remaining milk and dates, then blend again to combine all ingredients.
Pour the smoothie into tall glasses, garnish with chocolate shavings, and serve.
Enjoy as a mid‑morning snack or with a grilled tofu lettuce/spinach sandwich or oven‑baked sweet potato fries.

title: Boiled Egg With Salt And Pepper Recipe - Finger Food For Babies Above 9 Months
instructions: To begin making Boiled Egg with Salt and Pepper for the baby or toddler, make sure to pick the freshest of eggs for preparing this finger food.
On a saucepan, add 2 cups of water and bring it to a brisk boil.
Place the egg into the boiling water and leave it there for 10 minutes. Turn off the flame.
Drain the hot water and place the egg in cold water. Crack the skin of the boiled egg open.
Cut the boiled egg into bite size pieces and sprinkle some salt and pepper on top of the sliced egg pieces and serve it to your baby/ toddler.
Serve these boiled egg pieces to your baby/ toddler who is above 9 months as a healthy evening snack or as a meal.

title: Bajri Ki Roti Recipe
ingredients: Lukewarm Water, to bind the dough
instructions: To begin making the Bajri Ki Roti Recipe first sift the bajra flour, whole wheat flour and salt together in a deep mixing bowl.
Knead the dough well 1/4 cup of lukewarm water at a time, until it comes together in a smooth ball. The dough will be similar to what we prepare for Makke Ki Roti.
Grease the dough with ghee, cover with a muslin cloth and let rest for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile heat a skillet or tava over medium heat. Dust your rolling surface with little whole wheat flour.
Divide the dough into 6-8 equal portions and roll out a portion of the dough into a round and thick roti. You can shape the roti by pressing out a circle with your fingers as well.
Place the roti over the pre‑heated skillet and cook it for a few seconds on one side or till a few bubbles appear on top.
Turn over the roti and cook the other side for a few more seconds. Lift the roti with tongs and roast over the direct flame till brown spots appear on both sides.

Similarly, prepare the remaining Bajra Rotis. Serve Bajra Roti immediately smeared with white butter or ghee along with Lahsun Ki Chutney or Bharva Baingan, Panchmel Dal and Mooli Raita to make a delicious lunch or dinner for the family.

title: Roasted Peanut & Fried Gram Chikki Recipe
instructions: Grease a rectangular tray with ghee and set aside.
In a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat, add the roasted peanuts and roasted gram dal; stir for a couple of minutes until aromatic, then transfer to kitchen paper towel.
In the same pan, add the grated jaggery on low heat, allowing it to melt; stir occasionally and remove any scum.
When the jaggery thickens and darkens, add the ghee and give a gentle stir.
Add the roasted peanuts and roasted gram dal to the jaggery‑ghee mixture; stir well for another couple of minutes, then turn off the heat.
Spread the mixture evenly onto the greased tray and flatten with the back of a large spoon, wooden spatula, or rolling pin.
Let it cool for 1‑2 minutes; the chikki will begin to set. Cut into squares with a sharp knife if desired.
For ball shape, grease your palm and fingers, take portions of the warm chikki, and roll into balls.
Once shaped and cut, serve the roasted peanut & fried gram chikki with masala chai.
Store in an airtight container for up to a couple of weeks.

title: Onion Bajji Recipe -Vengaya Bajji/ South Indian Onion Pakora
instructions: Begin by preparing the besan pakora batter.
In a mixing bowl, combine gram flour, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, ajwain, asafoetida, and salt.
Add just enough water to form a thick batter that can coat the back of a spoon; set the batter aside.
Heat oil in a kadai over medium heat for deep frying.
Coat each onion roundel in the batter and gently drop into the oil; deep fry until golden brown.
Drain the fried onions on absorbent paper to remove excess oil and serve hot.
Serve Onion Bajji with green chutney and a steaming cup of adrak chai.

title: Meat Masala Stuffed Bharwa Baingan Recipe
instructions: Hold the tip of each brinjal and make two opposite slits.
Add salt to the meat masala and mix well; stuff each brinjal with the meat masala using a teaspoon.
Heat mustard oil until it smokes, then add asafoetida and cumin seeds, followed by the chopped onion; cook until the onion is soft.
Add the stuffed brinjals and roast for one minute; then add the chopped tomatoes and any remaining meat masala stuffing.
Add 1/2 cup water and cook until the brinjals are tender.
Serve the Meat Masala Stuffed Bharwa Baingan with Dal Tadka and Tawa Parathas.

title: Spiced Mulled Apple Juice Recipe
instructions: Bring the apple juice to a boil in a saucepan with the cinnamon stick, nutmeg, cloves, black pepper powder, ginger, and orange peel.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes or until the spices have infused into the apple juice.
Strain the mulled apple juice and serve hot.
Serve the spiced mulled apple juice alongside Jalapeno Potato Cheese Balls with Four Pepper Cheese Dip and Roasted Mushroom & Caramelized Onion Bruschetta for a party.

title: Oats Chivda Recipe- Oats Poha Mixture- No Onion No Garlic
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat and dry roast 3/4 cup oats until golden brown (3-5 minutes); turn off heat and set aside to cool.
In the same pan, roast 1 cup poha for about 5 minutes; transfer to the bowl with the oats.
Heat olive oil in a deep frying pan, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add the raw peanuts and the broken dry red chilli to the pan and fry until the peanuts turn golden.
Add the slit green chilli and continue cooking until the peanuts are well roasted.
Turn off the gas.
Stir in a pinch of red chilli powder, a pinch of turmeric powder, salt to taste, and 1 teaspoon sugar; mix well.
Add the roasted poha and oats to the pan and toss to combine.
Mix in the green moong sprouts and combine thoroughly.
Allow the chivda to cool completely, then sprinkle flax seeds; serve immediately or store in an airtight container.

title: Mamsaam Chops Recipe (Lamb Chops in Black Pepper Gravy)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Whole Black Peppercorns, roughly pounded
instructions: Wash and dry the lamb chops, then half‑cook them in a pressure cooker with 1/2 cup water, salt, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder; cook for about 3–4 whistles.
Grind all the listed masala ingredients to a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan; once hot, add all the dry whole spices and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chopped onions and fry until deep brown, stirring to prevent burning. Add the par‑boiled lamb chops with a splash of water and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the ground masala paste, coriander powder, and whole black pepper; mix well and simmer covered until the lamb is fully cooked and the gravy thickens.
Serve the Mamsaam Chops with hot steamed rice, phulka, and Kerala style chicken tomato roast.

title: Badam Burfi Recipe - Almond Burfi
instructions: Soak the almonds overnight and peel the skin, or place almonds in boiling water for 10 minutes, then cool and peel.
Grind the almonds with milk to a fine paste using a mixer grinder; mix the almond paste with sugar and transfer to a kadhai, heating on high while stirring continuously.
Add a few spoons of ghee and continue stirring until the mixture starts to leave the sides of the pan, about 30 minutes.
Grease a plate with ghee, pour the mixture onto the greased plate, spread evenly, and let it cool completely.
Once cooled, cut the burfi into pieces and store in an airtight container.
Serve Badam Burfi as a sweet dish after a meal.

title: Italian Oats Bread Upma Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Italian Oats Bread Upma Recipe, first toast the bread. You can toast it in your toaster or on a skillet.
Once the bread is toasted, apply the softened butter over the toasted bread and cut the bread into small dices and keep aside.
In a large wok or a kadai, heat a teaspoon of oil; add the onions, carrots and green chilies and saute the onions and carrots on medium heat, until soft and tender.

Once the onions and carrots are soft, add in the tomatoes and oats; drizzle 1/4 cup of water and stir and cook the tomatoes and oats until they turn slightly soft and the oats is cooked through and most of the water is evaporated.
Add in a little salt and the toasted bread pieces. Stir well to combine all the ingredients and stir-fry on medium to high heat for a couple of minutes.
We stir fry just to make sure the bread pieces are well coated.
Finally, stir in the chopped coriander leaves into the Italian Oats Bread Upma and serve it for breakfast or a tea time snack for friends and family.
Serve the Italian Oats Bread Upma Recipe with a glass of Gajar Lauki Juice Recipe (Bottle Gourd Carrot Juice) or Mulled Apple Juice Recipe for your morning breakfast.

title: Dahi Methi Puri Recipe - Fenugreek Leaves Puri With Yogurt
ingredients: 3/4 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), washed and finely chopped
instructions: To begin making Dahi Methi Puri Recipe, we will first make the dough.
In a mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour along with methi leaves, salt, cumin seeds, ajwain and mix well to combine.
Next bring the dough together with the curd to make a smooth and soft dough. If required, use a little water, if the curd is not enough to make a soft dough.
Sprinkle a few drops of oil and smoothen out the dough. Make equal portions of the dough, similar to the size of a lemon.
Dust each portion of the dough in flour and flatten using a rolling pin to a 3 inch diameter of medium thickness.

Preheat oil in a kadai on medium heat, gently slide the flattened Dahi Methi Puri into the kadai, and gently fry the puri with a slotted spatula, continuously yet gently pouring oil onto the puri, allowing it to puff up.
Flip and cook on the other side for about 30-40 seconds. Remove from the kadai and place on an absorbent paper, to drain off the excess oil. Serve Dahi Methi Puris hot.
Serve Dahi Methi Puri along with Sukhi Aloo Sabzi Recipe or Peshawari Chole Recipe alongside some Rava Kesari Bhath and a glass of Kesar Pista Lassi Recipe for a Sunday brunch.

title: Akhrot Burfi Recipe - Walnut Burfi
instructions: In a pan add walnuts and slightly toast over a medium flame until the walnut skin starts getting off.
Peel and discard the walnut skin and grind the walnuts to a coarse powder using a blender. Grease a plate with ghee or butter and set aside.
Place a pan on medium heat, add condensed milk and the powdered walnuts. Cook the mixture over medium heat until it becomes thick.
Stir continuously to prevent the condensed milk from burning or sticking to the bottom of the pan.
Add cardamom powder, mix well, turn off the heat, and transfer the walnut mixture to the greased plate.
Spread the mixture evenly, garnish with chopped pistachios, and let it cool for 8-10 minutes.
Cut the Akhrot Burfi into squares, optionally garnish with additional pistachios or almonds, and serve immediately or store in the refrigerator for up to a week.

title: Bitter Gourd Juice Recipe - Karela Juice
instructions: To begin making the Bitter Gourd Juice Recipe - Karela Juice, get all the ingredients ready.

When you cut the bitter gourd to make the juice, do not remove the skin, as the skin has the maximum benefits and is full of nutrients. If the seeds are tender enough then you don't have to remove the seeds as well.

Place the bitter gourd and ginger into the juicer and extract the juice out. The first juice that comes out is very concentrated, so add some water into the juicer and squeeze out the juice from the remaining pulp.

Pour the juice into a jar, add all the remaining ingredients including lemon juice, turmeric powder, black salt, honey, salt, black pepper powder, mint leaves and give it a good stir. Check the concentration and add water to adjust. Check the salt and flavor levels and adjust as required.
Serve the Bitter Gourd Juice Recipe - Karela Juice immediately for maximum benefits to health and build immunity.

title: Healthy Oats And Nuts Energy Bar Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Dry coconut (kopra) , flakes, or coarse grated
Salt , a pinch or to taste
instructions: To begin making Healthy Oats And Nuts Energy Bar Recipe, take a pan and roast coconut flakes till light brown.
Add 1-1/4 cup oats, pecan nuts, pretzels, dates, toasted coconut flakes, almonds, salt and coconut oil in a food processor. Blend till a soft dough forms.
Take it out in a bowl and add chopped almonds and remaining 1/4 cup oats. mix it well with a wooden spatula.
Take a 9x9 inch pan lined with parchment paper.
Spread the dough on parchment paper and press it properly.
Freeze it for about 40 minutes or till solidified.
After 40 minutes, take the pan out and cut into bars. You can store it away for upto 2 weeks in an airtight container.
Serve Healthy Oats And Nuts Energy Bar Recipe along with a glass of Turmeric Milk Recipe (Haldi Doodh) or Ragi Kanji (Salt Version) Recipe.

title: Khatti Meethi Tindora Sabzi Recipe - Gujarati Tindora Nu Shaak
ingredients: 500 grams Tindora (Dondakaya/ Kovakkai), cut into rounds or thin slices lengthwise
4 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch (chopped)
Raw Peanuts (Moongphali), a handful of roasted peanuts, halved or pounded coarsely
instructions: Steam the vegetable in a steamer or a pressure cooker.
If using a pressure cooker, cut the tinda into the desired shape, place it in the cooker, sprinkle some salt and 2 tablespoons of water.
Cover the pressure cooker, place the weight on and cook the tinda until you hear two whistles; then turn off the heat.
Release the pressure immediately by running the cooker under cold water to avoid overcooking.
Open the pressure cooker once the pressure is released and set the steamed tinda aside.
Heat oil in a large wok or heavy‑bottomed pan; add mustard seeds and cumin seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add curry leaves, the steamed vegetable, and all remaining ingredients except the roasted peanuts and chopped coriander.
Sauté the tindora sabzi until the spices are well coated and combined onto the vegetable.
Check salt and spice levels, adjust to taste, and turn off the heat after the sabzi reaches a soft, juicy consistency (about 3–4 minutes of stir‑frying).
Stir in the peanuts and chopped coriander leaves, then transfer the tindora nu shaak to a serving bowl.
Serve the Khatti Meethi Tindora Sabzi with Gujarati Kadhi, Methi Thepla, and steamed rice.

title: Kanda Keri Nu Kachumber Recipe- Instant Mango Pickle
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups raw mango, peeled and grated
instructions: Keep all the ingredients handy and prepare them as per requirement.
Bring all the ingredients together in a large bowl.
Using hands, massage the mixture so that the jaggery mixes well.
Once well mixed, transfer the mixture into a glass serving bowl.
The relish stays well up to a week in the refrigerator.

title: Spinach Rice Recipe - Palak Pulao
ingredients: 200 grams spinach leaves (palak), rinsed and chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottom pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and grated ginger and sauté for a few seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes and turmeric powder; sauté until the tomatoes have softened.
Add the chopped spinach and salt, cover the pan and cook until the spinach is soft.
Increase the heat to high and let the released water evaporate.
Stir in the cooked rice and sambar powder, combine well, and adjust salt and spices to taste.
Turn the heat to low, cover the pan and simmer for a few minutes until the rice absorbs the spices and turns a rich green color.
Turn off the heat, transfer the spinach rice to a serving plate and serve, optionally with tomato onion raita, tadka raita, or any raita of choice.

title: Spicy Cabbage Rice Recipe (South Indian Style Mutta Kose Sadham Recipe)
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, add cumin seeds and green chillies, and cook for about 15 seconds.
Add the sliced onions and sauté until soft and translucent.
Stir in the shredded cabbage, salt, and turmeric powder; cook until the cabbage softens.
Add the cooked rice, red chilli powder, and sambar powder; mix everything well.
Cover and cook for 2 minutes, then uncover, stir, and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve the spicy cabbage rice with raita of your choice.

title: Baked Chana Dal Vada Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Chana dal (Bengal Gram Dal), soaked in water for 3-4 hours
instructions: Wash and soak the chana dal for 3-4 hours, then rinse, drain and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.

In a blender or food processor, combine the soaked dal, fennel seeds, cumin seeds, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander leaves, ginger, garlic, and salt; grind to a coarse mixture, adding water only if needed.
Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl, add the chopped onion and baking soda, and mix well.
Apply a little oil to your palms, shape the mixture into 2-3 inch flat discs, and place them on a parchment‑lined baking tray.
Bake for 18‑20 minutes, or until the vadas turn golden brown.
Remove from the oven, let cool slightly, and serve warm with mint chutney and khajur imli chutney.

title: Kesar Mango Lassi Recipe - Saffron Mango Lassi Recipe
ingredients: 3 tablespoons milk, lukewarm (plus more cold milk as needed)
instructions: Soak one pinch saffron in 2 tablespoons warm milk and set aside for a few minutes.
Prepare the other ingredients; extract mango pulp and set aside.
In a blender, add mango pulp, curd/yogurt, and cold milk, then blend until combined.
Add chopped almonds (2 tablespoons), honey or sugar, and a few ice cubes; blend again to make the lassi.
Garnish with the remaining chopped almonds and saffron, then serve.

title: Pineapple Jal Jeera Recipe - Sweet & Sour Pineapple Drink
ingredients: 2 cups fresh Pineapple juice, strained twice
2 teaspoons Jal Jeera powder (or to taste)
instructions: In a spice grinder jar, combine all the ingredients listed for the Jal Jeera powder (mint powder, roasted cumin seeds, black pepper powder, citric acid crystals, asafoetida, dry ginger powder, black salt, amchur, cardamom, salt, sugar, and roasted fennel seeds) and grind to a fine powder.
Pass the ground powder through a dry sieve to remove any larger particles; store the powdered mix for later use.

In a pitcher, mix the fresh pineapple juice, chilled water, lemon juice, and the prepared jal jeera powder (adjust amount to taste); stir well and garnish with mint leaves. Add more water if a thinner consistency is desired.
Serve the Pineapple Jal Jeera chilled as a refreshing summer drink, optionally alongside snacks such as Boti Masala Chaat or Banarasi Tamatar Chaat.

title: Cabbage Besan Fry Recipe
instructions: Chop the cabbage into fine thin pieces and set aside.
Add the salt, chilli powder and ginger-garlic paste to the cabbage; mix well.
Add besan and coriander leaves, stir, then add a little water and mix until the cabbage is coated with the besan mixture.
Heat oil in a wide pan, add the cabbage, and fry until the raw smell of the besan disappears.
When the besan starts forming small chunks, cover the pan and cook for about 2 minutes.
Remove the lid and continue frying on medium flame until the moisture evaporates.
Serve the Cabbage Besan Fry with Panchmel Dal, steamed rice, and phulkas.

title: Indian Spiced Brussel Sprouts Sabzi Recipe (Brussel Sprouts Stir Fry)
instructions: To begin making the Indian Spiced Brussel Sprouts Sabzi, first get all the ingredients ready and keep them by the side; when prepped, cooking becomes fun and easy.

Heat a teaspoon of oil in a large wok over medium heat, add the quartered brussel sprouts, sprinkle some salt, and stir‑fry until cooked through, about 5 minutes; then turn off the heat and transfer the sprouts to another bowl.

In the same wok, add a teaspoon of oil over medium heat, add mustard and cumin seeds and let them crackle, then add ginger, garlic, onions, and bell pepper and sauté until translucent; add tomato puree, bay leaf, and the remaining masala powders and sauté for a couple of minutes until the puree bubbles.
Add the stir‑fried brussel sprouts back to the wok and toss in the masala for a couple of minutes until well coated; check salt and spice levels and adjust to taste.
Turn off the heat, stir in the chopped coriander leaves, and serve.
Serve the Indian Spiced Brussel Sprouts Sabzi with Phulka, Sindhi Kadhi, and steamed rice for lunch or a weeknight dinner.

title: Vegan Date & Fig Payasam Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Vegan Date & Fig Payasam, chop the figs and dates roughly.
In a saucepan, add 500 ml of soy milk and soak the chopped dates and figs, bring to a rolling boil, then turn off the flame and let the dates and figs soak.
Transfer the dates and figs, along with some milk, into a mixer jar and grind into a coarse mixture.
In another saucepan, add the remaining soy milk and bring to a rolling boil, then reduce the flame and let the milk reduce to half its volume.
Add the fig-date coarse mixture and cardamom powder to the reduced milk, stir, increase the heat, and after the mixture boils once, switch off the flame.
Garnish with chironji and chopped pistachios.
Serve the Vegan Date & Fig Payasam/Kheer hot or cold as a festival dessert.

title: Ginger Cardamom Chai -Spice Infused Indian Style Milk Tea
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Assam tea leaves, adjustable according to how you want your tea
instructions: To begin making the Ginger Cardamom Chai, place a saucepan on the heat. Add water, tea leaves, ginger and crushed cardamom with the peels intact, into the water and bring it to a boil.
Allow it to simmer, with the heat on medium, for a good 5-7 minutes, till the colour of the water changes to a mild yellowish hue.
At this stage, add sugar and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes till the water gets a deep hue of red and the sugar has dissolved.
Simmering makes the tea strong. If you prefer a light version, reduce the simmering time, and check the colour.
Finally add milk and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and strain the tea through a sieve and pour into a cup.
Serve Ginger Cardamom Tea at a tea party, or enjoy it as an invigorating breakfast or tea-time beverage along with Onion Vegetable Bajji, Omapodi Mixture or Samosas.

title: Broccoli Egg Bhurji Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Broccoli, florets, chopped into small pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a frying pan or skillet and add finely chopped onions.
When onion turns pinkish, add chopped garlic and sauté till the raw smell of garlic goes away.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté till they turn mushy.
Add broccoli florets and cook them for 10 minutes. After 10 minutes, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt and mix everything well.
Break the eggs one by one directly into the skillet, mix well and wait for the eggs to cook.
Once you see the eggs getting cooked, take a spatula and scramble them in the skillet.
Scramble continuously till the eggs are finely minced and mixed well with the onion-tomato-broccoli mixture.
Adjust salt according to your taste and garnish with chopped coriander leaves, then mix well. Switch off the gas and serve hot.
Serve Broccoli Egg Bhurji with Whole Wheat Lachha Parathas and Lauki Raita, or with toast for breakfast.

title: Wheat Grass Shikanji - Wheat Grass Lemonade Recipe
instructions: Soak the cut wheat grass in water for a few minutes to remove the dirt.
Wash it well again, drain the water and then cut it into small pieces.
Add boiled water to it and grind in a blender along with ginger to make a fresh green juice and strain.
Drink the Wheat Grass Shikanji early morning on an empty stomach to get the best results.
Serve Wheat Grass Shikanji in the evening with snacks like Kala Chana Chaat or Baked Mathri; it can also be consumed on an empty stomach every morning.

title: Maize Daliya Khichri Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Govind Bhog Rice, or risotto rice
instructions: To begin making Maize Daliya Khichri, firstly wash rice and maize for two to three times. Keep it aside.
Heat a pressure cooker with ghee and add the ginger paste and rest of the dry ingredients; stir‑fry for a few minutes.
Add maize and rice, stir well with salt and the vegetables for 5 minutes.
Finally, add the water and cook up to 4–5 whistles on medium heat until maize is fully cooked.
Once it is cooked, add garam masala powder and a little water if it dried. Let it simmer for one more minute and serve.
Serve Maize Daliya Khichri along with Boondi Raita, Tadka Raita, or any other raita of your choice.

title: Spiced Prune Chutney Recipe
instructions: Heat a flat skillet with a little oil, crack the ajwain seeds and sauté the onion till it becomes translucent.
Add the tomato and the rest of the ingredients except prunes, mash well and cook until the tomato is cooked.
Add the prunes and ½ cup water, simmer for about 15 minutes, then let cool and blend to a coarse paste.
Serve the spiced prune chutney as an accompaniment for Cabbage Paneer Paratha or spread it in a sandwich.

title: Raab Recipe - Immunity Building Home Remedy Made From Millet Flour
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Dry ginger powder (or freshly ground ginger)
instructions: Combine the bajra flour, wheat flour, and 3 cups of water in a saucepan over medium heat; stir to ensure there are no lumps.
Stir in the jaggery and ginger powder, bring the mixture to a boil while stirring constantly, and continue stirring until it thickens slightly, about 5–8 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, add the ajwain (or cumin) and black pepper, and roast for a few seconds.
Pour the spiced ghee into the hot Raab mixture, taste, and adjust with more jaggery, ginger, or water as needed.
Serve the Raab as a side dish with Rajasthani Gatte Ki Sabzi, Phulka, and Mirchi Lahsun Ka Chunda.

title: Cheesy Garlic Broccoli Nuggets Recipe
ingredients: Nutralite Garlic & Oregano Spread, for pan roasting
instructions: Wash and finely chop the broccoli florets.
Melt Nutralite Garlic & Oregano Spread in a pan, add the broccoli and sauté for about a minute until it softens slightly.
Allow the softened broccoli to cool completely.
Add the cheese, Cheesy Garlic Mayo, corn flour, and salt to the cooled broccoli and mix well; adjust seasoning as needed.
Shape small portions of the mixture into oval kebab-sized nuggets.
Toss the nuggets in breadcrumbs to form a crust.
Heat a skillet and melt a little Nutralite Garlic & Oregano spread over medium heat.
Pan‑fry the nuggets on both sides until browned and crisp.
Serve the Cheesy Garlic Broccoli Nuggets with a Cocoa Banana Almond Date Smoothie or Nutralite Achari Mayo as a dip.

title: Kulia Fruit Chaat Recipe
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the pomegranate kernels with salt, boora, chaat masala, and lemon juice to make the filling.
Let the mixture sit for ten minutes so the flavors meld, or use immediately if short on time.
Peel the cucumber and create longitudinal strips with a peeler; divide the cucumber into three parts (or four if large).
Scoop out the center of each cucumber piece, leaving a base shell.
Stuff each cucumber shell with the prepared pomegranate kernel mixture.
Drizzle a little more lemon juice and the settled masala from the bowl over the filled cucumbers.
Garnish with mint leaves and sprinkle an additional pinch of chaat masala and boora on top.
Serve the Kulia Fruit Chaat as a snack on a hot summer evening, optionally with Watermelon Carrot Radish Juice.

title: Badam Milk Recipe - Almond Milk
instructions: Remove the skin of the soaked almonds and slice the almonds or grind them into a paste.
In a large pan, add the milk and bring to a boil.
When it boils, add almonds, cardamom, sugar and saffron and cook until the milk is slightly thickened.
Serve warm or serve chilled; it tastes fantastic in both ways.
Serve Badam Milk during breakfast or in the evenings along with Aloo Poha to your kids and family members.

title: Saunf Wale Aloo Baingan Recipe - Fennel Spiced Potato And Eggplant
ingredients: 1 cup Brinjal (Baingan / Eggplant), cut in cubes
1/2 cup Potatoes (Aloo), boiled and cut in cubes
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped for garnish
instructions: To begin making Saunf Wale Aloo Baingan, heat a wok in medium flame. Pour oil and add the cumin seeds, let them fry.
Now add the sliced onions, and sauté till the onions become translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste and cook for two more minutes.
Now add the brinjal cubes and sauté, once the brinjals are half cooked add the boiled potatoes cubes.
Stir them and leave them to fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
It's time to add the spices, add chili powders, turmeric powder, and some salt. Give it a stir and cook them by closing it with a lid.
Wait until the vegetables are cooked well.
In the mean, take another small pan and dry roast the coriander and fennel seeds in low flame till aromatic. Grind it using a mixer to a coarse powder.
Now, transfer the aromatic fennel and coriander powder to the vegetables and stir it in open for few minutes.
Garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves and switch off the flame.
Serve Saunf Wale Aloo Baingan with roti's and dal tadka to make it a weeknight dinner.

title: Jal Jeera Recipe - Indian Spiced Lemonade
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Cumin seeds (Jeera), roasted and powdered
Lemon juice, adjust according to taste
instructions: To begin making the Jal Jeera Recipe, first get all the ingredients together. If you don't have roasted cumin powder, then take some cumin and dry roast it in a pan.
Once the aromas come out, turn off the heat. Allow it to cool and then powder it fine to get roasted cumin powder, preferably using a pestle and mortar.

In a bowl filled with 4 cups of water, stir in all the ingredients including cumin seed powder, black salt, mint leaves, lemon juice, and salt until well blended. Refrigerate for a couple of hours before serving.
When you are ready to serve, adjust the salt and cumin levels. You can also add a dash of black pepper powder or crushed green chilies for extra zing.
Serve Jal Jeera as a welcome drink to guests in summer or for a chaat party, alongside chaats such as Indian Misal Bunny Chow, Karnataka Style Churumuri, or Delhi Style Matar Chaat.

title: Raw Banana Tikkis Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Raw Banana Tikkis, first remove the seeds from the dates and finely chop them. Next, add finely chopped the cashew nuts, ginger and green chillies and dates in a bowl along with some salt and keep aside.
Place the raw bananas in a pot of boiling water for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, cool the bananas completely, peel the skin and grate the bananas into a plate and keep aside.
Place a pan on low heat and add a teaspoon of ghee. Once the ghee is warm, add cumin seeds.
Once the cumin seeds crackle, add finely chopped green chillies, ginger and onions and saute until the onions are browned.
Once the onions are browned, add the grated banana, salt, red chilli powder, dry mango powder, lemon juice, gram flour (besan), clove powder, cinnamon powder and elaichi powder.
Mix all the ingredients until well combined. Stir the mixture for a few more minutes and turn off the heat.
Once the raw banana mixture is cool, add in the chopped coriander leaves and mix well.
Divide the raw banana mixture into equal portions.

Take a portion of the banana mixture in your palm and flatten it a little in circular shape. Make a cavity in the center and place a small portion of the dates filling inside it. Cover the filling completely and seal from all sides.
Prepare the remaining tikkis in this manner until all the raw banana mixture is used up.
Place a skillet on low-medium heat and add a tablespoon of ghee on it. Place the prepared stuffed kebabs on the skillet and shallow fry the tikkis on both sides until they are golden brown.
The process of shallow frying each tikki will take at least 8 to 10 minutes.
Take the Raw Banana Tikkis off the flame and they are ready to be served.
Serve Raw Banana Tikkis along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and a cup of Adrak Chai for a light and healthy evening snack.

title: Gooseberry Ginger Detox Health Drink Recipe
instructions: To begin making Gooseberry Ginger Detox Drink, combine all the ingredients in the blender adding very little water to get the desired consistency.
Once you get a smooth liquid, add some more water and blend the puree once again.
Strain the Gooseberry Ginger puree using a fine mesh strainer into a jug and discard the remaining pulp. Adjust the salt and sugar to suit your taste.
Serve the Gooseberry Ginger Detox Drink with some ice cubes.

title: Tofu Green Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves) , finely chopped
1/2 cup Spring Onion Greens , finely chopped
1/2 cup Green beans (French Beans) , finely chopped
instructions: To begin with the Tofu Green Pulao Recipe, first wash and soak basmati rice for 30 minutes and then strain the water using muslin cloth and keep it aside.
Meanwhile in a blender combine spinach leaves, methi leaves, coriander leaves, green chillies and blend till it forms a smooth puree.
Add oil and ghee in a pressure cooker, once hot; add cumin seeds, bay leaves, black cardamom, cloves, green cardamom, cinnamon stick.
After they begin to roast, add tofu cubes, cashew and fry for about 20 seconds.
Now add capsicum, green peas, french beans, finely chopped spring onions and soaked double beans. After a while add in the basmati rice and stir fry for a minute.
Add the prepared green puree and let it cook for a minute. Add 2 to 3 cups of water and mix everything well.
Close the cooker with a lid and let it cook till the cooker release 2 to 3 whistles. Once done, let the pressure release normally.
Open the lid, servie it in a bowl and garnish it with chopped coriander leaves.
This Tofu Green Pulao can be served with Burani Raita or any other raita of your choice for your weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Diabetic Friendly Moong Sprout Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Spring Onion Greens, finely chopped
Oil, to shallow fry the tikkis
instructions: To begin making Diabetic Friendly Moong Sprout Cutlets, cook the sprouted green moong dal in a pressure cooker using 1/4 cup of water and a pinch of salt. Cook for 2 whistles and turn off the heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Save a hand full of the par boiled sprouted moong, and add the rest of the par boiled sprouts along with green chillies and ginger to a mixer and make a smooth mixture.
To this ground moong sprout mixture, add chopped spring onions, oats, coriander powder, garam masala, season with salt and mix well until all the ingredients come together.
Make small tikkis with the Moong Sprout mixture and keep them ready to pan fry them.
Heat a flat skillet on medium flame, brush a little oil on its surface, once it's hot add a batch of moong sprout tikkis and let it cook on its bottom for a few minutes.
Once the moong sprout tikkis are golden brown on the bottom, flip over and cook the other side as well. To cook one tikki, it will take up to 10 minutes for it to nicely brown on both sides.

Serve the Diabetic Friendly Moong Sprout Cutlet Recipe along with a dip or tomato sauce and a cup of masala chai as an evening snack. You can also make a chaat of this cutlet by adding some onions, chutneys, sev, and chaat masala for a party appetizer.

title: Rajma Cutlet (Kidney Beans Patties) Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Rajma (Large Kidney Beans), soaked and pressure cooked
instructions: To begin with Rajma Cutlet, firstly take the potatoes and kidney beans in a mixing bowl. Add red chilli powder, fennel seed powder, garam masala powder and salt in the mixture and mix everything well.
Once it is done, make medium sized patties out of this mixture.
In a different bowl, mix all-purpose flour with enough water to make a paste.
Dip the patties in the flour paste and roll them gently in the bread crumbs.
Once finished, arrange them in the fridge for an hour.
After an hour, heat oil in a deep fry pan to fry the cutlets. Drop the cutlets and cook on both sides until they turn golden brown.
Serve Rajma Cutlets with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai during your tea time break.

title: Leftover Dal Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Arhar dal (Split Toor Dal), cooked or leftover
instructions: Add the leftover dal (or cooked toor dal), wheat flour, Kashmiri red chili powder, salt, curd, coriander leaves, and onions in a bowl. Mix well and knead into a smooth dough.
If the dough is too watery, add a few tablespoons of flour incrementally and knead until smooth. Cover and let rest for about 15 minutes.
Heat a roti tawa. Pinch a lemon‑sized ball of dough, shape it into a ball, dust with flour, and flatten with a rolling pin to a 7‑cm circle. Rub 1/4 teaspoon ghee on the surface.
Fold two opposite edges so they meet at the edges.
Fold the remaining two edges over the already folded sides, forming a square.
Dust lightly with wheat flour and roll the square as thin as possible.
Place on the hot tawa and cook both sides until done. Rub about 1/4 teaspoon ghee on each side. Remove and repeat with remaining dough.
Serve hot with Lauki Raita, Pumpkin Raita, or any raita of your choice.

title: Chia Seeds Shikanji Recipe
instructions: Add chia seeds to 2 cups of water, mix well, and let it sit for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, add sugar, lemon juice, 3 cup water, black salt, and black pepper powder; stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add ice cubes, the soaked chia seeds, and mint leaves; mix properly and serve in a glass (optional: use honey instead of sugar).
Serve the Chia Seeds Shikanji with Baked Mathri or fresh fruits as a refreshing summer snack.

title: Wheat Paratha Recipe With Pizza Topping
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Oil, and more for smearing on paratha
1/2 cup Homemade Pizza And Pasta Sauce
1/4 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), chopped into small pieces
1/4 cup Red Bell pepper (Capsicum), chopped into small pieces
1/4 cup Yellow Bell Pepper (Capsicum), chopped into small pieces
instructions: To begin making the Pizza Topping Wheat Paratha recipe, firstly add wheat flour, salt, oil in a mixing bowl.
Next add water little by little and start kneading the dough. Knead till you get soft, smooth dough. Cover and let it rest for 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, take a portion of dough and roll it to big chapati. Spread 1 to 2 tablespoons of pizza sauce on the top of the chapati.

Sprinkle some grated mozzarella cheese on the pizza sauce and then spread the chopped vegetables including bell peppers, onions and sweet corn on the top. Sprinkle oregano seasoning and red chilli flakes as per your taste.
Now, roll another portion of the dough to the same size as the first one. Place this chapati over the first one having the toppings, covering the toppings.
Using the edge of the fork, seal the edges of both the chapati, sealing the pizza topping inside.
Place the stuffed paratha on a hot Tawa. Cook it on a low flame using a little oil on both the sides. Cook until the chapatis turn crisp and brown from both the sides.
Once ready, take it on a plate and serve hot.
Serve Pizza Topping Wheat Paratha along with Indian Style Macaroni Pasta for a weekend dinner or make it for your evening snacks along with a cup of Masala Chai.

title: Masala Karela Recipe
instructions: De-seed the karela and slice; do not remove the skin.
Add the karela to a pressure cooker with 3 tablespoons of water, salt, and turmeric powder; pressure cook for three whistles, then release pressure and set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadhai, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle, then add onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add the cooked karela, red chilli powder, amchur powder, coriander powder, and besan; stir to combine the masalas with the karela.
Drizzle a little extra oil on top, mix again, cover the pan, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until everything comes together well; then turn off the heat.
Transfer the Masala Karela to a serving bowl and serve.
Serve Masala Karela along with Panchmel Dal and Phulka.

title: Bread Batata Vada Recipe-Crispy Bread Bonda Stuffed With Spicy Aloo
ingredients: 8-10 Whole Wheat Brown Bread, white or brown
instructions: Peel and mash the boiled potatoes with a potato masher.
Grind the green chilies and ginger in a mixer to a fine paste.
Heat a shallow frying pan with a teaspoon oil. Add the ginger‑chili paste and sauté well.
When the ginger‑chili paste releases its aromas and is cooked, add turmeric powder, coriander leaves, salt and the mashed potatoes. Mix well, turn off the heat and set aside to cool.
Remove the edges of the bread slices and set aside.
Take water in a shallow wide dish. Partially dip each bread slice in water, then drain off excess water carefully without breaking the slice.
Make a medium lemon‑sized ball of the potato filling.
Place the ball in the middle of the wet bread slice, fold the edges and seal the open edges.
Gently roll into a round laddoo shape, ensuring the filling is well sealed by the bread on all sides.
Repeat with the remaining bread slices and keep the bondas ready.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan. Deep‑fry the bondas on medium flame, 3‑4 at a time, until golden colored.
Remove the fried bread batata vada onto a kitchen towel and serve hot.
Serve warm with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Date and Tamarind Chutney or roasted tomato sauce.

title: Carrot, Radish & Peanut Salad with Lemon Recipe
instructions: Keep the grated carrots and radish ready in a bowl.
In a mixing bowl, combine carrots, radish, green chilli, toasted peanuts, cumin powder, ginger powder, lemon juice and coriander leaves; toss the salad well and serve.
Serve the Carrot, Radish & Peanut Salad with Lemon alongside Thepla, Dal Palak, and Dahi Bhindi.

title: Egg Kothu Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Leftover roti, torn into 1 inch bits
1/2 teaspoon Garam masala powder, or egg curry masala
instructions: To begin making the Egg Kothu Paratha Recipe, into a preheated pan add oil and mustard seeds and allow the seeds to crackle.
Once done add the asafoetida, onions, garlic, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves and saute until the onions soften and turn golden brown in colour.
After the onions have become golden brown add the tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and saute until the tomatoes soften.
Once done crack three eggs and add to the onion tomato masala. Stir well until the eggs becomes a scramble.
After the eggs are done add the torn leftover roti. Sprinkle salt to taste and stir well for three to four minutes.
Once all the ingredients are well combined add juice from one lemon and chopped coriander leaves. Stir well to combine and turn off the heat.
Transfer the Egg Kothu Paratha into a serving plate and serve hot.
Serve Egg Kothu Paratha Recipe for breakfast or a quick dinner with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita Recipe.

title: Boiled Peanut Raita Recipe
instructions: Cook the peanuts with 2 cups of water and salt in a pressure cooker for 3 to 4 whistles; turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Drain the excess water from the boiled peanuts and let them cool.
In a bowl, whisk the curd until smooth.
Add water, salt to taste, black pepper powder, and cumin powder to the curd and mix well.
Add the boiled peanuts, chopped mint leaves, and chopped coriander leaves, then mix thoroughly.
Serve the Boiled Peanut Raita with Chettinad Mint Potato Biryani or Punjabi Aloo Paratha.

title: Raw Mango And Spring Onion Chutney Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup spring onion greens, roughly chopped
instructions: Cut and wash spring onion leaves, then place in a mixer grinder jar.
Add raw mango pieces, whole red chilies, cumin seeds, and sugar; add a little water and grind to a thick chutney.
Add oil and blend again for a few seconds; adjust salt to taste.
Serve the raw mango and spring onion chutney as a spread or accompaniment.

title: Pasta Payasam Recipe - Fusion Payasam With Pasta
instructions: To begin with Pasta Payasam Recipe, boil the pasta until al dente and keep aside. Rinse it in cold water to prevent over cooking the pasta.
Combine the coconut and cashew nuts in a mixer-jar and grind using very little warm water to make a smooth paste and keep aside.

Next, heat a heavy bottomed saucepan on medium flame, add the sugar, cardamom powder and bring the milk to a brisk boil, add the coconut cashew nut paste and give it a stir. Stir in the cooked pasta, saffron and simmer for another 5 minutes until the payasam gets a good consistency.
Once done, turn off the heat and transfer to a serving bowl.
Heat ghee in a skillet over medium heat and add broken cashew pieces, fry until golden brown and crisp. Add the raisins and toss for a few seconds. Once done add it to the payasam and serve.
Serve Pasta Payasam as a dessert along with an Indian meal like Spinach Rice Recipe or simply as a snack for your kids.

title: Sweet & Spicy Totapuri Mango Chutney Recipe
instructions: Wash and wipe the totapuri mango.
Peel the mango and roughly chop into small pieces.
In a mixer-jar combine the mango, cumin seeds, salt, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and half the jaggery; grind to a fine paste.
Add the remaining jaggery and blend until a chutney consistency is attained.
Store the chutney in a sterilized bottle in a dry place.
Serve the chutney with puri and aamras for a light summer meal.

title: Veg Noodle Pakora Recipe
instructions: Empty the noodle packets in a bowl and keep the taste maker sachet aside.
Add the noodles into boiling water with a little salt. Once the noodles are half cooked, drain the water and wash under cold water to prevent further cooking.
In a large mixing bowl add all the mentioned vegetables—carrots, capsicum, cabbage—along with besan, salt and the Archana's Kitchen spice mix/tastemaker masala, and dry mix them all with a spoon.
Add the boiled noodles into the bowl and mix well with the vegetables until it becomes a sticky and thick mixture. (Don't add water)
Heat oil in a wok on medium flame for deep frying the pakoras.

Scoop out a spoonful of noodle mix, gently shape it into a pakora and carefully drop it into hot oil. Deep fry the pakoras until golden in colour, then collect them on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil.
Serve the Veg Noodle Pakora hot with green chutney, any favorite dip, or a simple tomato sauce. It can also be served with masala chai as a tea‑time snack.

title: Masala Chai Kulfi Recipe With Bourbon Chocolate Syrup
instructions: To begin making the Masala Chai Kulfi, we proceed by making the masala chai first.
In a pestle and mortar or a mixer grinder, blend the cardamom, cinnamon stick, black peppercorns, cloves and ginger to a fine powder.
Place water in a saucepan, bring it to a boil and add the spices. Add the tea leaves, bring to a boil and simmer for 1 min. Now add sugar and milk as per taste. Stir to combine and turn off the heat.
Strain into a container and let the masala chai cool completely.

To make the kulfi, add the milk and custard powder to a saucepan. Place the milk on medium heat and keep stirring continuously until the milk thickens to form a custard‑like consistency. Add the masala chai mixture to the kulfi mixture and keep stirring.
