Once the milk has reached a custard‑like consistency, add the pistachios and allow it to cool completely.

Once the masala chai kulfi mixture has cooled, stir in the condensed milk and combine well till you get a creamy kulfi mixture. Pour the masala chai kulfi into molds and freeze for at least 12 to 15 hours.
To make the biscuit crumble, powder the Marie biscuits with a rolling pin. Mix the almond meal to it. Add butter to the mixture so it has a sand‑like texture.
Bake at 180 °C for 10 minutes till the mixture is golden brown in colour. Remove from the oven and cool before serving.
For the sauce, melt the chocolate in a pan by double‑boiling method. If not, you can melt the chocolate in a microwave, stirring every 20 seconds to keep it from burning.
Remove from flame and add the cream and bourbon, a dash of salt and mix thoroughly. Keep in the fridge to cool completely.
To serve the Masala Chai Kulfi, on a plate lay down the biscuit and place the kulfis on top of them. Add a drizzle of chocolate sauce on top of Masala Chai Kulfi and some chopped pistachio and enjoy.
Serve Masala Chai Kulfi Recipe With Bourbon Chocolate Syrup after a meal of Aloo Matar Sabzi, Ajwain Puri and Boondi Raita Recipe Spiced With Black Salt.

title: Cauliflower Rice and Lentil Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Masoor Dal (Whole), cooked to hold the grain
instructions: To begin preparing Cauliflower Rice and Lentil Curry recipe, prep up with all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Grate cauliflower using a large grater to resemble grains of rice, in terms of size, alternately you can use the pulse motion in your food processor to mince the cauliflower to resemble rice.

Heat oil in a wide pan, add mustard seeds and let them splutter, add the cumin and cinnamon and allow the cumin to crackle, add curry leaves and turmeric, tip in the grated cauliflower and cook for a minute on medium to high flame, add the tofu and mix gently to combine.
Continue cooking for 2-3 minutes until the cauliflower is cooked, retaining a bite texture (not cooked very soft/mushy).
Season with salt and dish it out onto a bowl.
In another pan heat oil, add the onions and ginger-garlic paste and cook until the onions start to change color, then add the tomato puree and cook this mixture for 5-7 minutes.
Now add turmeric, chili powder, homemade garam masala, curry powder and salt, cook for 5 more minutes until the tomatoes start looking slightly reduced.
Now add the cooked lentils into this mixture and let it simmer for 4-5 minutes until it absorbs all the flavors of the curry.
Pour in the coconut milk and gently stir it around and cook on gentle heat for a couple of minutes, adjust the salt and garnish with coriander.
Serve Cauliflower Rice and Lentil Curry with a nice Raita like Burani Raita or Lauki Raita or a fresh salad like Carrot Ribbon Salad With Asian Sesame Dressing.

title: Chicken Wings With Bhuna Masala Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Chicken Wings With Bhuna Masala Recipe, we will first boil the chicken wings in a sauce pot with some water.
Boil the wings for about 20 minutes till it's half done. This parboiling method will help the wings to absorb less oil once you fry them. Drain the water and keep the wings in a bowl.
Pre heat the oven to 180 degree Celsius and keep it ready until you move on to make the Bhuna masala.
Heat a saucepan with oil, add onions, garlic and ginger and saute until for 3-5 minutes. Add tomatoes and sprinkle some salt and cook until the tomatoes are mashed well.
Now add in the dry masala powders- red chilli powder, turmeric powder, garam masala powder, cumin powder and salt. Mix well and turn off the flame. Allow it to cool.
Transfer into a mixer-jar and blitz it into a smooth paste. Place the bhuna masala in a mixing bowl add the chicken wings to this and coat it well.
Place the wings on a baking tray. Drizzle some oil and bake it in the grill mode for 15 minutes and then flip it over and bake it again for another 15 minutes.
Serve the Chicken Wings With Bhuna Masala Recipe along with some Greek Yogurt Dip or Pudina Dahi Chutney as a delicious appetizer.

title: Kabuli Chana Salad Recipe With A Tangy Orange Dressing
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), ashed and soaked
1 Cucumber, chopped to thin round slices
1 Onion, chopped to thin round rings
1 Orange, sliced into thin round slices
1/2 cup Cherry tomatoes, cut into thin round slices
instructions: Wash and soak the chana in water overnight.
In a pressure cooker, add the chana and water and pressure cook for 6 whistles on high flame, reduce the flame and continue to cook for 15 more minutes; then turn off the flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, drain the water and transfer the chana into a bowl; set aside.
In a mixing bowl, add orange slices, cucumber slices, onion rings, sliced tomatoes, and boiled chickpeas; combine them well.
To make the dressing, combine orange juice, lemon juice, chaat masala, salt and pepper in a bowl; mix well.
Keep the salad bowl and the dressing bowl separately in the refrigerator until serving.
Just before serving, toss the salad with the dressing and serve chilled.
Serve the Chana Salad with orange dressing.

title: Basil Tea Recipe
instructions: Bring two cups of water to a rolling boil in a saucepan.
Wash the holy basil leaves and add them to the boiling water; simmer on low flame for 5 minutes.
Add the tea leaves and turn off the heat; cover the saucepan and let the tea leaves infuse for a few minutes.
Filter the prepared basil tea into cups and add sugar or honey to sweeten before consuming.
Serve the basil tea with a grilled tomato and cheese sandwich or paneer capsicum sandwich at tea time or for breakfast.

title: Khakhra Vegetable Pizza Recipe
ingredients: 1/3 cup Homemade Pizza And Pasta Sauce
1 cup Red Yellow and Green Bell Peppers (Capsicum), sliced
instructions: To begin making the Khakhra Pizza, firstly keep the khakhras and the pizza sauce ready.
You can either make Homemade Khakhras or use store bought ones.
Similarly, you could either use store bought pizza sauce or make your own by following the Homemade Pizza Sauce Recipe.
Getting ahead, keep all your ingredients ready to get started.
To roast the bell peppers.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the bell peppers along with some salt until softened, roasted in texture but still crunchy; turn off the heat and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Spread the pizza sauce on the khakhras, top with a layer of grated cheese, and arrange the sautéed bell peppers, sweet corn, sliced olives, and sliced jalapeños.
Flash bake in the oven for 4–5 minutes or until the cheese has melted.
Remove the Khakhra Vegetable Pizza from the oven and serve hot with a sprinkle of mixed herbs and red chilli flakes.
Optionally add any topping of your choice such as roasted mushrooms, baby corn, zucchini, or spinach.
Serve Khakhra Vegetable Pizza as an evening snack, optionally with Mango Iced Tea.

title: Matki Kala Chana Salad Recipe
instructions: Keep the sprouts ready (use store‑bought or homemade).
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan over medium flame, add cumin seeds; when they sizzle, add matki and kala chana sprouts.
Add dry spices – turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, chaat masala, and salt to taste.
Mix well, cover with a lid, and cook for 3–4 minutes on low flame.
Turn off the stove and transfer the cooked sprouts to a mixing bowl.
Add chopped onion, tomato, green chillies, and lemon juice; mix thoroughly.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander and serve.
Serve as a light dinner or snack, optionally with soup or a sandwich.

title: Shrimp Spinach Cheese Swirl Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Shrimps, cut into small pieces
instructions: To begin making the Shrimp Spinach Cheese Swirl recipe, remove pastry sheet out from freezer at least 40 minutes before preparing the recipe.
Heat oil on medium high heat and add chopped shrimps. Cook for 5-7 minutes.
Once the shrimps turn pink, add cayenne pepper, coriander powder, garlic powder and mix. Add tomato ketchup, sriracha sauce and mix.
Add chopped green onions, spinach and mix everything properly. Sprinkle some salt and mix.
Switch off the stove and let the mixture cool down completely. Brush puff pastry sheet with egg wash.
Once the mixture is cooled, add cheese and mix. Beat an egg to prepare egg wash.
Unfold the pastry sheet and brush it with egg wash on one side. Pour the prepared mixture over it and roll it.
Seal the side using little water. Now cut into small swirls with sharp knife about 1 inch in thickness.

Place them on the greased silver foil kept on a baking tray. Brush each swirl with egg wash and bake at 400°F preheated oven for 10-15 minutes or until crisp. Remove out and enjoy these quick and yummy swirls.
Serve Shrimp Spinach Cheese Swirl along with tomato chutney or any other chutney of your choice.

title: Sarson Saag Pulao Recipe-Spinach Mustard Greens Pulao
instructions: To begin making Sarson Saag Pulao Recipe first prep all the leaves. Take the bathua, palak, methi and sarson leaves. Discard the stems of the leaves, wash them thoroughly and chop and keep them aside.
Wash and keep coriander and mint leaves separately.
Wash the basmati rice and keep it soaked for about 15 to 30 minutes.

Next in a pressure cooker add ghee; add all the whole spices including bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, shahi jeera, cardamom and let them splutter. Next add the onions, ginger and garlic and saute till the onions turn soft.
Now add all the chopped sarson, bathua, palak and methi leaves except coriander and pudina leaves. Saute till they wilt a little.
Add the drained basmati rice and salt and mix everything together. Add water, garam masala and lemon juice, check seasoning and close the lid.
Give the Sarson Saag Pulao 3 whistles on high and turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally.
Once the pressure has released completely, open the pressure cooker and gently stir in the coriander and mint leaves into the Sarson Saag Pulao and serve hot.
Serve Sarson Saag Pulao with Cauliflower and Vegetable Curry (With Almonds and Spices) and Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita for a lovely weekday lunch.

title: Moong Sprouts Salad with Grated Carrots & Coriander Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch finely chopped
instructions: Grate and chop all the ingredients and keep them aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine all the salad ingredients—moong sprouts, onions, carrots, green chilli, coriander leaves, honey, lemon juice and salt. Toss well to combine.
Adjust the taste accordingly and serve chilled.
Serve this Moong Sprouts Salad with Grated Carrots and Coriander along with other dishes.

title: Broccoli And Tofu Green Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1 broccoli, washed and cut into florets
2 tablespoons soy sauce (or Thai fish sauce)
1 inch galangal, peeled and sliced (or use ginger)
2 kaffir lime leaves, torn (or use dried leaves)
1 sprig coriander (dhania) leaves, washed and chopped
instructions: Blend the curry paste ingredients (lemongrass, Thai basil, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, coriander leaves, garlic, and any other paste components) into a fine paste using a mortar and pestle or food processor.
Heat oil in a Kadai and add the curry paste. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until aromatic.
Add the broccoli florets, mix and stir‑fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add the tofu cubes and stir for another 1-2 minutes.
Add 1/2 to 1 cup of vegetable stock, soy sauce, and coconut milk.
Stir and cook for 7-8 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Adjust the consistency of the curry as desired, adding more stock or coconut milk if needed.
Serve the green curry hot with cooked rice and lemon wedges on the side.

title: Khatte Pudina Aloo Recipe - Tangy Mint Potatoes
ingredients: Salt, to taste or sendha namak
Ghee, or cooking oil as required
instructions: Wash and boil potatoes until al dente, peel, cut into cubes, and set aside.
Blend washed coriander and mint leaves (stems removed) with green chilies into a smooth puree and set aside.
Heat ghee or cooking oil in a pan or wok.
Add cumin seeds and wait for them to sputter.
Add the mint‑coriander puree and cook for about 3–4 minutes until the rawness fades.
Stir in red chilli powder, turmeric powder, amchur powder and salt, and cook for about a minute.
Add the mint‑coriander puree again, mix well and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add the cubed boiled potatoes and toss them in the masala.
Add a little water and simmer until potatoes absorb the spices and the liquid evaporates.
Serve hot and enjoy.

title: 7 Cups Burfi Recipe
instructions: Sieve the besan and set aside; grease a plate with ghee and keep it ready for pouring the prepared burfi.
Place a pan on low heat, add the sieved besan and roast the flour for a few minutes, then turn off the heat and transfer the roasted besan to a plate.
In the same pan on low heat, add sugar and 1/4 cup water, stirring until the sugar melts.
Add the remaining ingredients – roasted besan, milk, grated coconut, and melted ghee – to the pan.
Mix well using a whisk to ensure there are no lumps, and keep stirring the mixture while cooking.
When the mixture starts getting thicker, add the cardamom powder.
Continue stirring until the batter froths, becomes thick, and starts leaving the pan; then turn off the heat and pour it into the greased plate, spreading it evenly.
Gently tap the plate to level the mixture and pat it with the back of a ladle to make it smooth.
Allow it to cool for a few minutes, then cut into the desired shape.
Let it cool completely, then remove the cut pieces and store them in an airtight container.
7 Cups Burfi is ready to be savoured.
Serve 7 Cups Burfi as a dessert after a simple meal of steamed rice, Thakkali rasam, and carrot poriyal.

title: Soya Chunk And Green Peas Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Soybeans (Whole Soya dal) or soya chunks
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in water for at least 30 minutes.
Grind the tomatoes along with green chilli and ginger to a smooth puree and set aside.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan with oil, add cumin seeds and let them splutter, then add bay leaf and the tomato puree.

Sprinkle a little salt and cook until the tomatoes are done, about 4-5 minutes. Add all the dry spice powders (red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, salt) and cook for another 10 minutes.
Squeeze out all the water from the soy chunks, add them to the pan and sauté for about 2-3 minutes.
Add green peas and a little water, cover with a lid and cook for about 10 more minutes. After 10 minutes, turn off the heat and serve hot.
Serve the Soya Chunk & Green Peas Sabzi with Tawa Paratha and Beetroot Raita.

title: Oats Cheela Recipe Stuffed With Creamy Palak Paneer
instructions: To begin making the Oats Cheela Stuffed With Palak & Paneer Recipe, in a mixing bowl combine the flour and the oats, add little water at a time to make a semi thick batter. The batter should be the consistency of the dosa batter so you can spread it easily on the tawa. Keep this aside.
The next step is to prepare the filling.
Add Nutralite Classic into a wok on medium heat. Add the chopped spinach, sprinkle some salt and sauté until the spinach wilts down and all the moisture is evaporated.
Once the moisture is evaporated, add the crumbled paneer, cumin powder, chilli powder, salt to taste and Nutralite Veg Mayo. Stir fry for a minute and turn off the heat.
Keep this aside. Preheat a skillet/dosa tawa over medium heat.
Pour a ladle full of the oats cheela batter over the tawa and spread in a circular motion to make a thin crepe/cheela. Spread the Nutralite classic around the cheela and allow it to melt.
Cook the Oats Cheela on both sides by flipping over, until it turns lightly golden and crisp.
Once done, remove the Oats Cheela from the skillet and place it on a platter. Place the creamy palak paneer filling in the center of the cheela and fold it into half and serve.
Proceed the same way with the remaining cheela batter.
Serve the Oats Cheela Recipe Stuffed With Creamy Palak Paneer along with a Papaya Banana Smoothie for a wholesome high protein breakfast.

title: Quinoa Vangi Bath Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Quinoa Vangi Bath, firstly wash the quinoa with water and bring 1 cup of quinoa and 2 cups of water to a boil.
Cover and simmer until it's cooked and all the water has evaporated, approximately 15 to 20 minutes. Let it cool down.
In a heavy bottomed pan, heat some oil and add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add urad dal, chana dal, cashews and stir on low heat until they slightly change colour; then add hing, red chillies and curry leaves.

Now add brinjal and chickpeas with 1 tablespoon of Vangi Bath powder, a little salt, and juice of half a lemon; mix, sprinkle some water and cook until the juices are absorbed and the flavours develop.
It's important that the brinjal and chickpeas absorb the flavour or the dish will taste bland.

Tip in the cooked quinoa, add the remaining Vangi Bath powder, salt to taste, and lemon juice; mix together and cook covered on low heat until heat is evenly distributed, about 3–4 minutes. Serve hot.
If you don't have Vangi Bath powder, simply add 2 tablespoons of Sambhar powder with 1/2 teaspoon of freshly roasted and powdered cloves and cardamom.
Adding a small bunch of chopped methi leaves enhances the flavour of this dish.
Serve Quinoa Vangi Bath with plain yogurt, tomato‑onion‑cucumber raita, or any other raita of your choice.

title: Spiced Rajma Pulao Recipe - Spiced Kidney Bean Rice
instructions: Soak the kidney beans for at least 8 hours, then cook them in a pressure cooker with salt until soft.
Drain the excess liquids from the Rajma; keep the beans for the pulao and reserve the liquid for soup or stock.
Rinse the cooked beans and set aside; rinse the rice in water and keep aside.
Using a pestle and mortar, pound the cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves to a fine powder and set aside.
In a saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon of ghee, add garlic and the ground spices, stir-fry briefly, then add rice, cooked rajma, black pepper powder, salt to taste, and 1½ cups of water.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the rice is fully cooked and water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and let the Rajma Pulao rest for 10 minutes before stirring.
Serve the Rajma Pulao with Punjabi Kadhi or Palak Raita, accompanied by crispy Masala Papad.

title: Crispy Fried Kurkuri Bhindi Recipe Spiced With Cumin & Chaat Masala
instructions: Wash bhindi thoroughly, dry them as much as possible with a kitchen towel and trim the edges.
Slice vertically into thin strips; if they are long, cut them in half horizontally and then slit into long strips.
Place the strips of bhindi into a large mixing bowl.
Sprinkle all the spices, besan and rice flour over the vegetable.
Gently mix with a spoon or clean hands to coat it evenly.
Ensure the okra is evenly coated with the spices, besan and rice flour.
If needed, sprinkle a few drops of water and add more besan or rice flour; this helps the masala paste adhere to the vegetable.
Do a taste test and add more spices if required.
Heat oil for deep frying in a kadai or deep saucepan.
Add the coated bhindi in batches over medium heat, separating clumps as much as possible.
Deep fry until crisp and golden brown on medium‑high heat; the oil bubbles will subside once the okra is cooked.
Remove with a slotted spoon and place on absorbent paper or a kitchen towel to soak excess oil.
Deep fry curry leaves for a few seconds until crisp, in the same oil, then switch off the heat.
Serve hot, spicy, crispy, golden brown bhindis garnished with fried curry leaves.
Serve with phulka and paneer makhani, or enjoy as a snack with filter coffee or masala chai.

title: Karnataka Style Mixed Vegetable Pulao Recipe
instructions: To begin making Karnataka Style Mixed Vegetable Pulao Recipe, first get all the ingredients ready.

Grind the ingredients mentioned in "For pulao masala" including fresh coconut, pearl onions, garlic, ginger, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, coriander leaves, tomato, cinnamon stick, cloves, cardamom and green chillies to a fine paste using a mixer grinder. You can add a little warm water to make it into a smooth paste.
Steam the vegetables using a steamer and keep aside.

Cook Basmati rice in 3‑1‑/2 cups of water in a saucepan, along with salt and bring it to a brisk boil. Once it comes to a boil, turn the heat to low, cover the pan and cook the rice until all the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and allow the rice to cool and then fluff the rice up with a fork.

Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan, add the bay leaf and the ground paste. Saute the pulao masala till it turns brown and fragrant. Add the cooked rice, paneer, bread croutons and vegetables to this masala and mix well.
Check the salt and adjust to suit your taste and serve.
Serve the Karnataka Style Mixed Vegetable Pulao along with a bowl of Tomato Onion Raita for lunch or dinner or even pack it into your lunch box.

title: Sago Kheer Recipe - Tapioca Milk Pudding
ingredients: 1 cup Sabudana (Tapioca Pearls), also called sago
instructions: Wash sago pearls under running water, strain and keep aside.
In a large bowl, add 2 cups of water and soak sago pearls for minimum 1 hour or till they bloom completely.
Heat milk in a heavy-bottomed pan until it starts to boil; simmer, add saffron and cardamom powder, and cook until the milk starts to thicken.
When the milk is pale yellow and reducing from the sides, add the soaked sago pearls and cook for 5 to 6 minutes on low heat.
Add sugar and stir nicely until it dissolves, noticing the sago pearls turn transparent and light.
Add chopped cashews and cook the kheer for another 10 minutes until it becomes creamy in texture.
Turn off the gas and add raisins if desired; avoid adding raisins earlier to prevent splitting the milk. Serve hot, warm, or chilled as preferred.
Serve the Sago Kheer as a dessert alongside dishes such as Palak Makhana, Punjabi Dal Tadka, Garlic Naan, and Jeera Rice.

title: Curd Rice Style Overnight Oats Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Instant Oats (Oatmeal), quick or rolled
instructions: In a mixing bowl, add oats, milk, and 3/4 cup of yogurt; mix until combined and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
After soaking, add the remaining 1/4 cup yogurt, salt to taste, grated ginger, chopped onions, and chopped coriander; mix well.
In a tadka pan, heat some oil, add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add hing, cumin seeds, peppercorns, urad dal, chana dal, and cashew nuts; cook on low heat, stirring to colour evenly.
Add curry leaves, green chilli, and red chilli; once done, spoon the tadka onto the curd oats.
Optional: add pomegranate seeds, raisins, or fresh grapes to enhance the taste.
Serve the Curd Rice Style Overnight Oats on its own with Elai Vadam and Cauliflower Thoran for a healthy and light dinner.

title: Traditional Panakam Recipe
instructions: Take water in a bowl, add powdered jaggery to the water and mix until it dissolves.
Add washed ginger, pepper seeds and cardamom to a mortar, crush everything coarsely using a pestle, and add it to the jaggery water.
Squeeze the juice of half a lemon into the jaggery water, stir well and filter using a strainer.
Add basil leaves and serve the panakam chilled, ideally during hot afternoons or tea time.

title: Carrot And Capsicum Rice Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (dhania) leaves, few chopped sprigs for garnish
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai and add cumin seeds, green chillies, and onions.
When the onions turn a little brown, add the curry leaves and capsicum; cook until the capsicum becomes soft.
Add the grated carrot and cooked rice, and mix everything well.
Stir in the required salt, red chilli powder, and black pepper powder.
Cover with a lid for 2 minutes; then uncover, mix again, and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve the carrot and capsicum rice with raita of your choice.

title: Sesame Bread Patties Recipe (Bread Cutlets)
instructions: To begin making the Sesame Bread Patties (Cutlets) Recipe first prepare the sliced bread by trimming the sides. In a bowl pour some water. Dip 6 of the 10 bread slices into the water, immediately take them out and squeeze out as much of the water as possible.
Place the soggy bread in a bowl. Over this, crumble the remaining slices of bread and mash it all up together to form a soggy dough.

To the dough add the hung curd, finely chopped onions and green chillies. Mix well and sprinkle in the black and white sesame seeds, sugar, red chilli powder, salt and cornflour. Mix it all together very well till it forms a mixture that is wet, but not so soggy that it cannot be easily handled.

Set the mixture aside for 10-15 minutes to rest. Then divide it into 12-14 equal parts and shape them into small patties. To shape the patties with ease, it may help to grease your palms with a little oil so that the batter doesn't stick.
The patties shouldn’t be too thick, as that will make it take longer to cook and absorb too much oil. Ensure that they are thin enough to cook easily and also hold shape.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat. Place the patties on the skillet, drizzle some oil on the top and cook them evenly until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
Keep turning them around until they are golden on both sides. Once done, remove the patties and place them on kitchen paper to drain the excess oil.
Serve the Sesame Bread Patties (Bread Cutlets) along with lime wedges, tomato ketchup or salad and serve it for a weeknight dinner.

title: Eggplant In Coconut Milk Gravy Recipe -Baingan Masala Sabzi
ingredients: 10 Small Brinjal (Baingan / Eggplant), cut to inch long pieces
1 teaspoon Ginger, finely chopped or grated
instructions: To prepare Eggplant In Coconut Milk Gravy Recipe (Baingan Masala Sabzi), combine all the filling ingredients in a mini food processor and make a smooth paste. Set aside.
Slit the brinjals cross wise just half way through, so it remains as a whole. The slit should be just enough to place the filling in. Stuff the above filling mixture in the slit brinjals.
If you are not using small brinjals, then use the filling mixture directly into the gravy just after adding the tomato puree.
Heat oil in a heavy bottom pan (I like to use a cast iron casserole for cooking as it helps in slow and even cooking of this dish).

Add the cumin seeds and grated ginger; allow it to crackle. When the seeds crackle, add the tomatoes, filling mixture, turmeric powder, coriander powder, salt, garam masala powder, chilli powder, jaggery and sauté for a few minutes. Place the stuffed brinjal pieces in the pan adding 1/4 cup of water over it.
Place the stuffed brinjal pieces in the pan adding 1/4 cup of water over it.

Turn the heat to low, and allow the mixture to simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, taking care not to split the brinjal. Towards the last 10 minutes of the cooking process, stir in the coconut milk and cook until the brinjal is soft and tender – when you insert a toothpick it should go in smoothly.
Once cooked, turn off the heat and stir in lots of chopped coriander leaves and allow the vegetable to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Heart Shaped Tea Sandwiches Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons beetroots, peeled and finely chopped
2 tablespoons green bell pepper (capsicum), finely chopped
1 tablespoon spring onion greens, finely chopped
2 teaspoons jam (or any red‑colored fruit jam spread or preserve)
instructions: Begin by preparing the beet‑mayo filling.
Finely chop the beetroot, bell pepper, cabbage and spring onion greens (or use a food processor) and transfer to a bowl.
Stir in 2–3 tablespoons mayonnaise, black pepper powder and red chilli flakes, then mix well.
Taste the mixture and adjust spices and salt as needed.
Use heart‑shaped cutters: the larger cutter for the beet‑mayo sandwiches and the smaller cutter for Nutella and jam sandwiches.
Place a cutter on a slice of bread to cut out a heart‑shaped piece; repeat for all slices.
Continue cutting the remaining bread into heart shapes; leftover bread can be turned into breadcrumbs.
Butter one side of all 12 larger heart‑shaped bread slices for the beet‑mayo sandwiches.
Spoon a small teaspoon of the beet‑mayo filling onto half of the larger slices (about 6) and spread evenly with a palette knife.
Place the remaining 6 buttered slices on top, butter side down, and press gently to form the beet‑mayo tea sandwiches.
For the Nutella sandwiches, spread Nutella on three of the smaller heart slices, then top each with another slice and press gently.
Similarly, spread jam on the remaining smaller heart slices, top with another slice, and serve the assorted heart‑shaped tea sandwiches with masala tea or espresso coffee.

title: Tomato Methi Rice Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), roughly chopped
instructions: To begin making the Tomato Methi Rice Recipe, cook the rice to a fluffy consistency using an open pan or pressure cooker method and keep aside.
Heat ghee in a wok/kadhai on medium flame, add the cinnamon stick, cloves and cardamom and let it release its aroma into the ghee.
Add the sliced onion and saute until it turns translucent.
Roughly pound the ginger and garlic cloves using a mortar and pestle and add it to the pan. Cook until the raw smell goes away.
Add the tomatoes and saute until the tomatoes are soft and well cooked.
Add the red chilli, coriander and garam masala powder, and saute until the ghee separates out on the sides.
Add the chopped methi or fenugreek leaves, season with salt and mix well.
Cook the mixture until the fenugreek leaves are well cooked, and occasionally saute in between.
Once the tomato methi mixture is ready, add the cooked rice into the pan and mix it well using a fork.
Let it simmer for 2 minutes and switch off the flame. Serve hot.
Serve the Tomato Methi Rice Recipe along with Tomato Onion Cucumber raita and roasted papad for kids lunch box or for a light weeknight dinner.

title: Kela Anar Raita Recipe  (Banana Pomegranate Yogurt Dip Flavoured With Mustard)
instructions: In a high-walled bowl, whisk the yogurt, salt, red chilli powder, sugar, dijon mustard and cumin powder until smooth and creamy.
Stir in the diced bananas and pomegranate.
Transfer the raita to a serving dish and refrigerate for two hours before serving.

title: Aloo Aur Mooli Ke Patton Ki Sabzi Recipe - Radish Greens And Potato Stir Fry
ingredients: 2 Dry Red Chillies, broken into half
instructions: Chop off the leaves from the radish.
Rinse the radish leaves a couple of times in a bucket/bowl of running water. Once washed well and all the dirt and mud has been removed, drain the excess water and finely chop the leaves.
Cook the radish greens separately before adding them to the potatoes to retain nutrition and preserve the green color.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add the chopped radish greens, sprinkle some salt and stir‑fry on low to medium heat until the greens start wilting.
Cover the pan and cook the greens until soft, about 8 to 10 minutes. Then turn off the heat and uncover to cool down, preserving the color. Set aside.
Note: Radish greens take a little longer to cook than other greens.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan. Add cumin seeds and broken dry red chilies and sauté until the chilies are lightly roasted.
Add the chopped garlic and stir‑fry until the aroma is released.
Add the boiled potatoes and roast on medium‑high heat until the potatoes are lightly roasted.
Add salt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder and cumin powder, and toss well until the potatoes are well coated with the spices.
Add the cooked radish greens to the spiced potatoes and stir well. Check salt and spice levels and adjust to taste.
Transfer the sabzi to a serving bowl and serve warm.
Serve Aloo Aur Mooli Ke Patton Ki Sabzi with Panchmel Dal, Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, and Phulka for a healthy weeknight dinner.

title: Ridge Gourd Peel Chutney Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Ridge Gourd Peel chutney, roughly chop the peels of the ridge gourd.
Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a pan, stir and roast the peels in the oil till the moisture evaporates and they become crisp.
Alternatively, you can also microwave the peels with oil for about 1-1/2 minutes.
Let the roasted ridge gourd peels cool down and then coarsely grind them in a mixer grinder.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan and add cumin seeds, and once they start to sizzle, add the roasted sesame seed and allow it to crackle.
Add the ground Ridge gourd peels and red chilli powder to the oil and stir for a minute, turn off the heat, add salt and sugar, and mix well and serve warm.
Serve the Ridge Gourd Peel chutney as a side dish along with Phulka or Steamed rice, Maharashtrian Aloo Bhujne and Pumpkin Dal with Garlic Tadka.

title: Saoji Methi Pulao Recipe - Maharashtrian Style Fenugreek Leaves Pulao
ingredients: 2 cups Rice, soaked for 10 to 15 minutes
1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), finely chopped
instructions: Dry roast all the spices for Saoji masala: whole black peppercorns, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, black cardamom, cardamom, star anise, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, poppy seeds, desiccated coconut powder (excluding chilli powder).
Grind the roasted spices in a mixer grinder together with chilli powder into a fine powder; if using dry red chilli, dry roast it with the other spices before grinding.
Heat oil in a cast iron handi, add cumin seeds, then add the finely chopped onions. When the onions become translucent, add the ginger-garlic paste.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes. Once the tomatoes are tender, add red chilli powder, the prepared Saoji masala, and salt.
Allow the masala to cook thoroughly, then stir in green peas and fenugreek leaves and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the soaked rice and 4 cups of water to the pot.
Cook the rice on high flame until most of the water evaporates; then lower the flame, cover with a lid, and let the rice finish cooking through.
Serve the Saoji Methi Pulao with Ajwaini Tamatar Bhindi and Phulka.

title: Strawberry Raita Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Rinse the strawberries in water, remove the green stems, finely chop them, and set aside in a bowl.
In a large bowl, add the yogurt, sugar, salt, cumin powder, and black pepper powder, then whisk until soft, fluffy, and free of lumps.
Stir in the chopped onion, green chillies, coriander, and strawberries; observe the yogurt turn pink and adjust salt and spices to taste.
Garnish the raita with strawberry slices just before serving.
Serve the strawberry raita with Paneer Tikka Masala and Pudina Tawa Paratha.

title: Achari Masala Puri Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Achari Masala Puri Recipe, first get all the ingredients ready. If you don't have achar masala you can also use a few tablespoons of the ready mango pickle to make the puris, it will give a great taste.

In a large mixing bowl, add all the ingredients except the oil. Combine all the ingredients well, add a tablespoon of oil and add little water at a time to make a smooth firm puri dough. Add a little oil on the top and knead more to make a smooth dough.
Preheat the oil for deep frying the puris in a deep frying pan. Divide the puris into 20 small portions and roll the puri dough on an oiled surface into a 3 inch diameter circle.
Deep fry the Achari Masala Puri until it puffs up and gets golden brown in color. Once done, drain from the oil and serve. Proceed the same way to make the remaining puris.
Serve the Achari Masala Puri along with a Urulai Kizhangu Masiyal (Lemony Potato Curry) and Paka Kela Raita for a weekend breakfast, lunch or a weeknight dinner.

title: Papad Raita Recipe
instructions: Roast the masala papad using a stove top or microwave and keep aside.
Take a big bowl, pour the curd and whisk it to a smooth and creamy consistency.
Add the cumin powder, paprika powder and rock salt to taste, mix well and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Just before serving, add the roughly crushed roasted papads and finely chopped coriander leaves and mix well.

title: Vegetarian Kabuli Pulao Recipe - Rice Layered With Chickpea Curry
ingredients: 2 cups Basmati rice, soaked in water for 10-15 minutes
instructions: To begin making the Vegetarian Kabuli Pulao Recipe (Rice Layered with Chickpea Curry), wash and soak the kabuli chana overnight. In the morning, pressure cook with enough water for 3 whistles or till cooked al dente or mildly soft but not mushy, and keep aside.
Wash and soak the basmati rice in water before proceeding further.
Heat a tablespoon of ghee, add the sliced onions and saute until it turns brown and crispy. Keep aside. We will use it while layering the rice.
Now, we proceed to making the kabuli chana masala.
Heat ghee in a pan, and add the finely chopped onions on a medium low heat and saute until they turn translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste, saute until the raw smell goes away.
Add the tomato puree and cook until the mixture comes together from the sides of pan.
Add the paprika, cinnamon, roasted cumin, garam masala and red chilli powder, and mix well.
Now add the boiled kabuli chana, about a cup of water, season with required salt and let it simmer for about 10 minutes.
Keep cooking further till you have a thick consistency of the gravy. Once the curry thickens, switch off the heat and keep it aside.
Now to make the aromatic rice, heat ghee in another wide pan, add the cinnamon stick, cloves, green and black cardamoms and let it flavour the ghee.
Drain the water from the soaked rice, add it to the pan.
Season with salt, add 1.5 cups of water and let it cook with the lid on till 3/4th in medium heat. This will take around 15-20 minutes.
Once the rice is cooked to al dente, drain all the water with the help of a colander.
Now, to layer the Vegetarian Kabuli Pulao, place half the portion of the prepared kabuli masala in the same wide pan.
Add half of the cooked rice above it, add half of the fried onions and mint.
Layer again with the kabuli masala, rice, fried onions, and mint leaves.
Close it with the lid and let it cook in dum with a lid on for 10 minutes.
Serve the Vegetarian Kabuli Pulao (Rice Layered with Chickpea Curry) along with Cauliflower & Cucumber Raita, Paneer Stuffed Millet Patties, and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney for a weekend meal.

title: Homemade Ghee Recipe
instructions: To begin making homemade ghee or clarified butter, first dice the butter into cubes so it melts faster when heated.
Place the chopped butter in a heavy bottomed saucepan, on a medium heat. Begin to melt the butter and keep stirring occasionally until the butter melts completely.

Once the butter has melted completely and has been simmered for about 5 minutes or more on medium heat you will notice that the melted butter starts to foam and boil. At this stage when you move the foam away, the liquid beneath is is still a solid yellow and not a clear liquid. This is an indication that the butter has to simmer for a longer time.

Turn the heat to low and continue to simmer the butter. After a few more minutes of simmering you will notice that the colour of the liquid below the foam will begin to turn clear. At this stage the butter will foam again, and this indicates that the ghee is beginning to get ready.
Turn off the heat and allow the foam to settle down. You will notice the clear golden brown liquid. You will also notice that the milk solids have separated and have settled in the bottom of the pan.
Allow the ghee to cool slightly and then strain the ghee into a clean, dry jar. The ghee can stored at room temperature for about 2 months.
Use the fresh homemade ghee to temper Dals, Vegetables, when making Parathas or even for Indian Halwa Recipe. You can also add a dollop of ghee to Steamed Rice or a Hot Phulka.

title: Carrot Orange Walnut Raita (Fruity Nutty Yogurt) Recipe
ingredients: Salt, or sugar as per preference
instructions: Whisk the curd to a smooth texture in a mixing bowl.
Add the peeled and grated carrot, then the orange segments, chopped walnuts, and cashew nuts.
Mix well and add the seasonings: 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon cumin powder, and a pinch of raita masala, if using.
If you prefer a sweet version, add 1 teaspoon sugar and mix well.
Serve the raita with lunch or dinner; it also makes a great party food.

title: Fish Sukka Recipe - Fish With Spicy Masala Filling
instructions: Cut the fish into thin slices.
Keep only the flesh of the fish, discard bones and organs, wash well and apply some salt.
Marinate fish with red chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger garlic paste and lime juice in a big bowl; mix and set aside for 10 minutes.

While the fish marinates, prepare the sukka gravy: in a shallow fry pan, dry roast all whole spices (coriander seeds, cloves, whole black peppercorns, black cardamom, cinnamon stick) on medium heat until fragrant, leaving out the poppy seeds.
Push the roasted spices to the sides of the pan to make room in the center.
Add poppy seeds to the center and roast briefly until they change color slightly; then switch off and let cool.
Combine the roasted spices with desiccated coconut in a mixer‑grinder.
Add a tablespoon of red chilli powder and a little water (about ¼ cup) and grind to a smooth paste; set aside.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a kadai, add the slit green chilies and chopped onion.
Fry on medium‑high heat until the onion turns light brown, then add the prepared coconut paste and sauté for 5–6 minutes until the gravy dries.
Add salt and half of the chopped coriander leaves, mix well, and stir in the marinated fish.
If the gravy is too dry, add one or two tablespoons of water and a teaspoon of lime juice.
Cover and cook on medium heat for about 10 minutes, checking occasionally; avoid stirring the fish too much to prevent it from breaking.
Gently stir or shake the kadai intermittently so the fish coats well with the gravy.
Check doneness with a toothpick, then sprinkle the remaining chopped coriander leaves and remove from heat.
Serve the Fish Sukka as an appetizer alongside dal, rice or phulka, or with other complementary dishes.

title: Buttered Potato Cubes Recipe - Finger Food For Babies Above 9 Months
instructions: Pressure cook the washed potato with a cup of water for 3-4 whistles, then turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Take out the cooked potato, let it cool, and remove the skin.
Dice the potato into bite‑size cubes and set aside.
In a pan, melt 1 teaspoon of butter over low heat.
Add the diced potatoes to the pan and stir.
Sprinkle a pinch of salt and sauté the potato cubes for a few minutes until they are well coated with butter.
Turn off the flame and transfer the potatoes to a baby bowl.
Optionally sprinkle a pinch of cumin powder and black pepper powder.
Serve the buttered potato cubes as finger food for babies aged 10 months and above.

title: Tandoori Paneer Samosa Recipe - With Baked Option
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), finely chopped
instructions: Marinate the paneer cubes with the listed spices and curd; mix well and let it rest for about 2 hours.
While the paneer is marinating, prepare the dough by mixing all purpose flour with oil until a sandy texture forms, then add water gradually to form a firm yet smooth dough; cover and set aside.
After marinating, shallow fry the paneer in a little oil until crisp, then drain on paper towels and reserve the leftover marination.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them crackle; add chopped onions and sauté until glossy and translucent, then add chopped capsicum and cook briefly.

Add 2 tablespoons of the reserved paneer masala to the pan, mix, then add chilli powder and salt if needed; add the grilled paneer, combine well and cook until the filling is dry and cooked through; turn off the heat.
Prepare a sealing paste by mixing 2 tablespoons of maida with water to a smooth consistency.
Heat oil for deep frying the samosas.
Pinch a lemon-sized ball of dough, roll it into a thin 7‑inch circle, cut into two semicircles; repeat with remaining dough.
Place a portion of the paneer filling on one semicircle, fold into a cone shape and seal the edges with the flour paste, applying gentle pressure to prevent leakage.
Deep fry the samosas in hot oil over medium flame until golden brown, then drain on absorbent paper.
For a baked version, preheat the oven to 180 °C, bake the samosas for 20 minutes, flip and bake an additional 10 minutes.
Serve the samosas hot with green chutney, tamarind chutney, and tomato sauce, alongside a cup of masala chai.

title: Vegan Coconut Yogurt Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Agar agar, or 3 tablespoons arrowroot powder (optional)
instructions: To begin making the Vegan Coconut Yogurt recipe, in a saucepan add coconut milk, coconut sugar and sprinkle agar-agar and bring this to a gentle boil.
Now let this cool down until it is warm around 100 °F. Stir in the dairy-free yogurt starter with a whisk into the coconut milk mixture and pour them into a sterilized glass jar.
Cover the jar with a breathable cloth and secure it with a string or a rubber band and leave it in a warm place for 12 to 24 hours depending on the outside temperature.
Taste after 7 to 8 hours and continue to let it ferment longer if it has not fermented or become sour enough, for a couple more hours.
Stir this with a spoon to ensure it thickens evenly in the refrigerator. Refrigerate for 4 hours and enjoy.

If using arrowroot in place of agar-agar, whisk the arrowroot powder into half a cup of the coconut milk from the saucepan, return it with the remaining milk into the saucepan, and follow the rest of the steps as mentioned above.
Serve Vegan Coconut Yogurt along with Quinoa Vangi Bath for a perfect weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Ragi & Whole Wheat Halwa Recipe - Finger Millet Pudding
ingredients: 1/4 cup Whole Almonds (Badam), blanched, peeled and slivered
instructions: To make the Ragi Halwa Recipe, melt the ghee in a heavy bottomed pan on medium heat; add both the ragi and wheat flours into the ghee.
Stir them along with the ghee on low heat until you get a roasted aroma.
This takes about 10 minutes and sometimes more. Please avoid turning the heat to high to fasten the process. The slow process helps in gradual cooking of the halwa.
In the meantime, in another saucepan dissolve the water and sugar. Stir in the cardamom powder to this.

After about 10 minutes and the roasted aromas come out, add the hot sugar water mixture to the flour mixture and stir continuously for about 2 minutes or until the water is fully absorbed into the flour.
Once absorbed, add a tablespoon of more ghee and keep stirring for another 5 minutes until you get the flavors and the right texture.
The texture of the halwa is a little coarse and not gooey. Turn off the heat, transfer to a serving bowl and serve the Ragi Halwa with the almonds.
Serve the Ragi Halwa or Finger Millet Pudding as a dessert for any festival or also as a party dessert.
Note: Take care to ensure that the flour does not get burnt, hence keep the flame low and stir constantly.

title: Simple Steamed Indian Beet Salad Recipe
instructions: Wash the beetroots and cut them in half.
Place the beetroot halves in a pressure cooker with 1/2 cup of water.
Pressure cook for 6-7 whistles, then turn off the flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Open the cooker, remove the beets, and let them cool to room temperature.
Peel the skin off and slice the beetroot.
Sprinkle salt, black pepper powder, cumin powder, chaat masala powder, and squeeze lemon juice over the beet slices; serve chilled.
Serve the beet salad with phulkas, smoked dhaba dal, layered vegetable tricolor biryani, and boondi raita, followed by a dessert if desired.

title: Oats and Besan Cheela Recipe (High Protein Spiced Crepes)
ingredients: 80 grams Rolled Oats or Instant Oats, powdered
instructions: Combine all the ingredients for the Besan Chilla in a large bowl.
Gradually add water to make a thick batter.
Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.
The cheela batter should have the consistency of a dosa or pancake batter and be able to coat the back of a spoon.
Cook the Oats Besan Cheela in a pan.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat, pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin crepe/dosa.
Drizzle some oil around the cheela and cook until the top is set and the edges turn brown; flip and cook the other side for a few seconds.
Transfer the cooked cheela to a plate and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve the Oats Besan Cheela with Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Senai Pachadi Recipe (Elephant Yam Raita)
instructions: Peel the skin of yam and chop them into squares.
Add water to cover the yam and steam them in pressure cooker till the cooker releases 3 whistles.
Add coriander leaves, chilli, ginger and yam into a mixer.
Strain the water before adding yam but do not throw the water. Grind the mix.
Heat oil in a tadka pan and add the items given in ‘For Tempering’ in the order given.
Mix the ground mixture, yogurt and remaining water and give it a stir.
Once it is done, mix everything with the raita, pour the tempering and serve.
Serve Senai Pachadi along with Mixed Vegetable Sambar, Cauliflower Thoran and Hot Steamed Rice.

title: Kesar Peda Recipe
ingredients: 300 grams Khoya (Mawa), store bought or homemade
instructions: Warm the milk gently without boiling and soak the saffron in it; set aside for 10 minutes.
In a pan or kadai, add crumbled khoya and sugar; cook on low heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring continuously until the sugar dissolves and the khoya melts and thickens.
Stir continuously until the khoya thickens further, being careful not to burn it.
Add the saffron milk and powdered cardamom; cook a few more minutes until the mixture becomes a sticky dough-like consistency and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Turn off the heat and allow the peda mixture to cool.
When cool enough to touch, knead lightly to remove lumps; optionally add a little ghee for shine.
Roll the mixture into a log and cut into 12 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a small ball, make a small dent in the center, and insert a pistachio slice (or use a peda mould).
Serve the Kesar Peda as a dessert.

title: Bhindi Raita Recipe (Okra Salad)
ingredients: 250 grams Bhindi (Lady Finger/Okra), cleaned, ends removed and sliced
instructions: To begin making the Bhindi Raita first, mix 1-1/2 tablespoon oil with the Bhindi and rub lightly to coat the slices. Add some salt and half of the chilli powder.
Microwave (in batches) for 5 to 6 minutes on high till crisp. Stir at 1 minute interval so that they cook evenly.
Alternatively you can pan fry or air fry the slices till crisp. Cool it down.
In a mixing bowl add the curd. Add little salt, sugar, groundnut powder, chaat masala and mix.
In a small wok/pan, heat oil. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, red chilli powder and hing.
Add the crisp okras to the curd and pour the tempering over the curd. The raita is ready to be served.
Serve Bhindi Raita with roti or rice and Panchmel Dal for a light everyday meal.

title: Lemon Pepper Fish Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Basa fish, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat a kadai with oil, add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle for a few seconds.
Add curry leaves and let them crackle, then add fennel seeds and sauté briefly.
Add chopped garlic, green chilies and sauté for a few minutes until softened.
Add basa fish, sprinkle turmeric powder, crushed pepper, salt and sauté until everything combines.
Cook until the fish is done, serve hot, then add lemon juice and mix thoroughly.
Serve the Lemon Pepper Fish with Peppery Mushroom Biryani, Palak Raita, and salad.

title: Atta Biscuit Recipe (Whole Wheat Flour Cookies Spiced with Cardamom)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170 C and line two baking sheets with parchment paper or grease with little butter.

Sift together flour, bran, sugar and cardamom pods powder in a large mixing bowl. Now add the cubed and chilled butter into the dry ingredients, mix using your fingers or a pastry cutter, until the cookie dough forms a crumbly sandy mixture.
Next add one tablespoon of milk at a time to make a soft and firm cookie dough. When you notice the flour has come together and is well combined, then you can stop kneading the dough.
To shape the cookies, divide the dough into equal size small portions and roll into balls.
Flatten each ball into a disc about 1/4" thick. Arrange the biscuits on the lined baking sheets at some distance apart. Press half a cashew into the centre of each biscuit.
Bake biscuits for approx. 20-22 minutes each or until done and golden around the edges. Rotate each sheet halfway through for even baking.
Once baked, transfer biscuits to a wire rack to cool down before storing.
Serve Atta Biscuit with a cup of masala chai for the evening snacks or store in an airtight box at room temperature.

title: Chaat Masala Recipe
instructions: Heat a pan on low flame and dry roast the cumin seeds, coriander seeds and black peppercorns.
Roast on medium-low heat until fragrant, about 8-10 minutes.
Turn off the flame and allow the mixture to come to room temperature.
Transfer to a mixer jar, add the black salt, dry mango powder, asafoetida and salt to taste.
Grind to a fine powder.
Use the chaat masala in various chaat and buttermilk recipes.

title: Homemade Sev Recipe - Gram Flour Vermicelli Snack
instructions: Combine all the ingredients except water, then gradually add water to make a stiff dough, adding extra water if required.
Grease the Sev Press or the Sev Sancha with oil and place the plate with many tiny holes into the press.
Heat oil in a frying pan until hot.

Fill the sev dough into the press and press out thin strands into the hot oil; turn the pressed sev to fry the other side, and when golden, drain excess oil with a slotted spoon and place on a plate to cool.
Press the remaining batches of the sev dough in the same manner.
Cool the entire homemade sev and store in airtight containers.
Serve the sev with chaats like Bhel Puri, Sev Papdi Puri Chaat, Khakra Chaat, or Chole Tikki Chaat as a tea‑time snack.

title: Sweet Potato Flatbread Recipe - Sweet Potato Chapati
ingredients: 1 cup Sweet Potato, boiled and mashed
instructions: To begin making the Sweet Potato Flatbread recipe, boil sweet potatoes in a pressure cooker till firm and smash them using your hands or ladle. Use 1 cup of mashed sweet potato for each cup of wheat flour.
Take a big bowl, add wheat flour, sweet potato, salt, red chilli powder, ajwain, jeera seeds and mix everything together.
Now add water little by little and make a soft dough. Cover it with a cotton cloth and let it rest for 10 mins.

Now using chapati roller, make a round shape roti or chapati. Heat pan and flip the roti on both sides. Drizzle little oil to get mild golden colour. When it is cooked, switch off the stove and serve hot.
Serve Sweet Potato Flatbread along with Boondi Raita and Aam Ka Achaar for your breakfast or for a light dinner.

title: Pineapple Lassi Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Pineapple, cut into small dices
instructions: Heat a pan, add grated pineapple and sugar, mix well and sauté for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender; keep aside and allow it to cool completely.
Add yogurt, milk, heavy cream, ice cubes, saffron and salt into a blender and blend until smooth.
Add the cooked pineapple into the yogurt mixture, stir well to combine, then pour into glasses and serve chilled.
Sprinkle black pepper on top of the pineapple lassi and serve.
Serve pineapple lassi alongside Jaipuri Aloo Pyaz Ki Sabzi, Ajwain Puri and Pyaaz Pudina Kachumber Salad for a weekend lunch.

title: Date and Tamarind Chutney Recipe - Khajur Imli Chutney
instructions: Add dates, jaggery, tamarind, and water to a pressure cooker. Pressure cook for 3 to 4 whistles, then turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Open the cooker and blend the tamarind and dates with a hand blender to a coarse mixture.
Return the cooker to heat and add red chilli powder, cumin powder, dry ginger powder, black salt, and salt to taste. Add a little water to adjust consistency and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Turn off the heat, cool the chutney, then refrigerate and store in an airtight container until ready to serve.
Serve the Date and Tamarind Chutney with samosa, bread pakora, or add it to Dahi Batata Puri Chaat and enjoy.

title: Kobiche Vade Recipe - Cabbage And Multigrain Fritters
ingredients: 1 to 1 1/4 Cabbage (Patta Gobi/ Muttaikose) , finely chopped
1 tablespoon Oil , as required for shallow frying
instructions: To begin making the Kobiche Vade Recipe, first grind together chillies, ginger, cumin seeds and garlic in a blender or mortar pestle.

In a mixing bowl add all the ingredients like the cabbage, multigrain flour, gram flour, rice flour, green chillies, ginger, garlic, cumin seeds, ajwain, coriander leaves, lemon juice and salt. Use some water to make a thick batter of dropping consistency.
Heat a non-stick Appam pan. Drizzle some oil in each of the cavities.
Drop about 2 tablespoon batter into each cavity. Cover and cook on low flame till they brown.
Using a wooden skewer turn the Kobiche vade upside down and cook for a couple of minutes more till golden brown on all sides.
Serve Kobiche Vade with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai.

title: Kesar Elaichi Lassi Recipe
ingredients: 6 Cardamom (Elaichi) Pods/Seeds, ground to make a coarse powder
1 tablespoon Whole Almonds (Badam), slivered for garnish
instructions: Blend all the ingredients including curd, saffron strands, honey, and cardamom pods (but excluding the nuts) in a blender or mixer.
Check the sweetness and adjust the honey to suit your taste; add water or more yogurt to adjust the thickness if desired.
Pour the Kesar Elaichi Lassi into serving glasses and garnish with pistachio and almond slivers.
Serve the Kesar Elaichi Lassi chilled, either with a lunch of Chana Masala and Bhatura or as a post-dinner sweet treat.

title: Falsa/Phalsa Ka Sharbat Recipe - Indian Berry Juice
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mint Leaves (Pudina), chopped (plus extra for garnish)
instructions: Wash the falsa and mash it with a spatula until the pulp separates from the seeds.
Combine the mashed falsa, black salt, roasted cumin powder, a little water, and sugar; blend in a mixer grinder to a smooth paste.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl, filter it, and pour the juice into a serving jug, adding water to taste.
Add ice cubes and mint leaves, then garnish with lemon slices and additional mint leaves.
Serve the Falsa/Phalsa ka sharbat chilled as a refreshing drink.

title: Mushroom Methi Brown Rice Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Mushroom Methi Brown Rice, rinse brown rice twice. Soak in water for about 30 minutes.
Drain the rice from water and add 2-1/2 cup clean water to soaked rice in a pressure cooker. Pressure cook for 2 whistles.
In a heavy bottomed pan, heat oil. Add garlic and onions and green chilies, sauté until onions turn translucent.
Once the onions have turned translucent add the finely chopped tomatoes and cook till tomatoes turn mushy.
After the tomatoes have turned mushy add the red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and salt. Mix well to combine.
Now add button mushroom and cook for about 2 to 3 minutes. Mushrooms will release moisture, cook it in its own moisture.
After the moisture from the mushrooms has evaporated add finely chopped fresh fenugreek leaves and cook for another 3 minutes.
When mushrooms and fenugreek leaves are fully cooked, add cooked brown rice and gently mix it. Check for salt and adjust accordingly.
Transfer the Mushroom Methi Brown Rice into a serving plate and serve hot.
Serve Mushroom Methi Brown Rice along with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, Beetroot Raita or any other Raita of your choice.

title: Paan Gulkand Sharbat Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Mixed nuts (almond and pistachios), roughly pounded
instructions: To begin making Paan Gulkand Sharbat, get all the ingredients ready.
Make a fine paste of the betel leaves with a little water using a mixer grinder and transfer it to a big bowl once churned completely.
Add the cold milk, gulkand, honey, almonds and pistachios, and ice cubes, then whisk slowly until the gulkand and honey dissolve well into the drink.
Serve this refreshing Paan Gulkand Sharbat for your guests in summer, optionally with Kesar Pista Mango Ice Cream and Poha Chivda.

title: Whole Masala Gobhi Recipe - Spiced Whole Roasted Cauliflower Masala
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Poori Masala Gobhi Recipe, wash the cauliflower and remove the stem and leaves, while keeping the cauliflower as a whole.

Boil the whole cauliflower in a large pot filled with water for 10 minutes until it is just about cooked through. The color of the cauliflower to a greenish color. Once done, remove the cauliflower from the water and allow it to cool a bit.
Preheat the oven to 200 C.
In a small bowl, mix together yogurt, a tablespoon of oil, red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, ginger garlic paste and salt.
Once the cauliflower is cool, rub the yogurt mixture all over the cauliflower, potatoes and onions.
Brush an oven proof skillet or roasting pan with oil. The pan should be large enough to fit the cauliflower, potatoes and onions.
Place the poori gobi (cauliflower) along with the along with onions and potatoes in the roasting pan.

Drizzle with the remaining oil over the poori gobi masala. Bake the poori gobi masala in a preheated oven for 20 -25 minutes till the top is golden brown and the cauliflower is cooked through. Since the cauliflower is already partially cooked, this process will not take time.
Once you notice it is cooked, remove the Poori Masala Gobi from the oven and serve.

Optionally sprinkle some chaat masala over the Poori Masala Gobhi Recipe and serve it as a side dish for dinner or for parties along with Lachha Parathas and Punjabi Dal Tadka and Paneer Butter Masala.

title: Arbi Ke Meethe Chande Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Arbi Ke Meethe Chande Recipe, clean and dry Arbi. Apply mustard oil to hands and cut 1/4 inch thin chips out of it. Chips should be not too thin as they may burn during frying. Wash them again and spread it out on a towel to dry.
Let them dry for 2 hours under the fan or medium sunlight.
Now heat ghee in a kadai/deep frying pan and fry them till golden. You can alternately shallow fry them, for a healthier version too.
Transfer the fried arbi chips on an oil absorbent paper to immediately to get rid of any excess oil.
Meanwhile prepare the sugar syrup of one string consistency. In a saucepan, pour sugar and water and bring it to boil while continually stirring the mixture.

Let it simmer on medium heat till you obtain a one string consistency when you drop the syrup from your ladle. Take a drop of sugar syrup on your forefinger and stretch it with the thumb to observe one string consistency.
Once done add the Arbi Chips in the prepared sugar syrup and start stirring them fast. Your stove should be on a medium heat while doing this.
Gradually, you will see sugar getting dried up and coating the Arbi Chips.
Keep stirring on low heat till all the chips are coated well with the sugar syrup.
Now take them out on a tray and let the Arbi Ke meethe chande cool down and serve.
Once cooled you can store the Arbi Ke Meethe Chande in an airtight container up to 4 days.
Serve Arbi Ke Meethe Chande Recipe with Moong Dal Mini Samosas and Masala Chai Recipe as an evening snack.

title: Avocado Raita Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To prepare the Avocado Raita, take the peeled avocado, scoop out the flesh and roughly chop it up into small bits.
Put the chopped avocado bits into the blender. Add the 2-3 tablespoons of yogurt, salt, coriander leaves, chat masala, cumin powder and green chilli and blend them together to form a smooth paste.
In another bowl, pour in the remainder of the yogurt, beat it gently, adding in the avocado mixture at this stage. Check the salt and adjust to suit your taste.
Finally, add the roasted peanuts and sprinkle red chilli powder into the Avocado Raita just before serving. Serve the Avocado raita along with Parathas for breakfast to make a wholesome meal.

title: Mixed Vegetable Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1 Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), de-seeded and finely chopped
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Take the mashed potatoes in a large bowl. Add the carrots, capsicum, cheese, onion, garlic, and ginger to the mashed potatoes and mash all the ingredients together using a food processor, your hands, or a potato masher until well combined, retaining a subtle coarseness for texture.

Add the remaining ingredients (garam masala, coriander powder, red chilli powder, green chillies, coriander leaves, beaten egg, and bread crumbs) except the oil, mix well, and adjust salt and spices to taste.
Shape the mixture into small lemon-sized balls, flatten them slightly between your palms, dip each flat cutlet first in the beaten egg and then coat with the bread crumbs.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat, place a few cutlets at a time, drizzle oil on them, and fry until crisp and browned on both sides. Continue with the remaining cutlets.
Serve the hot mixed vegetable cutlets with chutney or a yogurt dip.

title: Moong Dal Mini Samosas - Delicious Tea Time Snack
ingredients: 1/2 cup Lukewarm Water (to bind the dough)
2 teaspoon Mixed Spices (powders of cumin, coriander, red chilli, mango, fennel, pomegranate seed or anardana and chaat masala)
2 teaspoons Corn flour, or maida dissolved in 2 tablespoons water (to bind edges)
instructions: Mix the all-purpose flour with a little cooking oil.
Add ghee, salt, Kasuri Methi, and Ajwain; knead gently with lukewarm water until the dough is soft and pliable, then cover with a moist cloth and rest for 30 minutes.
Crush the moong dal namkeen in a blender to a coarse powder.
Dry roast the mixed spices in a pan over medium heat, then combine with the crushed namkeen and asafoetida, adjust salt and seasoning, and set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan for deep frying.
Divide the rested dough into small lemon‑sized balls and roll each ball into a small circular disc like a chapati.
Cut each disc into two equal halves.
Take one half, join the corners with water and the corn‑flour mixture to form a cone shape, and fill the cone with about 1 teaspoon of the moong dal filling.
Seal the open edge with the corn‑flour mixture and gently press to close.
Repeat the shaping, filling, and sealing process for the remaining dough pieces.
When the oil is hot (test by dropping one samosa, it should rise to the surface), fry 3‑7 samosas at a time on medium flame until they turn golden brown.
Remove the fried samosas with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper; continue frying the rest.
Serve the hot mini Moong Dal samosas with green chutney or date tamarind chutney, and store any leftovers in an airtight container at room temperature.

title: Chicken Malai Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 250 grams Chicken breasts, cut into 2 inch cubes
Oil, as required for shallow frying
instructions: Using a fork, prick the chicken pieces slightly and transfer to a bowl.
Add the onion paste, ginger garlic paste, chilli powder, curd, fresh cream, cumin powder, and salt to taste; mix well and allow to marinate overnight.
Heat a grilling pan on medium heat, add a few teaspoons of oil and place the chicken pieces on a low‑medium flame. Flip after a few minutes.
Ensure the chicken is cooked through well.
Serve the Chicken Malai Kebab with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Pickled Onions as a party appetizer.

title: Crunchy Ginger Capsicum Rice Recipe
ingredients: 2 teaspoon Sesame seeds (Til seeds), mixed black and white, dry roasted
instructions: Wash the basmati rice in running tap water until clear and soak for 30 minutes.

In a large pan, add 3.5 cups of water and bring to a rolling boil. Add the soaked and drained rice, salt to taste, cover with a lid and cook for 20 minutes on low flame until al dente; then switch off the flame and let rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork so it does not become lumpy after cooling and set aside.
Heat a kadai with some butter and a teaspoon of oil to prevent the butter from burning.
Add the finely chopped bell peppers and green chillies; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the grated ginger and stir well.
Add 2 cups of cooked basmati rice, season with salt, and gently toss to combine.
Garnish with toasted black and white sesame seeds and switch off the flame.
Serve the Crunchy Ginger Capsicum Rice for a kids' lunch box or with chicken/vegetable Manchurian for dinner.

title: Badam Sharbat Recipe - Almond Milk With Nuts & Spices
instructions: To begin making the Badam Sharbat recipe, soak the almonds in enough water overnight.
Soak melon seeds in water for 2-3 hours. Peel off the skin of almonds and blend with melon seeds in a mixer adding 1/4 cup water until you get a smooth mixture.
Heat jaggery in 1 cup water in a saucepan. Once jaggery is completely dissolved, add almond milk and cardamom powder.
Cook till the mixture is reduced to half. It may take around 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.
For Sharbat, use 1 or 2 tablespoons of prepared badam syrup and mix with cold milk. Add few drops of Kewra essence and saffron strands. Mix everything well and serve chilled with ice cubes.
Serve Badam Sharbat along with Whole Wheat Flour Chakli and Leftover Roti Cutlet to your guests.

title: Tofu and Chickpea Patty Recipe (Cutlets)
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
1 cup kala chana (brown chickpeas), cooked until soft
Extra virgin olive oil, for shallow frying
instructions: To begin making the Chickpea & Tofu Patties Recipe, we first have to cook the chickpeas until soft. Note, that the chickpeas have to be soaked in water for at least 6 hours before you can cook them.

Once the chickpeas are cooked, drain any water from the cooked peas and use them in your soups, vegetable stock or any other recipe that would need water. To make the patties we need to use the cooked chickpeas that have all the water drained out.
Add the chickpeas to a large mixing bowl, mash it with a potato masher or a fork. Once coarsely mashed, add the remaining ingredients and stir well to combine. Use your fingers to mix the patty.

Divide the chickpea patty mixture into 10 to 12 equal portions and shape them into oval or round balls. Flatten them slightly in the palm of your hand. Oiling your fingers makes it easier to shape the patties.

Preheat a skillet and place the patties on the preheated skillet. Drizzle olive oil over each patty and cook them on low to medium heat. Flip them a couple of times so they become golden brown on all sides.
Serve the chickpea and tofu patties along with coriander chutney as an appetizer, pack them into a kids' lunch box, or make burgers out of these patties.

title: Spring Onion Pakora Recipe - Made In Kuzhi Paniyaram Pan
ingredients: 10 stalks Spring Onion (Bulb & Greens), a bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Heat a pan on medium heat and add the coriander seeds. Roast until they change colour and emit a nice aroma, then turn off the heat and let the seeds cool.
Once the coriander seeds have cooled slightly, crush them to a coarse mix using a mortar and pestle and set aside.

In a mixing bowl combine besan, rice flour, enos fruit salt, crushed roasted coriander seeds, chilli powder, chopped spring onions, mint leaves, green chillies, and salt; mix well and add water little at a time to form a thick batter.
Heat a Kuzhi paniyaram pan over medium heat and add about 1/2 teaspoon oil to each cavity.

Spoon the batter into each cavity, drizzle a little oil over the pakoras, and let them steam. When the top is cooked, flip them, drizzle more oil, and pan‑fry on medium heat until browned on all sides and cooked through.
Transfer the cooked pakoras onto a plate lined with oil‑absorbent paper and serve hot.
Serve the Spring Onion Pakoras as an evening snack with green chutney and masala chai.

title: Chicken Bharta Recipe - Dhaba Style Chicken Masala
ingredients: 2 whole eggs, boiled, peeled and halved
instructions: Wash and clean the chicken breast, cut into large chunks, and boil the chicken in water with salt for 15 to 20 minutes.
Take out the chicken pieces, let them cool, shred the chicken into thin long strips, and set aside.
Boil the tomatoes with water for about 5 minutes, then peel off the skin, grind to a fine paste, and keep aside.
Soak the cashew nuts in warm water for 10 minutes and grind to a fine paste in a mixer grinder.
In a bowl, mix the cumin powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder with 3 tablespoon water and set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan, add the crushed cloves, black and green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf; sauté for about 30 seconds.
Add the chopped onions and sauté over medium heat until golden brown, then add ginger‑garlic paste and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the tomato puree, green chillies, and a pinch of salt; mix well, cover and cook on low‑medium heat until the tomatoes are done and oil separates. Then add the wet masala, mix and cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and slowly stir in the whisked yogurt continuously.
Return to low heat, add the shredded chicken pieces with 1/4 cup water, cover and cook over medium heat for 5 to 10 minutes; then add the cashew paste and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Separate the yolk and white of the boiled eggs; mash the yolk and add to the chicken, chop the whites and add to the curry.
Cover and cook for 10 minutes on low heat, stirring occasionally; check seasoning and adjust, then add a few drops of kewra essence.
Reduce the flame, add fresh cream, sugar, and kasuri methi; mix well and turn off the heat.
Add melted butter and garam masala powder, immediately cover the pan, garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve.
Serve chicken bharta with garlic naan, boondi raita, and jeera rice.

title: Besan Bread Toast Recipe On Tawa - Vegetarian French Toast
ingredients: 4 Whole Wheat Brown Bread, whole wheat
instructions: In a large bowl, combine besan, onion, tomato, green chillies, coriander leaves, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, and enough water to form a semi‑thick batter that coats the back of a spoon.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and brush it lightly with oil.
Dip each bread slice into the batter, ensuring it is well‑coated, and place it onto the heated skillet.
Drizzle a little oil around the sides of the bread and continue cooking over medium heat.
When the bottom is cooked and golden, flip the toast and cook the other side until golden brown; optionally use butter or olive oil for extra flavour.
Repeat the process for the remaining bread slices and keep the toasts hot.
Serve the Besan Bread Toast hot, accompanied by Masala Chai and sliced bananas.

title: Baby Potatoes Pulao Recipe - Aloo Pulao Recipe
instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice in enough water until further cooking.
Peel the skin of the baby potatoes and keep them immersed in a bowl of water to avoid discoloration.

Heat ghee in a heavy bottomed pan, drain the potatoes from water, dry them using a kitchen towel and then fry in the ghee until they turn golden in colour; drain them on a kitchen towel and keep aside.
In the same pan, add the whole garam masalas including star anise, bay leaf, cloves, green cardamoms, and cinnamon stick and let them release their aroma into the ghee.
Add the thinly sliced onions and sauté until they turn brown. Add the ginger garlic paste and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and slit green chillies and sauté till the tomatoes turn mushy.
Whisk the red chilli powder, coriander, and garam masala into a bowl of curd to a smooth texture and add it to the pan.
Add the fresh coriander and mint leaves and cook the mixture until all the masalas are well combined and the oil separates out.

Drain and add the soaked basmati rice to the pan, along with the fried baby potatoes, 2-1/2 cups of water, season with salt and lemon juice, and let it simmer for 20 minutes with the lid closed until the rice and baby potatoes are cooked.
Once the rice and potatoes are cooked, switch off the heat, fluff the rice with a fork and mix gently.
Serve the Baby Potatoes Pulao along with Cucumber Green Chilli Raita, Kachumber Salad, and a roasted Papad.

title: Peach Lassi Recipe - Peach Yogurt Smoothie
instructions: Peel and cut the peaches into equal size pieces.
Add the yogurt, diced peaches, mint leaves, and honey into a blender; blend until smooth with no lumps.
Add a little water to adjust consistency if needed, blend again, and adjust sweetness by adding more honey as desired.
Pour the peach lassi into serving glasses, garnish with peach slices and mint leaves, and serve chilled.

title: Grilled Rajma Masala Sandwich Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Grilled Rajma Masala Sandwich Recipe, soak 1/2 cup of rajma overnight and cook the rajma until soft. Drain the excess water and keep aside.
Boil the potatoes, peel the skin and cut the potatoes until small cubes. Keep this aside.
In a skillet, heat a teaspoon oil, add the ginger, garlic and saute for a few seconds. Add the cooked rajma, cut potatoes and all the masalas.

Stir to combine all the ingredients and saute on medium high heat until you get a good rajma masala filling for the sandwich. There should be very little moisture. Check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste.

Once done turn off the heat and allow the rajma masala to cool. Once cooled, add the thinly sliced onions and optionally green chilies chopped into the masala. This will give a good crunch to the sandwich.
To prepare grilled sandwich, place the bread slices on the platform. Spread a spoonful of rajma masala mixture over one slice. Cover with another bread slice and press it down.

Spread some softened butter on the top slice and place it in a sandwich maker or grill pan with the butter side facing down. Spread butter on the other side and grill the rajma sandwich until golden brown and crisp.
Serve the Grilled Rajma Masala Sandwich as a wholesome breakfast or even serve it for summer weeknight dinner along with a Summer Lettuce Salad Recipe or a Coconut Kewra Drink Recipe.

title: Masala Palak Bhurji Recipe
instructions: We begin making the Masala Palak Bhurji Recipe by heating a pan with oil, splutter the ajwain seeds, add in the onions and bell peppers saute till the onions become translucent.
Then add in the tomatoes and add the spice powders along with salt and pepper. Give it a stir.
Add the chopped spinach and wet the spinach and cook till it wilts. Then finally crack one egg at a time.
Start mixing the egg with the masala that is been sautéed. Mix well and combine all the ingredients together. Check for seasoning once done, and serve.
Serve the Masala Palak Bhurji Recipe along with toasted bread and a Chickoo Banana Date Smoothie for your healthy breakfast.

title: Multigrain Crepe Recipe Filled With Spicy Mashed Potatoes
instructions: Gather all the ingredients, including boiling and mashing the potatoes.
In a large mixing bowl, add the flours, a pinch of salt, black pepper, and water to make a smooth batter that is thick yet pourable, similar to dosa batter.
Set the crepe batter aside.
