In a heavy‑bottomed pan, heat a teaspoon of oil over medium heat, add cumin seeds and let them crackle, then add green chilies and chopped onion and sauté until the onion caramelizes.
When the onion turns brown, add the mashed potatoes, red chilli powder, and salt; stir well, adjust seasoning, then mix in chopped coriander leaves and turn off the heat.
Heat a nonstick crepe skillet over medium heat, pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan and swirl to spread; cook until the top sets, then flip and cook the other side for a few seconds.
Transfer the cooked crepe to a platter and repeat the process with the remaining batter.
Place a spoonful of the potato filling in the centre of each crepe, roll it up, and serve.
Serve the Multigrain Crepes filled with spicy mashed potatoes with yogurt dip or Mexican salsa.

title: Masala Mixed Sprouts Sandwich Recipe
ingredients: 8 Whole Wheat Brown Bread , sides cut
instructions: To begin making the Masala Mixed Sprouts Sandwich, add the sprouts and 1 cup water to a pressure cooker and pressure cook for 1 whistle.
Switch off and let the pressure get released.
Heat a kadai and add oil. When oil gets heated, add onion and saute.
When onion turns pinkish, add tomato and fry till tomato turns soft and mushy.
Add garlic and fry till the raw smell of garlic goes away. This will take 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, open the pressure cooker and add the boiled sprouts and mix. Add red chilli powder, chaat masala powder, turmeric powder, salt and give it a good mix. Let it simmer for 10 minutes.
Adjust salt and switch off the heat. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Now the filling is ready. So let us assemble the sandwich.
Take a slice of bread and spread 2 tablespoon of the sprout mixture.
Top this with one or two onion slices and close it with another slice of bread.
Either eat the sandwich as it is or grill it if you prefer.
Assemble the other sandwiches in the same way and serve the masala mixed sprout sandwich hot.

title: Spicy Coconut Peanut Stuffed Baby Brinjal Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mustard oil or vegetable oil
instructions: Make two perpendicular vertical slits in each eggplant without cutting all the way through.
Dry roast the peanuts and grated dry coconut until lightly golden, then let them cool.

In a food processor, grind the roasted peanuts, coconut, cumin seeds, coriander powder, garam masala, salt, and red chili powder into a homogeneous mix; add tomato puree and chopped coriander and combine.
Stuff the eggplants with the prepared mixture, place them in the fridge for 10 minutes to firm up the stuffing.
Heat mustard (or vegetable) oil in a non‑stick pan.
Add mustard seeds to the hot oil and let them splutter.
Add the sliced garlic and sauté until lightly golden.
Add the stuffed eggplants to the pan, toss with the tempering, and add the required amount of salt.
Cook over medium‑high heat for 15–20 minutes until the eggplants become tender.
Cover the pan with a lid and simmer for an additional 5–7 minutes; the dish is then ready to serve.

title: Methi Matar Pulao Recipe | Fenugreek Leaf Green Peas Pulao
ingredients: 200 grams Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), rinsed and chopped
instructions: To begin making the Methi Matar Pulao Recipe, we will be cooking the pulao in a pressure cooker.
Before starting this Methi Matar Pulao recipe, have all your ingredients ready and your green peas already steamed. This will make the cooking process smoother.
In a pressure cooker, warm 2 tablespoons of ghee over medium heat. The aroma of ghee adds a wonderful depth to this recipe.

Once the ghee is hot, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds. Next, stir in the ginger, green chillies and garlic to release its fragrant oils. Then, toss in the cloves, cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté these whole spices until they become aromatic, about 30 seconds.

Reduce the heat slightly and add the chopped methi leaves (fenugreek leaves). Sprinkle the turmeric powder over them, stir, and let the leaves cook down for a minute or two. This step is key in this recipe because cooking off some of the natural bitterness of fenugreek ensures a better flavour.
Gently stir in the rinsed rice. Coat the rice grains with the sautéed spices and methi leaves. This step helps infuse each grain with the flavours of the recipe.

Carefully add 1 cup of coconut milk along with 1 cup of water. Stir well to evenly distribute the liquids. At this point, season with salt to suit your taste. The coconut milk in this recipe gives a creamy hint that pairs beautifully with fenugreek and peas.
Cover the pressure cooker, increase the heat and cook for two whistles. After two whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure is released, let the pulao rest, covered, for 5 minutes. This resting time is a small but critical part of the recipe—it allows the grains to firm up and absorb any remaining steam.

After 5 minutes, remove the lid and gently fold in the steamed green peas. Add an extra tablespoon of ghee if desired, then fluff the rice carefully with a fork or spoon so that the grains remain separate.
Serve your aromatic Methi Matar Pulao recipe with a cooling Tomato Onion Raita and a crispy roasted papad. This combination creates a complete meal, perfect for lunch or dinner.

title: Aloo Parwal Sabzi Recipe - A Classic Bengali Dish
ingredients: 500 grams Pointed gourd (Parval), peeled and sliced into wedges
instructions: To begin making the Aloo Parwal Sabzi Recipe, we will cook the vegetables in two stages.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan; add the mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Once the mustard seeds crackle, add the parwal into the pan, sprinkle some salt, stir to combine, and cover the pan.
Allow the parwal to cook on low to medium heat until cooked, then add 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder and red chilli powder, stir and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and allow them to crackle. Add the potatoes, sprinkle a little salt, stir, cover, and cook until roasted and cooked through.
In the final stage, stir in turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and amchur powder, and cook for a couple of minutes.
Stir the cooked parwal into the aloo sabzi and fry until the masala coats everything well; check salt and adjust to taste.
Turn off the heat, transfer the Aloo Parwal Sabzi to a serving bowl, and serve hot.
Serve the Aloo Parwal Ki Sabzi with Cholar Dal or Makhana Moongphali Ki Kadhi and a bowl of steamed rice or Phulka.

title: Mint And Coriander Spicy Multigrain Cracker Recipe (Mathri)
ingredients: Mint Leaves (Pudina), a handful, finely chopped
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
1 Green Chilli, slit and finely chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, gram flour, ragi flour, ghee (or butter), and salt; rub together with your fingers to form coarse crumbs.

Add the remaining ingredients except water, mix into the dough, then gradually add a little water at a time and knead until smooth. Cover and rest for about 30 minutes; knead again adding a little ghee or oil to keep the dough non‑sticky and smooth.
Divide the dough into lemon‑size balls, roll each out on a floured surface, and prick the rolled sheets with a fork to prevent puffing.
Cut the rolled dough into desired shapes using a cookie cutter, knife, or roller to form diamonds or squares.
Deep fry the crackers until brown, or proceed to bake them.
To bake: preheat the oven to 180 °C, place the cut crackers on a greased and dusted baking sheet, and bake for about 15 minutes until evenly browned and crisp.
Monitor baking time as it may vary with different ovens.
Serve the spiced multigrain crackers as a tea‑time snack or appetizer, optionally topped with cheese or fresh salad.

title: Hariyali Egg Curry Recipe In Coriander and Mint Gravy
ingredients: 2 cups coriander (dhania) leaves, tightly packed, chopped
instructions: Begin by preparing the Hariyali Masala.
In a mixer grinder, combine coriander leaves, mint leaves, green chillies and 1/2 cup water; blend into a smooth paste and set aside.
In a small mixer grinder jar, grind the onions, ginger, and garlic into a paste.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a kadai over medium heat, add the bay leaf, cloves, and cinnamon stick; roast briefly, then add the onion‑ginger‑garlic paste.
Saute for 4 to 5 minutes until the raw onion aroma disappears.
Add garam masala powder and coriander powder; saute for a few seconds.
Stir in the Hariyali coriander‑mint mixture, fresh cream, and the boiled eggs.
Add water as needed to achieve the desired consistency, then cover and simmer the curry for 5 minutes.
Check and adjust salt and spices to taste, then transfer the Hariyali Egg Curry to a serving bowl.
Serve the Hariyali Egg Curry with Malabar Parotta or Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha and Burani Raita.

title: Chiroti Recipe - Delicious Crispy Layered Sweet Puri
instructions: In a wide bowl, mix maida and ghee, then knead into a stiff dough adding water gradually; you can also use a food processor to knead the dough and bring it together.
Cover the dough and set aside for 15-20 minutes until firm and smooth, similar to that of a puri.
Prepare sugar syrup by adding sugar and water in a pan and bringing it to a boil; then reduce the flame to low and cook until the syrup reaches a one‑string consistency.
Add cardamom powder to the syrup, turn off the heat, and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix ghee, rice flour, and maida (all‑purpose flour) together; stir and keep aside.
Divide the rested dough into 6 equal parts and roll each ball into a large round roti.
Apply the ghee‑flour mixture evenly on one roti, place a second roti on top and apply the mixture again, then place a third roti and apply the mixture.
Roll the layered rotis into a log and cut the log into small pieces, forming mini Swiss‑roll or pinwheel shapes.
Press each pinwheel lightly and flatten them into discs, creating flattened chiroti dough ready for frying.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan and deep‑fry the chiroti discs until they turn light golden and crisp.
Immediately soak the fried chiroti in the warm sugar syrup (not too hot nor room temperature) for about a minute until well coated.
Remove the chiroti, place on a platter, sprinkle chopped nuts over them, and allow to cool; store in an airtight container once cooled.
Serve the chiroti as a sweet accompaniment to festive meals or snacks.

title: Mahunada Khaja Recipe - Rose Cookie Recipe
instructions: To begin making Mahunada Khaja Recipe (Andhra Style Gulabi Puvvulu), take all dry ingredients in a mixing bowl and add milk little by little. Using a whisk, mix this well till combined. The batter should be semi thick consistency.
Also heat the cooking oil for deep frying, on medium heat.
Keep the mould inside the oil.
When oil is properly hot, remove the mould from oil.

And put inside the batter. Here is the tricky part, just fill the mould to half so that the batter does not stick to upper most part of the mould. Any batter sticking to the upper part of the mould results in being unable to unmold the cookies.
Now dip the mould into the kadai immediately. Immerse it in hot oil for some time.
When it changes colour and is about half done, take the sauté stick and just scrape the mould to remove the Mahunada Khaja. This stage ensures that the Mahunada Khaja does not loose its shape.
After about a minutes, remove from hot oil. Remember that it will further crisp up when cooling.

Repeat the same process till the batter is completed. After unmolding the mahunada khaja, again dip the mould in hot oil and the dip in batter. Within a few fried Mahunada Khaja are done, you will know how to maximise the frying. You can dip the mould again in batter and fry, such that you will cover 3 cookies in the time that it takes to do 2 otherwise.
This diwali, indulge in Mahunada Khaja Recipe (Andhra Style Gulabi Puvvulu) and served during tea time with Coffee Recipe With Instant Coffee Powder or anytime you want to munch on.

title: Vegetable Biryani Recipe With Chatpata Aloo
ingredients: 3 Red Yellow or Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum)
instructions: Soak the rice in water for 15 to 30 minutes. Temper all the spices listed under 'For Spices' on dry heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant, using low flame.
Coarsely grind the spices or leave them whole.
Cut potatoes into chunks and dunk them in cold water or freeze for 10 minutes to make them crispy.
Heat about a tablespoon of oil on high in a heavy‑bottomed pan or biryani handi.
Add the potato chunks and pan‑sear until light golden; remove and place on kitchen paper towel to absorb excess oil.
Season the potatoes with chaat masala, salt, freshly ground pepper, and lemon juice; set aside.
In the same heavy‑bottomed pan, add 2 tablespoons of oil and heat to medium.
Add onions, green chillies, ginger, and garlic; sauté until the onions become translucent.
Add bell peppers and carrots; sauté for a couple of minutes, then add the tempered spices and cook for about a minute.
Add the soaked rice along with enough water (about 1.5 inches above the rice) and cover; let it steam‑cook until fully cooked.
When the rice is done, top with the chatpata aloo, lemon slices, and slit chilies; add ghee and fresh onion before serving.
Serve the vegetable biryani with Lauki raita, raw mango raita, or any raita of your choice.

title: Coriander Tamarind Millet Rice Recipe
ingredients: 6 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, chopped (leave bit for garnishing)
instructions: In a vessel add 1/2 cup millets with one cup of water and bring this to a boil, turn the heat to simmer and cook the millets covered with a steam vent cracked open for 8-10 minutes or until the water evaporates. Let it sit for 2 minutes and transfer this to another bowl and let it cool completely.
In a mixie jar add coriander, green chillies, cumin powder, garlic, tamarind extract and salt, grind to a smooth paste. Set aside.
In a pan heat some oil, crackle the mustard seeds, followed by urad dal, channa dal, peanuts, and roast them on low heat until golden.
Now add the asafoetida, turmeric, red chilli and curry leaves.
Add the ground paste and saute until the raw smell disappears, approximately 4 minutes. Add a tiny splash of water if the mixture becomes very dry.
Finally add the cooked millets and gently mix so that the mixture is uniformly applied. Adjust the salt if required.
Top with chopped coriander and serve.
Serve Coriander Tamarind Millet Rice along with Tadka Raita, Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita or any other raita of your choice.

title: Yogurt Lamb Curry Recipe
instructions: Soak Kashmiri red chilies in water for about 30 minutes, then drain and grind into a paste.
Pressure cook lamb with a little salt and a teaspoon of cumin seeds for 1 whistle in a pressure cooker.
In a wide deep bottom pan, heat ghee. Add cumin seeds, green cardamom, black cardamom, cinnamon and cloves to hot oil. Then add onion paste and sauté until the paste turns golden brown.
Add the minced garlic and dry ginger powder (you can also add fresh grated ginger in place of dried ginger powder) and sauté for a minute. Add ground red chilies paste and cook for a minute.
Add cooked lamb pieces without the water and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes. Whisk yogurt well, add that to the curry, and give it a stir.
If required add about 1/4 cup water, salt to taste, cover and cook the lamb until tender.
Finally sprinkle garam masala, dried mint leaves, mix and serve hot.
Serve Yogurt Lamb Curry along with rice, whole wheat lachha parathas or garlic naan for a perfect meal.

title: Calcutta Style Chicken Biryani Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Boneless chicken , cut into pieces of uniform size
instructions: To start preparing this delicious Calcutta Style Chicken Biryani Recipe, marinate the chicken pieces with curd, red chilli powder, turmeric and salt for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Partially cook the rice along with black cardamom and bay leaves. The rice needs to be boiled till 50% done.
Drain away the water and set aside the rice for later use.
Dry roast the rest of the whole spices namely, peppercorns, cloves, green cardamom and cinnamon for 30 seconds or till fragrant. Let it cool and then grind it into a fine powder in a mixer grinder.
Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee in a deep & heavy bottomed pan. Add chopped onions and sauté till soft and lightly browned.
Mash the ginger, garlic, and green chillies together using a mortar & pestle.
Add the ginger-garlic-chilli paste to the onions once they are lightly browned. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder and sauté further for a minute.
Add the marinated chicken to the above, and mix well till the chicken is well-covered with spices. Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes on low flame. Add a little water if required.
While the chicken is cooking, chop the potatoes into four pieces and fry them till crisp and cooked.
Now take a heavy bottomed non-stick Biryani pot or earthen pot and grease it with ghee. Spread one layer of rice and top it with a layer of chicken gravy and 2 potatoes.
Repeat this three times ending with a layer of rice. Heat the rest of the ghee and pour it on the top layer.

Seal the mouth of the pot with wheat flour dough to tighten the lid if using earthen pot and place a heavy weight like mortar on top of it. Cook this on low heat for 10 to 15 minutes and let it stand for another 30 minutes before opening.
Serve Calcutta Style Chicken Biryani hot with Burani raita or Tomato Onion & Cucumber raita and non-veg gravy like Laal Maas or Creamy Butter Chicken.

title: Mustard Egg Curry Recipe
ingredients: 4 whole eggs, boiled, cut into 2 or 4 pieces
1-1/2 tablespoon mustard seeds (Rai/Kadugu), plus 1 teaspoon extra
instructions: Grind together 1-1/2 tablespoon mustard seeds, green chillies, grated coconut, and turmeric using a little coconut milk to help; set the ground masala aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add 1 teaspoon mustard seeds; when they crackle, add curry leaves and the onion. Sauté until the onion softens.
When the onion is soft and translucent, add the ground masala and 1/4 cup water; bring to a boil.
Add the remaining coconut milk, salt, and a pinch of sugar; bring to a boil again. Add the cut egg pieces and cook until the gravy becomes creamy.
Serve the mustard egg curry with tawa paratha or steamed rice and tomato‑onion‑cucumber raita.

title: Kaju Katli Recipe (Kaju Barfi)
instructions: To begin making the Kaju Katli Recipe (Kaju Barfi), take a large heavy bottomed pan, and pour in the sugar and water. Mix them well and boil for about 10 minutes, until the sugar syrup thickens up to a two string consistency.
Grind all the cashew nuts together along with corn flour to a fine powder.
Once the sugar syrup has arrived at a two string consistency, add the cashew nuts and corn flour powder to it.

Continue stirring the Kaju Katli (burfi) mixture together till no lumps remain. Add a teaspoon of ghee and cook for another 7 to 10 minutes, until the Kaju Katli (burfi) mixture contents thickens up and begins to leave the sides of the pan.
The final consistency of the Kaju Katli (burfi) mixture should be of dough consistency.
Once it reaches the dough like consistency, turn off the heat and spread it evenly in a tray keeping about 1/2 inch thickness. Spread the silver varak at this stage and allow it to set.
Once cooled, cut the Kaju Katli (burfi) into desired shapes. You can also optionally make a sandwich of two the Kaju Katli (Burfi) with crushed pistachios and serve.

The delicious Kaju Katli (Burfi) is ready to be eaten, or it can even be refrigerated for future use. Hope you get to make the delicious Kaju Katli Recipe this Diwali and share with friends and family.
Serve Kaju Katli Recipe (Kaju Barfi) as a party dessert or along with Crispy Masala Peanuts Recipe (Gujarati Sing Bhujia) or Baked Chevdo Recipe (Chivda Mixture -Tea Time Snack) during tea time.

title: Soya Chunks Sabzi
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water and salt for 15 minutes.
Chop all the vegetables; heat a kadai with oil and add the chopped onions, cooking until translucent.
Add sliced garlic and thinly sliced ginger, sautéing for 10-15 seconds.
Add slit green chilies and the finely chopped tomatoes.
When the tomatoes are cooked, add red chilli powder to taste.
Stir in garam masala and chaat masala powders.
Drain the water from the soaked soy chunks and squeeze them well.
Add the soy chunks to the pan and mix to coat evenly with the masala.
Adjust salt to taste and switch off the flame.
Add lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the soy chunks sabzi with hot phulkas, chapati, capsicum masala gravy, hot rice, or thakkali rasam.

title: Curried Tofu Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Chinese 5 spice powder (or curry powder)
2 red, yellow, or green bell peppers (capsicum), cubed
instructions: Soak at least 8 wooden skewers in water.
Mix together the ginger, garlic, lime juice, soy sauce, turmeric, curry powder and chilli pepper flakes in a large bowl.
Add the tofu and vegetables into the marinade and stir well to combine. Cover the bowl and marinate the vegetables for an hour or more.
Because the marinade will stain your fingers, wear rubber gloves to thread the tofu and vegetables onto the skewers.
When ready to serve, grill the kebabs using a stovetop grill, a BBQ grill, or the broil function in the oven.
Skewer the marinated vegetables onto the soaked skewers and set aside.
Grease and preheat a grill pan with oil; place the vegetable skewers on the grill and cook until the vegetables are cooked through and lightly browned.
Serve with warm brown rice or as a party snack, optionally alongside a yogurt or cheese dip.

title: Rose Flavoured Golden Almond Milk Recipe - Badam Doodh
instructions: To begin making the Rose Flavoured Golden Almond Milk Recipe, soak almonds in hot water for 10 minutes. Peel the skin and add it to a blender.
Add a teaspoon of milk and blend into smooth or coarse paste as per your preference.
Boil milk in a saucepan, once it comes to boil, add crushed cardamom and sugar.
Stir well and keep boiling on low flame until it reduces a little. Stir at all times.
Add the almond paste to the boiling milk. Mix and boil for 2-3 minutes stirring, often. Take care not to get burnt.
Now add turmeric powder to the milk. Mix and remove from flame.
Let it cool, pour rose water to the milk and give it a mix.
Pour into serving glass and garnish with chopped almonds and serve.
Serve Rose Flavoured Golden Almond Milk Recipe along with Fresh Fruits and Spicy Potato Chutney Sandwich for a healthy morning breakfast.

title: Spiced Watermelon Curry Recipe With Carrots & Peppers
ingredients: 2 cups Watermelon, cut into cubes (without skin)
instructions: To begin making the Spiced Watermelon Curry Recipe with Carrots & Peppers, we will first make sure we have the watermelon, carrots and peppers diced and kept ready. Make sure to remove the seeds of the watermelon.
Make the homemade tomato puree and keep aside. Get all the ingredients ready and keep it by the side.
The next step is to cook the carrots and pepper.

Heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan or wok. Add the ajwain seeds, carrots and bell peppers. Sprinkle some salt and stir fry until the carrots and peppers are cooked through. You can cover the pan so the vegetables get cooked faster.

Once the vegetables are cooked, add the turmeric powder, chilli powder, cumin powder and give it a stir for a few seconds. Add the tomato puree, watermelon, salt and a cup of water. Cover the pan and allow the watermelon curry to simmer for about 10 minutes until you can smell flavors of the curry coming through.
After 10 minutes, check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste. Turn off the heat and transfer the watermelon curry to a serving bowl. Stir in the coriander leaves.
Serve the Spiced Watermelon Curry Recipe with Carrots & Peppers along with steamed Jasmine Rice and Carrot Cucumber Tomato Salad with Lemon and Coriander for a summery weeknight dinner.

title: Makhane Ki Phirni Recipe - Lotus Seed Milk Pudding
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Dry Fruits (Raisins, Almonds, Cashew, Pistachio)
instructions: Heat the ghee on a skillet and roast the makhana for about 5 minutes; then pulse it in a blender for a minute until it becomes a coarse powder. Set aside.
Mix together all the flavoring ingredients and lightly crush them with a rolling pin or pulse once in a grinder; set aside in a bowl.
In a heavy‑bottomed pan, pour in the milk, add the flavoring mixture and sugar, and boil on low flame for about 10 minutes, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Add the crushed makhana to the milk mixture and simmer on low flame for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Switch off the heat and let the phirni cool.
Pour the phirni into small serving bowls, garnish with rose petals and spoonfuls of mixed dry fruit powder.
Cover each serving bowl with cling film and refrigerate for 2–3 hours.
Serve the chilled Makhane Ki Phirni with a snack plate or as a dessert after lunch.

title: Egg Curry Masala Recipe With Sunny Side Up Eggs
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch finely chopped (for garnish)
instructions: To begin making the Sunny Side Up Egg Curry Masala Recipe, preheat a pan with oil over medium heat.
Once the oil is hot, add the onions and cook till onion turns soft and translucent. This will take about 2 minutes.
Next, add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, salt and saute until the spice powders are well combined. It will take 2 to 3 minutes.
Add in the tomatoes and give it a good mix. Cover the pan with a lid and let the gravy cook for about 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, add in the coconut milk and mix well.
Keep the heat low and let the Egg Curry masala come to a boil. Add water to adjust to the consistency of your choice and let it cook for another 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, break the egg directly into the gravy at 4 different spots one after another. Sprinkle some salt on the yolk.

Cover the pan with a lid and let the eggs cook for about 8 to 10 minutes. If you like the yolk half cooked, reduce the cooking time to 6 minutes and serve the Sunny Side Up Egg Curry Masala Recipe immediately.
If you like a runny yolk, cover and cook for just 4 minutes or until the egg whites are cooked and you can see the yolk through a thin film formed on top.
Once the egg is cooked according to your preference, garnish the Sunny Side Up Egg Curry Masala Recipe with coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve Sunny Side Up Egg Curry Masala Recipe along with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha, Burani Raita and Kachumber Salad for a weeknight dinner.

title: Raw Banana and Banana Stem Stuffed Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 banana stem, cut into small pieces
instructions: Boil the raw bananas in a pressure cooker with water and salt for about 4 whistles; then release pressure naturally, peel and mash them into a fine mixture.
Heat a saucepan with oil, add cumin seeds and let them splutter for 10 seconds, then add chopped onions, garlic, and ginger and sauté until softened.
Add the chopped banana stem along with ½ cup water, cover and cook for about 15 minutes until the stem is tender.

Stir in all the spice powders – turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, amchur powder, salt and black pepper powder – and also add the mashed raw banana; mix well and cook on low heat for another 10 minutes, then turn off the heat.
In a bowl, combine the whole wheat flour with the prepared filling and knead into a soft dough, adding water as needed.
Divide the dough into large lemon‑sized balls, dust each piece with flour, flatten and roll into a 3‑inch diameter circle.
Place the filling on half of the circle, fold the edges over to seal and form a dumpling‑shaped paratha.
Gently press and roll the stuffed paratha with a rolling pin, being careful not to roll too thin or let the filling escape.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat, place the rolled paratha on it and cook one side for 10‑15 seconds.
Flip the paratha, smear a little oil or ghee on the surface, and continue cooking, flipping a few times until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
Serve the raw banana and banana stem stuffed paratha with fresh curd or a side dish such as Aam Ka Chunda.

title: Methi Bajra Poori Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves) , cleaned, washed and chopped
1 teaspoon Red Chilli powder , or green chilli paste
instructions: To begin making the Methi Bajra Poori, firstly mix all the ingredients except the oil for deep frying, in a mixing bowl or in the bowl of a food processor.
Gradually add water and knead it into a firm yet pliable dough. Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Make small balls from the dough. Roll them out into small round discs. Keep them covered till they are ready to be fried.
Heat oil in a Kadhai/Wok. Gently slide in the rolled poori or 2-3 pooris (depending on the size of your wok).
Deep fry on medium high heat until they puff and turn golden brown on both sides.
Take out the pooris using a slotted spoon and place on absorbent paper. Serve hot.
Serve Methi Bajra Poori on its own as a snack or it can be teamed up with Aloo Dum or any other curry for an indulgent meal.

title: Badshahi Chicken Recipe
instructions: Wash the chicken pieces, transfer to a bowl and marinate with salt for half an hour.
In a mixer jar, combine the cashew nuts and grind with some water until smooth.
In a skillet, dry roast the ingredients – green cardamom, black cardamom, mace and nutmeg till fragrant on low heat.
Allow the roasted spices to cool, then pulse them in a mixer‑grind to a fine powder; reserve about 3/4 tablespoon for the recipe.
In a kadai, add oil and deep‑fry the chicken on medium‑high flame.
When the oil is hot, add the chicken pieces gradually and fry for about 3 minutes on medium flame; remove with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil.
Alternatively, shallow‑fry the chicken for 10‑12 minutes until done if less oil is preferred.
In a kadai, heat a bit of oil and add cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon stick; sauté until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and fry until golden brown and caramelized over medium‑high heat.
Add ginger, garlic, and onion paste one by one; sauté until the raw aroma disappears.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, and cumin powder; sauté, reserving Kashmiri chilli powder for later.
In a small bowl, mix curd, ground cashew nut paste, and Kashmiri chilli powder until smooth; add this mixture to the kadai and stir until it leaves the sides of the pan.
Add the fried chicken pieces and mix well.
Add slit green chillies and the freshly ground masala (about 3/4 tablespoon); adjust to taste.
Stir occasionally and continue cooking for about 5 minutes, then add milk and check salt level; adjust water if needed.
Cover and cook until the chicken is tender.
Once tender, add ghee and rose water (if using); cover and cook for another 2‑5 minutes until well combined, then switch off.
Serve the Badshahi Chicken with homemade butter naan, chilli coriander fried rice, and mutton shami kebab.

title: Masala Soda Shikanji Recipe
ingredients: 700 ml Sprite, or any lemon soda
Mint Leaves (Pudina), a few, roughly torn
instructions: To begin making the Masala Soda Shikanji Recipe, fill the pitcher with ice cubes.
Add the lime juice and top it up with sprite. Stir it well.
Using a pestle and mortar, muddle the green chillies along with the chaat masala.
Add a little water to it and pour into the sprite filled pitcher. Add the lemon wedges and the roughly torn mint leaves into the pitcher and stir.
Serve Masala Soda Shikanji Recipe immediately with Baked Aloo Tikki Recipe (Spicy Potato Patties or Cutlets) or Bhel Puri Recipe - An Indian Street Food & Tea Time Snack in the evening.

title: Achari Chicken Tikka Wrap Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Chicken Tikka Wrap Recipe marinate the chicken with lemon juice, ginger garlic paste, turmeric powder and salt in a mixing bowl. Marinate this for about an hour.
Heat a sauce pan with oil on medium flame, add ajwain seeds and allow them to sizzle for few seconds. Reduce the flame and add the gram flour and mix well switch off the heat.
Into the marinated chicken, add curd and the spice powders, add the heated gram flour mixture and mix well.
Rest this marinated chicken mixture in the fridge for one more hour.
Heat a grill pan, grease it with oil, once it heated, take the chicken pieces out and skewer them into a wooden skewers.
Place the skewers gently and cook on all the sides until the chicken pieces are charred and cooked well. Keep them aside.
Make the Tawa paratha using the link in the recipe or you can also use tortillas.

Place the tawa paratha on a flat surface, spread lettuce leaves, sliced onions, tomatoes and the chicken pieces to one corner. Drizzle the Nutralite Achari Mayo and start rolling them tightly and wrap it using a foil and serve.
Serve the Chicken Tikka Wrap Recipe as a snack along with glass of Mulled Apple Juice Recipe or a Chickoo Banana Date Smoothie Recipe by the side.

title: Tomato Jam Recipe
ingredients: 2 Cinnamon Stick (Dalchini), crush into coarse powder
instructions: To begin making the Tomato Jam recipe, wash tomatoes and make a slit in cross (X) in endways.
Boil water nicely. Switch off and drop tomatoes inside hot water. Let it remain in it for about 5 to 10 minutes. This will help to peel skin off from tomatoes easily.
Take them out from water, allow to cool. Peel off skin and discard them. Squeeze out some of the juice and seeds from it. You can use it for something else.
Chop tomato into very fine pieces or blend in a processor for few seconds.
Take a heavy bottom large pan/kadai. Pour tomatoes into it. Boil for about 15 minutes on medium high flame to reduce liquid.
Add sugar, cinnamon and cloves powder. Mix well and let the gas be on medium flame. Bring mixture to full boil stirring frequently in between.
As it thickens, stir constantly and reduce the flame. Make sure not to overcook. Jam will thicken as it cools.
When the jam has reached a thick sauce consistency, add lemon juice. Mix well, turn off flame. Cool for about 10 minutes and pour into clean sterilised glass bottles.
When the jam has reached a thick sauce consistency, add lemon juice. Mix well, turn off flame. Cool for about 10 mins and pour into clean sterilised glass bottles.
Once it cools completely, close the lid and refrigerate/store in a cool dry place. Use when required for bread, buns, chapathi etc.
Serve Tomato Jam during breakfast on toast and along with a cup of Masala Chai.

title: Gajar Amla Raita Recipe - Carrot Gooseberry Raita Recipe
instructions: In a bowl, add yogurt and salt, then whisk until smooth and lump‑free; set aside.
Cut the amla, discard the seeds, toss the pieces with rai kuria, red chilli powder, and salt; let rest for 15 minutes.
Stir the grated carrot, green chilli, the rested amla, and grated coconut into the yogurt mixture; mix well and adjust salt to taste.
Heat a tadka pan over medium heat, add 1/4 teaspoon oil.
When the oil is hot, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; allow the mustard seeds to crackle, then add curry leaves and turn off the heat.
Pour the tempering over the prepared raita and mix well.
Serve the Gajar Nariyal Amla Raita with Hyderabadi Vegetable Biryani and Mirchi Ka Salan.

title: Beetroot Tambuli Recipe
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep ready.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat, add the grated beetroot with a little salt, and cook for a few minutes until soft; then turn off the heat and let the beetroot cool.
In a mixer jar, combine the fresh coconut, cooked beetroot, green chilli, cumin seeds and whole peppercorns; add 1/2 cup warm water to grind into a smooth coconut masala and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the whisked curd with the freshly ground coconut‑beetroot masala and season with salt.

For the tadka, heat coconut oil over medium heat; add mustard seeds, cumin seeds and split urad dal, allowing them to crackle and turn golden brown. Add the broken dry red chilli and curry leaves, roast for a few seconds, then turn off the heat.
Pour the prepared tadka over the beetroot tambuli and mix gently.
Serve the Beetroot Tambuli with steamed rice and Padpe Uppukari (Harive Soppu Palya) for a simple South Indian lunch.

title: Quick And Simple Egg Curry Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few leaves, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Quick & Easy Egg Curry Recipe, firstly boil the eggs. Add the eggs in a saucepan with enough water to cover them and boil for 15 minutes or until the shells crack.
Let the boiled eggs cool down, then peel the shells and set the eggs aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok; add the onion, garlic and ginger paste. Sauté for a few minutes until the raw smell disappears and the onion changes color.
Add turmeric powder, sugar, garam masala powder, coriander powder and red chilli powder to the roasted onion. Stir the spices into the onion masala and cook for about 3–4 minutes.
Add tomato puree, salt and the boiled eggs. Cover and simmer the egg curry for 10–15 minutes until the eggs are well coated with the gravy.
Check salt and spice levels and adjust the consistency with water if needed. Stir in chopped coriander leaves and serve.
Serve the egg curry with steamed rice, carrot salad and boondi raita for a complete meal.

title: Mango Kesari Recipe | Mango Sooji Halwa | Mango Sheera
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups Water (depending on the consistency you desire)
instructions: Prepare the mango pulp by washing, peeling, chopping, and blending the mango until smooth; set aside.
In a small tadka pan melt a teaspoon of ghee and toast the halved cashew nuts over low heat until golden brown; set aside.
Heat 1/4 cup of ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat and dry‑roast the semolina (sooji) until lightly toasted and aromatic.
In a saucepan, combine 2‑1/2 cups of water with sugar and bring to a boil; cook for about a minute.
Slowly add the boiling sugar‑water mixture to the roasted semolina while continuously stirring to avoid lumps; lower the flame.
Continue stirring as the semolina absorbs the liquid and thickens into a halwa‑like consistency, breaking any lumps that form.
Add the prepared mango pulp to the semolina mixture and cook for 5‑7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the halwa pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle cardamom powder, and garnish with the toasted cashew nuts (both halved and chopped); give a final stir.
Serve the Mango Kesari warm as a dessert or with a savory dish like Sooji Upma.

title: Mung Pani Recipe - Whole Green Mung Soup
ingredients: 1/2 cup Green Moong Dal (Whole), soaked for 4 hours
instructions: To begin making the Mung Pani Recipe, soak the beans for about 3 to 4 hours. Next we will cook the mung lentils in one and a half cups of water until soft and mushy. To cook it in the pressure cooker place the beans along with the water, cover the cooker, place the weight on and cook until you hear two to three whistles.
After two to three whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer to cook for another 10 minutes. After 10 minutes turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure is released, open the cooker and you will have a mushy well cooked mung beans.

Puree the cooked mung beans in a blender. If you have a heat‑tolerant blender, blend the beans with 2 cups of water into a smooth puree; otherwise let the dal cool slightly before blending until smooth.
Heat ghee in a saucepan, add the cumin seeds and allow them to crackle for a few seconds.
Stir in the pureed mung mixture, asafoetida, black pepper, and salt; bring the soup to a boil for a couple of minutes, then turn off the heat and adjust seasoning to taste.
Serve the Mung Pani Soup as an immunity builder at least two times a week or as a warming winter soup.

title: Besan Arbi Roast Recipe - Spicy Colocasia Stir Fry
instructions: Scrub the arbi to remove mud and dirt, then pressure cook it with a little water and a pinch of salt for 1 whistle; turn off the heat and open the cooker once pressure releases.
Peel the skin off the cooked arbi and cut the pieces lengthwise in half, placing them in a large mixing bowl.
In a wide plate, mix gram flour (besan), red chilli powder, coriander powder, salt, turmeric powder, amchur powder, and roasted cumin powder.
Add the mixed spice powder to the cut arbi and toss well to coat evenly.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan, add the besan‑coated arbi in small batches and roast until golden brown on all sides; repeat in 2‑3 batches, adding oil as needed, then drain the roasted arbi on a kitchen towel and set aside on a serving platter.

In another pan, heat 1 teaspoon of oil, add cumin seeds, ajwain (carom) seeds, and the finely chopped green chilli, sauté for about 10 seconds, then combine this tempering with the roasted besan arbi and toss gently.
Sprinkle chopped coriander leaves and drizzle lemon juice over the besan arbi, then serve.
Optionally, serve the Besan Arbi Roast with Dal Palak and Steamed Rice for a complete meal.

title: Creamy Mocha Lassi Recipe
instructions: To begin making this Creamy Mocha Lassi Recipe, get prep with all the ingredients mentioned.
Blend all ingredients - yogurt, milk, coffee powder, honey and cocoa powder in a blender jar until smooth, creamy and frothy. Do a taste test and add more honey or sugar to adjust to your sweetness.
Adjust the consistency of the lassi according to your preference by adding more water or milk. Also adjust honey/sugar to taste.
Serve immediately or keep in refrigerator until serving time.
Serve Creamy Mocha Lassi Recipe with snacks like Makki Paneer Pakora Recipe or Mangalorean Style Biscuit Roti Recipe.

title: Egg Biryani Recipe With Coconut Milk
ingredients: 1 Green Chilli, slit down the middle
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
Mint Leaves (Pudina), small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Boil the eggs: fill a heavy saucepan with water, add the eggs, bring to a boil, boil for 3-4 minutes, then medium heat for another 10 minutes, turn off heat, let cool, peel and set aside.
Heat a pressure cooker with ghee on medium heat, add whole spices (cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, black peppercorns) and let them sizzle.
Add sliced onions, minced ginger and garlic; sauté until the onions turn deep golden, using low to medium heat.
Stir in turmeric powder and red chilli powder, sauté a few seconds, then add diced tomatoes and the slit green chilli; sauté until tomatoes soften.
Add cumin powder, coriander powder, and salt; cook the masala until the oil separates and the tomatoes become mushy.
Mix in garam masala and coconut milk, combine well; add the boiled eggs and simmer on low heat for about 15 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly.
Taste and adjust salt and spices as needed.
Add washed and drained rice, water, chopped coriander and mint leaves; stir, close the pressure cooker and cook for about 3 whistles, then turn off heat.
Allow pressure to release naturally, open the cooker, gently mix and fluff the rice, transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.

title: Spicy Indian Style Onion Rings Recipe
ingredients: 3 Onions, cut into thick rounds, rings separated
instructions: In the mixer grind together the ginger, garlic, red chillies, green chilli and curry leaves with a tablespoon of water into a coarse paste. Transfer to a bowl and set aside until required.
Heat oil for deep frying the onion rings over medium heat while you prepare the batter to coat the onion rings.
In a mixing bowl, sift together the flour, besan, corn flour, soda along with salt and ginger paste.
Whisk gently to mix well. Gradually add little water at a time to make thick batter. The batter should be thick dropping consistency so it coats the onion rings.
Add a few thick onion rings into the batter and using a fork, allow them to get well-coated. Using the fork transfer them into the hot oil, fry till golden and crisp.
Transfer to a plate lined with oil absorbent paper. Similarly fry the remaining onion rings.
Serve Spicy Indian Style Onion Rings along with Green Chutney or a yogurt dip for a sunday evening teatime snack.

title: Curry Fried Quinoa Rice Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups quinoa, cooked beforehand, cold or day old
1 cup brown rice, cooked beforehand, cold or day old
1/2 teaspoon garlic, finely diced or crushed
2 whole eggs, whisked in a bowl
instructions: Mix the cooked quinoa and brown rice in a bowl, break down any lumps with your hands (greasing them with a little oil if needed) and set aside.
Heat a little oil in a pan, add the whisked egg and scramble vigorously until cooked, then transfer the scrambled egg to a plate.
In the same wok, add the remaining oil, then sauté garlic and curry leaves for 30 seconds, followed by onions and red bell pepper for another 30 seconds.
Add the peas and carrots, sauté on high heat for a minute or two until half‑cooked.
Stir in curry powder, soy sauce, salt, brown sugar and black pepper, cook for 30 seconds, then add the quinoa‑rice mixture and stir‑fry until well combined.
Add the scrambled egg, combine, turn off the heat and transfer to a serving plate.
Serve the curry fried quinoa rice with pumpkin raita or lauki raita.

title: Spicy Matar Masala Recipe
ingredients: 1 Bay leaf (tej patta), broken into two pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and add cumin seeds and mustard seeds.
When they splutter, add curry leaves, bay leaf, cloves and cardamom pods.
After a minute, add green chillies and ginger garlic paste, cooking for about a minute.
Add the chopped onions and cook until soft and translucent.
Stir in the onion paste and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, then add tomato puree along with all the masalas and salt.
Cook for 5 to 8 minutes or until the oil starts separating.
Add the green peas and cook for another 2 minutes.
Check salt and spice, adjust to taste, and switch off the flame.
Serve the Spicy Matar Masala with roti and dal.

title: Spicy Chickpeas Aloo Salad Chaat Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked overnight
instructions: Soak the chickpeas overnight and keep it ready.
In a pressure cooker, add the chana and water and pressure cook for 6 whistles on medium flame, reduce the flame and continue to cook for 15 more minutes. Turn off the flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, drain the water and transfer the chana into a bowl and set aside.
In the same pressure cooker boil the aloo for at least 3 whistles, then peel the skin off and cut them into cubes.
In a mixing bowl, combine the kala chana, onion, tomato, green chilli, aloo, black salt, pepper powder, chaat masala and lemon juice.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve immediately.
Serve the Spicy Chickpeas Aloo Salad Chaat with Indian Style Beetroot Soup and Masala Cheese Bread Loaf for a hearty dinner.
You can also serve this salad with Masala Chai or Carrot Amla Pomegranate Juice during the evening.

title: Soya Chunks And Beetroot Biryani Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups Basmati rice, soaked in enough water for 20 minutes
15-20 Soy Chunks (Nuggets), soaked in warm water for 20 minutes
instructions: Soak the soya chunks in warm water for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the water and chop them.
Blend mint and coriander leaves in a mixer grinder with 2 tablespoon water to a smooth paste and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoon groundnut oil in a heavy‑bottom pan; add cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and ajwain, sauté for about 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add chopped onions and green chilies; sauté until the onions turn golden brown.
Add tomatoes and sauté until soft and mushy.
Add chopped beetroot and the soaked soya chunks; stir well.
Stir in the mint‑coriander paste, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and salt; add 1 cup water, cover and cook for 10 minutes.

Add coconut milk and 1/2 cup water; when it starts boiling, add the soaked rice, lemon juice and salt, mix well and cook covered on low‑medium heat until the rice is done. Fluff the biryani and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve the Soya Chunks and Beetroot Biryani with Burani Raita, Lauki Raita, or any raita of your choice.

title: Satvik Carrot Sprouts Salad Recipe - No Onion No Garlic
ingredients: 1/4 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), finely chopped
1/4 cup Raw Peanuts (Moongphali), soaked in water for 3-4 hours
instructions: Grate the carrots and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine the grated carrots, green moong sprouts, capsicum, coconut, peanuts, lemon juice, and season with salt and black pepper powder.
Mix the salad well and serve fresh.
Serve the Satvik Carrot Sprouts Salad as a side dish with Panchmel Dal, Bhindi Masala, and Phulkas.

title: Maharashtrian Masale Baath Recipe - Spicy Vegetable Rice with Goda Masala
ingredients: 1 Carrot (Gajjar), peeled and cut into cubes
1/2 cup Green beans (French Beans), cut small
1 Potato (Aloo), peeled and cut into cubes
instructions: To prepare the Maharashtrian Masale Bhath Recipe, first clean, wash and soak the rice in enough water for 30 minutes or so.
Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the mustard seeds, allow seeds to crackle. Add bay leaf and fry for few seconds.

Add the sliced onions and fry till they turn light brown in color. Next add all the chopped vegetables - carrot, beans, cauliflower, potatoes, onions and fry for a few minutes. Now add the yogurt and stir to combine, saute the vegetables for next few minutes.
In the meanwhile heat 2.5 cups of water and bring it to a boil in another pan.
Add the rice along with red chili powder, goda masala, asafoetida, salt to the sauteed vegetables. Stir to combine and saute for a minute or so. Now add the hot water to the rice mixture.
Cover the pan and simmer the rice on a low flame till the grains are softened and cooked well.
If you are using the pressure cooker to cook the rice, turn off the heat after one or two whistles. Let the steam escape naturally from the pressure cooker before opening the lid.
To serve Masala Baath, in a small pan heat ghee over medium heat, roast the cashews till golden brown in colour. Turn off the heat.
Serve Maharashtrian Masale Bhat Recipe along with Boondi Raita Recipe Spiced With Black Salt and Kothimbir Vadi Recipe (Maharashtrian Coriander Fritters) for the flavorful weekday lunch.

title: Mixed Beans Vegetable Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Rice , washed and soaked for 10 min
1/4 cup Rajma (Large Kidney Beans) , washed and soaked overnight
1/8 cup Double Beans , washed and soaked overnight
instructions: To begin making the Mixed Beans Vegetable Pulao recipe, pressure cook the rajma in a cooker and double beans with enough water until soft. (Take care not to turn them mushy). Wait till pressure settles. Drain excess water and set it aside.
In a heavy bottom cooking vessel, add oil and to it add cloves, cardamom and cinnamon stick.

When the spices start to leave their aroma, add sliced onions. Fry till translucent. Now add ginger-garlic paste. Fry for another minute and add boiled rajma and double beans. Saute for a minute or two.
After a minute or two, add chopped potato, carrot, green beans, green chilies, garam masala and turmeric powder. Saute for two minutes.

Add 4 cups of water to this along with salt. Let it come to boil. Now add rice (by draining the water, in which rice was getting soaked). Gently stir and cook covered on low flame till rice is completely cooked.
Sprinkle lemon juice and garnish with coriander leaves before serving.
Serve Mixed Beans Vegetable Pulao with Lauki Raita, Beetroot Raita or any other raita of your choice and a roasted papad.

title: Homemade Doodh Peda Recipe - Milk Peda
instructions: To begin making the Homemade Doodh Peda Recipe, in a wide non stick pan, combine the condensed milk and milk powder and mix it into a smooth paste without any lumps.
Add in the cardamom powder, ghee or butter into the mixture and stir to combine well.
Place the pan on medium heat and stir continuously until it becomes a thick batter. Turn off the heat as soon as the mixture thickens and you see it leaving the sides of the pan.
Be careful, as the mixture will thicken up quickly. The mixture will thicken further when it is cooling down.

Once it becomes thick and leaves the sides of the pan, turn off the heat and transfer the peda dough to another bowl and allow it to cool to a temperature such that you can use your hands to knead them.
Once cooled, knead the peda dough until smooth and fluffy.

You can add a little ghee to knead if the peda dough. Divide the dough into small lemon sized balls. Make an impression with the thumb in the center and place a piece of pistachio in the center and serve.
Serve the delicious Doodh Pedas as a snack or make them during festivals like Diwali or as a dessert after a festive meal like Vegetable Oatmeal Poha with Peanuts, Coriander & Ginger.

title: Green Beans Fry Recipe
instructions: Clean the beans and chop them finely. Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan and add hing and cumin seeds. Sauté for 15 to 20 seconds.
Add green chillies and beans to the pan.
Add salt and turmeric powder and cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add red chilli powder and coriander powder.
Cover the lid and cook until the beans become soft and cooked through.
Stir occasionally to prevent burning.
Switch off the stove and serve the green beans fry with boiled/steamed rice and Mixed Vegetable Sambar.

title: Sing Paak Recipe - Spiced Peanut Burfi
instructions: Heat the sugar and water in a small pan over medium heat until the sugar melts completely and the syrup reaches a stringy, two‑thread consistency.
Add the saffron to the syrup and stir, then add the powdered peanuts and mix until well combined while still on the heat.
Turn off the gas and stir in the ghee, followed by the pistachios. Keep stirring until the mixture comes away from the sides of the pan.
Spread the mixture evenly on a large tray greased with ghee, preferably one with a rim just large enough to hold the burfi.
Allow the peanut burfi to rest in the tray and cool completely, about 5–6 hours, until firm.
Cut the cooled burfi into small square or diamond pieces and serve.

title: Egg Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Whole Black Peppercorns, freshly crushed
3 cups Basmati rice, soaked for 45 mins
instructions: To begin making the Egg Pulao recipe, we will firstly fry the eggs. In a pan, heat 1 tablespoon of ghee and add the boiled eggs.
Add red chilli powder and toss well. Add freshly cracked pepper and fry until eggs are slightly brown and a little crisp. Keep them aside.
The next step is to make the pulao. Take another deep bottom pan or handi, heat ghee or oil.
Add cumin seeds, green cardamom, cinnamon, black peppercorns, star anise and fry them for few seconds till the cumin seeds crackle.
Meanwhile, add green chilli, garlic and ginger in a grinder and make a paste.
Once the cumin seeds crackle, add the ground coarse paste of green chili, garlic, ginger and saute for a minute.
Add onions and fry until it just starts picking up the golden color. Do not over-fry the onions.
Add sliced tomatoes, slit green chilies and cook until the tomatoes are mushy. Add turmeric and mix everything properly.
After 2 minutes, add in the whisked yogurt and stir until the yogurt is well combined with the spices.
Add salt, chopped mint, lemon juice and coriander leaves. Cook for half a minute.
Add soaked and drained rice and gently mix it. Give a slight slit to the fried eggs and add it along with the water. Bring it to a boil and cook until 80% of the water dries up.
Cover and simmer until done. (Approximately for 15 to 20 mins)
Gently fluff up the rice using a fork. Cover, let it rest for few minutes and Egg Pulao is ready to be served.
Serve Egg Pulao along with Burani Raita, Beetroot Raita or any other Raita of your choice and a roasted papad for your everyday meal.

title: Cabbage Carrot Onion Pudina Thepla Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Cabbage Carrot Onion Pudina Thepla Recipe, we will first attach the chopping blade into the food processor and then add the cabbage and onion in the processor. Close the lid and turn on the food processor. Finely chop the onion and cabbage.
Remove the chopping blade and attach the grating blade. Add the carrot through the spout of the food processor and grate the carrots.
Once done remove the grating blade and attach the kneading blade. Add the flour, close the lid and turn on the food processor to mix everything well.
Next add in the green chillies, mint leaves, cumin powder, salt to taste and start the blender.
Slowly, add little water at a time to bring the dough together. Drizzle oil through the spout and continue to blend until the dough comes away from the side of the bowl.
If your dough looks too sticky, then add some more flour to the processor and blend. Once done, take out the dough into a bowl.
Divide the Cabbage Carrot Onion Pudina dough into lemon sized portions and keep aside.
Dust a worktop with flour and roll the dough in flour. With the help of the rolling pin flatten the balls into a 5 inch diameter circle. The thepla should be nice and thin to cook evenly and quickly.
Preheat a tawa on high heat and place the Cabbage Carrot Onion Pudina Thepla on the hot tawa.

Flip after a few seconds once you notice small bubbles forming on the top. Drizzle oil over the Cabbage Carrot Onion Pudina Thepla and flip again after a few seconds. Drizzle oil on the other side again.
Continue to flip and cook the thepla on high heat until golden brown spots appear.
The continuous flipping and cooking motion helps to cook the theplas properly and also ensures that they remain soft.
Continue the similar process with the remaining rolled portions and serve hot.
Serve the Cabbage Carrot Onion Pudina Thepla Recipe along with Gujarati Kadhi Recipe and Khatti Meethi Tindora Sabzi for a delicious everyday meal.

title: Coriander Tadka Raita Recipe
instructions: In a bowl combine the water and curd and whisk well.
Add the coriander leaves, mint leaves, green chilli, salt, and cumin powder to the bowl and mix everything well.
Heat oil in a tadka pan over medium flame, add the cumin seeds and garlic, and fry until they turn a lovely brown colour; turn off the flame.
Add the prepared tadka to the curd mixture, stir, and serve.
Serve the coriander tadka raita alongside Chettinad vegetable biryani and mirchi bajji for a simple weekday meal.

title: Bajra Matar Ki Khichdi (Gluten Free Breakfast Recipe)
instructions: To prepare Bajra Matar Ki Khichdi, soak bajra in water for about 4 hours or overnight. Soak moong dal in water for about an hour.

In a pressure cooker, add soaked bajra, moong dal, green chilies and turmeric powder. Add 4 cups of water and cook over medium flame for 4 whistles. Ensure water is added more to get the creamy consistency. Bajra takes time to cook, hence cook for 4-5 whistles depending on the pressure cooker. Set aside.
Meanwhile, chop all the vegetables required for Bajra Matar Ki Khichdi.
In a Kadai, add oil and heat over medium flame.
Once the oil is hot, add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, hing and cook until the seeds clutter. Cook until the cumin seeds become light brownish.
Add onions and cook until they become translucent.
Add tomatoes and cook until they become mushy.
Now, stir in the chopped vegetables and combine them well.
Add red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala, required salt and cook until the vegetables become soft and cooked.
Combine the vegetable mixture with the gluten free bajra-dal mixture.
Combine until they are blended together and cook over low flame for about 3-4 minutes.
Switch off the flame and garnish with coriander leaves.
Add lime juice to the khichdi at the time of serving.
Serve Khichdi warmly with pickle of your choice.

title: Lauki Aloo Sabzi Recipe - Bottle Gourd Potato Vegetable Curry
instructions: To begin making the Lauki Aloo Sabzi Recipe first get the potatoes and lauki (bottlegourd) peeled and diced. Get the remaining ingredients ready.
We will be cooking using a pressure cooker, but you can cook the same vegetable in a heavy bottomed pan if you don't have a pressure cooker.

Heat oil in the pressure cooker or the pan on medium heat. Add the nigella seeds and allow it to crackle. Add the onions and ginger; saute until the onions become slightly soft. Add all the remaining ingredients along with 1-1/2 cups of water and salt to taste as well.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook until you hear a couple of whistles. After a couple of whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for about 3 to 4 minutes and turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally in the pressure cooker as the vegetables will continue to cook and soften inside while there is pressure.
If you were cooking in the pan, cook on low heat until the vegetables get cooked completely and the curry has a gravy-like texture.
Open the cooker/pan and give the Aloo Lauki Sabzi a stir. Check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste.
Serve the Lauki Aloo Sabzi along with Phulkas and a Grated Carrot Salad for a weeknight dinner along with a glass of buttermilk.

title: Paneer Frankie Recipe - Delicious Kid Friendly Snack
ingredients: 4 Whole Wheat Tawa Paratha, made into round large sizes for rolls
200 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), cut into strips
instructions: To begin making the Healthy Paneer Frankie (Rolls) Recipe prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Make the whole wheat paratha according to the Tawa Paratha Recipe; cook the parathas in ghee or oil and keep aside.

Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat; add the red capsicum and onion and roast them well till it soft and tender. Once the capsicum and onion are tender, add the cut paneer pieces, the Del Monte Tandoori Mayo and toss until well coated. Avoid over cooking the paneer at this stage as it can make the paneer rubbery.

Spread the aluminium foil on the flat surface and place the tawa paratha over it. Next, place the lettuce evenly over the paratha, add spoon two tablespoons of the paneer filling over one side of the frankie. Roll the paneer frankie tightly till the other end.

Fold the ends of the paneer frankie to pack it tightly in the aluminum foil on all sides. This is a great way to carry a frankie to picnics or a party. All you have to do later is to warm it in the oven at 200 C for 5 minutes and then cut it in the center and serve.
Serve the Paneer Frankie (Rolls) Recipe along with a glass of Indian Spiced Buttermilk as an after school snack or even for a saturday afternoon kids party with their friends.

title: Baked Masala Namak Para Recipe - Carom Seeds Spiced Biscuits
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Oil, and more to brush
1 teaspoon Chaat Masala Powder, for sprinkling at the end
instructions: Gather all the ingredients.
In a mixing bowl, add the whole wheat flour, all‑purpose flour, ajwain (carom seeds), crushed black pepper, asafoetida, turmeric powder, salt, and ghee.
Mix until the mixture resembles crumbs; if it starts forming a ball, begin adding water, otherwise add a bit more ghee and continue mixing until the texture is right.
Add water little by little to form a firm, stiff, smooth, and pliable dough. Apply a thin layer of oil on the surface and let the dough rest for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
Divide the rested dough into two equal portions and shape each into a ball.
Lightly oil the rolling surface and roll each ball into a roti about half an inch thick.

Using a knife, cut the roti into 1 cm wide strips, then cut those strips at an angle to form small diamond‑shaped pieces (or any desired shape). Arrange the pieces about half a centimeter apart on a parchment‑lined or greased baking tray.
Brush the cut pieces with oil.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 10 minutes, or until the edges turn golden.
Flip the pieces and bake for another 10 minutes until both sides are golden and the para are cooked through.
Remove from the tray while hot, sprinkle with chaat masala, and allow to cool before storing in an airtight container.
Serve the baked masala namak para as a tea‑time snack.

title: Dhaba Style Spicy Ghee Rice Recipe Made From Whole Spices
ingredients: 1 cup rice, washed and soaked for 20 minutes
instructions: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker over medium heat. Once hot, add the green chilli, bay leaf, cumin seeds, cardamom, cloves, star anise, cinnamon sticks, whole black peppercorns, and curry leaves.
Stir for a few seconds until the aromas are released.
Add the washed rice, 1½ cups water, and salt to taste. Cover and pressure cook for 3 to 4 whistles, then turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally so the rice continues cooking while still under pressure.
Let the rice rest for 10 minutes, then open the cooker, fluff the rice, and serve hot.
Serve the Dhaba Style Spicy Ghee Rice with Tandoori Paneer Tikka Masala, Smoked Dal Makhani Dhaba Style, and Tadka Raita for a complete meal.

title: Lehsun Methi Raita Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup fresh methi leaves (fenugreek leaves), finely chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a pan on medium flame, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add chopped garlic and sauté until golden and the raw garlic aroma disappears.
Add chopped methi leaves and sauté on high flame.
Add salt to taste and cook until the methi leaves wilt.
Turn off the heat and set the cooked methi aside to cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the whisked yogurt with cumin powder, chaat masala, black salt, and the cooled methi mixture.
Add water as needed to achieve the desired raita consistency.
Serve the methi raita with garlic alongside Rajasthani Gatte Ki Sabzi and phulkas.

title: Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha Recipe-Multilayered Layered Indian Flat Bread
ingredients: Ghee (for layering and cooking the parathas)
instructions: To begin making the Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha Recipe we will first knead to make the dough.

In a large mixing bowl, add the whole wheat flour and salt. Mix well. Add a tablespoon of oil and rub it into the flour until you see coarse crumbs. Add a little water at a time and knead well to make a smooth and soft paratha dough. Cover the dough and allow it to rest for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, knead again until the paratha dough is soft and pliable. Divide the dough into 10 equal portions.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat. If using a cast iron skillet, grease the skillet well and allow it to preheat.
Keep some flour aside for dusting while rolling the dough. Shape each dough portion into a round ball, press it between the palm of your hands.

Dust the dough in flour and roll it into a 6‑inch diameter circle. Smear some ghee or oil on this rolled out dough. Dust some flour over the ghee; this flour and ghee will help the lachha paratha split into layers.
Fold the lachha paratha dough like an accordion, similar to a saree pleat. Start from one end and pleat to the other, then roll the pleated dough into a Swiss roll.
Flatten the pleated Swiss roll between the palms, dust with flour and roll into a 4‑to‑5‑inch diameter circle, revealing the layers.
Place the rolled layered Lachha Paratha on the preheated skillet. Cook on medium heat on both sides for a few seconds, then smear ghee and cook until golden brown and cooked through.
Proceed the same way with the remaining portions of the paratha dough.
Serve the Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha with Matar Paneer, Smoked Dal Makhani Dhaba Style, Carrot Cucumber Tomato Salad, Kesar Elaichi Aam Chunda Pickle, or Homemade Yogurt.

title: Spicy Poppy Seeds Pulao Recipe - Gasa Gasala Saddi
instructions: To begin making the Spicy Poppy Seeds Pulao Recipe, heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan; add the mustard seeds, urad dal and allow it to crackle and roast.
When the dal starts to brown, add the curry leaves, chopped garlic and slit green chillies. Stir fry for a few seconds.
When the chillies start to splutter, add the poppy seeds and stir for a few more seconds. Finally, add the rice, cumin powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder and the salt as per taste.

Stir well to combine all the ingredients. Cover the pan and allow the rice to simmer in the poppy seed mixture for about 5-7 minutes. This helps the rice to absorb all the flavors. Turn off the heat and give the rice a stir and check the salt. Adjust to suit your taste.

Heat a teaspoon of ghee in a Tadka pan; add the cashew nuts and roast until brown and crisp. Once the nuts are roasted add the raisins and allow it to puff up in the ghee. Turn off the heat and pour this over the Poppy Seed Pulao and stir.
Serve Spicy Poppy Seeds Pulao along with Hyderabadi Bagara Baingan and Phulka to complete your everyday meal.
Editor’s Notes: If you are not using leftover rice, ensure that the rice you use in the recipe is cooked fully for at least 5 minutes to bring out its flavour.

title: Jaggery Sweetened Apple Oatmeal Recipe
ingredients: Apple, cut into cubes as required
instructions: In a saucepan, add cubed apple, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 15 minutes or until the apples are soft.
Stir in quick cooking oats and milk. Cook for about 10 minutes or until the oats are soft and the oatmeal thickens.
Add grated jaggery and vanilla extract, stir to combine, then remove from heat and pour into serving bowls.
Serve topped with hazelnut, raisins, sesame seeds, and chopped apples. Add any other preferred nuts or dried fruits.
Enjoy the Jaggery Sweetened Apple Pie Oatmeal with a cup of hot Masala chai.

title: Soya Keema Matar Masala Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Soy Chunks (Nuggets), soaked in hot water for 30 min
1/2 tablespoon Red Chilli powder, adjust as per your spice preference
instructions: Soak soya granules or chunks in hot water for half an hour.
Drain the soaked soya granules, squeeze out excess water and pulse in a mixer grinder once or twice to achieve a coarse keema texture.
If using fresh green peas, blanch them in hot water until cooked, then drain and set aside.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a wok. Add finely chopped onions, ginger, garlic and green chilies and cook till the onions turn soft.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, sugar, and salt; mix well and cook for about 15 seconds.
Add the soya granules, mix well, simmer and cook for 10 minutes in its own juices. Adjust salt and spices to taste.
Turn off heat, garnish with coriander leaves, transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha, Palak Tovve or Palak Dal, and Boondi Raita.

title: Corn Matar Kachori Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (dhania) leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Make the dough for the outer crust by combining the dough ingredients in a large mixing bowl, adding water gradually, and kneading until smooth and soft.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Prepare the filling by pulsing all filling ingredients in a food processor to a coarse mixture; adjust salt and spices as needed.
Divide the rested dough into 12‑15 equal portions and roll each into a 2‑inch diameter circle.
Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of each dough circle, bring the edges together, and seal by twisting the dough.
If desired, reshape each sealed ball into a 3‑inch diameter circle, being careful not to spill the filling.
For air fryer or oven: preheat to 180 °C (350 °F) for 15 minutes, then bake the kachoris until golden brown and crisp on all sides.
For deep frying: heat oil, fry the kachoris on low to medium heat until deep golden brown and crisp, then drain on absorbent paper.
Serve the corn matar kachoris hot with green chutney and date chutney.

title: Mixed Sprouts Sabzi Recipe
instructions: Pressure cook the mixed sprouts with 3 cups water in a pressure cooker for 3‑4 whistles until lightly mushy.
Let the cooker cool, then transfer the sprouts and cooking liquid to a bowl and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds and a pinch of asafoetida.
When the cumin seeds crackle, add the chopped onion and sauté until light brown.
Add ginger‑garlic paste and sauté until the raw aroma disappears.
Add chopped tomato and green chilies and sauté until the tomato softens.
Stir in turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, and red chilli powder, mixing well.
Add the cooked mixed sprouts together with the reserved stock and salt to taste; mix thoroughly.
Cover and cook on low heat for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle chopped coriander leaves and stir.
Serve the Mixed Sprouts Sabzi with pulao.

title: Sweet Corn And Raw Mango Salad Recipe
instructions: Peel the mangoes, grate them, and place in a medium sized bowl.
Wash the corn and add it to the bowl containing the grated raw mangoes; mix well.
Drizzle the Kasundi mustard sauce and honey over the mixture, add the minced green chillies, sprinkle half a teaspoon of black salt, and toss to combine.
Garnish the salad with finely chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the Sweet Corn and Raw Mango Salad as a side dish with Fish Molee and steamed rice.

title: Spinach And Millet Pulav Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Foxtail Millet , or broken wheat (dalia)
instructions: To begin making the Spinach and Millet Pulao Recipe, get all the ingredients ready and keep it by the side. In this recipe, I will show you how to cook using a pressure cooker.

If you dont use a pressure cooker, then I suggest the same cooking procedure, using a heavy bottomed sauce pan with a lid. You will cover the pan after the procedures below and cook until the millets or broken wheat is edible.

Into a pressure cooker, heat a tablespoon of oil. Add the ginger, green chillies, bay leaves, cardamom pods and stir-fry for a few seconds. After which, add in the turmeric powder, cumin powder, tomatoes, salt and the millet.

Add 2 cups of water (sometimes if the millet or broken wheat is old- then it might need more water). Stir all the ingredients and cover the pressure cooker (or the saucepan). Place the weight on and pressure cook until you hear 2 whistles.

After a couple of whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer for another 3 minutes. After a couple of minutes, turn off the heat. Allow the pressure from the cooker to release naturally. If using a saucepan, make sure you cover the pan and cook until the millets are done to suit your taste.
Once the pressure is released, open the cooker, stir all the ingredients. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.

If, by chance the millets did not cook with the amount of water you added, then sprinkle some more water as required, cover the pressure cooker and allow it to steam on low heat. Don't place the weight on at this stage. You will have to just cover and cook.

Next we will stir fry the spinach in wok and then add it to the cooked millet. In a wok, add a teaspoon of oil, add the chopped spinach, salt and stir fry on medium heat until the spinach is cooked and almost all the water is evaporated. Stir in the spinach to the cooked millets.

Once the Spinach and Millet Pulav is done, stir in the ghee. You can skip adding ghee on top if you are not very keen on that. Ghee adds an additional flavor to the Pulao making it delicious. Serve the Spinach and Millet Pulav along with a Raita of your choice.

title: Restaurant Style Phool Gobhi Masala Recipe
ingredients: 2-1/2 tablespoons Mustard oil (adjust as per need)
instructions: To begin making the Restaurant Style Phool Gobhi Masala Recipe, first clean the florets and toss it along with salt and turmeric powder.
Heat a kadai with oil on a medium heat and fry the florets for about 5 minutes or till the raw smell vanishes. Take them out onto a plate.
In the same kadai, add the onions, fry till translucent. Switch off the stove and let the onions cool down.
Once it cools down, add the onion mixture in a mixer grinder and make it into a fine paste.
Add bay leaf and cumin seeds in the leftover hot oil. Once the cumin seeds crackle, add ginger and garlic paste with 2 teaspoons water. Let it cook for about a minute or two.
After a minute, add the fried florets, tomato puree and mix everything well.
Immediately add the fried onion paste, kashmiri red chilli powder and 1 cup water, cook for about 5 minutes.
Turn to low flame. After 5 minutes, add the cream, garam masala powder and ghee. Check for salt seasoning.
Garnish with cashews and serve. Serve Restaurant Style Phool Gobhi Masala Recipe along with Tawa Tandoori Roti Recipe, Mushroom Do Pyaza Recipe and Boondi Raita for a dinner meal.

title: Pyaaz Kachori Recipe
instructions: Add flour, salt and ghee into a mixing bowl and mix well until the mixture holds together into a ball; add more ghee if required.
Gradually add water and knead to form a soft, smooth dough.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 1 to 2 hours; meanwhile, prepare the filling.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan, add 1 tablespoon mustard oil, then add hing and fennel seeds and let them sizzle.
Add finely chopped onions, ginger, garlic and green chilies; sauté until onions turn translucent.
Add mashed potatoes and all spice powders (red chilli, turmeric, coriander, garam masala, amchur) and salt; mix well.
Stir in chopped coriander leaves, turn off heat and let the filling cool completely.
Take the rested dough, lightly knead on a clean surface, and divide the dough and filling into equal portions.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan with enough oil for deep frying.
Roll one portion of dough into a smooth ball, flatten to a 3‑inch circle, place filling in the center, bring edges together and seal tightly.
Flatten the sealed ball into a 3‑inch circle, pressing gently to keep filling intact; repeat for remaining portions.
Deep fry the kachoris in small batches (2‑3) over medium heat for about 3 minutes per side until golden, puffed and crispy.
Remove kachoris, place on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil, and serve hot.

title: Chana Pulao Recipe - Spicy Chickpea Pulao
ingredients: 1-3/4 cups Water for pressure cooking rice
instructions: Rinse and soak the chickpeas/chole overnight or for 8 to 9 hours in enough water.
Drain the soaked chickpeas and add them to a pressure cooker with water.
Add about ½ teaspoon of salt and pressure cook until the cooker releases 8‑9 whistles or until the chickpeas are tender.
Drain the cooked chickpeas and set aside. Rinse the rice well until the water runs clear of starch.
Soak the rice in enough water for 30 minutes, then strain and set aside.
Make a smooth paste of the ‘for paste’ ingredients—including ginger, garlic and green chilli—in a grinder with a little water, and set aside.
Heat oil in a wide pan, add sliced onions, and fry until golden brown.
Soak saffron in a little lukewarm milk and set aside.
In a pressure cooker, heat oil and add all the whole spices (caraway seeds, cardamoms, mace, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf).
Sauté the whole spices for a few seconds until fragrant, then add sliced onions.
Sauté the onions until golden brown, add the ginger‑garlic‑chilli paste and sauté until the raw aroma disappears, then add chopped tomatoes and red bell pepper and sauté for two minutes.

Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, and kasuri methi; sauté the tomatoes for a minute, then add the drained cooked chickpeas. Mix well and sauté for about 7‑10 minutes so the chickpeas absorb the masala.
Add the basmati rice, curd, half of the fresh herbs, and the saffron‑milk mixture; mix everything well.
Add 1.75 cups of water, season with salt, and pressure cook for 1 whistle without opening the cooker.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, then open the lid and gently fluff the rice.
Garnish with coriander leaves, mint leaves, dry fruits, and pomegranate arils.
