Cover and let the pulao rest for 15 minutes before removing the foil and fluffing the rice prior to serving.
Serve Chana Pulao with Burani Raita, Pomegranate Raita, or any raita of choice, and a roasted papad.

title: Sweet And Spicy Thai Style Paneer Recipe
ingredients: 200 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), cut to small squares
Salt and Pepper, as per taste
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine Thai red curry paste, sriracha sauce, lemon juice, chopped garlic, chopped green chillies, salt, pepper, and oil; stir well.
Add the paneer cubes to the bowl and gently mix to coat them evenly with the marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, being careful not to break the paneer.
Soak the skewers in water and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill, brushing it with 2 tablespoons of oil.
Grill the marinated paneer for 2–3 minutes on each side until grill marks appear, avoiding overcooking.
Baste the paneer while grilling with any remaining marinade or additional oil/butter.

Remove the paneer from the grill, transfer to a serving plate, and garnish with toasted sesame seeds, roasted peanuts, spring onion greens, and chopped coriander leaves; serve with lemon wedges and sliced onion.
Serve the Sweet and Spicy Thai Style Paneer with Chilli Coriander Fried Rice and Roasted Eggplant in Schezwan Sauce.

title: Boondi Raita Recipe Spiced With Black Salt
instructions: To begin making the boondi raita recipe, keep all the ingredients ready and keep aside.
In a bowl, whisk yogurt, red chilli powder, chat masala powder, black salt, cumin powder and salt until well combined.
Gently fold the boondi to the whisked yogurt.

Transfer boondi raita to a serving dish and garnish with chopped coriander leaves. If the raita thickens up a bit after sometime, then you can add little water and whisk it well to get the desired consistency.
Serve the Boondi Raita along with Plain Paratha and Aloo Simla Mirch Ki Sabzi for lunch or dinner.

title: Moong Sprouts Pulao Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Moong Sprouts Pulao recipe, soak rice in water for at least 10 minutes or you can start this as your first step of preparation which will give you enough time to soak.
Heat oil in a thick-bottomed pan, add cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, peppercorns, cumin and bay leaf; let them crackle and take care as they can burn easily.
Add green chillies and stir, followed by onions and grated ginger and a pinch of salt to enable them to cook faster.
Toss in the tomatoes and mint leaves and cook until the tomatoes are soft but not mushy. Now tip in the sprouts and a little salt and stir it around.
Drain the rice from water and add it into the pan.
Mix everything gently and add 2 cups of water, season with salt and bring this to a boil.
Cover the lid, simmer and cook for 10 to 15 minutes or until all the water has evaporated.
Let this rest for 10 minutes before you serve. Gently fork out the grains so they remain separate. Garnish with coriander and serve hot.
Serve Moong Sprouts Pulao along with Avocado Raita, Onion Tomato Cucumber Raita for a wholesome and fulfilling weekday meal. You can even pack it in your kids' lunch box.

title: Lagan Ki Machli Recipe - Delicious Pomfret Curry
instructions: Wash the fish well and make slits on both sides of the surface.
In a mixing bowl combine ginger paste, garlic paste, salt, lemon juice, red chilli powder and turmeric powder; rub the mixture into the slits and marinate the fish.
Heat a skillet on medium flame with a teaspoon of oil, place the marinated fish in the skillet and fry until the outside is nicely browned.
Cook the fish for about 3 minutes on each side, focusing on crisping the outer surface.
The interior of the fish will finish cooking later when simmered in the gravy.
Heat a kadai with oil on medium flame and add cumin seeds, star anise, cinnamon stick, and dry red chillies.
When the spices sizzle, add sliced onions and sauté until deep brown (about 8‑10 minutes); then turn off the heat and let cool.
Grind the cooled onion mixture into a fine paste using very little water and set aside.
In the same kadai add tomato puree, bring to a boil, then stir in the ground onion paste and whisked yogurt.
Add red chilli powder, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder and salt; then add the pre‑cooked pomfret fish and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, turn off the heat, mix in coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Sprouted Moong And Methi Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Rice, washed and soaked in water for 30 minutes
1 Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), small bunch, chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a kadhai or wok.
Add the mustard seeds and, once they splutter, add the cumin seeds. Then add asafoetida, turmeric powder, garlic, onion, green chillies, ginger, bay leaf, star anise and peppercorns.
Stir and sauté for a few seconds. Next, add moong sprouts and methi and sauté for a minute.
Drain and add the rice, stirring everything well. Add water (about 2½ to 3 cups, adjusting for rice quality).
Add salt, cover and cook until the rice softens and the water has evaporated. Turn off the heat and keep covered for 5–10 minutes.
Serve the Sprouted Moong and Methi Pulao with Tadka Raita, Mooli Raita, or any raita of your choice.

title: Spinach Mushroom Chickpea Curry Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Spinach Leaves (Palak), washed and finely chopped
1/2 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked for 8 hours
2 Fresh Red chillies, finely chopped or green chillies
instructions: To begin making the Spinach Mushroom Chickpea Curry Recipe, wash and soak the chickpeas in water for 8 hours or overnight.
Transfer the chickpeas along with the water, add some salt and pressure cook for 6-8 whistles, reduce the flame and further cook for another 15 minutes. Turn off the flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally and set the chickpeas aside.
In a skillet, heat oil on medium flame, add the ginger garlic and saute for about a minute.
Next add the onions, and cook them until they turn into a deep brown colour. This will take about 4-5 minutes.
To this add the green chilies, turmeric powder, garam masala powder, cumin powder, salt and mix well.
Once the spices are well combined, add in the mushrooms and tomato puree, cover and cook until it bubbles.
Open the lid, add in the washed and cut spinach leaves and further cook till the spinach is completely cooked and combined.
Finally, add in the coconut milk, the cooked chickpeas and simmer the Spinach Mushroom Chickpea Curry on low flame for about 5 minutes.

Once done, check the salt and seasonings and adjust to suit your taste. Turn off the heat and transfer the Spinach Mushroom Chickpea Curry into a serving bowl and add in finely chopped mint and coriander leaves as well. Serve hot.

title: Baingan Tamatar Sabzi - Brinjal/ Eggplant Masala Recipe
ingredients: 1 Brinjal (Baingan / Eggplant), cut into 1 inch thick wedges
1/2 teaspoon Red chilli powder, to taste
instructions: Add the cut baingan wedges to a pan with oil, sprinkle with salt, and stir to combine.
Cover the pan and cook the baingan on low to medium heat until partially cooked, allowing steam to cook it without water.
Uncover the pan and roast the baingan until fully cooked, keeping the pieces firm.
Turn off the heat once the baingan is cooked and transfer it to a bowl.
In the same pan, heat a teaspoon of ghee or oil; add onion and garlic and sauté until the onion softens.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté until they become mushy and soft.
Stir in turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, salt, and red chilli powder to taste.
Mix the masala with the tomato mixture and give it a brisk stir over high heat.
Add the roasted eggplant back to the pan, cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer in the tomato masala for about 5 minutes; adjust salt as needed.
Turn off the heat, stir in the freshly chopped coriander leaves, and transfer the bhindi tamatar sabzi to a serving bowl.
Serve the Baingan Tamatar Sabzi with phulkas and carrot salad.

title: Carrot And Coriander Soup Recipe
ingredients: 1 Green Chilli, slit in the middle
instructions: To begin making the Carrot And Coriander Soup recipe, Iin a large pressure pan or cooker, heat ghee or butter and add chopped onions and garlic along with slit green chillies. Fry until the onions are translucent; about 1 minute.
Stir in chopped carrots, coriander and cloves and sauté again for another minute on high. Add water to immerse the vegetables and pressure cook for one whistle.

If you do not have a pressure cooker, cook in a deep saucepan until the carrots are cooked and turn soft. Once the pressure in the cooker goes down, drain the vegetables and pour the stock into an another saucepan.
Remove green chilli and cloves from the drained vegetables and blend the rest to a fine puree.
Pour the puree into the stock and mix well. Add salt and pepper to taste and bring to a boil.
Once it comes to a boil, lower the heat and simmer for about 5 minutes. Garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with a squeeze of lemon or lime.
Serve Carrot And Coriander Soup with Garlic Bread and Moong Sprouts Salad With Grated Carrots and Coriander for a healthy and light dinner.

title: Mint And Pomegranate Raita Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Mint and Pomegranate Raita, first blend together the mint, coriander, garlic and green chillies in a mixer using little water, into a chutney like paste. Transfer the paste to a bowl and set this aside.
In another bowl, whisk the curd using hand blender or wire whisk, add 1/4 cup or so of water to get the desired consistency. Whisk the curd well to ensure that no thick lumps remain.
Next, add the salt, cumin powder, chaat masala and sugar in the yogurt, and whisk it all together until well combined.

Then, add the mint paste in the yogurt. Stir gently, to combine. Taste and adjust the seasoning according to your requirement. If not serving immediately, keep the yogurt in the refrigerator, to cool.
When ready to serve the raita, add the pomegranate pearls and stir to combine. Serve Mint And Pomegranate Raita chilled or at room temperature with your favorite main course meal.
Serve Mint and Pomegranate Raita along with Layered Paneer Butter Masala Biryani Recipe or Methi And Palak Paratha Recipe.

title: Raw Mango Carrot Cucumber Salad Recipe With Peanuts
ingredients: 1/3 cup tomatoes, deseeded and finely chopped
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
In a mixing bowl, combine the raw mango, carrots, cucumber, tomatoes, roasted peanuts, coriander leaves, and mint leaves, and give it a good mix.
Add the salt, black pepper, chaat masala, and cumin powder to the bowl and toss the salad; taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Transfer the salad to a serving bowl and serve chilled.
Serve the salad alongside Nawabi Paneer Curry, Cheese Garlic Naan, and Papad Raita for a complete meal.

title: Plain Dalia Recipe- How To Cook Broken Wheat In Pressure Cooker
instructions: Wash the broken wheat a couple of times and soak the dalia/broken wheat for half an hour.
Add the broken wheat/dalia into a pressure cooker and close the lid.
Pressure cook on heat for one whistle; then reduce heat to medium and cook for another two whistles, then turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally and open the lid of the pressure cooker.
Fluff the dalia/broken wheat with a fork or spoon and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve the dalia/broken wheat with Palak Tovve or Palak Dal, Masalewali Turai Sabzi, and Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita.

title: Beetroot And Tofu Patty Recipe
ingredients: 1 Beetroot, peeled, diced and cooked until soft
instructions: To begin making the Beetroot And Tofu Patty Recipe, we will pulse all the ingredients except oil in the food processor or blender, without adding any water.
Once you pulse and get all the ingredients mashed, remove from the processor and transfer to a bowl. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.

Shape the beetroot tofu pattie mixture into lemon size balls and flatten them a little between your palms. It's a good idea to oil your palms and fingers before you begin shaping the patties, so they don't stick to your palms.

Once you have shaped the Beetroot And Tofu patties, pan fry them on a preheated iron skillet. Place the shaped beetroot patties on the preheated skillet, drizzle some oil over the patties and cook them until evenly brown on both sides.
Once the Beetroot And Tofu Patty is cooked, transfer them onto a serving plate and serve.
Proceed the same way with the remaining patties.
Serve the Beetroot And Tofu Patty Recipe along with a yogurt dip for your parties or along with Green Chutney Recipe and Masala Chai Recipe as a tea time snack.

title: Raw Mango Murabba Recipe - Cinnamon Spiced Mango Jam
instructions: To begin making Raw Mango Murabba Recipe, peel the mangoes and cut them in cubes and set aside.
In a saucepan, add the sugar & 1/2 cup water and make a thin syrup.
Once the syrup starts boiling, add the mango cubes, add the saffron strands & cinnamon powder, simmer on low flame, until the mango pieces are cooked.
This will take 5 minutes more.
Remove the Raw Mango Murabba from the flame & let the murabba cool.
Once cooled, store the Raw Mango Murabba Recipe in a glass jar or steel jar.
The Raw Mango Murabba Recipe can be stored for more than 6 months in the fridge & can be enjoyed with hot Spicy Yogurt Chapati Recipe or Whole Wheat Bread Recipe With Oatmeal And Flaxseeds.

title: Kachumber Salad Recipe With Cucumber, Onion & Tomatoes
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped
instructions: Wash and chop all the vegetables into small pieces and keep them ready.
In a mixing bowl, combine the chopped cucumbers, onion, green chilli, tomatoes, carrots, and pomegranate seeds and mix well.
Prepare the dressing by adding lime juice, pepper powder, roasted cumin powder, and salt to the vegetables; mix thoroughly.
Add the finely chopped coriander and mint leaves, give the salad a gentle stir, and serve immediately.

title: Hariyali Machali Recipe - Carp Fish In Green Spinach And Coriander Gravy
instructions: Clean the fish and dry it, then season with salt and pepper for about 5 minutes.
Grind together spinach, coriander, green chillies, lemon juice and a little water into a puree.
Heat a frying pan with oil and fry the fish for about five minutes until cooked, then remove the fish.
In the same pan, add cumin seeds and red chillies; after 30 seconds add garlic, ginger, and onion and cook for about 5 minutes. Add Kashmiri red chilli powder and garam masala powder.
Pour the spinach puree into the pan and fry for a few minutes. Check the seasoning of salt, then add the fried fish back and coat it for 2 minutes. Serve immediately.
Serve Hariyali Machali with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha or steamed rice, and optionally with Kachumber salad.

title: Sago Khichdi Recipe (Savory Tapioca Pearls Stir Fry)
ingredients: Salt, as required (kala namak, if making it for fasting)
instructions: Soak the sabudana (sago) in water for 4-5 hours until soft and puffed up.
Drain all the water and let the sabudana dry; otherwise it will stick and become lumpy.
Heat oil in a wok and add the peanuts; roast them until they turn brown.
Add the boiled potatoes, tomatoes, and green chilies to the wok and sauté for about 5-8 minutes until the potatoes become soft.
Add the drained sabudana, salt, and chopped coriander; mix everything well.
Switch off the flame, add lemon juice and pomegranate kernels (or anardana powder), and toss gently.
Serve the Sago Khichdi on its own or with any raita of your choice.

title: Spinach, Apple and Carrot Smoothie Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Spinach, Apple and Carrot Smoothie Recipe, add all the ingredients like the spinach, carrots, mint, ginger, oats, honey and flax seeds powder into a blender and blend well with very little water to get a smooth paste.
Once all the ingredients have blended well then add some more water to make a smooth smoothie. You can optionally add some yogurt as well if you like to make the smoothie.
Once the smoothie is ready, transfer it into the serving glass with ice cubes in it and serve chilled.
Serve the Spinach, Apple and Carrot Smoothie immediately, preferably with Spicy Avocado Scrambled Eggs and Toast.

title: Paneer Matar Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Basmati rice, washed and soaked
2 sprig Mint Leaves (Pudina), chopped for garnishing
200 grams Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), cut into cubes
instructions: To begin making the Paneer Matar Pulao Recipe, firstly wash the rice and soak for 15-20 minutes and drain.
Heat the ghee in a pressure cooker on medium heat; add the fennel seeds, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and bay leaf and saute until you get a lovely aroma.
Add the ginger, garlic and green chilies, and saute for a few seconds. At this stage, add onions and saute until the onion turns pink.
Once done, add in the rice, two cups of water, and salt. Close the pressure cooker.
Pressure cook for 2-3 whistles and turn off the flame. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Open the pressure cooker and fluff the rice with a fork.
Heat a skillet, with ghee on medium flame, to this add the paneer cubes and saute for about a minute.
To this, add the steamed green peas and salt.
Toss the paneer on high heat for about a minute or two and turn off the flame.
Now add the paneer-green peas into the pulao and mix well.
Add in the fresh chopped mint leaves and transfer the Paneer Matar Pulao to a serving platter.
Serve Paneer Matar Pulao Recipe along with Shabnam Curry and Boondi Raita for a delicious weekday lunch.

title: Sweet And Sour Lemon Pickle Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 kg Lemons (thin skinned variety), cut into wedges
instructions: Wash lemons well and wipe them completely dry with a clean cotton cloth; ensure no moisture remains. Cut the lemons into quarters and remove the seeds.
Into clean, dry, sterile bottles, add sugar and salt, shaking well to mix. Add the cut lemons into the bottles and shake again to ensure all the lemons are well coated.
Close the lid tightly and place the lemon bottles in sunlight for about 10 to 15 days. If sunlight is unavailable, keep the lemons inside for about 25 to 30 days to soften in their own juices.
After 25-30 days, transfer the softened, partially cooked lemons and their juices into a hot saucepan. Bring to a boil and let it boil for 3 minutes to fully cook the lemons.
Add the red chilli powder, mix well, and continue cooking for another minute. Turn off the flame and let the mixture cool completely.
Transfer the cooled pickle into clean, dry, sterile bottles. Store properly; the pickle can stay good for up to a year if stored well. Always use clean, dry spoons when serving.
Serve the Sweet And Sour Lemon Pickle with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha for breakfast or alongside Curd Rice with Mint Flavour for a comforting South Indian meal.

title: Cauliflower Curry With Bell Peppers And Carrots In Spiced Milk Gravy
ingredients: 1 cup milk, mixed with 1 teaspoon corn flour
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add cumin seeds and allow them to crackle; then add bell peppers and onions and sauté until tender.

Stir in cardamom pods, tomato puree, turmeric powder, cumin powder, garam masala powder, and red chilli powder; sauté until the tomatoes start to bubble. Add the milk mixture and steamed vegetables, turn heat to low, cover and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat, stir in chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with phulkas.

title: Dudhi Dal Gosht Recipe-Mutton With Bottle Gourd & Lentils
ingredients: 1 kg Bottle gourd (lauki), chopped into cubes
5 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped to garnish
instructions: Mix all the dals in a pressure cooker and cook until they are properly cooked and mushy; then blend with a hand blender.
Boil the mutton with a little salt and water in a pressure cooker for 15 minutes.
Heat oil and ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and add all the whole spices (bay leaf, whole peppercorns, cinnamon stick, and cumin seeds).
Cook the spices for about 30 seconds, then add the finely sliced onions and cook until they turn slightly brown without burning.
Add ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and salt; stir well.
Add the chopped bottle gourd and tomatoes, mix everything properly and cook until the bottle gourd is half cooked.
Stir in the whole mint leaves, then add the boiled mutton and the blended daal; cook for 5 minutes.
Add whole amchur and lemon juice; let it cook for another 5 minutes and garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the Dudhi Dal Gosht with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, Phulka and Steamed Rice.

title: Cauliflower & Cucumber Raita Recipe (Cauliflower Yogurt Salad)
ingredients: 2 cups Cauliflower (gobi), cut into small florets
instructions: To begin making the Cauliflower & Cucumber Raita Recipe, we will first roast the cauliflower.

Heat a teaspoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add the cauliflower florets, sprinkle some salt and stir‑fry on low to medium heat until the cauliflower is cooked through; then turn off the heat and allow the cauliflower to cool completely.

Whisk the yogurt along with salt, roasted cumin powder, green chillies and coriander; stir in the cucumber and cooked cauliflower, adjust seasoning if needed, and transfer the raita to a serving bowl.
Serve the Cauliflower & Cucumber Raita as a refreshing yogurt salad or accompaniment with parathas.

title: Coffee Recipe With Instant Coffee Powder
ingredients: 1-1/2 teaspoons Instant Coffee Powder (adjust the strength to desired taste)
instructions: Gather all ingredients. Optionally use cream for a creamy taste and texture.
Pour milk into two microwave‑safe serving cups and add sugar.
Microwave on full power for a minute.
Remove the cups, stir well, and microwave again for 30 seconds if the coffee is still cold.
When hot, add the instant coffee powder and stir until dissolved.
Top with cream and stir to combine.
Serve the coffee with snacks such as Methi Khakra, Indian Spicy Masala Cookie, Phool Makhana, or other coffee‑time snacks.

title: Corn Korma Recipe
ingredients: Few sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making Corn Korma, heat a pan on low flame, add the ghee, and when heated add the mustard seeds and asafoetida, letting the mustard seeds splutter.
Add the curry leaves and finely chopped green chili and sauté for a minute.
Add the grated corn kernels and stir for 5 minutes until the raw corn smell disappears.
In a small bowl, combine the rice flour, black pepper powder, and whisk smoothly with the thick coconut milk.
Pour this coconut mixture into the corn mixture and keep stirring for 5 minutes.
Add more water to reach the desired consistency.
Season with salt and garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves.
Switch off the flame; the Corn Korma is ready to be served with phulkas or parathas.

title: Hara Dhania Paratha Recipe - Coriander Paratha
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Hara Dhania Paratha Recipe, combine the wheat flour, cumin powder, turmeric powder, coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, salt and pepper into a large mixing bowl. Add a little water at a time and knead to make a firm and smooth dough. Drizzle a teaspoon of oil over the dough and knead for a couple of minutes until the dough is smooth and soft.
Keep the dough covered in a bowl for at least 10 minutes before you can start making the paratha.
Divide the dough into 10 to 12 portions. Take each paratha ball, dust in flour and roll it out into a round circle of about 8 inch diameter.
Now, heat the flat iron skillet on medium heat for a few minutes.

Place the rolled paratha dough on the heated skillet and cook the paratha on medium heat until you notice spots appear on the top. At this point flip and cook the dhania paratha the other side. Smear some oil or ghee and flip again. Cook on both sides, until you notice that the parathas have golden brown spots on both sides and is cooked.
Continue the same process of cooking the remaining hara dhania parathas and stack them one over the other.
Serve these delicious Hara Dhania Paratha or Coriander Parathas along with Aam Ka Achaar Recipe and Boondi Raita Recipe Spiced With Black Salt.

title: Simple Lemon Tea Recipe
ingredients: 2 Lemon wedges, or slices, to garnish
instructions: To begin making Simple Lemon Tea Recipe, keep all the ingredients handy.
In a carafe or saucepan, heat water on high heat with added lemon zest.
Once the water comes to a rolling boil, squeeze in lemon juice, demerara sugar and switch off heat; keep the container covered for a minute.
Stir to dissolve any demerara sugar that is still left at the bottom. Strain the tea, pour into tea cups and adorn it with a lemon slice/wedge to serve.
Serve Simple Lemon Tea Recipe with light snacks like Jwarichya Lahyancha Chivda or Crispy Oven Roasted Curried Chickpeas.

title: Samosas with Spinach & Cottage Cheese Filling
ingredients: 500 grams Spinach, washed and finely chopped
Oil, as needed to deep fry or to brush while baking
instructions: Prepare the dough by mixing together the flour, salt, ghee and ajwain/carom seeds to form a mixture of coarse crumbs. Add water gradually to make a soft and firm dough, knead for 2-3 minutes, cover with a moist cloth and let rest 15-20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan; add the chopped spinach and sauté on high heat until softened and all water evaporates. Turn off heat and let the spinach cool completely.
Once the spinach has cooled, combine it with crumbled paneer, chopped green chillies, garam masala powder, chaat masala powder, and salt. Adjust seasoning and set aside.
Fill a small cup with water for sealing the edges. On a floured surface, roll each dough portion into a 3‑inch diameter circle and cut each circle in half.
Lightly spread water along the edge of each semi‑circle.

Place 1–2 teaspoons of the spinach‑paneer filling in the center, fold the semi‑circle into a half‑moon shape, and press to seal the edges. Use a fork to create patterned edges. Repeat for remaining samosas.

Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan over medium heat. Gently slide a few samosas into the oil, turning them when they float to the top, and fry until light golden‑brown on all sides. Keep heat medium throughout. Drain on absorbent paper.

For baking (optional): preheat oven to 200 °C. Arrange samosas on a baking tray and brush with ghee or oil on all sides. Bake for 10–15 minutes, turning once or twice, until evenly browned. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

title: Cauliflower In Coconut Milk Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1 Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), deseeded and cubed
1 teaspoon Coriander Powder (Dhania), freshly made with roasted coriander seeds
instructions: To begin making the Cauliflower In Coconut Milk Curry Recipe, in a large bowl whisk together the yogurt, gram flour, coconut milk, ginger, coriander powder, salt and red chilli powder. Add in two cups of water, whisk it well and keep aside.

Heat oil in a casserole pan; add the cumin, curry leaves, cloves, and cinnamon along with the bell peppers and cauliflower. Sprinkle some salt and water, cover the pan and roast the cauliflower on medium heat until lightly tender and cooked.
Once tender and cooked, add in the coconut milk curry mixture and stir well. Keep stirring continuously with heat on medium high until the mixture thickens and begins to boil.
If the mixture is too thick for your taste, adjust the consistency by adding a little water and boil just for a couple of minutes. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Serve the Cauliflower In Coconut Milk Curry for winters or parties along with steamed Foxtail Millet or Pearl Millets or Rice.

title: No Onion No Garlic Raw Tomato Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: Salt or sendha namak, to taste
Garam masala powder, a generous pinch (optional)
instructions: Chop the raw tomatoes lengthwise into slices.
Heat oil in a kadhai or wok; when hot, add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add finely chopped green chillies and curry leaves, stir, then add turmeric powder and mix.
Add the tomato slices, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt (or sendha namak); mix well.
Cook until the tomatoes are al dente, retaining some crunch; do not overcook.
Stir in powdered jaggery and garam masala powder, mixing thoroughly.
Remove from heat, garnish with fresh coriander leaves, and serve hot.
Serve the sabzi with Dal Banjara and phulkas as a weekday meal.

title: Banana Date Smoothie Recipe
instructions: Slice the bananas.
In the blender jar add sliced banana, half of milk, pitted dates and honey.
Blend first with half amount of milk, then add the remaining amount of milk and blend once again to get a smooth consistency.
Pour the smoothie into serving glasses and serve immediately.
Serve the Banana Date Smoothie with Beet and Sprout Vegetable Sandwich or Avocado Paratha and pickle for breakfast.

title: Green Moong Dal Khichdi Recipe
ingredients: 1 Green Chilli, slit (or more if you prefer)
instructions: To begin making the Green Moong Dal Khichdi Recipe, first wash and soak the rice and moong dal for about 1 to 2 hours. Drain the water.
After the soaking period is over, we will now begin to cook the Khichdi. You can cook the kichadi in the pressure cooker or in a saucepan.
Into the pressure cooker, add the soaked rice and moong dal, and the remaining ingredients into the pressure cooker.
Add 2-1/2 cups of water, cover the cooker, place the weight on and pressure cook until you hear 2 whistles. After two whistles turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes and turn off the heat.
Allow the cooker to rest until pressure released naturally.
Once the pressure has released, open the cooker and you will notice the rice and dal has a mushy texture. Stir well, adjust the salt to suit your taste.

To serve, spoon the Green Moong Dal Khichdi onto your plate, add a teaspoon of ghee on the top and serve hot along with Batata Nu Shaak (Potatoes in Gravy) or even a Kadhi Pakora, making your weeknight dinners simple and healthy.

title: Crispy Ribbon Pakoda Recipe - South Indian Diwali Snack | Easy Ribbon Murukku Recipe
instructions: Combine all the ingredients listed above except water, until you get coarse crumbs. Gradually add water to make a stiff yet smooth dough.
Grease the Sev Press or the Sev Sancha with oil and place the plate with many thin strips into the press.
Heat oil in a frying pan, until hot, on medium heat. Deep frying on high heat will brown the pakoda quickly and not crisp it. Fill in the ribbon pakoda dough into the press.
Press out thin strips of the ribbon pakoda dough into the hot oil. Only press in enough to cover the oil pan.

These ribbons cook and turn dark quickly. Gently turn the pressed ribbons to fry the other side on medium heat. Once the ribbon pakoda starts to turn golden, using a slotted spoon drain excess oil out and transfer the ribbon pakodas on a plate with an oil absorbent paper to cool completely.
Press the remaining batches of the ribbon pakoda dough in a similar manner.
Cool the Ribbon Pakodas and store them in airtight containers.
Serve Ribbon Pakoda as an evening snack with a hot cup of Masala Chai.

title: Fusion Style Paneer Malai Makhani Recipe
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Red Chilli powder (adjust to taste)
1 Kokum (Malabar Tamarind), soaked in 2 tablespoon water
Whole Black Peppercorns, a few, crushed
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a few sprigs for garnishing
instructions: To begin making Fusion Style Paneer Malai Makhani Recipe, prep all the ingredients needed for this recipe.

In a kadai heat coconut oil, when it is hot enough, add in the cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds and peppercorns and let them sizzle. Wait for about 10 seconds or till sizzling, and add in the curry leaves. Wait till they splutter (takes about a couple of seconds).
Add the onion and sauté for about 3-5 minutes till the onion is tender.
Now add in the ginger garlic paste, some salt and turmeric powder. Sauté till the raw smell goes and appears even.
Now add in the coriander powder, black pepper powder and red chilli powder, continue frying for another 2 minutes or till the spices are evenly mixed.
Add the tomatoes and fry for another 2 minutes or so, till the tomatoes are softened. Cover the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes till tomatoes are fully cooked.
Add the paneer (cottage cheese) cubes and mix it well but careful not to break the cubes.
Add the kokum or kokum extract, coconut milk and water. Adjust salt. Cover the pan and simmer for about 3-5 minutes on a low‑medium heat.
Switch off heat and garnish Paneer Malai Makhani with fresh coriander.
Serve Paneer Malai Makhani Recipe with Pudina Tawa Parath or phulkas, accompanied by Indian Style Black Chickpea Salad for a complete meal.

title: Methi Namak Pare Recipe
instructions: Wash the methi leaves, pat dry, chop finely, and set aside.
In a mixing bowl combine whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, crushed green chillies, chopped methi leaves, turmeric powder, cumin seeds, salt, and enough water to form a stiff dough; knead well.
Add the melted butter to the dough, knead again until smooth, then divide the dough into equal balls.
Flatten each ball and roll out to about 1/4 inch thickness; cut into diamond shapes or desired patterns with a knife.
Test oil temperature by dropping a small piece of dough – if it rises to the surface immediately, the oil is ready; otherwise heat a bit longer.
Deep‑fry the cut pieces on low flame until golden brown.
Drain the fried pare on paper towels to remove excess oil; let cool.
Store in an airtight container and serve with hot masala chai or coffee.

title: Indian Spicy Masala Cookie Recipe (Khara Biscuit)
instructions: To begin making the Indian Spicy Masala Cookie Recipe (Khara Biscuit), in a large bowl combine all the ingredients together and knead to make smooth firm dough. Knead well for about 3-4 minutes.
Refrigerate the khara cookie dough covered for about 20 to 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180 C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Remove the khara biscuit from the refrigerator and on a lightly floured surface roll the dough out until it has a 2 mm thickness.

Using cookie cutters, cut the rolled dough into desired shape and place it on the prepared baking sheet. Place the tray in the oven and bake for about 20 mins or until the edges begin to start during golden brown.
Remove the Indian Spicy Masala Cookie (Khara Biscuit) from the oven and allow it to cool completely. The cookies continue to cook as they are cooling. Store them in airtight containers.

title: Sautéed Aubergine With Tamarind Recipe
ingredients: 6 Small Green brinjal (green aubergine), cut to bite size
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Slice each aubergine into 4 and dice into medium sized chunks; soak tamarind in water for a few hours, then pulp and strain the extract.
Heat oil in a pan and shallow fry the diced aubergines until they wilt slightly and are soft but al dente; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add more oil, sauté finely sliced onions until translucent, then add the shallow fried aubergine pieces and combine well.
Add diced tomatoes and salt, mix, then add a little water, cover and cook until the tomato softens, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the chilli and turmeric powders, add a little more water, cover and cook on low heat until the aubergine is fully cooked.
Remove the lid, add tamarind juice or paste gradually, adjusting sourness to taste, and combine well.
Cook uncovered until the gravy reduces to a semi‑thick consistency; add powdered jaggery, mix, garnish with chopped coriander leaves, and serve with rotis/chapatis or plain rice.

title: Palak Baingan Ki Sabzi Recipe | Healthy Spinach & Eggplant Stir Fry | Quick Indian Vegan Side Dish
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon red chilli powder, adjust to taste
instructions: Heat a teaspoon of oil in a pan; add the chopped spinach and a pinch of salt, cook until softened, then set aside.
Cook the spinach for a couple of minutes on medium heat.
Turn off the heat and keep the spinach aside.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in the same pan (or another pan); add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add onion, ginger, garlic, and the brinjal wedges; sprinkle some salt and stir to combine.
Cover the pan and cook the brinjal, stirring occasionally, until roasted and soft when pierced.
Stir in tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and garam masala powder; add a teaspoon of ghee and simmer until the tomatoes and spices blend into a masaledar subzi.
When the brinjal is cooked, stir in the cooked spinach and adjust salt if needed; simmer for another 3–4 minutes on high heat, then turn off the heat.
Transfer the Palak Baingan Ki Sabzi to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve the dish with Boondi Raita and Phulka.

title: Sabudana Kheer Recipe - Tapioca Pearl Milk Pudding
instructions: To begin making the Sabudana Kheer Recipe, soak the sabudana in water for an hour. Once soaked well, we will cook the sabudana in water.

Heat a large sauce pan filled with the milk. Add in the sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves. Once the milk begins to boil, reduce the heat and allow the milk to reduce itself to about half its quantity.
This process is called condensation of the the milk. Condensation gives out special flavors that enhances the taste of the Sabudana Kheer (Payasam).

While the milk is condensing, in a large sauce pan, boil 2-1/2 cups of water. Once the water begins to boil, add the soaked sabudana pearls and boil until it is cooked. Once cooked, drain the excess water and transfer to another bowl and keep aside.

Once the milk has condensed, stir the cardamom powder and the cooked sabudana. Simmer for another 10 minutes on low heat. Turn off the heat and transfer the Sabudana Kheer (Payasam). to a serving bowl.

Heat the ghee in a small pan; add the almonds and roast them a little. Finally stir in the raisins for a few seconds until you see it puff up. Turn off the heat and stir this into to the Sabudana Kheer (Payasam).
Serve Sabudana Kheer as an excellent evening tiffin item, with Medu Vadas, Sambar and Chutney for a tea time snack party, or as a dessert along with a hearty South Indian Meal plate.

title: Tangy Lemon Pickle Recipe With Kalonji & Rock Salt
instructions: Take a deep pan and boil 3 cups of water in it.
Turn the heat to low and add washed whole lemons.
Let them simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, turn off the heat and drain out the water from the lemons; let them cool completely.
Cut the lemons into quarters (or as desired) and deseed them, then add black pepper, salt, chilli powder, and turmeric and mix well in a bowl.
Heat mustard oil in a tadka pan; when the oil is hot enough to see smoke, add mustard seeds.
Once they splutter, add kalonji and asafoetida, remove the pan from heat, and add it to the spiced lemon chunks; mix very well and leave for about an hour so the spices seep into the lemons.
Serve the tangy lemon pickle with parathas and yogurt or rice, poriyal, and Thakkali rasam.

title: Warm Red Lentil Salad With Goat Cheese Recipe
ingredients: 2 teaspoon Black pepper powder, freshly crushed
instructions: Take a bowl and add the lentils. Wash them twice or thrice and then strain the water.
Place the washed lentils in a pressure cooker, add the required water and a bay leaf, close the cooker and pressure cook until the lentils are tender yet firm enough to retain shape.
While the lentils are cooking, chop the vegetables and set them aside.
Prepare the dressing by mixing olive oil, vinegar, mustard paste, garlic, salt, and pepper powder in a bowl; mix thoroughly with a spoon.
Once the lentils are cooked, strain the water and let them cool down a bit.
When the lentils have cooled, combine the lentils, vegetables, and dressing (excluding the goat cheese) in a bowl and toss well.
Just before serving, add the crumbled goat cheese and mix gently.
Serve the warm red lentil salad with goat cheese on its own or alongside a light meal such as smoked vegetarian Spanish rice.

title: Coconut Burfi Recipe - Kopra Pak/ Fresh Coconut Fudge
instructions: In a medium size saucepan, stir in the sugar and water over medium heat. Once the sugar has melted, continue to boil the mixture until it reaches a two‑string consistency.
Test the consistency by dropping a bit of syrup into cold water; it should form a softball shape and not dissolve.
Add the grated coconut and cardamom powder to the syrup and continue stirring over medium heat to prevent sticking.
Cook for 10–15 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan as the coconut releases its oil.
Turn off the heat and stop stirring to avoid over‑cooking, which can harden the burfi.
Transfer the mixture to a greased 8 × 8‑inch tray (about 2‑inch high).
Level the mixture, cut into squares with a knife, and let it cool and set for a couple of hours.
Once completely cooled, separate the pre‑cut burfi pieces and serve.
Store the burfi in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.
Serve the coconut burfi after meals such as Jodhpuri Aloo, Ajwain Puri, and Boondi Raita.

title: Peppery Mushroom Biryani Recipe
instructions: Begin by making the Biryani Spice Mix.
In a small pan, dry roast the spice mix ingredients on medium heat, then grind into a fine powder and set aside.
Heat oil in a large saucepan with a lid; sauté ginger and garlic for a minute, add onions and sauté another minute, then add slit chillies and tomatoes, cooking until tender and oil separates.
Add sliced mushrooms, increase heat to high, and cook 3-4 minutes until they shrink and change color.
Stir in the Biryani Spice Mix powder, then add the rice and 3 cups of water, mixing well.
Stir in lemon juice and salt to taste, cover, and cook on medium heat until the water is absorbed and the biryani is cooked.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves or roasted raisins & cashews or caramelized onions.
Serve the Peppery Mushroom Biryani with beetroot raita.

title: Ragi Malpua With Rabri Recipe (Indian Pancakes With Creamy Pudding)
instructions: Combine all the ingredients for the Malpua batter – Ragi flour, whole wheat flour, fennel seeds, cardamom powder, baking powder, salt, and fresh cream – in a large mixing bowl.
Add water or milk to make a thick Malpua (pancake) batter and keep covered for about 10 minutes.
Prepare the sugar syrup: in a saucepan, add sugar, water, and saffron on medium heat, stirring continuously until the sugar dissolves.
Turn the heat to low and simmer the syrup until it reaches a one‑string consistency; then set aside.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat, grease it with ghee, and pour a ladleful of batter onto the skillet; drizzle a teaspoon of ghee around the edges and cook.
When the raw batter on top is set, flip the Malpua to cook the other side; remove when done and repeat for remaining batter.
Dip the cooked Ragi Malpuas in the warm sugar syrup for a couple of seconds, then remove.
Arrange the sugar‑coated Malpuas on a dessert platter, spoon some Rabri over the top, and sprinkle chopped nuts.
Serve the Ragi Malpuas with Rabri as a dessert for parties, festivals, or special occasions.

title: How to Cook Fluffy Quinoa Recipe in a Pressure Cooker | Easy Quinoa Recipe
instructions: Rinse 1 cup of quinoa thoroughly under cold running water using a fine mesh strainer.
Place the rinsed quinoa in the pressure cooker and add 1‑1/2 cups of water.
Secure the lid, set the valve to the sealing position (or place the weight), and turn the heat to high.
Cook for 2 whistles, then lower the heat and simmer for 3–4 minutes before turning off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally.
After 10 minutes, carefully release any remaining pressure by turning the valve to venting.
Open the lid and fluff the quinoa with a fork; if excess moisture remains, let it sit with the lid off for a couple minutes.

title: Pumpkin Curry With Chicken Recipe
ingredients: 400 grams Chicken breasts, cut into small pieces
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Pumpkin Curry With Chicken, heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan.

Add the garlic, onion, ginger, green chillies and chopped pumpkin. Sprinkle some salt and stir them for about a minute, cover the pan and simmer until the pumpkin has softened. This will take about 6-8 minutes on medium heat.

Using a hand blender, blend the pumpkin into a puree while it is in the pan. Add the tomato puree, and the spices like the cumin powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and garam masala.
Give it a good mix and saute for about 2 minutes.
After 2 minutes add the chicken pieces along with a cup of water, cover the pan, turn the heat to low and cook until the chicken is cooked completely.
Adjust the consistency of the curry by adding more water and also adjust the spices to suit your taste.
Once done, turn off the heat. Stir in the chopped coriander leaves, transfer the Pumpkin Curry With Chicken into a serving bowl and serve.
Serve Pumpkin Curry With Chicken along with Pudina Tawa Paratha and Kachumber Salad.

title: Pisarna Manga Recipe -Instant Raw Mango Pickle
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Mustard seeds (Rai/ Kadugu), halved (rai kuria)
instructions: To begin making the Pisarna Manga Recipe, cut the mango into small pieces along with the skin.

Combine all the ingredients like the red chilli powder, methi seeds, mustard seeds, turmeric powder, asafoetida, sesame oil, raw mango pieces and salt in a bowl. Stir well until all the ingredients are well combined.
Store the Pisarna Manga Pickle - Instant Raw Mango Pickle in the refrigerator and use as and when required.
You can also use whole mustard seeds, crackle them in oil and add it to the pickle mixture. This is the way traditional South Indians make the pickle and called it Pisarna Manga.
Serve Pisarna Manga Recipe - Instant Raw Mango Pickle with dals, parathas, rice and just about anything that needs an accompaniment.

title: Pineapple Cucumber Salad Recipe With Lemon Dressing
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon black pepper powder (adjust to taste)
instructions: Prep all ingredients, chopping the pineapple, cucumbers, and coriander leaves.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the chopped pineapple and cucumbers, add the coriander leaves and lemon dressing, then season with salt and pepper.
Add lemon zest, mix everything well, and serve immediately.
Serve the salad with Mexican Vegetarian Bean & Cheese Enchiladas or Mexican Salsa Chicken with Italian Cream Cheese.

title: Healthy Foxtail Millet Raw Mango & Vegetable Salad Recipe
instructions: Cook the foxtail millet: add 1/2 cup millet and 1 cup water to a saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes until water is absorbed and millet is cooked; optionally use a pressure cooker for faster cooking. Millet should be grainy.
Stir in a teaspoon of olive oil and salt into the cooked millet to prevent sticking, then let it cool completely; it will fluff up as it cools.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled millet with the raw mango, cucumbers, radish, onion, coriander leaves, Dijon mustard, honey, lemon juice, and black pepper. Toss well to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed.
Serve the Foxtail Millet Salad, optionally accompanied by Ragi Tawa Paratha and Dhingri Matar for a complete meal.

title: Beetroot, Amla And Pudina Juice Recipe | Mint Gooseberry Beet Juice
ingredients: 1/4 teaspoon Black Salt (Kala Namak) , or to taste
instructions: To begin making the Beetroot, Amla And Pudina Juice Recipe, wash and cut all the ingredients and keep them ready.
In a mixer jar, combine the beetroot, amla, mint leaves, cucumber, black salt, black pepper powder and roasted jeera powder.

To this add 1/2 cup of water and a few ice cubes, grind until the veggies are fully pureed. Once well blended you add additionally add another 1/2 cup of water and ice cubes and blend again to make the juice a little thinner.
Once blended give it a taste and add honey if required to sweeten the Beetroot, Amla And Pudina Juice.
Serve Beetroot, Amla And Pudina Juice recipe as a refreshing immunity boosting drink any time of the day. This juice can also be served on empty stomach in the early morning.

title: Ragi Badam Soup Recipe - Finger Millet Almond Soup With Vegetables
ingredients: 1/4 cup Green beans (French Beans), finely chopped
instructions: Soak almonds in hot water for 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove the skin from the almonds and blend to make a smooth paste of the badam.
Dissolve the ragi and almond paste in 2-1/2 cups of water. Keep this aside.

Add the carrot and beans into the pressure cooker, add 1 tablespoon of water and a pinch of salt. Pressure cook for one whistle and turn off the heat. Release the pressure immediately to retain the fresh colors of the green beans and carrots.
Chop all the vegetables and set them aside.
Heat a little oil in a saucepan, add the onions and ginger and sauté until the onions turn translucent.
Once the onions are done, add 2-1/2 cups of ragi badam soup water and bring it to a boil.
Keep stirring continuously and ensure the ragi thickens to a smooth soup-like consistency. Add more water if needed to adjust the consistency.
When the ragi badam soup mixture is cooked, stir in the vegetables, ghee, black pepper, cumin powder, and salt to taste. Give it a brisk boil, check the taste and adjust accordingly.
Serve the Ragi Almond Soup with vegetables as a healthy Indian diabetic dinner.

title: Palak Paneer Stuffed Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 inch Ginger, finely chopped or grated
Mint Leaves (Pudina), a handful, finely chopped
1 cup Whole Wheat Flour, and more for dusting
1 tablespoon Oil, and more for smearing
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Puree the spinach, mint, green chilli, ginger and mint in a blender.

In a large bowl, add wheat flour, gram flour, cumin powder, salt and oil; mix well and add the blended spinach. Add water gradually and knead to a soft, smooth dough. Add a teaspoon of oil on top and knead a little more until smooth. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
In another bowl, combine all the paneer stuffing ingredients and set aside.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal portions depending on desired paratha size.

Roll each portion into a thick circle, place a generous amount of stuffing in the center, bring the edges together to enclose the filling, pinch to seal, press gently, dust with wheat flour and roll gently into a paratha. Repeat for remaining portions.
Heat a skillet over medium heat; place the rolled paratha on it and cook both sides with a little oil or ghee until golden brown, maintaining medium heat.
Serve the paneer stuffed palak parathas with curd, carrot and turnip pickle, and ginger cardamom chai.

title: Tomato Garlic Chutney Recipe
ingredients: 1 teaspoon red chilli powder, to taste
instructions: To begin making the Tomato Garlic Chutney, get all the prep work done like chopping tomatoes and peeling garlic, and bring all the ingredients together.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add the mustard seeds and allow them to crackle, then add the garlic and roast for a few minutes until a roasted aroma develops.

Once the garlic is well roasted, add the tomatoes and sauté on low to medium heat until the tomatoes become very soft, mushy, and most of the water evaporates, resulting in a thick chutney-like mixture.
When the tomatoes reach the desired consistency, add the red chilli powder and salt, and check the taste to ensure it suits your palate.
Using a hand blender, pulse the garlic-tomato mixture to make a semi-smooth chutney.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve the Tomato Garlic Chutney as a spread over breads, along with parathas, Litti Choka, and more.

title: Moong Bean Sprouts Upkari Recipe - Moong Beans Stir Fry
ingredients: 3 Dry Red Chillies, broken into 2 to 3 pieces
instructions: To begin making the Moong Bean Sprouts Upkari Recipe, we will sprout the moong beans firstly.
Take 1 cup of moong beans and wash thoroughly in water. Drain and soak in plenty of water for at least 6 to 8 hours or even overnight.
Next day, drain the soaked beans thoroughly and place in a large bowl; make sure there is some moisture left in the beans.

Close the bowl with a lid and keep in a warm place to allow the mung beans to sprout for about 8 to 12 hours, depending upon the weather. Mung beans start sprouting faster in warm weather. After you have got the desired length of sprouts, you can use it in any dish you like.
To make the Moong Bean Sprouts Upkari Recipe, heat coconut oil in a heavy bottomed pan.
Once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds and once they begin to crackle, stir in the cumin seeds, dry red chillies and hing. Sauté for a few seconds.
Immediately add 2 cups of bean sprouts, turmeric powder and salt to taste; give it a good stir.
Sprinkle some water and close the pan with a tight lid. Let the sprouts cook in its own steam.
As soon as the sprouts are cooked to the texture you like (some people prefer it soft and some with still a bite in it, like the way I do), stir in the grated coconut.
Heat through for about a minute and remove from heat. Serve hot.
Serve Moong Bean Sprouts Upkari Recipe along with Methi Chaman and Phulkas for a weekday meal with family.

title: Gavar Pumpkin Sabji Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Gawar Phali (Kothavarangai / Cluster beans), washed strings removed and cut
1 cup Kaddu (Parangikai/ Pumpkin), peeled and chopped
4 Dry Red Chillies, chopped (or 1 teaspoon red chilli powder)
1 teaspoon Fennel seeds (Saunf), toasted and crushed
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, for garnishing, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Gavar Pumpkin sabji, first heat a small wok.
Add the fennel seeds. Toast them lightly and cool. Crush them coarsely using a mortar pestle or a rolling pin.
Heat oil in a pressure pan or wok. Add the mustard seeds and once they splutter add the cumin seeds.
Add the methi seeds, red chillies, hing and turmeric. Add the crushed garlic and onion and saute for a minute.
Add the gavar beans and pumpkin pieces. Add the other spices including crushed fennel, coriander powder, amchur powder (or tamarind pulp) and mix well.
Season with salt and add 1/2 cup (or more) water. Pressure cook for 1 whistle and 5 minutes on low heat or till the beans and pumpkin just become soft.
You can alternatively cook covered in a wok till the vegetables just become soft.
Adjust the water quantity (depending on whether you want a dry sabji or wet), sprinkle peanut powder (if using). Mix well and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Serve hot garnished with coriander leaves.

title: Semolina Vegetable Chilla Recipe
instructions: In a bowl, make a batter of semolina, curd, and water by mixing them together. Add wheat flour too. The consistency of the batter should not be runny, nor too thick. Let the batter rest for at least 20-25 minutes.
Add all the vegetables, salt and pepper to the rested batter. If the batter becomes thick after adding vegetables, add a little water or curd.
Heat a non-stick pan on low‑medium flame and brush it with a little olive oil. Once hot, pour a ladleful of batter and spread it evenly into a thin pancake.
Cover the pan with a lid and steam‑cook the chilla on low flame for 5-7 minutes. Flip occasionally so both sides become evenly golden. Repeat for the remaining batter.
Serve the Semolina Vegetable Chilla with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Tomato Chutney, or any chutney of your choice.

title: Coal Smoking Method For Tandoori Recipes - Smoke Food Using Charcoal
instructions: To begin, first take a piece of coal (about 3 inches big) and hold it over a gas flame with the help of tongs.
The coal will begin to turn red hot and grey in about 5 minutes. This indicates that the coal is ready to be used for smoking.
At this point heat a frying pan to medium heat and pour in the contents of the dish that you want to get the smoked flavor.
Make a well in the centre of the pan, by pushing a glass or steel cup into it. Place the hot coal inside the cup. Pour a spoon of ghee on the coal.

It will begin to smoke. Immediately cover the pan and reduce the heat to low and allow it to rest for about a minute. Open the lid and remove the coal cup. You dish will now have a smoked tandoori flavor.

title: Ragi Tawa Paratha - Healthy Vitamin Rich & Diabetic Friendly Paratha
instructions: To begin making the Healthy Ragi Tawa Paratha Recipe, in a large bowl combine the ragi flour, whole wheat flour salt and knead adding little water at a time to make firm and smooth dough.
Add one tablespoon of oil to coat the ragi tawa paratha dough and knead again. Cover and set the paratha dough aside for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 portions. Preheat the iron skillet over medium heat.

Roll the dough portions into balls and flatten them with the palm of your hand. Toss them on flour and roll them out into circles of approximately 3 inches in diameter. Put 1/4 teaspoon oil and spread it on the rolled dough.
We need to get a triangle shape, to do so, first fold into a semi-circle, then fold the semi-circle into half again. You get a mini triangle shape.
Tossing the triangle on a little flour, roll it out gently into a larger triangle. Continue the same process of rolling with the remaining ragi tawa paratha portions.
With skillet on medium high heat, place one rolled out ragi tawa paratha on the skillet. After a few seconds you will notice an air pockets popping out.
At this point flip the Ragi Tawa Paratha and smear about 1/2 a teaspoon of ghee. Using a flat spatula do a light pressing and turning motion to cook to the tawa paratha.

Flip to the other side and press and turn the Ragi Tawa Paratha in a similar way. You will notice brown spots around the paratha and it will be slightly crisp. Remove from heat and place on a platter or serve hot.
Continue the similar process with the remaining rolled portions and stack the cooked Ragi Tawa Paratha one above the other and serve hot.

title: Cheesy Potato Peas Potli Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly roasted and crushed
instructions: Mix the all purpose flour, ajwain, salt, baking soda and oil in a mixing bowl. Add water as required to form a firm dough. Knead a dough that is not too soft or hard. Cover with a moist kitchen cloth and keep aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds to hot oil and allow to crackle.
Once the cumin seeds crackle, add ginger paste and green chillies and sauté for a minute or till the rawness disappears.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté till the onions turn translucent, about 4-5 minutes on low/medium flame.
Add the boiled and mashed potatoes and coarsely crushed green peas.
When the peas are cooked, add turmeric powder, coriander powder, kasuri methi, red chilli powder, amchur powder, garam masala and salt. Mix well.
Add chopped coriander leaves and mix well. Saute for about a minute, then turn off the flame and let the mixture cool.
Once the filling has cooled, add the grated cheese and mix well to combine.
Knead the dough lightly again and roll it lengthwise with a rolling pin.
Make small round balls from the dough (like puri). Use a cookie cutter or lid to shape the roundels.
Roll each ball on a lightly floured surface to a diameter of about 6 inches.
Place 1-2 teaspoons of the prepared stuffing in the center of each rolled disc.
Close the disc and shape it into a potli (small basket).
Repeat the process for all dough balls, covering them with a kitchen towel to prevent drying.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Brush all the potlis with oil on all sides.
Bake the potlis at 180°C for 30-35 minutes or until the crust is golden brown and crisp.
Serve the cheesy potato peas potlis with tomato ketchup, dhaniya pudina chutney, and peanut chilli dipping sauce.

title: Vermicelli Biryani Recipe
instructions: To begin the preparation of Vermicelli Biryani, first heat half a teaspoon of oil in a pan and add the ingredients to grind one after the other and slowly sauté them on low flame until they slightly wilt and the raw smell goes. Cool and grind to a smooth paste. Keep aside.

In a pan, heat oil, add jeera; once it starts spluttering, add onions and sauté till they're translucent. Add the carrot, capsicum, beans, and peas, slowly sauté them till they're slightly tender. Then add turmeric, garam masala, dhaniya powder, biryani masala and mix until well incorporated.

Add the ground paste, salt and fry for 2-3 minutes. Add 1 cup of water and let it come to a boil. Now add the roasted vermicelli and mix everything together. Cook covered for about 5-7 minutes until the vermicelli is cooked al dente.
Sprinkle some coriander leaves and enjoy the Vermicelli Biryani while it is hot.

title: Hari Dhania Ki Sabzi ( Fresh Coriander leaves Dry Curry) Recipe
ingredients: 6 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, washed and finely chopped
instructions: Heat a medium sized pan with 2 teaspoons sesame oil and temper the mustard seeds, green chillies, cumin seeds, and asafoetida.
Add the gram/besan flour and turmeric powder, roasting over low heat for about 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chopped coriander leaves and mashed potatoes, season with salt, then cover and cook for another 4-5 minutes.
Sprinkle a little water while cooking so the besan and potatoes become crumbly and fully cooked; adjust salt and spices to taste.
Remove from heat; the Hari Dhania Ki Sabzi is ready to be served.

title: Moong Dal Khichdi Recipe For Babies And Toddlers Over 10 Months
instructions: Add yellow moong dal and rice along with 1 cup water in a pressure cooker.
Pressure cook the dal and rice for 3 whistles, reduce the flame to low and leave it for 2 minutes.
After 2 minutes, turn off the flame and let the pressure release naturally.
Meanwhile, in another pressure cooker, add the chopped carrots, beans, add 2 tablespoons water and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the heat and run the pressure cooker under cold water to release the pressure, preserving colour and nutrition of the vegetables.
Place a kadai on low heat and add ghee; once the ghee melts, add cumin seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add asafoetida and mix well into the ghee, then add cooked carrots, beans, cooked dal and rice khichdi along with a pinch of salt.
Stir to combine the Moong Dal Khichdi until it becomes almost smooth, then turn off the heat.
Serve the Moong Dal Khichdi to babies/toddlers over 10 months for a wholesome lunch.

title: Homemade Methi Ajwain Jeera Powder (Herbal Home Remedy for Digestion)
instructions: Dry roast the methi, ajwain and kala jeera separately until each releases a roasted aroma, about a minute or less for each.
Combine all the roasted ingredients and blend to make a fine powder; then add the remaining ingredients into the blender and mix well.
Store the Methi Ajwain Kala Jeera Powder in a glass bottle and freeze for 5 to 6 months.
The powder can be served in multiple ways.
Add a teaspoon of powder to a cup of yogurt, add another cup of water, salt to taste and whisk to make buttermilk, or serve with plain yogurt.
Add a teaspoon of powder to a cup of warm water and drink early in the morning or before/after a heavy meal.
Stir a teaspoon of the powder into a bowl of curd rice and serve chilled.

title: Kara Sevai Recipe (Lemon Vermicelli)
instructions: Make a coarse paste of coconut, green chilies, and mustard seeds in a grinder without adding water.
Heat oil in a wok/kadai and temper it with the ingredients listed under ‘to temper’.
When the dal and peanuts turn golden brown, add turmeric powder and asafoetida; sauté for a second and add the ground paste.
Roughly sauté the mixture, then add the cooked sevai, salt, and sugar; mix well and cook on low flame for 2 minutes.
Add coconut oil, fresh coconut, lemon juice, and coriander leaves; mix everything properly and serve hot.
Optionally, pack Kara Sevai with Burani Raita or Tomato Onion Cucumber raita for a lunch box.

title: Chocolate Rava Ladoo Recipe
instructions: Melt a teaspoon of ghee in a small pan over low heat; roast the cashew nuts until lightly golden and crisp. Add the raisins and sauté for a few seconds, then turn off the heat and set aside.
Heat 1/4 cup of ghee in a pan; add the rava/semolina and roast on very low heat, stirring continuously, until it becomes aromatic and slightly golden.
Add the almond powder, roasted cashews, raisins, cardamom powder, and sugar to the roasted rava and mix well.
Sauté for a few more seconds until well combined, then let the mixture cool slightly. Once cooled, stir in the cocoa powder and shape into 15 equal-sized balls.
If the mixture is too crumbly to shape, add a tablespoon of milk, ghee, or both to help it bind.
The rava ladoos are ready. Store them in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks and serve as a snack or dessert.
Serve the Chocolate Rava Ladoo during festivals or special occasions, optionally alongside tea‑time snacks like cheese crackers or baked banana chips.

title: Chicken Chops Recipe
ingredients: whole wheat bread crumbs, for coating
instructions: To begin making the Chicken Chops recipe.

In a mixing bowl, combine minced chicken, onion, green chilies, egg, ginger garlic paste, coriander and mint leaves, red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, salt and lemon juice; use your hands and bring the entire mixture together.
Keep the chicken chop mixture covered for about 15 minutes in the fridge.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a deep‑fry pan for deep frying the chicken chops. Make small lemon‑sized balls from the minced chicken mixture and shape them into oblong or cylindrical shapes.
Carefully roll the chicken chops in bread crumbs.
When the oil turns piping hot, reduce the flame to medium and carefully transfer the coated chops into the oil. Deep fry the chicken chops for about a minute or until all sides turn golden brown.
Drain the chicken chops on a kitchen towel and repeat the process for the remaining mixture.
Serve the crunchy‑outside, soft‑inside chicken chops immediately with raw mango and spring onion dip as a party appetizer or enjoy while watching a movie.

title: Til Chikki Recipe - Healthy Sesame Bars
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Ghee, + 1/2 teaspoon more for greasing
instructions: To begin making the Til Chikki recipe, we will first grease an 8 x 8 square pan with ghee that has a minimum of two inch rim and keep aside.
Place a pan on medium heat and roast the (til) sesame seeds till they are light golden in color. Turn off the heat and allow the sesame seeds to cool.

Heat ghee in a sauce pan on medium heat; stir in the crushed jaggery to the ghee and allow the jaggery to melt. Turn the heat to low and continue stirring until the jaggery caramelizes. When you drop a small amount into cold water it should form a hard ball.
Turn off the heat and immediately stir in the roasted (til) sesame until well combined with the melted jaggery.
While the mixture is hot quickly spread the mixture onto the greased pan and smoothen the surface with a flat spatula. Allow the mixture to cool completely allowing it to set.
When completely cool, cut the Til Chikki bars into desired shapes and serve as a healthy sweet for the festivals.
You can serve Til Chikki to kids along with Khakra Chaat and Turmeric Milk Recipe (Haldi Doodh).

title: Rajma Aloo Cutlet Recipe (Tikki/Patty)
ingredients: 1 cup Rajma (Large Kidney Beans) , washed and soaked overnight (6-8 hrs.)
instructions: To begin making the Rajma Aloo Cutlet Recipe (Tikki/Patty), we will first cook the rajma in the pressure cooker with enough water until very soft. Once cooked, allow the rajma to cook completely and drain out the excess water. You can use this water in a soup or cooking rice.

Mash the rajma along with boiled mashed potatoes, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, chopped green chili, salt, amchur powder, minced coriander leaves and besan. You can use a food processor to make the process of mixing all of them together easier.
Check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste.
Grease your palms with oil and take small portions of the rajma patty mixture, flatten them to shape it into a circular disc. Proceed the same way with the remaining portions of the cutlet mixture.

The next step is to cook the Rajma Aloo Cutlet. Preheat a skillet on medium heat. Place a few Rajma Aloo Cutlets at a time, drizzle a little at a time and cook the cutlets evenly on both sides until crisp.
Serve the Rajma Aloo Cutlet as a tea time snack along with tomato ketchup or a chutney of your choice.

title: Amla Achaar Recipe | Hot & Sweet Indian Gooseberry Pickle
instructions: To begin making Amla Achaar Recipe | Hot & Sweet Indian Gooseberry Pickle, select green, unblemished amla (gooseberry) for this pickle. Wash the Amla, pat dry and prick all over with fork. Keep them in a colander.
Heat up 4-5 cup water in a big saucepan. Keep the colander of Amla over it and cover it. Let the Amla cook on the steam for about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile dry roast the fenugreek kuria on a heated skillet until fragrant. Cool and grind to powder.

Let the amla cool down after steaming. Once it is cooled, remove seed and make small wedges of the cooked amla using a knife. Wear hand gloves while doing so as handling amla for a long time make cause blackening of nails in few cases.
In a big mixing bowl, first spread the Amla wedges. Now sprinkle the Turmeric powder all over it followed by the Fenugreek powder, Hing , Mustard Seed dal , Salt and Red Chili powder.
Mix it nicely with a spatula. Now add in the grated Jaggery and mix again.

Heat up the Oil in a kadai, on a low to medium heat until heated but not fuming. Put off the heat and let the oil cool down a bit. Now add this Oil to the pickle masala and mix very well. Keep the pickle covered overnight.

Next day oil will float up . Stir it again and fill in clean and dry glass jars. The oil layer should always cover the pickle in the jar. This pickle stays good at room temperature for about 2-3 months. But color may darken slightly, hence you can refrigerate.

Serve Amla Achaar Recipe | Hot & Sweet Indian Gooseberry Pickle as an accompaniment with Carrots & Sweet Potato Stuffed Paratha Recipe or along with Steamed Rice and Thatta Payaru Sambar Recipe (Black Eyed Beans Sambar).

title: Khatte Baingan Recipe
ingredients: 250 grams Small Brinjal (Baingan / Eggplant) (crown removed and cut into 4 pieces each)
instructions: Wash and pat dry the cut Brinjals with a towel.
Heat oil in a pan and deep fry the brinjals till they turn soft and slightly change colour.
Transfer the fried brinjals to a plate and keep ready.
Wash and extract the pulp of tamarind and keep this tamarind water ready as well.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and mustard seeds and saute for a minute.
Add black peppercorns and sesame seeds and saute for a few seconds.
Add ginger garlic paste and sauté till the raw smell goes.
Add tomato puree, red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder and salt and mix well.
Cook till oil starts separating. Then add coriander leaves and tamarind water.
Bring the gravy to a boil and cook for a couple of minutes.
Add the fried Brinjals, mix well and cook for a minute.
Reduce heat, close a lid and cook for about 5 minutes till the brinjals are cooked and have absorbed the masalas.
When the brinjals have cooked and the gravy has become thick, switch off the gas. Transfer the Khatte Baingan to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve Khatte Baingan along with Panchmel Dal, Kachumber Salad and Phulkas for a weekday meal.

title: Methi Turai Ki Sabzi (Fenugreek Leaves And Ridge Gourd Stir Fry)
ingredients: 500 grams Ridge Gourd (Turai/ Peerkangai), cut into 1 inch cubes
2 cups Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), roughly chopped
2 Dry Red Chillies, broken into halves
instructions: Warm the oil in a heavy bottom pan or kadhai. Add the cumin seeds and broken red chilies to it and allow them to crackle.
Add the finely sliced onions and sauté them until pink, soft, almost translucent.
Add coarsely crushed garlic, green chilies, turmeric powder and coriander powder and sauté it all together for a minute or two.
Add the cubed ridge gourd and toss on high heat for 3-4 minutes. The ridge gourd will release water, cover and cook for 3-4 minutes more on medium heat, till it is soft and cooked through.
When done, uncover the kadhai, add the methi leaves, garam masala powder, lemon juice, salt and mix well once again.
Cook this together for 3-4 minutes again on high heat until all the water released by methi and ridge gourd dries up.
Leave the sabzi uncovered so that the vegetables can dry up completely, check the salt and spices, adjust to taste, turn off the heat, transfer to a serving bowl and serve warm.
Serve Methi Turai Ki Sabzi along with hot salad for a quick lunch or a weeknight dinner.

title: Potato And Cauliflower In Peanut Curry Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Coriander (Dhania) Leaves , chopped, for garnish
instructions: To begin making the Potato & Cauliflower In Peanut Curry Recipe, dry roast the peanuts and remove the husk completely. If you want you can roast them again for better flavor. Collect the roasted peanuts in a grinder jar and grind to make a fine powder and keep aside.
In a kadai/wok, heat a bit of oil and add bay leaf and mustard seeds and wait till they crackle. Add grated ginger and saute.
Now add besan and roast it for few seconds and immediately add the tomato puree in it and stir nicely.
Add coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder and garam masala powder and fry the masala till oil starts leaving from sides.
Now add curd (you can skip this step if you want) and fry for another minute or so.
Once the masala starts smelling great and flavoured, add roasted peanut powder and mix nicely.
Cook for another 2-3 mins and add cauliflower and potato pieces, add water to make the curry. The curry is thick hence be careful while adding water. Adjust salt and let the curry come to a boil.
Simmer the gas, and cook the curry for another 5 mins on low flame with lid closed till the vegetables are cooked.
Once the Potato & Cauliflower Curry is done, turn off the gas and transfer the curry in a serving bowl and garnish with some fresh coriander.
Serve Potato & Cauliflower In Peanut Curry Recipe with Butter Naan and Mooli Raita for your weeknight dinner.

title: Achari Chole Aloo Tikki Chaat Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked for 8 hours
2 tablespoon Sev, for garnishing and crunch
Achari Mayo, as needed for each tikki
Nutralite Garlic & Oregano Spread, for cooking
instructions: Soak the Kabuli Chana (chickpeas) in water for about 8 to 10 hours.
Cook the soaked chickpeas with salt and the soaking water, adding more water if needed, until they are soft and tender; set aside.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan, add cumin seeds, chopped ginger and a bay leaf, and stir‑fry for a few seconds until aromatic.

Stir in the tomato puree along with turmeric, amchur, garam masala, coriander powder, anardana powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, black pepper powder and black salt; sauté until the mixture turns dark brown.
Add the cooked chickpeas to the masala, stir to coat evenly, adjust salt and spices, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20–30 minutes until the chickpeas are well coated and browned.
Continue to simmer, covered, on low heat for another 30 minutes until the chickpeas develop an outer brown coating; taste and adjust seasoning, then keep aside.
In a large mixing bowl, mash the boiled potatoes and sweet potatoes together.
Add grated ginger, finely chopped green chillies, finely chopped onion, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, salt and a tablespoon of corn flour to the mashed potatoes; mix well.
Shape the mixture into circular discs about 1 to 1.5 inches in diameter.
Flatten each disc, place a little Achari Mayo in the centre, then close the disc to form the Achari Aloo tikki.
Dust each tikki with whole wheat bread crumbs.
Preheat a tawa or skillet and pan‑fry the tikkis with a little Nutralite Garlic & Oregano Spread until they are browned and crisp on both sides.
Arrange the cooked Aloo tikkis on a serving platter.
Spoon hot chana masala over each tikki.
Top with chopped green chillies, finely chopped onions, a spoon of green mint chutney and a spoon of sweet date‑tamarind chutney.
Garnish with additional chopped onions, fresh coriander leaves and sev; serve immediately as a snack or dinner.

title: Chewy Pumpkin Seed Chikki Recipe
instructions: Grate the coconut.
Heat a heavy-bottomed kadhai and melt the jaggery and cardamom powder; add the grated coconut and stir continuously till the mixture turns sticky, about 10 minutes.
Add the pumpkin seeds and mix well; brush the two steel moulds with oil.
Divide the mixture to fill the moulds and keep refrigerated for 30 minutes.
Serve it cold or slightly warm before eating.

title: Chenna Recipe (Homemade Cottage Cheese | A High Protein Snack)
instructions: Pour the milk into a heavy bottomed pan, turn the heat to high, and wait for the milk to come to a boil.

When the milk begins to boil, add the freshly squeezed lemon juice; the milk will curdle, separating into cheese (chenna) and whey. Turn off the heat and let the cheese rest in the whey for about a minute.
Separate the whey and the chenna using a thin sieve strainer.
Once most of the water is drained, transfer the chenna/cottage cheese into a bowl; season with salt or sugar and serve for breakfast.
Season the chenna with a little sugar or honey, and optionally top with granola, almonds, and raisins for a wholesome breakfast.
Serve the chenna with plain sugar and bananas if desired.
Enjoy the homemade chenna as a natural wholesome protein supplement.
If you like the recipe, leave a comment below.

title: No Onion No Garlic Cabbage Kofta Curry Recipe
instructions: Grate cabbage and press in batches to remove excess water.
Collect the dry grated cabbage in a large mixing bowl.
Add besan, green chili, coriander, cumin powder, turmeric, garam masala, red chili powder and salt; stir well to make a dry mix.
Heat oil in a kadhai/wok and shape the mixture into medium lemon‑sized kofta balls; set aside on a plate.
When the oil is hot, carefully drop the kofta balls into the wok, 4‑5 at a time, and fry until golden.
Place the fried kofta balls on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil.
In a separate kadhai/wok, heat oil to prepare the curry.
Add bay leaf and, after a few seconds, add grated ginger and sauté.
Add besan and roast briefly, then immediately stir in the tomato puree.
Add coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder and garam masala powder; fry the masala until oil separates from the sides.
Stir in 2 tablespoons of curd (optional) and fry for another minute.
Add fresh cream and mix well.
Cook for 2‑3 minutes, then add water to achieve the desired consistency, being careful as the curry is thick.
Adjust salt and bring the curry to a boil.
Reduce heat, add freshly crushed cardamom, and simmer for 5 more minutes with the lid closed.
Gently drop the fried kofta balls into the curry and turn off the heat.
Transfer the curry to a serving bowl, swirl fresh cream on top and garnish with chopped coriander.
Serve with Pudina Tawa Paratha and Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita.

title: Prawn Cutlets With Sweet Potatoes Wedges Recipe
ingredients: 4 Sweet Potatoes, cut into thin stripes
Extra Virgin Olive Oil, as required
instructions: Shell medium king prawns, leaving their tails on.
Make a cut lengthwise of each prawn's back and remove the digestive tract.
