Make another cut, a little deeper, so the prawn meat ‘butterflies’ open.
If the prawns are large, flatten them gently with a wide-bladed knife.
Set up three flat plates for coating: flour mixture, beaten eggs, and seasoned breadcrumbs.
In the first plate, combine plain flour with corn flour and flavor with garlic powder and red chilli powder; mix well.
In the second plate, add 2 well-beaten eggs.
In the third plate, add the bread crumbs and season with salt and black pepper powder.
Coat each prawn cutlet by dredging in the flour mixture, then dip in the egg, and finally press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep‑frying pan and fry the coated cutlets on medium heat for 2–3 minutes until golden brown; then place on paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Prepare the sweet potato wedges by tossing them with olive oil, paprika, salt, and black pepper powder.
Arrange the seasoned wedges in a single layer on a greased baking tray.
Bake at 200 °C for 20–30 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
Serve the prawn cutlets with the baked sweet potato wedges, optionally with cottage cheese dip.

title: Oreo Paneer Modak Recipe
instructions: To begin making Oreo Paneer Modak Recipe, remove the creamy portion in the Oreo biscuits in a mixing bowl, take all the biscuits and grind the biscuits to a fine powder in a mixer grinder. Take it out in a bowl.
Grate the paneer and grind it until it turns to a fine paste.
Add the powdered biscuits and cream to the paneer. Knead the mixture well.
Add butter, condensed milk and Cardamom Powder into a hot kadai on medium low heat and slowly stir until the mixture is bubbly.
Add the Paneer and Biscuit mixture to it and slowly mix it well with a spatula. Once the mixture becomes thick switch off the heat.
Let the mixture cool a little.
Grease the Modak mold with little butter and take a small portion of the mixture at a time in your palm and roll it.

Press the mixture in the mold and shape it. Remove the excess mixture. You can do this with your hands also, but since there is no frying or baking involved after this step and due to ingredients used in this recipe, the modaks may not be uniform and hold shape well.
Now slowly remove the Modak and keep on butter paper or butter greased plate.
Serve Oreo Paneer Modak Recipe as a prashad or during snack time along with Baked Chevdo Recipe and Masala Chai.

title: Turmeric Milk Recipe - Haldi Doodh / Golden Milk
ingredients: 1 inch fresh turmeric root, or 1 teaspoon turmeric powder
instructions: Bring the grated turmeric root (or turmeric powder) and milk to a boil for a couple of minutes.
Once the mixture boils, turn off the heat and let it rest for a couple of minutes to extract the essential compounds and color from the turmeric.
After resting, strain the turmeric milk into a glass, stir in sugar or honey and black pepper, and serve while still hot.
Turmeric milk (Haldi Doodh / Golden Milk) is a great home remedy for coughs and colds and can be given to children as young as one year.
If using turmeric powder instead of fresh root, simply boil the milk with the powder, add sugar or honey, and serve without straining.

title: Cheesy Potatoes Recipe
ingredients: Red Chilli flakes, as needed, optional
instructions: Boil the potatoes, peel them, and cut into thick round slices.
Heat butter in a heavy-bottomed pan and add onions; sauté until translucent, then add corn and salt.
Sprinkle oregano flakes and red chilli flakes, mixing well.
Add lemon juice and switch off the flame; brush a flat pan with a little oil.
Place the sliced potatoes on the pan, roast and flip until lightly golden.
Sprinkle some salt on the potatoes and switch off the flame.
Take one potato slice, place the prepared corn mixture on it, and sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top.
If the potatoes are hot, the cheese will melt quickly; if cooled, microwave for a few seconds to melt the cheese.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve as a tea-time snack.

title: Homemade Pomegranate Juice with Ginger Recipe
instructions: Remove the pomegranate seeds from the shell and transfer them to a bowl.
Add the pomegranate seeds, grated ginger, and a little water to a juicer.
Blend all the ingredients using a juicer or blender until smooth, ensuring the seeds are ground as well.
Strain the juice into a large bowl and season with salt or chaat masala to taste.
Serve the pomegranate juice with ginger immediately, optionally with rosemary mushroom oatmeal or broccoli pesto toast.

title: Mustard Vegetable Curry Recipe
ingredients: 2 Carrots (Gajjar), cut into rounds or lengthwise of 1 inch thickness
5 to 6 Green beans (French Beans), cut into 1 inch pieces, steamed
instructions: To begin making the Mustard Vegetable Curry Recipe, we will first have to steam the vegetables and keep them ready. You can use a steamer or a pressure cooker to cook the vegetables.
Potatoes take a longer time to cook, so I suggest you cook them separate from the beans, carrots and peas.

To begin making the curry base; heat a teaspoon of oil in a pan on medium heat. Add in the cumin seeds, garlic and onion and saute on medium heat until the onion has turned light pink and translucent.
Once the onions are ready; add in the turmeric powder, chilli powder and stir for a few seconds. Finally add in the coconut milk, the vegetable stock and the dijon mustard.
Add in the salt and check the spice and salt levels. Adjust to suit your taste.
Finally stir in the steamed vegetables; turn the heat to low, cover the pan and simmer the curry 3 to 4 minutes. Turn off the heat and the Mustard Vegetable Curry is ready to be served.
Serve the Mustard Vegetable Curry hot with steamed rice or tawa paratha for dinner.

title: Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita Recipe
instructions: Chop all the vegetables (cucumber, tomato, onion, green chillies) and set them ready.
Whisk the yogurt well with salt and cumin powder, then add all the chopped vegetables and stir.
Transfer the raita to a serving bowl.
Serve the raita chilled alongside dishes like Vegetable Hyderabadi Biryani, Cabbage Paneer Paratha, or pulav.

title: Kerala Style Beetroot Pachadi Recipe
instructions: Wash, peel, and grate the beetroot; cook it with a little water in a pressure cooker until tender.
In a mixer, grind all the "for grinding" ingredients into a paste, adding very little water.
When the beetroot is cooked, add the ground paste and turmeric powder to it.
Stir well, add salt, and cook for a few minutes until the raw smell of the paste disappears.
Allow the mixture to cool, then whisk the curd and add it to the beetroot, mixing thoroughly.
Heat oil in a tadka pan, add mustard seeds, red chilli, and curry leaves; once they splutter, add this tempering to the pachadi and stir to combine.
Serve the Kerala Style Beetroot Pachadi with steamed rice, Vendakkai Uppadan, and Jack Fruit Seeds Stir Fry.

title: Paneer Bhurji Wraps Recipe
instructions: Heat oil in a wok/kadhai, add the chopped onion and sauté till it turns soft and translucent.
Add the tomatoes and green chillies and cook until the tomatoes are half done.
Add the grated paneer, season with salt and mix well; let it cook for 2 minutes with the lid closed.
Stir in the coriander leaves, give it a good stir and switch off the heat.
Heat the tortilla wraps in a skillet over medium flame using a little oil if desired, then set aside.
Place each tortilla on a surface and fill 2 to 3 tablespoons of the paneer mixture in the middle.
Fold one third of the tortilla at the bottom, then fold over the sides to form a wrap.
Serve the Paneer Bhurji Wraps with Tomato Garlic Chutney, Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, or any chutney of your choice.

title: Corn Halwa Recipe - Makki Ka Halwa
instructions: Boil or pressure cook sweet corn in 2 tablespoons of water for 2 whistles, then allow it to cool.
Add the cooked corn kernels to a mixer and grind into a coarse paste, adding a little water.
Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan, add the corn paste and sauté for 5 minutes until the colour turns golden.
Add milk, sugar, saffron, and crushed cardamom; stir well and cook on medium flame until slightly thick.
Add the remaining ghee and continue stirring until the ghee is absorbed and the mixture starts leaving the sides of the pan, about 6–8 minutes.
Heat a tadka pan with ghee, add the cashews and fry until they turn lightly brown.
Combine the fried cashews with the halwa, mix well, and the dish is ready to be served.
Serve the Corn Halwa as a dessert after a simple meal of Palak Dal, Sev Tamatar Ki Sabzi, and Phulka.

title: Chocolaty Fulzadi Recipe (Diwali Chocolate Sparklers)
instructions: Begin making this Chocolaty Fulzadi by mixing together milk powder, cocoa powder, grated chocolate bar, and nuts in a large bowl; set aside.
In another bowl, combine the sugar with 2 tablespoons of water and heat on medium until the sugar dissolves completely and the syrup becomes stringy; remove from heat and blend in the ghee.
Pour the sugar syrup into the bowl of dry powders and nuts and mix everything together.
Once mixed well, shape the mixture into small lemon-sized balls and roll them into cylinders, sprinklers, or fulzadi-shaped sticks; optionally place small silver balls over the rolls.
Take about 10 toothpicks or barbecue sticks and pierce each cylinder or fulzadi with a stick.
Your Chocolate Fulzadi (Chocolate Sprinklers) are now ready to eat.
Serve the Chocolaty Fulzadi with Mullu Murukku or Omapodi Diwali Mixture, or enjoy as a dessert.

title: Pudina Tawa Paratha Recipe (Mint Leaf Skillet Flat Bread)
ingredients: 2 Green Chillies (add more if you like it spicy)
instructions: Roughly blend the mint leaves and green chillies in a blender.

In a large bowl combine the flour, salt, ground mint mixture, and a tablespoon of oil; knead adding water gradually to form a firm, smooth dough. Add another tablespoon of oil, knead again, cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
Knead the rested dough again, divide it into 8 portions, and preheat an iron skillet over medium heat.
Roll each portion into a ball, flatten with your palm, dust with flour, and roll into circles about 3 inches in diameter. Spread 1/4 teaspoon oil on each rolled dough.
Fold each circle into a semi‑circle, then fold again to form a mini triangle, dust with flour, and gently roll into a larger triangle; repeat for all portions.
Place a rolled dough on the hot skillet over medium‑high heat; when air pockets appear, flip and smear about 1/2 teaspoon ghee, then press lightly with a flat spatula.
Flip to the other side, press and turn similarly until brown spots appear and the paratha is slightly crisp; remove from heat and keep hot.
Repeat the process with the remaining dough, stacking the cooked parathas and serving them hot.

title: Chicken Cooked in Banana Leaves Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Chicken Cooked in Banana Leaves, in a mixer-jar, combine the green chillies, coriander sprigs (stem as well), ginger garlic paste, cloves, peppercorns, star anise and grind to a coarse mixture.
In a mixing bowl, add the chicken, the freshly ground mixture, lime juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, salt.
Make sure the chicken pieces are completely coated with the mixture. Let the chicken pieces marinate for two hours.
Once the chicken is marinated, cut the banana leaves into squares of 4 inch squares, so that you can make parcels. Now put the one chicken piece in one banana leaf piece.
Fold the leaf to make a parcel and tie it using a thread.
Heat oil in a pan, add the parcels into the pan and make sure you are not crowding the pan. Cover the pan and cook the parcels from both sides for at-least 15-20 minutes.
Open the parcels and serve hot.
Serve Chicken Cooked in Banana Leaves as an appetizer along with other appetizers such as Mushroom Poha Cutlets Recipe and Easy Sabudana Vada With Arrowroot Powder.

title: Crispy and Spicy Chilli Chicken Recipe - Indian Style
ingredients: 5 Green Chillies, chopped, adjust to taste
instructions: Clean chicken and chop into bite‑sized pieces; slice the onions as well.
In a kadai, heat about 2 teaspoons oil and cumin seeds until they sizzle, then add ginger, garlic, green chillies, cinnamon sticks, and cloves; roast until the chillies brown slightly.
Transfer the roasted masalas and coriander leaves to a mixer and grind into a fine thick paste, adding a little water if needed.
Set the masala paste aside for later use.
In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with salt, curd/yogurt, the masala paste, turmeric powder, corn flour, all‑purpose flour, and egg white; stir until the chicken is evenly coated.
Marinate the chicken mixture for about 4 hours in the refrigerator.
After marination, heat enough oil in a deep‑frying pan for deep frying.
When the oil is hot, drop chicken pieces one by one into the pan over low flame and let them crisp up.
Once the pieces turn golden brown, remove them onto a kitchen towel; fry all chicken in batches until crisp and golden.
In the same hot oil, deep‑fry the onion slices and curry leaves until crisp on medium‑high heat.
Serve the crispy fried chicken topped with the fried onions and curry leaves.
Enjoy as a side dish with steamed rice and Milagu Rasam (Village Style Pepper Rasam).

title: Vegan Mango Lassi Recipe
instructions: Peel the skin of mangoes and cut them into small cubes. You can use store bought mango puree but it tastes best with fresh fruit pulp.
In a blender, add mango pieces, almonds, and blend them well. Ensure there are no fruit chunks left out in the jar.
Now, add salt, maple syrup, vanilla extract to the jar and grind them until smooth.
To add more richness to the lassi, you can add a cup of almond milk yogurt or soy milk yogurt to the drink and grind them together.
Serve Vegan Mango Lassi in glasses with ice cubes. Garnish with chopped pistachios and saffron.
You can optionally stir in rose syrup for enhanced flavor and taste.
Serve Vegan Mango Lassi along with Black Beans Stuffed Paratha, Aloo Paratha or any other stuffed paratha of your choice. You can also serve your favourite pickle to eat with the stuffed paratha.

title: Banana Apple Mash Recipe
instructions: Clean and wash the apple, peel off its skin, and chop it finely.
In a saucepan, put the apple pieces, add a bit of water and bring to a boil. Once the apple is cooked, remove from heat and transfer the apples to a bowl.
Add the banana and mash very well with the back of a spoon until mushy.
Mix the mashed banana and cooked apple together and mash until well combined.
Serve the banana and apple mash to your baby/toddler (6 months and older).

title: Kesar Pista Falooda Recipe
instructions: Soak sabja seeds (basil seeds) in enough water for 15 minutes; once expanded, drain and set aside.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, turn off the flame, add the falooda sev, let it sit for 15–20 minutes, then drain and set the sev aside.
In a pan, add milk and bring it to a boil.
When milk starts boiling, reduce the flame and add crushed pistachios, sugar, and saffron strands; stir well.
Continue boiling until the milk thickens slightly, then remove from heat and let it cool.
Refrigerate the cooled milk for 15 minutes.
To assemble, place a tablespoon of soaked sabja seeds in a tall glass, add 2 tablespoons of cooked falooda sev, and pour the chilled saffron‑pistachio milk up to three‑quarters of the glass.
Top with a large scoop of ice cream and garnish with tutti frutti and glazed cherries.
The Kesar Pista Falooda is ready to be served.
Serve chilled as a dessert.

title: Nellikai Oorugai/Amla Sambhariyo Recipe (Instant Gooseberry Pickle Recipe)
ingredients: 100 grams Amla (Nellikai/ Gooseberry), deseeded and finely chopped
1 teaspoon Methi Seeds (Fenugreek Seeds), roasted and powdered
instructions: We begin making the Nellikai oorugai/Amla Sambhariyo Recipe (Instant Gooseberry Pickle Recipe) by de-seeding the gooseberries and keeping it aside.
Heat oil in a small skillet, splutter seeds, hing and red chili powder and add this to the gooseberries along with the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Serve the Nellikai oorugai/Amla Sambhariyo Recipe (Instant Gooseberry Pickle Recipe) along with Sambar and some steamed rice.

title: Shakkar Para Recipe | Gur Para | Shankarpali - Diwali Festive Snack
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients and keep ready.
Into a large mixing bowl add the whole wheat flour, ghee, cardamom and a pinch of salt and mix well with your hands till the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the jaggery and mix well to combine.
Add water gradually and mix till the flour comes together to form a firm and soft dough. Cover it with a cloth and let it rest until ready to fry.
Roll and cut the dough; in the meantime preheat the oil for deep frying.
Roll the Shakkar Para dough into a 1/4 inch thick circle or desired thickness.
Using a knife or pizza cutter, cut the rolled dough into diamond shapes.
Heat oil for deep frying on medium heat.
Drop the Shakkar Para pieces into the hot oil and deep fry on low to medium heat until golden brown, turning constantly for even frying.
Drain the oil and place the fried pieces on a kitchen towel or tissues. Fry the remaining pieces similarly.
Once completely cooled, store in an airtight container.
Serve Shakkar Para as a tea‑time snack or a Diwali snack.

title: Pumpkin Chapati Recipe
instructions: Pressure cook the pumpkin until fully cooked (about 4-5 whistles), then allow the pressure to release and mash it well.

In a large bowl combine the flour, salt, mashed pumpkin, a tablespoon of oil, and knead adding little water at a time to make a firm and smooth dough. Add one tablespoon of oil to coat the dough and knead again. Cover and set aside for 15 minutes.
Knead the dough again and divide it into 8 portions. Preheat an iron skillet on medium heat.
Roll each dough portion into a ball, flatten it with the palm, toss on flour and roll into circles about 3 inches in diameter. Spread 1/4 teaspoon oil on the rolled dough.
Fold the circle into a semi‑circle, then fold again to form a triangle; toss the triangle on a little flour and gently roll it out into a larger triangle. Repeat with the remaining dough portions.
Heat the skillet on medium‑high, place one rolled‑out dough on the skillet. When air pockets appear, flip the paratha, smear about 1/2 teaspoon ghee, and lightly press and turn to cook.
Flip to the other side, press and turn similarly until brown spots appear and the paratha is slightly crisp. Remove from heat and serve hot.
Continue the same process with the remaining portions, stacking the cooked pumpkin chapatis and serving them hot.

title: Masala Methi Bhindi Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Bhindi (Lady Finger/Okra), chopped to bite size
3/4 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), coarsely chopped
instructions: Heat oil in pan and add cumin seeds.
Once the cumin seeds crackle add asafoetida, let the aromas release.
Add onion and garlic cloves and saute till onions turn light golden in colour.
Now add ladyfinger pieces and chopped fenugreek leaves and saute till well combined.

Add all dry ingredients except dry mango powder—add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala. Sprinkle the masalas on the cooking sabzi since this is a dry sabzi which otherwise the masalas might not mix evenly.
Mix everything well. Saute for 2-3 minutes.
Cover the lid and cook for another 3-4 minutes or until ladyfingers are soft and perfectly cooked on medium heat.
Once done add dry mango powder and mix well and cook the Masala Methi Bhindi Sabzi for another 1 minute and turn off the heat.
Transfer Masala Methi Bhindi Sabzi into a serving bowl.
Serve Masala Methi Bhindi Sabzi Recipe with phulka or Pudina Tawa Paratha along with Aloo Dum or a simple Gujarati Dal.

title: Kaju Pakoda Recipe (Cashew Nut Fritters)
instructions: To begin making Kaju Pakoda Recipe (Cashew Nut Fritters), prep up all the ingredients mentioned and keep ready. In a deep frying pan, heat enough oil to deep fry.
While the oil is getting heated, in a large mixing bowl, take besan, rice flour, red chili powder, and give them a quick stir till evenly mixed.
To the dry mixture, add ginger garlic paste, salt, fennel seeds, and mix well.
Add finely chopped mint leaves and mix well.
To this mixture, add whole cashew nuts and toss well till the cashews are coated.
Add 1 tablespoon of hot oil from the deep frying pan and mix.
Sprinkle water to the mixture, little by little, to make a lump‑free dough along with chunky cashews.
Pinch out small portions of the prepared dough and gradually drop the batter into the hot oil. Fry them in batches till golden and crisp.
Take the cashew pakodas out of the cooking oil and place them on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil.
Serve Kaju Pakoda (Cashew Nut Fritters) with tea‑time snacks for kids and masala chai for the whole family.

title: Raw Banana Dosa Recipe
ingredients: 1 Raw Banana, boiled and cut into small pieces
instructions: Begin by preparing the dosa batter according to the linked recipe.
Pressure cook the raw banana with water and turmeric powder for about 4 whistles until soft, then remove the skin and chop into small pieces.
Grind the raw banana together with coconut, adding a little water to form a smooth paste.
Add the banana-coconut paste to the dosa batter and mix well.
Check and adjust salt to taste.
Heat a skillet on high heat; pour a ladleful of batter in the center and spread to form an uttapam.
Drizzle about a teaspoon of oil around the edges and towards the insides.
Cook the dosa on both sides until browned slightly with crispy edges.
For extra crispiness, cook the dosa on medium heat, preferably on an iron skillet, which maintains heat evenly.
Serve the Raw Banana Dosa with south Indian chutney or tomato-onion chutney.

title: Chettinad Style Chilli Gobhi Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (dhania) leaves, a few sprigs, finely chopped
instructions: Boil water in a large pot and blanch cauliflower florets for one minute; drain and set aside.
In a bowl whisk together corn flour, rice flour, Kashmiri red chilli powder, salt, black pepper powder, ginger garlic paste and curd.
Dip the blanched cauliflower florets in the batter and deep‑fry them in oil or cook them in an air fryer.
In a small pan heat ghee for tempering, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, dry red chillies, and green chillies; fry for 2 minutes.
Pour the tempering over the fried gobhi and serve hot, garnished with coriander leaves.
Serve Chettinad Style Chilli Gobhi as a tea‑time snack with filter coffee, or as a starter or side dish.

title: Rajma Wrap Recipe With Carrot Cucumber Sandwich Spread
ingredients: 2 Whole Wheat Flour Tortilla (or large roti)
2 tablespoons Veeba Carrot Cucumber Sandwich Spread
1/2 cup Rajma (Large Kidney Beans), soaked for 8 hours
instructions: Soak the rajma overnight or for at least 6 hours, then boil until soft; drain and discard the water.
Heat a kadai, add oil, and once hot, add the chopped garlic and sauté for a few seconds.
Add the boiled rajma, Veeba Pizza & Pasta Sauce, and Eggless Mayonnaise; mix well and adjust salt and seasonings to taste.
Stir the rajma mixture over high heat until it thickens, then turn off the heat.
In a separate pan, add a little oil, sauté the sliced red bell pepper until softened, then set aside.
To assemble, spread Veeba Carrot Cucumber Sandwich Spread on the center of the tortilla or roti, add a line of the rajma filling, the sautéed red bell pepper, sliced onions, and mint leaves.
Gently roll up the tortilla to form the wrap and serve.
Optionally serve the Rajma Wrap with a glass of Banana Almond & Prunes Smoothie.

title: Namak Para Recipe - Traditional Diwali Snack Recipe
instructions: To begin with Namak Para recipe, prepare all the ingredients and keep ready.

Into a large mixing bowl add the whole wheat flour, ghee, ajwain and salt and mix well with your hands till the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Cover it with cloth and let it rest until ready to fry.
Next step is to roll and cut the dough. In the meantime preheat the oil for deep frying.
Roll the namak para dough into a 1/4 inch thick circle or the desired thickness you like. The thicker the para, the longer it will take to fry.
Using a knife or a pizza cutter, cut into diamond shapes.
Heat oil for deep frying on a medium heat.
Drop the namak para into the hot oil and deep fry on low to medium heat until they turn golden brown, turning them constantly for even frying.
Drain the oil and place them on a kitchen towel or tissues. Fry the remaining pieces in the same way.
Sprinkle chaat masala over the namak para if you like to give it an additional chatpata taste.
Once the namak para are cooled completely, store in an airtight container and serve.
Enjoy Namak Para with hot Masala Chai as an evening snack or festive snack for Diwali.

title: Baked Samosa Pinwheels Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Baked Samosa Pinwheels recipe, in a mixing bowl, add all the ingredients of dough, mix and knead it well to make a soft dough. Keep aside for 10 minutes until you make stuffing.
In another mixing bowl, add all the ingredients of stuffing and mix it well. Keep aside. After 10 minutes, take out the dough and knead it for couple of minutes.
Make 2 equal sized portions out of the dough. Dust one portion of dough in flour and roll it to slightly thicker chapati using rolling pin. Cut the edges of circle to make a pastry sheet.
Make 2 portions of the filling also. Take one portion of filling and spread it nicely in the rolled pastry sheet. Now roll the pastry sheet with the filling and cut it into pieces.

Take each chopped samosa pinwheels and press the open side gently to make it like a round shape so that the inner filling looks like a pinwheel. Now, rub the pinwheels into sesame seeds and keep them aside.

Preheat the oven to 400 degrees (or the temperature that is recommended on the puff pastry box). Place the pinwheels onto a parchment paper lined baking sheet and bake for 17-20 minutes until golden brown.
Your Samosa Pinwheels are ready. Serve warm as an appetizer or party snacks and use within two weeks.
Serve Baked Samosa Pinwheels with Linzer Cookies and Masala Chai for your tea time break.

title: Haryali Seekh Kebab Recipe
instructions: Soak channa dal for an hour in enough water.
Boil and mash the potatoes and set aside; steam the broccoli for 3-4 minutes and blend it using a food processor or blender in pulse motion.
Cook the soaked channa dal for 10 minutes in water until it holds its shape but is cooked through; drain and let it cool.
Dry roast the cardamom and cloves and grind them into a powder using a mortar and pestle.
In a food processor, add broccoli, cooked channa dal, salt, raw cleaned spinach, mint, coriander, freshly ground spices, pepper powder, and lemon juice; blend into a smooth paste.
Mix the paste into a bowl with mashed potatoes and cashew powder until fully combined.
Ensure the mixture is not sticky; make sure all ingredients are well drained before blending to avoid excess moisture.
Shape the mixture into long cylinders, pierce with skewers, and shape them between thumb and index finger, gently rolling on a flat surface.
Drizzle a little oil on a grill pan, place the skewers, and cook on all sides over low to medium heat until evenly cooked.
Sprinkle with chaat masala powder and serve with sliced onions and dip, alongside coriander‑mint chutney.

title: Crunchy Carrot Peanut Raita Recipe - Gajar Moongphali Raita
instructions: Prepare the peanut and red chilli spice mix.
Heat a small pan on medium heat, add the peanuts and red chillies and roast until the peanuts turn golden.
In a big bowl, add the yogurt and whisk until you attain a creamy consistency.
Add the grated carrots, the prepared peanut and red chilli spice mixture, chilli powder, and season with salt; mix well.
If the raita is too thick, add a little water and adjust the consistency to your liking.
Refrigerate the Crunchy Carrot Peanut Raita for an hour and garnish with chopped green chilies.
Serve the Carrot Peanut Raita as an accompaniment to Paneer Pulao with Green Peas, Aloo Palak Sabzi, and Phulka.

title: Ajwain Puri Recipe - Puri Flavoured With Carom Seeds
instructions: Mix the whole wheat flour, ajwain, turmeric powder, and salt with enough water in a bowl to form a dough.
Knead the mixture until a stiff dough forms, then add 2 tablespoons of oil and continue kneading to bind.
Divide the dough into equal small balls and roll each ball on a board using a rolling pin, ensuring the puris are not too thin.
Heat sufficient oil in a Kadai for deep frying the puris.
Test the oil by dropping a small piece of dough; if it rises quickly, the oil is ready.
Carefully slide the rolled puris into the hot oil, press gently with a ladle to help them puff, then flip and fry until both sides turn golden brown.
Remove the fried puris onto a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil.
Serve the puffed Ajwain puris with Amritsari Aloo, Palak Makhana, or Boondi Raita.

title: Crispy Crunchy Roti Ke Papad Recipe
instructions: Cut the leftover rotis into your desired shapes and set aside.
Heat oil in a deep‑fat fry pan.
When the oil is hot, drop the roti pieces in one by one and fry until they turn brown and crispy, being careful not to burn them.
Remove the fried pieces onto absorbent paper to drain excess oil.
Once cooled, add chaat masala, salt, and red chilli powder; mix well and serve.
Serve the crispy roti papad as an appetizer with spicy Mexican salsa verde or melon salsa, alongside a cup of masala chai.

title: Beetroot And Chickpea Kebab/Tikki Recipe - Evening Snack
ingredients: 2 Beetroots , peeled and cut into small cubes
instructions: To begin making Beetroot Chickpea Kebab/Tikki, we have to first wash and soak chickpeas/kabuli chana in enough water overnight.

The next day, add the chickpeas into the pressure cooker, add any additional water, salt and pressure cook the chickpeas for 7 whistles. After 7 whistles, turn the heat to low and continue to cook for 10 more minutes.
Release the pressure from the cooker naturally. It will approximately take 20 to 30 minutes to cook the chickpeas.
To a pressure cooker add the peeled and diced beetroots along with 2 tablespoons water and cook for 2 whistles. Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Drain any excess water from the cooked beets and chickpeas.

To a mixer or a food processor, add the cooked beetroot and cooked chickpeas along with coriander powder, cumin powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, dry mango powder (amchur powder), asafoetida and salt as per your taste.
Grind this mixture to a smooth paste without adding any water. The Beetroot Chickpea tikki mixture has to be thick in order to shape it like a tikki.
Transfer the Beetroot Chickpea Tikki mixture into a bowl and add 3 tablespoons gram flour (besan). Mix all ingredients well.
Crush peanuts coarsely with mortar pestle or in mixer and add it to the ground beetroot and chickpeas mixture.
Mix everything together and check for salt. Divide it into small balls and slightly flatten the balls in the shape of cutlets/ tikkis.
In a separate flat bowl, mix corn flour and water to form a thin paste. Keep the rava/semolina in another plate.
Dip the prepared Beetroot Chickpea Tikki into corn flour mixture and roll into rava. Dipping in corn flour is optional, you can also directly roll into rava or breadcrumbs.
Heat a griddle on medium flame, add oil. Place the Beetroot Chickpea Tikki/ Kebab and fry until it turns golden and crisp on both sides.
Repeat for remaining cutlets. You can also deep fry but shallow frying is a healthier option. Shallow frying takes roughly 10 minutes.
Serve this Beetroot Chickpea Kebab/Tikki along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or Fresh Basil Pesto as a healthy & light evening snack or as an appetizer/starter at brunch.

title: Baked Cauliflower Samosa Recipe
instructions: Prepare all ingredients and start by making the dough.
In a bowl, combine 2 cups whole wheat flour, oil, salt, and baking soda; mix by hand until crumbly.
Add water as needed to form a medium‑tight dough similar to chapathi dough; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, add raw peanuts and fry until roasted, then add dried red chilli, asafoetida, fennel and cumin seeds for tadka; sauté briefly.
Add blanched cauliflower and diced potato to the pan; fry for about 2 minutes.
Stir in salt, sugar, turmeric powder, grated ginger, and green chillies; cook on low heat, stirring occasionally until vegetables are cooked, then add kasuri methi and let the mixture cool.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C).
Divide the rested dough into 6‑7 balls; roll each into a medium‑thick circle and cut it in half.
Shape each half into a cone, fill with about 1½ teaspoons of the cauliflower‑potato stuffing, and seal the edges, brushing water on the seams; keep covered with a kitchen towel to prevent drying.
Place the formed samosas on a parchment‑lined baking tray and spray lightly with oil.
Bake for 40‑45 minutes, or until golden brown, checking after 30 minutes; remove and allow to cool slightly before serving.
Serve the baked cauliflower samosas with Khajur Imli chutney or plain tomato ketchup and enjoy.

title: Restaurant Style Hara Bhara Kebab Recipe - Vegetarian Green Patties
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Chaat Masala Powder, as needed
instructions: Begin preparing the Restaurant Style Hara Bhara Kebab mixture.
In a blender, blend spinach, coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, and cooked peas to a smooth paste.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the boiled potatoes, the green mixture, salt, amchur powder, gram flour, and chaat masala powder. Mix well. Add 2 tablespoons of bread crumbs if the mixture feels very loose.
Divide the mixture into equal portions and shape each into round, disc-shaped patties.
Heat a tawa over medium heat; place the patties on the tawa and drizzle oil while cooking the first side.
When the bottom of the kebab turns golden brown, flip and cook the other side, adding oil as needed to achieve browning without charring.
Remove the cooked kebabs onto a serving platter, optionally sprinkle additional chaat masala on top, and serve hot.
Serve the Hara Bhara Kebabs as an evening snack or appetizer with pudina chutney and Masala Chai.

title: Mixed Vegetable Curry Roll Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), finely chopped
1-1/2 cup Mixed vegetables (french beans, carrots, green peas and potatoes), finely chopped and steamed
instructions: To begin making the Mixed Vegetable Curry Roll Recipe, heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan.
Once the oil is mildly hot, add onions and saute them properly until they turn soft and golden brown in colour.
Once the onions have become golden brown in colour add chopped garlic and capsicum saute for a two minutes.
After two minutes add the chopped tomatoes and green chillies. Saute and let it cook till the tomatoes become soft.
Once done add the dry masala including curry powder, red chilli powder, salt to taste and let it cook until tomatoes are mushy.
After the tomatoes have become mushy add all steamed vegetables, mash them a bit with the back of the spoon and stir well to combine.
Add some water if you find the mixed vegetable mixture too dry as it should not dry out completely.
Once all the vegetables are cooked through and well combined, add the grated cheese, lime juice and fresh chopped coriander leaves. Stir well to combine and turn off the heat.
Our filling is ready and now the next step is to assemble the Mixed Vegetable Curry Rolls.
Slit a hot dog and remove some bread from the center of the hot dog to make space for filling.
Fill in the bread with the mixed vegetable curry masala. Keep them aside.
Heat a little butter on a preheated skillet and apply some butter on both the sides of hot dog.
Place the Mixed Vegetable Curry Rolls on the pan and warm them up on both sides and serve hot.
Serve Mixed Vegetable Curry Roll along with Carrot Pineapple Orange Juice Recipe for a wholesome breakfast or an after school snack.

title: Palak (Spinach) Puri Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoon Oil, more to deep fry
instructions: Chop spinach, ginger and green chilies and boil them together.
After boiling, strain the water and leave it aside for 15 minutes till the water is drained.
After cooling, take the boiled contents from the strainer and add to a mixer; make a thin puree without adding water.
In a mixing bowl, add whole wheat flour, the prepared puree, some oil, cumin powder and salt; mix to form a dough.
Do not add excess water as the spinach will release water on its own; cover the dough with a muslin cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, shape the dough into small marble‑sized balls.
Dust the rolling surface with whole wheat flour and flatten each ball with a rolling pin to make small thick‑sized rounds.
Heat a kadai and add oil; when the oil is hot, gently slide a flattened puri into it.
Using a frying spoon or slotted spoon, gently press the puri, add a little hot oil on top and move it in a circular motion.
When the puri puffs up, flip it and fry until it turns golden brown, taking care not to keep it in oil for more than 2 minutes.
Drain the fried puri on a kitchen towel and repeat the deep‑frying process for the remaining puris.
Serve the palak puris with Lahori Aloo and any raita of your choice.

title: Crispy Corn Chaat Recipe
instructions: To begin the Crispy Corn Chat Recipe, first keep the oil on a low flame in a deep pan for frying.
Add corn kernels, flour, red chilli powder, amchoor and salt in a mixing bowl and give it a good mix.
Add a tablespoon of water and mix it. The flour should coat the kernels. Add more water if needed. Do not make the mixture watery. Add just enough water to coat the kernels well.
Once the oil is hot, place a sieve inside the oil. Take a tablespoon of corn and scatter it inside the sieve which is inside the oil. Frying it inside the sieve makes it easy to drain.
Do not fry all of it together. Fry bit by bit.
Once the corn is crisp and golden, transfer it onto a kitchen towel.
Toss this corn with chopped onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves and top it with a generous squeeze of lemon.
Serve Crispy Corn Chat Recipe along with a hot cup of Filter Coffee for your tea time break.

title: Healthy Tomato Carrot Onion Soup Recipe
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Once hot, add chopped garlic and saute for about 20 seconds.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft and translucent, then add the thinly sliced carrots.
Add salt, mix well and cover the pan for about 3 minutes to partially cook the carrots.
Add chopped tomatoes and season with crushed black pepper; cook for about a minute.
Add some water, cover, and cook until the tomatoes are fully cooked and mushy. Switch off the heat and let the mixture cool to room temperature.
Strain the mixture, keep the water aside, and grind the solids into a puree.
Return the puree to the wok, add the reserved water, and cook for about a minute.
Add more salt and a little sugar if the tomato is too sour; cook for 3–4 minutes.
Switch off the heat and serve. (If a thinner consistency is desired, strain again, discard solids, and heat the strained soup for another minute.)
Serve the Healthy No Cream Tomato Carrot Onion Soup with garlic bread and bean sprout & corn salad.

title: Ulundhu Kali Recipe (Urad Dal Sweet)
instructions: Add urad dal, fenugreek seeds and cardamom to a mixer and grind into a smooth powder; set aside.
Prepare jaggery syrup by adding jaggery and water to a pan, boil, stir until jaggery dissolves, then strain to remove impurities.
Return the filtered jaggery syrup to the pan, add salt and dry ginger powder, stir well and bring to a boil.
Add the urad dal flour little by little, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Once the flour and jaggery are well combined, add 2 teaspoons of gingelly oil at regular intervals while mixing with a ladle.
Continue cooking until the mixture becomes thick and does not stick to the sides of the pan; then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Grease your hands with oil, take small portions of the dough, roll into medium-sized balls, and let them cool before serving.
Serve Ulundhu Kali during tea time with Irani Chai and Namak Para.

title: Sauteed Spicy Prawns Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Nando's Peri Peri Chicken Sauce
instructions: To begin making the Sauteed Spicy Prawns recipe, de-shell, de-vein the shrimp. Wash them well.
Apply a teaspoon each of red chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Mix well and marinate for about 10 minutes.
Chop coriander leaves and keep aside. In a medium saucepan, heat oil. Fry onions on medium heat until translucent.
Add grated garlic and fry on low heat for a few seconds. Add a few scallions.
Saute for a minute and add the marinated shrimp. Mix well, cover and cook for about 10 minutes on medium heat. Remove cover.
Add chopped coriander leaves, mix well, cover and cook for a minute. Remove the cover and add Peri Peri sauce or hot sauce and mix.
Remember, Peri Peri sauce already has salt, so no extra salt is needed. Let it simmer on low heat for 5 more minutes.
Switch off the flame. Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with scallion greens.
Serve Sauteed Spicy Prawns along with Shorshe Maach and steamed rice for a weekday meal.

title: Pan Fried Brussel Sprouts Recipe
instructions: To begin making Pan Fried Brussels Sprouts Recipe, clean the brussels sprouts and cut them into halves and keep aside.
Heat olive oil in a skillet, add the finely chopped garlic cloves and saute until the oil becomes fragrant.
Add in the brussels sprouts and let it char on one side, this will take around 5 minutes.
Now, flip over and let the other side char the similar way.
Add in the pepper powder, mixed herbs, season with garlic salt and mix well.
Saute for another 5 minutes on medium heat and switch off the flame.
Serve the Pan Fried Brussels Sprouts Recipe for a light dinner along with a hearty Tomato Noodle soup.

title: Mogre Ka Sharbat Recipe - Fresh Jasmine Drink
instructions: To begin making the Mogre Ka Sharbat Recipe, place a saucepan on medium flame, add in the sugar and water and allow it to come to a rolling boil, reduce the flame and add in the milk.
You will observe, the impurities from the sugar will float on the surface of the sugar syrup.
Using a tea strainer, skim off the impurities from the top and discard it in a small bowl placed close by.
Once the impurities have been removed, add in the cardamom powder, saffron strands and the fresh jasmine buds.
Once again bring to a rolling boil and turn off the flame. Allow this Mogre Ka Sharbat to cool down to room temperature.
Cover with a lid and set aside, for about 24 hours, allow the fresh jasmine flavour to infuse into the sugar syrup.
24 hours later, strain out the jasmine buds and discard them.
Pour the Mogre Ka Sharbat in a bottle and store in the refrigerator for up to a month. This makes the concentrated Mogre Ka Sharbat.
To serve, in a glass add a tablespoon of the concentrated Mogre Ka Sharbat, top with a few ice cubes and 200 ml of water. This Mogre Ka Sharbat is now ready to drink.
Serve Mogre Ka Sharbat Recipe as a summer evening drink along with Homemade Vada Pav Recipe With Aloo Vada for a simple evening snack.

title: Egg Lifafa Paratha Recipe
instructions: In a bowl add flour, salt, sugar, 1 egg and a little oil; mix well, add water and knead to a smooth dough, then let the dough rest for 20 minutes.
In another bowl beat 2 eggs, then add chopped onion, green chilli, chopped tomato, red chilli powder, cumin powder, chaat masala, chopped coriander leaves and salt; mix thoroughly.
Apply ghee or oil to the rested dough and knead again to make a smooth dough; divide the dough into 6‑7 equal balls.
Take one ball, dust with dry flour and roll out; brush with ghee/oil, fold from both reverse sides, brush again and fold; shape into a square.
Dust with dry flour again and roll out the folded dough into a square shape.
Cook on a low‑flame griddle: place the egg mixture on the dough, add mozzarella, fold the paratha from both sides, seal completely, and fry both sides with ghee or oil until golden; serve hot.
Serve Egg Lifafa Paratha with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Tomato Chutney, or any chutney of your choice.

title: Knol Khol Gravy Recipe - Kohlrabi In A Yogurt Based Gravy
instructions: To begin making the Knol Knol Gravy Recipe, peel the knol knol also known as Knol Khol and chop them into bite size pieces.
Make a couple of slits at the bottom of the tomatoes and put them in boiling water for 5 minutes until skin separates (blanching the tomatoes), cool completely and grind into smooth paste.
In a kadai, add oil on medium heat; once the oil is hot, add cumin seeds.
When cumin seeds begin to sizzle, add finely chopped onions and saute until the onions are translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add finely chopped ginger and garlic and saute until raw smell goes away.
Next, add the prepared tomato puree and cook for 5 minutes, continuing to cook until the oil comes to the surface.
Season the tomato and onion mixture with salt, chilli powder, coriander powder and finally add garam masala powder.
Stir well until all the masalas are well combined into the gravy.
Now toss in chopped knol khol and coat well with masala gravy; whisk curd and add it to the gravy.
Add half cup water, cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring in between and checking the water level; add more water if needed to adjust consistency, then turn off the heat.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Serve Knol Knol Gravy along with rotis/phulkas and Mooli Raita for a simple weeknight dinner.

title: Savoury Baked Arbi Chips Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Extra Virgin Olive Oil, to toss
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Wash, peel, and thinly slice the taro roots/arbi using a mandolin slicer.
In a small bowl, mix olive oil, amchur (if using), salt, and pepper; rub this mixture into the taro slices and toss well to coat.
Line a baking tray with greased parchment paper and spread the chips evenly without overlapping.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, then remove and toss; return to the oven and bake at 160°C for 4-5 minutes or until crisp, monitoring closely.
The crispy crunchy arbi chips are ready to munch.
Serve the baked arbi chips with a dip such as Tomato and Sunflower Seed Dip.

title: Chettinad Vendakkai Saddam Recipe (Spicy Okra Rice)
ingredients: 10 Bhindi (Lady Finger/Okra) , cut into small dices
instructions: To begin making the Chettinad Vendakkai Saddam Recipe (Spicy Okra Rice), we will first cook the okra along with the spices.

Take a heavy bottomed pan and heat the spoonful of oil on medium heat. Add the onions and the Vendakkai and salt to taste. Stir fry on low to medium heat until the okra (Vendakkai) is well cooked and roasted. This will take about 10 minutes.

Once the Vendakkai is well cooked, add the turmeric powder, curry leaves, cinnamon powder, black pepper powder, salt, thick tamarind paste and sauté the ladies fingers till it gets coated well with all the other ingredients.
Now, in another tadka pan, heat a teaspoon of oil. Add in the mustard seeds, channa dal and cashews. Allow them to crackle and get roasted until lightly browned. Add this to the Vendakkai mixture.

Stir the seasoning well into the Vendakkai mixture. At this stage add in the cooked rice. Stir together all the ingredients until well combined. Turn the heat to low, cover the pan and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes. Check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste.
Finally, turn off the heat and transfer the Chettinad Vendakkai Saddam to a serving bowl.
Serve the delicious tangy and spicy Chettinad Vendakkai Saddam Recipe (Spicy Okra Rice) hot along with a tomato onion raita.

title: Gulab Phirni Recipe - Rose Flavoured Rice Pudding Shots
ingredients: Mixed nuts (pistachio and almonds) for garnish
instructions: Soak the rice in water for half an hour.
Chop the dates and soak them in about 1/2 cup of hot milk for about 30 minutes.
Drain water and pulse the rice along with 2 tablespoons of milk in a mixer grinder until a grainy consistency is achieved; the grains should feel coarse between your fingers.
Bring the milk to a brisk boil in a large saucepan, add the rice and saffron while whisking continuously, then turn the heat to low and keep stirring to avoid lumps.
Keep stirring the mixture every couple of minutes.
After about 20 minutes the mixture will start to thicken; simmer the phirni for another 20 to 25 minutes until it thickens considerably and the rice is completely cooked.
Stir occasionally to avoid the phirni from sticking to the bottom of the pan and forming lumps.
When creamy, add the chopped and soaked dates and simmer for another 3 to 4 minutes, then add the gulab jal and stir it in.
Turn off the heat and allow the phirni mixture to cool.
Spoon the gulab phirni into small shot glasses and garnish with chopped pistachios or sliced almonds.
Cool the gulab phirni in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours or overnight and serve chilled.
Serve gulab phirni along with samosas and Mawa Gujiya with Badam and Pista for festive occasions.

title: Paneer And Badam Milk Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Whole Almonds (Badam), soaked and peeled
12 Whole Almonds (Badam), soaked, peeled and chopped
instructions: Grind 1/2 cup almonds in a blender with a little water until smooth and fine, then set aside.
Heat milk in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add the grated paneer to the boiled milk and cook on medium to low heat until the mixture thickens.
Add sugar, the almond paste, chopped almonds, cardamom powder, and saffron strands to the milk; mix well and garnish with saffron strands.
Serve the Paneer and Badam Milk during the Holi festival with snacks such as Hari Matar ke Pakode and Namak Para.

title: Ujju Rotti Recipe (Indian Rice Flat Bread)
instructions: To prepare Ujju Rotti Recipe (Indian Rice Flat Bread), in a medium sized vessel bring the water to a boil with salt and oil.
Lower the flame and pour the rice flour into the boiling water using a cup or a tumbler, pour it in the centre as much as possible.
Let it get cooked on a low to medium flame for 8-10 minutes uncovered.

Turn off the flame, take a wooden stick or a wooden spatula, run it under a tap to wet it and then mix the flour and water mixture vigorously until combined. This step must be done quickly to avoid lumps. This takes about 2 minutes. Cover for a couple of minutes and let it cool until you can handle the mixture.
Drop it on an oiled surface and knead well for about 5-7 minutes. Roll the mixture into a cylinder and divide them equally. This should give you about 4 equal sized balls.

Kneading should happen after wetting hands since the dough will stick to hands. Keep them covered at all times. Knead each ball for 15-20 seconds and roll it out just like regular rotis using rice flour. Just make sure you do it slow and steady since the edges might crack.
Roll out all the balls and stack the rotti on top of another on a plate first and then start roasting them. Use a little rice flour to avoid getting stuck to one another.
Heat a tawa and cook the Ujju Rotti just like a chapatti by smearing oil/ghee on both sides and serve with Badanekaayi Gojju, Peas curry, Malai Kofta or any pappu (dal).

title: A Creamy & Delicious Gulkand Kulfi Recipe
instructions: Heat milk in a heavy bottomed saucepan and bring it to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer the milk, stirring almost continuously, until its volume is reduced to about half.
Continue stirring continuously as the milk reaches less than half its original quantity to prevent it from sticking and burning.
Stir continuously because condensed milk can stick to the pan and burn, which gives an unpleasant and potentially toxic taste.
When reduced, stir in the sugar until fully dissolved, then add fennel seed powder, almond powder, saffron, and gulkand to the kulfi milk mixture.
Turn off the heat, let the Gulkand Kulfi mixture cool completely, then pour into molds about three‑quarters full, seal airtight, and freeze in the refrigerator.
Freeze the kulfis for at least fifteen hours or longer; optionally insert wooden ice‑cream sticks before freezing.
Run the molds under water to release the frozen kulfis onto a plate and serve.
Serve the Gulkand Kulfi for Holi, Diwali, or any special Indian dinner.

title: Dalia Pakora Recipe - Broken Wheat Pakora
ingredients: Water, as required to make a thick pakora batter
Oil, as required to fry the pakoras
instructions: Wash the dalia and set aside.
Heat a pressure cooker with 2 cups of water, add salt to taste, cooking oil and the washed broken wheat.
Close the pressure cooker and pressure cook for 4-5 whistles; turn off the flame and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Open the cooker, check that the broken wheat is cooked through and no water remains; if water is present, heat and stir until it evaporates.
Transfer the cooked broken wheat into a mixing bowl and let it cool.
Add besan, onion, coriander leaves, green chilli, salt, turmeric powder, cumin seeds, ajwain, cooking oil and enough water to make a thick batter.
Use just enough water to combine all the ingredients into a thick batter.
Heat a paniyaram pan on medium flame, add a few drops of oil to each cavity, then quickly add the eno fruit salt to the batter and mix well.
Drop tablespoonfuls of the batter into each cavity and cook on medium‑high heat for a couple of minutes on each side.
Ensure the inside of the pakoras is well cooked and the outer covering is crisp.
Drain the fried pakoras on absorbent paper and serve hot.
Alternatively, deep‑fry the pakoras in a kadai.
Serve Dalia Pakora with green chutney, date tamarind chutney and a steaming cup of adrak chai.

title: Savoury Oatmeal Porridge Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Savoury Oatmeal Porridge Recipe, prep the vegetables and keep them ready for cooking.

In a kadai or a wok, add a teaspoon of oil and place it over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and allow them to crackle. Once they crackle, add the chopped onions and green chilies. Saute the onions and chilies until they turn soft and lightly browned.
Next add the carrots, capsicum, and beans. Sprinkle some salt and a dash of water and cook them until done, about 4 minutes. Keep the pan covered so they cook faster in the steam.
Add the turmeric powder, the oats, and a cup of water. Check the salt and adjust to suit your taste.
Keep stirring the porridge and cook until the oats are done.
Once the oats are cooked through, stir in the chopped coriander leaves and serve.
Serve the Savoury Oatmeal Porridge along with a fried egg and fruits for a wholesome breakfast.

title: Golden Turmeric Almond Saffron Milk Shot Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Brown Sugar (Demerara Sugar) (reduce if you wish)
instructions: Grind the almond powder and the brown sugar together in a mixer attachment and set aside.
Crush the ginger and turmeric together in a mortar and pestle and set aside.
Heat the milk in a saucepan and bring it to a boil.
Simmer the milk and continue cooking for another 10 minutes, or until it becomes considerably thicker.

Add the remaining ingredients (almond and brown sugar powder, turmeric, ginger, honey, cinnamon stick, cardamom seeds, saffron strands) to the milk, leaving out the raisins, and let the milk continue to simmer.
After 10-15 minutes, turn off the heat and strain the milk to remove undissolved ingredients, then serve hot.
Add the raisins to each glass and serve the milk.

title: Instant Baked Aloo Tikki Recipe
ingredients: 3 tablespoons Whole Wheat Flour, or maida
instructions: To begin making Instant Baked Aloo Tikki Recipe, peel and grate potatoes. Chop all other required veggies.
In a mixing bowl, add all the veggies, salt and squeeze so that the water oozes out.
Now, add wheat and rice flour to bind the mixture. Add red chilli powder and mix well.
Take 2 tablespoons of the mixture, make tikkis with your palms and put them on a baking tray lined with parchment sheet.
Preheat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius. Lightly brush oil on the tikkis and bake for 10-20 minutes or till done and crisp.
Serve Instant Baked Aloo Tikki Recipe along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and tomato ketchup with a cup of hot Ginger Lemon Black Tea Recipe.

title: Sabsige Millet Pulav Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Sabsige Millet Pulav recipe, in a mixer jar, add all ingredients for grinding and grind to a paste with as little water as possible.
In a pan heat some oil, splutter cumin seeds and fry the cashews, then add the tomatoes, cook for 30 seconds to a minute now add potatoes and peas.
Add the finely chopped dill leaves and saute until the greens wilt and turn fragrant for approximately 2-3 minutes.
Now add the paste and cook until the raw smell disappears. Add washed millets and mix until well combined. Toss around for a minute.
Add 1-3/4 cup of water, salt to taste.
Bring this to a boil and turn the heat to simmer and cook with the lid cracked open slightly for 12-15 minutes on low heat or until all the liquid has evaporated.
Turn off the heat and gently transfer to a serving bowl immediately or the residual heat can make the millets mushy.
Serve Sabsige Millet Pulav along with Boondi Raita, Palak Raita or any other raita of your choice.

title: Bharwa Karela With Sweet Potato Filling Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Mustard oil, or more to cook
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep ready.

Lightly peel the skin of the karelas/bitter gourd, cut into 1 inch cylinders, scoop out and discard seeds and pulp, sprinkle salt and turmeric to remove the bitterness, and let rest for 20-25 minutes.
Pressure cook the peeled sweet potatoes with 1 cup of water for 3 whistles, allow pressure to release naturally, then peel and grate or mash the potatoes.
Heat a skillet with oil over medium heat; add ginger and sauté for a few seconds, then add chopped tomatoes, green chilies, and salt, cooking until the tomatoes become mushy.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, chaat masala, garam masala, and salt; mix well.
Cook for at least 2 minutes until flavors develop, then adjust salt and spices to taste.
Fill the karelas tightly with the sweet potato masala.
Heat a wide pan with oil, place the stuffed karelas and pan‑fry until cooked and browned.
Cover the pan and steam the karelas until fully cooked; sprinkle a little more chaat masala and serve hot.
Serve the Bharwa Karela with Sweet Potato Filling alongside Panchmel Dal and Phulka.

title: Badusha Recipe | Balushahi Recipe - Sweet Indian Doughnut
instructions: Prepare the Balushahi in two stages: first make the fried dough, then the sugar syrup.
In a large bowl combine flour, salt, and baking soda; add ghee and rub in with fingers to form coarse crumbs, then add yogurt and knead until the dough comes together.
Cover the dough with a wet muslin cloth and let it rest for about 30 minutes.
Divide the rested dough into lemon‑sized portions, make a dent in the center with the thumb, taking care not to press too hard.
Cover the dough portions with a wet cloth and let them rest for another 15 minutes.
Preheat oil for deep frying; fry a few dough balls at a time on medium heat until they float to the surface.
Flip the balls and fry the other side until both sides are a darker golden brown, maintaining medium heat.
Drain the fried dough balls and set them aside.
To make the sugar syrup, combine water, sugar, and cardamom powder in a saucepan; heat on medium, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the mixture boils.
After boiling, lower the heat and simmer until the syrup reaches a single‑thread consistency.
Test the syrup by touching it between fingers (it should feel sticky) and observing a long drop from the spoon.
Dip each fried dough ball individually into the hot sugar syrup, coating it thoroughly, then arrange on a platter.
Garnish the syrup‑coated Balushahi with chopped pistachios and let them rest until the sugar hardens.
Serve the Balushahi as a sweet treat for festive occasions.

title: Zafrani Mawa Cake Recipe (Saffron Flavored Milk Cake)
instructions: To begin making Zafrani Mawa Cake, sift the flour and baking powder and keep aside.
Bring the mava to room temperature if kept in fridge.
Grease a 7 inch cake tin and line it with parchment.
Preheat the oven at 350°F for 10 minutes.
In a bowl, beat butter and sugar till it turns creamy. Then add in eggs and beat well. Add in essence and mix.
Add in mava and continue to beat till all mixed and incorporated well.
Fold in flour and mix well, add warm milk and saffron to loosen the batter.
Pour the batter in the prepared cake tin.
Decorate the cake with almonds or nuts of your choice. Bake for 40-50 minutes at 350°F or till a skewer inserted comes out clean. Allow it to cool then slice and enjoy.
Serve Zafrani Mawa Cake along with Hot Coffee Latte and Namak Para during a cold winter evening.

title: Tawa Crispy Pomfret Fry Recipe
instructions: Wash and clean the pomfret fish properly and make gashes on both sides using a knife.
Add turmeric powder, salt, lemon juice and crushed black pepper, rub it onto the fish, and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Make a smooth paste by mixing curd, red chilli powder, fennel powder, finely chopped coriander leaves and curry leaves, then rub this masala paste onto the fish, pushing it into the gashes.
Marinate the fish for 1 hour in the refrigerator. Heat a non‑stick pan and add melted butter.
Place the pomfret in the pan and fry for 8–10 minutes on one side over medium flame. Carefully flip and cook the other side for another 8–10 minutes, avoiding overcooking.
Drain any excess butter with a paper towel and serve the fish hot.
Serve the Tawa Fry Crispy Pomfret with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or any chutney of your choice.

title: Thandai Phirni Recipe - A Delicious Indian Rice Dessert
ingredients: 1/2 tablespoon black pepper powder (for thandai powder)
instructions: Wash and soak the rice for about 1 hour.
Drain and pat dry the rice on an absorbent cloth, then blend it into a coarse powder.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, add the milk and bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and add the ground rice, stirring until the milk thickens.
Continue stirring while the mixture simmers; when it starts thickening, add the sugar and cardamom powder.
Add the thandai powder and stir for another 5 to 10 minutes until the mixture attains full flavor and a pudding-like consistency.
Turn off the heat, let it cool completely, then pour the phirni into small earthen pots and refrigerate for 3 to 4 hours.
Garnish with chopped pistachios, almonds, saffron strands (and rose petals if desired).
Serve chilled, optionally with snacks like dahi vada or pyaaz kachori during Holi.

title: Gulab Jamun Bread Pudding Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Gulab jamun (homemade or market ones)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C for 10 minutes.
Grease a baking dish with baking spray or butter. Line the tray with gulab jamuns, breaking them with your hands.
Mix eggs, milk, sugar, bread, almonds, and cardamom powder, and blend everything.
Place the mixture on top of the gulab jamuns and bake for 15–20 minutes until a golden crust forms.
Serve Gulab Jamun Bread Pudding as a dessert, e.g., after Paneer Pav Bhaji.

title: Beetroot Greens Rice Recipe
instructions: Remove the beetroot green leaves from the beetroot.
Wash the leaves thoroughly by rinsing in cold water 4-5 times, then finely chop the onion and leaves along with the tender pink stem.
Separate the pink stem from the greens and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add onion, ginger and garlic and sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the chopped pink stem, sprinkle some water, and cook for about 5 minutes. Then add the greens and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add red chilli powder and coriander powder and sauté for about 3 minutes. After that, add the cooked rice and mix well with the mixture.
Cover the pan with a lid and let the rice cook on low flame for 5 minutes.
Adjust salt to taste, turn off the heat, transfer the beetroot greens rice to a serving plate and serve.
Serve the beetroot greens rice with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita for lunch.

title: Prawns In Mashed Green Grams Soup Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Green Moong Sprouts, boiled and mashed
3 cups Vegetable stock, or more as needed
1 tablespoon Corn flour, dissolved in 1 tablespoon water
instructions: To begin making the Prawns In Mashed Green Grams Soup recipe, for green gram sprouts, you have to soak green grams in water in advance and then tie them in thin muslin cloth.
Keep them in warm place and after 2 days, you will get nice and big sprouted green grams. Wash them well and separate out the peels.
Boil a cup of sprouted green grams till soft. I pressured cooked them for up to 1 whistle to make the process faster.
You can also cook them in a saucepan with enough water for about 35-40 minutes. Remove and mash with spoon or fork. It need not be very smooth paste.
In a saucepan, heat oil and saute bay leaves, peppercorns and cloves for few seconds on medium heat.
Saute grated ginger garlic on low heat till the raw smell goes away. Add sliced onions and fry till they turn golden.
Once they turn golden, add diced tomatoes and let them cook till it becomes soft. It will take an additional 5 minutes.
Blend this in the blender along with celery cubes and mint leaves. Add very little water while blending if required.
In the same saucepan, add a tablespoon of oil and add shrimps. Fry for few seconds. Sprinkle with some pepper powder, chili flakes and saute them till they turn pink.
Once they turn pink, add vegetable broth and cook the shrimps covered for about 10 minutes. Remove the cover and pour in the tomato paste along with mashed green grams. Mix it well.
Add salt and let it come to a complete boil. Add corn starch if you want your soup to be very thick. Mix well and keep the heat on low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and pour it in a serving bowl, garnish with some mint leaves and sprinkle some black pepper powder. Serve hot.
Serve Prawns in Mashed Green Grams Soup along with Farm Fresh Vegetarian Pasta Salad for a weeknight dinner.

title: Methi Lachha Paratha Recipe
ingredients: Extra Virgin Olive Oil , as needed
instructions: To begin making the Methi Lachha Paratha wash the methi leaves thoroughly and chop them finely.
In a mixing bowl, add the all the ingredients like the chopped methi leaves, whole wheat flour, green chillies, garlic, salt and knead it into a soft dough. Rest it for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, knead for a minute again until the paratha dough is soft and pliable. Divide the dough into 10 equal portions.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat. If you are using a cast iron skillet, then grease the skillet well and allow it to preheat.
Keep some flour aside for dusting while rolling the dough. Shape each dough portion into a round ball, press it between the palm of your hands.

Dust the dough with flour and roll it into a 6-inch diameter circle. Smear some ghee or oil on this rolled out the dough. Dust some flour over the ghee. This flour and ghee will help the Methi lachha paratha split itself into layers.

Begin folding the Methi lachha paratha dough like an accordion, similar to a saree pleat. Start from one end of the dough and reach the end. The dough is essentially made into a pleat. Once you have stacked up all the pleats one over the other, roll the dough into a swiss roll.
Flatten the pleated swiss roll between the palm of your hands, dust in flour and roll into a 4 to 5-inch diameter circle. You will be able to see the layers very clearly.
Place the rolled layered Methi Lachha Paratha on the preheated skillet. Cook on medium heat on both sides for a few seconds, then smear ghee and cook until golden brown and cooked through completely.
Proceed the same way with the remaining portions of the paratha dough.
Serve the Methi Lachha Paratha along with Mango Achar, Paneer Butter Masala or your favorite Vegetarian Gravy for a weeknight dinner or even for breakfast along with a chutney.

title: Sweet Potato And Bitter Gourd Kulambu Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Sweet Potato And Bitter Gourd Kulambu recipe, soak tamarind in water and squeeze the juice.
Take a wok/kadai or a clay pot and add oil. Temper with mustard seeds, bengal gram, methi seeds, peanuts, red chilli and dry coconut.
Add onions and fry them until translucent. Add sweet potato and fry until they are half cooked.
At this stage add bitter gourd pieces and cook for 2 minutes. Add curry leaves, salt, turmeric powder, sambar powder & coriander powder. Mix them well.
After 2 minutes, add tamarind water and cook until the mix thickens. Once it is done, switch off the heat.
Sweet Potato Bitter Gourd Kulambu is ready to serve. Serve Sweet Potato And Bitter Gourd Kulambu along with Steamed Rice, Chow Chow Thoran and Elai Vadam for a weekday meal.

title: Mango Ladoo Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup desiccated coconut, plus more for dusting
instructions: Preheat a thick‑bottomed pan and dry‑roast desiccated coconut for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to brown or burn it.
Add the mango pulp to the pan and stir until well combined.
Stir in condensed milk, cardamom powder, and nuts; mix until the mixture becomes a little gooey, stirring continuously to avoid charring.
Continue cooking until the mixture reaches a doughy consistency, then turn off the heat and let it cool slightly.
When cooled, shape small balls between your palms and roll each ladoo in desiccated coconut powder; repeat for all ladoos.
Serve the mango ladoos as a dessert or snack.

title: One Pot Spicy Vegetable Pulao Recipe with Coconut Milk
ingredients: 1 cup Basmati rice (or any other rice)
instructions: Wash the rice under water and set aside.
Prepare the coconut milk, chop the vegetables, and have all spices ready. You can cook the pulao in a pressure cooker or a saucepan.
Pound the ginger and garlic together to make a paste.
In the pressure cooker or saucepan, heat a teaspoon of oil, add the ginger‑garlic paste and sauté for a few seconds, then add cloves, cardamom, cinnamon stick and bay leaf.
Add the vegetables, green chillies, rice, turmeric powder, salt and coconut milk. Add an additional cup of water, stir everything together and cover the pot.
If using a saucepan: turn the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to low, cover and simmer until the rice absorbs all the water.
Turn off the heat and let the pulao rest for at least 10 minutes before serving.
If using a pressure cooker: turn the heat to high, place the weight and cook until you hear two whistles, then turn the heat to low and simmer for about 3 minutes before turning off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, then open the cooker.
Stir in the ghee and serve the spicy vegetable pulao hot, optionally with raita or kadhi.

title: Eggless Thandai Cookie Recipe
instructions: Lightly dry roast almonds, poppy seeds, pepper, cardamom and fennel seeds in a wide pan; once cool, grind to a fine powder to make thandai masala.
In a bowl, sift together all purpose flour, corn flour, baking soda, salt and thandai masala.
Beat sugar and butter together with a hand blender on medium speed until creamy.
Add the flour mixture into the sugar‑butter mixture and add rose water.
Mix everything to form a thandai cookie dough, divide into two parts, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for at least one hour.
After chilling, take out the dough and roll into a round shape of desired thickness using a little flour.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Cut out the cookies with a cutter and arrange on a greased baking tray, leaving a 1/2 inch gap.
Sprinkle pistachio slices on top of each cookie and bake in conventional mode for 10–12 minutes until brown and golden.
After 15 minutes, remove the cookies from the oven and place them on a wire rack to cool; they will firm up while cooling.
Once completely cool, store the thandai cookies in an airtight container.
Serve eggless thandai cookies with hot masala chai (and optionally pan‑fried onion pakora) as an evening snack.

title: Pan Fried Avocado Kofta Recipe
ingredients: Sooji (Semolina/ Rava) , or breadcrumbs for dusting
1 teaspoon Tamarind Water , or lime juice
instructions: Peel the avocado and mash it well with a fork.
Heat a skillet and add a teaspoon of oil. Fry grated carrots on medium high heat for about a minute and remove from the heat.

In a bowl add the cooked carrot, chopped onions, grated ginger, garlic, green chilies and coriander leaves. Add all the spices, sprinkle some salt, add tamarind water and lemon juice. Mix everything well.
If the mixture is too soggy and cannot make Koftas, add a tablespoon of rice flour and mix so that the moisture gets absorbed.
Take slightly bigger than ping‑pong size ball of the mixture on your palm and start shaping them into an oval. Keep them aside on a plate.
Place some semolina or breadcrumbs on a plate and dust all the Koftas well, coating with semolina on all sides.
Heat a skillet and add oil. Place all the prepared kebabs on the skillet keeping some space between each. Let them fry on medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Turn them over and fry on the other side. Once they are browned and crisp, remove onto a plate and serve these crisp koftas hot as an appetizer.
Serve Pan Fried Avocado Kofta along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai for your evening break.

title: Indian Masala Curry Powder With Red Chillies Recipe
instructions: Remove the stem of dry red chillies. Dry roast red chillies in a wide pan for about 3 minutes on low flame until crisp, then transfer to a wide plate to cool.
Add coriander, cumin and mustard seeds to the pan, along with garlic pods (do not remove the skin).
Roast for about 5 minutes until a nice aroma arises, maintaining low heat and mixing continuously to avoid burning.
Take out all the spices onto the wide plate and roast fenugreek seeds for a couple of minutes until roasted, then switch off the heat. Allow all the spices to cool.
Add the cooled ingredients to a blender with a pinch of turmeric and salt.
In a mixer grinder, blend to a fine powder and store in an airtight container after spreading the masala on a plate for a few minutes.
Toss idlis with the Indian Masala Curry Powder and ghee to prepare podi idlis; it can also soothe a sore throat when eaten with rice topped with hot ghee.

title: Stuffed Palak Paneer Paratha
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Kasuri Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves), crushed
Nutralite Classic Spread, to cook parathas
instructions: Knead a soft yet pliable dough using the dough ingredients and set aside for 20 minutes.
Mix all the filling ingredients well, taste and adjust salt and chilli as needed.
Divide the dough into equal portions and set aside; also portion the palak paneer stuffing mixture and set aside.
Roll out each dough portion into a 3‑inch diameter disc, place the stuffing in the centre, bring the edges together and pinch to seal.
Dust the sealed paratha on dry flour and roll to a larger circle, taking care that the filling stays inside.
Repeat the stuffing and rolling process with the remaining dough and filling portions.
Preheat a tawa over medium heat, melt Nutralite spread, and cook the stuffed parathas on both sides until browned and crisp.
Serve the stuffed palak paneer parathas with Boondi Raita and Aam Ka Achaar.

title: Dry Fruit Barfi Recipe - A Healthy Dry Fruit Halwa
ingredients: 1 cup Dried Figs, dried, finely chopped
instructions: Roast pistachios, cashew nuts, almonds and walnuts in ghee until lightly golden and fragrant; set the roasted nuts aside.
Line an 8‑inch square pan with aluminum foil and set aside.
Blend the finely chopped dates and figs with 1 tablespoon of milk until smooth.
Sauté the blended paste in a nonstick wok for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it turns golden brown and pulls away from the sides of the pan; add the roasted nuts and mix well.
Pour the dry fruit barfi mixture into the prepared pan, smooth the surface, and let it cool completely until it firms up slightly.
Cut the hardened barfi into equal squares and store in an airtight container for festivals or as a snack for children.
Serve the dry fruit barfi as a festive treat or tea‑time snack.

title: Oats Banana And Apple Porridge Recipe For Babies And Toddlers
instructions: To begin making Oats Banana And Apple Porridge Recipe, we have to first peel, core and cut the apples.
Add the cut apple pieces into a pressure cooker with a tablespoon of water and pressure cook for 1 whistle.
Release the pressure immediately, open the lid and keep aside. Take the apples out and mash them with the back of a fork.
Alternatively, cook the apple pieces on the stove: add the apple pieces into a pot of water (enough to cover them) and boil until soft.
Peel the skin of a banana, place it on a plate and mash it with the back of a fork.
In a pan, add a cup of water and when small bubbles appear, add the instant oats (oatmeal) and stir until you get a liquidy porridge-like texture. Turn off the heat.
Add the mashed apples and bananas to the oat porridge and mix well until you get a uniform consistency.
Your baby's Banana Apple Oats porridge is ready to be served.
Serve Banana Apples Oats Porridge to your babies or toddler who are over the age of 8 months for a lunch or snack.

title: Palak Paneer Kathi Roll Recipe - High-Protein Spinach Cottage Cheese Wraps
ingredients: 1/2 cup Spinach Leaves (Palak), washed, chopped & pureed
1/2 teaspoon Black Salt (Kala Namak), to taste
instructions: To begin making the Palak Paneer Kathi Roll Recipe, first prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.

Puree the spinach along with the green chili and keep it aside. In a mixing bowl, add the wheat flour, palak puree, cumin powder, salt and knead to make a smooth dough, adding any additional water if required.
Finally, add a teaspoon of oil and knead well to make a soft palak paratha dough. Divide the paratha dough into 4 portions.
Heat a skillet over medium heat to make the palak parathas. Dust the dough with flour and roll to make a large circle of 8 inch diameter.

Cook the paratha on the heated skillet. Drizzle ghee or oil over the palak paratha and cook on both sides until cooked through. You will see light brown spots on both sides. Cook all the parathas in a similar way and stack them.
The next step is to make the Paneer Bhurji. Mix all the paneer bhurji filling ingredients, check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste. Keep aside.
To make the Onion Garnish, toss all the garnish ingredients in a bowl and keep aside.
To make the wrap, spread the palak paratha on a flat surface. Add a tablespoon of the mustard sauce on each paratha and spread well.
Spoon the Paneer Bhurji mixture on one side, add a small portion of the onion garnish, and roll into a wrap.
Cut the roll in half if desired. Serve hot or warm.
Serve the Palak Paneer Bhurji Roll along with Cold Coffee Smoothie or Cantaloupe Pomegranate and Mint Juice for breakfast or evening snack.

title: Teekha Murgh Recipe
ingredients: Curd (Dahi / Yogurt), as required for marination
instructions: Marinate the chicken with curd, salt and turmeric powder for at least 1 hour; set aside.

Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add nigella (kalonji) seeds and fennel seeds; after 10 seconds add onions and sauté until translucent, then add ginger and garlic paste and sauté for a few minutes.
Grind tomato and chillies into a paste; after about 2 minutes add the paste to the pan along with cumin powder, salt and black pepper powder, mix and add the marinated chicken.
