Mix everything well, cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked (about 20-25 minutes), stirring occasionally; add water to achieve desired consistency.
Crush the dry roasted curry leaves by hand and sprinkle them over the chicken gravy, then mix.
Cover and let the dish rest for 10-15 minutes for the flavors to blend before serving.
Serve Teekha Murgh with Garlic Naan and Boondi Raita, optionally alongside Pakki Mutton Biryani.

title: Thandai Mousse Cake Recipe With A Delicious Cardamom Sponge
instructions: To begin with Thandai Mousse Cake, preheat the oven at 180 degree celsius.
Line a 8 inch round cake pan with parchment paper, grease the sides and keep it aside.
In a mixing bowl sift dry ingredients for the cardamom sponge cake - flour, baking powder, baking soda, mix well and keep it aside.
Take another mixing bowl, add in oil, sugar, curd, vanilla essence, cardamom powder and mix well using a hand whisk or electric beater.
Now, fold in the dry mixture into the wet cake mixture little by little, use a spatula to fold in, do not over mix.

Once the batter is ready, transfer it into the lined pan and bake the cardamom sponge cake for around 25 minutes at 180 degree celsius or until a skewer inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean.
When the cardamom sponge cake is done, let it cool for 10 minutes within the pan, then demould the cake and let it cool on a wire rack.
Meanwhile prepare the Thandai mousse, chop white chocolate and place in a bowl.
Now take a small saucepan and bring the fresh cream to a boil on a low flame.
Pour the hot fresh cream on the white chocolate and let it sit for few mins, then using a spatula, stir the mixture and mix well until the chocolate completely melts and you get the ganache.
Keep the ganache to cool down, meanwhile beat the heavy whipping cream to stiff peaks.
When the ganache fully cools down, add in the thandai syrup and mix well.
Once it is done, start adding whipped cream to the white chocolate thandai mixture and fold lightly using a spatula. Be gentle and fold without deflating any air from the whipped cream.
To assemble, take a 8 inch/20 cm round springform pan and place the prepared cake into it.
Now top the cake with prepared mousse mixture and tap it so that the mixture settles. Smoothen the top with an offset spatula.
Garnish the Thandai Mousse Cake with chopped almonds, pistachios, saffron and keep in the refrigerator.
Chill the mousse cake for four to five hours, preferably overnight.
Once you are ready to serve, loosen the sides using a knife and demould the cake.
Serve Thandai Mousse Cake as an indian dessert for your parties like Holi or Diwali.

title: Stuffed Mussels Recipe
instructions: Open the mussels and remove the meat; wash and keep about 15-20 shells for stuffing later.
In a medium wok over medium heat, add oil and sauté garlic and onions until translucent. Add green chilies, thyme, and red chili powder and fry for a few more seconds.
Add the mussel meat, cover, and cook on medium heat for 7-8 minutes. Sprinkle turmeric powder and mix.
Add ketchup, mix, and remove from heat. Scoop a teaspoon of the mixture into each mussel shell and place the stuffed shells on a baking pan.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on each stuffed shell and broil at 350°F for about 4 minutes. Remove and serve immediately.

title: Pineapple Mawa Delight Recipe
ingredients: 6 Sponge cake slices, or mawa cake
instructions: Grate the pineapple.
Heat the grated pineapple with a little water and cook on medium heat until the water evaporates and the pineapple is cooked.
Add sugar to the cooked pineapple, then add saffron and cook until all the water evaporates.
In a separate pan, add ghee and cardamom powder, stir briefly, then add nuts and raisins on low heat and cook until lightly golden, then remove from heat.
Mix the fried nuts and raisins with the pineapple and sugar mixture.
Add fresh cream and grated khoya, cooking for about 5 minutes until everything is well incorporated.
Turn off the heat, crumble the sponge cake or mawa cake into small pieces and mix well with the pineapple delight.

title: Badam Ki Kheer Recipe - Spiced Almond Milk
ingredients: 1 cup Whole Almonds (Badam), soaked in warm-hot water for about 30 minutes
Whole Almonds (Badam), finely chopped, as required
Cashew nuts, finely chopped, as required
instructions: Soak the almonds in warm to hot water for about 30 minutes, peel the skin, and grind the soaked almonds with the cardamom and a little milk into a fine, smooth paste; mix the saffron in 2 tablespoons of milk and set aside.
Boil the remaining milk with the jaggery, ensuring the jaggery dissolves completely, then add the ground almond paste to the boiled milk.
Continue to boil on low flame after adding the almond paste, stirring very frequently to prevent burning.
Allow it to boil for a few minutes, then top the kheer with chopped almonds, cashews, pistachios, and saffron strands.
Serve Badam Ki Kheer as a dessert.

title: Cabbage & Dal Stuffed Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Cabbage (Patta Gobi/ Muttaikose), finely chopped
instructions: To begin with Cabbage & Dal Stuffed Paratha firstly boil the dal by adding 3 cups of water. Once it is boiled, drain the water and keep the dal aside. The dal water can be used to make the dough.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a kadhai. After the oil gets heated, add cumin seeds.
When the cumin seeds crackle, add finely chopped onion and fry till onion turns pinkish.

Once it is done, add the chopped garlic and green chilies and stir. Now add finely chopped cabbage, stir and close the lid of kadai, stirring in between. Let the cabbage get cooked for about 10-15 minutes.
After the cabbage softens, add the dal and mix well. Take care not to add any water as the stuffing should be dry.
Add turmeric and red chili powder and stir. Add salt according to your taste and mix well.
Switch off the gas and let the mixture get cooled down.

Mould wheat flour to make a firm dough. Add salt and oil to wheat flour and mix. Mould it into a soft yet firm dough by adding water little at a time. Cover the dough with muslin cloth for 30 minutes.
Make small balls from the dough of equal size. The size should be a little bigger than the table tennis ball.
Roll the dough ball into a little bit of dry wheat flour and roll it into small thick flat round shape. Place 2 tablespoon of the stuffing on it and close from all sides.
Dust it in dry whole wheat flour and roll it into bigger round shapes, just like a chapati.
If you see any air bubbles while rolling, simply pat it gently with your fingertips.
Then apply 1 teaspoon ghee on the pan and place the paratha on it.
After 2-3 minutes, apply 1 teaspoon ghee on the upper side and turn. Fry for another 2-3 minutes and your paratha is ready.
Serve Cabbage & Dal Stuffed Paratha hot with Lauki Raita and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Green Moong Sprout Salad Recipe With Vegetables- No Onion No Garlic
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Green Moong Sprout Salad, chop and keep the vegetables ready.
In a mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients—green moong sprouts, carrots, capsicum, tomato, lemon juice, salt, and coriander leaves. Toss and serve.
Serve the Green Moong Sprout Salad along with Watermelon and Cucumber Gazpacho and Boiled Egg Mayo Sandwich for a light summer meal.

title: Ajwaini Kache Kele Ki Sabzi Recipe -Plantains Cooked With Caraway Seeds
ingredients: 3 Raw Banana, cut into small cubes
2 teaspoons Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped for garnish
instructions: Peel the outer covering of the raw bananas, chop them into cubes and place them in a bowl of water until further use, to avoid the discolouration.
Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add the cumin seeds and let it splutter. Slightly crush the caraway seeds between your palms and add them to the oil to flavour it.
Drain the raw banana cubes from water and add them to the pan and mix well. Add the coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, season with salt and mix well.
Let the raw banana cook to three‑quarters with the lid closed. Then keep sautéing the plantains until they are well cooked and turn crispy on the outside, about 5 minutes.
Add the amchur powder and coriander leaves, mix the sabzi well and switch off the heat. Transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve the Ajwaini Kache Kele Ki Sabzi with Phulka and Dal Palak for lunch.

title: Sweet Potato & Beetroot Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Sweet Potatoes (about 2), cooked and mashed
1/4 cup Corn flour or gram flour (besan)
instructions: Heat a teaspoon of oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan; add the chopped onions and garlic and sauté until the onions are translucent and soft. Add the grated beetroot, turmeric powder, salt and cumin powder.
Cover the pan and simmer on low heat until the beetroot becomes soft.
Turn off the heat and let the mixture cool completely. Once cooled, stir in the corn flour, mashed sweet potatoes, coriander leaves and green chilies; adjust salt and mix well.
Shape the mixture into small lemon‑sized balls and set aside.

To bake: place the balls on a baking tray and bake in a pre‑heated oven at 200 °C for about 30 minutes, or until they turn golden brown. Test with a toothpick; serve with your favorite sauce (e.g., Schezwan, honey mustard, or sriracha).

To steam‑pan (paniyaram) cook: grease the paniyaram pan with a little oil, place the balls in the holes, and heat on medium. After 3–4 minutes the tops steam and the bottoms brown; flip each ball and roast the other side until both sides are browned and crisp.
Remove the cooked balls, arrange on a serving tray, and serve as an appetizer with your preferred sauce.

title: Kesar Mawa Gujiya Recipe- Gujiya Stuffed With Saffron, Khoya & Nuts
ingredients: A generous pinch saffron strands (for syrup)
instructions: Add flour and melted ghee in a wide bowl and mix them together using your fingertips.
Add warm water little at a time, knead into a soft yet stiff dough, cover with a wet cloth and set aside.
Crumble the mawa with your fingers, heat a non‑stick pan, add the crumbled mawa and stir continuously on low flame.
When the mawa turns smooth, add raisins, chironji nuts, cardamom powder and powdered sugar, mix well, remove from heat and let it cool completely.
To make sugar syrup, combine sugar and water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, stir until it reaches two‑string consistency, then turn off the heat and add saffron strands, letting it sit.
Divide the gujiya dough and mawa mixture into equal portions, roll each ball into a 3‑4 inch circle and brush the edges with water.
Place a portion of the mawa mixture in the centre of each dough circle, fold in half, seal and press the edges firmly.
Heat oil in a deep‑fry pan, and once hot, fry the gujiyas until golden brown; remove and drain on kitchen tissue paper.
After the gujiyas have cooled slightly, soak them in the kesar sugar syrup for 10‑15 minutes.
Remove the gujiyas from the syrup, garnish with slivered pistachios, saffron strands and dried rose petals, and serve.
Enjoy Kesar/Mawa Gujiya as a festive snack or sweet accompaniment with Thandai or Masala Chai.

title: Curd Rice Recipe With Mint Flavour
instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 15 minutes.
In a deep pan or rice cooker, add 1 1/4 cups water, the soaked rice, mint leaves and a pinch of salt; then cook.
Cook the rice until soft, then whisk the curd (no water) to keep it thick.
Lightly mash the cooked rice; once completely cooled, stir in the whisked yogurt and milk.
For tempering, heat oil in a tadka pan and add mustard seeds until they splutter.
Add fresh mint leaves, grated carrot, chopped coriander leaves, curry leaves and salt; stir for a few seconds and turn off the heat.
Pour the seasoning into the curd‑rice mixture, mix well, and refrigerate for about 30 minutes until cold.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and additional mint leaves.
Serve the curd rice with carrots and coriander fritters or Mangalorean style biscuit roti, or pack it for a lunch box.

title: Foxtail Millet Khichdi Recipe with Batata Aloo Nu Shaak
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Whole Black Peppercorns, coarsely pounded
instructions: Note: The method will produce a mushy texture; adjust water consistency to your preference.
Wash the millet and dal and place them in a pressure cooker.
Add 3-1/2 cups water, turmeric powder, grated ginger, salt, and cinnamon stick; cook until you hear three to four whistles, then turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally.
Open the cooker and stir the khichdi to combine all ingredients.
If using a saucepan, place the millet and dal in the pan, add water, turmeric powder, ginger, salt, and cinnamon, and cook until the khichdi is mushy; adjust salt to taste.
For the seasoning, heat ghee in a small tadka pan, add cumin seeds, crushed black peppercorns, and asafoetida, stir for a few seconds, then pour the tadka over the cooked khichdi.
Serve the Foxtail Millet Khichdi with Batata Nu Shaak (Aloo Tamatar Sabzi).

title: Dry Fruits Meetha Paneer Paratha Recipe
instructions: Prepare all ingredients, powder the nuts and set them aside.
In a large mixing bowl, combine all the filling ingredients to form a crumbly mixture and keep aside.
In another bowl, add the wheat flour and a pinch of salt, add water little at a time and knead into a smooth dough; set aside.
Divide the dough into 6 to 8 portions.
Roll each portion into a 3‑inch circle, dust with flour to prevent sticking.
Place a large spoon of the dry‑fruit paneer mixture in the center, bring the edges of the dough towards the center to seal the filling.
Flatten the stuffed paratha, dust with flour and roll it out to a thin paratha, not too thick.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat and cook the paratha on both sides with ghee until browned and cooked through.
Repeat the same process with the remaining parathas and serve hot or cold.
Serve the Dry Fruits Meetha Paneer Paratha with Aam Chunda pickle and Rose Lassi.

title: Cucumber Pineapple Raw Mango Salad Recipe
instructions: Wash and cut the cucumber, pineapple, and raw mango.
In a mixing bowl, add the diced cucumber, pineapple, and raw mango, then mix in the green chutney and mint leaves.
Mix the salad until well combined.
Set aside for a while to let the fruits and vegetables absorb the flavour, then serve the salad chilled.
Serve the cucumber pineapple raw mango salad with Thakkali Sadam (spicy tomato rice) and Papad Raita for a complete meal.

title: Dal Chawal/ Paruppu Sadam -Baby & Toddler Recipe above 10 months
instructions: Wash and pressure cook moong dal in a quarter cup of water along with a pinch of turmeric.
Pressure cook for 3 whistles and release the pressure naturally; remove the dal from the pressure cooker and set aside.
In the same pressure cooker, add 1/4 cup of rice with 1/2 cup water and pressure cook for 3 whistles.
After the 3 whistles, turn off the flame and release the pressure naturally.
Place a pan on low heat, add a teaspoon of butter, and once melted, add the cooked moong dal and a pinch of salt.
Mix the dal well and simmer for 2 minutes, then turn off the flame.
In a bowl, add the cooked rice and cooked dal, mix thoroughly; for a more mashed consistency, use a potato masher on the rice before adding the dal.
Optionally add a little salt and a dollop of ghee, then serve warm to the baby/toddler.
Serve Dal Chawal/ Paruppu Sadam to babies/toddlers above 10 months along with a vegetable like carrot poriyal or buttered mashed potatoes.

title: Sprouted Moong And Onion Fritters Recipe
instructions: To begin making Sprouted Moong And Onion Fritters Recipe, prep all the ingredients.
Take a large mixing bowl, add all the ingredients except oil and mix well with water to make a thick batter, adding water little by little to prevent lumps.
Heat oil in a kadai. Once the oil is hot, drop spoonfuls of batter into the oil and deep fry them until golden brown and crisp.
Drain the fritters on a kitchen towel once done.
Serve the Sprouted Moong And Onion Fritters with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, tomato ketchup, and optionally alongside Ginger Cardamom Chai or a tea sandwich.

title: Peas Pulao Recipe -  North Indian Matar Pulao
instructions: To begin making the Peas Pulao Recipe, wash the rice and soak in water for about 20 minutes.
Heat a pressure cooker with ghee on medium flame, to this add the whole spices - bay leaf, cumin seeds, star anise, cardamoms, cloves and cinnamon stick.
Once these spices begin to sizzle, add the sliced onions, and cook them only until they begin to sweat. This will take about a minute.
To this add the salt, green peas and drained rice.
Top the matar pulao with about 2-1/2 cups of water, depending on the age and quality of your rice and close the pressure cooker.
Pressure cook for about 3 whistles and turn off the flame, allow the pressure to release naturally. Once done, open the pressure cooker, give the Matar pulao a stir and fluff up the rice.
Transfer the Matar Pulao to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve Peas Pulao Recipe along with Smoked Dhaba Dal, Masala Lachha Paratha, Achari Paneer Masala, Easy Creamy Chicken Curry, Pickled Onions, and finish the meal with Rose Gulkand Phirni.

title: Egg Korma Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making Egg Korma Recipe, hard boil the eggs firstly. Keep all the ingredients ready.
Heat oil in a pan, once the oil is hot, on low medium heat, add cumin seeds, and let them splutter.
Once they splutter, add chopped onion and green chillies and saute on medium heat until onions are light brown in colour and starting to caramelize.
Immediately add ginger garlic paste and saute on low medium heat until the raw aroma of ginger and garlic goes away.
Now add the chopped tomatoes and saute till the tomatoes become soft and get cooked properly.
Turn off the flame and let the mixture cool down a bit.
Grind it to a corse paste in a mixer grinder.
Heat same pan again, and add the ground paste in it.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala and salt to taste.
Mix well and add about half cup water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Add coconut milk to the mixture and let it cook for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Now add boiled eggs and cook for 2 minutes more.
Egg korma is ready,garnish it with chopped coriander and serve hot.
Serve Egg Korma Recipe in lunch or dinner with Butter Naan Recipe or Methi Lachha Paratha Recipe and another side dish like Fansi Muthia Nu Shaak Recipe.

title: Cucumber Tomato Corn Peanut Salad With Lemon Recipe
instructions: Chop all the vegetables and keep them ready.
Heat a saucepan on medium heat, add the corn kernels along with 1/2 cup of water and boil for 6‑8 minutes.
Turn off the flame, drain the water and set the corn aside.
In a mixing bowl combine cucumber, tomato, onion, corn, green chilli, and peanuts.
Squeeze in the lemon juice, sprinkle salt and add coriander leaves and give it a mix.
Toss it nicely, check for salt and adjust accordingly. Sprinkle with toasted and crushed peanuts and serve.
Serve the salad along with tawa paratha, Dal Palak, and some steamed rice.

title: Poha Stars Recipe (Poha Potato Fritters Flavoured With Kasuri Methi)
instructions: Soak poha for 5 minutes in water and then drain the water.
Add the bread crumbs and all the other ingredients and mix to form a firm dough; add water if required.
Take a small ball of mixture, press it slightly, and use a star‑shaped cookie cutter to shape it; repeat with the remaining dough.
Heat oil in a deep‑frying pan; when hot, carefully place the poha‑potato stars in batches and deep‑fry until golden brown and crisp, avoiding overcrowding.
Remove the fried stars onto a kitchen towel to drain excess oil.
Serve the poha stars with tomato ketchup, date and tamarind chutney, and a smoothie such as cocoa banana almond date smoothie.

title: Steamed Rice Recipe - Pressure Cooker & Sauce Pan Methods
instructions: Rinse the rice well under running water. Place one cup of washed rice along with two cups of water in the pan of the pressure cooker.
Keep the weight on, cover the pressure cooker. Cook on medium high heat; after the first whistle, turn the heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally. Once the pressure is fully released, open the cooker and use the rice as desired.
Rinse the rice well under running water and optionally soak for about 15 minutes. In a heavy‑bottomed saucepan with a light‑fitting lid, combine 2 cups water, the washed rice and salt (optional).

Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat. When it begins to boil, turn the heat to low, cover with a lid and simmer for about 12 to 15 minutes, or until the rice is cooked and all water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest, covered, for at least another 10 minutes. Before serving, fluff the rice with a fork.

title: Baked Modak and Karanji/Gujiya Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Cashew nuts, cut into small pieces
instructions: To begin making the Baked Modak and Karanji recipe, first make the dough by mixing together maida, ghee and pinch of salt.
Add water little at a time, till you get nice dough like chapati dough. Knead it well, cover it with wet cloth and keep it covered for 10 minutes.
The next step is to make the stuffing. On a skillet, melt ghee and fry sooji until fragrant. Add coconut and fry for around a minute or until it slightly changes its colour.
Add sugar, mix and cook on low flame for around a minute. Add dry fruits and cardamom powder. Mix everything well and cook for another minute and switch off the stove. Keep the mixture for cooling.
Now let’s make karanji and modak. First make small balls out of dough. Size of a golf ball.
Roll them one by one with rolling pin to make thin discs.
Keep these discs covered with moist cloth or moist kitchen paper towel to keep them moist.
For karanji, place a spoon full of the filling at the centre of each disc and fold the circle in a half-moon shape and with the help of fork, press the folded side to make nice design.

For making modak, the same process but hold the disc on your left palm in the shape of a bowl and just place the filling in the centre of the disc and merge all the sides of the disc to make in the shape of a fresh fig.
After you make all the karanjis and modaks ready, lets bake them.
Place them on the baking trays lined with greased aluminium foil (Greased with little ghee).
Brush each karanji and modak with ghee to give them a nice glaze after they are baked.
Bake them at 350 degree Fahrenheit preheated oven for 20 minutes.
After every 10 minutes, flip them and bake on the other side. After 20 minutes, remove and keep on the cooling rack.
Once cooled down completely, store in the air tight container. Serve Baked Modak and Karanji along with some snacks such as Moong Dal Mini Samosas and Chana Chaat to your guests or family members.

title: Lal Bhoplyacha Bharit Recipe (Red Pumpkin Raita)
ingredients: 250 grams Kaddu (Parangikai/ Pumpkin), peeled and chopped
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few, chopped for garnish (optional)
instructions: Steam or microwave the pumpkin until soft, then drain any excess water.
Roughly mash the pumpkin pieces, leaving some chunks, and let it cool.
Add curd, salt, sugar, groundnut powder and mix everything well.
In a tadka pan, heat ghee, add cumin seeds, hing and green chillies; pour this tempering over the raita, mix and serve.
Serve Lal Bhoplyacha Bharit with roti, Bhagar, Sabudana Khichdi, Kala Vatana Amti, or Phulkas.

title: Rajma and Corn Salad Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kashmiri Rajma, or regular rajma
instructions: To begin making the Rajma and Corn Salad Recipe, wash and soak the rajma overnight.
Pressure cook the rajma with water for about 8-10 whistles. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
In a pan, boil water on medium flame, add the corn and cook until the kernels swell up. Drain out the water and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine the boiled rajma and corn, chopped mint leaves and jalapenos.
For the dressing, in a small bowl, add salt, pepper, lemon juice, sugar, vinegar, jeera powder, red chili powder, crushed garlic & olive oil.
Just before serving, toss in the dressing into the salad.
Serve Rajma and Corn Salad Recipe as a side dish along with Panchmel Dal and Phulka for a weeknight dinner.

title: Karupatti Coffee Recipe
instructions: Take all the ingredients mentioned for spice powder in a blender and grind them to a fine powder; store in an airtight container for later use.
In a saucepan, take a cup of water and add a teaspoon of the spice powder along with palm jaggery; mix and bring the mixture to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 2 to 3 minutes; strain the coffee into a mug and serve.
Serve Karupatti Coffee to friends and family to cure a cold or enjoy on a cold night.

title: Thandai Kulfi Recipe - Holi Recipe
instructions: Make a paste of the Thandai masala by blending all the listed ingredients in a mixer grinder and set the paste aside.
Condense the milk: heat the milk in a heavy-bottomed saucepan and bring it to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring almost continuously, until the milk reduces to less than half its original volume.
Continue stirring continuously as the milk thickens to prevent it from sticking to the bottom and burning.
Stir in the sugar until fully dissolved, then add the Thandai paste mix and whisk well (hand blender optional).
Turn off the heat, let the kulfi mixture cool completely, then pour it into molds about three‑quarters full, seal them airtight and freeze for at least fifteen hours.
Run the frozen kulfi molds under water to release the kulfis onto a plate.
Serve the Thandai Kulfi as a dessert.

title: Baked Vegetable Salad Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Potatoes (Aloo), chopped or 6 to 7 baby potatoes cut in half
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and ensure all ingredients are prepped before starting.
In a mixing bowl, combine the roughly chopped vegetables with crushed garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper; mix well to coat evenly.
Spread aluminium foil on a baking tray, cover it, and place the seasoned vegetables on the foil.
Bake the vegetables at 180°C for about 20 minutes, or until they are roasted thoroughly.
In a separate bowl, whisk together English mustard sauce, honey, vinegar, water, and dried oregano to make the dressing; toss the baked vegetables with this dressing.
Add chopped parsley and toss everything together; the baked vegetable salad is now ready to serve.
Serve the baked vegetable salad with Roasted Tomato and Pumpkin Soup for a healthy, light weekday dinner.

title: Tulsi Kashayam Recipe (Kaada) - Herbal Drink From Tulsi
instructions: To begin making the Kashayam Recipe, prep all the ingredients and keep them handy.
Add water into a saucepan, tear the tulsi leaves and give it a brisk boil.
Once the color of the water changes, add the black pepper powder, ginger powder, palm sugar (Panakalkandu), boil for a few more minutes and turn off the heat.
Serve the Tulsi Kashayam hot and have it 2 to 3 times a day to get maximum relief from cough and cold.

title: Nongu Paal Recipe - Palm Fruit Drink
instructions: Boil the milk along with cardamom powder and let it cool down completely.
Peel the palm fruit.
Blend 5 of the fruits in a blender until smooth and finely chop the remaining into small pieces to add the delicious chew in the drink.
Add the pureed fruit and chopped palm fruit, sugar or honey, and rose water to the cooled milk and mix well until the sugar dissolves.
Chill the palm milk in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 hours. Just before serving, add some ice cubes and top it with pomegranate seeds and rose petals.
Serve Nongu Paal Recipe - Palm Fruit Drink on its own or with Dry Fruit Barfi (Halwa) Recipe (A Healthy Dry Fruit Snack) or Papaya Orange Pomegranate Salad Recipe with Roasted Peanuts.

title: Bhindi Masala Curry Recipe
instructions: To begin with the Bhindi Masala Curry, wash the bhindi and dry them properly or you might face the problem of stickiness. Cut the ends of the Bhindi and and chop them into half.
Heat a non stick pan and drizzle some oil, Add the bhindi, then sprinkle some salt and sauté them for 20 minutes on medium flame. Once done you can take them out and keep it aside.
Meanwhile in the same frying pan, add a tablespoon oil. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds, when it start splutter add chopped garlic and sauté them.
Now add sliced onion and add 1 teaspoon sugar and a pinch of salt. The caramelization takes place as the sugar is added and the salt helps the onions to cook fast.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté them for a minute until the tomatoes have softened.
Turn the heat to low and cook and add the cooked bhindi and stir well until the Bhindi's are mixed well into the sauteed mixture.
Add all the spice powder - red chilli powder, turmeric, sambar powder, salt and stir well. Check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste. Once done, turn off the heat and serve.
Serve the Bhindi Masala Curry along with Tawa Paratha, Methi Kadhi and Palak Raita to make your meal complete or you can pack for your lunch box as well.

title: Horsegram Dal Recipe - Kulith/Kollu Dal
instructions: To begin making the Horsegram Dal, first step is to soak horse gram in 1 cup of water overnight.
Next morning, in a pressure cooker, add the soaked horse gram dal and 3 cups of water. Add salt to taste and turmeric powder.
Close the cooker with a lid and pressure cook for 6-7 whistles. Let the pressure release naturally.
Heat ghee in a heavy bottomed pan on medium flame. Once the ghee has melted, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add asafoetida and let it cook for few seconds.
Add ginger garlic paste, sauté it and cook on medium flame until the raw aroma disappears, about a minute or two.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add tomatoes, red chilli powder, salt and coriander powder. Cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the mashed horse gram into the pan, cover and let it simmer for about 3 to 4 minutes.
Turn off the flame and garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve Horsegram Dal along with Phulkas, Aloo Baingan Ki Sabzi and Boondi Raita for a complete and wholesome meal.

title: Broccoli Puree With Butter and Garlic Recipe (For Babies/toddlers over 7 months)
instructions: Wash the broccoli florets thoroughly.
Add half a cup of water to a pressure cooker, add the broccoli florets and a pinch of salt, then close the lid.
Let 2 whistles out and release the pressure immediately to retain the green color and nutrients.
In a pan, melt a teaspoon of butter, add chopped garlic and sauté until the raw smell disappears.
Add the broccoli florets and sauté for 2 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Let the broccoli cool down.
Add the cooled broccoli to a mixer and grind until smooth puree.
Serve the broccoli puree with garlic and butter to babies/toddlers over 7 months for lunch or dinner.

title: Savoury Carrot And Coriander Pancakes Recipe
instructions: In a large bowl, add all the ingredients except the buttermilk and mix evenly.
Gradually add the buttermilk, stirring slowly to form a thick batter that is slightly thicker than regular pancake batter.
Heat a griddle over medium heat, pour a ladleful of batter onto it, gently spread into a medium-sized circle, and dot with a little butter on the sides.
Cook for two minutes on medium heat, then flip and cook for another two minutes until done.
Serve the savoury carrot and coriander pancakes with tomato garlic chutney or spiced hung curd dip.

title: Tamarind Chilli Potato Recipe
instructions: To begin with the Tamarind Chilli Potato, first lets boil the potatoes and keep them aside.
In a pan add some oil and potatoes once the oil is hot. Saute them till they turn into golden brown.
Take the potatoes from the pan and keep it aside.
In the same pan add some more oil and add carom seeds once the oil is hot.
Now add cashew nuts and saute till it becomes golden brown, now add garlic and onions and saute till they are transparent.

It is time to add the red chillis and curry leaves, leave it for a minute so the spice is induced in the onions. After this add tamarind paste and some sugar, combine the entire mixture and add salt as per your taste.
As the tamarind paste cooks well you can add the potatoes and allow it to cook for 2 – 3 minutes.
Put off the flame and add the coriander leaves at the end, taste and add more salt if needed.
Your Tamarind Chilli Potato is ready, transfer it to a serving plate and serve them.
You can serve the Tamarind Chili Potato as a starter or even as a subji for roti, phulka and naan.

title: Healthy & Delicious Jamun Fruit Smoothie - Black Plum Smoothie Recipe
instructions: Blend deseeded jamun fruit and honey in a mixer or blender until smooth.
Add milk, curd, and crushed ice, then blend for a few seconds.
Pour the smoothie into tall glasses and serve immediately.
Serve the smoothie with a Grilled Spinach and Cottage Cheese Sandwich for a wholesome breakfast.

title: Beet and Avocado Chapati Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Whole Wheat Flour, more for dusting
2 tablespoon Extra Virgin Olive Oil, more for cooking
instructions: To begin making Beet and Avocado Chapati, add whole wheat flour, cumin powder, sesame seeds, chili paste, ginger paste, coriander, mint, olive oil, salt, grated beetroot and mashed avocado to a mixing bowl; mix well and bring together using fingers or a dough hook on low speed.
Add water if necessary and knead to a soft dough; rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Knead briefly and divide the dough into equal portions, yielding about 14‑16 medium‑sized chapatis.
Roll each portion into a ball and flatten with the palm of your hand.
Dust the dough in flour and roll out into thin circles about 6 inches in diameter, dusting with additional flour as needed to prevent sticking.
Repeat rolling for the remaining dough balls.
Preheat a skillet, place a rolled dough on it, and when small air pockets appear, flip the chapati, smear about 1/2 teaspoon oil, and lightly press and turn with a flat spatula to cook.
Flip to the other side, press and turn similarly until brown spots appear; remove from heat and place on a flat plate.
Serve the Beet and Avocado Chapati with Punjabi Chana Masala and Masala & Plain Lacha Pyaz (pickled onions) for lunch or dinner.

title: Matar Pudina Oat & Broken Wheat Tikki Recipe
ingredients: 80 grams rolled oats or instant oats
instructions: Prepare all ingredients: boil the sweet potato, steam the peas, and have the rest ready.
In a food processor, add the boiled sweet potato, oats, paneer, steamed peas, grated ginger, green chilies, onion, mint leaves, and chaat masala.
Blend until the potatoes are coarsely mashed and the mixture comes together, stirring halfway through for even blending.
Transfer the dough to a bowl and adjust salt, keeping in mind the oats already contain some salt.
Grease your fingers with a little oil, shape the dough into bite‑size tikkis or lemon‑size balls, and set them on a tray.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat and add a little oil.
Place a few tikkis in the skillet, drizzle a few drops of oil on each, and cook on low to medium heat until browned and crisp on both sides. Remove onto paper towels and serve.
Optionally, shape the dough into cylinders, skewer them, and grill.
Serve the mint matar & pudina tikkis with sweet & spicy tomato chutney and a cooling yogurt dip, alongside masala chai or as an appetizer.

title: Chickpea Salad Recipe With Raw Mango
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked overnight
instructions: Wash and soak the chickpeas overnight.
In a pressure cooker, add the chana and water and pressure cook for 6 whistles on high flame, then reduce the flame and continue to cook for 15 more minutes; turn off the flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, drain the water, and transfer the chana into a bowl; set aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine the chana, onions, chopped green chilli, tomatoes, salt, and red chilli powder; stir well.
Add raw mango pieces, chaat masala, and lemon juice; toss the salad mix.
Garnish with chopped coriander and mint leaves.
Serve the Chickpea Salad With Raw Mango as a tea‑time snack with Masala Chai, Watermelon Carrot Radish Juice, or Baked Mathri.

title: Spicy Yogurt Chapati/Roti Recipe
instructions: In a large saucepan or vessel, add yogurt, cumin seeds, chilli paste, coriander leaves, salt, and oil.
Whisk everything until smooth and lump-free, then add 1/2 cup of water and mix together.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, lower the flame, and pour the wheat flour into the centre, cooking on low heat for about 4 to 5 minutes.
Turn off the flame and vigorously mix with a wet wooden stick or spatula until the mixture comes together, about 2 minutes.
Cover the mixture and let it cool slightly until it can be handled by hand.
Knead thoroughly for 5 to 6 minutes, then divide the dough into 10 equal portions.
Knead each ball for 20 seconds and shape it into pedas (round flattened balls).
Roll the pedas into chapatis by dusting with wheat flour; optionally stack them with flour between each chapati.
Roast each chapati on a hot tava on both sides, smearing oil or ghee as needed.
Serve the Spicy Yogurt Chapatis with Panchmel Dal and Bharwa Besan Mirch Sabzi, or pack for a lunch box.

title: Grilled Cherry Tomato Pickle Recipe
instructions: Take a bowl, add halved cherry tomatoes, some salt, one tablespoon oil, black pepper powder, and toss to coat evenly.
Heat a grill pan and, when hot, grill the tossed tomatoes on the preheated pan for 20-25 minutes.
Heat a kadai and dry‑roast mustard seeds, fennel seeds, and carom seeds together until fragrant; let cool, then coarsely grind the spices in a blender and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add grilled tomatoes, salt (if required), ground spices, chopped mint leaves, sugar and vinegar; mix well and turn off the heat.
Allow the mixture to cool, then store the cherry tomato pickle in an airtight container.
Serve the grilled cherry tomato pickle with steamed rice, coriander chicken roast, or lahsuni palak dal.

title: Whole Wheat Masala Papdi Recipe / Kadak Puri Recipe
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Whole Black Pepper Corns, coarsely pounded
instructions: To begin making the homemade Papdi, we will first have to make the dough.
Mix all the flour, ajwain, pepper, oil and salt together. Add water a little at a time and knead the papdi dough until it becomes firm and smooth and firm. It should not be soft.
You can make 30 small balls and roll them out thin about 1-1/2 inches in diameter and 1/8 th thickness.
Or you can divide the dough into two portions and roll out into a big large circle and cut small rounds using a cookie cutter.
Make sure the papdi you roll out are thin.
After rolling prick the papdi / kadak puri with a fork all round to prevent it from puffing when baked.

Place the oil for deep frying over medium heat. To check the right temperature, put a small tiny ball of dough into the oil and if it comes sizzling up, then you know the oil is heated to the right temperature.
Slide the papdi into the oil in small batches and deep fry until golden brown.
Drain the excess oil by placing in a kitchen paper. You can optionally at this stage sprinkle chaat masala on the top to make it chatpata.
Allow it to cool and store the Papdi / kadak puri in an airtight container.
Use the Papdi to make chaats like Mumbai Style Bhelpuri, Sev Papdi Chaat, and many more. You can innovate your topping, maybe like chilli-cheese, or chilli corn and cheese, etc.

title: Raw Papaya, Apple & Carrot Salad Recipe
instructions: Prepare all the vegetables and fruit for the salad.
In a mixing bowl, add the grated carrot, papaya, apple, and green chilies; mix well. Add lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toss well, check for salt, then add pounded peanuts and mint leaves, toss once more and serve.
Serve the Raw Papaya, Apple & Carrot Salad with Horsegram Dal and Ragi Tawa Paratha for a diabetic‑friendly meal.

title: Scrambled Eggs With Ridge Gourd Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 2 teaspoon Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped for garnish
instructions: Wash, peel the ridge gourds and dice them; set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add ginger and green chillies and sauté for a minute.
Add onions and curry leaves and sauté until onions turn translucent. Add ridge gourd, coriander powder, turmeric, red chilli powder, season with salt and mix well.
Cook the ridge gourd for about 5 minutes, then break the eggs into the pan and mix well.
Stir continuously until the eggs and ridge gourd combine and the scramble is cooked through.
Turn off the heat and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve the scrambled eggs with ridge gourd sabzi alongside Panchmel Dal, phulkas, or bread toast.

title: Cucumber, Red Radish, Tomatoes & Onion Salad Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Cucumber, Red Radish, Tomatoes & Onion Salad Recipe, first get all the ingredients chopped.
In a large mixing bowl, add all the vegetables—cucumber, radish, tomatoes, onions, and add salt, pepper, green chilies, lemon juice and coriander. Toss the salad well and serve it fresh.
Serve the Cucumber, Red Radish, Tomatoes & Onion Salad along with Golden Glow Smoothie Recipe for a simple evening snack during the summer season.

title: Mango Tofu Smoothie Recipe
ingredients: Kiwi, few pieces or any other fruit
instructions: Place all the ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth.
Serve in a tall glass or jar and top with black sesame seeds, basil leaves, and kiwi.
Enjoy the mango tofu smoothie as a breakfast or post‑workout protein‑rich meal.

title: Moon Biscuits Recipe (Moon Shaped Baked Cookies)
instructions: Take maida, milk powder, and baking powder and combine them well.
Add the softened butter, confectionery sugar (powdered sugar) and vanilla extract into a bowl.
Combine the butter mixture well and add the dry ingredients to make a dough.
Preheat the oven to 350°F, roll out the dough with a rolling pin and cut it into moon-shaped cookies using a round cookie cutter.
Arrange the cookies on a baking tray, set the cooking time to 15 minutes, bake, then cool them before serving.
Serve the moon biscuits during tea time.

title: Rava Ladoo Recipe | Sooji Laddu Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Sooji (Semolina/Rava), roasted & lightly pulsed to coarse powder
1/2 cup Ghee, plus more if required
instructions: Heat a teaspoon of ghee in a small pan on low heat; roast the cashew nuts until lightly golden and crisp. Add the raisins and sauté for a few seconds. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Preheat a pan over medium heat and roast the rava/sooji/semolina for about 4 to 5 minutes until aromatic, ensuring it does not brown or burn.
Turn off the heat and keep the roasted sooji aside.
In a mixer grinder, add the sugar and blend to make a fine powder.
Add the roasted sooji/rava, desiccated coconut, and cardamom powder to the powdered sugar and blend to make a coarse powder.
Grinding the rava/sooji a little gives a better texture and bite for the ladoo.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sugar‑rava‑coconut mixture with the roasted cashew nuts and raisins.
Stir the mixture well.
Add the melted ghee and mix thoroughly, then shape the warm mixture into 20 equal‑size balls.
If the mixture does not hold, add a tablespoon of milk or additional ghee (or both) to help it come together.
Compress the mixture firmly with your fingers to form solid balls.
Store the shaped Rava Ladoos in an airtight container for about two weeks.
Serve the Rava Ladoo as a dessert.

title: Carrot Cucumber Tomato Salad with Lemon and Coriander Recipe
instructions: Get all the ingredients ready.
Combine the grated and chopped vegetables—carrots, cucumber, tomatoes, coriander leaves—along with lemon juice and salt to taste.
Toss well and serve immediately, or chill for best flavor.
Serve the salad with Asian Style Chicken Noodle Soup or Peanut & Ginger Pasta (with vegetables & lime) for dinner.

title: Baked Potato & Peas Samosa With Phyllo Pastry Recipe
ingredients: 2 Potatoes (Aloo), boiled, peeled and finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Baked Peas Samosa with Phyllo Dough Recipe, firstly we will boil the potatoes. Add potatoes in the pressure cooker with water and cook for about 2 whistles. Meanwhile, steam the green peas and keep it aside.
Once the potatoes are boiled, peel the skin and chopped them finely. Keep it aside.
The next step is to make the filling for the Samosas. Heat a teaspoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan.

Add the chopped onion and saute it until soft and tender. Once the onions are ranslucent, add the boiled and chopped potatoes, steamed peas, coriander powder, cinnamon powder, garam masala, dry mango powder, kashmiri red chilli powder and cook it for about 2 to 3 minutes.

This process will coat the potatoes and the peas with the samosa masala. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust it to suit your taste. Once done, turn off the heat and allow the samosa filling mixture to cool a bit.
Preheat the oven to 190 C. Grease a baking sheet with ghee or butter and set it aside.
The next step is to shape the phyllo dough into a samosa along with its filling.
Spread out one phyllo pastry sheet on a clean, dry work surface. Brush it with some butter or ghee. Keep the remaining phyllo sheets covered with a damp towel, else they will dry out.
Fold the sheet half lengthwise and fold an end to make a small triangle. The folded sheet will approximately be 2 inches wide.
Take care to handle the phyllo sheet gently, as they can tear apart quickly.

Spoon a small portion of the filling towards one end of the phyllo sheet leaving an edge space. Take the right corner and fold diagonally to the left, enclosing the filling and forming a triangle. Now take the left corner, along with the filling and fold diagonally to the right.

Keep folding in this way until you reach the end of the strip. Brush the outer surface with more butter or ghee. Place the potato and pea filled Phyllo Pastry Samosa onto a baking sheet and cover with a damp cloth.
Proceed the same way until you fill the remaining pastry sheets with the potato pea filling.
Arrange the Phyllo Pastry Samosas on the baking sheet and bake them in the oven for about 10 to 15 minutes, until you notice the crust is golden brown in colour.
Once completely baked with a golden crust, remove the samosas from the oven, allow them to cool down just slightly.
Serve the Phyllo Pastry Potato & Pea Samosas along with Green Chutney or a Yogurt Dip as a tea time snack or even as an appetizer for parties.

Note: You can also shape the Samosas into a square. The shape all depends on how well you can handle the phyllo pastry and shape them. With practice you will get a fair idea and develop the skill. Be prepared for some of the phyllo sheets to tear while you shape them.

title: Potato Latkes Recipe
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Whole Black Peppercorns, freshly ground
Extra Virgin Olive Oil, for shallow frying
instructions: Peel, wash and grate the potatoes into thin long strands using a food processor or the thickest side of a grater; move hands in long swift motions to get longer strands.
Add the finely chopped onion to the grated potatoes and let them stand in a strainer to drain the water for 15 minutes, or squeeze out the water by pressing the potatoes in a muslin cloth.
Let the water stand still for 10 minutes, then drain the liquid on top and add the starch collected at the bottom back to the potatoes.
Whisk together 1 egg, salt and pepper; add this egg mixture and the grated garlic to the potatoes.

In a cast‑iron pan, add 2 tablespoons of olive oil and spoon the potato mixture into 4‑5 rounds. Press down gently with the back of a flat spatula and fry each side for 3‑4 minutes until evenly browned.
Serve the latkes with sour cream, unsweetened apple sauce, tomato ketchup, a slice of toast, and fresh orange juice.

title: Indian Style Beetroot Soup Recipe
instructions: Dice tomatoes into small pieces and put them in an oven proof pan. Add crushed garlic onto the tomatoes and drizzle some olive oil.
Roast the tomatoes in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Make a puree of tomatoes once they have cooled down in a mixer grinder.
Take a big pan for making soup and pour some oil or butter and heat it up. Add bay leaf, cloves, black peppercorns, cinnamon into the pan and keep stirring till the aroma of the spices appears.
Add finely chopped onion into the pan and cook it for 4-5 minutes till it becomes tender and pink.
Add grated beetroot and tomato puree into the pan and cook for 5 more minutes. Now add vegetable stock, salt and pepper into the pan and cook the soup for 10 to 15 minutes.
Taste the soup and adjust the seasoning as per your taste. Let the soup cool down and make a smooth puree using a blender. Strain the soup and keep it aside.
Heat a saucepan and add the strained soup. Serve it hot, garnish with some sesame seeds and coriander leaves.
Serve Indian Style Beetroot Soup along with Bean Sprout & Corn Salad for a weekday dinner, or as a starter before your Indian meal.

title: Nankhatai Recipe - A Spiced Eggless Indian Cookie
ingredients: 3 tablespoons Curd (Dahi / Yogurt), or more if required
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and prepare a baking sheet greased with butter or ghee.
In a stand mixer or a large bowl, combine all the dry ingredients together. Add the wet ingredients and beat until a dough forms.
Place the dough in cling wrap and refrigerate for about 3 hours until chilled (optional, for crunchier cookies).
Divide and shape the dough into lemon‑size balls (about 25‑30), give a slight thumb impression in the center, and dip the balls in crushed nuts.
Arrange the Nankhatai on the baking sheet and bake in the preheated oven until lightly golden brown, about 15‑20 minutes.
Serve the spiced Nankhatai with hot chai or store in an airtight container for later.

title: Coconut Kewra Drink Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon fresh coconut, chunks/tender coconut chunks
instructions: To make this super easy Coconut Kewra Drink, get the ingredients handy first.
Mix all the ingredients including fresh coconut chunks, kewra essence, and tender coconut water (excluding crushed ice) and shake well for a minute.
Serve the coconut kewra drink with crushed ice topped on it.
For best enjoyment, serve the drink on a hot day alongside Lemon Grass Oats & Almonds Pudding with Macerated Berries.

title: Buttered Green Peas with Cumin Powder - For Babies & Toddlers 10 Months and Above
instructions: Wash the green peas. If using frozen peas, ensure they are completely thawed.
In a pressure cooker, add one cup peas with a cup of water and a pinch of salt, then close the lid.
Pressure cook the peas for 2 whistles, then turn off the heat and release the pressure immediately.
Remove the peas from the pressure cooker and set them aside.
In a pan, melt 1/2 teaspoon of butter. Once melted, add the cooked peas to the pan.
Sprinkle a pinch of cumin powder over the peas and toss them well in the butter.
Turn off the heat after 2-3 minutes.
Serve Buttered Green Peas to your baby toddler above 10 months of age as a finger food or healthy snack.

title: Chicken In Curry Leaves Gravy Recipe
ingredients: 1 Onion, finely chopped, few more onion rings to garnish
instructions: To begin making Chicken In Curry Leaves Gravy Recipe, in a mixer grinder, grind curry leaves, coriander leaves, mint leaves and green chillies to a fine paste by adding a little water.
Heat oil in a kadai on a medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add onions and sauté on a low heat till the onions turn soft.
Add ginger garlic paste and sauté till the raw smell goes. This will take about a minute or two.
Add the ground paste of mint, green chillies and curry leaves, mix well. Add salt and about 1 cup of water and bring to a boil.
When it comes to a boil, add the chicken pieces and mix well. Continue cooking for 5 more minutes, then reduce heat and close with a lid.
Cook for about 15 minutes or till the chicken is tender while stirring occasionally.
You will get a thick gravy. Add lemon juice at this stage and stir till combined.
Check for seasoning and adjust salt and add white pepper powder to suit your palate. Let it cook for about a minute.
Switch off gas and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve Chicken In Curry Leaves Gravy along with Steamed Rice and Burani Raita. You can also serve this with Phulka and Kachumber Salad for a weekday meal.

title: Egg Stuffed Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Oil or ghee (for making parathas, as required)
instructions: Make a soft dough of whole wheat flour with salt, adding a little water at a time, and let it rest.
Break the eggs into a bowl, whisk well, and add the chopped onion, green chilies, coriander leaves, pepper, and salt; whisk again and set aside.
Take a lemon‑sized ball of dough, dust with a little flour, and roll it into a large circular disc.
Apply a little oil or ghee, fold the disc into a semi‑circle, then fold it into a triangle.
Dust the triangle with flour and roll the mini triangle into a bigger triangle.
Repeat the process to prepare the rest of the paratha triangles.
Heat a skillet, place a prepared triangle on it, cook until the bottom is done, then flip and cook the other side halfway.
Gently lift one pocket of the triangle and pour a ladleful of the egg mixture into it.
Add a little oil or ghee, flip gently, and cook on low heat until the egg inside is cooked.
Add a little oil or ghee on top, flip again, and cook until both sides are golden brown; remove and repeat for remaining parathas.

title: Lemon Oats Recipe
instructions: Wash chana dal well and soak in enough water for about 10 minutes.
Dry roast oats on low flame until a nice fragrant smell is released.
Heat oil in a wide pan, add mustard seeds and wait until they crackle; then add urad dal and soaked chana dal and fry till golden.
Add finely chopped onions, green chilies, curry leaves, grated ginger and sauté until onions turn translucent.
Add turmeric powder, salt and mix well; then add water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, add roasted oats, mix ensuring no lumps form, cover and cook for 3–4 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and cook for another 3 minutes uncovered.
Garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves, roasted peanuts, and some grated coconut.
Serve Lemon Oats with Masala Chai and a bowl of fruits for a healthy breakfast.

title: Poha Breakfast Bowl Recipe With Sprouts & Crunchy Peanuts
instructions: Wash the poha two to three times and drain water.
Mix salt, lemon juice and sugar with a fork and keep aside.
In a deep pan, add oil and once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds, curry leaves. Once it crackles, add onion and sauté for a minute on low heat.
Add the diced potatoes, salt (only as per the potatoes because salt in the poha has already been added) and turmeric powder. Cover and cook until the potatoes are cooked.
Add poha and mix through. Cover and let it cook for another minute or so. If the poha becomes very dry and is still thick, sprinkle some water, cover and cook for a minute. Keep aside.
For spicy peanuts, heat oil in a small kadai and add peanuts. Let them roast on low heat until slightly browned.
Add salt, red chili powder, chaat masala, black pepper powder, cumin powder. Mix well and switch off the flame.
For sprouts salad, in a mixing bowl, mix sprouts, tomatoes, onion, lemon juice, salt, coriander, black pepper and mix well.
Use a peeler/mandolin to get vertical carrot strips. Roll each strip and mix with sprouts salad.
For coconut chutney, grind together coconut, green chilies, salt, lemon juice, sugar with very little water until a smooth paste is formed.
To assemble, take a bowl and place hot poha, spicy peanuts, sprouts salad, carrot roll-ups, some fresh coriander, with a heapful of coconut chutney.
Serve Poha Breakfast Bowl Recipe With Sprouts & Crunchy Peanuts with Mango Tofu Smoothie Recipe in the morning.

title: Phool Mathri Recipe
ingredients: Lukewarm Water, for kneading the dough
instructions: To begin making the Phool Mathri recipe, In a bowl add maida, ajwain, salt and ghee. Mix it and knead a tight dough using lukewarm water.
Cover it with a kitchen napkin and keep aside for 10 minutes. Make equal size balls from dough and roll every ball into 4" diameter. For perfect shape we can use a cutter or a lid.
Pinch every roll with the help of plucker to give it a phool/flower like shape. Keep pinching in layers.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan. Deep fry all mathri on medium flame till golden brown in colour. Take them out on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil. Crispy and tasty Mathri are ready to serve.
Serve Phool Mathri along with Poha Chivda and Masala Tea for your tea time break.

title: Makki Paneer Pakora Recipe
instructions: In a small mixer jar, grind fennel seeds, green chilies, and ginger without adding any water to a coarse paste and set aside.
Add the corn to a food processor and grind to a coarse paste without adding any water.
Heat enough oil in a kadai over medium flame for deep frying.
In a medium bowl, combine the ground corn, prepared ginger‑green chilli paste, grated paneer, chopped onions, coriander leaves, curry leaves, gram flour, and salt; mix well.
If the batter is dry, sprinkle water as needed to achieve pakora batter consistency.
When the oil is hot, drop spoonfuls of the batter into the oil.
Fry the pakoras until golden, then remove onto a paper towel.
Repeat the process until all batter is used.
Serve the Makki Paneer Pakora with mint chutney or sweet dates chutney.

title: Carrot Poriyal/Sabzi for Babies and Toddlers 10 Months and Above
instructions: Wash and peel the carrot, then cut it into small pieces.
Add 2 tablespoons water and the chopped carrots to a pressure cooker with a pinch of salt.
Cook the carrots for one whistle, then release the pressure immediately and set the carrots aside.
In a pan, melt 1/2 teaspoon of butter over medium heat.
Add 1/2 teaspoon of mustard seeds to the melted butter and let them crackle.
Reduce the heat, add a pinch of asafoetida and the finely chopped curry leaves.
Add the cooked carrots to the pan and mix well.
Cook on low heat for a couple of minutes, then turn off the heat.
Serve the Carrot Poriyal as a baby/toddler food alongside curd rice and dal chawal.

title: Palak Raita Recipe (Spinach Yogurt Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Whole Black Peppercorns, coarsely pounded
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan; add the cumin seeds and allow them to crackle. Add chopped spinach and sauté on high heat until tender and most of the water has evaporated.
Set aside and allow the spinach to cool completely.

Whisk together the yogurt, cumin powder, red chilli powder, black pepper, and salt. Fold the cooled spinach mixture into the whisked yogurt. Transfer to a serving dish and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving.
Prepare the seasoning by heating oil in a tadka pan; add mustard seeds, white urad dal, curry leaves, and any other desired seasoning ingredients, and roast until they crackle.
Pour the roasted seasoning over the chilled Palak Raita.
Serve the Palak Raita with parathas or as a side dish with your main course.

title: Khajoor (Thekua) Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Khajoor (Thekua), in a wide bowl mix whole wheat flour with semolina, baking soda, sugar, cardamom powder and fried cashew nuts. Mix well. Add ghee slowly and using your fingers mix gently until you get coarse crumbs.
At this stage slowly add in milk and knead the dough gently with your fingers till you get thick firm khajoor dough. Cover the dough and allow it to rest for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a frying pan for deep frying. In the meanwhile using your fingers knead the dough once again until you get smooth dough easy enough to roll.
Apply ghee/oil to the rolling surface and rolling pin. Roll the dough to 1 inch thick circle.
Using a knife cut the Khajoor dough into diamond shapes. Alternatively you can use a cookie cutter to cut into desired shapes or make a pattern using a fork.
Deep fry the cut diamonds in the preheated oil, dropping them one by one into hot oil.

Fry till golden brown on both sides on low heat for 2-3 minutes and then on medium till done. Once done, remove the Khajoor cookies using a slotted spoon to remove excess oil. Cool and store in an airtight container.
The Khajoor (Thekua) can stay fresh for 2-3 days when stored in a clean and dry airtight container.
Serve Khajoor as a delicious snack along with masala chai on a breezy evening.

title: Cabbage & Buttermilk Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1 Cabbage (Patta Gobi/ Muttaikose), medium sized, shredded
instructions: Prep up with all the ingredients needed.
Heat oil in a Kadai on a medium flame and add mustard seeds.
Once mustard seeds splutter, add asafoetida, salt, and turmeric.
Add chopped cabbage and saute for 2 minutes.
Blend all the ingredients of buttermilk curry well with a wire whisk, then transfer the mixture to a pan.
Let the buttermilk mixture boil; once done, mix it with the cabbage curry and switch off the flame.
Garnish with coriander and serve with hot chapati, phulka, or plain cooked rice.

title: Restaurant Style Chicken 555 Recipe
instructions: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly under running water.
In a mixing bowl, marinate the chicken with red chilli powder, haldi, garam masala, rice flour, semolina, and salt; mix well and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a shallow frying pan.

When the oil is hot on medium heat, place the marinated chicken in the pan in a single layer with a little space between pieces; do not overcrowd; pour the marinated mix into the pan, frying in batches if needed.
Once the chicken is crisp and done, add a few curry leaves and sauté until the leaves become crisp.
Serve the chicken topped with the leftover masala and curry leaves.
Serve the chicken with a complementary meal such as Mughlai Style Chicken Changezi and Whole Wheat Onion Stuffed Kulcha.

title: Bhaji Vada Recipe (Lentil And Vegetable Fritters)
ingredients: Oil, for deep frying the fritters
instructions: To prepare the Bhaji Vada, first clean, rinse and soak the chana dal in water for about 30 minutes.
Drain the soaked chana dal in a colander and let it sit in the colander till all the excess water is drained.
In the food mixer grind chana dal into a thick paste of coarse consistency. Transfer the chana dal paste to a large mixing bowl.
Add the chopped amaranth leaves along with grated ginger, turmeric powder, red chili powder, green chili and salt. Combine well and check the taste to adjust the salt and spices.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. While the oil is heating shape the Bhaji Vada mixture into flat and round balls using your palm.
Gently place the fritter into the hot oil and deep fry until crisp and golden on both sides. Place the fried vadas in a plate lined with paper towel. Similarly fry the remaining Bhaji Vadas.
Serve Bhaji Vada with the Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and a hot cup of Masala Chai on a rainy afternoon or evening time.

title: Grilled Chicken With Vegetables Recipe
instructions: Begin by sautéing the vegetables.
Heat olive oil in a skillet or stir‑fry pan; add onion and pounded garlic and sauté for a minute or two.
Add all the vegetables—including red pepper, green pepper, broccoli, cherry tomatoes, onion and baby corn.)
Sprinkle some salt, cover the pan with a lid, and cook for 3–4 minutes.
Add mixed herbs and crushed peppercorns, mix well, and set aside.
Prepare the grilled chicken.
Pat the chicken breasts flat so they cook evenly.
Season with salt, crushed black pepper, dried basil leaves, and red chilli flakes; rub ginger‑garlic paste onto both sides.
Drizzle olive oil over the chicken and rub the mixture into both sides.
Heat olive oil in a skillet, place the chicken breasts in the hot pan, and cook for 4–5 minutes.
Flip the chicken breasts and cook the other side for another 4–5 minutes.
Check doneness by cutting against the grain; the interior should be white, not pink.
Serve the grilled chicken with vegetables, optionally alongside creamy garlic mashed potatoes, whole‑wheat seeded loaf, and homemade herb butter.

title: Moong Dal Pani Recipe- Dal Soup For Babies 6 months & above
ingredients: Few chopped Coriander (Dhania) Leaves (optional, from 8 months onward)
instructions: Pressure cook the Yellow Moong Dal with a pinch of salt and 1/2 cup water in a pressure cooker for 3-4 whistles; then turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, then transfer the cooked dal to a mixer grinder and blend into a smooth puree.
Prepare the tadka (tempering) for the soup.

Heat the ghee in a pan over medium heat, add asafoetida, turmeric powder, and cumin powder, and stir for a few seconds; pour the pureed dal into the tadka, bring to a quick boil, adjust consistency with additional water if needed, and turn off the heat.
Serve the Moong Dal Pani/Soup to the baby or toddler as a lunch or dinner.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve after 8 months of age.

title: Vegan Instant Coffee Recipe
instructions: Gather all ingredients. (You can see how to make almond milk at home if needed.)
In a saucepan over medium heat, warm the soy milk or almond milk with the sugar until the milk is hot and the sugar dissolves.
Remove the saucepan from heat and add the instant coffee powder to the sweetened milk.
Stir well until the coffee powder fully dissolves and forms an emulsion.
Pour the mixture into a large vessel or cup once or twice to mix well and create froth, then transfer to coffee mugs. Optionally sprinkle a little instant coffee powder on top before serving.
Serve the vegan coffee with cookies or alongside traditional breakfast items such as parathas.
Optional microwave method: pour a cup of soy milk into two coffee mugs, add sugar, heat on full power for one minute, then add instant coffee powder and stir until fully dissolved before serving.

title: Ginger Walnut Chutney
ingredients: 50 grams Walnuts, roasted (make sure it is not old and bitter)
instructions: Dry roast the ginger, walnuts, coriander seeds, methi seeds, cumin seeds, and whole black peppercorns as mentioned in the ingredients and allow them to cool.
Once cooled, grind all the ingredients together in a blender to make the ginger walnut chutney. Check for salt levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Serve the ginger walnut chutney with idlis, dosas, dhoklas, or mix it with hot steamed rice.

title: Apple Puree Recipe (Baby Food - 4 months onwards)
instructions: Wash and peel the apple, then cut into slices or chunks.
Add the apple slices to a pressure cooker, add 2‑3 tablespoons water, and pressure cook for 2 whistles; then cool under running water, or alternatively steam the apple pieces in a baby steamer.
You can also cook the apples in a covered pan until soft; cooking in a pressure cooker or steamer saves time and preserves nutrition.
Blend the cooked apple pieces in a portable blender or mixer grinder until smooth, adding more water to achieve a smooth, thin consistency.

title: Pumpkin Kofta Curry Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Pumpkin Kofta Curry Recipe, we will first pressure cook the pumpkin and potatoes with water and salt for about 4 whistles.
Allow the pressure to release naturally and drain all the water out. Mash the pumpkin and potatoes well.
Heat a sauce pan add the mashed pumpkin along with all the spice powders and keep sautéing until all the water has evaporated from it.

Make sure the mixture dries up. Add corn flour besan, Salt and coriander leaves to the mixture and bring all of it together. You will get a sticky dough. Switch off the heat, allow it to cool down for some time.
Meanwhile go ahead to make the curry, for that heat a sauce pan with oil, add onions, garlic and ginger and saute until it softens.
Add tomatoes and sprinkle little salt so that it will help to become mushy easily. After 5 minutes of sautéing add green chili along with all the spice powders except whole spice.
Saute until all the spice powders have mixed well. Switch it off and cool it down and blitz it in the mixer along with curd to a smooth paste. Keep it aside.
Shape the kofta dough into bite-size lemon balls and keep them aside. (About 8 to 10).

If you plan to use the Kuzhipaniyaram Pan; then place the kofta balls in the pan's cavities; drizzle the kofta's with a little oil and pan fry them until golden brown on both sides. You will have to flip the kofta balls so they fry on all sides evenly.
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan, add cardamom pods and cloves. Pour in the curry paste and add about 1/4 cup of water and bring it to a boil. Check for salt.
Once the Pumpkin Kofta curry has thickened, add in the pan fried Pumpkin Kofta Balls and simmer for another couple of minutes.
Transfer the Pumpkin Kofta Curry into a serving bowl, garnish by drizzling with fresh cream or just coriander leaves.
Serve the Pumpkin Kofta Curry along with phulka, naan or Tawa paratha along with a subzi by the side.

title: Vellarikka Kosumalli Recipe- South Indian Style Cucumber Salad
instructions: In a large mixing bowl add cucumber, carrots, coriander leaves, green chillies, salt to taste and lemon juice; stir and combine everything well.
Heat a tadka pan and add 1 teaspoon oil.
When the oil is hot add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and once they crackle add the chana dal and urad dal; when the dals turn golden brown add the dry red chillies and curry leaves.
Sauté everything for a few seconds and turn off the heat.
Add the tempering to the Vellarikka Kosumalli and combine; check the salt and adjust according to taste.
Serve the Vellarikka Kosumalli with steamed rice, Thakkali Vengaya sambar, and Elai Vadam.

title: Dahi Sabudana Recipe (Savory Tapioca Pearls Seasoned with Yogurt)
ingredients: 1 cup Curd (Dahi / Yogurt), fresh, whisked with 2 cups water (or use buttermilk)
instructions: To begin making Dahi Sabudana, first dry roast the sabudana in a heavy bottom pan for 8-10 minutes or till it just starts to pop (You can see that each grain will increase in size).
Cool and add it with the curd-water mixture in a mixing bowl.
Cover and keep aside for about 2 hours until the sabudana grains soften.
After 2 to 2½ hours, check the consistency of the sabudana (tapioca pearls) and add more yogurt/curd/water if required.
Add groundnut powder, sugar, salt and mix.
In a small wok/pan, heat ghee; add the cumin seeds and green chillies and allow them to crackle.
Turn off the heat and pour this tadka over the Dahi Sabudana.
Serve Dahi Sabudana for breakfast option on regular day or on fasting days. You can also serve Dahi Sabudana on its own or along with a sweet lime pickle.

title: Buttered Peas Puree Recipe For Babies Above 6 months
instructions: To begin making Buttered Peas Puree, pressure cook one cup of fresh peas with 2 tablespoons water and a pinch of salt for 2 whistles. Turn off the heat.
Release the pressure immediately by running the pressure cooker under water and drain the peas from the water.
In a pan, add half a tablespoon of butter and allow it to melt on low heat.
Once the butter has melted, add the cooked peas to it.
Saute for 2 minutes until the butter has coated the peas.
Turn off the flame and allow the peas to cool.
Add the cooled buttered peas to a mixer and blend until smooth.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve this peas puree to your baby.
Serve Buttered Peas Puree to your babies from 6 months onwards as lunch or an evening meal.

title: Kitkat Cake With Sponge Recipe (Eggless)
instructions: In a medium sized bowl, add milk, oil and sugar together and mix well; then add vanilla extract and mix.
In another bowl, sieve whole wheat flour, baking soda, baking powder and cocoa powder together; add this flour mixture to the milk-sugar mixture and whisk well.
Preheat the microwave to 180°C and bake the cake for 20-25 minutes; the chocolate sponge is ready.
To make chocolate ganache, boil fresh cream on medium heat, add the dark chocolate and mix well, then refrigerate for 1 hour.
Apply the chocolate ganache on the cake and refrigerate for 25 minutes; place KitKat bars around the cake, sprinkle M&M’s candies on top, and refrigerate for one hour to set.
Serve the KitKat Cake for birthday parties and special occasions.

title: Homemade Multigrain Baby Cereal Recipe (Baby Porridge)
instructions: Gather all the ingredients and blend the grains in a mixer grinder to a fine to coarse powder, depending on the baby's age.
If the cereal is for babies between 4 to 6 months, grind it into a fine powder; for older babies, make the powder coarser to adjust consistency.
Start with 2 tablespoons of the homemade baby cereal powder at a time when feeding the baby, as the quantity increases after cooking.
Place 2 tablespoons of the cereal powder in a saucepan, add 1/2 cup of water, and cook, stirring continuously, until it becomes a thick porridge without lumps.
After cooking, let the porridge cool slightly and stir in some breast milk (or milk of choice) to adjust consistency and improve taste.
Serve the homemade multigrain baby cereal to babies of all age groups and toddlers; you can also keep some for yourself as a wholesome breakfast with fruit.
Store any leftover cereal (about 300 grams total) in an airtight container in the refrigerator to keep it fresh longer.

title: Cinnamon Spiced Black Lemon Tea Recipe
ingredients: Lemon wedges or slices to garnish
instructions: To begin making Cinnamon Spiced Black Lemon Tea Recipe, keep all the ingredients handy.
In a carafe or saucepan, heat water on high heat with cinnamon and bring it to a rolling boil.
Once the water comes to boil, add the Assam tea leaves and squeeze in lemon juice and switch off heat. Keep the container covered for a minute.
Stir in honey, if you are using. Strain the tea, pour to tea cups and adorn it with a lemon slice/wedge to serve.
Serve Cinnamon Spiced Black Lemon Tea Recipe along with a Ginger Brandy Cookie Recipe, Tea Sandwich Recipe With Beets, Radish, Avocado and Arugula or Mumbai Style Spicy Murmura Recipe during evening.

title: Methi Aur Kache Kele Ki Sabzi Recipe-Fenugreek Greens & Raw Banana Stir Fry
ingredients: 1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), roughly chopped
instructions: Peel the skin of the plantains, chop them into cubes and place them in a bowl of water until further cooking to avoid oxidation.
Heat oil in a kadai, add the cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add the onions and sauté till they turn translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste and sauté for about a minute on low‑medium heat until the raw smell vanishes.
Add the tomatoes and green chilies, sauté until the tomatoes turn mushy.
Add the fenugreek leaves, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and turmeric powder (haldi) and mix well.
Let the fenugreek leaves wilt a bit; then drain the water from the raw bananas and add them to the kadai/pan. Add a bit of water if needed to help them cook evenly.
Season with salt and mix everything well. Cover and cook for around 10 minutes on medium heat.
Once the plantains are cooked, sauté until the water dries out. Switch off the heat.
Serve the Methi Aur Kache Kele Ki Sabzi with Lobia Masala, Tawa Paratha, and Carrot Cucumber Tomato Salad.

title: Pumpkin Thoran Recipe - South Indian Pumpkin Sabzi
instructions: To begin making the Pumpkin Thoran Recipe, prepare all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Into a mixer grinder, make a paste of the coconut, curry leaves, cumin seeds and green chillies. You don't need to add any water to grind to a paste.
Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Immediately, add curry leaves and stir for a couple of seconds.
Add finely chopped onions and saute the onions until they soften. Once the onions soften, add the slit green chillies.
Once the onions turn pink, add the cut pumpkin, turmeric powder, salt and stir. Sprinkle some water and cover the pan. Cook the pumpkin until it is soft and tender.
Stir in between, as required. Once the pumpkin is cooked, add ground coconut mixture and toss for a few seconds on high heat and turn off the heat.
Check the taste of the Pumpkin Thoran and adjust the seasonings accordingly. Once done, transfer the Pumpkin Thoran to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve Pumpkin Thoran with Cherupayar Curry, Steamed Rice and Moru Kachiyathu for a weekend lunch or dinner.

title: Ragi Or Finger Millet Powder/ Malt Recipe for Babies 6 Months & Above
instructions: Sprout the ragi seeds first.
After sprouting, transfer the sprouted ragi to a plate and dry it in shade for 4-5 hours.
Dry ragi seeds are roasted on a pan over low flame for 5 minutes to enhance nutritive value.
Cool the roasted ragi sprouts, then grind them into a fine powder using a mixer grinder.
Sift the ground powder through a sieve, retaining only the fine grain.
Store the ragi powder in an airtight container and use within 3 months.
Use the ragi flour to prepare ragi porridge/kanji, ragi dosa, or ragi & oats rava idli.

title: Carrots And Coriander Fritters Recipe
instructions: Grate the carrots and keep them aside in a bowl.
Add the chopped coriander leaves, green chilli, gram flour, season with salt and mix well.
Allow the carrots to release water, which will help bind the mixture together.
The batter will be a little thicker than the usual pancake batter.
Heat the skillet on medium flame and brush it with oil.
Pour a ladle full of the batter and carefully spread it out to form a small disc.
Pour oil over the sides and let it cook for 2 minutes.
When the bottom is cooked, flip over and cook the other side for another 2 minutes.
Remove the fritter onto a plate and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve the carrots and coriander fritters with milk or Dhaniya Pudina chutney as a snack.

title: Lauki and Whole Green Moong Dal Cheela Recipe
instructions: Soak whole green gram for 5 hours, then wash and drain.
Blend soaked green gram, ginger and chilies in a mixer to a smooth batter adding enough water; batter should be thicker than dosa batter as lauki will add water. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Grate the lauki and add to the batter. Add chopped coriander leaves, salt, rice flour and hing. Add water if needed to achieve dosa batter consistency.

Heat a tava or frying pan. Take a ladle full of batter, pour on the tava and spread in a circular motion. Drizzle a teaspoon of oil/ghee over the sides and cook till golden brown on both sides. Repeat for remaining batter.
Serve with Red Chilli Coconut Chutney or Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney, and optionally Masala Chai.

title: Besan Cheela Recipe Stuffed With Chatapa Paneer
ingredients: 6 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped (for batter)
6 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, finely chopped (for stuffing)
instructions: Combine all the ingredients for the Besan Cheela in a large bowl.
Gradually add water to make a smooth batter, ensuring the batter is not too watery or too thick; it should have a light spreading consistency.
Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Ensure the batter consistency is similar to dosa batter, a little lighter, and able to coat the back of a spoon thinly.
In a large mixing bowl, combine all the paneer stuffing ingredients and set aside, adjusting salt as needed.
Preheat a skillet on medium heat, pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan, and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin crepe/dosa.
Drizzle oil around the cheela and cook until the top no longer looks raw and the edges turn brown.
Flip the cheela and cook the other side for a few seconds.
Place the paneer filling in the center of the cheela, then fold it over.
