Transfer the stuffed Besan Cheela to a plate and serve hot.
Serve the Besan Cheela with Sweet And Spicy Tomato Chutney and Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Mooli Gobhi Aur Methi Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup methi leaves (fenugreek leaves), tightly packed
instructions: Cut cauliflower into small florets, soak it in hot water with turmeric and salt for 10 minutes to deworm it before use.
Heat mustard oil in a pan on medium heat, and let it smoke.
Add the garlic and saute until it turns golden.
Add the green chillies and saute for 30 seconds.
Add the cauliflower florets, sliced radishes, fenugreek leaves and mix well.
Add the turmeric, red chilli powder, season with salt and saute for a minute.
Let the vegetables cook in its own juices, occasionally stirring in between.
Once the vegetables are cooked well, switch off the flame.
Serve the Mooli Gobhi Aur Methi Sabzi along with phulkas and tomato onion cucumber raita, and carrot cucumber tomato salad.

title: Roasted Coriander Potatoes With Thyme Recipe
instructions: Par boil the potatoes in a pressure cooker for one whistle and let the pressure release.
Peel the skin and cut them in medium slices and keep aside.
Heat a wide heavy-bottomed pan on low heat and add butter. When it melts, place the sliced potatoes and cook until roasted, about 6 to 7 minutes.
Flip and cook on the other side, then keep aside.
In the same pan add the coarsely crushed whole coriander seeds and fresh thyme sprigs and sauté till aromatic.
Add the already roasted potatoes, season with salt and pepper, and give it a gentle toss.
Serve the roasted coriander potatoes with thyme, either hot or as a salad, optionally alongside Burnt Garlic Pasta With Mushroom.

title: Ragi Kanji / Porridge (Baby Food - 6 months onwards)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Ragi Flour (Finger Millet/ Nagli), Homemade powder
instructions: To begin making Ragi Porridge/Kanji, make sure to stock up on Ragi powder. Ragi powder is best made at home as it will not contain any preservatives or added sugar as in cases on store bought powders.
Here's how to make Ragi Powder at home.
In a small pan, add 1/2 cup water and 2 tablespoons of ragi powder. Stir well to combine before placing it on heat.
Once combined, place it on heat and keep stirring the baby ragi porridge continuously until it thickens.
Once done, turn off the heat and allow it to cool completely.
Add in the breast milk or formula and stir until all combines well.
If you add formula to the porridge, make sure to add a little water so that the formula melts into the porridge/kanji. Do not add formula directly to the pan while it's cooking.
Let the porridge be cooled to room temperature or warm, whichever way your baby prefers.
Serve Ragi Porridge/Kanji to your babies who are over 6 months of age.

title: Kabuli Chana & Moongphali Salad Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked overnight
instructions: Cook the soaked kabuli chana in a pressure cooker with water and salt for about 5 whistles until just done (soak overnight or at least 6 hours).
Allow the pressure to release naturally, drain the water, and keep the cooked chickpeas aside. Add whole peanuts with some water into the pressure cooker, sprinkle with salt, and cook for 2 whistles.
Once the peanuts are cooked, let the pressure release, then add the cooked peanuts and kabuli chana into a mixing bowl.
Add chopped onions, tomatoes, capsicum, green chilli, coriander leaves, amchur powder, red chilli powder, dry ginger powder, and salt; mix well. Drizzle fresh lemon juice, mix again, and serve fresh.
Serve the salad as a snack with evening Masala Chai or alongside Punjabi Kadhi Pakora and phulka.

title: Homemade Tamarind Paste Recipe
instructions: Heat about 2-3 cups of water in a saucepan; ensure the water is hot, not just warm.
Add tamarind to 1-1/2 cup hot water and keep the rest of the water aside (we'll need it later).
Let it sit for an hour or until the tamarind turns soft.
Squeeze off the tamarind well.
Pass the squeezed tamarind through a strainer into a heavy-bottomed pan.
Discard the seeds and any remaining discard left in the strainer.
Add the pulp back to the first pot where we added tamarind and water, then add water to the tamarind pulp again.
Let it sit for 10 minutes, squeeze it again and pass it through a strainer.
You will obtain a thick paste (if not, repeat the process once more).
Boil the paste over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring frequently, ensuring it does not burn.
Turn off the flame, cool the tamarind paste, and store it in a glass jar in the refrigerator.
The homemade tamarind paste will stay good for a month in an airtight jar; use a clean, dry spoon each time.

title: Matar Masala Tofu Recipe
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes.
In a bowl, mix all the dry masala—including red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala powder—with 1/4 cup of water and set aside.
Heat a frying pan with 1 teaspoon of oil, fry the tofu cubes, then set them aside.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan, temper with cumin seeds, curry leaves, ginger, and the masala paste; fry for a minute.
Add the tomato puree, salt, and peas; cook for 5 minutes. When it starts to thicken, add the tofu and cook for a few more minutes. Garnish with garam masala powder and fresh curry leaves.
Serve the Matar Masala Tofu with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha and Palak Raita.

title: Tawa Idli Recipe
instructions: Cut the idlis into cubes.
Heat butter in a wok, then add onions and sauté until translucent.
Add salt, red chilli powder, garam masala, and pav bhaji masala; stir.
Add about 1/2 cup of water and bring to a boil.
Add the chopped idlis and mix well until the spices coat the idlis; cook for half a minute.
Sprinkle lemon juice and garnish with coriander leaves; give a quick stir.
Serve Tawa Idli with Tomato Onion Chutney as a snack.

title: Sweet Potato Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 3 Sweet Potatoes, washed, peeled and cut into 1/4 inch round slices
1 Dry Red Chilli, cut into 2 pieces
instructions: Heat oil in a broad non-stick pan. Add dry red chilli and mustard seeds. Once mustard seeds crackle, add cumin seeds, green chilli, and hing.
Add sweet potato slices and mix well. Saute for 5 minutes, then add salt and turmeric powder. Continue sauteing for 10-15 minutes until the potatoes are cooked.
Add coriander powder and cumin powder, mix well, and remove from heat.
Sprinkle chopped coriander leaves on top.
Serve the Sweet Potato Sabzi with phulka and buttermilk.

title: Sprouted Ragi Chicken Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1/3 cup Ragi Seeds, soaked overnight and sprouted
instructions: Partially cook the chicken for about 10 minutes in a kadai with enough water, cool it and grind with some salt and pepper (not to a fine paste).
Cook potatoes and carrots in a vessel until al dente, then drain the water (save it for stock if desired).
Coarsely grind the sprouted ragi in a mixer grinder.
Preheat a convection oven to 200 °C. Grease a baking dish or line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Mash the boiled potatoes and carrots, then add the ground ragi, chicken, chopped onions, ginger‑garlic paste, green chilies, garam masala, black pepper, roasted cumin powder, coriander leaves and oats.
Combine everything well; add more oats if the mixture feels too moist.
Shape the mixture into cutlets, place them on the greased dish, drizzle a little oil on top, and bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes followed by 10 minutes of grilling until crisp.
Enjoy the hot and crispy sprouted ragi chicken cutlet.
Serve with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Date and Tamarind Chutney, Kachumber Salad and Adrak Chai for a tea‑time snack.

title: Malpua Recipe with Rabri (A Spiced Indian Pancake with Milk Pudding)
instructions: To begin making Malpua Recipe, first prepare the batter. To do this, in a mixing bowl mix stir together the flour, sugar, milk powder, crushed cardamom pods and fennel seeds.
Now add the khoya and yogurt in the flour mixture. Stir and mix well to combine.
Using a little water at a time, mix continuously until the batter forms a thick flowing consistency without lumps. It should flow like dosa batter. Set it aside so the batter can rest for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile prepare the sugar syrup in which you will soak the malpua. To do this, add sugar and water in a heavy bottom saucepan. Set it on a low heat and let it simmer until the sugar has melted completely.

Once sugar is dissolved add the lemon juice and saffron strands. Stir once to combine. By now, the sugar syrup should have reached one-string consistency. You will know this, when you touch the sugar syrup between your fingers, it will be sticky.
While the sugar syrup is simmering, heat 2 - 3 tablespoon of ghee in a non stick skillet over medium heat.
Mix baking soda in the batter and stir to evenly combine. Pour a spoonful of batter on the pan and gently spread with the back of the spoon to form a small sized pancake-like round.
Fry the malpua on a low to medium till crisp and golden on both sides.
When they're golden and ready to be taken off the skillet, take them off heat and immediately soak them in the warm sugar syrup, either by dipping them in or pouring the sugar over the malpuas.
Proceed the same way with the remaining Malpuas.
Serve Malpua With Rabri as a dessert along with Jalebi during the festive season.

title: Apple Tea Latte Recipe
instructions: Bring the cinnamon, milk, and honey to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Meanwhile, in a blender, combine the brewed tea and the chopped apple; blend until smooth.
Pour the tea‑apple mixture into 2 mugs and top with the milk mixture from the saucepan. Sprinkle some cinnamon powder on top and serve.
Serve Apple Tea Latte with Choco Swirl Cookies or Orange Zested Shortbread Cookies.

title: Grain Free Chocolate Porridge Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups Cauliflower (gobi), cut into florets, cleaned
instructions: Add 1 cup of coconut milk and cauliflower florets to a saucepan and simmer, cooking for 10 minutes or until tender.
Using an immersion blender, blitz the cauliflower to a grainy consistency, or let it cool completely and blend in a regular blender.
Transfer the blended mixture to a mixing bowl and add cocoa powder, date syrup, salt, and cinnamon, mixing until well combined.
Serve the porridge in a bowl, topping with sliced strawberries, pistachios, chopped dried fig, walnuts, and drizzle the reserved coconut milk on top.
Enjoy the Grain Free Chocolate Porridge in the morning as a healthy start to your day.

title: Baked Fish Crisps Recipe (Fish Fry In Oven)
instructions: To begin making the Baked Fish Crisps Recipe, clean the fish and in a large vessel add in the ingredients mentioned in the “To Marinate” table and make a fine paste and add the fish to it and mix well.

Allow it to marinate for half an hour. Meanwhile line your baking tray with Parchment paper. Preheat the oven at 180 °C for about 10 mins. Arrange the marinated fish pieces in the lined baking tray and using grill mode grill it for 7 mins.

After 7 mins flip the fish and then grill for another 7 mins. Now that the colour of the fish would have slightly turned dark. Flip the side of the fish once again and brush it with oil if required. And grill for another 5 mins.
Once done flip the fish once again and brush with little oil or sprinkle little oil and grill for another 5 mins.
Fish would have cooked by now and it is ready to be served. If you feel the fish is not yet cooked grill for another 4 mins by flipping the fish sides after 2 mins. Serve hot as an appetizer/starter.
Serve Baked Fish Crisps Recipe along with Dhaniya Pudina chutney or any other chutney of your choice.

title: Egg Butter Masala Recipe
instructions: To begin with Egg Butter Masala, soak cashew nuts in hot water for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes drain the water and retain the cashew nuts.
Boil the eggs and after cooling, crack and discard the shell. Keep them aside.
In a kadhai, add 2 tablespoon butter. After the butter melts, add onion and fry till onion turns pinkish. Add tomato and saute till tomato turns mushy.
Add garlic, ginger and saute till raw smell of garlic goes away. Add the boiled cashew nuts and mix.
Switch off the gas. After cooling, grind the sauteed onion tomato mixture by adding 1 cup water.

Strain this gravy by passing through a strainer. While passing through a strainer, take a spoon and keep on pressing the contents against the strainer. Let the entire gravy pass through. Only seeds of tomato will remain on strainer as a residue which you can discard.
Heat the kadai again, add 1 tablespoon butter. Add bayleaf and ginger garlic paste and fry for 1 minute.
Add the gravy and mix everything well. Add 2 tablespoons butter and simmer the gravy for 10 minutes.
Add chili powder, garam masala, kasuri methi and mix well. Finally, add the boiled eggs and simmer for 5 minutes. Add salt to taste.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves or fresh cream if you wish.
Serve Egg Butter Masala with Whole Wheat Lachha Paratha and Jeera Rice.

title: Onion Raita Recipe - Pyaz Ka Raita Recipe
instructions: Slice the onions and chop the green chilli, mint, and coriander leaves.
In a mixing bowl, add yogurt, salt, and jeera powder and whisk well until smooth.
Add water to adjust the consistency, then add the onions, green chilies, mint, and coriander leaves; mix well to combine. Transfer into a serving bowl and serve.
Serve the Onion Raita along with Ambur Star Chicken Biryani, Chettinad Mint Potato Biryani, and Mirchi Ka Salan for a simple Sunday lunch.

title: Buttered Carrot Fingers Recipe (Finger Food For Babies Over 9 Months)
instructions: Dice the washed and peeled carrots into sticks about an inch wide and 4 inches long.
Add the diced carrots to a pressure cooker with a pinch of salt and 2 tablespoons of water.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook for one whistle; then turn off the heat and release the pressure immediately by running the cooker under cold water to prevent overcooking.
Place a pan on low‑medium flame, add one teaspoon of unsalted butter, let it melt, then add the steamed carrots.
Sauté for a couple of minutes until the butter coats the carrots, then turn off the flame.
Sprinkle a small pinch of cumin powder or black pepper powder on top of the carrots and optionally add a pinch of salt.
Serve the buttered carrot fingers to toddlers as a snack or finger food.

title: Spring Onion and Peanut Raita Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Spring Onion Greens, finely chopped
2 tablespoon Roasted Peanuts (Moongphali), toasted and pound
instructions: Whisk the curd to a smooth mixture.
Add toasted peanuts, spring onions and sprinkle with cumin powder; serve fresh.
Serve the Spring Onion and Peanut Raita along with Thepla, Aloo Palak Sabzi, and Gujarati Dal to make a complete meal.

title: Chutney Chilli Cheese Toast Recipe
ingredients: 4 Whole Wheat Brown Bread, whole wheat
Mozzarella cheese, or cheddar cheese, grated
instructions: Grind all the chutney ingredients in a mixer grinder to form a smooth paste without adding water, then transfer to a bowl.
Preheat oven to 180°C for 10 minutes and line a baking tray with foil.
Take a bread slice and cut into 2 or 4 halves.
Spread butter on one side of a bread half, then spread a teaspoon of chutney over the butter.
Top with chopped tomato and green capsicum.
Sprinkle cheddar cheese and chilli flakes, arrange slices on the tray, and bake for 5-8 minutes.
Serve the Chutney Chili Cheese Toast with hot Masala Chai and Linzer Cookies.

title: Pakki Mutton Biryani Recipe
ingredients: 1 kg Mutton, cut into small pieces
1-1/2 cups Basmati rice, washed and soaked in water for 30 minutes
2 Onions, sliced very thin for garnishing
Mixed Spices: 2-3 bay leaves, 2-3 ansi, 8-10 cloves, 8-10 black pepper corns, 1 stick cinnamon, 1-2 black cardamom
5-6 Saffron strands, soaked in 2 tablespoons of warm milk
instructions: Wash goat pieces well with water, drain and set aside.
Heat a little oil on a skillet and fry sliced onions until caramelized and brownish black; set aside for garnishing.
Add oil to a pressure cooker and fry garam masala with onions, ginger garlic paste, and a little salt; when the onion changes colour, add the goat pieces.
Add biryani masala, green chilies, a handful of coriander leaves, red chilli powder, lime juice, yogurt, and cover with a lid.
Pressure cook for up to 5-6 minutes, then turn off the pressure cooker.
In a separate vessel, bring 2-3 cups of water to a boil, add a little salt, cumin seeds, and the soaked rice; cook until the rice is about 90% done (approximately 10 minutes), then strain.
In a baking pan, layer half of the rice, sprinkle with ghee, chopped coriander, and saffron milk, then arrange some cooked goat pieces (without the gravy) on top.
Add the remaining rice, sprinkle with ghee, chopped coriander, saffron milk, and pour the reserved goat gravy over it.
Cover the pan tightly with aluminium foil and bake in a preheated oven at 350°F for about 20 minutes; remove and serve.
Serve Pakki Mutton Biryani with Burani raita or any raita of your choice.

title: Raw Jackfruit Kofta Curry Recipe - Kathal Kofta Curry Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Jackfruit Raw (Kathal) , cut into pieces
3 teaspoon Oil , as required, or ghee
4 teaspoon Oil , as required or ghee
2 teaspoon Fresh cream , as required, for garnish
instructions: To begin making the Raw Jackfruit Kofta Curry Recipe, first clean the jackfruit pieces and then cook for up to 1-2 whistle in a cup of salted water and a cinnamon in a pressure cooker.
Switch off the stove and let the pressure release naturally.
Once fully cooked strain the water and keep the jackfruit aside to dry.
Take a blender, add boiled jackfruit with coconut and green chilli without adding water. Blend it into a paste.
Once it is done, add the all purpose flour, salt, cardamom and cumin powder. and mix everything well.
Mix everything well and keep it aside to cool down the jackfruit kofta mixture.
Now make small flat oval shaped balls with the mixture. Heat a paniyaram pan with oil in each cavity and fry the kathal koftas from both the sides till they turn golden brown.
The next step is to make the kofta gravy. Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida and saute for about 10 seconds.
After 10 seconds, add onions, salt and cook till they become soft and translucent.
Next add tomatoes, ginger paste cook for about 6 to 8 minutes until the tomatoes are soft. Switch off the heat.
Once the tomato mixture is cooled down, blend this mixture with a hand blender to smooth gravy adding a cup of water.
Add this kofta gravy back in the wok and switch on the heat. Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cook on medium to low till thick gravy is forming with bubbles on top.
Add garam masala powder, salt to taste and coriander leaves. Let this kofta gravy cook for about 6 to 8 minutes.
Drop the jackfruit koftas in the gravy, let it soak for few minutes before serving. Finally garnish the Raw Jackfruit Kofta Curry with fresh cream and chopped coriander leaves.
Serve Raw Jackfruit Kofta Curry Recipe along with Palak Raita, Phulka and Satvik Carrot Sprout Salad for your weekday Indian Vegetarian meal.

title: Instant Cucumber Pickle Recipe
instructions: Place the sliced cucumber in a bowl.
Add the red chilli powder, asafoetida, turmeric powder, powdered methi seeds, sugar, and lemon juice to the cucumber and mix until well combined.
Let the mixture sit for an hour so the flavours meld with the cucumber.
Serve the instant cucumber pickle as an accompaniment with Panchmel Dal and Phulkas.

title: One Pot Masala Vegetable Rice Recipe
instructions: Prep all the vegetables and keep them aside.
In a pressure cooker pan, add one tablespoon of coconut oil and let it warm. Reduce the flame to low and add cumin seeds, sauté for a minute.
Add the sliced ginger, chopped garlic, and onions; sauté until the onions turn soft and translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté until they become mushy.
Add the turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and garam masala powder; stir the spices well into the onion‑tomato mixture.
Add the washed rice and chopped vegetables (carrots, beans, and cabbage). You may also add peas if desired.
Mix well until the vegetables and rice are coated with the masalas. Add 2 cups of water, close the pressure cooker lid, and increase the flame to high.
Allow the cooker to weight, then let out 2 whistles; reduce the flame to low and cook for 2 more minutes. Turn off the flame and let the pressure release naturally.
Garnish with chopped coriander if you wish.
Serve the One Pot Masala Vegetable Rice with a raita such as Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita or Tadka Raita.

title: Black Forest Cupcake Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup butter (salted), melted or vegetable oil
2 whole eggs (or 3/4 cup beaten thick yogurt as an egg substitute)
1-1/2 cup pitted cherries, chopped (fresh or frozen) plus 12 fresh cherries with stems for garnish
1/2 cup Britannia cream cheese, at room temperature
Britannia cream cheese (additional for frosting, if needed)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Line 12 muffin cups with paper liners. In a bowl, combine all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and cocoa powder; mix well.
In a separate large bowl, whisk together sugar, melted butter or vegetable oil, vanilla extract, eggs (or beaten yogurt), and milk until the mixture is creamy.
Gradually add the wet mixture to the dry ingredients, mixing until fully combined.
Fold in the chopped cherries until just incorporated, then divide the batter evenly among the prepared muffin cups.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a cupcake comes out clean. Transfer to a wire rack and allow to cool completely.
While the cupcakes cool, prepare the frosting: beat the cream cheese, sour cream, and icing sugar with an electric or hand mixer until smooth.
Refrigerate the frosting for about 2 hours until very cold. Spread the chilled frosting over the cooled cupcakes, sprinkle chopped chocolate on top, and garnish each cupcake with a fresh cherry.
Serve the Black Forest cupcakes with your choice of side dishes or beverages.

title: Carrot Puree Recipe - First Food For Babies
instructions: Wash and peel the carrots, then cut them into slices.
Add the carrot slices to a pressure cooker, add 2-3 tablespoons water, and pressure cook for 2 whistles. Cool under running tap water, or alternatively steam the carrot pieces in a baby food steamer.
You can also cook the carrots in a covered pan until soft; however, using a pressure cooker or steamer saves time and retains more nutrition.
Blend the cooked carrot pieces in a baby food blender until smooth, adding more water to achieve a thin consistency.
Serve the carrot puree to the baby, adjusting the consistency with a little water if needed.

title: Pyaz Wali Bhindi Recipe | Bhindi Do Pyaza - Okra Onion Stir Fry
ingredients: 2 tablespoon Mustard oil, or Sunflower oil
1 teaspoon Red Chilli powder (or more to taste)
instructions: To begin making Pyaz Wali Bhindi Recipe Bhindi Do Pyaza, first wash bhindi in water. Pat dry with the kitchen towel. To cut okra first remove the stem of the bhindi and then cut into thin strips of 4 pieces. Keep aside until ready to use.
Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat. Add the ajwain seeds and allow it to crackle.
Add the cinnamon stick, bay leaf and saute for a few seconds. Add the thinly sliced onions, turn the heat to low and saute the onions until they soften.
At this stage add in the chopped lady's finger, sprinkle salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and amchur powder.

Stir until all the ingredients get well combined. Cover the pan with the lid slightly ajar. Keep the heat on low and let bhindi do pyaza cook until it turns soft and tender. This process will take about 15 minutes on medium heat.
Ensure to keep stirring the bhindi do pyaza a few times in between so it gets cooked evenly and towards the end you will notice the onions have slightly caramelised as well.
Once done, turn off the heat and check the salt and spices and adjust to taste accordingly.
Transfer the Pyaz Wali Bhindi/ Bhindi Do Pyaza to a serving bowl and serve hot.
Serve the Pyaz Wali Bhindi/ Bhindi Do Pyaza Recipe along with Parathas and Kadhi Pakora for a delicious lunch or dinner.

title: Bharwa Karela Masala Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Fresh coconut, grated and roasted
instructions: Wash karela and grate their outer surface with a knife or grater, remove seeds inside, cut them 2 inches long, add salt and leave aside for 10 minutes.
Squeeze the excess water from the vegetables, wash them completely to reduce bitterness, slice the gourds halfway through to facilitate filling, and keep aside.
In a saucepan, bring water to a boil, cook pieces of karela until the skin becomes tender (avoid overcooking), drain and allow to cool enough to handle.
Dry roast peanuts until slightly brown; divide half for stuffing and half for gravy.
In a kadai, heat oil and add cumin seeds, frying until brownish.
Add garlic pods and fry until brownish.
In a mixer, add roasted peanuts, roasted coconut, garlic pods, cumin seeds, jaggery, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt; grind coarsely without adding water.
Add a teaspoon of oil to the ground mixture and mix well.
Stuff half of the spice mixture inside the bitter gourd and keep the remaining half for the gravy.
In a medium-sized frying pan, add the remaining oil and heat over medium heat.
Place the stuffed karelas in the pan and roast until the outer skin turns brownish.
In another medium-sized pan, add a half teaspoon of oil, heat, add the remaining masala and sauté for a few minutes; add 1‑1/2 cups of water and cook until the gravy thickens slightly.
Add a little more tamarind paste if a sour taste is desired.
Cover with a lid and cook over medium flame until the gravy reduces and the ground powders are fully absorbed; adjust salt, switch off the flame, pour the gravy over the karelas and serve hot.
Serve Bharwa Karela Masala with Dhaba Style Dal Fry, Phulka, and Masala Khichia.

title: Matki Dal Sabzi Recipe - Sprouted Moth Bean Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch, chopped
instructions: Add the moth sprouts to a pressure cooker with 1/4 cup water and salt, and pressure cook until the cooker releases one whistle; let the pressure release naturally.
Drain any water and keep the sprouts aside in a bowl.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add mustard seeds, ginger, onions, and green chilli, and sauté until the onion becomes soft and translucent.
Add curry leaves, turmeric powder, and garam masala powder; cook for about 2 minutes.
Add the cooked moth sprouts, mix well, and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add tomato, coconut, salt to taste, and coriander leaves; stir and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more.
Check the seasoning and adjust salt and spice as needed.
Serve the Sprouted Moth Bean Sabzi with Gujarati Kadhi, Kachumber Salad, and Phulka.

title: How To Make Homemade Ragi Idli & Dosa Batter Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups White Urad Dal (Whole), soaked overnight
3 teaspoons Methi Seeds (Fenugreek Seeds), soaked overnight
instructions: Soak the rice and ragi together in water, ensuring all ingredients are fully immersed with water level about an inch above the rice; let soak for about 6 hours or overnight.
Soak the urad dal and methi seeds in water, with the water level about 2 inches above the dal; let soak for about 6 hours.
After soaking, grind the batter.
First, grind the urad dal into a fine, very smooth batter, adding just enough water to achieve a fluffy texture.
Grind the rice and ragi into a smooth batter, adding only the required amount of water to obtain an almost smooth consistency; avoid adding too much water.
Combine the urad dal batter with the rice‑ragi batter, add salt to taste, and set aside for at least 12 hours or overnight to ferment, allowing the batter to rise in volume.
Place the batter in a large container to give it sufficient room to increase in volume during fermentation.
Ferment the batter in a warm environment (ideally summer); in colder places, keep the batter in a warm oven with the light on or preheated briefly, then turned off, to promote fermentation.

title: Snow Drop Cookies Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Dates, paste or any filling of your choice
3/4 cup Sugar, powdered sugar for coating the cookies
instructions: To begin making the Snow Drop Cookies recipe, firstly pre heat the oven at 275 degree celcius for 15 minutes.
Beat the butter untill it is smooth and a little pale in colour. Next add the sesame seeds and mix it well.

Sift the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt together in batches until it forms a soft dough. You may need more or less flour according to the type of flour you use. It should not stick to your hands and should not crack when formed into a ball.

If you want to add filling then take a small ball size of the dough and flatten them a bit with your fingers on your palm then take a small pea sized filling of your desire and place it in the center then bring the ends together and form a ball. (its the same process as making a kachori)
In a baking sheet place small balls of cookies but do not flatten them with your hands.
Bake it at 200 degree celcius for about 30 minutes, keep a close eye to the cookies while its baking as we do not need to brown the cookies from top, which makes them melt in your mouth.
Take out the cookies once baked and nicely browned from bottom and let them cool down a little in the sheet itself. Do not try to touch them at this point as they are likely to break.
Once the cookies are cooled down but slightly warm sprinkle powdered sugar on top of them with the help of a sieve. Do not dip them directly in the sugar as they are very soft and likely to break.

The sugar will slightly melt after sometime then do a second round of sprinkling sugar, be generous in coating them with sugar as we do not have any sugar in the cookies itself. Store them in an air tight container or serve it immediately.
Serve Snow Drop Cookies along with Espresso Coffee for your tea time break. You can also pack these cookies for your kids snacks box.

title: Homemade Rice Cereal Recipe (Babies-4 months onward)
instructions: Wash the rice, drain completely in a colander, spread on a clean white cloth, and let it air dry or fan dry for 30 to 50 minutes.
Dry roast the rice on low flame in a pan over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until it begins to pop and splutter, then turn off the heat and let the rice cool.
Grind the cooled rice in a clean mixer jar to a smooth powder, store in an airtight container.
To prepare the rice cereal, mix one tablespoon of rice cereal with 1/2 cup water in a bowl, pour into a saucepan on medium heat, stir continuously and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the rice cereal to a serving bowl, feed warm to baby; optionally mix with milk or formula and adjust consistency with more water or milk.

title: Moong Dal Tikki Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum) , finely chopped
1/4 cup Green peas (Matar) , boiled and mashed
instructions: To begin making the Moong Dal Tikki Recipe, wash the moong dal and transfer it to a pressure cooker along with 1/2 cup water and salt to taste.
Pressure cook the dal for one whistle and turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally. We want the dal to be cooked well but not mashed.
Once the pressure has released, drain the excess water if any and set the dal aside. You can use the water in cooking rice and making soups.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the chopped green chillies, ginger, onion, garlic, capsicum, paneer, mint leaves and the cooked dal.
To the same bowl, continue and add the cornflour, cumin powder, salt, amchur, black pepper powder and chaat masala.

Mix the Moong Dal Tikki mixture well and check the taste and adjust the seasonings accordingly. Divide the Moong Dal Tikki mixture int0 10 to 12 lemon sized balls and shape them into flat round tikkis.
Heat oil in a tawa over medium-high heat and shallow fry the Moong Dal Tikkis on both sides until they turn into a lovely brown colour.
Serve hot Moong Dal Tikki Recipe along with Green Chutney and Khajur Imli Chutney and a cup of Masala Chai for your Monsoon evenings.

title: Kadai Mushroom Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Kadai Mushroom recipe, first prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Preheat ghee in a wok or a kadai over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and allow it to crackle.
Add the ginger, garlic and saute for a few seconds.
Next add the onions, bell peppers and carrots and saute until the vegetables are well roasted and cooked. It should have a firm bite.

Once the vegetables are well roasted, add the mushrooms, tomato puree, badi elaichi, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala powder, salt, kasuri methi and honey.
Give it a stir, cover the pan and simmer until the mushrooms are cooked. This will take about 3 to 4 minutes over medium heat.
Once done, check the salt and spices of the Kadai Mushroom Sabzi and adjust according to taste.
Turn off the heat, transfer the Kadai Mushroom to a serving bowl and serve hot along with phulka or jeera rice.

title: Matar Aur Chilke Ka Sabzi (Peas & Peel Stir Fry Recipe)
ingredients: 300 grams Green peas (Matar), with pod, fresh & firm
instructions: Wash the green pea pods, take out the peas from the pods into a bowl and set aside.
Take half of the pea peels (discard the rest), break the tip and bottom of each pod peel, discard the long fibrous membrane, and chop each pod in the middle to bite‑size pieces.
Chop the white part of the spring onion lengthwise and the green part into 1–2 inch pieces.
Heat the oil in a kadai and add panch phoron; when the seeds begin to splutter, add the chopped white part of the spring onion and stir‑fry briefly.
Add the chopped pea pod peels, spring onion greens, and half of the green peas extracted from the pods; stir again.
Add turmeric powder, chopped green chilies, and salt.
Cover and cook on low‑medium heat until the vegetables are just tender.
Remove from heat and serve hot as a side dish with paratha or phulkas.

title: Ragi Rava Dosa Recipe With Oats - Finger Millet & Oats Dosa Recipe
instructions: In a large bowl combine the semolina, ragi and rice flours and salt. Stir 3 cups of water to make a thick batter and allow it to rest for about 10 minutes.
Stir in the remaining ingredients – green chillies, grated ginger, peppercorns, cumin seeds and finely chopped coriander leaves – and combine well.
Add 1/2 cup more water to the batter to achieve a thin, pourable consistency, thinner than typical pancake/dosa batter.
When the batter is thin, it spreads on a heated skillet, producing holes and a crisp texture.
Heat an iron skillet or dosa tawa on high heat until very hot; test by sprinkling water, which should sizzle.
Pour a ladle of the batter starting from the outer edges; let it sizzle and spread, pouring from a height to fill gaps and create holes.
Turn the heat to medium if you want a crisp ragi‑oats dosa; slower cooking yields a crispier result.
Drizzle about 1/2 teaspoon of ghee around the dosa and cook for 2–3 minutes on medium heat.
When one side is golden and crisp, flip the dosa and cook for another minute until both sides are golden brown.
Remove the dosa from the skillet and repeat to make the remaining dosas.
Serve the ragi rava dosa with a cup of yogurt, Thakkali Vengaya Sambar, tomato chutney, or simply with jaggery and butter.

title: Gajar Lauki Juice Recipe - Bottle Gourd Carrot Juice
instructions: Blend all the ingredients (bottle gourd, carrots, ginger, mint leaves, lemon juice, salt, honey) in a blender with 1 cup of water until smooth, forming a fine puree.
Transfer the puree to a decanter and add 2 more cups of water, adjusting the amount to achieve the desired consistency.
Adjust the salt to taste and stir well.
Serve the lauki juice immediately, optionally with spicy jalapeno scrambled eggs and bread toast.
Alternatively, use a juicer to extract the juice from the carrots and gourd; note that the pulp will be lost and you may need more produce to obtain the same quantity.

title: Instant Kalakand Recipe -Indian Festive Sweet Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Instant Kalakand, place the paneer and condensed milk in a non stick pan. Place the pan on low heat and cook. Keep stirring this mixture until it becomes thick.
Once you notice the kalakand mixture is beginning to turn thick, add the cardamom powder and a few drops of rose water. Keep stirring until the mixture begins to leave the sides of the pan.
When the kalakand mixture leaves the sides of the pan, turn off the heat.
Grease a square pan with ghee. Add the hot kalakand mixture and spread it evenly with your fingers or the back of a spoon. Sprinkle chopped nuts like almonds or pistachios.
Set the Instant Kalakand and let it cool completely. Once cooled, refrigerate the kalakand for 30 minutes before cutting into the desired shape.
Once fully set, cut into desired shapes and serve. The kalakand can be refrigerated for up to 2–3 days.
Serve Kalakand along with other festival recipes like Saffron Pilaf and Churma Ladoo.

title: Meetha Daliya With Milk & Fruits Recipe - Broken Wheat Porridge
ingredients: 1/2 cup Broken Wheat (Dalia/ Godumai Rava) (I used the smaller grains)
Sugar, to taste or drizzle with honey
instructions: To begin making the Meetha Dalia – Broken Wheat Porridge recipe, first dry the broken wheat.
Add the broken wheat to a pan placed on low heat and roast till it becomes golden brown.
To the same pan, add water and fennel seeds and cook till it softens.
Next add milk and let the contents come to a boil. Simmer on medium‑low flame till milk and broken wheat are well assimilated and start to thicken slightly.
Switch off the heat. Stir in the sugar. Allow the contents to cool or serve warm with fruits of your choice.
If serving with fruits, ensure the porridge is not hot, otherwise the fruits will release water and become mushy.
Serve Meetha Daliya on its own or along with a hot cup of Espresso coffee for a weekday breakfast.

title: Creamy Mango Kulfi Recipe With Cream Cheese
ingredients: 1 cup ripe mango, fresh peeled and diced
instructions: Beat the cream cheese with a mixer at high speed until smooth.
Combine whipped cream and whip until light and fluffy.
Add the mango puree and continue to whip; when the mixture forms stiff peaks, turn it off.
Add in the diced mangoes and whip for a few seconds.
Spoon the mixture into kulfi molds, cover and freeze for 10 to 12 hours until firm.
Serve the Cream Cheese Mango Kulfi as a dessert for a Holi party or during the summer.

title: Lemon 7 Up Cake Recipe
instructions: Cream butter and sugar together for 20 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition. Add flour and lemon zest, then fold in 7-Up. Pour into a well‑greased 12‑cup Bundt pan.
Bake at 325°F for 1 to 1¼ hours.
Make the lemon glaze by mixing powdered sugar and lemon juice together; set aside. When the cake is cooled, drizzle with the lemon glaze.
Serve the Lemon 7 Up Cake for special occasions or birthday parties.

title: Coriander Garlic Baked Chicken Recipe
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts (make slight incisions on the surface)
instructions: Make the marinade first.
Combine coriander leaves, garlic, green chillies, salt, lemon juice, olive oil, and honey; grind to a coarse paste without adding water.
Transfer the coarse paste from the mixer to a large bowl.
Add the chicken breasts to the bowl and smear the marinade all over the chicken; let marinate for at least one hour.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Line a baking tray with aluminum foil, grease generously with oil, place the marinated chicken breasts on it, and bake for 15–18 minutes, reserving some extra marinade in a separate bowl.
Halfway through baking, baste the chicken with the remaining marinade and a drizzle of olive oil.
When the chicken is done (about 15 minutes), remove from the oven, let it rest a few minutes, and serve hot.
Alternatively, the chicken can be pan‑roasted in a non‑stick pan over gas flame, drizzling olive oil and basting with remaining marinade until fully cooked, then serve hot.
Serve the coriander garlic baked chicken with side dishes such as jalapeno cilantro lime rice, baked potato wedges, and sour cream onion dip.
For winter meals, serve it with garlic knots and roasted cherry tomato soup.

title: Broccoli and Paneer Paratha Recipe
ingredients: Ghee, or oil for cooking the paratha
instructions: Begin making Broccoli Paratha recipe by first making the dough for the paratha.

Combine the flour and salt for the dough in a large bowl. Add a little water at a time and knead to make a smooth dough. Drizzle a little oil on the top and continue to knead until the dough is smooth and not sticky. Cover the dough and allow it to rest until preparing the filling.
Combine all the ingredients for the filling in a large bowl. Check for salt and spice levels and adjust to taste.
With both dough and filling ready, begin the process of making the stuffed Broccoli Paratha.

Divide the dough into 6-8 equal portions. Take one portion and dust in dry flour. Roll the dough to make a 3-4 inch diameter circle. Place 2 tablespoons of the filling in the center and bring the dough edges together towards the center. Seal the edges and pinch out any excess dough.
Flatten the paratha with fingers, dust in flour again, and roll gently to a 5-6 inch diameter circle.
Repeat the same process with remaining dough portions, stuffing and rolling each paratha.
Preheat a skillet (roti tawa), preferably an iron skillet.
When the skillet is hot, place the stuffed rolled paratha on it and cook for a minute on both sides until a few brown spots appear.

When brown spots appear, smear some ghee or oil on both sides and cook until the paratha is golden brown and lightly crisp on both sides. Cook on medium heat for even cooking. Transfer to a platter and repeat with remaining parathas.
Serve Broccoli and Paneer paratha with pickle of choice, Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, and a hot cup of Adrak Chai.

title: Vankaya Pakodi Koora Recipe - Andhra Style Brinjal Pakora Curry
ingredients: 8 Small Brinjal (Baingan / Eggplant), cut into wedges
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Cut the brinjal into wedges and place it in water to prevent discolouration.
Make the pakora batter by mixing gram flour, rice flour, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, green chillies, garlic, onion and salt; add water gradually to form a thick batter.
Heat oil in a paniyaram pan over medium heat, add a tablespoon of batter into each cavity and pan‑fry until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
If needed, drizzle additional oil into the cavities to make the pakoras crisp.
Set the fried pakoras aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat, add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add onion, garlic and green chillies; sauté until the onions soften and turn light brown.
Add the drained brinjal wedges, sprinkle salt and a little turmeric powder, and roast on low‑medium heat until cooked through.
Stir in curry leaves, chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and sambar powder; sauté until the tomatoes become mushy, then add 1/4 cup water and mix to form a semi‑thick mixture.
Add the pakoras to the tomato‑onion mixture, cover and simmer for 3–4 minutes until the eggplant and pakoras are well coated with the masala.
Check seasoning and adjust salt or spices as needed.
Turn off the heat, stir in chopped coriander leaves, and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve hot with steamed rice and Jeera Milagu Rasam.

title: Mughlai Style Chicken Changezi Recipe
ingredients: 2 Onions, roasted till soft and ground to paste
instructions: Pat dry the chicken and prick it with a fork to allow the marinade to penetrate.
In a mixing bowl, combine the chicken with curd, ginger garlic paste, coriander powder, cumin powder, salt, turmeric powder, kasuri methi, Kashmiri red chili powder, and oil; marinate for 3-4 hours.
Bake the marinated chicken at 180 °C for 30‑40 minutes, depending on piece size.
Burn a small piece of charcoal on a direct flame.
Place the cooked chicken in a dish, add a katori in the centre, put the hot charcoal in it, pour ghee over the charcoal, cover and let the smoke infuse the chicken.
For the gravy, heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan and add the ginger and garlic; sauté for about 30 seconds until the raw smell disappears.
Add tomato puree and the onion paste; cook for 2‑3 minutes until well combined, then add salt, red chili powder and the baked chicken.
Cook for 5‑7 minutes so the gravy is absorbed by the chicken; stir in fresh cream, mix well and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve the Chicken Changezi with garlic naan or jeera rice and pickled onions.

title: Spicy Mushroom Puffs Recipe (Empanadas stuffed with Mushroom Recipe)
instructions: We begin making the Spicy Mushroom Puffs Recipe (Empanadas stuffed with Mushroom Recipe) by making the dough, mix all the ingredients, and only half the whisked and knead it to a very soft dough. Rest it with a damp cloth covered over it.
Now to make the filling, heat a kadai with oil, add the garlic and onions and fry for few minutes till it become translucent.
Then add in the mushroom and green chilli, fry them till the water evaporates and becomes dry.
You can add in the other ingredients and check for seasoning. Once done switch it off and keep it aside.
Now pre heat the oven to 200 degree Celsius for 10 minutes.
Take out the dough and knead once, pinch out small medium sized balls. Flatten it and start rolling one by one in the shape of puri to medium thickness and not too thin.
Take the filling and place it on one side of the dough, overlap the dough and shape it into a semi-circle.
Make sure you're completely sealing the edges, with the help of the fork, press the edges and poke it in the center.
Place it on a greased baking tray, and grease the empanadas with the remaining egg to give a nice color to your empanadas. Bake it in the oven for about 15 minutes.
Serve the Spicy Mushroom Puffs Recipe (Empanadas stuffed with Mushroom Recipe) along with Pan Fried Onion Pakora Recipe (A Perfect Diwali & Evening Snack) to make your tea time snack healthy.

title: Badam Halwa Recipe - Delicious Almond Halwa With Khoya
instructions: Powder the almonds (badam) using a mixer grinder; you can soak, peel, and powder them with or without the skin.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add the powdered almonds to the pan and stir continuously until they turn brown and emit a roasted aroma, using low to medium heat.
In a separate saucepan, heat the milk and sugar until the sugar fully dissolves.
Add the roasted almond powder to the milk mixture and keep stirring; the mixture will thicken and become coarse.
Once thickened, add the crumbled khoya and continue stirring until ghee separates from the sides of the pan.
Continue cooking and stirring for 15 to 20 minutes until the halwa becomes shiny, smooth, and releases from the pan sides.
Turn off the heat and transfer the Badam Halwa to a serving bowl.
Garnish with mixed nuts and serve warm.

title: Veggie Pearl Millet Tart Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Red, Yellow and Green Bell Peppers (Capsicum), finely chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C and grease tart molds with oil.
In a mixing bowl, sift bajra flour, wheat flour, sugar and salt together; add cold butter cubes and rub with fingertips until the mixture resembles bread crumbs.
In a small bowl, whisk 1 tablespoon oil, 2 tablespoons cold water and 1 teaspoon baking powder until well incorporated; add this wet mixture to the dry mixture and combine well to form a dough.
Ensure the dough is firm, then wrap in cling film and chill for at least 30 minutes.
After chilling, shape the dough into small balls, roll each out to about 1/4-inch thickness and fit into the tart molds, pressing gently to cover the mold evenly.
Prick the dough base with a fork and bake at 150°C for 10 minutes.
While the crust bakes, heat oil in a pan and sauté the finely chopped red, yellow, and green bell peppers for 2–3 minutes.
Add crumbled paneer and chopped spinach, stir quickly, then season with black pepper powder, oregano, chili flakes, and salt; cook for about 1 minute.
Allow the vegetable mixture to cool completely, then fold in cream cheese and mozzarella cheese; the filling is ready.
By the time, the tart base must

title: Orange Kulfi Recipe In Orange Shells
instructions: To begin making the Orange Kulfi Recipe, we will first prepare the shell of the orange. Using the knife, cut the orange into half and scoop out the pulp of the orange or peel the pulp out of the orange skin/shell. Ensure the shell does not break. Keep the shell aside.
Peel the thick skin of the pulp, remove any seeds and cut the pulp into tiny pieces and keep this aside.
The next step is to condense the milk to make the Kulfi. For this heat milk in a heavy bottomed saucepan and bring the milk to a boil.
Once the milk comes to a boil, turn the heat to low and simmer the milk with almost continuous stirring and reduce the milk to more than half its quantity.
During the initial stages of milk condensation frequent stirring is important, but as it begins to condense and reaches less than half the quantity it is absolutely important to stir continuously.
This is because condensed milk tends to get stuck to the bottom and sides of the pan and burn, leading to an unpleasant taste. Burning of milk is also toxic, so be extra careful.
Once it is reduced to about more than half of its quantity, stir in the sugar until it dissolves completely. Then allow the kulfi milk mixture to cool completely.
When the kulfi cools, stir in the orange marmalade and the orange pulp mixture into the condensed kulfi mixture.

Pour the orange kulfi mixture into the orange shells you kept aside, or set it in another bowl and later serve the orange kulfi in the shells. The latter method makes it easier to scoop the orange kulfi like ice cream and place it in the shells for serving.
Freeze the orange for at least fifteen hours or more to set well.
Serve the orange kulfi as a cold Indian dessert for parties, during the festival of Holi, or simply in the summer, and enjoy it with your family.

title: Spiced Turnips with Spinach Recipe
ingredients: 3 Turnips, peeled and diced into cubes
instructions: To start preparing Spiced Turnips with Spinach Recipe, get all the ingredients handy. In a pan, heat oil. Once the oil is hot, add in the cumin seeds and allow them to sizzle.
Add sliced onions and saute it till it changes colour on a medium flame.
Add ginger and garlic paste and saute it for a minute until the raw smell goes.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt and coriander powder. Cover and cook for another 2 minutes till done.
Add turnips, mix it well. Cover it and cook on a low flame till it 3/4th done, takes about 5-10 minutes.
Add chopped spinach, green/red chillies and cilantro. Mix well, cover it and cook on a low flame till it changes the colour or looks roasted.
Serve the prepared Spiced Turnips and Spinach Recipe hot with chapatis or naan.

title: Spiced Cabbage Rice Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Cabbage (Patta Gobi/ Muttaikose) , finely sliced
1/2 cup Soy granules , soaked in water until soft or paneer (Optional)
instructions: Heat a teaspoon of in a heavy bottomed pan on medium heat; add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick and maze, let the aroma fill your kitchen for few seconds.
Now add the onions, green chillies, ginger and garlic and sauté until onion is tender and golden.
In the mean while, pressure cook the rice with water in a pressure cooker and keep it aside.

Add cabbage and soy granules (optional) and sauté with the pan covered until the cabbage is soft, tender and cooked. You will find the cabbage has a nutty smell to it. At this point add all the spice powders and give it a toss well.
Stir in the cooked rice, chopped coriander leaves, salt and ghee and simmer for a couple of more minutes to get the flavours into the rice.
Serve the Cabbage Rice with Soy Granules along with a Vegetable Raita of your choice for your lunch and dinner.

title: Homemade Paneer Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Homemade Paneer, pour the 3 liters of milk into a heavy bottomed pan, turn the heat to high and wait for the milk to come to a boil.
When the milk begins to boil, add the freshly squeezed lemon juice; the milk will curdle, separating into cheese and whey.
The cheese, called chenna, should be left to rest in the whey for about 5 minutes after turning off the heat.
After the chenna rests, separate the whey and chenna using a thin sieve strainer and a muslin cloth.
Press down the chenna with a flat spatula to drain excess water and give the paneer its shape.
Fold the muslin cloth, place it on a flat plate with a larger plate beneath, and set a heavy weighted object on top of the chenna in the cloth.
Refrigerate the entire set‑up for about 2 hours to obtain a firm paneer; the bottom plate will collect some whey.
Remove the muslin cloth, cut the paneer into pieces, and use as desired.

title: Muskmelon Juice Recipe
ingredients: 600 grams Musk Melon, peeled and chopped
instructions: To begin making the Muskmelon Juice Recipe, blend all the ingredients in a blender, into a smooth puree. Make sure you select a juicy and ripe muskmelon for best taste.
Adjust the consistency by adding water as desired. Check the salt and sweetness and adjust to suit your taste.
This is a refreshing summer special drink is ready in minutes.

Just add few ice cubes to the Muskmelon Juice Recipe and serve chilled for the hot summer days with a late afternoon snack like Rajasthani Makki Ka Chatpata Dhokla Recipe or Baked Maddur Vada Recipe for kids.
You can even serve it as a welcome drink to your guests during hot days.

Note: Muskmelon juice should be consumed within 15-20 minutes of extraction to prevent any oxidation and loss of nutrients. You can use soda instead of water and add some crushed mint leaves for extra freshness.

title: Baked Vegetable Seekh Kebab Recipe
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) for 10 minutes and grease a baking tray with oil.
Heat oil in a non‑stick pan, add cumin seeds and sauté until fragrant.
Add green chillies and sauté for a minute, then add carrot and sauté for 2‑3 minutes.
Add French beans, cabbage and green peas and sauté for 2‑3 minutes; add turmeric powder, mix well and cook until combined.
Transfer the vegetable mixture to a mixer jar and grind coarsely; set aside.
In the same pan, add gram flour and sauté until fragrant, then add cashew nut powder and sauté.
Reduce heat, add the ground vegetables, mix well and sauté for 2‑3 minutes until the raw smell disappears; transfer this mixture to a bowl.
Add breadcrumbs, salt, crushed peppercorns, cardamom powder, garam masala powder, and mashed potatoes; mix well.
Divide the mixture into equal portions and shape each around a satay stick to form a seekh kebab.
Place the sticks on the greased baking tray and put the tray in the preheated oven.
Bake for 10‑12 minutes, turning every 4‑5 minutes to cook both sides evenly.
Serve the vegetable seekh kebabs with green chutney, pickled onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Brinjal Prawns Masala Curry Recipe - Baingan Prawn Masala
instructions: Soak a lemon-sized tamarind in 1/4 cup hot water for 15-20 minutes, then squeeze to extract the pulp into a bowl, adding extra water if needed.
Grind onion, ginger, garlic, chillies, and coriander leaves together in a mixer without adding water to form a paste; set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottom pan and add the ground paste, sautéing for 2-3 minutes over medium flame.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, and sambar powder; stir and cook for about a minute to remove raw aromas.
Add the brinjal cubes and a pinch of salt, cover, and cook on low flame until the brinjal is well roasted.
Add prawns, tomato puree, tamarind water, and salt to taste; stir to combine.
Cover the pan and cook for 3-4 minutes, as prawns cook quickly.
Taste and adjust salt and spices as needed, then turn off the heat.
Transfer the Brinjal Prawns Masala Curry to a serving bowl.
Serve hot with steamed rice, optionally accompanied by Kachumber salad and beetroot raita.

title: Carrot Pistachio Coconut Cake Recipe
ingredients: 240 ml Oil, or any flavorless oil
40 grams Fresh coconut, toasted and shredded
instructions: Preheat your oven at 180°C for 10 minutes.
Prepare either two 9 inch round pans or one 10 inch bundt pan by coating with butter/oil and dusting with flour.
Peel and finely grate the carrots and set aside; chop pistachios coarsely.
Slightly toast the shredded coconut over medium flame for about 2-3 minutes, avoiding browning.
Using a hand mixer, beat all 4 eggs until frothy.
Slowly add sugar and continue beating until the mixture doubles in volume and looks pale yellow (about 4 minutes).
Add oil to the mixture, then beat in the vanilla extract; whisk together flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and ground cinnamon in a bowl.
Add the flour mixture to the egg‑sugar mixture and beat just until incorporated; finally fold in grated carrots, chopped pistachios, and toasted coconut gently.
If using 9‑inch round pans, divide batter equally between the two pans and bake for 25‑30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
If using a bundt pan, bake for about 30‑35 minutes; remove from oven and let cool on a wire rack.
After about 5‑10 minutes invert the cakes onto the wire rack and let them cool completely.
Serve Carrot Pistachio Coconut Cake with espresso coffee and cucumber sandwich with yogurt and dill spread.

title: Barnyard Millet And Mushroom Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Barnyard Millet, soaked in water for 30 minutes
1 Potato (Aloo), boiled and skin peeled and mashed
Whole Wheat Bread crumbs, for coating
instructions: Heat a saucepan with oil, add onions, ginger, garlic and green chilli. Saute until the onions soften.
Add the mushroom and saute until the water is all evaporated. Add chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder and salt.
Saute for 3 minutes till the raw smell goes away. Add mashed and boiled potato and as well as the barnyard millet that has been soaked in water.
Keep sautéing until the millet is cooked, this will take about 10 minutes. Make sure the mixture combines together so that you can start shaping them into cutlets.
Switch off the heat, spread the mixture over a tray to cool down. Take some amount of the cutlet mixture, shape them into balls and flatten them using your palm.
Coat the cutlet well with bread crumbs and do the same for the rest of the mixture.
Heat a flat skillet with oil, once it is heated, place the cutlet carefully and fry them on either side till it browns.
Serve the Barnyard Millet And Mushroom Cutlet along with ketchup, as an accompaniment to a Pulao and Raw Mango Raita.

title: Buckwheat Dosa Recipe
instructions: Grind split black urad dal into a fine powder.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; add mustard seeds and let them splutter, then set aside.
In a bowl, combine buckwheat flour, urad dal powder, rice flour, salt, asafoetida, green chilies, and coriander leaves.
Add the tempered mustard seeds to the dry mixture. Gradually add water, mixing until a batter-like consistency is achieved.
Heat a crepe pan, lightly oil it, and pour a ladle of batter onto the pan, spreading in a circular motion.
Drizzle oil into the holes of the dosa and cook on both sides until it turns a slight golden colour.
Remove the cooked dosa onto a serving plate; it is ready to serve.
Serve the buckwheat dosa with South Indian Coconut Chutney or Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney.

title: Stuffed Capsicum With Sweet Potato Recipe
ingredients: 150 grams Sweet Potato, cooked and skin peeled
instructions: To begin making the Stuffed Capsicum with Sweet Potato Recipe, we will first cook the sweet potato in a pressure cooker with water and salt and keep it ready. Pressure cook it for 4 whistles.
Later, switch off the heat and release the pressure naturally and take the potatoes out. Peel the skin and by using a potato masher, mash to a smooth mixture.
Heat a kadai with little oil, add cumin seeds and allow them to splutter for few seconds. Add chopped garlic and saute till it softens.

Add cooked sweet potato along with all the spice powder including turmeric powder, red chilli powder, black pepper powder, garam masala powder and give it a mix. Once the spice powders are mixed, switch off the heat. Drizzle the mixture with olive oil at the end so that the mixture will stay moist.

Preheat the oven to 180 degree Celsius. Prep the bell peppers by carefully cutting the top of the capsicum which contains the stem and removing the core and seeds. Make sure you remove everything from inside without tearing.
To the mixture, add the dried fenugreek leaves at the end and give it a toss. Stuff this mixture into the bell peppers till the brim. Place them on a baking tray.
Bake them for about 20 minutes until the bell peppers are cooked. You can drizzle some olive at the top before baking.
Serve the Stuffed Capsicum with Sweet Potato Recipe along with Rajasthani Dal, Bhindi Masala and Phulka for an everyday meal.

title: No Onion No Garlic Aloo Makhana Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: salt, to taste (kala namak for fasting)
instructions: Boil the baby potatoes with their skins until well cooked, then peel and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add the makhana and roast over medium‑low heat until crisp; remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan, then add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add fennel seeds and chopped green chillies and sauté for about 20 seconds.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt (or black salt); mix quickly.
Add the boiled potatoes to the pan and toss well to coat with the spice mixture.
Add the roasted makhana, toss again, lower the flame, and cook while stirring for 3–4 minutes.
Remove from heat, garnish with coriander leaves, and serve hot.

title: Jhinga Gawar Recipe -Shrimps & Cluster Beans Sabzi
ingredients: 500 grams Gawar Phali (Kothavarangai / Cluster beans), bite sized
instructions: Prep all the ingredients first and cut the gawar to bite sized.
Heat oil in a kadai and add cumin seeds; let them crackle.
Add slit green chillies and finely sliced onions; sauté till translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and sauté for a few seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook till they are mushy.
Add the cumin powder and the gawar; sauté for half a minute, then add about half a cup of water and cover the pan to cook on medium heat.
After about 10 minutes, check and sauté as needed; once the gawar is almost cooked, add the shrimps and cook until done, allowing the water to evaporate for a dry sabzi.
Serve the Jhinga Gawar sabzi with Lauki Chana Dal, Phulka, Makki Ki Roti, or Steamed Rice, and pair with Dangar Pachadi with grated carrots.

title: Quinoa Brown Rice and Vegetable Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Brown Rice, soaked in water
1/4 cup Green beans (French Beans), finely chopped
1 tablespoon Extra Virgin Olive Oil, or ghee
instructions: To begin making the Quinoa Brown Rice Pilaf, place a heavy bottom pan on medium heat. Add a teaspoon of oil or ghee. Once it is medium hot, add onions, garlic, ginger, green chilies and fennel seeds. Saute them for a minute.
Add the chopped vegetables - cauliflower, potato, carrot, green beans and green peas. Saute the vegetables on medium flame for about 5-7 minutes until they soften.
Add garam masala powder, turmeric powder, black pepper powder and salt to taste. Grate ginger and garlic to it.

After a minute add the chopped green chilli. Add 2 cups boiling water and coconut milk. Mix all the ingredients well and bring the mixture to a boil. Once the water comes to a boil, turn the heat to medium.

At this stage, drain the soaked rice. Add quinoa and rice into the boiling mixture, turn the heat to low, cover the pan and cook on low heat until all the water is absorbed and Quinoa Brown Rice Pilaf is cooked.
At this stage, the quinoa and rice should be perfectly cooked. Once done, turn off the heat and allow it to remain covered for about 5 to 10 minutes before you can serve.
Once ready, open and fluff it up with a fort and transfer the Quinoa Brown Rice Pilaf in a serving plate. Stir it with freshly chopped coriander and lemon juice and serve.
Serve Quinoa Brown Rice Pilaf with Burani Raita Recipe (Garlic Based Yogurt) or Mint And Pomegranate Raita Recipe for a comforting weeknight dinner or lunch.

title: Indian Tea Masala Powder
instructions: To begin making the Indian Chai masala powder, use the mixer grinder to powder the dried ginger, green cardamom, cinnamon and black pepper.
Now add the remaining spices into mixture jar and make smooth powder of it.
Indian Chai masala powder is ready to use. Store it in container in room temperature, it can be used for many months.
Use this Indian Chai masala powder in your regular tea and make it even more flavourful.

title: Beetroot Poriyal Sabzi Recipe For Babies And Toddlers Over 10 months
instructions: Wash and peel the skin off the beetroot.
Cut the beetroot into small pieces and set aside.
In a pressure cooker, add the beetroot pieces, 2 tablespoons water, and a pinch of salt.
Cook the beetroots for one whistle, then release the pressure immediately and set aside.
In a pan, melt 1/2 teaspoon butter over medium heat.
Add 1/2 teaspoon mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Lower the heat, add a pinch of asafoetida and the finely chopped curry leaves.
Add the cooked beetroot pieces to the pan and mix well.
Cook on low heat for a couple of minutes, then turn off the heat.
Beetroot Poriyal (Sabzi) for toddlers is ready to be served.
Serve the Beetroot Poriyal as a baby/toddler food along with curd rice and dal chawal.

title: Bajra & Dal Cheela Recipe (Spicy Pearl Millet  & Lentil Crepe Recipe)
instructions: Soak whole green moong dal, chana dal, bajra, and whole urad dal together in enough water for 5 to 6 hours.

Drain the excess water. Grind all the soaked dals and bajra together with ginger, coriander leaves, and chilies in a mixer grinder, adding a little water at a time to obtain a smooth, pourable batter. Add salt and asafoetida, then transfer the batter to a mixing bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat and grease it. Pour a ladleful of batter onto the skillet and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin crepe.
Drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil around the sides and cook until both sides turn golden brown. Remove and serve, repeating with the remaining batter.
Serve the Bajra & Dal Cheela with Peanut Chutney, a glass of Masala Chaas (buttermilk), or ginger tea.

title: Aloo Paneer Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup whole wheat bread crumbs (for coating)
instructions: Prepare all ingredients and boil the potatoes until soft.
Mash the boiled potatoes together with the paneer until well combined.
Add cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, ginger garlic paste, 1/4 cup bread crumbs, sesame seeds, and salt to the mash; mix thoroughly.
Shape the mixture into large lemon-sized balls.
Roll each ball in the remaining 1/2 cup whole wheat bread crumbs, pressing gently to coat evenly.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a shallow pan over medium heat.
Place the coated balls in the pan and shallow fry on both sides until golden and crisp.
Alternatively, preheat an oven to 180°C and bake the kebabs for about 15 minutes on each side for a healthier option.
Serve the Aloo Paneer Kebabs with pudina chutney, date & tamarind chutney, or use them in Chole Aloo Tikki Chaat.

title: Dum Murgh Kali Mirch Recipe - Chicken In Rich White Gravy
instructions: Cut chicken into cubes and marinate with ginger garlic paste, half of the curd, garam masala powder, and salt; set aside for 2-3 hrs or overnight.
In a kadai, heat a little ghee over medium flame, add chopped onions and green chilies and sauté until onions are translucent and softened.
Let the onions and green chilies cool slightly, then blend them into a thick paste, adding a few teaspoons of water only if required.
Heat a little more ghee in the same kadai and add the cubed chicken; sauté on medium flame, covered, until the chicken is cooked through; remove chicken and set aside.
Add another tablespoon of ghee, heat, then add ginger-garlic juliennes and sauté for a minute; add the blended onion paste, cashew paste, cumin powder, curd and cook until the gravy comes together.
Return the cooked chicken to the mixture, stir, and add water if needed.
Cook on medium-low flame for about 2 minutes until the gravy is slightly absorbed and well mixed with the chicken.
Add garam masala, ground black pepper, and fresh cream; mix well.
Stir in chopped coriander and continue cooking on low flame.

Heat coal until red-hot, place it in a small steel katori, set the katori in the middle of the kadai, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil on the coal, and immediately cover the kadai to let the smoke infuse the dish.
Keep the dum covered until the steam settles, then turn off the flame and transfer to a serving dish.
Serve with whole wheat naan, chicken keema biryani, and papad raita (optional).

title: Mint Flavoured Mixed Vegetable Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 3 tablespoons Mint Leaves (Pudina), chopped/or dried pudina, crushed
instructions: To begin making Mint Flavoured Mixed Vegetable Pulao Recipe, prep all the ingredients and veggies needed. Chop carrots, beans and coriander leaves and also pudina leaves if you are using fresh ones. If you use dried pudina leaves, crush them between your palms and keep ready.
Also soak basmati rice in a pressure cooker for 20 minutes and cook for 2 whistles and wait till the pressure releases. Once done, fluff it up and keep ready.
Heat oil in pan or kadai and once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds and allow them to splutter.
Once the mustard seeds splutter, throw in the cumin seeds and allow them to sizzle.
Once they sizzle, immediately add the bay leaf, clove, and saute a bit.
Add the onions and saute till translucent. Once done, add the crushed garlic and saute till they are cooked.

Now, add the chopped chillies, chopped carrots, beans, peas and sauté for about 2 minutes. At this stage, add the chopped mint leaves if you are using fresh leaves, and saute till the leaves wilt a bit and the veggies are cooked al dente.
Add cooked basmati rice and mix carefully with a spatula, so that the rice is not broken or made mushy.

At this point, season the pulao with dried and crushed mint leaves if using the dried leaves and stir until it coats all the rice well. Remember to keep flame high and toss well on high heat and switch off. Sprinkle coriander leaves. Serve hot.
Mint Flavoured Mixed Vegetable Pulao Recipe can be served with a Dangar Pachadi With Grated Carrots Recipe (Urad Dal Raita) and a Tindora Ka Salan Recipe for a weeknight dinner.

title: Stuffed Dahi Vada Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup White Urad Dal (Whole), soaked overnight
1/2 teaspoon Cumin powder (Jeera) or chaat masala
instructions: Soak the avarekai (broad beans) and whole urad dal overnight in water, then grind them together in a mixer to a smooth paste, adding enough water as needed.

Transfer the dal paste to a mixing bowl, add the finely chopped onion, green chilies, grated ginger, and salt; mix well and let the mixture rest for about 10 minutes (optional: add chopped curry leaves and coriander leaves).

Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed kadai or pan. Wet your hands, take a tablespoon of batter, form a small disc, place the stuffing in the centre, then cover with another tablespoon of batter and deep‑fry until golden brown. For a low‑fat version, cook the stuffed vada in a paniyaram pan instead of deep‑frying.
Whisk the curd until smooth, add water and combine well. Stir in red chilli powder, cumin (or chaat) powder, finely chopped green chilies, and salt to taste.
Allow the fried vadas to cool to room temperature, then soak them in the prepared curd mixture for at least 1–2 hours.
Garnish the soaked vadas with grated carrot and chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the stuffed dahi vada as a side dish, optionally with Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma.

title: Ginger Garlic Tofu Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Spring Onion (Bulb & Greens), whites, chopped
Black pepper powder, according to your taste
1 teaspoon Sweet and Spicy Red Chilli Sauce (Tomato Chilli Sauce)
1 teaspoon Corn flour, dissolved in 2 tablespoon water
instructions: To begin making Ginger Garlic Tofu curry, heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pan. Add crushed ginger and garlic and cook it till it turns golden brown.
Once it is done, add chopped spring onion whites, greens and chilies into the pan. Stir it well.
Add chopped carrot and mix it properly. Add turmeric powder, tomato chili sauce and pepper powder. Make sure everything is mixed properly.

Add soy sauce, vegetable stock and coconut milk and stir everything nicely. Cover the pan and cook it for about 10 minutes. Add tofu cubes and salt according to your taste. Let it cook for about 10 minutes more.
Add corn flour dissolved water and cook for another 2 minutes. Switch off the heat and transfer it to a serving bowl.

title: Barnyard Millet Mushroom Biryani Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup Barnyard Millet, washed and soaked in water
300 grams Button mushrooms, cut into halves
instructions: Prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
Heat a pressure cooker with oil on medium heat.
Once hot, add all the whole spices: bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and star anise.
When the spices begin to sizzle, add curry leaves, ginger, garlic, onion and slit green chillies. Saute until the onions turn slightly caramelised over medium-low heat.
Add the quartered mushrooms, salt, black pepper powder, and garam masala powder. Saute for about a minute.
Reduce the heat; add curd, chopped coriander, mint leaves, and the drained barnyard millet along with 1-1/2 cups of water.
Pressure cook for 2 to 3 whistles, then turn the heat to low and simmer for 2 minutes. Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure has released, fluff the biryani with a fork and serve.
Serve the biryani along with spinach raita.

title: Saffron Milk Pudding Recipe
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Whole Almonds (Badam), powdered (grind 1/4 almonds in a mixer grinder at medium speed)
instructions: Add the gelatin into a bowl, pour hot water and stir; wait a few minutes until the gelatin dissolves completely.
Take 1/4 cup milk into a bowl, add custard powder, whisk to make a smooth paste ensuring no lumps form.
Heat the remaining milk in a saucepan, adding granulated sugar, saffron, and almond powder; stir and keep boiling until the sugar dissolves completely.
Remove the saucepan from heat and add custard powder, gelatin (stir again with a fork), rose water, and kewra essence; stir continuously.
Heat this mixture for 2 minutes over medium flame without letting it boil.
Remove the mixture from heat and let it cool down.
Pour the mixture into each small individual bowl or a large bowl through a strainer; let it sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour, then refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours.
Before serving, take the pudding out of the fridge, loosen the sides with a knife, and invert it onto a plate.
Serve the Saffron Milk Pudding as a dessert alongside Aloo Gobhi Matar Ki Sabzi, Boondi Raita, and Puri.

title: Cashewnut Stuffed Paneer Balls Recipe
instructions: Put the bread slices into a grinder jar and pulse to get bread crumbs. Reserve 1/4 of the crumbs for coating the paneer balls and soak the remaining crumbs in enough buttermilk for 2-3 minutes.
Crush ginger, green chilies and coriander leaves together and set aside. Grate or crumble the paneer in a bowl and add the crushed mixture to the paneer.
Add all the spices (black pepper, roasted cumin powder, kasuri methi, dry mango powder) to the paneer and knead well.
Add the soaked bread crumbs and salt to the paneer mixture, mix well and knead into a smooth dough.
Heat 1 teaspoon ghee in a pan and shallow fry the chopped cashew nut pieces on low flame until golden.
Divide the paneer dough into 10-12 equal parts, flatten each portion into a small disc, stuff 1/2 teaspoon of the roasted cashew pieces, close and roll into a ball. Repeat for all portions.
In another bowl, combine 3-4 tablespoons water with corn flour to make a paste.
Dip each paneer ball into the corn flour paste and roll it over the reserved bread crumbs.

Heat oil in a wok and deep fry the stuffed paneer balls in small batches until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Alternatively, shallow‑fry them in a Kuzhi Paniyaram pan for a healthier version, flipping when golden.
Remove the fried paneer balls onto an absorbent paper to drain excess oil.
Serve the Cashew Nut Stuffed Paneer Balls with green chutney.

title: Carrot Chutney Recipe
instructions: Soak the dry red chillies and mustard seeds in just enough water for 1 hour or more.

Chop the carrots very finely (do not grate them). Make a fine paste of the red chilly and mustard in a mixer grinder. Add 3/4th of the carrots and give it one quick blend. Do not make it into a paste.
Heat the oil for tempering in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let it crackle.
Add curry leaves and let it crisp up. Once done, add the ground carrot and chopped carrot in the pan.
Add 1/4 cup of water to the pan, add salt and jaggery and boil on a low flame until the oil separates.
Allow it to cool, then store in an airtight jar.
Serve Carrot Chutney with Kanchipuram Idlis, Phulkas or Neer Dosa.

title: Instant Mixed Vegetable Pickle Recipe
ingredients: 100 grams Carrot (Gajjar), diced into 1/2 centimetre cubes
100 grams Green beans (French Beans), chopped similarly
instructions: To begin making the Instant Mixed Vegetable Pickle recipe, clean and dry all the vegetables on a kitchen towel.
Chop them finely and tip them into a mixing bowl and add the juice of one lemon and a teaspoon of salt and mix through the vegetables.
In a small mixing jar, add the ingredients for the marinating paste and grind to a smooth paste in a grinder without adding any water.
Mix this paste through the vegetables and let it sit for at least 2 hours before serving.
It stays fresh for a week to a fortnight and needs to be kept in the fridge at all times.
Serve Instant Mixed Vegetable Pickle with curd rice for a comforting week day meal.

title: Tea Spiced Nuts Recipe (Skillet Roasted)
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Vanilla Extract , or 1 vanilla pod
instructions: To begin making the Tea Spiced Nuts Recipe, heat 1/2 tablespoon of butter on medium flame and add in all the nuts.
Roast till the nuts are aromatic and turn golden brown. Once done remove it into a bowl and keep aside.
Now, add the remaining butter to the same pan, add in the tea leaves and dried rose petals. Saute for 30 seconds.
Add the cinnamon powder, vanilla extract, pepper, paprika powder and mix well.
Add the honey and let the mix bubble. Now, add in the roasted nuts, sea salt and let the spice mixture coat the nuts well. Keep stirring for a minutes.
Once done, switch off the heat and transfer the nuts into a plate and separate out each nut. Let it cool and store it into a jar until serving.
Serve the Tea Spiced Nuts Recipe as a mid-morning snack along with a fruit or a hand full as a post workout snack.

title: Safed Murgh Handi Recipe - Chicken In White Gravy
instructions: To begin making Safed Murgh Handi Recipe, prep all the ingredients and keep them ready.
