In a kadai, heat a little oil and add onions when the oil is hot. Saute till translucent and switch off.
Take the onions out on a plate and allow the sauteed onions to cool a bit. Once the onions are cooled, with the help of a hand blender, blend it to a smooth paste.
Heat ghee in the same kadai and once the ghee is hot, on a medium heat, add cumin seeds. Saute for a few seconds until they sizzle.
Immediately add green cardamom, cinnamon stick, stir for a few more seconds till the cardamom puffs up and theres a nice aroma arising from the kadai.
Add ginger garlic paste in saute on low heat for about half a minute to one minute, till the raw smell goes away.
Now add onion paste and saute till the mixture comes together and appears blended well.

At this point, add yogurt and coconut milk, keep the heat to medium and add all the masalas including kadhi masala and cook till the yogurt and coconut milk gets blended well and appears as one white gravy.
Add chicken now, add in curry leaves and raisins and mix well.
Close the kadai and cook well for about 10 minutes or till the chicken is tender. (You can add about 1/2 cup of water at this stage)
Serve Safed Murgh Handi Recipe (Chicken In White Gravy).

title: Air fried Yogurt & Cottage Cheese Kebabs Recipe
instructions: Wash and boil the potatoes, peel off their skins, and place them in a mixing bowl.
Add crumbled cottage cheese, chopped green chillies, and grated ginger to the bowl.
Add thick yogurt (or hung curd), salt, red chilli powder, garam masala, and chopped coriander leaves and mix.
Add singhara flour and combine everything well.
Take small portions, shape them into patties, and place them on a plate.
Preheat the air fryer to 180°C for 10 minutes.
Place the kebabs in the air fryer basket and brush the tops with a little oil.
Air‑fry for 15–18 minutes until golden brown; optionally brush with more oil halfway through.
Serve the kebabs with green chutney, Palak Makhana, Rajgira Puri, or Singhare Atte Ka Halwa.

title: Spicy Mixed Vegetables Rice Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: Oil, as needed to shallow fry
instructions: To prepare Spicy Mixed Vegetables Rice Cutlet Recipe, take a mixing bowl and add cooked rice, mashed boiled potato, chopped onion, chopped green chilli, grated carrot, chopped coriander leaves, mix everything well.
Now add all the spices: start with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala and salt.
Mix everything well and make sure that cooked rice also gets mashed properly.
Shape the mixture into medium‑size patties.
Take another bowl and add all purpose flour and water, mix them to get a pourable consistency batter.
Put some plain flour on one side and bread crumbs on the other side on your work surface.
Roll patties in plain flour first, then dip them in the all purpose flour batter and then in bread crumbs.
Repeat the same process: first plain flour, then dip in all purpose flour batter, then in bread crumbs.
Now heat 3–4 tablespoons oil in a frying pan or skillet, and place the cutlets in the pan.
Let them cook until the base is lightly browned and crispy, then flip and fry the other side.
Flip again and fry them until they are crisp and golden.
Once they are nicely crisp and golden, remove the cutlets from the pan and place them on a paper towel.
Spicy Mixed Vegetables Rice Cutlet Recipe is ready to be served with green chutney and date‑tamarind chutney.

title: Beetroot Raita Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Beetroot Raita, first get all the ingredients ready and finely grate the beetroot and keep aside.

In a large mixing bowl, add the yogurt, salt, cumin powder, green chillies and grated beetroot. Whisk well to combine. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste. Transfer the raita to a serving bowl.
Make the seasoning.
Heat oil in a tadka pan; add the mustard seeds, urad dal and allow it to crackle and the dal to turn golden brown and crisp. Finally stir in the curry leaves and turn off the heat.
Pour the seasoning onto the Beetroot Raita and serve.
Serve the Beetroot Raita along with Paneer Stuffed Ragi Paratha or as a side dish with your main course meal.

title: Soya Pilaf/Pulav Recipe
ingredients: Mint Leaves (Pudina), a few sprigs chopped
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch chopped
instructions: To begin making the Soya Pilaf recipe, wash, drain and soak rice in fresh water for minimum 30 minutes before cooking.
In a saucepan, boil water and add soya chunks in it and boil. Drain and keep aside to cool. Once cool, squeeze them to take off excess water and keep them separate in a plate/bowl.
Heat oil/ghee in a wok, add the potatoes, fry them and keep it aside. In the same pan, add bay leaf, all the dry whole garam masala, shahi jeera in the remaining ghee/oil and allow it to splutter.
Add finely chopped onions and fry till light and translucent. Add green chillies, ginger paste, garlic paste and fry for about a minute on low medium heat.
Add chopped tomato along with coriander powder, red chilli powder and fry well till the ghee starts leaving from the sides.
Add soya chunks and salt, mix all together, fry again for 1-2 minutes.
After 1-2 minutes, add a little water just to wet the masala and cook it with the lid closed on low flame.
Meanwhile in another large thick bottomed vessel, add lots of water with little salt, few drops of oil and lemon juice and allow it to boil.
Once the water is hot and starts boiling, add soaked rice and cook till the rice is 90% done.
Turn off the gas and strain the rice very carefully and spread it in a big flat tray so that the grains doesn't stick to each other. Allow it to cool a bit. Do not stir them as the grains may break.
The next step is to assemble and layer the Soya Pilaf. Take a vessel in which you want to assemble the pilaf. Spread rice at the bottom of the vessel and then layer it with some soya gravy.
Spread some rice again and then pour the remaining soya gravy on it with fried potatoes.
Again, spread some rice and garnish it with fresh mint leaf, freshly chopped coriander, lemon juice, fried onions, some kewda water and fried dry fruits.
Close the lid and allow the pilaf to cook for another 10 mins on low flame. For this take an iron tawa and place the pilaf vessel on it.
Once the pilaf is done, hold the vessel from both sides and shake it vigorously, this will mix the soya gravy and the rice evenly inside without breaking the grains.
Serve Soya Pilaf with Burani Raita, Beetroot Raita or any other Raita of your choice.

title: Carrot Custard Pudding Recipe
instructions: Wash the carrot, peel the skin and grate it. Take custard powder in a bowl, add 6 tablespoons of milk to it and mix without lumps. Keep aside.
Boil 3 cups of milk in a pan. Once it comes to boil, reduce the flame and add grated carrots to it.
Mix well and cook for 5 to 10 minutes until the carrots get cooked. Add the sugar and prepared custard mixture.
Keep stirring over medium flame until the custard becomes slightly thick. Switch off the flame and allow it to cool.
Refrigerate for an hour before serving. Transfer the chilled custard to a serving bowl and garnish with chopped nuts.
Serve Carrot Custard Pudding as a dessert after your meal of Aloo Ki Sabzi, Boondi Ka Raita and Puri.

title: Instant Chilli Pickle Recipe
instructions: To make instant chilli pickle, wash and chop the green chillies.
Heat oil in a thick bottomed pan.
Now add chillies, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix well.
Cover and cook for approximate 2 to 3 minutes on low heat or till tender.
Now open the lid and add pickle masala.
Stir fry for a minute on low heat. Switch off.
Instant chilli pickle recipe is ready to be served as an accompaniment with cooked rice, roti, poori or aloo paratha.

title: Chili Coriander and Capsicum Rusk Chutney Recipe
instructions: Clean the coriander leaves thoroughly, wash them, pat dry and set aside.
Dry roast the peanuts in a skillet until crisp and golden, crush them roughly between your palms and remove the skins if present.
Add all the ingredients into a mixer grinder and grind into a smooth paste; adjust salt and spice to taste, then transfer the chutney to a serving bowl.
The chutney keeps well for a week when refrigerated.
Serve the chutney as a spread on top of Sabudana Vada or any tea‑time snack.

title: Garlic And Pepper Mushroom Stir Fry Recipe
ingredients: 10 cloves Garlic, crushed (in a mortar and pestle)
4 tablespoons Black pepper powder, freshly ground
3 sprig Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, chopped for garnish
instructions: Thoroughly wash the mushrooms, pat dry, and set aside; smash the garlic pods and crush the pepper, setting both aside separately.
Heat a wok, add oil, then add garlic and pearl onions, sauté for about a minute until aromatic.
Add pepper powder and salt, mixing well.
Add mushrooms to the spicy mix, toss until coated, stir constantly and cook for 3-5 minutes until water evaporates and mushrooms are cooked, avoiding overcooking.
Remove from heat, sprinkle with freshly chopped coriander leaves, and serve.
Serve the Garlic & Pepper Mushroom Stir Fry with Caramelised Onion Rosemary Chicken and Spring Onion & Roasted Garlic Brown Rice.

title: Achari Paratha Roll Recipe
instructions: Add salt and water to the wheat flour and knead to a smooth dough; add 1 or 2 tsp oil and knead again, then set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add chopped pumpkin, green peas and potato cubes.
Mix well, then add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala, asafoetida and salt to taste; cook for 8-10 minutes on low flame.
Turn off the heat and ensure the mixture is well combined.
Divide the dough into equal balls, press each between the palms, dust both sides, and roll into a thin round paratha.
Spread 1 or 2 tsp achari masala on one side of the paratha and roll it in one direction to form a Swiss‑roll shape.
Press the rolled paratha again between the palms, dust with flour, and roll into a round paratha.
Heat a tava or skillet and cook the rolled paratha until golden brown on both sides; repeat with remaining dough.
Take a cooked paratha, stuff it with the potato‑pumpkin masala, fold the sides, and seal the top with a toothpick.
Serve the Achari Masala Roll with ketchup, any dip of choice, or a smoothie.

title: Methi Muthiya (Wheat Flour And Fenugreek Dumplings) Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), washed and roughly chopped
Oil, for deep frying (for fried Muthiyas)
instructions: Add all the ingredients under ‘Muthiya dough’ in a mixing bowl.
Add some water and mix till everything just comes together; do not knead the dough too much.
Pinch small lime sized balls from the dough and shape them into small elongated dumplings using the palm of your hands.
Heat oil in a deep fry pan and deep fry the dumplings on medium heat until golden brown.
Drain the fried dumplings on a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil and serve them hot.
Lightly oil a strainer or steaming bowl and steam the dumplings for about 12-15 minutes, or until a knife inserted comes out clean.
In a flat non‑stick pan, heat oil and add mustard seeds; when they crackle, add cumin and fennel seeds.
Add the steamed dumplings to the pan and fry until they turn a light golden colour.
Serve Methi Muthiya with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or Gujarati Kadhi.

title: Tofu Masala Rice Recipe (Tofu Pulao)
ingredients: 1/2 Red Yellow or Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), chopped
instructions: To begin with Tofu masala rice, wash and soak basmati rice in water for 1/2 an hour. Drain and keep aside.
Heat ghee in a saucepan on medium heat. Once hot, add the cumin seeds and let it splutter. Add chopped onions, green chilli and ginger garlic paste and sauté till onion turns golden brown.
Now add the tomatoes and capsicum in the pan along with chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and garam masala, and let it cook for 5-7 minutes.
Add the diced tofu along with salt and sauté till the tofu turns slightly brown in colour.
Add 2 cups of water and check for salt (add more salt if necessary).
Cover the pan and once the mixture comes to a boil, turn the heat to low and simmer until all the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and allow the rice to rest for about 5 minutes before opening.
Garnish with chopped coriander and serve the Tofu Masala Rice hot with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita or any other vegetable raita of your choice.

title: Railway Mutton Curry Recipe
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Curd (Dahi / Yogurt) , or lemon juice
instructions: To begin making the Railway Mutton Curry, firstly marinate the Mutton with ginger garlic paste, yogurt, turmeric powder, mustard oil, red chilli powder, salt for minimum 3 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Dry roast fennel seeds, black peppercorn, coriander and cumin seeds and grind them to a fine powder.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into half. Fry the potatoes. Don’t make them brown and fry till the color becomes light golden brown. Remove and keep them aside.
Heat oil in the Pressure cooker and once the oil is heated, put the whole Garam masala. Let them fry and sizzle for couple of minutes.
Now add the ginger and garlic pastes and sauté till their raw smell is gone.
Add the sliced onions along with a pinch of salt and sauté till they turn brown.
Now add the tomato puree, green chilli, turmeric powder, red chili powder, fennel, coriander, cumin, black peppercorn powder and saute till oil leaves the sides.

Add the mutton pieces. Increase the heat to a high and stir continuously to avoid sticking to the bottom. Now reduce the heat to a medium and continue cooking the meat without the lid. The meat will release juices and you can see a thin layer of oil on top of the pieces.
Once it gets to this point, add the fried potatoes and water. Close the lid and pressure cook for 3 to 4 whistle on high heat and then reduce the heat and cook on a low flame for 5 minutes.

Once done, switch off the heat and let it sit for sometime till the pressure dies down. After opening the lid add the coconut milk and give everything a good stir. Add a spoon of ghee and 1/2 teaspoon of powdered garam masala.
Close the lid and let the flours seep into the meat properly for 10 to 12 minutes and serve hot.
Serve Railway Mutton Curry along with Jeera Rice / Phulka and Burani Raita for a weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Chicken Kofta Curry Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Chicken Kofta Curry Recipe, first prep all the ingredients and keep it ready.
To mince the chicken, place it in your mixer grinder jar and mince until smooth.
In mixing bowl, add the minced chicken, the garlic, onion, garam masala, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and salt. Sir well to combine and make balls of the mixture and keep aside.
The next step is to make the kofta curry gravy.
Heat oil or ghee in a pan; add the onion, ginger and garlic. Saute until the onion becomes soft and tender.

Once the onions have softened, add the tomato puree, the turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, coriander powder and salt. Stir well and add the chicken kofta balls and simmer the gravy until the chicken kofta is cooked well.

It will take about 5 to 6 minutes. Ensure you cover the pan and simmer the chicken kofta curry. Once done, cut the kofta a little to check if it is cooked. You can add water to adjust the consistency of the Chicken Kofta Curry.
Check the salt and spices of the Chicken Kofta Curry and adjust according to your taste.
Once done, stir in the honey and cream and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes and turn off the heat. Transfer the Chicken Kofta Curry into a serving bowl, stir in the coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve this delicious Chicken Kofta Curry along with a Garlic Naan, Palak Paneer and Dal Makhani for a delicious Indian Dinner.

title: Mahali Kizhangu Thayir Urugaai Recipe (Mahali Root Curd Pickle)
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Mustard seeds (Rai/ Kadugu), ground to powder
instructions: To begin making the Mahali Kizhangu Thayir Urugaai recipe, soak the mahali in water as it would have mud in it. Wash it nicely.
Remove any black parts by chopping. We need to ideally identify while picking up but at times we can make out only while cutting.
Peel the skin. Cut the Mahali from the middle and remove the thick stem like part which is found in the middle. It is very hard and cannot be consumed.
Chop the mahali into small cubes. In a big mixing bowl, add turmeric powder, chilli powder, mustard seeds powder, curd, lemon juice and the required salt.
Mix everything well and leave it for 2 days in an airtight container.
After 2 days, the pickle is ready to be consumed. Serve Mahali Kizhangu Thayir Urugaai along with Curd Rice or Spinach and Coriander Dosa for a light lunch or dinner.

title: Horsegram Tikki Recipe
ingredients: 5 tablespoons Gram flour (besan), for coating before frying
instructions: Clean and wash the horse gram, soak for one hour and pressure cook for up to 6 whistles with 1.5 cups of water.
Open the cooker, strain the water, cool the horse gram and grind with very little or no water together with dry mango powder and cloves of garlic into a fine paste.
Dry roast red chilies, coriander seeds and cumin seeds until aromatic, let cool, then grind into a dry powder.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan on medium, add some oil, then add cumin seeds and stir‑fry until brown; add chopped onion and sauté until browned.
Add ginger paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears; add chopped tomatoes and cook until mushy.
Add the ground masala powder and sauté until it combines well with the onions and tomatoes.
Add the horse gram paste and potato mash, mix well and keep the pan covered for 3‑4 minutes; season with black salt and amchur powder.
Mix again, keep the lid closed for another 2 minutes, then turn off the heat; garnish with chopped coriander leaves and lemon juice.
Once the mixture cools, take a handful and shape into a tikki.
Coat each tikki with gram flour (besan) and set aside.
In a shallow pan with some oil, shallow‑fry the tikkis for about 2 minutes on each side until browned; drain on paper towels.
Serve the horsegram tikkis with dhania pudina chutney or imli chutney, accompanied by ginger cardamom chai.

title: No Onion No Garlic Aloo Gajar Ki Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 3 Green Chillies, slit or finely chopped
Salt, to taste or kala namak (for fasting)
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, handful for garnish, chopped
instructions: Prep all ingredients. Cook the potatoes in a pressure cooker, peel the skin and cut into cubes.
Steam the carrots either in the pressure cooker or in a steamer and keep aside.

Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat, add the cumin seeds and allow them to crackle. Add the ginger and sauté for a few seconds. Add the potatoes, carrots, and the remaining masalas; toss well. Add salt, cover the pan and cook until the vegetables are done.
Check the salt and spices, adjust to taste, then add a squeeze of lemon and stir in the coriander leaves.
Serve the Aloo Gajar Ki Sabzi with Phulkas and Rajasthani Kadhi.

title: Cauliflower And Methi Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), finely chopped
instructions: Heat oil in a kadhai; when the oil gets heated, add cumin seeds.
Once the cumin seeds start crackling, add finely chopped onion and fry till onion turns pinkish and soft.
Add finely chopped garlic and green chilies and stir till the raw smell of garlic goes away.
Add grated cauliflower and let it cook for another 10 minutes.
Add the finely chopped methi leaves and stir till the methi leaves are cooked.
Add turmeric and red chili powder and stir.
Finally, add salt according to your taste, mix and switch off the gas. Let the stuffing cool down.
While the stuffing cools down, make the dough for the parathas. Add salt and oil to wheat flour and mix.
Mould it into a soft yet firm dough by adding water little at a time. Cover the dough with muslin cloth for 30 minutes.
Make small balls from the dough of equal size. The size should be a little bigger than a table tennis ball.
Roll the dough ball into a little bit of dry wheat flour and roll it into a small thick flat round shape.
Place 2 tablespoons of the stuffing on it and close from all sides. Dust it in dry whole wheat flour and roll it into a bigger round shape, like a chapati.
If you see any air bubbles while rolling, simply pat it gently with your fingertips.
Apply 1 teaspoon ghee on the frying pan and place the paratha on it.
After 2-3 minutes, apply 1 teaspoon ghee on the upper side and turn. Let it cook for 2-3 minutes more.
Serve Cauliflower And Methi Paratha with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Pumpkin Raita.

title: Potato Onion Cheela Recipe
ingredients: Nutralite Garlic & Oregano Spread, as required
instructions: To begin making the Potato Onion Cheela recipe, add finely grated potatoes for 5 minutes in cold water.
Take a bowl, add gram flour and whole wheat flour. Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, black pepper powder and salt to taste. Add water and make a smooth batter.
Take grated potato out from cold water and add it to the gram and whole wheat batter. Mix it well and keep it aside.

Heat one tablespoon Nutralite Garlic & Oregano Spread in a nonstick pan, spread one portion of potato and onion mixture on the pan thinly and cook, turning sides until crisp and properly cooked. Serve hot.
Serve Potato Onion Cheela along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Tomato Chutney or any other chutney for your breakfast or with Masala Chai during your tea time break.

title: Chicken In A Foil Recipe
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Cashew nuts, ground to paste
1-1/2 tablespoons Poppy seeds, ground to paste
instructions: To begin making Chicken In A Foil Recipe, marinate chicken legs in a mixing bowl by adding in the ginger garlic paste, tandoori masala, curd, red chilli sauce, salt and lemon juice.
Mix well to coat the chicken and let the chicken legs rest for about 30 minutes.
Preheat oven at 400 Deg F for about 10 minutes.
Arrange the chicken pieces on a sheet of foil, close the foil around the chicken to make a parcel and bake for 25 minutes.
In a pan add oil, tomato puree, chilli powder, poppy seed paste, dry coconut powder, cashew paste, cumin powder and cook till the mixture is cooked and comes together.
When the chicken is done in oven, mix it with the prepared sauce.
Serve Chicken In A Foil Recipe along with Cheese Garlic Naan Recipe, Pickled Onions, Pakki Mutton Biryani Recipe and Burani Raita for a complete Sunday lunch.

title: Baked & Crisp Whole Wheat Methi Puri Recipe (Healthy Snack)
instructions: To begin making the Whole Wheat Methi Puri Recipe, combine all the ingredients in a large mixing bowl. Add the ghee as well into the flour mixture and you will notice it will form a crumb like texture.
Check the salt levels and adjust to suit your taste. You can optionally add chilli powder or crushed black pepper to add to the spice.
Gradually add little water at a time and knead to make a firm yet smooth dough. It should be more firm than the roti dough.
Preheat the oven to 180 C. Dust the baking sheets with flour and keep aside.

Next, roll the Methi Puri (Mathri) Dough into a large circle, using a circular cookie cutter, cut the puris into circles. At home we like our puris to be on the thinner side. So based on your personal preference, adjust the thickness of the puris.
Arrange the cut methi puris on the dusted baking tray and place it in the preheated oven to bake until golden brown and crisp (about 10 to 12 minutes).
Once done, allow the Baked Methi Puris (Mathris) to cool down before storing it in airtight containers.
Serve the Baked Methi Puris (Mathris) as a tea time snack or pack into the school snack boxes for kids topped with cheese.

title: Watermelon Seeds Rice Recipe
instructions: To begin making Watermelon Seeds Rice Recipe, dry roast the watermelon seeds and dry red chilies until the seeds start spluttering and popping. Turn off the heat and let them cool.
Once cooled, transfer the dry roasted seeds and chilies to the mixie jar. Add salt and grind it to a coarse powder.
Place a kadai on medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon oil to it. Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle. Once the mustard seeds crackle, add the urad dal, curry leaves and hing.
At this stage, add the peanuts and fry until they turn slightly brown. Add the rice and mix well. Add the coarsely ground watermelon seeds powder. Mix all the ingredients well.
Serve Watermelon Seeds Rice warm or at room temperature with papad as a one dish meal.
You can try this recipe with pumpkin seeds or melon seeds as well.

title: Mushroom Poha Cutlets Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Poha (Flattened rice), soaked for 15 minutes
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a handful, finely chopped
Whole Wheat Bread crumbs or Semolina, for coating
instructions: Wash and soak poha in water for fifteen minutes, then drain excess water and set aside.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a small pan over medium-low heat, add the onions and sauté until translucent.
Add green chillies, ginger, grated carrot and chopped beans to the pan; sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened, then switch off heat and let the mixture cool.
When the mixture is lukewarm, add chopped mushrooms, red chilli powder, garam masala, chaat masala, amchur, the soaked and drained poha, and salt; mash slightly to form a thick mixture.
Take small portions, roll them into balls, then press to flatten into cutlets; continue until all mixture is used.
Heat a non‑stick shallow frying pan with a tablespoon of oil over medium heat.
Spread a layer of semolina or bread crumbs on a plate for coating.
Press each cutlet onto the breadcrumbs/semolina to coat all sides.
Shallow fry the cutlets until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side on low‑medium heat.
Serve the Mushroom Poha Cutlets with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Date and Tamarind Chutney, Kashmiri Style Nadir Monjvor (Lotus Stem Cutlets) or Herbed Baby Potatoes as appetizers.

title: Murgh Aloo Tikki Recipe - Chicken & Potato Tikki
ingredients: 4 Green Chillies, (adjust as spice preference) finely chopped
instructions: In a mixing bowl, add the minced chicken, boiled and mashed potatoes, onion, green chillies, coriander leaves, mint leaves, salt, black pepper powder, ginger-garlic paste, and egg; mix until well combined.
Heat a cast iron pan for shallow frying.
Divide the chicken mixture into equal portions, roll each portion into a ball and flatten into discs.
Add 1 teaspoon of oil to the pan, place the chicken patties, and shallow fry on medium flame until golden brown and cooked on both sides.
Remove the patties from the pan and place them on kitchen paper to drain excess oil.
Serve the Murgh Aloo Tikki with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai as an evening snack.

title: Meat Ka Achaar Recipe (Goat Pickle)
ingredients: 1 kg Mutton, boneless, cut in small bite size pieces
instructions: To begin making the Meat Ka Achaar recipe, in a heavy bottomed pan of suitable size, add the meat, turmeric powder and salt.
Cook the meat on medium heat (covered), stirring it occasionally to make sure it doesn’t stick to the bottom. The meat will take about 40 minutes to cook though it depends on the size of the pieces.

If the liquids dry up and you find the meat is sticking too much to the bottom of the pan, add water a tablespoon at a time and make sure all the water has completely dried up once the meat is cooked.
In a separate heavy bottomed pan, heat the oil, add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf.
Then add the cooked meat and keep the flame low-medium so as not to excessively fry the meat which in turn would make it hard.
After a couple of minutes add the garlic and continue cooking for a minute or two. If using mustard oil, heat it to smoking point first, cool slightly then use as usual.
Take it off the heat and add the fennel, cumin and nigella seeds. Let it cool for 2 to 3 minutes then add the chilli powder and lemon juice. Taste for salt and adjust accordingly.
Store in a sterilized jar if you plan to keep it for long. Keep the pickle refrigerated in a regular jar with a lid, as it never lasts more than a week.
Serve the Meat Ka Achaar as a side dish with dal chawal or Tawa Parathas.

title: Indian Chicken Keema Sliders Recipe
ingredients: 2-3 tablespoon Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, chopped, for garnish
instructions: To begin making the Indian Chicken Keema Sliders Recipe, firstly roast all the masalas including cumin seeds, cinnamon stick, cloves, black pepper corns, coriander seeds, star anise and Kashmiri dry red chillies at low heat in a flat pan till fragrant. Set it aside.
Once cool, powder them or pound in a pestle and mortar. Heat the oil in a pan on medium-high flame.
Once the oil is hot and simmering, add the onion, ginger, garlic and green chillies.
Keep an eye on it and keep sautéing for about 15-20 minutes till the onions moisture and start to turn brown.
Reduce the flame to low, add the ground spices. Saute for 20 seconds and add in the onions. Add the chopped tomatoes with their water and keep cooking till the tomatoes soften and turn mushy.
If the mixture is burning, add a splash of water. This should take another 10 minutes. Add yogurt in 3 batches, mixing well every time you add the yogurt.
Cook for about 2 minutes. Next add in the chicken keema and with your ladle break any clumps and mix well.
Do this step quickly before the chicken starts to cook to avoid lumps. Add water if required, cook the chicken in the spices for about 10-15 minutes till the curry starts to simmer.
Once it simmers (bubbles on the surface) cook for another 5 minutes to ensure it's done. Finish with juice of one whole lemon and coriander leaves.
Toast the slider buns with a little bit of butter. Scoop the chicken keema inside and serve.
Serve Indian Chicken Keema Sliders along with other starters such as Paneer Tikka and a chilled glass of your favourite mocktail for house parties.

title: Cauliflower Moong Dal Recipe
instructions: Dry roast the moong dal for a few minutes to get a nice aroma.
Soak the dal in water for about 15-20 minutes.
Wash the dal and put it in a saucepan. Add around 4 cups of water, salt, turmeric powder, cumin powder and the whole green chili to the dal.
Let the dal cook for around 15-20 minutes or until the dal becomes just soft.
Heat oil or ghee in another pan/kadai.
Add the chopped onion in the oil and fry until soft.
Add the ginger, tomato and stir to mix. If needed, add a little water so the masala does not burn. Stir until everything is cooked well.
Add the cauliflower florets in the pan and stir carefully to coat all the florets with the masala.
Carefully pour the cooked dal into the pan, give a stir, cover and let it cook for another 15-20 minutes or until the cauliflower becomes soft.
Sprinkle garam masala on top, switch off the heat and serve.

title: Stuffed Chicken Recipe With Mixed Vegetables
ingredients: 4 tablespoons cashew nuts, ground to paste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper powder, freshly ground
2 tablespoons coriander leaves, chopped (plus more for garnish)
instructions: Wash and clean the whole chicken thoroughly.
Marinate the chicken with tandoori masala, curd, salt, and lemon juice; let it rest for 2-3 hours.
Bake the marinated chicken at 425 °F for 45 minutes.
Prepare the stuffing by mixing boiled mashed potatoes, grated carrots, boiled green peas, chopped coriander leaves, chaat masala, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl; set aside.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Heat oil in a pan over medium flame, add tomato puree, tomato ketchup, salt, red chilli powder, and cashew paste; once bubbling, reduce heat and stir in the fresh cream.
Simmer the gravy for a couple of minutes until thick and creamy.
Cut open the baked chicken, stuff it with the vegetable mixture, top with the tomato gravy, and bake at 350 °F for an additional 15 minutes.
Serve the stuffed chicken with butter garlic naan and carrot cucumber tomato salad with lemon and coriander.

title: Moong Dal With Radish Greens Recipe
ingredients: Mooli Ke Patte (Radish Greens), a bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Clean and wash the moong dal, then soak it in water for 10-15 minutes.
Wash the radish greens well and chop them finely.
In a pressure cooker, heat a teaspoon of oil over medium heat, add chopped garlic and grated ginger, and stir‑fry on low heat until garlic turns light brown.

Add the soaked moong dal along with turmeric powder, red chili powder, mango powder and 2 cups of water; stir to combine. Close the lid and cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 whistles, then turn off the heat and allow pressure to release naturally.
While the dal cooks, heat a teaspoon of oil in a pan over medium heat, add the chopped radish greens and cook until wilted and cooked through; set aside.
Once pressure has released, open the cooker and gently mash the dal with the back of a spoon to thicken. Add the cooked radish greens, stir to combine, and adjust salt and spices to taste.
Prepare the tempering: in a tadka pan heat some ghee on medium heat, add cumin seeds and let them crackle, then add the dry red chillies and roast for a few seconds before turning off the heat.
Pour the tempering over the dal, stir to combine, and serve hot with phulkas, rice, or salad.

title: Tomato Onion Gravy Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Tomato Onion Gravy Sabzi recipe, firstly heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan.
Add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing. Let the mustard seeds splutter.
Once it is done, add green chillies, garlic cloves and onions. Cook it till the onions becomes soft and translucent.
Once it is done, add tomatoes and let it cook for about 2 to 3 minutes.
Once done, add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and salt.
Let it cook for about 4 to 5 minutes. Next, add the required water and let it cook for about 8 to 10 minutes.
When it is properly cooked, garnish it with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.
Serve Tomato Onion Gravy Sabzi along with Gujarati Dal and Phulkas for a weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Spicy Broken Wheat Khichdi With Vegetables Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, few sprigs, finely chopped
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy bottomed pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, bay leaf, curry leaves, dry red chillies and cloves.
When the mustard seeds splutter, add the ginger-garlic paste and green chillies; sauté for a few seconds on low flame.
Add the onions and cook until they turn translucent.
Add the peas, carrots, and potatoes; cook for about 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and the broken wheat, then stir in red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and salt to taste.
Cook for 2 minutes, then add the required water. Cover with a lid and cook until the broken wheat and vegetables are fully cooked.
Turn off the flame and garnish with chopped coriander.
Serve the Spicy Broken Wheat Khichdi with Lauki Raita, papad, and Aam Ka Achaar for a quick weeknight dinner.

title: Dal And Vegetable Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked & cooked
1/4 cup Black Eyed Beans (Lobia), soaked & cooked
1/4 cup Kala Chana (Brown Chickpeas), soaked & cooked
Mint Leaves (Pudina), small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Dal and Vegetable Kebab Recipe, soak the dal for 8 hours, cook them until soft in a pressure cooker for 2 whistles and let the pressure release naturally. Drain the excess water and coarsely mash them using a food processor or a hand blender.
Powder the bread by grinding in a mixer. Chop mint and any other leaves included for the vegetables.
Combine all the ingredients except the oil. Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste.
Take a 6 medium size bamboo skewers and soak it in water for an hour. This is needed else the sticks will burn.

Take an oven tray and cover it with aluminum foil and brush with oil. Shape the kebabs into cylinders and slice the skewers into the vegetable kebab. Shape the vegetable kebabs and press them so it holds well.
Place the Dal and Vegetable Kebab on the greased baking tray. Brush the vegetable kebabs with oil and refrigerate in for at least one hour.

Preheat the oven for 180 C for about 10 minutes. Place the kebabs in the oven and make for about 20 minutes until golden brown. Keep checking if the bottom portion of kebab is cooked. If it's cooked and crispy turn around to cook the other side. If needed you may brush the oil.
Ensure all the sides are crispy and inside is soft, that’s the indication that the kebab is cooked. Remove the Vegetable Kebab from the oven and serve warm.
Serve the Dal and Vegetable Kebab Recipe along with Mint Chutney and a cup of Filter Coffee as a tea time snack or as an appetizer for parties.

title: Instant Red Chilli Pickle Recipe
instructions: Wash the fresh red chillies and wipe them with a kitchen towel.
De-seed the chillies and cut them lengthwise; in a separate bowl, mix the mustard seeds, fennel seeds, salt, turmeric powder, lemon juice, and about half the oil.
Add the red chillies into this mixture and stir well.
Transfer the mixture to a pickle jar, pour the remaining oil over it, and let it rest for 2-3 hours.
After 3 hours, serve the instant red chilli pickle with parathas or seasoned curd rice.

title: Green Chilli Chicken Fry Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Chicken, cut into medium size pieces
18 Green Chillies, adjust as per spice preference
instructions: Wash chicken pieces well and pat dry them.
Add 1 teaspoon salt and juice of half lime into the chicken pieces, mix well; cover and marinate for at least 30 minutes in fridge.
Grind together the green chilies, ginger pieces, garlic cloves, coriander leaves, and onions into a paste in a mixer grinder.
Add the tomatoes in a mixer grinder with a little water and puree them; set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Once hot, add cloves and cinnamon stick, then add the green chilli paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears, about 2 minutes.
Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook until the colour of the chicken changes.
Add tomato puree and cook till oil separates from the sides of the pan.
Add coriander powder and salt to taste and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add 1/2 to 1 cup water and cook the chicken covered until fully cooked; then remove from pan.
Serve the Green Chilli Chicken Fry as a starter or side dish with Dal Fry and Steamed Rice.

title: Zucchini Thogayal (Tangy and Spicy Zucchini Chutney)
ingredients: 2 Green zucchini, cut into small cubes
instructions: Heat a teaspoon oil in a heavy bottomed pan; add the cut zucchini along with a little salt and saute until soft and tender. Turn off heat and allow it to cool.
In another small pan, roast the fenugreek seeds, dry red chillies and urad dal until it releases a roasted aroma and is slightly browned.
Grind the roasted ingredients, the cooked zucchini, the tamarind and curry leaves together until it forms a smooth paste. Check the salt and adjust to taste.
Heat a little oil in a pan; add mustard seeds, dry red chillies and curry leaves. Allow it to crackle and the red chillies to roast. Add this tempering to the zucchini thogayal.
Serve the Zucchini Thogayal along with Mixed Vegetable Sambar, a hot bowl of rice and ghee.

title: Peanut Bhel Recipe
instructions: Begin by preparing the spiced peanuts.
Heat oil in a pan, add the peanuts and roast until they pop and turn brown, stirring on medium heat; you may remove the outer skin if desired.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, chaat masala, and salt; mix well and sauté for a couple of minutes until the peanuts are well coated.
In a large bowl, combine the chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, and coriander leaves; mix thoroughly.
Add the spiced peanuts and lemon juice to the bowl; mix well and adjust salt seasoning as needed.
Divide the bhel into four plates, garnish with additional coriander leaves and sev, then serve.
Serve the Peanut Bhel as a party appetizer or evening tea‑time snack, optionally with a cup of Adrak Chai (Indian style ginger tea).

title: Grated Beetroot Chilli Paratha Recipe
instructions: Wash and peel the beetroot, then grate it finely.
In a mixing bowl, combine the grated beetroot, cumin powder, salt, red chilli powder, and ghee; mix all ingredients except the wheat flour.
In another bowl, add whole wheat flour and knead it into a smooth dough with enough water.
Take a small portion of the wheat flour dough and flatten it with a rolling pin into a small circle large enough to hold the filling.
Place 1–2 tablespoons of the beetroot filling in the center, bring the edges together with fingers, and remove any excess dough after joining the ends.
Using some dry flour to prevent sticking, roll the stuffed dough with a rolling pin to a uniform, slightly thick paratha.
Heat a tawa over medium heat and place the paratha on the hot surface.
Roast for about a minute, then flip and cook the other side for a minute or until done.
Apply butter or oil as needed to grease the paratha while cooking.
Serve the Grated Beetroot Chilli Paratha with Burani Raita, Mooli Raita, or homemade ghee.

title: Potato Patties Stuffed With Bell Pepper, Coconut & Dry Fruits Recipe
instructions: Take a mixer jar and add green bell pepper, spicy chili, ginger paste, lemon and sugar and make a fine paste; then add peanuts and sesame seeds and grind them coarsely.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl, add freshly grated coconut, raisins, clove powder, cinnamon powder, and salt, and form small balls (about 10‑12 medium‑size).
In another bowl combine the boiled and mashed potatoes with salt; mix well and, if needed, add 2‑3 tablespoons arrowroot flour (or corn flour/rice flour) to bind.
Take one ball of the potato mixture, flatten it, place a stuffing ball inside, and gently seal the edges, ensuring the stuffing is fully covered by the potato mixture.
Repeat the shaping process to prepare all the patties.
Coat each patty with arrowroot flour and dust off any excess flour.
Heat oil in a frying pan; once hot, deep‑fry all the patties until golden and crisp.
Serve the potato patties stuffed with bell pepper, coconut & dry fruits with masala chai.

title: Punjabi Lobia Masala Recipe (Punjabi Style Black Eyed Beans Curry)
ingredients: 1 inch Ginger, cut into juliennes for garnish
instructions: Wash and soak the lobia for 4 to 5 hours, then pressure cook with enough water for 2 whistles and set aside.
Make a puree of tomatoes using a hand blender and set aside.
Heat ghee in a wok on medium flame, add the cinnamon stick, cloves and bay leaves and let release their aroma into the ghee.
Add the cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add the ginger‑garlic paste and cook until the raw smell goes away.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they turn light brown.
Add the slit green chilli, tomato purée and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the red chilli, turmeric and cumin powder, mix well and cook until the ghee separates from the sides.
Add the cooked lobia along with the water in which it was boiled and simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently smash a few lobia for the gravy to thicken further.
Slightly crush the kasuri methi between your palms and add it to the gravy along with garam masala; mix well.
Switch off the flame and garnish with the ginger juliennes.
Serve the Punjabi Lobia Masala with phulkas or steamed rice for a weeknight dinner.

title: Chicken Tikki Recipe - Chicken Cutlet
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk the egg and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the minced chicken with all dry spices: garam masala, red chilli, turmeric, coriander, and cumin powders, mixing well.
Add ginger garlic paste, chopped onion, chopped coriander leaves, rice flour, 1/4 cup bread crumbs, and salt; mix thoroughly.
If the mixture is too sticky, incorporate additional bread crumbs; shape into lemon‑sized balls and flatten into patties.
Dip each patty into the whisked egg, then coat with bread crumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat a skillet over medium heat, add a tablespoon of oil, and place the patties in the pan, drizzling a little more oil over each.
Fry for about 5 minutes on each side until crisp and golden brown; remove and serve hot.
Serve the chicken tikki with dhaniya pudina chutney, tomato chutney, or any preferred chutney and pickled onions.

title: Instant Garlic Pickle Recipe
instructions: Peel the skin of the garlic and cut into slices or coarsely pound them.
Heat sesame oil in a deep pan, add mustard seeds and allow spluttering.
Add garlic pieces, chilli powder, and turmeric powder and fry till golden brown.
Add fenugreek powder, salt, and curry leaves and mix well.
Once cooled, serve the garlic pickle fresh with curd rice or store it in a dry, airtight container.

title: Bhaji Miligai And Baby Potato Fry Recipe
ingredients: 5 Green Chilli (bajji variety, light green ones)
instructions: Pressure cook the baby potatoes for 1 or 2 whistles until al dente; meanwhile prepare all ingredients and cut the miligai into large chunks.
Once the pressure releases, peel the potatoes.
In a shallow frying pan, heat oil and fry the chopped garlic, then add the bhajji miligai and fry for about a minute.
Add the small potatoes and sauté with curry leaves, salt, and turmeric; optionally add besan and rice flour at this stage for extra crunch.
Mix everything well and sauté lightly until crispy, then turn off the heat.
Serve the Bhaji Miligai and Baby Potato Fry as a side dish with Tomato Onion Sambar, steamed rice, and Elai Vadam.

title: Sweet Potato Thepla/Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Sweet Potato, pressure cooked till firm and mashed
Spinach Leaves (Palak) or Coriander leaves, a bunch
Oil or ghee to smear as needed
instructions: Combine all the ingredients including whole wheat flour, sweet potato, salt, spinach leaves, cumin powder, and turmeric powder into a large bowl and knead to make a firm dough; add a little water if required to make the dough smooth, and finally add 1 teaspoon of oil to prevent it from becoming sticky.
Make lemon-sized balls and roll them out thin to approximately 6 inches in diameter, as thin as possible, taking care that the parathas do not tear apart.
Toss the dough in dry flour while rolling to prevent it from getting sticky.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat, place the rolled out parathas on the skillet, cook for about 30 seconds, flip over and add 1 teaspoon of ghee around the paratha.
Lightly press the parathas while on the skillet so the dough cooks evenly.
Flip and cook the other side for about 30 seconds, cooking until light golden spots appear on both sides.
Serve the Sweet Potato Thepla/Paratha with Aam Chunda pickle and a cup of Masala Chai for breakfast.

title: Date Obattu Recipe (Date Puran Poli)
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients required for the Date Obattu recipe.
Soak dates in 1/2 cup of hot water for 1-2 hours.
Grind the almonds to a powder.
Grind the dried coconut into a thick paste with very little water.
Grind the soaked dates mixture without any additional water to a smooth paste.
Combine the date paste, almond powder, coconut paste, and jaggery (if using) in a pan and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Let the mixture cool slightly, shape it into 4 equal‑sized balls, and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, add semolina, maida, salt and enough water to make a soft dough; knead well for 6–8 minutes and let it rest covered with a moist cloth for 1 to 1½ hours.
Knead the rested dough briefly again and pour enough oil to coat it completely.

On a sheet of grease‑proof paper, smear some oil, pinch a gooseberry‑sized portion of dough, flatten it with your fingers, place a date ball on it, then stretch the dough ends to cover and seal the ball securely.
Place the dough‑encased date ball on the grease‑proof paper and pat it with your fingers to the desired thickness.
Transfer the patty onto a hot tava, peel off the paper after about 30 seconds, and cook both sides, drizzling oil or ghee as needed.
Serve the Date Obattu with South Indian Kosambari (raw mango, cucumber, carrot, beetroot) and Paruppu Rasam for a wholesome meal.

title: Paneer Stuffed Millet Patties Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Foxtail Millet, cooked until soft and mushy
1/2 cup Green peas (Matar), steamed with salt
instructions: Cook foxtail millet: for each cup of millet add 1.5 cups water, pressure cook 2-3 whistles or cook in a saucepan until water is absorbed and millet is soft and mushy; then combine all patty ingredients until the mixture forms a dough-like consistency.
Divide the patty mixture into 10 equal balls and set aside.
Combine the crumbled paneer with a little salt, divide into 10 small balls, and set aside.
Smear a little oil on your hands, flatten each patty ball, place a paneer ball in the center, and enclose the paneer to form a stuffed patty.
Repeat the stuffing process with the remaining patty and paneer balls and keep them aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat, roll each stuffed patty in whole wheat bread crumbs, and place them on the hot skillet.
Drizzle a little oil over the skillet and cook the patties on medium heat until both sides are evenly browned and crisp.
Cook 2 to 3 patties at a time, adjusting to the size of your pan; using an iron skillet or roti tava helps achieve even cooking and extra crispness.
Serve the Paneer Stuffed Millet Patties as a healthy tea‑time snack with Coriander Mint Chutney and Adrak Chai.

title: Dry Fruit & Nut Modak Recipe
instructions: To begin making Dry Fruit & Nut Modak Recipe, in a kadai, dry roast the almonds, pistachios & cashew nuts on a low heat. Once they are a bit roasted and the brown spots begin to appear, switch off, transfer them to a plate and allow them to cool.
In a mixer grinder or a food processor, make them into a fine powder once they are cooled.
Roughly chop the dates and add them along with the finely chopped figs into the same pan with a little ghee.
On a low heat, fry them continuously for about 8-10 minutes until dates and fig turn thick and crisp. Switch off heat & let the dates-fig mixture cool down.
Grind the mixture into a smooth paste when it cools.
Transfer the contents to the kadai once again and add the dry fruits and nuts powder, pan roasted poppy seeds & cardamom powder to the date & ghee mixture.

Fry for 3-4 minutes until all the dry fruits come together as a lump. This is a ghee rich recipe and you may add more ghee to help it make a lump. Switch off and start making the modaks. You will have to work on making the modaks when the dry fruit mixture is warm, since the dry fruits and nuts tends to fall in crumbles once completely cooled.
Add enough of the dry fruits mixture into the modak mould, press for a few seconds and release the mould with care, & prepare the modaks.
The above quantity of ingredients will make 8 modaks of the size about 2 inches.

Dry Fruit & Nut Modak Recipe is a festive sweet recipe and also can be served for an after school snack for kids, along with a Chaat Style Mashed Potato Toasted Sandwich Recipe and Chocolate & Orange Smoothie with Pea Protein Recipe.

title: Sabudana Tikki Recipe ( Spiced Tapioca Pearls Patties Recipe)
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Whole Almonds (Badam), boiled and skin peeled
instructions: Soak the sabudana in water covering it by about 1 inch for 4–6 hours, then drain well.
Boil the potato until tender, mash it, then add the soaked sabudana along with the remaining ingredients and mix until the mixture binds together.
Divide the mixture into medium‑sized patties and set aside.
Heat peanut oil in a flat non‑stick pan and fry the patties on both sides until crisp and golden brown.
Serve the Sabudana Tikki with No Onion No Garlic Dhaniya Pudina Chutney.

title: Moong Ki Khichdi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Mixed vegetables (carrot, potatoes and green peas), chopped
instructions: Soak the whole moong, basmati rice, chana dal and yellow moong dal together in a mixing bowl with water for an hour.
Heat a pressure cooker with ghee and add cloves, cumin seeds and mustard seeds.
Let them splutter, then add all the vegetables and all the spices with salt and mix them well.
Add the soaked and drained moong mixture to the cooker and cook until the cooker releases 3 whistles.
After the 3 whistles, turn off the heat and allow the cooker to cool.
Serve Moong Ki Khichdi with Gujarati Kadhi for a light and healthy meal.

title: Moong Bhajji Recipe-Moong Fritters
ingredients: 1 cup Yellow Moong Dal (Split), soaked in water for 2 hours
instructions: Wash and soak the moong dal for an hour.
Drain the water completely and coarsely grind the dal together with garlic, ginger, green chillies, salt, cumin seeds and hing in a mixer grinder without adding any water.
Transfer the dal mixture to a mixing bowl and add chopped onion and coriander leaves.
Heat oil in a wok or kadhai, drop small portions (about ½ teaspoon) of the batter, fry until golden brown in batches, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on absorbent paper.
For a healthier version, heat a Kuzhi paniyaram pan over medium heat and add ½ teaspoon oil to each cavity.
Spoon a tablespoon of the batter into each cavity, pan‑fry until browned and crisp, then flip and cook the other side.
Serve the Moong Bhajji with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Date Tamarind Chutney.

title: Beetroot Chicken Cutlets Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a handful, finely chopped
instructions: To begin making Beetroot Chicken Cutlets Recipe, heat 3-4 cups water in a deep-bottomed saucepan, add salt and pepper and bring to boil.
Add the chicken and cook it for about 20 minutes or till the chicken is cooked.
Meanwhile, in a mixing bowl mash the potato until no lumps are present and grate the cooked beetroot into it.
Once chicken has cooked, drain the water and let cool. Once cooled, shred the chicken.
Mix the shredded chicken, mashed potato, grated beetroot, green chillies, ginger-garlic paste, coriander leaves, and curry leaves, jeera, chilli powder and garam masala.
Adjust the salt and mix until you get a smooth but firm dough like consistency.
Make round cutlets by making medium sized balls, and press them between your palms, and coat it with bread crumbs. Arrange on parchment paper until all the cutlets are made.

Drizzle oil in a shallow frying pan and place the cutlets on pan. Take care to place the cutlets sparsely on the pan and not to overcrowd the pan, to help them shallow fry evenly. You can shallow fry them in batches.
Flip to the other side when the bottom of cutlets is nicely crisp and browning.

Serve Beetroot Chicken Cutlets Recipe as party appetizers along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney Recipe or Party Style Creamy Spinach Dip Made with Cheesy Garlic Mayo, may be along with Vegetarian Tandoori Kebab Recipe.

title: Shakkarkandi ke Laddu | Sweet Potato Laddu Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Sweet Potatoes, boiled and mashed
3/4 cup Sugar, adjust as per taste
instructions: Heat ghee in a non-stick pan, add mashed sweet potatoes and sauté for 12-15 minutes.
Add grated coconut, green cardamom powder, almonds and cashews, raisins, and sugar; mix well over medium heat.
Keep stirring until the mixture comes together as a single mass, about 3-5 minutes.
When the mixture is still warm, shape it into small balls.
Put grated coconut on a plate and roll the balls over it.
Place the laddus in the fridge for 10-15 minutes and serve.

title: Cabbage and Methi Paratha Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Cabbage (Patta Gobi/ Muttaikose) , finely chopped
150 grams Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves) , finely chopped
instructions: To prepare Cabbage and Methi Paratha, first finely chop the cabbage, methi and onion. Heat oil in a stir-fry pan over medium heat and saute the onions till they turn soft. Add the cabbage and cook covered till soft. Turn off the heat and let the vegetables cool down.

To bind the dough for the paratha, combine together whole wheat flour, oat bran, cabbage, methi leaves, curd and spices and bind the dough using a little water if needed. Knead the dough well for few minutes. Let the dough rest for about 30 minutes, this helps the dough to soften.

Divide the dough in small size equal parts. Roll out each portion into a round parantha to a prefered thickness. Do make sure you keep dusting it in flour, so the the paratha does not stick to the surface while rolling.
Preheat the tawa (griddle) on medium heat. Place the rolled out dough on the heated tawa and cook on medium heat both sides till it is slightly browned.
When you notice the brown spots, smear a teaspoon of ghee or oil on both sides and cook until the paratha has turned golden brown and lightly crisp on both sides.
Once the paratha is done, place it on a platter and proceed to cook the remaining parathas.
Serve Cabbage and Methi Paratha with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita and Mango Pickle.

title: Spicy Pressure Cooker Mutton Curry Recipe
instructions: Marinate the mutton: In a large mixing bowl, combine the washed and cleaned mutton with curd, salt, lemon juice, and turmeric powder; mix well, cover, and set aside for at least an hour.
Make a paste by grinding the onions, garlic, and ginger together; set aside.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker over medium heat; add the whole spices (cloves, bay leaf, cardamom, fennel seeds, and cinnamon stick).
When the whole spices begin to sizzle, add the green chillies and sauté for 30 seconds until the raw smell disappears.
Add the onion‑ginger‑garlic paste and sauté for about a minute.
Stir in red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and meat masala; continue to sauté for another minute.
Add the tomato puree, cover, and cook for 2 minutes until the raw tomato smell fades.
Add the marinated mutton to the cooker, stir well, and check seasoning; adjust salt and spices as needed.
Close the pressure cooker and cook on high pressure for about 5‑6 whistles; turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Open the cooker, stir in kasuri methi, and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve hot with whole wheat lachha paratha and tomato onion cucumber raita.

title: Chicken In Tomato Onion Gravy Recipe
ingredients: 500 grams Chicken, chopped to bite size
instructions: To begin making Chicken In Tomato Onion Gravy Recipe, take onions, green chillies and tomatoes (de seeded) in a mixer jar and grind to a smooth paste.
In a pressure cooker, add the onion-chilli and tomato paste, curd, salt, chicken masala powder, lemon juice and ginger garlic paste. Stir to combine.
Add the chicken pieces and about half cup of water and close the lid of the pressure cooker and cook on high flame for about 3 whistles or till the chicken is cooked till tender.

Once the pressure is released on its own, heat a bit of oil in a kadai and once the oil is hot, transfer the gravy of the cooked chicken from the pressure cooker. Retain the cooked chicken in the pressure cooker. you may do this by refraining the chicken with a slotted spoon while pouring the gravy.
Cook for a few minutes while stirring, till the gravy starts bubbling and thickening.

Once the gravy is thickened to desired consistency, add the chicken pieces to the kadai, close a lid and cook on a low flame for about 5 minutes or till the flavours seep in a bit more in the chicken pieces.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serv.
Serve Chicken In Tomato Onion Gravy Recipe along with Homemade Butter Naan Recipe (Soft Yogurt Bread) or Jeera Rice Recipe - Cumin And Ghee Flavored Rice and Pickled Onions for a complete meal.

title: Spinach And Paneer Samosa Recipe With Figaro Pure Olive Oil
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (for dough)
1 cup spinach, washed and finely chopped
Extra virgin olive oil, for deep frying
instructions: Prepare the dough by mixing whole wheat flour, sooji, extra virgin olive oil, ajwain and salt to form a coarse crumb mixture.
Add water a little at a time and knead into a soft, firm dough; continue kneading for 2–3 minutes.
Cover the dough with a moist cloth and let it rest for 15–20 minutes.
Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a pan; add the chopped spinach and sauté on high heat until the spinach softens and all moisture evaporates.
Turn off the heat and allow the sautéed spinach to cool completely.
Combine the cooled spinach with crumbled paneer, chopped green chilies, garam masala, chaat masala, and salt; mix well to form the filling.
Fill a small cup with water for sealing the samosa edges.
On a floured surface, divide the rested dough into portions, roll each portion into a 3‑inch diameter circle and cut each circle in half.
Lightly wet the straight edge of each half‑circle with water, then fold it into a cone shape.
Place 1–2 tablespoons of the spinach‑paneer filling into the cone and seal the edges, pressing with a fork to create decorative marks.
Repeat the shaping and filling process with the remaining dough and filling.
Heat extra virgin olive oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan over medium heat for deep‑frying.
Carefully slide a few samosas into the oil; fry on medium heat, turning them when they float to the surface, until they turn light golden‑brown on all sides.
Maintain medium heat throughout; avoid high heat which may brown the crust too quickly.
Remove fried samosas with a slotted spoon and drain on absorbent paper.
Allow the samosas to rest for about 5 minutes before serving.
Serve hot spinach and paneer samosas with green mint chutney or date tamarind chutney.

title: Lemon Coconut Chia Energy Balls Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Fresh coconut, unsweetened and shredded
1/2 cup shredded coconut (for dusting the balls)
instructions: Add dates in the food processor and process them to break into small pieces.
Add almonds, chia seeds, lemon juice and process them until they are combined together.
Add lemon zest and process them until they come together as a dough. Scoop using a spoon and roll them into balls.
Dust the rolled balls with the shredded coconut. Place in an airtight container and store in refrigerator for about a month.
Serve Lemon Coconut Chia Energy Balls as a tea time snack or pack it in your kids snack box.

title: Mango Rice Recipe
ingredients: 1-1 1/2 cups mango (ripe or raw unripe), peeled and chopped
instructions: Soak the rice for 20 minutes, then cook it in a pressure cooker; spread the cooked rice on a plate and set aside.

Peel and chop the mangoes. In a blender add the chopped mangoes, dry red chilies, 1 chopped green chili, 1 teaspoon sesame seeds, peanuts, 1/2 cup grated coconut, and powdered jaggery; blend to a semi‑fine paste.
Grind the mixture to a semi‑fine paste, avoiding a completely smooth texture.
Heat oil in a pan, add peanuts and sauté on low flame until they change colour. Then add mustard seeds, chana dal, and urad dal.
Add 12–15 curry leaves and 1–2 dry red chilies; sauté briefly. Add a pinch of asafoetida and 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder.
Stir in the mango‑coconut paste, sauté for 3–4 minutes, and season with salt.
Add the cooked rice to the pan and mix thoroughly so the rice is well coated with the paste.
Serve the mango rice with spicy potato roast, raita, or pickle.

title: Cauliflower And Peas Bhurji Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Cauliflower And Peas Bhurji Recipe, in a wide bowl, add in enough water and add some salt to it. Cut the cauliflower into florets and soak them in salt water for 10-15 minutes.
When done, chop the cauliflower and green chillies finely. Wash the green peas and drain the excess water.
Heat oil in a kadai and temper it with mustard seeds. To this, add in chopped green chillies, cauliflower, green peas, turmeric powder and salt. Mix them well.
Cover and cook them in low flame for 7-8 minutes or until done. They should have cooked yet should remain crunchy (al dente)!
Serve Cauliflower And Peas Bhurji Recipe along with Palak Dal, Lauki Raita and Phulka for your everyday meals.

title: Paneer Stuffed Bread Fritters Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Paneer Stuffed Bread Fritters, first lets first make the paneer bhurji.
In a pan, on medium heat, warm a tablespoon of oil. Add jeera and let it sizzle. Next, add chopped green chillies and then crumbled paneer to this.
Toss together and mix, then sprinkle the amchur powder, garam masala powder, salt and give it a good mix once again.
Cook it for another 2 minutes. Switch off the heat and let the mixture cool.
Add the prepared bhurji into a mixing bowl, add chopped onions, mashed potato and coriander leaves to this and knead the mixture well.
Make lemon size balls out of this mixture. This should make around 12 to 14 balls.
In a deep pan or kadai warm the oil to deep fry the fritters.
In a deep plate add half the milk. Chop the sides of the sliced bread and lay the bread slices one at a time, in the milk.
Let the bread soak in the milk for a few seconds, then place it between your palms and gently squeeze flat till the milk is drained.
Keep the slice as flat as possible so as not to break it.
Now place the paneer mixture in the centre of the milk soaked slice, and bring the corners together to cover it with the soaked bread slice.
Roll the fritter between your palms to make it a smooth ball. Sprinkle some semolina over it or roll it in a plate of semolina to encrust it.
When the oil is warm, slowly slide the fritters into the kadai, taking care not to add too many and overcrowd the pan.
Gently fry on a medium heat till the fritters are golden.
Remove from the oil with a slotted spoon and serve hot with Pudina Chutney as an appetiser or with Ginger Cardamom Chai to perk up your tea time.

title: Prawn Fritters Recipe (Shrimp Vadai)
instructions: To begin making the Prawn Fritters recipe, clean and de-vein the prawn and set it ready. In a blender add in the prawns, coconut along with all the ingredients mentioned in the “To grind” table.
Now take the ground mix to a big bowl; to this add the Rice flour, chopped onions, coriander leaves, curry leaves and fennel seeds. Mix everything well so that all the ingredients are mixed evenly.
Divide the dough into equal sized small shaped balls and flatten it. Heat oil for deep frying. Once the oil is hot drop in 4-5 vada’s per batch and start frying.
Once the vada’s are cooked, strain them and place on paper towels to absorb excess oil. Serve hot.
Serve Prawn Fritters along with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Date Tamarind Chutney for your evening snacks or serve them for your party.

title: Mooli Makki Roti Recipe
ingredients: Spinach Leaves (Palak) , or salad leaves as required
instructions: To begin making the Mooli Makki Roti recipe, In a large bowl add grated radish, sprouts, spring onions, ginger, chilli paste, coriander and salt. Mix well with a spatula.
To this add makki atta little by little and mix without adding any water. The moisture in the mooli should be enough to combine the dough.
This mixture will look crumbly but will come together when rested. Rest the mixture for 15 to 20 minutes.

Cut out a greaseproof paper according to the size of your pan. Smear some oil over this and place a fistful of dough made into a ball on the centre of the paper and pat it into a round roti by wetting/greasing your fingers as thin or as thick as you like.
Heat a roti tava and pour some oil and spread it with a paper towel. Now transfer the roti onto the tava and let it cook for a minute until you peel the paper.
Now peel the paper, drizzle some oil and cook until crispy by flipping both sides.
Transfer it onto a plate, smear dhaniya pudina chutney and top it with salad and enjoy a wholesome breakfast with a cup of tea.
Enjoy this flavourful Mooli Makki Roti with a cup of Masala Chai for a healthy wholesome breakfast.

title: Steamed Sweet Corn Recipe Flavored with Chaat Masala Recipe
ingredients: 1 Sweet corn, whole on the cob
instructions: Steam the corn in a steamer.
Peel the excess fibers and husk from the corn, then cut the corn into halves (or three portions depending on size).
Place the corn in the steamer and steam for about 5 minutes until the kernels are softened; then remove and place on a serving platter.
Combine salt, kala namak, and chaat masala in a bowl; rub this mixture generously over the corn and squeeze lemon juice over it.
Serve the steamed sweet corn as a tea‑time snack, optionally with masala chai.

title: Croquettes Recipe With Bhetki Fish
ingredients: 1 cup Whole Wheat Bread crumbs (or more) for coating
instructions: To begin making Croquettes Recipe With Bhetki Fish, for the fish stuffing, in a mixing bowl, add the fish steaks, quartered onions, crushed garlic cloves, bay leaves, crushed green cardamom, cinnamon, a generous sprinkle of salt and about a cup of water to a pressure cooker.
(You can also pressure cook the potatoes separately during this process and allow to cook and then mash the potatoes after deskinning them.)
Cook over high heat, one whistle.
Allow the pressure to be released by itself. Once it cools down, carefully debone the fish steaks and mash the fish with a wooden masher or ladle. Keep aside till needed.
Heat about 1 tablespoon oil in a pan, once hot add the chopped onions and garlic, fry on medium‑high heat until close to caramelised.
Add the chopped green chillies and sauté for a minute or two.
Add the mashed fish, tomato ketchup, salt and sugar.
Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, for 5‑7 minutes until well combined. Switch off and allow to cool to lukewarm so it can be handled with bare hands.
Form 10 oval roundels and keep aside.
Sprinkle a little salt and black pepper into the mashed potatoes and mix well until combined.
Divide the potatoes into 10 equal portions.
Take one portion of mashed potato in the palm of your hand and make a well in the centre.
Place a portion of the fish filling in the potato well, bring the corners of the potato case together and cover the fish stuffing, creating a thin coating of mashed potato over the filling.
Gently shape into elongated croquettes. Prepare a plate of flour, a bowl of whisked egg, and a plate of bread crumbs.
Roll each croquette in flour, dip into the whisked egg, then roll over the breadcrumbs.
Place the coated croquettes in the refrigerator to set for about 30 minutes or longer.
Heat oil in a deep‑frying pan; once hot, deep‑fry the croquettes until golden.
Remove the croquettes onto a kitchen towel to absorb excess oil.
Serve the Bhetki fish croquettes as an evening snack with dips such as tomato ketchup, peanut chilli sauce, or tzatziki.

title: Quick Cauliflower Fried Rice Recipe
ingredients: 1 Red Yellow or Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum), julienned
1/4 cup Sweet corn, steamed or boiled
instructions: Chop the cauliflower into florets and add it to water with 2 tablespoon salt; after 30 minutes, drain, wash and set aside.
Pulse the cauliflower in a food processor for 1 minute until it resembles rice grains, or grate it using a grater.
Heat a kadai or wok, add 3 tablespoon oil, then add sliced garlic and sauté until the raw garlic smell disappears.
Add onion and fry until it turns pinkish; then add julienned capsicum and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the boiled green peas and boiled sweet corn, mixing well.
Stir in the chopped spring onion greens and mix.
Add ginger–garlic paste, soy sauce, and green chili sauce, mixing well.
Finally, add the shredded cauliflower and mix well; cook for 5 to 7 minutes.
Season with black pepper powder and salt to taste, mix well, and serve.

title: Makki Ki Puri Recipe (Maize Flour Fried Indian Bread)
ingredients: 1 cup Makki Ka Atta (Yellow Corn Meal Flour)
instructions: Take maize flour and add wheat flour, the required salt, 1/2 teaspoon carom seeds, 2 teaspoons oil and water in small portions in a mixing bowl.
Knead a stiff, tight dough and let it rest for 15 to 20 minutes; then divide the dough and roll each ball into poori.
Heat oil in a deep‑fry pan and slide the rolled poori into it; fry until golden brown on both sides.
Drain the fried puri on paper kitchen towels and serve hot.

title: Multi-Grain Crackers With Sesame Seeds, Chives And Chili Flakes Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Sesame seeds (Til seeds), lightly toasted
6 tablespoon Coconut Oil, or olive oil
instructions: To begin making Multi-Grain Crackers With Sesame Seeds Recipe, add all the flours into a large mixing bowl. Add the toasted sesame seeds, chopped chives, chili flakes and salt. Mix well.
Add the oil and mix all the ingredients till well combined. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add little water at a time and knead this mixture into a soft and firm dough. Cover the dough and leave to rest for around 15 to 25 minutes at room temperature.
Meanwhile, pre-heat oven at 180 Degree Celsius.
Roll out the dough into a large circle and cut out desired shapes with a cookie cutter. You can also use a pizza cutter to cut these into diamond shapes.

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the edges turn a light brown. Take care not to burn them. You can create your own flavor combination by adding other spices into these crackers like kasuri methi, ajwain etc..
Serve Multi-Grain Crackers With Sesame Seeds Recipe in a serving plate. Gift your valentine these healthy crackers, make it for your tea parties or pack it for your snack box.

title: Palak And Kala Chana Sukhi Sabzi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Kala Chana (Brown Chickpeas), soaked overnight
1 cup Spinach Leaves (Palak), washed and roughly chopped
instructions: To begin making the Palak Kala Chana Recipe first clean, wash and soak chickpeas in water overnight or at least 5 - 6 hours.
First make puree of tomato and green chili using 2 - 3 tablespoons of water in blender.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a pan; add in the chopped spinach and saute until the spinach is soft and tender. Keep this aside.

Note: We cook the spinach separately from the chola, as the cooking times for the chickpeas and spinach are very different. Spinach takes a couple of minutes, while the chola/ chickpeas take 20 to 30 minutes.
In a pressure cooker heat oil over medium heat, once oil is heated add in the bay leaf and cardamom pods; saute for 1 minute or until spices start releasing aroma.
Now add in chopped onion, ginger and garlic and saute over medium heat until onion turn light brown in color.
Once onion is ready add tomato puree, salt, turmeric powder, garam masala, and coriander powder, red chili powder until you see the mixture coming together and thickening a little bit.
Add the chickpeas along with the water it was soaked in into the masala and stir well. Add in additional water so that the water level is atleast 2 inches above the soaked Kala Chana.

Give it a good stir and cover the pressure cooker and place its weight on. Cook the kala Chana in the pressure cooker until you hear 4 to 5 whistles. After 4 to 5 whistles, turn the heat to low and simmer the chana for another 15 minutes and then turn off the heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally. This will take another 15 minutes. Once the pressure releases naturally, open the cooker, add in the sauteed spinach and give it a good stir.

Check the salt and spice levels and adjust to suit your taste. Gently mash the chickpeas little bit with the back of the ladle to thicken the gravy little bit and the Palak Kala Chana Sukhi Recipe is ready to be served.
Serve the Palak & Kala Chana Sukhi Sabzi Recipe along with Dal Tadka, Dill Cucumber Raita, Jeera Rice and Phulka for a delicious weekday meal.

title: Banana Puree (Baby Food- 4 months onward)
ingredients: Water, formula milk or breastmilk as needed
instructions: Peel 1 ripe banana and place it in a bowl.
If the banana is ripe, mash it with a fork (no processor needed) and add water, breast milk or formula milk to achieve the right consistency and texture.
Alternatively, place the banana in a baby food blender and blend until smooth.
Transfer the banana puree to a serving bowl, add water, breast milk or formula as needed to adjust consistency, and serve the baby.

title: Thenga Vada Recipe (Spicy Coconut Fritters)
ingredients: 6 Green Chillies , oarsely ground (you can also use red chilly powder)
instructions: To begin making the Thenga Vada Recipe, first mix the rice flour, maida, coarsely ground chillies, scraped coconut and salt in a mixing bowl and set it aside.
Preheat the heat oil in a Kadai, for deep frying.
When the oil is hot enough, add about 1 tablespoon of hot oil to the flour mixture and combine. The mixture should resemble breadcrumbs.
Add a little water to the thengai vadai flour mixture and mix well till everything comes together to form a firm ball of cough (similar to the dough formed for chapatis).

When you are ready to fry the vadai, take a small lemon sized ball of the dough and flatten it on your hand to make thin discs or vadas. You can optionally grease your fingers with oil so they don't stick to your fingers.
Make a hole in the middle of the vadai disc with your finger so it resembles a donut.
Drop the thengai vadas gently into the hot oil, one by one, taking care not to crowd the kadai.
Fry the vadas till golden brown and crisp. Then lift them out of the oil with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper towels. Cool slightly and serve.
Serve the Thengai Vadas along with a tea time snack. You can also store them in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

title: Delicious Butter Chicken Pani Puri Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Hung curd (Greek yogurt) for mint yoghurt dip
1/4 cup green chutney (coriander & mint) for mint yoghurt dip
instructions: Wash the chicken thoroughly and drain any excess water.

In a large mixing bowl combine the hung curd, ginger, garlic, turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, amchur, cumin powder, garam masala, honey, mustard oil, tomato puree, tomato ketchup, kasuri methi, mint leaves, coriander leaves, lemon juice and salt; mix well to form a marination.
Add the shredded chicken breast to the marination and let it rest for about 30 minutes.

Heat butter in a kadai, add the marinated chicken mixture, cover and cook on medium flame for about 20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked and the masala coats the pieces; allow to cool to obtain a semi‑gravy butter chicken.
For the mint yoghurt dip, combine the green chutney with the hung curd in a bowl and whisk until smooth.
Place each puri on a platter and gently tap the top to create a half‑inch hole.
Fill each puri with about half a tablespoon of the butter chicken, add a few pickled onion rings, drizzle with the mint yoghurt dip and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve immediately as a party appetizer.

title: Baked Mini Bread Cups Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Baked Mini Bread Cups Recipe, preheat the Oven to 180 C and grease the Muffin Pan with butter.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a pan; add the onion and bell pepper and saute until lightly softened and golden.

Once the bell peppers have a roasted aroma, add the ginger, garlic, corn and chopped potatoes. Stir fry on high heat for a couple of minutes, so the vegetables get roasted. Finally add the chili powder, tomato ketchup and stir well. Check the salt and chili and adjust to suit your taste and allow the filling to cool.
The next step is to make the bread cups, fill and bake them in the oven.
Trim the edges of the bread, flatten with the rolling pin a bit and press them into the greased muffin pans.
You can optionally spray oil over the bread slices or leave them as it is. Spoon the potato filling mixture into each one of the bread cups.
Tear the cheese slices and place them on top of the filling. You can also optionally spread grated mozzarella cheese.
Place the mini bread cups in the preheated oven and bake for about 10 minutes until the sides of the bread become crisp and the cheese has melted.
Once done, remove from the oven, allow it to rest for a few minutes and serve.
Serve the Baked Mini Bread Cups either for breakfast, an after school snack or even as an appetizer for parties.

title: Ripe Guava Chutney Recipe (Amrood Ki Chutney)
