instructions: Peel the ripe guavas, cut them into large pieces, and place them in a microwave‑safe pan; add 1/3 cup water and a pinch of salt.
Cook in the microwave for 10 minutes, then let the mixture cool to room temperature.
Mash the guava pieces and remove the seeds by draining the mixture carefully.
In a mixer jar, combine the mashed guava, chillies, peanuts, finely chopped parsley, garlic, lemon juice, jaggery, and salt; blend into a smooth paste.
For tempering, heat oil in a pan, add white urad dal (split) and curry leaves, let them simmer, then stir the tempering into the smooth paste.
Serve the ripe guava chutney with ajwain besan ka paratha.

title: Spinach Buns Recipe (Masala Palak Pav)
ingredients: Milk, as required, to brush on top
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling water and puree it in a mixer.
In a mixing bowl, add flour, salt, sugar, instant yeast, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, kasuri methi, garam masala, and spinach puree; mix well.
Add yolk and olive oil, mix, then slowly add water to make a soft dough; cover and let it double in size.
Punch out air, cut into six parts, shape each into a smooth ball, place in a baking pan/tray, and allow to double; brush with milk and sprinkle nigella seeds.
Bake in a pre‑heated oven at 180 °C for 22‑25 minutes until browned on top; cool and serve.

title: Crispy & Spicy Paneer Starter Recipe
instructions: To prepare Crispy & Spicy Paneer Starter Recipe, get ready with all the ingredients and start with making achar masala. Pulse the spices in the mixer‑grinder to get a coarse mix for the pickle.
Wash and pat dry the paneer. Cut the paneer into 1/2" thick and 2" long cuboid; 500 g paneer yields approximately 24 pieces.
Marinate paneer with a tablespoon of pickle mix, juice of half a lemon and salt only if required.
Spread the black pepper urad dal papad on a kitchen towel and keep under open sun or fan for 45 minutes to an hour, or until the papads are dry.
Pulse the dried papad in a mixer‑grinder to make a coarse powder.
Heat oil for frying in a deep‑bottomed pan.
Make a thick paste of cornflour, a pinch of salt, and water.
Dip the marinated paneer in the cornflour paste and roll it in the black pepper urad dal papad powder.
Fry 5‑6 pieces of the prepared paneer at a time until golden brown.
Serve the crispy & spicy paneer starter with roasted tomato sauce or dhaniya pudina chutney and masala chai as an appetizer or snack.

title: Homemade Ginger Garlic Paste
instructions: Peel the skin of the garlic and ginger.
Grind the ginger first in a blender, then add the garlic and blend together into a fine paste; add the vinegar and blend again to mix everything.
Transfer the ginger garlic paste to a glass jar and refrigerate; it will last for a few weeks (optional: adjust garlic amount, add lemon juice or oil for extra flavor).
Store the paste in a well‑cleaned, dry glass jar and keep it refrigerated.
Always use a clean spoon when taking the paste; it will stay fresh for more than three weeks.

title: Indian Style Tapenade Recipe
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil, as required for garnishing
1/2 dry red chilli, crushed for garnishing
instructions: Heat a wide pan with 1-1/2 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil.
Add chopped onions, chopped garlic, and chopped black and green olives; mix well and sauté for a minute.
Add the boiled moong dal along with salt, mash lightly, then add lemon zest and mix.
Turn off the heat and transfer the mixture to a bowl; add chopped cilantro or parsley.
Stir in crushed dry red chilies, lemon juice, and the remaining 1-1/2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil; mix well.
Cut diagonal slices of French bread, toast them lightly, and arrange on a serving platter.
Spread the moong tapenade mixture over each bread slice, drizzle with extra virgin olive oil, and sprinkle crushed red chilies on top.
Serve the Indian Style Tapenade with hot Masala Chai or as a breakfast item.

title: Fruit-Chia Rice paper rolls in a Mango Tahini Dipping sauce Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup coconut milk or almond milk
1/2 teaspoon black sesame seeds or white sesame seeds
instructions: Mix all the chia pudding ingredients together, stir gently every 15 minutes for the first two times, then let sit at least 2 hours or overnight in the fridge.

Blend mango, tahini, red chilli, lemon juice, salt, and coconut milk into a smooth paste; add spring onion, sprinkle with sesame seeds and chilli powder, add sriracha if using, and refrigerate until needed.
Slice the fruits and set aside.
Dip one rice paper in warm water for 30 seconds, place on a damp towel, arrange sliced strawberries, spoon 1 tablespoon of the chia pudding on top, and roll the rice paper.
Repeat with the remaining fruit; mint can also be included inside the wrap.
Serve the rolls with mint and the mango‑tahini dipping sauce.

title: Apple Onion Chutney Recipe
ingredients: 5 tablespoons Jaggery, grated or brown sugar
instructions: Heat oil or butter in a pan.
Add the onions and sauté till they become soft and golden brown, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Add ginger, apples, salt, jaggery, vinegar, allspice powder and thyme leaves.
Stir and cook till the apples soften. Adjust the amount of jaggery or vinegar to taste.
Serve the Apple Onion Chutney as preferred with crackers, sandwiches, etc.
Store it in airtight jars in the refrigerator for increased shelf life.

title: Mint Coriander Spice Pulao Recipe
instructions: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker on medium flame, then add star anise, fennel seeds, bay leaves and cinnamon stick.
When the whole spices begin to sizzle, add the coriander and mint leaves and give it a quick stir.
Add the washed and drained rice, 3 cups of water, salt and close the pressure cooker.
Pressure cook for 2-3 whistles and turn off the flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, then open the cooker, give the pulao a gentle stir and transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve the Mint Coriander Spice Pulao with spinach mushroom chickpea curry, Rajasthani style mutton Banjara, pickled onions, and a dessert of Shahi Tukda Gajar Halwa shots with Rabri.

title: Cottage Cheese And Peas Oatmeal Pancakes Recipe
ingredients: Oil or butter for making pancakes
instructions: Blanch the green peas in hot water, keep aside, and save a few teaspoons to be included later.
Add the oatmeal flour, blanched green peas and grated paneer in a blender and blend to a coarse mix.
Take the ground pancake mix in a bowl, add the saved few teaspoons of green peas, season with salt and mix well; the mixture should be slightly thicker than usual pancake batter.
Heat a skillet on medium flame, grease with a little oil or butter, pour a ladle full of the pancake mix and gently spread; cook for 3 minutes until the bottom is cooked.
Flip gently and cook the other side for another 2 minutes, then remove to a plate.
Prepare the rest of the pancakes with the remaining batter.
Serve the Cottage Cheese and Peas Oatmeal Pancakes with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney and Masala Chai.

title: Puffed Rice Bar Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup mixed nuts, dry roasted and chopped
Butter (salted), melted to grease the tin/tray
instructions: Heat a pan and add jaggery, stirring continuously until it becomes smooth and shiny.
Add puffed rice, mixed nuts, shredded coconut, and green cardamom powder one by one, mixing well.
Turn off the heat, transfer the mixture into a greased tray or cake tin, and use wet hands to press the mixture down evenly.
Cut the set puffed rice bar into desired shapes and serve or pack for snacks.

title: Instant Lemon Pickle Recipe
instructions: To prepare Instant Lemon Pickle Recipe, select good quality ripe yellow lemons with thin skin and no spots on them for this pickle. Wash them in clean water and pat dry with kitchen towel.
Cut each lemon into 8 pieces. Remove the seeds using a knife. Make sure no seeds are left inside the lemon pieces as it may lend a bitter taste to the pickle.
Add 3-4 cups of water in a pressure cooker. Keep all the lemon pieces in a vessel and place the vessel in the cooker. Cover the vessel with a plate so that water from steam doesn’t fall in it.
Pressure cook the lemons for 1 whistle and then lower the flame and allow to cook for another 10-12 minutes.
Open the cooker once the pressure has released. You will see the lemon pieces are cooked well and the juice has accumulated.
Strain the lemon pieces and collect the juice in a pan.
Do not add any water to it. Add sugar to the lemon juice and cook on low flame.
Keep stirring. The sugar will melt and you will get the syrup. Cook the syrup until all the sugar has dissolved and you see bubbles in the syrup.
The syrup attains a 2 string consistency by this stage. As the juice is very less and we do not add any extra water, this stage attains very fast, say in about 5-7 minutes.
Add salt and red chili powder to the syrup and stir well. At the end add the cooked lemon pieces and put off the flame. Mix the pieces well with the sauce. Keep stirring the pickle for 1-2 minutes.
The Instant Lemon Pickle Recipe is ready. Let it cool down completely. Transfer to a clean, dry, and sterilized bottle and refrigerate. Use as needed.

title: Nigella Seed Beetroot Rice Recipe
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, for garnish (chopped for garnish)
instructions: To begin making the Nigella Seed Beetroot Rice recipe, firstly cook the rice and keep it aside. Let it cool down.
Heat a heavy bottomed wok with oil, add half the nigella seeds and the green chillies.
Add the beetroot and salt, toss it well for 2 minutes.
Pour the water and bring to a boil then reduce to low heat and cover to cook the vegetable.
Stop the flame when few spoons of water is left in wok. Add the cooked rice, mix it well and let it cook for 2 minutes. Check for seasoning.
Serve warm on dinner plate with coriander leaves, black pepper and half of nigella seeds on top for garnish.
Serve Nigella Seed Beetroot Rice along with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, Tadka Raita or any other raita of your choice.

title: Mushroom Masala With Corn Recipe
ingredients: 300 grams Button mushrooms , cut into cubes
instructions: To begin making Mushroom Masala With Corn Recipe, clean the mushrooms and chop into cubes. Keep aside.
Make a coarse paste of ginger, garlic and green chilies using a pestle and mortar and keep aside.
Now, take a bowl add the mushrooms, steamed corn kernels, ginger, garlic and chilli paste and mix well.
To this add the turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander, cumin and corn starch powder. season with salt and mix well.
Heat oil in a pan, add the onions and saute until translucent.
Add the dried red chillies and saute until the oil becomes aromatic.
Add in the mushroom and corn mixture and mix well.
Let it cook in medium heat till the mushrooms are cooked well and the mixture becomes semi dry. Occasionally stir in between.
Switch off the heat and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve the Mushroom Masala With Corn Recipe as an appetiser along with a warm Vegetarian Pumpkin And Chickpea Soup Recipe or Spiced Carrot And Onion Soup Recipe for a light supper.

title: Leftover Roti Cutlet Recipe
instructions: Grind the leftover rotis into a grainy mixture using a mixer grinder.
Heat oil in a pan, add onions and green chillies, and sauté until translucent; then add carrot and cook for about a minute.
Add the mashed peas, corn, and potatoes; cook for about 20‑30 seconds.
Stir in black pepper, red chilli flakes, amchur powder, and red chilli powder; mix well.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl, add semolina, the grainy roti mixture, and lemon juice; mix thoroughly.
Shape the mixture into small patties and set aside.
Mix corn flour with a little water; dip each patty in this mixture and roll in bread crumbs.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the cutlets one by one until hot.
Flip the cutlets a few times until both sides are brown and crispy.
Serve the leftover roti cutlets with dhaniya pudina chutney or tomato ketchup, and enjoy with masala chai.

title: Manga Ogre Recipe (Mango Rice)
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch finely chopped
instructions: To begin making the Manga Ogre first.

Grind together in a blender mango, coconut, mustard seeds, green chillies, turmeric powder, jaggery (if using), little salt and coriander leaves to a fine paste. (Don’t add water to the paste. The rice is already cooked in salted water so add salt just enough for this chutney).
Add this chutney to the cooled rice and mix.
In a small Kadai/wok, heat oil.
Add the mustard seeds; once they splutter, add the cumin seeds, the chana dal and sauté for a few seconds.
Add the hing and curry leaves and take it off the heat.
Pour this tempering over the rice. Mix well.
Your Manga Ogre Recipe is ready to be served; serve with some mint and pomegranate raita for a flavourful meal.

title: Authentic Punjabi Mango Pickle (With Mustard Oil) - No Sun Required Aam Ka Achar
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kashmiri Red Chilli Powder , 40 grams approx
1/4 cup Methi Seeds (Fenugreek Seeds) , 40 grams approx
1/4 cup Mustard seeds (Rai/ Kadugu) , 40 grams approx
1/4 cup Kalonji (Onion Nigella Seeds) , 35 grams approx
instructions: To begin making the Punjabi Mango Pickle recipe (Aam Ka Achaar Recipe), wash the mangoes and dry them completely making sure there is no moisture or dust.

Make sure your knife and the platform you use for cutting the mangoes is clean and moisture free. Cut the mangoes in half, deseed and further cut them into one inch cubes. You can leave the skin on provided they are tender and smooth.
In a large steel bowl, combine the salt, turmeric powder and cut mangoes. Cover the bowl and allow it to marinate for 1 hour.

Heat a small pan on medium heat, and roast the coriander seeds until you start smelling the aroma. Turn off heat and allow it to cool. Once cooled, coarsely crush the coriander seeds with a pestle and mortar.
Blend the mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds into a coarse powder. There is no need to roast the seeds.
To the marinated mangoes, add the powdered mustard and fenugreek seeds, red chilli powder, fennel seeds, kalonji seeds, and coriander seeds. Stir well to combine.
Add 1 cup of mustard oil and stir well again. Do not heat the mustard oil. Check the salt; it should be extra salty, adjusting with more salt if needed.
Cover the steel bowl with a muslin cloth, tie it tightly around the rim, place a steel lid over the covered bowl and set aside.
After 24 hours, open and stir. Cover again with cloth and lid and let rest for another day. On the third day, when the mangoes have softened, add the remaining 2 cups of mustard oil and stir.
Cover tightly with muslin cloth and a steel lid, keep aside for 2 more days, and give it a stir.
By the end of the 5th day the pickle is ready to eat. The mangoes will be softened but may retain a firm texture and will continue to mature in stored bottles.
Clean and sterilize the bottles and lids for storage. Store in multiple small 500 g glass bottles, opening only when needed.
Transfer the pickle into the clean, dry bottles. Add a tablespoon of mustard oil on top, seal tightly and enjoy.
Use a clean, dry spoon to serve, ensuring no moisture contacts the pickle.
Serve the Punjabi Mango Pickle with Pyaz Ka Paratha or Aloo Methi Paratha for a complete breakfast.

title: Cuban Inspired Bheja Fry With Stir Fried Onion And Pepper
ingredients: Red Yellow and Green Bell Peppers (Capsicum), Few long cut pieces
instructions: Wash the goat brains and dry them.
In a medium glass bowl, marinate the goat brain with ginger paste, chopped garlic, lemon juice, green chillies, Kashmiri red chilli powder, salt and an egg yolk for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, coat the brain pieces in bread crumbs and set aside.
Heat oil for frying in a deep pan and fry the brain pieces in batches until golden and crispy; drain on a kitchen towel.
Heat 2 teaspoons oil in another pan and stir‑fry the peppers, chopped onion, green chillies, ginger, tomato ketchup and salt until the vegetables are soft; then turn off the heat.
Skewer the fried brain pieces, place on a serving platter, serve with the stir‑fried vegetables, and drizzle with a little lemon juice.
Serve the Bheja Fry with stir‑fried onion and pepper alongside Dhaniya Pudina Chutney, Tomato Garlic Chutney, or any chutney of your choice.

title: Green Chilli Pickle Recipe (Gujarati Raiwala Marcha)
ingredients: 1/2 cup Yellow mustard seeds, coarsely crushed
instructions: To prepare Green Chilli Pickle Recipe (Gujarati Raiwala Marcha), in a mixing bowl, combine the split mustard seeds, salt, turmeric powder, hing, 1 teaspoon of oil and mix well.
Rub the bhavnagari chillies in a little of the prepared mixture and place them on a big plate.
Sprinkle the remaining mixture evenly over them along with the remaining 3 teaspoons of oil and lemon cubes and toss gently.
Fill them in a glass jar and keep it aside for atleast 1 hour.
Serve or store Green Chilli Pickle Recipe (Gujarati Raiwala Marcha) in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Serve with steamed rice, kadhi or parathas.

title: Soya Beans Paniyaram Recipe (Pan Fried Soy Fritters)
ingredients: Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, small bunch, finely chopped
instructions: Soak the soy beans and urad dal separately for at least 2 hours; then pressure‑cook the soy beans with just enough water until soft, drain excess water.
Blend the boiled potato, cooked soy beans, and soaked urad dal with very little water to form a thick, smooth batter.
Stir in salt, green chillies, and coriander leaves; mix well and adjust salt as needed.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and curry leaves; let them crackle and then add this tempering to the batter, achieving a thick pouring consistency.
Preheat the Kuzhi paniyaram pan and drop spoonfuls of batter into each cavity.
Drizzle oil over the batter, cover the pan, and steam until the tops are set; flip the paniyarams and cook the other side, optionally adding more oil, until all sides are golden brown on medium heat.
Serve the hot Soya Beans Paniyaram with sauce or green chutney.

title: Thayir Semiya Recipe (Curd Semiya)
instructions: Boil the vermicelli in 2 cups water, drain and spread on a colander.
Pass cold water through it to prevent sticking, then set aside to cool.
Heat a kadai/wok, add oil, add the peanuts and roast till brownish, then remove and set aside.
In the same kadai, add more oil if needed, add mustard seeds and after they splutter add the other tempering ingredients.
Add the boiled vermicelli, mix, add salt to taste and mix.
Just before serving, add curd and mix well.
Serve Thayir Semiya on its own for a light and healthy lunch or dinner.

title: Health Benefits of Rasna (Alpinia Galanga) - Ayurvedic Medicinal Plant
instructions: To begin making Rasna, Ayurvedic Medicinal Plant Tea Recipe in a saucepan add all the ingredients, the rasna roots, washed and chopped, the rasna leaves torn into bits and water.
Boil for about 15 minutes till the water reduces to half and forms a strong rasna tea decoction.
Stir in the black pepper powder and cumin powder and give it another brisk boil.
Once combined and infused well, strain the rasna tea and discard the herbs and spices.
Add honey if you like before serving.

title: Aval Kesari Recipe
instructions: In a wok/kadai, add aval and dry roast for about 5 minutes until light brown but not burnt.
Cool the roasted aval and grind it into a powder similar to the consistency of rava.
In a small pot, add water and bring it to a boil.
Heat a pan and add a tablespoon of ghee.
Once the ghee melts, add the powdered aval and combine well.
Add the boiling water slowly to the aval while stirring continuously and cook over low flame until the aval no longer sticks to the bottom of the pan.
If the aval is touched with wet hands, it won’t stick, confirming it is fully cooked.
Add sugar to the cooked aval and stir until the sugar dissolves completely.
Finally, add the remaining ghee and roasted cashews, then remove from the flame.
Serve Aval Kesari with Masala Vada or alongside Keerai Sambar, steamed rice, and raw banana thoran.

title: North East Khapse Recipe (Deep Fried Biscuits From Arunachal)
ingredients: 1/4 cup Oil, & more to deep fry
instructions: To begin making North East Khapse, dissolve the sugar in 1/2 cup of warm water. Combine flour, oil, sugar water and milk in a mixing bowl.
Mix everything together to make a smooth ball of dough. Roll out the dough to about a 1/4 inch thickness.
Cut the dough in strips and slice a slot in the middle of each piece. Pull one corner of the piece of dough through the slot in the middle, creating a twist.
Fry them in a deep fry pan on medium-high heat till the Khapse turns golden brown, moving them around fairly often and very gently.
Serve with hot Masala Chai and Grilled Spicy Potato Sandwich for a perfect tea party.

title: Steamed Cauliflower Curry Recipe (Healthy Stir Fry)
instructions: Steam the cauliflower using a steamer or pressure cooker.

If using a pressure cooker, place the florets in the cooker, sprinkle some salt, add a tablespoon of water, cover, place the weight on, and cook for one whistle; then turn off heat and immediately release the pressure under running cold water.
Open the cooker; the cauliflower should be lightly steamed and firm, which is the desired texture.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in a wok or kadai; add cumin seeds and curry leaves and allow them to crackle, then stir in black pepper powder.
Add the steamed cauliflower to the wok and stir‑fry until the cauliflower is well coated with the pepper and cumin, about one minute, then turn off the heat.
Transfer the steamed cauliflower curry to a serving bowl and serve, or pack into lunch boxes.
Serve the steamed cauliflower curry with Boondi Raita and Phulka for a weekday lunch or dinner.

title: Bloomed Potato Cheesy Muffins Recipe
instructions: To prepare these yummy Bloomed Potato Cheesy Muffins recipe, prep up with all the ingredients first.
In a bowl, add all-purpose flour, oil, salt and water and knead to make a stiff pastry dough. Cover it with a damp cloth.
Boil the potatoes and mash them. Add oregano, salt, black pepper powder, dry basil and rosemary and mix well.
Apply butter generously along the muffin cases.
Preheat the oven for 10 minutes at 200 degree Celsius.
Meanwhile, roll the pastry dough into thin round shapes and place them on the muffin cases.
Brush butter along with the rolled pastry dough. Using a spoon, add half of potato stuffing in each pastry puff placed in the muffin tray.
Add mozzarella cheese cubes in each cups.
Now again add the rest of potato fillings over the cheese.
Sprinkle some chopped coriander leaves over the top.
Place the muffin tray in the oven and bake for 12-15 minutes at 150 degree Celsius.
Once it is baked, let it cool for 5 minutes before removing from the tray, else it might crack.
Once cooled, remove the potato muffins carefully and place them on the serving tray.
Serve Bloomed Potato Cheesy Muffins recipe hot with your favorite dips like cottage cheese dip, tzatziki or peanut chilli dipping sauce to make a yummy appetizer.

title: Stir Fried Carrot And Green Beans Recipe
ingredients: 50 grams green beans (French beans), sliced diagonally
instructions: Heat a flat skillet with some oil and crackle the cumin seeds.
Add the chopped vegetables and sauté, adding a little salt to speed up the process.
Add all the spice powders – red chilli powder, black pepper powder, coriander powder, and salt – and sauté for another 5 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Serve the stir-fried carrot and green beans with Keerai Sambar and steamed rice, or with Mattar Paneer and Makki Ki Roti.

title: Quinoa Phirnee Recipe (Quinoa Milk Pudding)
ingredients: 2 cup Milk (or almond milk for vegans)
1/2 tablespoon Condensed Milk (or khoya/mawa; can be omitted for vegans)
instructions: Heat a saucepan over medium heat, add ghee, and once warm, add quinoa. Roast until light brown.
Add 1 cup hot water to the roasted quinoa and bring to a boil; when reduced to half, add 2 cups hot milk and the saffron strands.
Bring the quinoa‑milk mixture to a boil, then reduce to low heat and simmer for 7‑8 minutes until quinoa is cooked.
Stir in sugar and cardamom powder, cooking until the sugar dissolves; adjust consistency with more hot water if needed.
Add condensed milk (or khoya) and simmer for 5 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Serve the pudding in individual bowls, garnish with chopped mixed nuts, and enjoy warm or chilled.

title: Cheese Masala Omelette Recipe
instructions: Chop tomatoes, onions, chillies and coriander leaves. Grate the required amount of cheese and keep aside.
Break 2 eggs into a mixing bowl and add the chopped tomatoes, onions, green chillies, coriander leaves and grated cheese. Mix all the ingredients well to make the omelette mixture.
Place an omelette pan on medium heat and add some oil to grease the pan. Once the pan is hot, reduce the flame to low and add the egg mixture to the pan, spreading it evenly.
Cover the pan with the lid so that the omelette cooks a little faster.

Remove the lid and check if the omelette has cooked. Flip the omelette to cook the other side or fold it in half and cover the pan again so the cheese melts inside and all ingredients cook thoroughly.
Keep the lid on for 30 seconds to a minute, then turn off the flame.
Serve the Cheese Masala Omelette with a cup of Adrak Chai and a fruit bowl for a sumptuous breakfast.

title: Stuffed Potato Cutlet Recipe With Mint Mayo
instructions: Boil the potatoes, peel them, and grate into a bowl.
Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, amchur powder, coriander leaves, oregano, and salt to taste. Mix well.
Mix the corn flour with 1 teaspoon water, whisking to ensure no lumps. Set aside.

Take a portion of the mashed potatoes, roll into a ball, make a small hole in the center, spoon in Del Monte Mint Mayo and top with grated cheese. Cover with another portion of the potato mixture, seal, and flatten into a disc.
Whisk the corn starch mixture again, dip each cutlet in it, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs. Set aside and repeat for all cutlets.
Heat oil for deep frying. When hot, carefully drop a few cutlets at a time and fry on medium heat until crunchy and golden brown on all sides. Remove and place on kitchen paper to drain.
Serve the stuffed potato cutlets with chutney or ketchup as an appetizer.

title: Lemon Pudina Curry Leaf Shikanji Recipe
instructions: In a mixer jar, combine the curry leaves, mint leaves, freshly squeezed lemon juice, roasted cumin seeds, jaggery, and black salt to taste; pulse in the mixer grinder.
Add water to the mixture and pulse once again.
Serve the Lemon Pudina Curry Leaf Shikanji chilled over ice in glasses as a party drink.

Optionally, serve the shikanji as a welcome drink alongside party foods such as Crispy Baby Corn Cheese Lollipops, Smoked Dal Makhani Dhaba Style, Butter Garlic Naan, and Shahi Tukda Gajar Halwa Shots with Rabri.

title: Apple Jalebi Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup All Purpose Flour (Maida) - for batter
1 tablespoon All Purpose Flour (Maida) - for dusting
instructions: In a mixing bowl, add all purpose flour, yogurt and some water, mix well to make a thick batter; let it rest for 5 to 6 hours.
Make sugar syrup by adding sugar, water, saffron, rose water and green cardamom in a saucepan; cook until slightly thick (about 2-string consistency).
On a plate, combine 1 tablespoon all purpose flour and 1 tablespoon cinnamon powder and mix well.
Peel the apples, remove the cores, cut into round slices, and coat the apple slices in the flour‑cinnamon mixture.
Dip the coated apple slices into the batter, then deep‑fry in hot oil or ghee over low heat until light golden; soak the fried apples in the sugar syrup for 2 to 3 minutes, avoiding over‑soaking.
Remove the apples from the syrup and garnish with chopped cherries and pistachios.
Serve the apple jalebi as a party dessert, optionally with vanilla ice‑cream or alongside other festive dishes.

title: Jackfruit Seed Modak Recipe
ingredients: Ghee, as required, for rubbing the hands
Thonnai (dried leaves), as needed, to cover the pan
instructions: Begin by preparing the jackfruit seed stuffing.
Take a pressure cooker, add the jackfruit seeds with enough water, and pressure cook for 4 whistles.
Allow the pressure to release naturally, drain the water, remove the outer thick white skin (brown skin is fine), and let the seeds cool completely.
In a mixer grinder, combine the cooked jackfruit seeds, powdered palm sugar, and cardamom powder; blend well without adding water.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and divide into 14 equal balls, rubbing your palms with ghee to prevent sticking.
Prepare the outer layer of the modak.
Take 1 cup of rice flour, add a pinch of salt and half a teaspoon of sesame oil; boil 2 cups of water (may not need all).
Gradually pour the hot water onto the rice flour, mixing to form a pliable dough; add sesame oil and keep covered with a wet cloth.
Rub your hands with ghee, take a small portion of the rice dough, and shape it into a round ball.
Press the dough to form a cup shape, place the stuffing inside, and seal it.
Place dried thonnai leaves in a pressure cooker, arrange the modaks on the leaves, and steam for 15 minutes.
Serve the Jackfruit Seed Modak on festivals or as a dessert.

title: Karachi Biscuits Recipe
instructions: To prepare Karachi Biscuits Recipe, in a large mixing bowl, sieve in All-purpose flour and Custard powder and Mix well.
Add in roughly chopped cashew nuts and Tutti frutti. Mix.
In another mixing bowl add butter and powdered sugar. Cream the butter and sugar well by whisking and then add in milk. Whisk everything together.
Once the milk, butter and sugar are well combined, add prepared mixture of flour, custard nuts and tutti frutti, in batches. Make sure there are no lumps.
Add a little mil if you feel that the dough is too dry.
Roll the prepared dough to form rectangular logs or any desired shapes and cover it using a cling wrap and freeze it for about 15 mins or until it become firm.
Meanwhile, preheat oven at 180 Deg C.
Once firmed, remove cling wrap from the dough and cut into even sized biscuits.
Arrange cookies to be baked on a baking sheet with 1 inch gap in between and bake in preheated oven for about 15 minutes or until the cookies start darkening in colour.
Once the completely cooled store Karachi Biscuits recipe in airtight containers and enjoy with Ginger Cardamom Chai.

title: Cauliflower Matar Bhurji Recipe
instructions: Bring water to boil in a pot, add cauliflower florets and keep aside for 10 minutes.
Drain the water and grate the florets into fine pieces or process in a food processor.
Heat half a tablespoon of oil in a kadai over medium heat.
Add grated cauliflower and fry for about 5 minutes until water is absorbed; set aside.
In a kadai, add oil and the finely chopped onions.
Cook onions until transparent, then add ginger garlic paste and mix well.
Add tomato pieces and cook until mushy.
Add peas, turmeric powder, red chili powder and salt as required.
Cook for about 5 minutes until the spices are well mixed with the peas.
Add the fried cauliflower to the peas mixture and combine well.
Close the lid and cook until the grated florets are cooked through.
Do not overcook the cauliflower to avoid it becoming soggy.
Sprinkle garam masala powder over the bhurji and toss well.
Switch off the flame and allow the dish to cool slightly.
Serve the cauliflower bhurji with Matar alongside Boondi Raita and Phulkas.

title: Bhang Thandai Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup whole almonds, blanched and skin removed
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients. Blanch the almonds, peel the skin and set aside.
In a mixer grinder, powder the poppy seeds, fennel seeds, blanched almonds, black peppercorns, cardamom seeds and bhang paste into a smooth powder or paste.
In a saucepan, bring the milk and saffron to a brisk boil. When the milk boils, stir in the prepared bhang thandai masala and sugar; whisk well, optionally using an electric hand blender.
Turn off the heat and let the thandai cool. Once cooled, refrigerate for at least 5‑6 hours or add ice to chill faster.
Serve the chilled Bhang Thandai during Holi, optionally with snacks such as baked Maddur Vada or Makki Paneer Pakora.

title: Beetroot, Sweet Potato And Oatmeal Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Whole Wheat Bread crumbs, made fresh
instructions: To begin making Beetroot, Sweet Potato and Oatmeal Cutlet Recipe, boil the sweet potato using pressure cooker, peel the skin off, mash and keep aside.
In the mean, dry roast the rolled oats in a wide pan and keep aside.

Now, take a big bowl and add in the grated beetroot, boiled & mashed sweet potatoes, roasted oatmeal, boiled corn kernels, green chillies, coriander, grated ginger, along with the spices mentioned and half of the bread crumbs and mix well.
Divide the mixture to equal portions and shape them to a oval flat cutlets or any shape you desire.
Now, take each cutlet formed, coat it with the remaining bread crumbs and gently press it so that the bread crumbs stick to the surface of the cutlets.
Heat oil in a pan on medium heat and place the crumb coated cutlets and let it cook till a golden crust forms on its surface. This will take around 5 minutes.
Now, flip over and cook the other side a well till it is golden brown.
Likewise, prepare the rest of the cutlets.
Serve the Beetroot, Sweet Potato and Oatmeal Cutlet Recipe as an after school snack for kids or as a tea time snack along with Green Chutney and Masala Tea.

title: Royal Bread Gulab Jamun Recipe
instructions: Combine the khoya and chopped dry fruits in a bowl and set aside.
Cut out the sides of the milk bread.
Dip each bread slice in milk and squeeze out the milk.
Knead the bread slices to make a soft dough; knead well and form small balls.
Flatten each dough ball in your palm, place a small portion of the khoya and nuts mixture in the center, seal, and roll into a small round ball.
Repeat the process with the remaining dough portions.
In a saucepan, heat the sugar with 2 cups water and make a syrup of one-string consistency; set aside.
Heat ghee for deep frying over medium heat and fry the bread jamun balls until golden brown, then drain excess oil.
Dip the fried Bread Jamuns in the sugar syrup and allow them to soak and fluff up.
Serve the Bread Gulab Jamun.

title: Khatta Meetha Petha Recipe (Yellow Pumpkin Sabzi)
instructions: Peel, deseed and cut the pumpkin into cubes of approximately 3/4 inch each. Chop the green chillies as well and set aside.
In a kadai or skillet on medium heat, dry roast the fennel seeds and peppercorns until fragrant. Transfer them to a bowl to cool.
In the same skillet, heat oil over medium heat, add the pumpkin cubes, stir in salt and cook for a few minutes until the pumpkin begins to soften.
Reduce heat to low, add sugar, salt, green chillies and stir to combine. Cover and cook until the pumpkin is fully soft.
Pound the roasted fennel seeds and peppercorns to a coarse powder using a mortar‑pestle or grinder.
Open the skillet lid, add the fennel‑pepper powder along with dry mango powder and stir to combine. Adjust salt and spices to taste, then cook for another minute and turn off the heat.
Stir in the chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the Khatta Meetha Petha with phulka and raita, or pack it for lunch.

title: Sukhe Methi Chole Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cups Kabuli Chana (White Chickpeas), soaked for 8 hours
2 cups Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), washed and finely chopped
instructions: Wash and soak the kabuli chana overnight.
Next morning, add the kabuli chana with a cup of water and some salt into a pressure cooker; cook for 7-8 whistles (about 30 minutes).
Reduce the flame and simmer for another 10 minutes, then turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Drain the excess water and set the boiled kabuli chana aside.
In a kadai, heat ghee over medium flame, add cumin seeds and bay leaf and let them sizzle.
Add ginger, garlic and green chilli; sauté for about a minute.
Add the onions and sauté until they turn translucent.
Add salt, turmeric powder, and tomatoes; sprinkle some water, cover, and cook until the tomatoes become mushy (2-3 minutes on medium‑high flame).
Uncover and mix well to combine the onion‑tomato mixture.
Add the washed and chopped fenugreek leaves; cook until they wilt.
After a couple of minutes, ensure the methi leaves are well combined with the onion‑tomato mixture.
Stir in the dry spice powders—red chilli powder, cumin powder, garam masala powder, coriander powder—and the boiled chole; mix thoroughly.
Stir‑fry the Sukhe Methi Chole for another 3‑4 minutes, turn off the heat, and adjust salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

title: Baked Vermicelli Malpua Recipe
instructions: Cook the vermicelli with the required amount of water; use very fine roasted wheat vermicelli.
Drain the excess water and allow the vermicelli to cool down.
In a saucepan, make the sugar syrup by heating the sugar and water with 2 cardamom pods; boil until slightly thick and sticky.

Take the cooled vermicelli, lightly mash it, add cottage cheese and mash well, then add milk powder, gulab jamun mix, fennel seeds, cardamom powder and baking soda; mix everything, add milk slowly and form a thick batter.
Let the batter stay at room temperature for an hour.
Grease a baking tray with oil and ghee, pour the batter with a ladle, keeping space between each portion.
Bake in a preheated oven at 200 °C for about 15 minutes, checking time and temperature for your specific oven.
Once baked, dip each malpua in the sugar syrup and remove, or drizzle the syrup on top if preferred.
Garnish with chopped pistachios and serve them warm.
Serve the baked vermicelli malpua as a dessert after a Holi meal or during snack time, alongside Dahi Vada and Thandai.

title: Broken Wheat Porridge For Babies And Toddler
instructions: To begin making Broken Wheat Porridge with Apples and Oranges, we have to first pressure cook the broken wheat/ Dalia.
In a pressure cooker add 1/2 cup broken wheat or dalia along with 1/2 cup water.
Pressure cook for 3 whistles and turn off the heat. Release the pressure naturally.
Meanwhile, we can get the apple and banana ready.
Peel the banana and mash it fine on a plate with the back of a fork, keep aside.
Peel, core and chop the apple into small pieces. Add these apple pieces into a pot with enough water to cover them.
Boil the apples in the water until soft, about ten minutes, ensuring there is enough water in the pot.
Once the apples are soft, turn off the heat, remove the apple pieces from the pan and mash them with the back of a fork.
Alternatively, pressure cook the chopped apples for 1 whistle and release the pressure naturally.
In a medium‑sized bowl, add the cooked broken wheat, mashed banana, and mashed apples and mix well until all ingredients are combined.
Your Broken Wheat Porridge with Bananas and Apples is ready to be served.
Serve the Broken Wheat Porridge to babies and toddlers over 10 months of age for a wholesome lunch or dinner.

title: Niramish Aloo Dum Recipe
instructions: Wash, boil, peel and coarsely mash the potatoes so that large chunks remain intact.
Make a paste of the dry ginger powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and garam masala powder with a little water.
Heat oil in a wok/kadhai. Add dry red chilies and cumin seeds; once they splutter, add the hing and turn off the gas.
Add the masala paste, stir well, turn the gas back on, and add the mashed potatoes along with salt.
Saute for 1 minute, then add water as required for the gravy.
Let it boil, then cover and simmer for 5–6 minutes or until the desired gravy consistency is reached.
Serve the Niramish Aloo Dum with Bengali Luchi (or your preferred accompaniment).

title: Aval Puttu Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Aval Puttu, grind the aval in a mixer grinder to make a coarse powder.
Sprinkle 1/4 cup of water and mix gently with hands. Make sure that you don’t mash the aval. Keep it aside for 10 minutes.
Again sprinkle some water after 10 minutes and mix it properly.
Take jaggery in a deep micro-safe container, add water just immersing jaggery powder and microwave it for about 2 minutes.
Filter jaggery water to remove impurities. Now microwave it for 6 to 8 minutes more to achieve the desired consistency.
Now heat ghee and fry cashews till they turn golden brown. Add grated coconut, fried cashews, aval and mix everything properly.
Microwave it for 2 minutes more and it is ready to be served.
Serve Aval Puttu as a sweet dish during the festival of Krishna Jayanti.

title: Raw Banana Raita Recipe
instructions: To begin making Raw Banana Raita Recipe, pressure cook the plantain or raw banana for 2 whistles using a pressure cooker.
Once it is cooked, peel the skin, grate it using a fine grater and keep aside.
Add the yogurt to a big bowl and whisk it into a creamy consistency.
To this add the grated plantain or the raw banana, grated ginger, cumin powder, salt and mix well.
Now heat oil in a small tadka pan, add mustard seeds, urad dal and let it crackle.
Add the red chilli and curry leaves and let it splutter.
Pour this tadka over the raita and sprinkle a pinch of cumin powder on top.
Serve the Raw Banana Raita along with Vegetable Biryani and Salad for the weekend lunch.

title: Healthy Snack Bowl Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup soy milk, coconut milk or almond milk
1 to 2 tablespoons maple syrup, or honey
instructions: In a saucepan, add 1 tablespoon coconut oil and heat on medium; after 30–40 seconds drop 2 to 3 corn kernels and wait for them to pop.
Once they pop, scoop them out, add all the kernels, stir quickly, and cover the lid, leaving a gap for steam to escape to prevent burning.
Shake the saucepan every few seconds to ensure even heat.
When popping slows and stops, turn off the heat, remove the lid, sprinkle a tiny amount of salt, and give it a shake.
In another saucepan, combine peanut butter, cocoa powder, milk, and maple syrup; stir on low heat until saucy and smooth, then turn off once it starts to bubble.
Place the popcorn in a bowl, add sultanas, walnuts, and apple cubes, drizzle the sauce over, and serve.
Optional: add pretzels, other nuts, or dried fruit as desired.
Do not add too much salt, as peanut butter already provides some saltiness.
Serve the healthy snack bowl during a movie night or pack it in a snack box.

title: Broccoli Paneer And Peanut Masala Recipe
instructions: To begin with Broccoli Paneer And Peanut Masala, heat a teaspoon of oil in a wok. Add pepper corns and 1 teaspoon Jeera/ Cumin.
Once it splutters, add the chopped onions and chillies. Roast till the onions turn slightly brown.
Add the peanuts and roast for 3-4 minutes on medium flame.
After 3-4 minutes, add the chopped tomatoes and mix well. Once the tomatoes turn mushy switch off the flame and allow it to cool.
Once it reaches the room temperature, blend it into a fine paste in a blender. Keep the paste aside.
Heat a teaspoon of oil in the same wok. Add jeera/cumin, chili powder and turmeric/ haldi. Add broccoli and sauté on medium flame for 8 to 10 minutes.
Add paneer, garam masala and biryani masala. Mix well and ensure it does not burn. Add the onion-tomato paste and mix well.
Add salt, butter and let it simmer on medium flame for 5 to 8 minutes. Lastly, add kasuri methi and mix well. Switch off the flame after 5 minutes and it is ready to be served.
Serve Broccoli Paneer And Peanut Masala with phulka or whole wheat Lachha parathas and Beetroot Raita for a delicious meal.

title: Buckwheat Vegetable Khichdi Recipe
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat in water and soak it for at least 2 hours.
Soak the moong dal for about half an hour.
In a pressure cooker, add oil and ghee. Once hot, add shahi jeera and wait till it turns golden brown.
Add slit green chilies, peppercorns, and cloves; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped vegetables and cook on medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Drain the soaked buckwheat and moong dal and add them to the cooker. Sauté for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring continuously.
Add 5 cups hot water to the cooker, along with salt to taste, and mix well.
Cover the pressure cooker lid and cook for 2 whistles.
When the pressure releases, open the cooker and mix the khichdi well.
In a tadka pan, heat 1 teaspoon ghee. Fry sliced garlic and onion until golden brown, then pour over the khichdi.
Serve the Buckwheat Vegetable Khichdi with Tomato Onion Cucumber Raita, Tadka Raita, or any raita of your choice.

title: Masaura And Potato Tarkari Recipe
instructions: Heat a heavy-bottomed pan and add one tablespoon of oil.
When the oil is hot, fry the masauras until golden brown, then set aside on a plate.
In the same pan, add another tablespoon of oil, heat, add cumin seeds and let them splutter; then add chopped onions and turmeric powder and fry until onions turn light brown.
Add the chopped potatoes, salt, and black pepper; fry on low heat for about ten minutes until potatoes are light brown and half‑cooked.

Stir in garlic paste, ginger paste, green chilli paste, and cumin powder for a couple of minutes; then add the fried masauras, followed by tomatoes, water, and fresh cream. Cover and simmer for about fifteen minutes until the potatoes are fully cooked.
Turn off the heat and serve.

title: Methi Corn Dal Vada Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Chana dal (Bengal Gram Dal), soaked at least for 4 hours/overnight
1/2 cup Arhar dal (Split Toor Dal), soaked at least for 4 hours/overnight
instructions: To prepare Methi Corn Dal Vada Recipe, soak Toor Dal and Chana Dal in water overnight or at least for 4 hours.
Drain the water from the dal and set it aside.

In a blender, add soaked dals, green chilies, ginger, and cumin seeds. Grind them into a coarse paste in a mixer. Do not add water while grinding. The addition of water will make the vada absorb oil more than required, while deep frying.
In a bowl, add the grounded dal, methi leaves, turmeric powder, red chili powder, corn, curry leaves and salt. Combine them together.
Meanwhile, in a medium-sized Kadai, heat oil over high heat.
Once the oil is smoking hot, reduce the flame to medium and maintain an even temperature throughout cooking.
Take a lemon sized ball in hand and flatten it with your fingers. Ensure the Methi Corn Vada is not too thick and too large.
Gently slide in the flattened balls into oil and cook until they become light brownish.
Flip it occasionally to ensure that the vadas are cooked evenly. Once they are cooked, drain excess oil from the vadas and spread them on a paper towel to pat them off excess oil.
Serve Methi Corn Dal Vada recipe warm with Mysore Chutney or any chutney of your choice.

title: Pumpkin Wade (Sweet Pumpkin Pooris) Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Kaddu (Parangikai/ Pumpkin), peeled and finely chopped
instructions: To begin with Pumpkin Wade, pressure cook the pumpkin by adding sufficient water for 3 whistles. Switch off the gas and let it cool down.
After the pressure gets released, open the pressure cooker, drain and retain the water.
Now in a mixing bowl add the whole wheat flour, boiled pumpkin and other ingredients and mix well. Add 1/2 cup water, preferably the water which was used to boil the pumpkin.
Knead well to make a soft dough. Ensure that the pumpkin gets nicely mashed while making a dough.
Keep the dough covered with a lid or soft muslin cloth for about 20 minutes.
After 20 Minutes, apply some oil to your hands and make small balls from the dough.
Spread some loose flour on the rolling table and flatten the balls into small circles of approximately 2 inches in diameter. Do not flatten the dough like regular pooris, as the wade will be crispy.
Flatten them a bit thicker than that we do for regular pooris. One by one flatten all the balls into small thick pooris and keep them ready on a separate plate.
In a kadai or wok, add oil. Let the oil get heated. Now add one flattened wade/poori into the hot oil carefully.
Using a frying spoon or slotted spoon gently press the poori, put some hot oil on top and move in a circular way.

You will notice that the poori gets puffed and rises up. At this point, turn it to the other side and fry till it turns golden brown. Do not keep the poori in oil for more than 3 minutes else it will become brittle.
Drain it on kitchen towel. Continue the deep frying process for all the other flattened pooris.
Serve Pumpkin Wade with Sabudana Kheer or you can have it with Masala Chai during your tea time break.

title: Kachcha Kela Masala Sabzi Recipe (Raw Banana with Tomatoes & Spices)
ingredients: Red Chilli powder , as required to taste
instructions: To begin making the Kachcha Kela Masala Sabzi Recipe, we will first cook the raw bananas in the pressure cooker. Cut the raw bananas in half and place it in the cooker. Add 1/4 cup of water, cover the cooker and place the weight on. Pressure cook until you hear 3 to 4 whistles and turn off the heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the pressure has released, open the cooker and peel the skin of the bananas. Cut them into dices and keep aside.

The next step is to make the masala and cook the kachcha kela sabzi. Heat a teaspoon of oil in a heavy bottomed pan or a wok. Add the grated ginger, tomatoes, turmeric, asafoetida, bay leaves, garam masala, coriander powder and red chili powder.

Stir all the ingredients well and add the cooked raw banana and salt and stir to combine. Turn the heat to low, cover the pan and cook the Kela Masala Sabzi until you see the masala is well coated with the sabzi. This will take about 5 minutes.
Once done, check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste.
Serve the Kachcha Kela Masala Sabzi Recipe along with favorite Dal for a lunch or even pack it into a lunch box.

title: Creamy and Delicious Fruit Custard Recipe
ingredients: 3 Ripe Bananas (small), cut into small cubes
1/2 cup Green Grapes, cut in half
instructions: Mix the custard powder with a little milk to form a smooth mixture with no lumps, then add the remaining milk and stir well.
Place the custard milk in a saucepan and cook over medium heat, continuously stirring until the custard thickens.
Once thickened, add the sugar and stir for another 3 to 4 minutes; ensure the custard is cooked and creamy.
Allow the custard to cool completely.
Add the chopped seasonal fruits to the cooled custard and stir.
Serve the fruit custard as a dessert.

title: Masala Cornflakes Chicken Recipe
ingredients: 1 kg boneless chicken, cut into bite‑sized pieces
2 cups corn flakes, processed to a coarse powder
instructions: Marinate the chicken in a mixing bowl with red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, ginger‑garlic paste, chopped coriander leaves, and salt; let it rest for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep‑frying pan until hot.
Dip each marinated chicken piece in beaten egg, then coat it thoroughly in the corn‑flake mixture.
Carefully lower the coated chicken pieces into the hot oil and deep‑fry until they turn golden brown.
Remove the fried chicken onto paper towels to absorb any excess oil.
Serve the Masala Cornflakes Chicken with dhaniya pudina chutney, date tamarind chutney, or any chutney of your choice.

title: Motichoor Modak Recipe
ingredients: Oil, as required, for frying boondis
instructions: Sieve the besan, then add salt, orange food colour and ghee.
Mix well and add water gradually to form a smooth batter with a consistency similar to thick dosa batter.
Heat oil in a wok/kadai; just before making the boondis, add baking soda and give a quick mix.
When the oil is hot, use a perforated ladle to make boondis; remove them when 3/4 done and drain on a kitchen towel. Repeat until all boondis are fried.
Allow the fried boondis to cool completely, then grind them into a coarse powder.
Heat sugar and water in a kadai/wok over medium flame; when it reaches one‑string consistency, add orange food colour and turn off the flame.
To the coarse boondi powder, add crushed almonds, melon seeds, salt, rose water, cardamom powder, saffron and ghee; mix roughly.
Add the sugar syrup little by little, mixing well; cover and let rest for 15–20 minutes so the boondi absorbs the flavours.
After 20 minutes, mix again by hand, grease a modak mould with ghee, fill with the boondi mixture, shape into modaks, refrigerate briefly and then serve.
Serve Motichoor Modak as a religious offering during Ganesh Chaturthi or as a sweet dish after a meal of Achari Masala Puri and Aloo Dum.

title: Chocolate Kaju Katli Recipe - Chocolate Kaju Barfi
ingredients: 1 cup Milk chocolate, or dark chocolate
instructions: Grind the cashew nuts in a blender to make a fine powder.
Take a heavy‑bottomed pan, add the sugar and water, place over medium heat and bring to boil. Once the sugar has dissolved, reduce heat and boil until the syrup reaches a one‑string consistency.
Test the consistency by dropping a few drops of the syrup on a clean plate, let cool 15–20 seconds, and check for a single thread between thumb and index finger.
If the syrup has reached single‑thread consistency, add the ground cashew nut powder to the syrup and stir continuously for 4–5 minutes until it becomes a thick paste.
Remove the mixture from heat, let it cool to room temperature, then grease your palms with a dash of ghee and knead until smooth, uniform, and dough‑like.
Spread a sheet of butter paper on the countertop, place the dough on it and roll out with a rolling pin to a thickness of 5–6 mm evenly.
Place a saucepan with water on heat, set a heat‑proof bowl over it and melt the dark chocolate in the bowl, ensuring the water does not touch the bowl.
Pour the melted chocolate over the rolled kaju katli dough and spread evenly with a spatula.
Allow it to cool slightly, then transfer to a surface and refrigerate for 15–20 minutes to let the chocolate solidify.
Once set, cut the chocolate kaju katlis into intersecting diagonal lines to form diamond shapes.
Serve the chocolate kaju katli with Angoori Rasmalai at a festive gathering with family and friends.

title: Green Spinach & Oats Cutlet Recipe
instructions: Get all the ingredients ready.
Heat a heavy bottomed pan and roast the oats for a few minutes until a roasted aroma develops; then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the chopped spinach and sauté until wilted and excess moisture evaporates; remove from heat and let cool.
Combine the roasted oats, cooked spinach, green peas, green chillies, coriander, salt, pepper, oregano and lemon juice in a food processor to make a coarse mixture.
Check and adjust salt and spice levels to taste.
Divide the mixture into 8-10 portions, grease your fingers with oil, flatten and shape each cutlet.
Grease and preheat a skillet over medium heat, place the cutlet portions, drizzle a little oil and cook both sides until lightly browned and crisp.
Serve the cutlets with green chutney or tomato ketchup as a tea‑time snack.

title: Cheese Salad Wrap Recipe
ingredients: 1 Red, Yellow and Green Bell Peppers (Capsicum), thinly sliced
4 tablespoons Roasted tomato pasta sauce, or chilli sauce
3 tablespoons Hung Curd (Greek Yogurt), or cream cheese/veg mayonnaise
instructions: To begin making the Cheese Salad Wrap recipe, prepare the dressing.
To the hung curd add minced garlic, cumin powder, chat masala, crushed pepper and salt to taste. Mix it nicely.
In a big mixing vessel take shredded cucumbers, shredded carrots, shredded cabbage, sliced capsicum and sliced onions.
To the shredded veggies add the dressing. Mix well and taste test. Filling for cheesy salad wrap is ready.
On a griddle slightly warm the tortillas / roti without applying oil.
Place a tortilla on a clean dry surface and spread tomato sauce or chilly sauce on it.
Place few lettuce on the centre of the flatbread.
Now add 1 to 2 tablespoon of the cheesy salad mixture in the central part. Finish it off with some grated cheese. And roll it up tightly.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients to make 3 more wraps. Serve the veggies Cheesy salad wrap immediately.
Serve Cheese Salad Wrap along with Creamed Spinach as a tea time snack with Hot Masala Chai.

title: Honey Glazed Corn Fritters Recipe
ingredients: 1-1/2 cup sweet corn, boiled and mashed coarsely
3 teaspoons sweet corn, boiled (for honey sauce)
instructions: Mix the mashed corn, mashed potato, chopped green chillies, chopped ginger, and salt together.
Add the bread crumbs to the mixture and shape into balls or desired fritter shape.
Prepare a thin batter by mixing all purpose flour with water; coat the balls with this batter.
Deep‑fry the coated balls in oil until golden brown; set aside.
In a wok, heat a little oil and sauté grated ginger.
Add boiled corn kernels, roasted tomato pasta sauce, green chilli sauce, and soy sauce; cook for about 5 minutes.
Stir in honey, then add the fried fritters and sauté for another 5 minutes, coating them well with the sauce.
Garnish with finely chopped spring onion and serve hot as a tea‑time appetizer.

title: Baked Paneer Bread Pakora Recipe
instructions: Prepare the bread by cutting off the brown edges/crust. Gently roll each slice with a rolling pin and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
In a mixing bowl, combine the grated paneer, ginger, mint leaves, coriander leaves, red chilli flakes, salt, and pepper. Mix well and set the paneer mixture aside.
Take a rolled bread slice, place a tablespoon of the paneer mixture near one edge, brush the opposite edges with a little water to help seal, and tightly roll the slice. Repeat for all slices.
Place the rolls on a baking tray, brush them with melted butter, and bake in the preheated oven for 12–15 minutes until golden. Remove from the oven.
Serve the baked paneer bread pakoras with tomato sauce or green chutney.

title: Banana And Ragi Porridge Recipe For Babies And Toddlers
instructions: Make sure you have homemade ragi powder.
In a pan, add 1/4 cup water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and add the ragi powder, stirring continuously.
Continue stirring until the porridge becomes slightly thick.
Turn off heat and let the porridge cool a bit.
Mash the banana on a plate until smooth, without lumps.
Mix the mashed banana into the ragi porridge thoroughly.
Serve the porridge to babies/toddlers over 6 months.

title: Murmura Jaggery Laddu/ Pori Urundai Recipe
instructions: We begin making the Murmura Jaggery Laddu Recipe by dry roasting the puffed rice and roasted channa separately and keep it ready.
Next you can also dry roast the desiccated coconut in the same pan till it is golden brown and keep it ready. Add all the roasted ingredients along with cardamom powder in one bowl and keep it aside.

Once that is done, add the powdered jaggery with a tablespoon of water and melt the jaggery slowly. Keep stirring till it thickens. Keep a water in a bowl. Add a drop of jaggery into the bowl to check if it has reached the soft boil stage, which forms small droplets.
When jaggery has reached that stage, carefully add the mixture and mix without smashing the puffed rice.
Switch off the heat and apply ghee on your palm and start making laddus depending on your required shape and size.
Serve the Murmura Jaggery Laddu / Pori Urundai (Puffed Rice Balls with Jaggery) as a crunchy snack or tea‑time snack.

title: How to make Sprouts at Home
instructions: To begin making the sprouts, soak the grains or legumes, completely immersed in water for at least 12 to 15 hours. You will know it's soaked enough, when you take a bite and it feels good to eat.

At this stage, drain the water. Place the soaked grains/legumes in a wet muslin cloth and sprinkle some water over the grains. Place the muslin cloth with the soaked grains in a bowl and cover it lightly with a lid so there is air circulation.

When you notice the muslin cloth is dry, sprinkle some water on the cloth, so there is continuous moisture in the cloth. The moisture and air will help the grains/legumes sprout. The process of sprouting will take at least 12 hours based on the size of the grain or legume.
Once you notice the grains/legumes have sprouted, transfer them to a storage container and store them in the refrigerator for about a week and use them as desired.

title: Matar Ajwain Ki Puri Recipe
instructions: Grind the peas together with the green chillies and set the paste aside.
In a bowl combine wheat flour, turmeric powder, salt, chopped coriander leaves, ajwain, and cumin seeds; mix well.
Add the ground pea‑chilli paste to the flour mixture and knead, adding water little by little, until a slightly stiff dough forms.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into small golf‑ball sized portions, roll each into a disc, and dust with dry flour.
Deep‑fry the discs on medium‑high heat until they puff up and turn lightly golden.
Serve the hot Matar Ajwain Ki Puri with yogurt.

title: Chicken In White Gravy Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Chicken In White Gravy recipe, melt butter in a pressure cooker, add onions, cardamom and cinnamon and sauté till the onions turn golden.
Next add ginger garlic paste and sauté for a couple of minutes till the raw smell goes away.
At this stage add curd and mix well. Next add in the chicken pieces, salt and white pepper powder and mix well.
Add 1/3 cup water and close the lid of the pressure cooker. Pressure cook for 2 whistles and switch off the gas.
Once the pressure has released transfer to a serving bowl.
Serve Chicken In White Gravy along with Garlic Naan and some Pickled Onions for a complete meal.

title: Chicken Keema Samosa Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon chaat masala powder, as required
instructions: Place the flour, ghee, salt and ajwain in a food processor. Add little water at a time and make a firm and yet smooth dough.
Divide the dough into large lemon size portions. Cover the dough and keep aside.
In the same food processor jar, attach the chopper blade. Add the chicken and blend to make a fine mince of the chicken. Keep aside.
The next step is to make the chicken keema samosa filling.
Heat oil over medium heat in a pan; add the ginger, garlic, green chillies and onions and saute until the onions soften.
Once the onions soften, add the red chilli powder, garam masala powder, amchur powder, chaat masala powder, minced chicken and salt.
Saute the chicken keema along with the spices until the chicken is cooked, about 4 minutes, until it resembles an egg scramble.
Turn off the heat, check the salt and spices and adjust to taste. Stir in the mint or coriander leaves and allow it to cool.
Fill a small cup with water and keep aside; this will be used for sealing the edges of the cone.
On a floured surface, roll each portion into a 6‑inch diameter circle and cut each circle into half.
Spread water lightly along the edge of the semicircle. Fold the semicircle into a cone shape and seal the side edges, leaving the opening open.
Fill the cone with one or two tablespoons of the chicken keema filling. Press the filling down gently, then close the top of the cone into a triangle shape, pinching the top edge to seal.
Heat oil in a heavy‑bottomed pan for deep frying on medium heat; gently slip in a couple of samosas and fry until they float to the top.
Fry them until they turn light golden‑brown on all sides, maintaining medium heat.
Continue with the remaining samosas and drain them on absorbent paper.
Serve chicken keema samosas as a snack with dhaniya pudina chutney and date tamarind chutney.

title: Sweet Boondi / Meethi Boondi Recipe
instructions: To prepare Sweet Boondi/Meethi Boondi Recipe, take gram flour/besan in a sifter and sieve it.
In a Mixing bowl, mix gram flour, baking soda with water. The batter should be little thick, a bit thinner than normal bajji batter.

Take a big ladle full of batter for orange color in a separate small bowl. Add orange food color to the batter in the small bowl, yellow food color to the batter in the main bowl and mix both well separately. This is an optional step, only if you are adding food colors.
Slotted ladles are needed. One for making boondi and another for draining boondi from oil.

Now heat oil for deep frying. Oil should be moderately hot. To test, drop a pea size batter in the oil, batter should rise immediately without changing color which means oil is ready for frying boondis.

Now hold one slotted ladle just over oil (neither too low nor too high). Use another deep ladle to pour batter over slotted ladle. Pour one ladle full of batter over the slotted ladle and spread in a circular motion by the back of the deep ladle. The batter will fall drop by drop.
Fry them till little crispy. Drain and place them on a paper towel to absorb excess oil.
Repeat the process with rest of the batter.
Then make sugar syrup from 3/4 cup sugar & 1/2 cup water of 1 string consistency by bringing it to boil. Add in cardamom powder, mix well to make syrup.
Add the fried yellow and orange boondis into the syrup. Gently toss them and mix till boondis are well coated in sugar syrup.
Let this set for 1-2 hours until the sugar syrup is completely absorbed by Sweet Boondi / Meethi Boondi Recipe and the sugar in the syrup is crystallized.
Store Sweet Boondi/Meethi Boondi Recipe in an air-tight container and serve as needed, as a sweet munch after meals.

title: Shallow Fried Oysters Recipe
ingredients: 20 Oysters, well-rinsed and drained in colander
instructions: Clean the oysters, drain excess water in a colander, and pat dry with a paper towel.
Mix garam masala powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, Sooji, and rice flour together on a plate.
Heat a skillet or pan and add a tablespoon of oil.
Coat each oyster thoroughly with the prepared masala mixture and place them in the skillet.
Cover the pan with a plate and cook on medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes.
Check the oysters; if they look dry, add a little more oil and continue frying.
After about 3 minutes, flip the oysters and cook uncovered for an additional 2-3 minutes.
When the oysters are dark browned on both sides and fully cooked, turn off the heat.
Serve the shallow fried oysters hot with rice, mutton biryani, or fish curry.

title: Diabetic Friendly Green Moong Dal/ Mung Beans Soup Recipe
instructions: Wash the green moong dal and soak it in water for 4 hours or overnight.
Add the soaked dal to a pressure cooker and cook for 3 whistles. Mash or puree the cooked dal with a hand blender, adding a cup of water.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle. Add asafoetida and sauté for a minute.
Pour the mashed dal into the pan with a cup of water, then add salt, slit green chilli, and crushed black peppercorns.
Mix well and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes. Turn off the flame and stir in lemon juice.
Garnish with coriander leaves, mix, and serve hot.
Optionally, serve the soup alongside Sweet Potato & Methi Stuffed Paratha and Raw Papaya, Apple & Carrot Salad.

title: Moong Dal Ke Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Green Moong Dal (Whole), soaked overnight
instructions: Soak the whole moong dal overnight. After soaking, drain the dal and keep it in a bowl. Keep all the other ingredients handy.
Take a saucepan, heat about 1 tablespoon ghee and add cumin seeds.
When the seeds start crackling, add the drained soaked moong dal, add salt and mix everything well.
Cook the dal on medium heat for about 5 minutes, then turn off the heat. Transfer the cooked dal to a bowl and allow it to cool.
Once the dal cools to near room temperature, grind it in a mixer without adding any water until it has a coarse powder-like consistency.
Add salt, black pepper powder, red chilli powder, and garam masala powder to the bowl and mix thoroughly.
Add the hung curd and knead gently to make a soft dough. Divide the dough into about 10 equal parts, shape them into smooth balls, and press gently to flatten.
Heat a shallow frying pan with a little ghee. Fry the kebabs in batches until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with raw onion rings and green chutney.

title: Achari Paneer Mini Bread Bowl With Cheesy Twist Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Achaari Paneer Mini Bread Bowl With Cheesy Twist Recipe, cut the soup buns from center and scoop out to create a pot like hollow center. Once done, keep them aside.
The next step is to make the filling. To make achari paneer/cottage cheese filling, cut the paneer in rough chunks.
Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan. Add green chilies, onions and let it cook for about a minute or two. Add ginger garlic paste and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes.
Take a bowl, add red chilli powder, coriander powder, achari masala, garam masala powder and one tablespoon water. Mix everything and add the masala in pan. Cook for about 3 to 4 minutes.
After 3 to 4 minutes, add capsicum and cook for 4 to 5 more minutes. Add tomatoes and cook till the tomatoes becomes soft and mushy. Add Paneer and give it a stir.
Mix well, put Achaari masala & Kasuri methi/dried fenugreek leaves. Add salt & cook for 2-3 minutes, your Achari Paneer/Cottage cheese filling is ready.
Now take out cheese spread and nicely spread it in the hollow bread bowls, one tablespoon in each bowl would be sufficient.
Put the Achari Paneer/Cottage cheese filling till the top into the bread bowls. Top them with mozzarella cheese.
Now on convection bake the pots for 8-10 minutes at 180 degrees. Your Achari Paneer Mini Bread Bowl with Cheesy twist is ready. Sprinkle some oregano and serve them hot.
Serve Achari Paneer Mini Bread Bowl With Cheesy Twist along with some Masala Chai and Linzer Cookies during your tea time on weekends.

title: Easy Vegan Date Roll Recipe
ingredients: 200 grams mixed nuts, chopped or ground (e.g., peanuts, walnuts, cashews, almonds)
Almond butter or any vegan butter, as needed
instructions: Clean the dates, ensure they are deseeded, then add them to a grinder and blend to a smooth paste; add almond butter or vegan butter for proper mixing.
Roast the mixed nuts well and grind them.
Grind the roasted nuts, then add vegan butter and mix to achieve a crumbly texture similar to the date mixture.
On a plastic surface, spread the date mixture into a flat sheet about half an inch thick, ensuring even thickness.
Cover the date sheet with the nut mixture and gently press it onto the dates.
Roll the layered sheet into a log, pressing gently to keep the roll intact.
Place the roll in the freezer and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Slice the chilled roll into half‑inch thick pieces.
Serve the vegan date rolls as a dessert or a healthy snack.

title: Mooli Aur Kaccha Kela Kofta Recipe (Grated Radish And Raw Banana Dumplings In Gravy)
ingredients: 7 cashew nuts, ground to a paste
2 teaspoons coriander (dhania) leaves, finely chopped for garnish
instructions: Steam the raw bananas in a steamer or pressure cook for one whistle, peel, mash and keep aside.
Grate the radishes, sprinkle some salt over and leave it to release all its water, squeeze and keep aside.
Prepare the onion paste, tomato puree and cashew paste one by one using a mixer grinder and keep aside until you begin to cook the gravy.
Make the kofta mix by combining the mashed raw banana, grated radish, roasted besan, green chilli, grated ginger, red chilli powder, caraway seeds, and season with salt in a big bowl.
Form small koftas and keep them ready to fry using a paniyaram pan.
Heat the paniyaram pan, brush it with a little oil, place the koftas in each cavity and let them roast on the bottom.
Once the bottom is cooked, flip over and cook the other side, applying a little oil if required, then set aside.
Prepare the rest of the koftas similarly.
Heat oil in a pan, add the bay leaf and cardamom and let it release its flavour into the oil.
Add the onion paste and sauté until it turns golden brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add the tomato puree, slit green chilli, Kashmiri red chilli, coriander, and garam masala and cook until the oil separates.
Whisk together the yoghurt and cashew paste with a little water to a smooth consistency and add it to the pan.
Add 2 cups of water (or as needed for desired consistency), season with salt and let the gravy simmer for 10 minutes.
Gently drop the prepared koftas into the gravy and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve the kofta with the accompanying dishes.

title: How To Make Homemade Rose Syrup Recipe
instructions: To begin making the homemade rose syrup recipe, first clean and dry the fresh rose petals. Skip the following process if you are using store‑bought dried rose petals.
If using fresh petals, clean them in running water, then dry completely on kitchen paper towels at room temperature; drying will take a couple of days until the petals are crisp and break apart.
Once the petals are dry (or if using store‑bought dried petals), proceed to make the rose syrup.

Boil the water in a saucepan. Place the petals in a glass bowl and pour the boiled water over them, stirring briefly. Let the petals steep until the water cools, then refrigerate the bowl for 12–15 hours.

The next day, strain the infused water into a saucepan (the rose water will be dark red). Heat on medium, add the sugar and the clove, and stir until the sugar dissolves. When it begins to froth, let the foam subside, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes before turning off the heat.
Allow the rose syrup to cool completely; it will thicken as it cools.
The rose syrup is now ready for use in ice creams, milkshakes, juices, or classic rose milk. Store in a glass bottle in the refrigerator for up to two months.

title: Chocolate Modak Recipe
ingredients: 2 cups Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), made fresh at home
instructions: Refer to the Homemade Paneer Recipe or follow the process to make homemade chenna/paneer.
In a large mixing bowl, add the homemade chenna, icing sugar, desiccated coconut, vanilla extract, and cocoa powder, then knead well for at least 5 minutes until the mixture is well combined.
Ensure the mixture is smooth without lumps, form it into a ball, and pinch lime-sized portions to shape into modaks.
Use modak moulds to give them the trademark shape, optionally placing a whole almond inside each before shaping.
Serve the chocolate modaks along with other festive sweets.

title: Cheesy & Spicy Pull Apart Bread Recipe With Indian Spices
instructions: To begin making the Cheesy & Spicy Pull Apart Bread Recipe With Indian Spices, in a mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients for the dough except the oil. Add a little warm water at a time and knead to make a smooth dough. Once the dough has come together, add the oil and knead for 3 to 4 minutes until smooth.
Cover the bread dough and keep it aside in a warm place to rise until doubled for about 2 hours.
Cook the soy nuggets in hot boiling water until it feels soft and spongy. Once cooked, drain the water out and squeeze the excess water. Mince the soy nuggets and keep aside.
While the dough is rising we will prepare the spicy masala for the filling.

Heat oil in a heavy bottomed pan over medium heat. add the cumin seeds, chopped onions, green chilies and saute until the onions are translucent. Add the diced potatoes, chopped bell pepper, baby corn and saute until the potato and the vegetables get cooked well.
Once the vegetables have cooked through, add the garam masala powder, chili powder, salt and cook in medium flame, now add the minced soya nuggets and stir well to combine.
Check the salt and spices and adjust to suit your taste. Keep the masala aside.
After couple of hours, once the dough has risen, punch down the dough and roll it into a large disc on a floured surface.

With a cookie cutter, cut medium sized round discs and spoon enough masala in the center. Fold the disc filled with masala into a half moon and tuck the edges together. It will look like a calzone or a gujiya. Proceed the same way with the remaining dough portions.
Arrange the half moon filled dough in a round springform baking pan. Allow the dough to rest for an hour in a warm place. This will help the dough to rise the second time.

Preheat the oven to 165°C. Sprinkle some cheese over the Spicy Pull Apart Masala Bread and place it into the oven for 35 to 40 minutes until the crust has turned golden brown and the bread feels cooked through.
Once done, remove from the oven and serve warm.
Serve the Cheesy & Spicy Pull Apart Bread as a side dish or even as a main dish along with a bowl of Roasted Cherry Tomato Soup and Pasta Primavera With Fresh Basil for dinner.

title: Mohan Bhog Recipe - Bengali Style Sooji Ka Halwa
instructions: Boil water, milk, sugar, saffron and cardamom in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar melts; keep the liquid mixture aside on simmer on another stove.
In a wide heavy-bottomed pan, heat 1/2 cup ghee over medium heat, add the sooji and roast until aromatic and light golden, without over‑browning.
Gradually stir in the hot milk mixture, keeping the heat medium as it may splutter.
Continue stirring until the halwa thickens and leaves the sides of the pan; cover and simmer a few minutes, stirring occasionally.
When the halwa is fully cooked and separates from the pan, turn off heat, cover with a lid and let rest for a few minutes.
In a small pan, heat 1 tablespoon ghee over medium heat, add cashew nuts and raisins and roast until the cashews turn golden brown.
Turn off the heat and mix this tempering into the Mohan Bhog.
Serve the Mohan Bhog with Luchi, Aloo Dum, and Moong Sprouts Salad with grated carrots and coriander.

title: Shalgam Gajar Aur Gobhi Ka Achar Recipe
ingredients: 250 grams Cauliflower (gobi), cut to small florets
2 teaspoon Red Chilli powder (adjust to taste)
instructions: Wash the turnips, carrots, and cauliflower thoroughly.
Peel the turnips and carrots, then cut them into thin slices.
Cut the cauliflower into small florets.
Bring 2 liters of water to a boil in a large pot.
Add the vegetables to the boiling water.
Cook the vegetables for 3-4 minutes, then drain the water.
Spread the vegetables on a cotton cloth and let them dry completely for 3-4 hours, ensuring no moisture remains.
In a bowl, mix the mustard seeds, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt, and the dried vegetables.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until it starts to fume, then turn off the heat and let it cool slightly.

Pour the oil over the spiced vegetables, stir well, and transfer the pickle into a clean, sterilized jar along with the oil; cover the jar with a muslin cloth tied with a string and keep it in the sun for 2-3 days to marinate.
After marination, serve the pickle with parathas, mathris, or rice. Store in a cool, dry place for up to 3 months or refrigerate for 4-5 months.

title: Seem Paal Recipe - Steamed Colostrum Milk Pudding
instructions: Add water to the idli steamer and place a plate at the bottom to separate the bowl from the steamer.
Take colostrum milk in a wide bowl that fits inside the steamer.
Add sugar and cardamom to the milk and mix well with a spoon until the jaggery/sugar dissolves.
Place the bowl inside the steamer and steam for 15-20 minutes until the milk becomes firm, like pudding.
Switch off and let it remain in the steamer for a while.
Remove the bowl, run a knife along its edges and invert the Seem Paal gently onto a plate. Serve it as a dessert.
Serve Seem Paal after a meal of Karnataka Style Avarekalu Pulao, Karuvepillai Pachadi, and South Indian Style Green Moong Sprouts Raw Mango Salad.

title: Sweet and Spicy Strawberry Chutney Recipe
ingredients: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), for garnish
instructions: In a saucepan, add the strawberries, jaggery, and lemon juice; cook while stirring continuously until the strawberries soften and the jaggery melts.
