When the strawberries are halfway cooked, add turmeric powder, grated ginger, salt, and red chilli powder; stir and continue cooking until the chutney thickens, then turn off the heat and transfer to a serving bowl.
In a small pan, heat 1/4 teaspoon oil and add cumin seeds, allowing them to crackle; remove from heat, pour the tempering over the chutney, stir, and garnish with kasuri methi.
Serve the strawberry chutney as an accompaniment for chaats, a dip with crackers, a spread over breads, or alongside parathas.

title: Chana Dal Pulao Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Garam masala powder (or pulao masala)
instructions: Wash and soak the rice for about 30 minutes. Clean, wash and soak the Bengal gram dal in water for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker over medium heat, add cumin seeds and sauté for a few seconds until they turn brown.
Add the dry red chilies and green chilies, sauté for a minute, then add the sliced onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté until soft and mushy. Add salt, turmeric powder and garam (biryani) pulao masala, and sauté briefly.
Drain the soaked rice and Bengal gram dal, then add them to the pressure cooker with 2 cups of water.
Stir to combine, close the lid, place the weight on, and cook over medium heat for one or two whistles.
Turn off the heat and allow the steam to escape naturally.
Open the lid, add lemon juice and mix gently with a spoon.
Serve the Chana Dal Pulao with Tomato Onion Raita and Satvik Carrot Sprout Salad.

title: Prawn Masala Rice Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 Red Yellow or Green Bell Pepper (Capsicum)
instructions: Marinate the prawns by applying chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt; set aside for 30 minutes.
Scrape the outer skin of the carrot and cut it into fine long slices; chop the capsicum into thin long slices.
Par‑boil the basmati rice in a saucepan with bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves and a pinch of salt.
Add 1 teaspoon oil to the boiling rice to prevent it from becoming sticky.
After par‑boiling, spread the rice on a colander or big strainer to drain and let it dry for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle cinnamon powder and black pepper powder over the dried rice.
In a kadai or wok, heat oil and fry onions until pinkish, then add a paste of garlic and ginger and fry briefly.
Add the sliced veggies, fry briefly, then add the marinated prawns (cut into 2‑3 pieces) and fry for about 8 minutes.
Add the sauces (soy sauce, green chilli sauce, roasted tomato pasta sauce) and fry for another minute.
Season with salt and mix well.
Add the cooked basmati rice, mix gently ensuring the grains do not break, then add butter and mix thoroughly.
Turn off the heat and garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Serve the Prawn Masala Rice with green salad and raita of your choice.

title: Cheesy Chicken Tikka Recipe
instructions: Thoroughly wash and clean the chicken.
For the first marination: add chicken pieces, ginger paste, garlic paste, black pepper powder, and lemon juice to a mixing bowl; coat well, cover, and rest for 15-20 minutes.
For the second marination: in another bowl, combine the egg, cheese, cream, corn flour, green chilli, coriander leaves, nutmeg powder, mace powder, garam masala powder, and salt.
After 15-20 minutes, add the first-marinated chicken to the second marination mixture, adjust salt, mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4-6 hours.
Oven method: preheat the oven to 180 °C, line a baking tray with aluminum foil, grease wooden or metal skewers with oil/butter.
Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto the skewers (4–5 pieces per skewer), place on the tray, drizzle with oil, and cook for 20 minutes.
Flip the skewers after 7‑8 minutes and cook the other side; if they appear dry, brush with oil/butter.
Stove‑top method: heat a tava or griddle, apply butter, and when it sizzles place the skewers on it.
Turn the skewers frequently and cook until golden brown on all sides; serve with salad on the side.
Serve the Cheesy Chicken Tikka with a dip such as Pudina Dahi Chutney and optional sides like Smoked Tandoori Paneer Tikka.

title: Doodh Dudhi Recipe- Bottle Gourd In Milk Curry
instructions: Peel and slice the doodhi into cubes, semi‑circles, or rounds, as desired.
Heat oil in a kadhai and add the cumin seeds; when they crackle, add salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric powder.
Cook the spices for 2–3 minutes, then add the doodhi and mix well, ensuring it is coated with the masala. Cover and cook for 4–5 minutes.

When the doodhi is soft, add half of the milk and cook for another 2–3 minutes until the milk evaporates; then add the remaining milk and simmer until the doodhi is fully cooked and the gravy thickens.
Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with chopped coriander.
Serve the Doodh Dudhi with phulkas or whole wheat lachha parathas.

title: Honeycomb Toffee | Cinder Toffee Recipe
ingredients: 4 tablespoon Corn syrup, or golden syrup
instructions: To prepare Honeycomb Toffee | Cinder Toffee Recipe, it is very important to get all the ingredients at an arm’s reach, since it is a quick recipe. Also, grease the parchment paper thoroughly and line a baking sheet.
Take a Large Saucepan and pour in sugar, corn syrup/golden syrup, and water and mix well till combined.
Now, on a high flame, let the sugar melt. Do not try to sauté or mix. You can only swirl the pan a couple of times, though.
Dip in a Candy thermometer set it to 300 degrees Fahrenheit. (Mine reached this stage after 4 minutes 50 seconds).

Witness magic of soda now. Take the pan off the flame and add baking soda and whisk vigorously with a wooden ladle for about 30 turns. The mixture will bubble up high like lava at this stage (thrice the initial volume). The color changes to amber.
Pour the bubbling mixture on a lined baking pan with greased parchment paper and let it set for 2 hours in open air at room temperature.
Break the honeycomb candy brittle, with a kitchen hammer or a heavy spoon.

Store in an airtight jar away from moisture and enjoy homemade honeycomb toffee whenever you want, dipped in warm chocolate ganache. Serve it along with Fresh Ginger Lemonade to pair with Spinach Corn Sandwich Recipe during snack time.

title: Nellikai Pachadi Recipe (Amla/ Gooseberry Raita)
instructions: Into a blender, grind the raw gooseberries, grated coconut, green chillies and salt into a coarse mixture; set aside.
In a bowl, whisk the yogurt until smooth. Stir in the ground gooseberry mixture and grated cucumber. Adjust salt and spices to taste.
Transfer the Nellikai (Amla) Raita into a serving bowl.
Heat oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds and curry leaves, and allow them to crackle.
Pour the seasoning over the Nellikai Pachadi (Amla Raita), stir well, and serve with your choice of Pulao.

title: Masala Puri Chaat Recipe
instructions: Wash and soak the dried green peas overnight; in the morning wash again, drain and pressure cook with 2 cups water for 3 whistles until well cooked, then set aside.
Dry roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds and dried red chillies until aromatic, let cool, and grind into a fine powder using a mixer grinder.
Return the cooked green peas to the heat, add the freshly prepared spice powder, season with salt, and lightly mash with the back of a ladle.
If the masala is too thick, add water to reach the desired consistency, check seasoning, simmer for a few minutes, then switch off the heat.
To assemble, roughly crush a handful of fried pani puris on a plate, pour a couple of ladlefuls of the hot green peas masala over them, and add a teaspoon of green chutney.
Garnish with chopped onions, tomatoes, sev, coriander leaves, squeeze the juice of 1/4 lemon on top, and serve.
Serve the Masala Puri Chaat as an evening tea-time snack with Masala Chai, optionally alongside Peanut Chaat With Spiced Yogurt or Homemade Canape Papdi Chaat.

title: Kimami Sewai Recipe
ingredients: 1/4 cup Whole Almonds (Badam), slivered, 1/4 cup for garnish
1 tablespoon Cashew nuts, slivered, 1/4 tablespoon for garnish
1 tablespoon Sultana Raisins, 1/4 tablespoon for garnish
instructions: Heat a pan on low flame and roast dry sewai until dark brown; set aside, avoiding over‑roasting.
In the same pan, heat ghee and fry the fox nuts/makhana until crunchy (5–6 minutes on low‑medium heat).
Add dry fruits and sauté for about 2 minutes; finally add coconut (it burns quickly), fry all together and set aside.
In a deep pan, combine sugar, khoya, milk, and water; stir over flame until the first boil, then reduce heat and cook the syrup until it thickens and feels heavy.
Add 1/2 cup water or milk to the thick syrup and bring to another boil.
Add the roasted sewai and the dry‑fruit‑makhana‑coconut mixture; cook on low flame for 4–5 minutes, then switch off.
Sprinkle green cardamom powder, mix well, cover and let stand for 10 minutes; then give a final stir and garnish with almonds, cashews and raisins.
Serve the Kimami Sewai.

title: Quick Indian Style Ginger Pickle Recipe
instructions: To prepare the Ginger Pickle, first peel and wash the ginger. Pat dry it with the kitchen towel.
Cut ginger into thin juliennes or strips. Place the juliennes in a glass mixing bowl, add the salt and give it a good stir. Set this aside for 5 minutes or till ginger releases water and turns soft.
While the ginger is in the bowl slice the chillies diagonally into thin, long slices.
Add the chillies and lemon juice to the ginger and give it a good stir. Let the pickle rest for a few minutes at room temperature and the ginger changes color to light pink.
Transfer instant ginger pickle to a clean and dry glass jar, seal the jar with a lid and store the pickle in the refrigerator.
Serve the Quick Indian Style Ginger Pickle with paratha for breakfast or along with any other main course dish.

title: Veg Tunday Kabab Recipe
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Yellow mustard seeds , and black mustard
instructions: Start to prepare Veg tunday kababs recipe by taking out all the dry spices in a pan and temper them well.
Grind them to make a fine powder and keep it aside.
Boil the Paneer/Cottage Cheese to make sure its soft.
Chop the paneer, capsicum, onion into chunks for sticking on to the skewers.
Puree the half onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli into a paste and keep aside.
Now lets prepare the marinade - add in curd, tempered spice powder, pureed ginger-garlic-onion-chilli paste.
Using both hands mix together the marinate to the chopped veggies and paneer and keep in the refrigerator for a good one to one and a half hours for marination. The longer the better.
Take a flat pan, pour in one tablespoon oil and spread uniformly bringing to low-medium heat.
Take your skewers and line them with capsicum followed by onion followed by paneer and so on. You can add other vegetables like zucchini, tomato also to it.
Place the skewers on the hot flat pan and reduce the flame to low.
Cook each side rotating the skewers and brushing in the marinate on the cooked side as soon as it cooks.
Serve Veg tunday kababs recipe hot as a starter or a dry curry with bread of your choice.

title: Gajar Methi Sabzi Recipe (Carrot Fenugreek Leaves Stir Fry)
ingredients: 1 cup Methi Leaves (Fenugreek Leaves), tightly packed
instructions: To begin making the Gajar Methi Sabzi recipe, firstly peel, wash and chop the carrots into small pieces.
Pick the methi leaves from stem and wash the leaves well. Chop the methi leaves fine.
Heat oil in a wok/kadai. Add cumin seeds to hot oil and wait till it turns brown. Add asafoetida, mix.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté till onions turn soft and translucent.
Add coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt to taste and give it good mix.
Now add chopped carrots, mix and cook until for 5 minutes on medium flame.
Add 1/4 cup water and continue to cook the carrots. When carrots are half done, add finely chopped methi leaves.
Cook until all vegetables are cooked, keep stirring in between.
When all water evaporates and carrots turn tender, sprinkle amchur powder and 1 more teaspoon oil over the vegetables and stir well.
Cook for 2 minutes on low flame, remove the pan from stove and serve hot.

title: Dry Fruits Suzhiyam (Boorelu) With Black Rice Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Dry Fruits (raisins, dried cranberry, dates)
3/4 cup Mixed nuts (almond, walnut, pumpkin seeds)
instructions: Prepare the batter by soaking urad dal, black rice, and idli rice for a minimum of 4 to 5 hours or overnight.
Grind the urad dal in a mixer until it becomes like a butter consistency.
Add idli rice, black rice, salt and water to the urad dal mixture and grind until the consistency is like idli batter.
Leave the batter for 4 to 6 hours for fermentation (optional).
Add rawa to the batter and mix to make it thick enough to dip the dry fruit balls.
For the stuffing, dry roast the mixed nuts until the raw smell disappears and grind them in a mixer.
Add ghee and dry fruits to the ground nuts and mix well; after about 3 minutes, add cardamom powder and cook until the mixture becomes sticky, adding water if needed (especially when using raisins).
Add the powdered nuts to the mixture and mix thoroughly; turn off the heat.
Grease your palms with ghee and shape the hot mixture into round balls.
Heat oil in a deep-fry pan, dip the nut balls into the batter, and fry until cooked through.
Remove the fried suzhiyam and place on tissue paper to absorb excess oil.
Serve the Dry Fruits Suzhiyam (Boorelu) with Black Rice as a festive dessert.

title: Goat Curry In Yogurt Gravy Recipe
ingredients: 800 grams Mutton, cut into about 1 inch size pieces
instructions: Wash the goat meat well and set aside.
Slice the onion vertically into very thin slices.
Add ghee (or oil) to a large saucepan over medium‑high heat, then add the whole spices and sliced onions, sprinkling a little salt to help moisture evaporate.
Sauté the onions until they turn brown, then add the goat meat and mix well.
Fry for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally; add yogurt, red chilli powder, turmeric and salt, mix, cover and cook on medium‑high heat for 40 minutes.
Check the curry; if it looks dry, add some water and continue cooking. Stir in garam masala and grated garlic.
Cover again and cook until the meat is soft when tested with a toothpick (about 50 minutes total, depending on meat tenderness).
Sprinkle chopped coriander leaves, mix well, remove from heat and serve.
Serve the goat curry in yogurt gravy with Jeera Pulao and sliced onions.

title: Safed Achari Baingan Recipe - White Aubergine in pickled spices
instructions: To begin making the Achari Baingan Recipe, we will first make the achari masala.

To prepare marinade for Achari masala, in a pan add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, nigella seed, carom seeds, fenugreek seeds and dry red chilies. Dry roast the spices and chilies over medium heat till fragrant and slightly browned. Turn off the heat. Transfer spices to the jar of mixer and grind into a coarse powder. Keep the achari powder aside.
Wash and clean baingan and keep aside.
Heat oil in a wok and add mustard and cumin seeds in it and wait till they crackle.
Add chopped onions and saute till raw smell goes off. Now add ginger garlic paste and fry well till golden.
Now add turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chili powder and the achari masala along with chopped tomatoes.
Saute until the tomatoes soften. Meanwhile slit the baingan from the middle into two but keep the joint intact. This is done so that the masala gets inside the aubergine nicely while cooking.
Add the baingan in the fried masala and mix well such that everything incorporates well.
Add little amchur if required and stir well. Add little water just to make sure the masala doesn't stick to the bottom of the heavy bottomed pan.
Add salt as per your taste and slow cook the baingan in low flame with lid closed.
Once the baingan softens, turn off the heat and garnish with freshly chopped coriander and stir.
Serve the Safed Achari Baingan Recipe along with hot Phulkas smeared with ghee or along with hot steamed rice as a one dish dinner or a quick weeknight dinner.

title: Chatpata Peanut Salad - Peanut Chaat Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Roasted Peanuts (Moongphali), steamed and skin peeled
Coriander (Dhania) Leaves, a small bunch finely chopped
instructions: To begin making Chatpata Peanut Salad/ Peanut Chaat, prep all the ingredients.
Prepare Green Chutney by following the link Green Chutney Recipe - Coriander Mint Chutney Recipe.
Toss all the ingredients for the peanut chaat in a large mixing bowl.
Adjust the seasonings to taste of the peanut chaat and serve.
Serve Chatpata Peanut Salad as a starter to your party and pair it along with a main course of Spicy Paneer Pulao With Vegetables, Almond and Cashew Nut Mushroom Curry and Dahi Vada.

title: Instant Carrot Pickle Recipe
instructions: Combine all the ingredients except the oil in a bowl and mix everything well; set aside.
Heat the mustard oil in a small pan, then add the hot oil to the carrot mixture and mix well. Serve immediately or keep refrigerated until use.
Serve the instant carrot pickle with phulka, whole wheat lachha paratha, or puri.

title: Stove Top Green Peas Seekh Kebab Recipe
instructions: Pressure cook peas and whole potatoes together. Keep aside to cool.
Strain the peas and peel the potatoes.
In a large bowl, take boiled peas and potatoes and mash them well with hands or a fork.
Add gram flour for binding along with onions, ginger garlic paste, mint, coriander, dry spices and salt. Add few drops of lemon juice too.
Mix them well and bind to make a dough. Cling wrap the bowl and refrigerate for 30 mins before use.
Take bamboo skewers and grease them with oil. Pinch a small ball of dough and coat it all around the skewer, such that the skewer passes from middle. Leave space from both sides to hold.
Similarly, prepare the rest of the seekhs too.
Heat a nonstick broad base pan. Place the seekhs on the pan and brush oil on top and sides of the seeks.
Keep turning the skewers so that the Green Peas Seekh Kebab get fried from all sides. Shallow fry till golden.
Transfer the kebabs onto kitchen towel or tissue paper so that the excess oil gets absorbed.
Arrange them on a serving platter and serve with a spicy minty dip, lemon wedges and onions.
If desired, slide the kebabs off the skewers, cut into pieces and serve as a party appetizer.

title: Dry Jamun Recipe
ingredients: 1/2 cup Water, to make sugar syrup
instructions: Begin by making the sugar syrup: place a saucepan on medium heat, add sugar and half a cup of water, and boil until the sugar dissolves and the syrup reaches a one‑string consistency; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine crumbled khoya, grated paneer, milk powder, cardamom powder, and powdered sugar; mix well.
Gradually add the all‑purpose flour to the mixture and knead into a smooth yet stiff dough; shape small lemon‑size balls and set aside.
Heat ghee in a pan and fry the jamun balls in batches until golden brown, stirring to avoid burning.
Transfer the fried jamun balls into the prepared sugar syrup and toss to coat all the balls evenly.
Allow the jamuns to soak in the syrup for a few minutes, then remove them onto a plate.
Spread desiccated coconut on a plate and gently roll each jamun ball in the coconut until fully coated.
Repeat the coating process for any remaining jamuns.
Serve the Dry Jamun as a festive dessert.

title: Jowar Bajra Garlic Roti Recipe
instructions: To begin making Jowar Bajra Garlic Roti, in a bowl mix jowar flour and bajra flour.
Add garlic, pepper powder and salt to it. Mix all the ingredients well.
Add water little by little and knead into soft dough.
Divide into small balls and roll it flat with a rolling pin dusting some flour if required.
Heat a roti tawa and place the rolled out Jowar Bajra Garlic Roti.
Cook the Jowar Bajra Garlic Roti on a medium flame turning both the sides until brown spots appear. Take it off the griddle, add a teaspoon of ghee on top of the roti.
Finish the rest of the rotis and your Jowar Garlic Roti is ready to be served.
Serve Jowar Bajra Garlic Roti Recipe along with Mixed Vegetable Kurma for breakfast.

You can even serve the Jowar Bajra Garlic Roti for a healthy lunch along with Horsegram Dal (Kulith/Kollu Dal) and Raw Jackfruit & Peanut Masala Poriyal with Sambar Powder for a diabetic‑friendly meal.

title: Hare Chane Ka Kebab Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup Hara Chana, soaked overnight in water
instructions: Pressure cook green chana with enough water until the cooker releases 4-5 whistles.
Remove from heat, drain the water completely, and reserve the water for later use.
Combine all ingredients except besan and blend together with the cooked chana to a coarse paste, adding a little water if needed.
Transfer the paste to a bowl, add 1 or 2 tablespoons besan, and knead into a smooth dough.
Cover and let the dough rest for an hour; you can deep fry, shallow fry, or bake the kebabs later.
Shape small patties from the dough and shallow fry them in a wide pan with a little oil until golden brown on both sides.
Serve the Hare Chane Ka Kebab with Dhaniya Pudina Chutney or Lahsun Ki Chutney.

title: Chicken Kathi Roll Recipe
ingredients: 200 grams Chicken breasts, cut into thin strips
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the washed and cleaned chicken strips with the yogurt, salt, turmeric powder, tandoori masala, and lemon juice; let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a pan with oil over medium flame, add ginger and garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, then add sliced onions and capsicum.
Cook the onion–capsicum mixture for another 3-4 minutes.
Add the marinated chicken along with any remaining marinade to the pan.
Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until the chicken tikka is cooked through and coated with the masala; then turn off the heat and transfer to a bowl.
In a large bowl combine flour, salt and a tablespoon of oil; knead adding water gradually to form a firm, smooth dough.
Coat the dough with another tablespoon of oil, knead again, cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
Knead once more, divide the dough into 4 portions, and preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Roll each portion into a ball, flatten with the palm, dust with flour and roll out into an 8‑inch circle.
Place a rolled‑out paratha on the hot skillet; after a few seconds flip to the other side.
Flip the plain paratha again, drizzle a little oil and cook until almost done.
Spread two tablespoons of beaten egg on one side of the paratha and flip; cook for about a minute until the egg is set, then remove and set aside.
Place the prepared chicken tikka filling on one side of the egg‑coated paratha, add pickled onions and sprinkle chaat masala.
Fold the paratha over the filling to form a roll and serve.
Serve the Chicken Tikka Kathi Roll with green chutney or accompanying drinks as desired.

title: Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney Recipe With Garlic
instructions: Prep the ingredients as described.
In a heavy-bottom pan, add all the ingredients except the jaggery, lemon juice, and red chilli powder.
Cook over medium flame, stirring continuously, until the tomatoes soften.
When the tomatoes soften, add the jaggery and red chilli powder; continue cooking on medium flame until the chutney thickens.
Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice, and stir. Adjust salt, sweetness, and spice to taste.
Serve the Sweet and Spicy Tomato Chutney with Garlic.

title: Methi Sprouts Salad Recipe - Healthy & Tasty Diabetic Snack
instructions: Ensure the methi sprouts are ready; you can use store‑bought sprouts or sprout them at home.
If sprouting at home, soak methi seeds in water overnight, then drain and wrap them in a muslin cloth kept in a warm place for 1 day.
After 24 hours, open the cloth to reveal the sprouts.
In a mixing bowl, combine the methi sprouts with roasted peanuts, chopped onions, chopped tomatoes, and coriander leaves; mix well.
Sprinkle salt, black pepper powder, chaat masala, and add lemon juice; stir to combine.
Transfer the salad to a platter and serve as a diabetic snack or side dish.
Optionally serve the salad alongside Ragi Tawa Paratha, Methi Moong Dal, Masala Karela, and Mooli Raita for a complete meal.

title: Besan Burji Recipe-Chickpea Flour Scramble Recipe
instructions: To begin making the Besan Burji Recipe we will make the batter and keep it ready.
For the batter add gram flour, flax seed powder and curd into a large mixing bowl and keep aside.

Heat a flat skillet, add oil and splutter the cumin seeds and fry the onions till it is translucent, once done add in the capsicum, mushrooms, green chilies and saute till the water from the mushrooms evaporate and the vegetables are cooked.

Once the vegetables are cooked add in all the spice powders, turmeric powder, cumin powder and red chilli powder. Stir well to combine. Spread the vegetables evenly in the pan, then slowly pour in the mixed batter and cover all the vegetables.
Cook on low heat for about 5 minutes. The batter gets slowly cooked at the edges. Now start mixing it slowly, making sure it does not become mushy.
Keep stir frying till it becomes brown and takes in the texture of bhurji, add salt and coriander leaves at this point.
Serve the Besan Burji Recipe along with a Banana Almond & Prunes Smoothie Recipe as a healthy breakfast.

title: Shakarkandi Chaat Recipe -Sweet Potato Tangy Salad
ingredients: 3 Sweet Potatoes, boiled, peeled and cut into cubes
instructions: Gather all the ingredients. Boil the sweet potatoes, peel them, and cut into cubes. Let them cool, optionally refrigerate.
Combine the boiled sweet potatoes, chopped onion, chopped green chillies, lemon juice, chopped coriander leaves, chaat masala powder, and salt in a bowl. Stir until well mixed.
Serve the Sweet Potato Tangy Salad immediately, optionally with picks for an appetizer.

title: Mustard Green Chilli Pickle Recipe
ingredients: 250 gram Green Chillies, washed & pat dried
instructions: Cut the green chillies into halves or more pieces.
Place the green chillies in a mixing bowl, add a pinch of salt and mix well.
Let the chillies sit for at least half an hour, then drain the salty water.
In another mixing bowl, combine mustard splits, asafoetida, oil, salt, jaggery, lemon juice, and turmeric powder.
Toss all the ingredients and beat them in a circular motion with your hand for about 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the green chillies to the mixture and toss thoroughly to coat.
Adjust salt and lemon juice to taste, then transfer to a sterilised bottle or glass jar and store in the fridge.
Serve the Mustard Green Chilli Pickle with any meal for extra tanginess and spiciness.

title: Sweet Potato & Peas Cutlet Recipe
ingredients: 3 Sweet Potato, boiled or roasted and mashed
1/2 cup Green peas (Matar), boiled and mashed
instructions: To prepare Sweet Potato & Peas Cutlet Recipe, take a bowl and mix mashed peas and cooked sweet potato.
Add ginger garlic paste, green chillies, and fresh coriander, mix well.
Add all the dry ingredients, chaat masala, salt, chilli powder, roasted cumin powder, dry mango powder, garam masala.
Add lime juice and mix everything well.
Also, mix corn flour and water in a small bowl.
Shape the mixture into medium size patties.
Dip the patty in corn flour mixture and roll into the breadcrumbs, making sure that the bread crumbs cover the cutlet well. Repeat for a batch of 3-4 patties at a time.
Heat oil in a pan and shallow fry them on both sides on low heat until golden brown.
Serve Sweet Potato & Peas Cutlet Recipe hot with dhaniya pudina chutney and dates and tamarind chutney or roasted tomato sauce.

title: Tandoori Chickpea & Cauliflower Curry Recipe (Vegan Curry)
ingredients: 1 or 2 pieces of coal, for smoking
instructions: Soak 1/2 cup raw chickpeas for 8 hours, then cook until soft; you should have about 1 cup of cooked chickpeas. Set aside.
Puree the tomatoes and set aside.
Pound the fennel seeds in a pestle and mortar until a coarse powder forms; set aside.
Prepare to cook the cauliflower for the tandoori curry.
In a large wok or kadai, heat a teaspoon of oil. Add cauliflower florets, sprinkle salt, and stir‑fry until cooked through but still firm, about 5–10 minutes.
Add turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, garam masala powder, and the fennel seed powder; stir. Then add tomato puree and cooked chickpeas, mixing well.
Adjust salt and spices to taste. Simmer on medium‑high heat for about 5 minutes while preparing the coal for smoking.
Heat a piece of coal (≈3 inches) over a gas flame with tongs until red‑hot and grey (about 5 minutes). Place the hot coal in a small steel or glass bowl.
Make a small well in the centre of the kadai, place the bowl with coal into it, and pour a spoon of ghee on the coal to generate smoke.
Cover the pan immediately, reduce heat to low, and let it rest for about a minute until the smoke subsides. Then remove the coal bowl.
The curry now has a smoked tandoori flavor.
Turn off the heat, transfer the curry to a serving dish, and sprinkle chopped mint leaves on top.
Serve the Tandoori Chickpea & Cauliflower Curry with hot steamed rice and a salad.
